Fischer.}}}} 38 [1884], p. 411) referred doubtfully to the textual readings in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=21|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=15|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=18|verse=12.14.19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, where the Masora uniformly inserts the termination ''û'', and to {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=48|verse=10}} in the Samaritan Pentateuch, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=35}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=13|verse=10}}. In his {{GHGcite|title=Beiträge zur sem. Sprachwiss.}}, p. 19, however, he observes that the construction of a fem. plural with the 3rd sing. fem. is not unexampled, and also that {{GHGheb|text=ה}} is often found as a mistake for {{GHGheb|text=ו}}. On the other hand Mayer Lambert ({{GHGcite|title=Une série de Qeré ketib}}, Paris, 1891, p. 6 ff.) explains all these K<sup>e</sup>thîbh, as well as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=50|verse=6}} (?), and (against Nöldeke) {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=49}} (where {{GHGheb|text=ה}} is undoubtedly the article belonging to the next word), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=16}} (where the {{GHGterm|masc.}} {{GHGheb|text=פָּנַי}} requires the marginal reading), also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=41}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=51|verse=56|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=14}}, as remains of the 3rd ''fem. plur.'' in {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}. The form was abandoned as being indistinguishable from the (later) form of the 3rd ''fem. sing.'', but tended to be retained in the perfect of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, as {{GHGheb|text=היה}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} six times in the above examples.

{{GHGmargin-letter|44|n}}
5. The afformatives {{GHGheb|text=תָּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=(תְּ)}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=נוּ}} are generally toneless, and the forms with these inflexions are consequently {{GHGterm|Milʿêl}} ({{GHGheb|text=קָטַ֫לְתָּ}}, &c.); with all the other afformatives they are {{GHGterm|Milraʿ}} ({{GHGpar|15|c}}). The place of the tone may, however, be shifted: (''a'') by the {{GHGterm|pause}} ({{GHGpar|29|i}}–v), whenever a vowel which has become vocal Š<sup>e</sup>wâ under the second stem-consonant is restored by the {{GHGterm|pause}}; as {{GHGheb|text=קָטָ֫לָה}} for {{GHGheb|text=קָֽטְלָ֫ה}} ({{GHGheb|text=דָּבֵ֫קָה}} for {{GHGheb|text=דָּֽבְקָ֫ה}}), and {{GHGheb|text=קָטָ֫לוּ}} for {{GHGheb|text=קָֽטְל֫וּ}} ({{GHGheb|text=מָלֵ֫אוּ}} for {{GHGheb|text=מָֽלְא֫וּ}}; (''b'') in certain cases after {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} of the {{GHGterm|Perfect}} (see {{GHGpar|49|h}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|44|o}}
6. Contraction of a final {{GHGheb|text=ת}} with the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} of the afformative occurs e.g. in {{GHGheb|text=כָּרַ֫תִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=2|verse=5}}, &c.; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=20}}, &c., in the ''Perf. Poʿel''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=25}} in the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} of {{GHGheb|text=שׁחת}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=2}}, &c., in the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} of {{GHGheb|text=שׁבת}}. Contraction of a final {{GHGheb|text=נ‍}} with the afformative {{GHGheb|text=נוּ}} occurs in {{GHGheb|text=נָתַ֫נּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=16}}; in ''Niph.'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=9|verse=7}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=14|verse=10}}; in ''Hiph.'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=29|verse=19}}; with the afformative {{GHGheb|text=נָה}} in the {{GHGterm|Imperfect Qal}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=17|verse=23}}; {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=71|verse=23}}, where with Baer and Ginsburg {{GHGheb|text=תְּרַנֵּ֫נָּה}} is to be read, according to others {{GHGheb|text=תְּרַנֶּ֫נָּה}} (cf. in ''Polel'' {{GHGheb|text=תְּקוֹנֶ֫נָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=32|verse=16}}), but certainly not {{GHGheb|text=תְּרַנֵּ֫נָה}} with the Mantua ed., Opitius and Hahn; with {{GHGheb|text=נָה}} in the ''Imperat. Hiph.'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=32|verse=9}}.
<section end=par44/>
<section begin=par45/>{{GHGpar-heading|45|The Infinitive}}

F. Prätorius, ‘''Ueber den sog. Inf. absol. des Hebr.,'' ’in {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1902, p. 546 ff.

{{GHGmargin-letter|45|a}}
'''1.''' The Infinitive is represented in Hebrew by two forms, a shorter and a longer; both are, however, strictly speaking, independent ''nouns'' ({{GHGterm|verbal substantives}}). The shorter form, ''the Infinitive construct'' (in Qal {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹל}},<ref>Cf. the analogous forms of the noun, {{GHGpar|93|t}}.</ref> sometimes incorrectly {{GHGheb|text=קְטוֹל}}), is used in very various ways, sometimes in connexion with pronominal suffixes, or governing a substantive in the genitive, or with an accusative of the object (§ 115), sometimes in connexion with prepositions ({{GHGheb|text=לִקְטֹל|translate=to kill}}, {{GHGpar|114|f}}), and sometimes in dependence upon substantives as genitive, or upon verbs as accusative of the object. On the other hand, the use of the longer form, the {{GHGterm|Infinitive absolute}} (in Qal {{GHGheb|text=קָטוֹל}}, sometimes also {{GHGheb|text=קָטֹל}}, obscured from original ''qăṭâl''), is restricted to those cases in which it emphasizes<section end=par45/><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

147.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="104.189.10.69" />{{GHGcorrected}}</noinclude><section begin="par45" />the abstract verbal idea, without regard to the subject or object of the action. It stands most frequently as an adverbial accusative with a finite verb of the same stem ({{GHGpar|113|h}}–s).<ref>The terms ''absolute'' and ''construct'' are of course not to be understood as implying that the Infin. constr. {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹל}} forms the {{GHGterm|construct state}} (see § 89) of the Infin. absol. ({{GHGheb|text=קָטוֹל}} ground-form ''qăṭâl''). In the Paradigms the ''Inf. constr.'', as the principal form, is placed before the other, under the name of Infinitive simply.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|45|b}}
The flexibility and versatility of the Infin. constr. and the rigidity and inflexibility of the Infin. absol. are reflected in their vocalization. The latter has unchangeable vowels, while the ''ō'' of the Infin. constr. may be lost. For {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹל}}, according to {{GHGpar|84|e|a}}, goes back to the ground-form ''qŭṭŭl''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|45|c}}
Other forms of the Infin. constr. Qal of the strong verb are—

(''a'') {{GHGheb|text=קְטַל}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שְׁכַב|translate=to lie}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=שְׁפַל|translate=to sink}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=4}}; especially with verbs which have ''ă'' in the second syllable of the Imperf.: hence sometimes also with those, whose second or third radical is a guttural (frequently besides the ordinary form). All the examples (except {{GHGheb|text=שְׁכַב}}, see above) occur in the closest connexion with the following word, or with suffixes (see {{GHGpar|61|c}}). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=33}} the Masora seems to treat {{GHGheb|text=לְטֶ֫בַח}} (verse 20, in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=לְטָבַח}}) as an Infinitive={{GHGheb|text=לִטְבֹּחַ}}; probably {{GHGheb|text=לַטֶ֫בַח}} should be read.

{{GHGmargin-letter|45|d}}
(''b'') {{GHGheb|text=קַטְלָה}} and, attenuated from it, {{GHGheb|text=קִטְלָה}}; {{GHGheb|text=קָטְלָה}} and {{GHGheb|text=קֻטְלָה}} (which are feminine forms<ref>According to the remark of Elias Levita on Qimḥi’s {{GHGcite|title=Mikhlol}}, ed. Rittenb., 14 ''a'', these feminine forms occur almost exclusively in connexion with the preposition {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}.</ref> of {{GHGheb|text=קְטַל}} and {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹל}}, mostly from intransitive verbs, and sometimes found along with forms having no feminine ending in use), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לְאַשְׁמָה|translate=to be guilty}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=26}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַֽהֲבָה|translate=to love}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׂנְאָה|translate=to hate}}; {{GHGheb|text=לְיִרְאָה}}, often in Dt., ''to fear''; {{GHGheb|text=זִקְנָה|translate=to be old}}; {{GHGheb|text=קִרְאָה|translate=to meet}} (in {{GHGheb|text=לִקְרַאת}} {{GHGpar|19|k}}); {{GHGheb|text=לְרִבְעָה|translate=to lie down}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=20|verse=16}}; {{GHGheb|text=לְמָשְׁחָה|translate=to anoint}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=29|verse=29}}; {{GHGheb|text=לְרָחְצָה|translate=to wash}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=30|verse=18}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=לְטָמְאָה}} (also a subst.= ''uncleanness'', like {{GHGheb|text=טֻמְאָה}}) ''to be unclean'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=15|verse=32}}; {{GHGheb|text=לְקָרְבָה|translate=to approach}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=36|verse=2}}, &c.; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=12|verse=4.5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=11|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=1|verse=6}}; also {{GHGheb|text=רָֽחֳקָה|translate=to be far off}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=8|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=חֻמְלָה|translate=to pity}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=5}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=7|verse=4}}. On the other hand in {{GHGheb|text=חֶמְלָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=16}}, the original ''ă'' has been modified to ''ĕ''; cf. {{GHGheb|text=חֶזְקָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=11}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|45|e}}
(''c'') In the Aramaic manner ({{GHGheb|text=מִקְטַל}} but cf. also Arab. ''maqtal'') there occur as ''Infin. Qal'': {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁלוֹחַ|translate=to send}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=9|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=מִקְרָא|translate=to call}} and {{GHGheb|text=מַסַּע|translate=to depart}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=10|verse=2}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=10|verse=11}}); {{GHGheb|text=מִקַּח|translate=to take}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=19|verse=7}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=מַשָּׂא|translate=to carry}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=4|verse=24}}, &c. (cf. even {{GHGheb|text=לְמַשְׂאוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=17|verse=9}}); also with a feminine ending {{GHGheb|text=מַֽעֲלָה|translate=to go up}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=7|verse=9}}, &c.; cf. for these forms (almost all very late) Ryssel, ''De Elohistae Pentateuchici sermone'', p. 50, and Strack on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=4|verse=24}}. {{:Gesenius' Hebrew Grammar/Additions and Corrections/123}}

(''d'') {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹ֫לֶת}} in {{GHGheb|text=יְב֫שֶׁת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְכֹ֫לֶת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=16}}; probably also {{GHGheb|text=חֲר֫שֶׁת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=31|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=35|verse=33|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|45|f}}
'''2.''' A kind of ''Gerund'' is formed by the ''Infin. constr.'' with the preposition {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}; as {{GHGheb|text=לִקְטֹל|translate=ad interficiendum}}, {{GHGheb|text=לִנְפֹּל|translate=ad cadendum}} (see {{GHGpar|28|a}}).
<section end="par45" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

148.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par45 />{{GHGmargin-letter|45|g}}
The blending of the {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} with the ''Infin. constr.'' into a single grammatical form seems to be indicated by the firmly closed syllable, cf. {{GHGheb|text=לִשְׁכַּב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=לִנְפֹּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=13}}, with {{GHGterm|Dageš lene}} in the {{GHGheb|text=פ}}=''lin-pōl''; hence, also ''liq-ṭōl'', &c.; but {{GHGheb|text=בִּנְפֹל}} ''bin<sup>e</sup>phōl'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=13}}; {{GHGheb|text=כִּנְפֹל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=34}}. Exceptions {{GHGheb|text=לִצְבֹא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=4|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=8|verse=24|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=לִנְתוֹשׁ וְלִנְתוֹץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=1|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=18|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=28|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=לִשְׁדוֹד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=47|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=לִטְבוֹחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=11|verse=19}}, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=37|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=לִבְדוֹק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=34|verse=10}}; according to some also {{GHGheb|text=לִסְבֹב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=4}} and {{GHGheb|text=לִכְבשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=28|verse=10}} (Baer {{GHGheb|text=לִכְבּשׁ}}); on the other hand {{GHGheb|text=בִּשְׁכֹּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=35|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=כִּזְכֹּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=2}}. For the meaningless {{GHGheb|text=לְדַרְיוֹשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=10|verse=16}} read {{GHGheb|text=לִדְרשׁ}}.<section end=par45 />
<section begin=par46 />{{GHGpar-heading|46|The Imperative}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|46|a}}
'''1.''' The ground-forms of the Imperative, {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹל}} (properly ''q<sup>e</sup>ṭŭl'', which is for an original ''qŭṭŭl''), and {{GHGheb|text=קְטַל}} (see below, c), the same in pronunciation as the forms of the Infin. constr. (§ 45), are also the basis for the formation of the Imperfect (§ 47).<ref>The ''Infin. absol.'', like the Greek Infin., is also sometimes used for the Imperative ({{GHGpar|113|bb}}). Cf. in general, Koch, ''Der semitische Inf.'' (Schaffhausen, 1874).</ref> They represent the ''second'' person, and have both fem. and plur. forms. The third person is supplied by the Imperfect in the Jussive ({{GHGpar|109|b}}); and even the second person must always be expressed by the Jussive, if it be used with a negative, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תִּקְטֹל|translate=ne occidas}} (not {{GHGheb|text=אַל־קְטֹל}}). The passives have no Imperative, but it occurs in the reflexives, as Niphʿal and Hithpaʿēl.<ref>In {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} an Imperative is found only twice ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=32|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer.|chapter=49|verse=8}}), and closely approximating in meaning to the reflexive.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|46|b}}
'''2.''' The Afformatives of the ''2nd sing. fem.'' and the ''2nd plur. masc.'' and {{GHGterm|fem.}} are identical in every case with those of the Imperfect ({{GHGpar|47|c}}). In the same way, the Imperative of the ''2nd sing. masc.'', in common with the Imperfect, admits of the lengthening by the {{GHGheb|text=־ָה|translate=paragogicum}} ({{GHGpar|48|i}}), as, on the other hand, there are certain shortened forms of this person analogous to the Jussive (§ 48. 5).

{{GHGmargin-letter|46|c}}
Rem. 1. Instead of the form {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹל}} (sometimes also {{GHGterm|plene}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שְׁמוֹר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=13}}; before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} {{GHGheb|text=קְטָל־}} with {{GHGterm|Qameṣ ḥaṭuph}}), those verbs which have an ''a'' in the final syllable of the ''Imperf.'' (i.e. especially verbs middle ''ē'') make their Imperative of the form {{GHGheb|text=קְטַל}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לְבַשֹׁ|translate=dress!}} (Perf. {{GHGheb|text=לָבַשׁ}} and {{GHGheb|text=לָבֵשׁ}}); {{GHGheb|text=שְׁכַב|translate=lie down!}} in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=שְׁכָ֑ב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=5.6.9}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|46|d}}
2. The first syllable of the sing. fem. and plur. masc. are usually to be pronounced with {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ mobile}} (''qĭṭ<sup>e</sup>lî'', ''qĭṭ<sup>e</sup>lû'', and so {{GHGheb|text=שִׁפְכִי}}, &c., without {{GHGterm|Dageš lene}}, and even {{GHGheb|text=מִֽשְׁכוּ}} with {{GHGterm|Metheg}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=21}}; but cf. {{GHGheb|text=אִסְפִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=10|verse=17}}, and with the same phonetic combination {{GHGheb|text=חֶשְׂפִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=2}}; see analogous cases in {{GHGpar|93|m}}); less frequently we find an ''ŏ'' instead of the ''ĭ'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מָלְכִי|translate=rule}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=מָשְׁכוּ|translate=draw}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=32|verse=20}}; {{GHGheb|text=חָרְבוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=12}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=חֳָרָ֑בִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=44|verse=27}}); on {{GHGheb|text=קָֽסֳמִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=8}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}, {{GHGheb|text=צֳעָ֫קִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer.|chapter=22|verse=20}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=13|verse=7}}), see {{GHGpar|10|h}}. This ''ŏ'' arises (see above, a) from a singular ground-form ''qŭṭŭl'', not from a retraction of the original ''ŭ'' of the second syllable. We must abandon the view that the forms with ''ĭ'' in the first syllable (cf. also<section end=par46 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

149.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="100.7.116.115" /></noinclude><section begin="par46" />{{GHGheb|text=אִמְרִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=חִגְרִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִכְרִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=עִבְרִי}}) arise from a weakening of the characteristic vowel ''ŏ''. They, or at least some of them, must rather be regarded with Barth ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1889, p. 182) as analogous to the original ''ĭ''-imperfects. See further analogies in {{GHGpar|47|i|doublesign=1}} and 48 i; 61 b, 63 n.

{{GHGmargin-letter|46|e}}
The ''pausal'' form of the 2nd plur. masc. is {{GHGheb|text=גְּזֹֽרוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=3|verse=26}}; from {{GHGheb|text=שְׁמַע}}, {{GHGheb|text=שְׁמָ֫עוּ}}, &c.; similarly the 2nd sing. fem. in {{GHGterm|pause}} is {{GHGheb|text=עֲבֹ֫רִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=12}}; even without the {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=מְל֫וֹכִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=10.12}}, {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}; {{GHGheb|text=קְס֫וֹמִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=8}}, {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} (cf. with this also {{GHGheb|text=מְלוֹכָה}}, &c., {{GHGpar|48|i}}); from {{GHGheb|text=שְׂמַה}}, {{GHGheb|text=שְׂמָ֫חִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=2|verse=21}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|46|f}}
3. In the 2nd plur. fem. {{GHGheb|text=שְׁמַ֫עַן}} occurs once, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=23}} (for {{GHGheb|text=שְׁמַ֫עְנָה}}) with loss of the {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} and insertion of a helping vowel, unless it is simply to be pointed {{GHGheb|text=שְׁמַ֫עְןָ}}. Also instead of the abnormal {{GHGheb|text=קִרְאֶן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=20}} (for {{GHGheb|text=קְרֶ֫אנָה}}) we should perhaps read as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=1|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=קְרֶ֫אןָ}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=מְצֶ֫אןָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=1|verse=9|hidebook=1}} and {{GHGheb|text=לֵ֫כְןָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=1|verse=12|hidebook=1}}).

On the examples of a 2nd plur. fem. in {{GHGheb|text=־ָ֫}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=32|verse=11}}, see {{GHGpar|48|i}}.
<section end="par46" />
<section begin="par47" />{{GHGpar-heading|47|The Imperfect and its Inflexion}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|a}}
'''1.''' The persons of the Imperfect,<ref>On the use of the Semitic Perfect and Imperfect cf. 106 ff. and the literature cited in § 106. For our present purpose the following account will suffice :—The name {{GHGterm|Imperfect}} is here used in direct contrast to the Perfect, and is to be taken in a wider sense than in Latin and Greek grammar. The Hebrew (Semitic) ''Perf.'' denotes in general that which is ''concluded'', ''completed'', and ''past'', that which has happened and has come into effect; but at the same time, also that which is ''represented'' as accomplished, even though it be continued into present time or even be actually still future. The ''Imperf.'' denotes, on the other hand, the ''beginning'', the ''unfinished'', and the ''continuing'', that which is just happening, which is conceived as in process of coming to pass, and hence, also, that which is yet future; likewise also that which occurs repeatedly or in a continuous sequence in the past (Latin Imperf.). It follows from the above that the once common designation of the Imperf. as a ''Future'' emphasizes only ''one'' side of its meaning. In fact, the use of Indo-Germanic tense-names for the Semitic tenses, which was adopted by the Syrians under the influence of the Greek grammarians, and after their example by the Arabs, and finally by Jewish scholars, has involved many misconceptions. The Indo-Germanic scheme of three periods of time (past, present, and future) is entirely foreign to the Semitic tense-idea, which regards an occurrence only from the point of view of Completed or incomplete action.—In the formation of the two tenses the chief distinction is that in the Perfect the verbal stem precedes and the indication of the person is added afterwards for precision, while in the Imperf. the subject, from which the action proceeds or about which a condition is predicated, is expressed by a prefixed pronoun.</ref> in contradistinction to those of the Perfect, are formed by placing abbreviated forms of the personal pronoun (preformatives) ''before'' the stem, or rather before the abstract form of the stem ({{GHGheb|text=קְטֹל}}). As, however, the tone is retained on the characteristic vowel of the Stem-form, or even (as in the ''2nd sing. fem.'' and the ''3rd'' and ''2nd plur. masc.'') passes over to the afformatives, the preformatives of the Imperfect appear in a much more abbreviated form than the afformatives of the Perfect, only ''one'' consonant ({{GHGheb|text=י}}, {{GHGheb|text=תּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=א}}, {{GHGheb|text=נ‍}}) remaining in each form. But as this preformative combined with the<section end="par47" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

150.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par47 />stem-form was not always sufficient to express at the same time differences both of gender and number, the distinction had to be farther indicated, in several cases, by special ''afformatives''. Cf. the table, {{GHGpar|40|c}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|b}}
'''2.''' The derivation and meaning, both of the preformatives and the afformatives, can still, in most cases, be recognized.

In the ''first'' pers. {{GHGheb|text=אֶקְטֹל}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=נִקְטֹל}}, {{GHGheb|text=א}} is probably connected with {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי}}, and {{GHGheb|text=נ‍}} with {{GHGheb|text=נָ֫חְנוּ}}; here no indication of gender or number by a special ending was necessary. As regards the vocalization, the Arabic points to the ground-forms ''ʾăqṭŭl'' and ''năqṭŭl'': the ''ĭ'' of the 1st plur. is, therefore, as in the other preformatives, attenuated from ''a''. The {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} of the 1st sing. is probably to be explained by the preference of the {{GHGheb|text=א}} for this sound (cf. {{GHGpar|22|o}}, but also {{GHGpar|51|p}}); according to Qimḥi, it arises from an endeavour to avoid the similarity of sound between {{GHGheb|text=אִקְטֹל}} (which is the Babylonian punctuation) and {{GHGheb|text=יִקְטִֹל}}, which, according to this view, was likewise pronounced ''iqṭōl''.<ref>Cf. {{GHGpar|24|e}}. In favour of the above view of Qimḥi may be urged the phonetic orthography {{GHGheb|text=אִשׁ}} (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=18|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=19}} (unless, with Perles, {{GHGheb|text=אָשֻׁב}} is to be read), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=6|verse=10}}, for {{GHGheb|text=יֵשׁ}}, and {{GHGheb|text=אִישַׁי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=2|verse=13}} for {{GHGheb|text=יִשַׁי}} (as verse 12). Also {{GHGheb|text=הַֽאֶזְכֶּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=6|verse=11}} is probably for {{GHGheb|text=הַֽאִזְ׳}} = {{GHGheb|text=הֲיִזְ׳}}, {{GHGheb|text=אפקד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=12}} for {{GHGheb|text=אנחמך ;יִטְקֹד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=19}} for {{GHGheb|text=יְנַֽחֲמֵךְ}}; and conversely {{GHGheb|text=יששכר}} is for {{GHGheb|text=אשש׳}}={{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ שָׂכָר}}. Similarly, {{GHGheb|text=ישוי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=49}} is probably for {{GHGheb|text=אִשְׁיוֹ}} or {{GHGheb|text=אִשְׁיָה}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=23|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=ישׁב בשבת}} is, according to the LXX, an error for {{GHGheb|text=ישבשת}}={{GHGheb|text=אִשְׁבּ֫שֶׁת}}. In Assyrian also the simple ''i'' corresponds to the Hebrew {{GHGheb|text=י}} as the preformative of the Impf. Qal.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|c}}
The preformative {{GHGheb|text=ת}} of the ''second'' persons ({{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטֹל}}, ground-form ''tăqṭŭl'', &c.) is, without doubt, connected with the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} of {{GHGheb|text=אַתָּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַתֶּם}}. &c., and the ''afformative'' {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} of the 2nd fem. sing. {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטְלִי}} with the ''i'' of the original feminine form {{GHGheb|text=אַתִּי}} (see {{GHGpar|32|h}}). The ''afformative'' {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} of the 2nd masc. plur. {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטְלוּ}} (in its more complete form, {{GHGheb|text=וּן}}, see m) is the sign of the plural, as in the 3rd pers., and also in the Perfect ({{GHGpar|44|a}}). In the Imperfect, however, it is restricted in both persons to the masculine,<ref>This is also the proper gender of the plural syllable ''û'', ''ûn''. In Hebrew, indeed, it is used in the 3rd plur. {{GHGterm|Perfect}} for both genders, but in the kindred languages even there only for the masculine, e.g. in Syriac ''q<sup>e</sup>ṭálû, q<sup>e</sup>ṭálûn'', with the feminine form ''q<sup>e</sup>ṭálên'', in Western Aram. ''q<sup>e</sup>ṭálû'', fem. ''q<sup>e</sup>ṭálā''; in Arab. ''qătălû'', fem. ''qătálnă'', Eth. ''qătălû'', ''qătălâ''.</ref> while the afformative {{GHGheb|text=נָה}} (also {{GHGheb|text=ןָ}}) of the 3rd and 2nd plur. fem. is probably connected with {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫נָּה|translate=eae}} and {{GHGheb|text=אַתֵּ֫נָה|translate=vos}} (fem.).

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|d}}
The preformatives of the ''third'' persons ({{GHGheb|text=י}} in the masc. {{GHGheb|text=יִקְטֹל}}, ground-form ''yăqṭŭl'', plur. {{GHGheb|text=יִקְטְלוּ}}, ground-form ''yăqṭŭlû''; {{GHGheb|text=ת}} in the fem. {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטֹל}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=תִָּקְטֹ֫לְנָה}}) have not yet met with any satisfactory explanation. With {{GHGheb|text=ת}} might most obviously be compared the original feminine<section end=par47 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

151.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="41.186.68.181" /></noinclude><section begin="par47" />ending {{GHGheb|text=־ַת}} of nouns, and of the 3rd fem. sing. perfect. For the afformatives {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} {{GHGheb|text=(וּן)}} and {{GHGheb|text=נָה}}, see {{GHGpar|47|c|nonumber=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|e}}
'''3.''' The characteristic vowel of the second syllable becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} before tone-bearing afformatives which begin with a vowel, but is retained (as being in the tone-syllable) before the toneless afformative {{GHGheb|text=נָה}}. Thus: {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטְלִ֫י}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִקְטְל֫וּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטְל֫וּ}} (but in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטֹ֫לִי}} &c.), {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטֹ֫לְנָה}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|f}}
Rem. 1. The ''ō'' of the second syllable (as in the inf. constr. and imperat.), being lengthened from an original ''ŭ'' in the tone-syllable, is only tone-long ({{GHGpar|9|r}}). Hence it follows that: (''a'') it is incorrectly, although somewhat frequently, written {{GHGterm|plene}}; (''b'') before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} the short vowel appears as {{GHGterm|Qameṣ ḥaṭuph}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּכְתָּב־שָּׁם|translate=and he wrote there}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=8|verse=32}} (but cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=37}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=18|verse=20}}); (''c'') it becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} before the tone-bearing afformatives {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} and {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} (see above, e; but Jerome still heard e.g. ''iezbuleni'' for {{GHGheb|text=יִזְבְּלֵ֫נִי}}; cf. {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZAW.|Zeitschrift für die alttestamentliche Wissenschaft, ed. by B. Stade, Giessen, 1881 ff., and since 1907 by K. Marti.}}}} iv. 83).

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|g}}
Quite anomalous are the three examples which, instead of a shortening to {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, exhibit a long ''û'': {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁפּוּטוּ הֵֽם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=18|verse=26}}, immediately before the principal pause, but according to Qimḥi (ed. ''Rittenb''. p.18<sup>b</sup>), ed. Mant., Ginsb., Kittel against the other editions, with the tone on the ultima; likewise {{GHGheb|text=לֹֽא־תַֽעֲבוּרִ֖י מִוֶּה֑}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=תִּשְׁמוּרֵֽם}} (in principal pause) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=14|verse=3}}. In the first two cases perhaps {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁפּ֫וֹטוּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=תַּעֲב֫וֹרִי}} (for {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁפֹּ֫טוּ}}, &c.) are intended, in virtue of a retrogressive effect of the pause; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=14|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=תִּשְׁמְרוּם}} is to be read, with August Müller.

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|h}}
2. The ''ō'' of the second syllable is to be found almost exclusively with transitive verbs middle ''a'', like {{GHGheb|text=קָטַל}}. Intransitives ''middle a'' and ''ē'' almost always take ''ă'' ({{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}})<ref>This ''ă'' is, however, by no means restricted to intransitive ''strong'' verbs; apart from verbs third guttural ({{GHGpar|65|b}}), it is to be found in {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}} and {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, and in many verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״א}} and {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}} (§§ 69–71).</ref> in the impf., e.g. {{GHGheb|text=רָבַץ}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִרְבַּץ|translate=to couch}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁכַב}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁכַּב|translate=to lie down}} ({{GHGheb|text=לָמַר}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִלְמַד|translate=to learn}} is also originally intransitive = ''to accustom oneself''); {{GHGheb|text=גָּדֵל}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִגְדַּל|translate=to become great}} (but cf. {{GHGheb|text=שָׁכַן}} and {{GHGheb|text=שָׁכֵן}} imperf. {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁכֹּן|translate=to dwell}} and ''to inhabit'', {{GHGheb|text=נָבֵל}} imperf. {{GHGheb|text=יִבֹּל|translate=to wither}}); also from verbs ''middle ō'', as {{GHGheb|text=קָטֹן|translate=to be small}}, the imperf. has the form {{GHGheb|text=יִקְטַן}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|i}}
Sometimes both forms occur together; those with ''ō'' having a transitive, and those with ''ă'' an intransitive meaning, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִקְצֹר|translate=he cuts off}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִקְצַר|translate=he is cut off}}, i.e. ''is short''; {{GHGheb|text=חָלַשׁ}} impf. ''ō'', ''to overcome'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=17|verse=13}}; impf. ''ă'', ''to be overcome'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=14|verse=10}}. More rarely both forms are used without any distinction, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִשֹּׁךְ}} and {{GHGheb|text=יִשַּׁךְ|translate=he bites}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֶחְפַּץ}} and {{GHGheb|text=יַחְפֹּץ|translate=he is inclined}} (but only the latter with a transitive meaning=''he bends'', in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=40|verse=17}}). On the ''a'' of the impf. of verbs middle and third guttural, cf. {{GHGpar|64|b}}; {{GHGpar|65|b}}. In some verbs first guttural ({{GHGpar|63|n}}), {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} ({{GHGpar|67|p}}), {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}} ({{GHGpar|69|b}}), and {{GHGheb|text=פ״א}} ({{GHGpar|68|c}}), and in {{GHGheb|text=יִתֵּן}} for ''yintēn'' from {{GHGheb|text=נָתַן|translate=to give}}, instead of ''ă'' or ''ō'' a movable {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} (originally ''ĭ'') is found in the second syllable. A trace of these ''i''-imperfects<ref>Cf. Barth, ‘''Das ĭ''-''Imperfekt im Nordsemitischen'',’ {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1889, p. 177 ff.</ref> in the ordinary strong verb is probably to be found in {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּטְמִ֫נוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=7|verse=8}}, since {{GHGheb|text=טמן}} otherwise only occurs in Qal. We call these three forms of the imperfect after their characteristic vowel impf. ''o'', impf. ''a'', impf. ''e''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|k}}
3. For the ''3rd sing. fem.'' {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטֹל}} (=''tiq-ṭōl''), Baer requires in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=תִּפְגשׁ}} (but read with ed. Mant., &c. {{GHGheb|text=תִּפְגּשׁ}}). For the ''2nd sing. fem.'' ({{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטְלִי}}) the form<section end="par47" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

152.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par47" />{{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטֹל}} is found in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=57|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=22|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=23|verse=32|hidebook=1}}, in every case after the regular form; but cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=14}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=10}}, where the 2nd fem. precedes and follows, probably {{GHGheb|text=תִּזְרָעִין וּב׳}} is to be read with Marti for {{GHGheb|text=תִּזְרָעֶ֫נּוּ}}.—For the ''3rd plur. fem.'' {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטֹ֫לְנַה}} we find in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=11}}, in pause {{GHGheb|text=תִּבְטָ֫חוּ}} (for {{GHGheb|text=תִּבְטַ֫חְנָה}}), and thrice (as if to distinguish it from the 2nd pers.) the form {{GHGheb|text=יִקְטֹ֫לְנָה}} with the preformative {{GHGheb|text=י}} (as always in Western Aram., Arab, Eth., and Assyr.), in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=38}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=8|verse=22}}. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטֹ֫לְנָה}} appears in some cases to be incorrectly used even for the fem. of the 3rd pers. or for the masc. of the 2nd pers. ''sing.'' as {{GHGheb|text=תִּשְׁלַ֫חְנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=26}} (where, however, perhaps {{GHGheb|text=תִּשְׁלָחֶ֫נָּה}} is to be read), and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ob|chapter=1|verse=13}}, for 2nd sing. masc., according to Olshausen a corruption of {{GHGheb|text=תִּשְׁלַח יָד}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=3|hidebook=1}} for {{GHGheb|text=תָּרֹ֫נָּה}} read {{GHGheb|text=תִּרְנֶה}} as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=39|verse=23}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=10}} read {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְרָאֵ֫נוּ}} with the Samaritan.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, as also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=17|verse=16}} (if we read {{GHGheb|text=טֽוֹבָתִי}} with LXX for the 2nd {{GHGheb|text=תקותי}}), it is equally possible to explain the form as a plural. This small number of examples hardly justifies our finding in the above-mentioned passages the remains of an emphatic form of the Impf., analogous to the Arab. ''Modus energicus I'', with the termination ''ănnă''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|l}}
For {{GHGheb|text=נָה}} we frequently find, especially in the Pentateuch and mostly after {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}}, simply {{GHGheb|text=ןָ|pron=nā}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=33.36}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=18.19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=25|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=3|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=55|hidebook=1}}; in Arab. always ''nă''. According to Elias Levita {{GHGheb|text=תִּלְבַּ֫שְׁןָ}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=18}}) is the only example of this kind in the strong verb. The form {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּגְּבְּהֶ֫ינָה}} (so also Qimḥi and ed. Mant.; but Baer, Ginsb. {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּגְּבְּהֶ֫נָה}}) for {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּגְבַּ֫הְנָה|translate=they were high}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=50}}, is irregular, with {{GHGheb|text=־ֶי}} inserted after the manner of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} and {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, {{GHGpar|67|d}}; {{GHGpar|72|i}}; according to Olshausen it is an error caused by the following form.

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|m}}
'''4.''' Instead of the plural forms in {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} there are, especially in the older books, over 300 forms<ref>[See details in F. Böttcher, ''Lehrb.'', § 930; and cf. Driver on {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=15}}.]</ref> with the fuller ending {{GHGheb|text=וּן}} (with ''Nûn paragogicum''), always bearing the tone; cf. {{GHGpar|29|m}} and {{GHGpar|44|l}}; on its retention before suffixes, see {{GHGpar|60|e}}; also defectively {{GHGheb|text=יְרִיבֻן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=22|verse=8|hidebook=1}}, &c. This usually expresses marked emphasis, and consequently occurs most commonly at the end of sentences (in the principal pause), in which case also the (pausal) vowel of the second syllable is generally retained. Thus there arise full-sounding forms such as {{GHGheb|text=יִלְקֹט֑וּן|translate=they collect}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=28}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִרְגָּז֑וּן|translate=they tremble}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=תִּשְׁמָע֑וּן|translate=ye shall hear}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=17}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=34|verse=13}}, with Zaqeph qaṭon, Athnaḥ, and Silluq; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=24|verse=15}}, with Segolta; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=13|verse=8}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=13|hidebook=1}} with Zaqeph qaṭon, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=12|hidebook=1}} with Athnaḥ and Silluq, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=5|hidebook=1}} after {{GHGterm|wāw consec}}. Without the pause, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=11|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=יִדְרְכוּן קֶ֫שֶׁת}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=4|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=28.29.30}} ff., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=32|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=4|verse=6}} ({{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁאָלוּן}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=9}} ({{GHGheb|text=יִקְצֹרוּן}} and {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁאֲבוּן}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=18}} after {{GHGterm|wāw consec}}.

Some of these examples may be partly due to euphonic reasons, e.g. certainly {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=17|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=16|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=32|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=9|verse=6}}, and often, to avoid a hiatus before {{GHGheb|text=א}} or {{GHGheb|text=ע}}. It was, however, the pause especially which exerted an influence on the restoration of this older and fuller termination (cf. {{GHGpar|159|c}}, note), as is manifest from {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=11}}: {{GHGheb|text=בַּל־יְֽחֱזָי֑וּן יֶֽחֱזוּ וְיֵב֫שׁוּ}} ''they see not; may they see and become''<section end="par47" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

153.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par47 />''ashamed''. All this applies also to the corresponding forms in the Imperfect of the derived conjugations.<ref>It is to be observed that the Chronicles often omit the ''Nûn'', where it is found in the parallel passage in the Books of Kings; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=38.43}} with {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=6|verse=29.33}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=12|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=11|verse=5}} with {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=11|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=23|verse=4|hidebook=1}}.</ref> In Aramaic and Arabic this earlier {{GHGheb|text=וּן}} (old Arabic ''ûnă'') is the regular termination; but in some dialects of vulgar Arabic it has also become ''û''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|n}}
With an affixed {{GHGheb|text=א}} we find (in the imperf. Niphʿal) {{GHGheb|text=יִנָּשׂוּא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=10|verse=5}}, evidently an error for {{GHGheb|text=יִנָּֽשְׂאוּ}}, caused by the preceding {{GHGheb|text=נָשׂוֹא}}.—In {{GHGheb|text=יְשֻׂשׂוּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=35|verse=1}}, since {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}} follows, the {{GHGheb|text=ם}} is no doubt only due to dittography.

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|o}}
5. Corresponding to the use of {{GHGheb|text=וּן}} for {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} there occurs in the 2nd sing. fem., although much less frequently, the fuller ending {{GHGheb|text=־ִין}} (as in Aram. and Arab.; old Arab. ''înă''), also always with the tone, for {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}}, generally again in the principal pause, and almost in all cases with retention of the vowel of the penultima; thus {{GHGheb|text=תִּדְבָּקִין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=8.21}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=3|verse=4.18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=14}} ({{GHGheb|text=תִּשְׁתַּכָּרִין}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=45|verse=10}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|p}}
6. On the reappearance in pause of the ''ō'' which had become {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} in the forms {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטְלִי}}, &c., see above, e; similarly, the imperfects with ''ă'' restore this vowel in pause and at the same time lengthen it (as a tone-vowel) to ''ā'', hence, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תִּגְדָּ֫לִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִגְדָּ֫לוּ}}. This influence of the pause extends even to the forms without afformatives, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּגְדַּל}}, in pause {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּגְדָּ֑ל}}. But the fuller forms in ''ûn'' and ''în'' have the tone always on the ultima, since the vowels ''û'' and ''î'' in a closed final syllable never allow of the retraction of the tone.

{{GHGmargin-letter|47|q}}
7. On the numerous instances of passive forms in the imperfect, mostly treated as Hophʿal, see {{GHGpar|53|u}}.<section end=par47 />

<section begin=par48 />{{GHGpar-heading|48|Shortening and Lengthening of the Imperfect and Imperative. The Jussive and Cohortative}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|48|a}}
'''1.''' Certain modifications which take place in the form of the imperfect, and express invariably, or nearly so, a distinct shade of meaning, serve to some extent as a compensation for the want of special forms for the ''Tempora relativa'' and for certain ''moods'' of the verb.

{{GHGmargin-letter|48|b}}
'''2.''' Along with the usual form of the imperfect, there exists also a lengthened form of it (the ''cohortative''), and a shortened form (the {{GHGterm|jussive}}).<ref>The perfect has only ''one'' form, since it cannot be used, like the imperfect, to express mood-relations (see {{GHGpar|106|p}}).</ref> The former occurs (with few exceptions) only in the 1st person, while the latter is mostly found in the 2nd and 3rd persons, and less frequently in the 1st person. The laws of the tone, however, and of the formation of syllables in Hebrew, not infrequently precluded the indication of the jussive by an actual shortening of the form; consequently it often—and, in the imperfect forms with afformatives, always—coincides with the ordinary imperfect (''indicative'') form.

In classical Arabic the difference is almost always evident. That language distinguishes, besides the indicative ''yăqtŭlŭ'', (''a'') a subjunctive, ''yăqtŭlă''; (''b'') a<section end=par48 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

154.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par48 />jussive, ''yăqtŭl''; (''c'') a double ‘energetic’ mood of the impf., ''yăqtŭlănnă'' and ''yăqtŭlăn'', in pause ''yăqtŭlā'', the last form thus corresponding to the Hebrew cohortative.

{{GHGmargin-letter|48|c}}
'''3.''' The characteristic of the cohortative form is an ''ā'' ({{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}) affixed to the 1st pers. sing. or plur., e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֶקְטְלָה}} from {{GHGheb|text=אֶקְטֹל}}.<ref>Probably this ''ā'' goes back to the syllable ''an'', which in Arabic (see above, Rem. to b) is used for the formation of the ‘energetic’ mood, and in Hebrew (see the footnote to {{GHGpar|58|i}}) often stands before suffixes.</ref> It occurs in almost all conjugations and classes of the strong and weak verb (except of course in the passives), and this final {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} has the tone wherever the afformatives {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} would have it. As before these endings, so also before the {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} cohortative, the movable vowel of the last syllable of the verbal form becomes ''Š<sup>e</sup>ewâ'', e.g. in Qal {{GHGheb|text=אֶשְׁמְרָ֫ה|translate=I will observe}}, in Piʿel {{GHGheb|text=נְנַתְּקָ֫ה|translate=let us break asunder}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=3}}; on {{GHGheb|text=אֶשְׁקֳטָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=18|verse=4}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} (cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=8|verse=25}}, &c.), see {{GHGpar|10|h}}; with the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} of these passages, compare the analogous cases {{GHGheb|text=ישׁפוטו}}, &c., {{GHGpar|47|g}}.—On the other hand, an unchangeable vowel in the final syllable is retained as tone-vowel before the {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}, as (e.g.) in Hiph. {{GHGheb|text=אַזְכִּ֫ירָה|translate=I will praise}}. In pause (as before ''û'' and ''î''), the vowel which became {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} is restored as tone-vowel; thus for the cohortative {{GHGheb|text=אֶשְׁמְרָ֫ה}} the pausal form is {{GHGheb|text=אֶשְׁמֹ֑רָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=59|verse=10}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=26}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|48|d}}
The change of {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} into the obtuse {{GHGheb|text=־ֶה}} seems to occur in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=15}}, unless, with Nestle, we are to assume a conflate reading, {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֶקְרִַא}} and {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֶקְרֶה}}; and with the 3rd pers. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=20|verse=4}}, in a syllable sharpened by a following ''Dageš forte conjunct.''; cf. similar cases of the change of {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} into the obtuse {{GHGheb|text=־ֶה}} in ''l'' and in {{GHGpar|73|d|doublesign=1}}, {{GHGpar|80|i|nosign=1}}, {{GHGpar|90|i|nosign=1}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=20|verse=4}}, however, {{GHGheb|text=יְדַשְּׁנֶ֫הָ}}—with suffix—is probably intended. An {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} cohort. is also found with the 3rd pers. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=19}} (twice); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=23|verse=20}}, and again in verse 16 according to the {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}, but in both these cases without any effect on the meaning. Probably another instance occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=11|verse=17}}, although there {{GHGheb|text=תָּעֻ֫פָה}} might also, with Qimḥi, be regarded as 2nd masc. For the doubly irregular form {{GHGheb|text=תָּב֫וֹאתָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=16}} (explained by Olshausen and König as a scribal error, due to a confusion with {{GHGheb|text=תבואת}} in verse 14), read {{GHGheb|text=תָּב֫וֹאנָה}}. For {{GHGheb|text=תְּבוֹאָֽתְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=21}} the noun {{GHGheb|text=תְּבוּאָֽתְךָ|translate=thine increase}}, might be meant, but the Masora has evidently intended an imperfect with the ending ''ath'', instead of {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}, before the suffix, on the analogy of the 3rd sing. fem. perfect, see {{GHGpar|59|a}}; on {{GHGheb|text=ותבאתי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=34}}, see {{GHGpar|76|h}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|48|e}}
The ''cohortative'' expresses the direction of the will to an action and thus denotes especially self-encouragement (in the 1st plur. an exhortation to others at the same time), a resolution or a wish, as an ''optative'', &c., see § 108.

{{GHGmargin-letter|48|f}}
'''4.''' The general characteristic of the {{GHGterm|jussive}} form of the imperfect is rapidity of pronunciation, combined with a tendency to retract<section end=par48 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

155.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par48 />the tone from the final syllable, in order by that means to express the urgency of the command in the very first syllable. This tendency has, in certain forms, even caused a material shortening of the termination of the word, so that the expression of the command appears to be concentrated on a single syllable. In other cases, however, the jussive is simply marked by a shortening of the vowel of the second syllable, without its losing the tone, and very frequently (see above, b) the nature of the form does not admit of any alteration. It is not impossible, however, that even in such cases the jussive in the living language was distinguished from the indicative by a change in the place of the tone.

{{GHGmargin-letter|48|g}}
In the strong verb the jussive differs in ''form'' from the indicative only in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} (juss. {{GHGheb|text=יַקְטֵל}}, ind. {{GHGheb|text=יַקְטִיל}}), and similarly in the weak verb, wherever the imperfect indicative has ''î'' in the second syllable, e.g. from {{GHGheb|text=יָשַׁב}} impf. ''Hiph.'' {{GHGheb|text=יוֹשִׁיב}}, juss. {{GHGheb|text=יוֹשֵׁב}}; from {{GHGheb|text=מוּת}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָמִית}} and {{GHGheb|text=יָמֵת}}; also in {{GHGterm|Qal}} of the verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=ע״י}}, as {{GHGheb|text=יָמֹת}}, ind. {{GHGheb|text=יָמוּת}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָגֵל}}, ind. {{GHGheb|text=יָגִיל}}; in all conjugations of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, so that the rejection (''apocope'') of the ending {{GHGheb|text=־ֶה}} in {{GHGterm|Qal}} and ''Hiph.'' gives rise to monosyllabic forms, with or without a helping vowel under the second radical, e.g. {{GHGterm|Qal}} ind. {{GHGheb|text=יִגְלֶה}}, juss. {{GHGheb|text=יִ֫גֶל}}; ''Hiph.'' ind. {{GHGheb|text=יַגְלֶה}}, juss. {{GHGheb|text=יֶ֫גֶל}}; and in the {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=יְצַו}} from the indic. {{GHGheb|text=יְצַוֶּה}} (called apocopated imperfects). But almost all<ref>Only in 1st plur. do we find a few shortened forms, as {{GHGheb|text=נַשְׁאֵר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=36}}, parallel with cohortatives; and {{GHGheb|text=נֵ֫רֶא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=23}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}</ref> the plural forms of the jussive coincide with those of the indicative, except that the jussive excludes the fuller ending {{GHGheb|text=וּן}}. Neither do the forms of the 2nd sing. fem., as {{GHGheb|text=תַּקְטִ֫ילִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=תָּמ֫וּתִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּגְלִי}}, &c., admit of any change in the jussive, nor any forms, whether singular or plural, to which suffixes are attached, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תְּמִיתֵ֫נִי}} as ind. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=38|verse=15}}, as jussive {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=41|verse=8}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|48|h}}
The meaning of the jussive is similar to that of the cohortative, except that in the jussive the command or wish is limited almost exclusively to the and or 3rd pers. On special uses of the jussive, e.g. in hypothetical sentences (even in the 1st pers.), see {{GHGpar|109|h}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|48|i}}
'''5.''' The imperative, in accordance with its other points of connexion with the imperfect in form and meaning, admits of a similar lengthening (by {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}, Arab. ''imper. energicus'', with the ending ''-ănnă'' or ''-ăn'', in pause ''-ā'') and shortening. Thus in {{GHGterm|Qal}} of the strong verb, the lengthened form of {{GHGheb|text=שְׁמֹר|translate=guard}} is {{GHGheb|text=שָׁמְרָה}}<ref>On the reading {{GHGheb|text=שָֽׁמְרָה}} (i.e. ''šām<sup>e</sup>ra'', according to the Jewish grammarians), required by the Masora in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=86|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=167|hidebook=1}} (cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=38|verse=14}}, and {{GHGheb|text=שָֽׁמְרֵנִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=16|verse=1}}), see {{GHGpar|9|v}}; on {{GHGheb|text=מלוכה}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=8}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, see {{GHGpar|46|e}}.</ref> (''šŏm<sup>e</sup>râ'', cf. {{GHGheb|text=קִטְלִי}} ''qîṭ<sup>e</sup>lî'', {{GHGpar|46|d}}); {{GHGheb|text=עֲזֹב}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָזְבָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=שְׁכַב}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁכְבָה|translate=lie down}}; {{GHGheb|text=שְׁמַע}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁמְעָה|translate=hear}}, in lesser pause {{GHGheb|text=שְׁמָ֫עָה}}<section end=par48 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

156.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par48 />{{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=9|verse=19}}; in Niphʿal {{GHGheb|text=הִשָּֽׁבְעָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=23}}. Cf., however, also {{GHGheb|text=מִכְרָה|translate=sell}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=25|verse=31}}, notwithstanding the impf. {{GHGheb|text=יִמְכֹּר}}; {{GHGheb|text=עֶרְכָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=33|verse=5}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=עִרְכוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=46|verse=3}}), but impf. {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעֲרֹךְ}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֶֽסְפָה|translate=collect}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=16}} (for {{GHGheb|text=אִס׳}} cf. {{GHGpar|63|l}} and the plural {{GHGheb|text=אִסְפוּ}}), but 2nd masc. {{GHGheb|text=אֱסֹף}}; {{GHGheb|text=נִצְּרָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=141|verse=3}}. Barth (see above, {{GHGpar|47|i}} note) finds in these forms a trace of old imperfects in ''i'', cf. {{GHGpar|63|n}}. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=קָרְבָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=69|verse=19}} (also Imperat. {{GHGheb|text=קְרַב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=9|verse=7}}, &c.), but impf. {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרַב}}. Without {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, we have the form {{GHGheb|text=לְךָ|translate=go}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=25|verse=17}}. The form {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹל}} in pause becomes {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹ֫לָה}}, the form {{GHGheb|text=קְטַל}} becomes {{GHGheb|text=קְטָ֫לָה}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יְרָ֫שָׁה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=23}}. But also without the pause we find {{GHGheb|text=מְ֫לוֹכָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=8}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} and {{GHGheb|text=צְרוֹפָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=26|verse=2}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, on which see {{GHGpar|46|e}}. On the other hand {{GHGheb|text=רְגָ֫זָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=פְּשֹׁ֫טָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֹ֫רָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֲג֫וֹרָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=32|verse=11}} are to be explained as aramaizing forms of the and plur. fem.; also for {{GHGheb|text=חִרְדוּ}} v. 11 read {{GHGheb|text=חֲרָ֫דָה}}, and for {{GHGheb|text=סֹֽפְדִים}} v. 12 read {{GHGheb|text=סְפֹ֫דָה}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|48|k}}
The shortened imperative is found only in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, e.g. in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=גַּל}} from {{GHGheb|text=גַּלֵּה}}. The shade of meaning conveyed by the imperatives with {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} is not always so perceptible as in the cohortative forms of the imperfect, but the longer form is frequently emphatic, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קוּם|translate=rise up}}, {{GHGheb|text=ק֫וּמָה|translate=up!}} {{GHGheb|text=תֵּן|translate=give}}, {{GHGheb|text=תְּנָה|translate=give up!}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|48|l}}
Rem. The form {{GHGheb|text=דְּעֶה}} for {{GHGheb|text=דְּעָה}}, best attested in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=14}} (where it is taken by the Masora as imperat., not as infin., {{GHGheb|text=דַּעָה}}) is evidently due to the influence of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} which follows it in close connexion (so Strack, on the analogy of {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=2}}); for other examples of this change of ''a'' to S<sup>e</sup>ghol, see above, under d, {{GHGpar|73|d}}, and {{GHGpar|80|i}}. On the other hand, it is doubtful whether {{GHGheb|text=רַבֶּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=29}} (from {{GHGheb|text=רָבָה}}) is intended for {{GHGheb|text=רַבָּה}}, and not rather for the common form of the imperative {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=רַבֵּה}}. In favour of the former explanation it may be urged that the imperative {{GHGheb|text=צֵ֫אָה}} (from {{GHGheb|text=יָצָא}}) follows immediately after; in favour of the latter, that the ending {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}, with imperatives of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, is not found elsewhere, and also that here no guttural follows (as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=14}}).<section end=par48 />

<section begin=par49 />{{GHGpar-heading|49|The Perfect and Imperfect with Wāw Consecutive}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|49|a}}
'''1.''' The use of the two tense-forms, as is shown more fully in the Syntax (§§ 106, 107, cf. above, § 47, note on ''a''), is by no means restricted to the expression of the past or future. One of the most striking peculiarities in the Hebrew ''consecution'' of tenses<ref>The other Semitic languages do not exhibit this peculiarity, excepting the Phoenician, the most closely related to Hebrew, and of course the Moabitish dialect of the ''Mêšaʿ'' inscription, which is practically identical with Old Hebrew. It also appears in the inscription of {{GHGheb|text=זכר}} of Hamāth (cf. Nöldeke, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZA.|Zeitschrift für Assyriologie und verwandte Gebiete, ed. by C. Bezold. Lpz. 18S6 ff.}}}} 1908, p. 379) where we find {{GHGheb|text=ואשּׂא ידי}} and ''I lifted up my hand'', {{GHGheb|text=ויענני|translate=and he answered me}}, after a perfect of narration.</ref> is the phenomenon that, in representing a series of past events, only the first<section end=par49 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

157.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par49 />verb stands in the perfect, and the narration is continued in the imperfect. Conversely, the representation of a series of future events begins with the imperfect, and is continued in the perfect. Thus in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=20|verse=1}}, ''In those days was Hezekiah sick unto death'' (perf.), ''and Isaiah''... ''came'' (imperf.) to ''him, and said'' (imperf.) ''to him'', &c. On the other hand, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=17}}, ''the Lord shall bring'' (imperf.) ''upon thee... days, &c.'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, ''and it shall come to pass'' (perf. {{GHGheb|text=וְהָיָה}}) ''in that day...''

{{GHGmargin-letter|49|b}}
This progress in the sequence of time, is regularly indicated by a pregnant ''and'' (called {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}}<ref>This name best expresses the prevailing syntactical relation, for by {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} an action is always represented as the direct, or at least temporal ''consequence'' of a preceding action. Moreover, it is clear from the above examples, that the {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} can only be thus used in immediate conjunction with the verb. As soon as {{GHGterm|wāw}}, owing to an insertion (e.g. a negative), is separated from the verb, the imperfect follows instead of the perfect {{GHGterm|consecutive}}, the perfect instead of the imperfect {{GHGterm|consecutive}}. The fact that whole Books (Lev., Num., Josh., Jud., Sam., 2 Kings, Ezek., Ruth, Esth., Neh., 2 Chron.) begin with the imperfect {{GHGterm|consecutive}}, and others (Exod., 1 Kings, Ezra) with {{GHGterm|wāw copulative}}, is taken as a sign of their close connexion with the historical Books now or originally preceding them. Cf., on the other hand, the independent beginning of Job and Daniel. It is a merely superficial description to call the wāw {{GHGterm|consecutive}} by the old-fashioned name {{GHGterm|wāw conversive}}, on the ground that it always converts the meaning of the respective tenses into its opposite, i.e. according to the old view, the future into the preterite, and vice versa.</ref>), which in itself is really only a variety of the ordinary {{GHGterm|wāw copulative}}, but which sometimes (in the imperf.) appears with a different vocalization. Further, the tenses connected by {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} sometimes undergo a change in the tone and consequently are liable also to other variations.

{{GHGmargin-letter|49|c}}
'''2.''' The {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} is (''a'') pronounced with {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} and a {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}} in the next letter, as {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּקְטֹל|translate=and he killed}}; before {{GHGheb|text=א}} of the 1''st pers. sing.'' (according to {{GHGpar|22|c}}) with {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}}, as {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֶקְטֹל|translate=and I killed}}. Exceptions are, {{GHGheb|text=וַֽאֲכַסֵּךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=10}} according to the ''Dikduke ha-ṭ<sup>e</sup>amim'', § 71; also {{GHGheb|text=וַֽאֲמֹתְתֵ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=1|verse=10}} according to Qimḥi; but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֲגָרֵשׁ}} should be read according to Baer, and {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֲ׳}} in both places in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=6}}. {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}} is always omitted in the preformative {{GHGheb|text=יְ}}, in accordance with {{GHGpar|20|m}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|49|d}}
(''b'') When a shortening of the imperfect form is possible (cf. {{GHGpar|48|g}}), it takes effect, as a rule (but cf. {{GHGpar|51|n}}), after {{GHGterm|wāw consec.}}, e.g. in Hiphil {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּקְטֵל}} ({{GHGpar|53|n}}). The tendency to retract the tone from the final syllable is even stronger after {{GHGterm|wāw consec.}} than in the jussive. The throwing back of the tone on to the penultima (conditional upon its being an open syllable with a long vowel, {{GHGpar|29|a}}), further involves the greatest possible shortening of the vowel of the ultima, since the vowel then comes to stand in a toneless closed syllable, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יָקוּם}}, juss.<section end=par49 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

158.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par49" />{{GHGheb|text=יָקֹ֫ם}}, with {{GHGterm|wāw consec.}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫קָם|translate=and he arose}} ({{GHGpar|67|n}} and x, {{GHGpar|68|d}}, {{GHGpar|69|p}}, § 71, {{GHGpar|72|t}} and aa, {{GHGpar|73|e}}).<ref>The plural forms in {{GHGheb|text=וּן}} also occur less frequently after {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}}; cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=וַיְרִיבוּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=6|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=44|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=5|verse=20|hidebook=1}}. The 2nd fem. sing. in {{GHGheb|text=־ִין}} never occurs after {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|49|e}}
In the ''first'' pers. sing. alone the retraction of the tone and even the reducing of the long vowel in the final syllable (''û'' to ''ō'', ''î'' to ''ē'', and then to ''ŏ'' and ''ĕ'') are not usual,<ref>In the 1st plur. {{GHGheb|text=וַנַּֽעֲמִיד}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=4|verse=3}} is the only instance in which the vowel remains unreduced (cf. {{GHGheb|text=ונשׁוב}}, i.e. {{GHGheb|text=וַנָּשׁוּב}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=4|verse=9|hidebook=1}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}; {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} {{GHGheb|text=וַנָּ֫שָׁב}}). On the treatment of the tone in the imperfect, imperative, and infinitive {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, see {{GHGpar|51|n}}.</ref> at least according to the Masoretic punctuation, and the apocope in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} occurs more rarely; e.g. always {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאָקוּם}} (or {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאָקֻ֫ם}}, a merely orthographic difference) ''and I arose''; ''Hiph.'' {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאָקִים}} (but generally written {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאָקִם}}, implying the pronunciation ''wāʾ{{GHGtranslit|a-macr-acut}}qem'', as {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאָקֻם}} implies ''wāʾāqŏm''); {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֶרְאֶה|translate=and I saw}}, more frequently than {{GHGheb|text=וָאֵ֫רֶא}}, {{GHGpar|75|t}}. On the other hand, the form with final {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} is often used in the 1st pers. both sing. and plur., especially in the later books, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֶשְׁלְחָה|translate=and I sent}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=21|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=8|verse=19}} ({{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֶתְּנָה}}, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=28}}, and often, probably a sort of compensation for the lost {{GHGheb|text=נ‍}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=12|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=22|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=3|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=7|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=90|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=55|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=15}} ff., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=7|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=8|verse=25|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=9|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=2|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=5|verse=7.8.13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=6|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=13|verse=7–11.21 f.|hidebook=1}}, &c.—Sometimes, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=3|verse=6}}, with a certain emphasis of expression, and probably often, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=10|verse=12}}, {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאוֹשִׁ֫יעָה}} before {{GHGheb|text=א}}, for euphonic reasons. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאָעִ֫ידָה}} may have been originally intended; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֲח׳}} and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=26}} {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֲי׳}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=3|verse=3}} read {{GHGheb|text=וָאֹֽכְלֶהָ}} or {{GHGheb|text=וָאֹֽכְלָהּ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|49|f}}
This {{GHGheb|text=ו·}} is in meaning a strengthened {{GHGterm|wāw copulative}}, and resembles in pronunciation the form which is retained in Arabic as the ordinary copula (''wă'').<ref>In usage the Hebrew {{GHGterm|wāw}} does duty for the Arabic ''fă'' ({{GHGterm|wāw apodosis}}, see {{GHGpar|143|d}}) as well as ''wă''.</ref> The close connexion of this ''wă'' with the following consonant, caused the latter in Hebrew to take {{GHGterm|Dageš}}, especially as ''ă'' could not have been retained in an open syllable. Cf. {{GHGheb|text=בַּמָּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=כַּמָּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָ֫מָּה}} (for {{GHGheb|text=לַמָּה}}), where the prepositions {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, and the particle {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}}, are closely connected with {{GHGheb|text=מָה}} in the same way ({{GHGpar|102|k}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|49|g}}
The retraction of the tone also occurs in such combinations, as in {{GHGheb|text=לָ֫מָּה}} (for {{GHGheb|text=לַמָּ֫ה}} {{GHGpar|102|l}}).—The identity of many {{GHGterm|consecutive}} forms with jussives of the same conjugation must not mislead us into supposing an intimate relation between the moods. In the consecutive forms the shortening of the vowel (and the retraction of the tone) seems rather to be occasioned solely by the strengthening of the preformative syllable, while in the jussives the shortening (and retraction) belongs to the character of the form.

{{GHGmargin-letter|49|h}}
'''3.''' The counterpart of {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} is {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} of the {{GHGterm|perfect}}, by means of which perfects are placed as<section end="par49" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

159.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par49 />the sequels in the future to preceding actions or events regarded as incomplete at the time of speaking, and therefore in the imperfect, imperative, or even participle. This {{GHGterm|wāw}} is in form an ordinary {{GHGterm|wāw copulative}}, and therefore shares its various vocalization ({{GHGheb|text=וְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=וּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=וָ}}, as {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=7|verse=4}}, and {{GHGheb|text=וַ}}); e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וְהָיָה}}, after an imperfect, &c., ''and so it happens = and it will happen''. It has, however, the effect, in certain verbal forms, of shifting the tone from the penultima, generally on to the ultima, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הָלַ֫כְתִּי|translate=I went}}, consecutive form {{GHGheb|text=וְהָֽלַכְתִּ֫י|translate=and I will go}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=1|verse=3}}, where it is co-ordinated with another {{GHGterm|perfect consecutive}}, which again is the consecutive to an {{GHGterm|imperative}}. See further on this usage in § 112.

{{GHGmargin-letter|49|i}}
As innumerable examples show, the {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} of the first syllable is retained in the strong perf. consec. Qal, as formerly before the tone, so now in the secondary tone, and therefore necessarily takes {{GHGterm|Metheg}}. On the other hand, the ''ō'' of the second syllable in verbs ''middle ō'' upon losing the tone necessarily becomes ''ŏ'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וְיָֽכָלְתָּ֫}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=18|verse=23}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|49|k}}
The shifting forward of the tone after the {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} of the {{GHGterm|perfect}} is, however, not consistently carried out. It is omitred—(''a'') always in the 1st ''pers. pl.'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וְיָשַ֫בְנוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=16}}; (''b'') regularly in Hiphʿil before the afformatives {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} and {{GHGheb|text=וּ}}, see {{GHGpar|53|r}}; and (''c'') in many cases in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}} and {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, almost always in the 1st sing. of {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=29|verse=14}}), and in {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} if the vowel of the 2nd syllable is ''î'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=17|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=4.6.7.10|hidebook=1}} ff., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=26}}, &c., except In {{GHGterm|Qal}} (only {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=24|verse=5}}, before {{GHGheb|text=א}}) and the 2nd sing. masc. of Hiphʿil-forms before {{GHGheb|text=א}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=20|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=20|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=13|verse=17}}; similarly in Piʿēl before {{GHGheb|text=א}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=25|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=27|verse=4}}. On the other hand the tone is generally moved forward if the second syllable has ''ê'' (in {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=10}} &c., in {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=40|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=33|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=32|verse=7}}); but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=וְיָרֵ֫אתָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=19|verse=14.32}} and frequently, always before the counter-tone, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=4|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=19|verse=14}}.<ref>The irregularity in the tone of these perfects manifestly results from following conflicting theories, not that of Ben Asher alone.</ref> With ''ā'' in the penultima the form is {{GHGheb|text=וְנָשָׂ֫אתָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=4}}, and probably also {{GHGheb|text=וְקָרָ֫אתָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=10|verse=2}} with little Tēlîšā, a postpositive accent.

{{GHGmargin-letter|49|l}}
But before a following {{GHGheb|text=א}} the ultima mostly bears the tone on phonetic grounds, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וּבָאתָ֫ אֶל־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=6|verse=10}} (by the side of {{GHGheb|text=וּבָ֫אתָ}}), &c. (cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=וְקָרָ֫אתָ}}, before {{GHGheb|text=א}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=7|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=36|verse=29}}); {{GHGheb|text=וְהִכִּיתָ֫ אֶת־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=16}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=25|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=24|verse=5}} (but also {{GHGheb|text=וְצִוִּ֫יתִי אֶת־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=25|verse=21}}). Likewise, before {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=8|verse=9}}, and {{GHGheb|text=ע}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=25}} (cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=וְקָרָ֫אתִי עָלָיו}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=38|verse=21}}); on verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, see {{GHGpar|67|k}} and § ee.

{{GHGmargin-letter|49|m}}
(''d'') The tone always keeps its place when such a perfect stands in {{GHGterm|pause}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וְשָׂבָֽעְתָּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=6|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=11|verse=15|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=וְאָמָ֑רְתָּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=8}}; sometimes even in the lesser pause, as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=3|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=29|verse=8}} (where see Driver), with {{GHGterm|Zaqeph qaṭon}}; and frequently also immediately ''before'' a tone-syllable (according to {{GHGpar|29|e}}), as in {{GHGheb|text=וְיָשַׁ֫בְתָּה בָּ֑הּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=17|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=14|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=17|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=1|verse=4.7.10.12}}—but also {{GHGheb|text=וְחָֽשַׁקְתָּ֫ בָ֔הּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=21|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=23|verse=14|hidebook=1}}. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=24|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=46}}.<section end=par49 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

160.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par50 />{{GHGpar-heading|50|The Participle}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|50|a}}
'''1.''' Qal has both an active participle, called {{GHGterm|Pôʿēl}} from its form ({{GHGheb|text=פֹּעֵל}}), and a passive, ''Pāʿûl'' ({{GHGheb|text=פָּעוּל}}).<ref>The constr. st. {{GHGheb|text=נְאֻם}} in the formula {{GHGheb|text=נאם יהוה}}, ''the word'' (properly the ''whispering'') ''of the Lord'', &c., is always written defectively.</ref>

''Pāʿûl'' is generally regarded as a survival of a passive of Qal, which still exists throughout in Arabic, but has been lost in Hebrew (see, however, {{GHGpar|52|e}}), just as in Aramaic the passives of {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} are lost, except in the participles. But instances of the form ''quṭṭāl'' are better regarded as remnants of the passive participle Qal (see {{GHGpar|52|s}}), so that {{GHGheb|text=פָּעוּל}} must be considered as an original verbal noun; cf. Barth, {{GHGcite|title=Nominalbildung}}, p. 173 ff.

{{GHGmargin-letter|50|b}}
'''2.''' In the intransitive verbs ''mid. e'' and ''mid. o'', the form of the participle active of Qal coincides in form with the 3rd sing. of the perfect, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יָשֵׁן|translate=sleeping}}, from {{GHGheb|text=יָשֵׁן}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָגוֹר}} (only orthographically different from the perf. {{GHGheb|text=יָגֹר}}) ''fearing''; cf. the formation of the participle in {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, {{GHGpar|51|a}}. On the other hand, the participle of verbs ''mid. a'' takes the form {{GHGheb|text=קֹטֵל}} (so even from the ''transitive'' {{GHGheb|text=שָׂנֵא|translate=to hate}}, part. {{GHGheb|text=שׂנֵא}}). The ''ô'' of these forms has arisen through an obscuring of the ''â'', and is therefore unchangeable, cf. {{GHGpar|9|q}}. The form {{GHGheb|text=קָטָל}} (with a changeable {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} in both syllables), which would correspond to the forms {{GHGheb|text=יָשֵׂן}} and {{GHGheb|text=יָגֹר}}, is only in use as a noun, cf. {{GHGpar|84|f|a}}. The formation of the participle in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, and ''Hîthpaʿēl'' follows a different method.

{{GHGmargin-letter|50|c}}
'''3.''' Participles form their feminine ({{GHGheb|text=קֹֽטְלָה}} or {{GHGheb|text=קֹטֶ֫לֶת}}) and their plural like other nouns ({{GHGpar|80|e}}, {{GHGpar|84|r|a}}, {{GHGpar|84|s|a|nonumber=1}}, {{GHGpar|94}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|50|d}}
Rem. 1. From the above it follows, that the ''ā'' of the form {{GHGheb|text=יָשֵׁן}} is lengthened from ''ă'', and consequently changeable (e.g. {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=יְשֵׁנָה}}); and that the ''ô'' of {{GHGheb|text=קֹטֵל}} on the other hand is obscured from an unchangeable ''â''.<ref>Cf. Vollers, ‘''Das Qâtil-partizipium'',’ in {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZA.|Zeitschrift für Assyriologie und verwandte Gebiete, ed. by C. Bezold. Lpz. 18S6 ff.}}}} 1903, p. 312 ff.</ref> In Arabic the verbal adjective of the form ''qătĭl'' corresponds to the form ''qāṭēl'', and the part. ''qâtĭl'' to ''qôṭēl''. In both cases, therefore, the ''ē'' of the second syllable is lengthened from ''ĭ'', and is consequently changeable (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קֹטֵל}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=קֹֽטְלִים}}; {{GHGheb|text=כָּבֵד}}, constr. pl. {{GHGheb|text=כִּבְדֵי}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|50|e}}
{{GHGheb|text=תּוֹמִיךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=16|verse=5}}, instead of the form ''qôṭēl'', is an anomaly; it is possible, however, that {{GHGheb|text=תּוֹמֵיךְ}} (incorrectly written fully) is intended (cf. {{GHGheb|text=סֹבֵיב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=8|verse=21}}), or even the {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} of {{GHGheb|text=יָמַךְ}}. The form {{GHGheb|text=יֹסִף}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=38|verse=5|hidebook=1}} appears to stand for {{GHGheb|text=יֹסֵף}}, but most probably the Masora here (as certainly in {{GHGheb|text=יוֹסִיף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=1|verse=18}}) intends the 3rd sing. imperf. Hiph., for which the better form would be {{GHGheb|text=יוֹסֵף}}; {{GHGheb|text=אוֹבִיל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=27|verse=30}}, being a proper name and a foreign word, need not be considered.—{{GHGheb|text=אֹבַד}} (constr. state of {{GHGheb|text=אֹבֵד}}), with ''ă'' in the second syllable, occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=28}} (cf. moreover, {{GHGpar|65|d}}). On {{GHGheb|text=ה֫וֹלֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=7}} (for {{GHGheb|text=הוֹלֵם}}), see {{GHGpar|29|f}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|50|f}}
2. A form like the pass. ptcp. ''Pāʿŭl'', but not to be confused with it, is sometimes found from ''intransitive verbs'', to denote an inherent quality, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אָמוּן|translate=faithful}}; {{GHGheb|text=אָנוּשׁ|translate=desperate}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=15|verse=18}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=בָּטוּחַ|translate=trustful}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=112|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=עָצוּם|translate=strong}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁכוּר|translate=drunken}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=21}}; and even from transitive verbs, {{GHGheb|text=אָחוּז|translate=handling}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=3|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=זָכוּר|translate=mindful}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=103|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָדוּעָ|translate=knowing}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=53|verse=3}}; cf. {{GHGpar|84|m|a}}.<section end=par50 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

161.text:
