<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par51 />{{center|Verba Derivativa, or Derived Conjugations.}}

<!-- section begins above -->{{GHGpar-heading|51|Niphʿal||<ref>Cf. A. Rieder, ''De linguae Hebr. verbis, quae vocantur derivata nifal et hitpael'', Gumbinnen (Progr. des Gymn.), 1884, a list of all the strong Niphʿal forms (81) and Hithpaʿēl forms (36) in the Old Testament; and especially M. Lambert, ‘L’emploi du Nifal en Hébreu,’ {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} 41, 196 ff.</ref>}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|a}}
'''1.''' The essential characteristic of this conjugation consists in a prefix<ref>See Philippi in {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1886, p. 650, and Barth, ibid. 1894, p. 8 f.</ref> to the stem. This exists in two forms: (''a'') the (probably original) prepositive ''nă'', as in the Hebrew perfect and participle, although in the strong verb the ''ă'' is always attenuated to ''ĭ'': {{GHGheb|text=נִקְטַל}} for original ''nă-qăṭăl'', participle {{GHGheb|text=נִקְטָל}}, infinitive absolute sometimes {{GHGheb|text=נִקְטוֹל}}; (''b'') the (later) proclitic ''in'' (as in all the forms of the corresponding Arabic conjugation vii. ''ʾinqătălă''), found in the imperfect {{GHGheb|text=יִקָּטֵל}} for ''yinqāṭēl'', in the imperative and infinitive construct, with a secondary {{GHGheb|text=ה}} added, {{GHGheb|text=הִקָּטֵל}} (for ''hinqāṭēl''), and in the infinitive absolute {{GHGheb|text=הִקָּטֹל}} The inflexion of {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} is perfectly analogous to that of Qal.

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|b}}
The features of {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} are accordingly in the perfect and participle the prefixed ''Nûn'', in the imperative, infinitive, and imperfect, the {{GHGterm|Dageš}} in the first radical. These characteristics hold good also for the weak verb. In the case of an initial guttural, which, according to {{GHGpar|22|b}}, cannot take {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}}, the emission of the strengthening invariably causes the lengthening of the preceding vowel (see {{GHGpar|63|h}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|c}}
'''2.''' As regards its meaning, {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} bears some resemblance to the Greek ''middle voice'', in being—(''a'') primarily {{GHGterm|reflexive}} of Qal, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נִלְחַץ|translate=to thrust oneself}} (''against''), {{GHGheb|text=נִשְׁמַר|translate=to take heed to oneself}}, φυλάσσεσθαι, {{GHGheb|text=נִסְתַּר|translate=to hide oneself}}, {{GHGheb|text=נִגְאַל|translate=to redeem oneself}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=נַֽעֲנֶה|translate=to answer for oneself}}. Equally characteristic of {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} is its frequent use to express emotions which react upon the mind; {{GHGheb|text=נִחַם|translate=to trouble oneself}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֶֽאֱנַח|translate=to sigh}} (''to bemoan oneself'', cf. ὀδύρεσθαι, ''lamentari, contristari''); as well as to express actions which the subject allows to happen to himself, or to have an effect upon himself (''Niphʿal tolerativum''), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=דָּרַשׁ|translate=to search, to inquire}}, Niph. ''to allow oneself to be inquired of'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=65|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=14|verse=3}}, &c.; so the Niph. of {{GHGheb|text=מָצָא|translate=to find}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָסַר|translate=to warn, to correct}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|d}}
(''b'') It expresses ''reciprocal'' or mutual action, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=דִּבֶּר|translate=to speak}}, Niph. ''to speak to one another''; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁפַט|translate=to judge}}, Niph. ''to go to law with one another''; {{GHGheb|text=יָעַץ|translate=to counsel}}, Niph. ''to take counsel'', cf. the ''middle'' and ''deponent'' verbs βουλεύεσθαι ({{GHGheb|text=נוֹעַץ}}), μάξεσθαι ({{GHGheb|text=נְלְחַם}}), ''altercari, luctari'' ({{GHGheb|text=נִצָּה|translate=to strive with one another}}) ''proeliari''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|e}}
(''c'') It has also, like {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} ({{GHGpar|54|f}}) and the Greek ''middle'', the meaning of the active, with the addition of ''to oneself'' (''sibi''), ''for {{hyphenated word start|one|oneself}}''<section end=par51 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

162.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude>
<section begin=par51/>''{{hyphenated word end|self|oneself}}'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נִשְׁאַל|translate=to ask}} (something) ''for oneself'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=6.28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=13|verse=6}}), cf. {{polytonic|αἰτοῦμαί σε τοῦτο}}, {{polytonic|ἐνδύσασθαι χιτῶνα}} ''to put out on'' (oneself) ''a tunic''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|f}}
(''d'') In consequence of a looseness of thought at an early period of the language, {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} comes finally in many cases to represent the {{GHGterm|passive}}<ref>Cf. Halfmann, {{GHGcite|title=Beiträge zur Syntax der hebräischen Sprache}}, I. Stück, Wittenb., 1888, 2. St. 1892 (Gymn.-Programm), statistics of the Niphʿal (Puʿal, Hophʿal, and qāṭûl) forms at different periods of the language, for the purpose of ascertaining the meaning of Niph. and its relation to the passive; the selection of periods is, however, very questionable from the standpoint of literary criticism.</ref> of {{GHGterm|Qal}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יָלַד|translate=to bear}}, Niph. ''to be born''; {{GHGheb|text=קָבַר|translate=to bury}}, Niph. ''to be buried''. In cases where {{GHGterm|Qal}} is intransitive in meaning, or is not used, {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} appears also as the passive of {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כָּבֵד|translate=to be in honour}}, Piʿēl ''to honour'', Niph. ''to be honoured'' (as well as Puʿal {{GHGheb|text=כֻּבַּד}}); {{GHGheb|text=כָּחַד}} Piʿēl ''to conceal'', Hiph. to ''destroy'', Niph. passive of either. In such cases {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} may again coincide in meaning with Qal ({{GHGheb|text=חָלָה}} Qal and Niph. ''to be ill'') and even take an accusative.

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|g}}
Examples of denominatives are, {{GHGheb|text=נִזְכַּר|translate=to be born a male}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=34|verse=19}} (from {{GHGheb|text=זָכָר}}; but probably {{GHGheb|text=הַזָּכָר}} should here be read); {{GHGheb|text=נִלְבַּב|translate=cordatum fieri|en=to become hearty}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=11|verse=12}} (from {{GHGheb|text=לֵבָב|translate=cor|en=heart}}); doubtless also {{GHGheb|text=נִבְנָה|translate=to obtain children}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=3|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|h}}
The older grammarians were decidedly wrong in representing {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} simply as the {{GHGterm|passive}} of {{GHGterm|Qal}}; for {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} has (as the frequent use of its imperat. shows), in no respect the character of the other passives, and in Arabic a special conjugation (''ʾinqătălă'') corresponds to it with a passive of its own. Moreover, the forms mentioned in {{GHGpar|52|e}} point to a differently formed passive of {{GHGterm|Qal}}.—The form {{GHGheb|text=נְגֹֽאֲלוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=4|verse=14}}, is not to be regarded as a passive of Niphʿal, but with König and Cheyne as a ''forma mixta'', in the sense that the punctuators intended to combine two optional readings, {{GHGheb|text=נִגְאֲלוּ}}, perf. Niph., and {{GHGheb|text=גֹּֽאֲלוּ}}, perf. Puʿal [cf. also Wright, {{GHGcite|title=Compar. Gramm.}}, p. 224]. Although the passive use of Niphʿal was introduced at an early period, and became tolerably common, it is nevertheless quite secondary to the reflexive use.

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|i}}
Rem. 1 The ''infin. absol.'' {{GHGheb|text=נִקְטוֹל}} is connected in form with the perfect, to which it bears the same relation as {{GHGheb|text=קָטוֹל}} to {{GHGheb|text=קָטַל}} in Qal, the ''ô'' in the second syllable being obscured from an original ''â''. Examples are, {{GHGheb|text=נִכְסֹף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=30}}; {{GHGheb|text=נִלְחֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=25}}; {{GHGheb|text=נִשְׁאֹל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=6.28}}, all in connexion with the perfect.

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|k}}
Examples of the form {{GHGheb|text=הִקָּטֹל}} (in connexion with imperfects) are, {{GHGheb|text=הִנָּתֹן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=32|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֵֽאָכֹל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=7|verse=18}}; once {{GHGheb|text=אִדָּרֹשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=14|verse=3}}, where, perhaps, the subsequent {{GHGheb|text=אִדָּרֵשׁ}} has led to the substitution of {{GHGheb|text=א}} for {{GHGheb|text=ה}}.—Moreover, the form {{GHGheb|text=הִקָּטֵל}} is not infrequently used also for the infin. absol.,<ref>But, like {{GHGheb|text=הִקָּטֹל}}, ''only'' in connexion with imperfects, except {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=7|verse=9}}. Barth is therefore right in describing ({{GHGcite|title=Nominalbildung}}, p. 74) both forms as later analogous formations (in addition to the original Semitic {{GHGheb|text=נִקְטוֹל}}), intended to assimilate the infinitive to the imperfect which it strengthens.</ref> e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=22|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=15|verse=31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=39}}. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=כְּהִנָּדֵף}} should simply be read for the wholly abnormal {{GHGheb|text=כְּהִנְדֹּף}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=3}} (commonly explained as being intended to correspond in sound with the subsequent {{GHGheb|text=תִּנְדֹּף}} but probably a ‘forma mixta’, combining the readings {{GHGheb|text=כְּהִנָּדֵף}} and {{GHGheb|text=כִּנְדֹף}}).
<section end=par51/><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

163.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par51" />{{GHGmargin-letter|51|l}}
Elision of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} after prepositions is required by the Masora in {{GHGheb|text=בִּכָּֽשְׁלוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=17}} (for {{GHGheb|text=בְּהִכָּ׳}}), {{GHGheb|text=בֵּֽהָרֵג}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=15}} and {{GHGheb|text=בֵּֽעָטֵף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=2|verse=11}}; also in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=3}} ({{GHGheb|text=לֵֽעָנוֹת}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=34|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=31|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=12}} ({{GHGheb|text=לֵֽרָאוֹת}}); in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=33|verse=30}} ({{GHGheb|text=לֵאוֹר}}). It is, however, extremely doubtful whether the ''infin. Qal'' of the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} is not rather intended in all these examples; it certainly is so in {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=2|verse=11}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=61|verse=3}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|m}}
2. Instead of the {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} in the ultima of the imperfect, {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} often occurs in pause, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּגָּמַֽל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=8}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=31|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=15}} (with final {{GHGheb|text=שׁ}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=23|hidebook=1}} (with {{GHGheb|text=ק}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jon|chapter=1|verse=5}} (with {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}}); see {{GHGpar|29|q}}. In the 2nd and 3rd plur. fem. {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} predominates, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תִּזָּכַ֫רְנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=65|verse=17}}; {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} occurs only in {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽעָגֵ֫נָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=1|verse=13}}, from {{GHGheb|text=עגן}}, and hence, with loss of the doubling, for {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽעָגֵ֫נָּה}}; cf. even {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽאָמַֽנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=60|verse=4}}.—With ''Nûn paragogicum'' (see {{GHGpar|47|m}}) in the 2nd and 3rd plur. masc. are found, {{GHGheb|text=יִלָּֽכְדוּן}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּלָּֽחֲמוּן}}, &c., in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=יִבָּֽהֵלוּן}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּשָּֽׁמֵדוּן}}, &c.; but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=24}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=24|hidebook=1}}) {{GHGheb|text=יֵחָֽצְבֽוּן}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|n}}
3. When the imperfect, the infinitive (in ''ē''), or the imperative is followed in close connexion by a monosyllable, or by a word with the gone on the first syllable, the tone is, as a rule (but cf. {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּאָֽבֵק אִישׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=25}}), shifted back from the ultima to the penultima, while the ultima, which thus loses the tone, takes {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} instead of {{GHGterm|Ṣere}}; e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִכָּ֫שֶׁל בָּהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=33|verse=12}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּעָ֫תֶר לוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=25|verse=21}}; in the imperative, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=13|verse=9|hidebook=1}}.—So always {{GHGheb|text=הִשָּׁ֫מֶר לְךָ}} (since {{GHGheb|text=לְךָ}} counts as ''one'' syllable) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=6}}, &c., cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=2}}; and even with {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} in the ultima, {{GHGheb|text=תֵּעָ֫זַב אָ֑רֶץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=18|verse=4}} (but cf. {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּעָֽתֵ֫ר אֱלֹהִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=21|verse=14}}). Although in isolated cases (e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=8|verse=23}}) the tone is not thrown back, in spite of a tone-syllable following, the retraction has become usual in certain forms, even when the next word begins with a toneless syllable; especially after {{GHGheb|text=ו}} {{GHGterm|consec.}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּשָּׁ֫אֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=23}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּלָּ֫חֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=1}} and frequently, {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּצָּ֫מֶד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=25|verse=3|hidebook=1}}; and always so in the imperative {{GHGheb|text=הִשָּׁ֫מֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=36|verse=21}}, and (before Metheg of the counter-tone) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=24|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=6|verse=9}}. On the avoidance of pausal-forms in the imperative ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=2|verse=12}} with ''Silluq'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=2|verse=11}} with ''Athnaḥ''), and imperfect ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=4}}, &c.), see {{GHGpar|29|o}}, and note; on the other hand, always {{GHGheb|text=הִמָּלֵט}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִמָּלֵט}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|o}}
In the {{GHGterm|imperative}}, {{GHGheb|text=נִקְבְּצוּ}}, for {{GHGheb|text=הִקָּֽבְצוּ}}, with the rejection of the initial {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=9}}, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Joel|chapter=4|verse=11}} in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=נִקְבָּ֑צוּ}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=נִלְווּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=50|verse=5}}); but in these examples either the reading or the explanation is doubtful. The 2nd sing. imperat. of {{GHGheb|text=נִשְׁבַּע}} is always (with {{GHGheb|text=־ָה|translate=paragogicum}}) {{GHGheb|text=הִשָּׁ֫בְעָה לִּי|translate=swear to me}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=23}}, &c. (also {{GHGheb|text=הִשָּֽׁבְעָה לִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=30|verse=15}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|51|p}}
4. For the 1st sing. of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}, the form {{GHGheb|text=אִקָּטֵל}} is as frequent as {{GHGheb|text=אֶקָּטֵל}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אִדָּרֵשׁ|translate=I shall be inquired of}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=14|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=אִשָּׁבֵעַ|translate=I will swear}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=24}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=20|verse=36}}, and so always in the cohortative, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אִנָּֽקְמָה|translate=I will avenge me}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=24}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=12|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=2}}, and in the impf. Niph. of {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} ({{GHGpar|69|t}}). The Babylonian punctuation admits only ''ĭ'' under the preformative of the 1st person.
<section end="par51" />
<section begin="par52" />{{GHGpar-heading|52|Piʿēl and Puʿal}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|a}}
'''1.''' The ''characteristic'' of this conjugation consists in the strengthening of the middle radical. From the simple stem ''qaṭal'' (cf. {{GHGpar|43|b}}) the form {{GHGheb|text=קַטַּל}} (cf. the Arabic conj. ii. ''qăttălă'') would naturally follow as<section end="par52" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

164.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="68.174.1.21" /></noinclude><section begin="par52"/>the {{GHGterm|perfect}} of the active (''Piʿ̄l''). The {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} of the first syllable is, however, with one exception (see m), always attenuated to ''ĭ'' in the {{GHGterm|perfect}}. In the second syllable, ''ă'' has been retained in the majority of cases, so that the conjugation should more correctly be called ''Piʿal;'' but very frequently<ref>So in all verbs which end in ''Nûn'', and in almost all which end in ''Lamed'' (Olsh. p. 538). Barth is probably right in supposing ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1894, p. 1 ff.) that the vowels of the strengthened perfects have been influenced by the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}.</ref> this ''ă'' also is attenuated to ''ĭ'', which is then regularly lengthened to ''ē'', under the influence of the tone. Cf. in Aram. {{GHGheb|text=קַטֵּל}}; but in Biblical Aramaic almost always {{GHGheb|text=קַטִּל}}. On the three cases in which ''ă'' before a final {{GHGheb|text=ר}} or {{GHGheb|text=ס}} has passed into {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, see below, l.—Hence, for the ''3rd sing. masc. perfect'', there arise forms like {{GHGheb|text=אִבַּד}}, {{GHGheb|text=לִמַּד}}, {{GHGheb|text=קִדַּשׁ}}; {{GHGheb|text=גִּדֵּף}}, {{GHGheb|text=כִּבֵּד}}, &c.—Before afformatives beginning with a consonant, however, ''ă'' is always retained, thus {{GHGheb|text=קִטַּ֫לְתָּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=קִטַּלְתֶּם}}, {{GHGheb|text=קִטַּ֫לְנוּ}}, &c. In the ''infinitives'' ({{GHGterm|absol.}} {{GHGheb|text=קַטֹּל}}, obscured from ''qaṭṭâl''; {{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=קַטֵּל}}), {{GHGterm|imperfect}} ({{GHGheb|text=יְקַטֵּל}}), {{GHGterm|imperative}} ({{GHGheb|text=קַטֵּל}}), and {{GHGterm|participle}} ({{GHGheb|text=מְקַטֵּל}}) the original ''ă'' of the first syllable reappears throughout. The vocal {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} of the preformatives is weakened from a short vowel; cf. the Arabic imperfect ''yŭqăttĭl'', participle ''mŭqăttĭl''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|b}}
The {{GHGterm|passive}} ({{GHGterm|Puʿal}}) is distinguished by the obscure vowel ''ŭ'', or very rarely ''ŏ'', in the first syllable, and ''ŏ'' (in pause ''ā'') always in the second. In Arabic, also, the passives are formed throughout with ''ŭ'' in the first syllable. The inflexion of both these conjugations is analogous to that of {{GHGterm|Qal}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|c}}
Rem. 1. The preformative {{GHGheb|text=מְ‍}}, which in the remaining conjugations also is the prefix of the participle, is probably connected with the interrogative or indefinite (cf. § 37) pronoun {{GHGheb|text=מִי|translate=quis? quicunque}} (fem. i.e. neuter, {{GHGheb|text=מָה}}); cf. {{GHGpar|85|e}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|d}}
2. The Dageš ''forte'', which according to the above is characteristic of the whole of {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and {{GHGterm|Puʿal}}, is often omitted (independently of verbs ''middle guttural'', {{GHGpar|64|d}}) when the middle radical has {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} under it (cf. {{GHGpar|20|m}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שִׁלְחָה}} for {{GHGheb|text=שִׁלְּחָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=17|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=בִּקְשֻׁ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=15|verse=15}} (but in the {{GHGterm|imperative}} always {{GHGheb|text=בַּקְּשׁוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=7}}, &c.), and so always in {{GHGheb|text=הַלְלוּ|translate=praise}}. The vocal character of the {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} under the ''litera dagessanda'' is sometimes in such cases (according to {{GHGpar|10|h}}) expressly emphasized by its taking the form of a {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph}}, as in {{GHGheb|text=לֻֽקֳחָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=23}}, with {{GHGheb|text=־ֳ}} owing to the influence of the preceding ''u'', cf. {{GHGheb|text=פָּֽעֳלוֹ}} for {{GHGheb|text=פָּעְלוֹ}}, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=16}}. In the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} and {{GHGterm|participle}} the {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} under the preformatives ({{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Pathaḥ}} under {{GHGheb|text=א}} in the ''1st sing. imperfect'') serves at the same time as a characteristic of both conjugations ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=14}} f.).

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|e}}
3. According to the convincing suggestion of Böttcher<ref>As Mayer Lambert observes, the same view was already expressed by Ibn Ǵanâḥ (see above, {{GHGpar|3|d}}) in the ''Kitāb el-lumaʿ'', p. 161. Cf. especially Barth, ‘Das passive Qal und seine Participien,’ in the {{GHGcite|title=Festschrift zum Jubiläum Hildesheimer}} (Berlin, 1890), p. 145 ff.</ref> ({{GHGcite|title=Ausführliches Lehrbuch}}, {{GHGpar|904|ff}}. and § 1022), many supposed perfects of {{GHGterm|Puʿal}} are in reality<section end="par52"/><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

165.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par52 />passives of Qal. He reckons as such all those ''perfects'', of which the {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} (which ought to express the corresponding active) is either not found at all, or only (as in the case of {{GHGheb|text=יִלֵּד}}) with a different meaning, and which form their {{GHGterm|imperfect}} from another conjugation, generally Niphʿal. Such ''perfects'' are the ''quṭṭal'' form of the stems {{GHGheb|text=אבל}} ({{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=תְּאֻבְּלוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=20}}), {{GHGheb|text=חפשׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=טרף}}, {{GHGheb|text=ילד}}, {{GHGheb|text=יצר}}, {{GHGheb|text=לקח}}, {{GHGheb|text=עבד}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׁגל}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׁטף}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׁפךְ}}. Barth (see below) adds to the list the apparent {{GHGterm|Puʿal}}-''perfects'' of {{GHGheb|text=אסר}}, {{GHGheb|text=בזז}}, {{GHGheb|text=זנה}}, {{GHGheb|text=חצב}}, {{GHGheb|text=כרת}}, {{GHGheb|text=נפח}}, {{GHGheb|text=עזב}}, {{GHGheb|text=עשה}}, {{GHGheb|text=ראה}}, and of verbs with middle {{GHGheb|text=ר}} (hence with ''ŭ'' of the first syllable lengthened to ''ō''), {{GHGheb|text=הרג}}, {{GHGheb|text=הרה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=3}} [{{GHGheb|text=זרה}}, see {{GHGpar|67|m}}], {{GHGheb|text=זרע}}, {{GHGheb|text=זרק}}, {{GHGheb|text=טרף}}, {{GHGheb|text=מרט}}, {{GHGheb|text=קרא}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׂרף}}; also the infinitives absolute {{GHGheb|text=הֹרוֹ וְהֹגוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=13}}. In these cases there is no need to assume any error on the part of the punctuators; the sharpening of the second radical may have taken place in order to retain the characteristic ''ŭ'' of the first syllable (cf. Arab. ''qŭtĭlă'' as passive of ''qătălă''), and the ''a'' of the second syllable is in accordance with the vocalization of all the other passives (see {{GHGpar|39|f}}). Cf. {{GHGpar|52|s}} and {{GHGpar|53|u}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|f}}
'''2.''' The fundamental idea of {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, to which all the various shades of meaning in this conjugation may be referred, is to ''busy oneself eagerly'' with the action indicated by the stem. This intensifying of the idea of the stem, which is outwardly expressed by the strengthening of the second radical, appears in individual cases as—(''a'') a ''strengthening'' and ''repetition'' of the action (cf. the ''intensive'' and ''iterative'' nouns with the middle radical strengthened, {{GHGpar|84||b}}),<ref>Analogous examples, in which the strengthening of a letter has likewise an ''intensive'' force, are such German words as ''reichen, recken'' (Eng. ''to reach, to rack''); ''streichen'' (''stringo''), ''strecken'': cf. ''Strich'' (''a stroke''), ''Strecke'' (''a stretch''); ''wacker'' from ''wachen''; others, in which it has the ''causative'' sense, are ''stechen, stecken''; ''wachen'' (''watch''), ''wecken'' (''wake''); τέλλω ''to bring to an end'' (cf. the stem τέλω ''to end'', in τέλος, τελέω); γεννάω ''to beget'', from the stem γένω ''to come into being'' (cf. γένος).</ref> e.g. {{GHGheb|text=צָחַק|translate=to laugh}}, Piʿēl ''to jest, to make sport'' (to laugh repeatedly); {{GHGheb|text=שָׁאַל|translate=to ask}}, Piʿēl ''to beg''; hence when an action has reference to ''many'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קָבַר|translate=to bury}} (a person) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=23|verse=4}}, Piʿēl ''to bury'' (many) {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=15}}, and often so in Syr. and Arab. Other varieties of the ''intensive'' and ''iterative'' meaning are, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=פָּתַח|translate=to open}}, Piʿēl ''to loose''; {{GHGheb|text=סָפַר|translate=to count}}, Piʿēl ''to recount'': [cf. {{GHGheb|text=כִּתֵּב}}, {{GHGheb|text=חִשֵּׁב}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִלֵּךְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=רִפֵּא}}, {{GHGheb|text=חִפֵּשׂ}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּפֵּשׂ}}; {{GHGheb|text=מְאַהֵב}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְרַצֵּחַ}}].

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|g}}
The eager pursuit of an action may also consist in ''urging'' and ''causing'' others to do the same. Hence {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} has also—(''b'') a ''causative'' sense (like {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לָמַד|translate=to learn}}, Piʿēl ''to teach''. It may often be turned by such phrases as ''to permit to, to declare'' or ''hold as'' (''the declarative Piʿēl''), ''to help to'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חִיָּה|translate=to cause to live}}, {{GHGheb|text=צִדֵּק|translate=to declare innocent}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִלֵּד|translate=to help in child-bearing}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|h}}
(''c'') ''Denominatives'' (see {{GHGpar|38|b}}) are frequently formed in this conjugation, and generally express a being occupied with the object expressed by the noun, either to form or to make use of it, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קִנֵּן|translate=to make a nest, to nest}} (from {{GHGheb|text=קֵן}}), {{GHGheb|text=עִפֵּר|translate=to throw dust, to dust}} (from {{GHGheb|text=עָפָר}}),<section end=par52 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

166.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par52 />{{GHGheb|text=עִנֵּן|translate=to gather the clouds together}} (from {{GHGheb|text=עָנָן}}), {{GHGheb|text=שִׁלֵּשׁ|translate=to divide in three parts}}, or ''to do a thing for the third time'' (from {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלשׁ}}); probably also {{GHGheb|text=דִּבֶּר|translate=to speak}}, from {{GHGheb|text=דָּבָר|translate=a word}}. Or again, the denominative may express taking away, injuring, &c., the object denoted by the noun (''privative Piʿēl'', cf. our ''to skin, to behead, to bone''), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁרֵשׁ}}, from {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁ֫רֶשׁ|translate=to root out, to extirpate}}, {{GHGheb|text=זִנֵּב}} prop. to ''injure the tail'' ({{GHGheb|text=זָנָב}}), hence ''to rout the rear'' of an army, ''to attack it''; {{GHGheb|text=לִבֵּב|translate=to ravish the heart}}; {{GHGheb|text=דִּשֵּׁן|translate=to remove the ashes}} ({{GHGheb|text=דֶּ֫שֶׁן}}), {{GHGheb|text=חִטֵּא|translate=to free from sin}} ({{GHGheb|text=חֵטְא}}), {{GHGheb|text=עִצֵּם}} ''to break any one’s bones'' ({{GHGheb|text=עֶ֫צֶם}}; cf., in the same sense, {{GHGheb|text=גֵּרֵם}} from {{GHGheb|text=גֶּ֫רֶם}}); {{GHGheb|text=סֵעֵף|translate=to lop the boughs}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=33}} (from {{GHGheb|text=סְעִיף|translate=a bough}}). Some words are clearly denominatives, although the noun from which they are derived is no longer found, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=סִקֵּל|translate=to stone, to pelt with stones}} (also used in this sense in {{GHGterm|Qal}}), and ''to remove stones'' (from a field), ''to clear away stones''; cf. our ''to stone'', used also in the sense of ''taking out the stones'' from fruit.

The meaning of the {{GHGterm|passive}} ({{GHGterm|Puʿal}}) follows naturally from the above, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בִּקֵּשׁ}} Piʿēl ''to seek'', Puʿal ''to be sought''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|i}}
In {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} the literal, concrete meaning of the verb has sometimes been retained, when {{GHGterm|Qal}} has acquired a figurative sense, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גָּלָה}}, Piʿēl ''to uncover'', Qal ''to reveal'', also ''to emigrate'', i.e. to make the land bare.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|k}}
Also with an intransitive sense {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} occurs as an intensive form, but only in poetic language, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חתת}} in Piʿēl ''to be broken in pieces'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=51|verse=56}}; {{GHGheb|text=פִּחַד|translate=to tremble}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=28|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=רִוָּה|translate=to be drunken}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=34|verse=5.7}}; [{{GHGheb|text=מִעֵט|translate=to be few}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=3}}]; but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=48|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=60|verse=11|hidebook=1}} instead of the Piʿēl of {{GHGheb|text=פתח}} the Niphʿal is certainly to be read, with Cheyne.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|l}}
Rem. 1. The (more frequent) form of the perfect with {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} in the second syllable appears especially before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=9|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=9|hidebook=1}}) and in the middle of sentences in continuous discourse, but at the end of the sentence (in {{GHGterm|pause}}) the form with {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} is more common. Cf. {{GHGheb|text=גִּדֵּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=21}} with {{GHGheb|text=גִּדַּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=4|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=3|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=מִלֵּט}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=33|verse=5}} with {{GHGheb|text=מִלַּט}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=9|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=קִצַּץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=8|verse=16}} with {{GHGheb|text=קִצֵּץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=129|verse=4}}; but Qameṣ never appears in this pausal form. The ''3rd sing. fem.'' in {{GHGterm|pause}} is always of the form {{GHGheb|text=קִטֵּ֫לָה}}, except {{GHGheb|text=קִבָּ֫צָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=1|verse=7}}; the 3rd plur. always as {{GHGheb|text=קִטֵּ֫לוּ}}; the ''2nd'' and ''1st sing.'' and ''1st plur.'' of course as {{GHGheb|text=קִטָּ֫לְתָּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=קִטָּ֫לְתְּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=קִטָּ֫לְתִּי}} (but always {{GHGheb|text=דִּבַּֽרְתִּי}} and {{GHGheb|text=לִמַּ֫דְתִּי}}), {{GHGheb|text=קִטָּ֫לְנוּ}}. In the ''3rd sing. perf.'' {{GHGheb|text=דִּבֶּר|translate=to speak}}, {{GHGheb|text=כִּפֶּר|translate=to pardon}}, and {{GHGheb|text=כִּבֶּס|translate=to wash clothes}} (also {{GHGheb|text=כִבֵּס}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=11}}) take {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, but become in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=דִּבֵּר}}, {{GHGheb|text=כִּבֵּס}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=25}}); the ''pausal'' form of {{GHGheb|text=כִּפֶּר}} does not occur.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|m}}
{{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} in the first syllable (as in Aramaic and Arabic) occurs only once, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=51}}, {{GHGheb|text=נַ֫שַּׁנִי|translate=he made me forget}}, to emphasize more clearly the play on the name {{GHGheb|text=מְנַשֶּׁה}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|n}}
2. In the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} (and {{GHGterm|jussive}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=25}}), ''infinitive, and imperative Piʿēl'' (as also in {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}}) the {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} in the final syllable, when followed by {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}}, is usually shortened into {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יְבַקֶּשׁ־לוֹ|translate=he seeks for himself}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=20}}; {{GHGheb|text=קַדֶּשׁ־לִי|translate=sanctify unto me}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=13|verse=2}}. ''Pausal-forms'' with {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} instead of {{GHGterm|Ṣere}}, as {{GHGheb|text=יְרַחֶף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=11}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲרַחֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=2|verse=6}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=6}} in the infinitive, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=9}} in the participle), owe their origin to some particular school of Masoretes, and are wrongly accepted by Baer; cf. the analogous cases in {{GHGpar|75|n}} and hh. If the final syllable of the {{GHGterm|imperfect Piʿēl}} has Pathaḥ (before a guttural or {{GHGheb|text=ר}}), it remains<section end=par52 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

167.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par52 />even in {{GHGterm|pause}}; cf. {{GHGpar|29|s}} and 65 e. In the 1st sing. imperfect the ''e''-sound occurs in two words for {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Pathaḥ}}, under the preformative {{GHGheb|text=א}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֱזָרֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=5|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=12|verse=14|hidebook=1}} and {{GHGheb|text=וְאֵסָ֣עֲרֵם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=7|verse=14}} (in accordance with {{GHGpar|23|h}}).—Before the full plural ending {{GHGheb|text=וּן}} (see {{GHGpar|47|m}}) the {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} is retained in {{GHGterm|pause}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תְּדַבֵּר֑וּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=58|verse=2}} (but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=תְּדַבְּר֣וּן}}), cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=6|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=12|verse=3}}; so before ''Silluq'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=58|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=11}} and even before {{GHGterm|Zaqeph qaṭon}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=7|verse=5}}. Instead of {{GHGheb|text=תְּקַטֵּ֫לְנָה}}, forms like {{GHGheb|text=תְּקַטַּ֫לְנָה}} are also found, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=13|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, in both cases before a sibilant and in pause. Also {{GHGheb|text=פַּלַּג}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=55|verse=10}} occurs as the 2nd sing. imperative (probably an intentional imitation of the sound of the preceding {{GHGheb|text=בַּלַּע}}) and {{GHGheb|text=קָרַב}} (for ''qarrabh'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=37|verse=17}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|o}}
3. The ''infinite absolute'' of {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} has sometimes the special form {{GHGheb|text=קַטֹּל}} given in the paradigm, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יַסֹּר|translate=castigando}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=18}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=19|verse=10}} (from a verb {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=40|verse=2}} (from a verb {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}); but much more frequently the form of the {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} ({{GHGheb|text=קַטֵּל}}) is used instead. The latter has also, in exceptional cases, the form {{GHGheb|text=קִטֵּל}} (with ''ă'' attenuated to ''ĭ'' as in the {{GHGterm|perfect}}), e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=8|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=שִׁלְחוֹ}}; perhaps also (if not a substantive) {{GHGheb|text=קִטֵּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=44|verse=21}}; and for the sake of assonance even for {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=14}} ({{GHGheb|text=נִאֵץ נִאַ֫צְתָּ}}). On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁלֵּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=35}} and {{GHGheb|text=דִּבֵּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=13}} are better regarded as substantives, while {{GHGheb|text=דִּבֶּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=6|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=3|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=15}} (in each case after {{GHGheb|text=בְּיוֹם}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=1|verse=2}} (after {{GHGheb|text=תְּחִלַּת}}), in all of which places it is considered by König (after Qimḥi) to be {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}}, is really perfect of {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|p}}
The infinitive construct {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, with the {{GHGterm|fem.}} ending (cf. {{GHGpar|45|d}}), occurs in {{GHGheb|text=יַסְּרָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=זַמְּרָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=147|verse=1}}; with {{GHGheb|text=ת}} of the {{GHGterm|fem.}} before a suffix {{GHGheb|text=צַדֶּקְתֵּךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=52}}. On the verbal nouns after the form of the Aram. inf. ''Pa‛il'' ({{GHGheb|text=קַטָּלָה}}), see {{GHGpar|84|e|b}}.

Instead of the abnormal {{GHGheb|text=מְאָֽסְפָיו}} (so Baer, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=62|verse=9}}) as ptcp. Pi‛el, read {{GHGheb|text=מְאַסְ׳}} with ed. Mant. and Ginsburg.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|q}}
4. In Puʿal ''ŏ'' is sometimes found instead of ''ŭ'' in the initial syllable, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מְאָדָּם|translate=dyed red}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=25|verse=5}}, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=2|verse=4}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=7|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=שָׁדְּדָה}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=72|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=80|verse=11|hidebook=1}}. According to Baer’s reading also in {{GHGheb|text=תְּרָצְּחוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=62|verse=4}}, and so also Ben Ašer, but Ben Naphtali {{GHGheb|text=תְּרַצְּחוּ}}. It is merely an orthographic licence when ''ŭ'' is written fully, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יוּלַּד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=18|verse=29}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|r}}
5. As {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}}, of {{GHGterm|Puʿal}} we find {{GHGheb|text=גֻּנֹּב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=15}}.—No instance of the ''inf. constr.'' occurs in the strong verb in {{GHGterm|Puʿal}}; from {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} with suffix {{GHGheb|text=עֻנּוֹתוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=132|verse=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|s}}
6. A few examples occur of the {{GHGterm|participle Puʿal}} without the preformative ({{GHGheb|text=מְ‍}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֻכָּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=יוּלָּד}} (for {{GHGheb|text=מְיֻלָּד}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=לֻקָּח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=2|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=סֹעֲרָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=54|verse=11}}. These {{GHGterm|participles}} are distinguished from the {{GHGterm|perfect}} (as in {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}) by the ''ā'' of the final syllable. For other examples, see {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=9|verse=12}} (where {{GHGheb|text=יוּקָשִׁים}}, according to {{GHGpar|20|n}}, stands for {{GHGheb|text=יֻקָּ׳}} = {{GHGheb|text=מְיֻקָּ׳}}); but, according to the Masora, ''not'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=17}}, since {{GHGheb|text=הַֽהֻלָּ֫לָה}} as ''Mil‛êl'' can only be the {{GHGterm|perfect}}. The rejection of the {{GHGheb|text=מְ‍}} may be favoured by an initial {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}}, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=18|verse=2.7}} (but also {{GHGheb|text=מְמֻשָּׁךְ}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=19}} (where, however, read {{GHGheb|text=מוֹעֶ֫דֶת}}); so also in the participle {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=מָאֵן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=7|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=2|hidebook=1}} (always after {{GHGheb|text=אִם}}, but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=הַמֵּאֲנִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=10}}, where, however, {{GHGheb|text=הַמָּֽאֲנִים}} = {{GHGheb|text=הַמְמָֽאֲנִים}} is to be read, with Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, p. 264 f.) and {{GHGheb|text=מַהֵר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=1|verse=14}} (and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=1.3}}?). Notice, however, Barth’s suggestion ({{GHGcite|title=Nominalbildung}}, p. 273) that, as the active of forms like {{GHGheb|text=אֻכָּל}} only occurs in {{GHGterm|Qal}}, they are perfect participles of former ''passives'' of Qal (see e), and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=32|hidebook=1}}, perfect participles of Piʿēl.—On {{GHGheb|text=מְרֻבַּע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=45|verse=2}}, see {{GHGpar|65|d}}.<section end=par52 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

168.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="CalendulaAsteraceae" /></noinclude><section begin=par53 />{{GHGpar-heading|53|Hiphʿîl and Hophʿal}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|a}}
'''1.''' The characteristic of the active ({{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}) is a prefixed {{GHGheb|text=הַ}} (on its origin see {{GHGpar|55|i}}) in the perfect {{GHGheb|text=הִ}} (with the ''ă'' attenuated to ''ĭ'', as in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}), which forms a closed syllable with the first consonant of the stem. The second syllable of the perfect had also originally an ''ă''; cf. the Arabic conj. iv. ''’aqtălă'', and in Hebrew the return of the {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} in the 2nd and 1st pers. {{GHGheb|text=הִקְטַ֫לְתָּ}}, &c. After the attenuation of this ''ă'' to ''ĭ'', it ought by rule to have been lengthened to ''ē'' in the tone-syllable, as in Aramaic {{GHGheb|text=אַקְטֵל}}, beside {{GHGheb|text=הַקְטִל}} in Biblical Aramaic. Instead of this, however, it is always replaced in the strong verb by ''î'',<ref>This ''î'' may have been transferred originally from the imperfects of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, as a convenient means of distinction between the indicative and jussive, to the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} of the strong verb and afterwards to the whole of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}; so Stade, Philippi, Praetorius, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZAW.|Zeitschrift für die alttestamentliche Wissenschaft, ed. by B. Stade, Giessen, 1881 ff., and since 1907 by K. Marti.}}}} 1883, p. 52 f.</ref>{{GHGheb|text=־ִי}}, but sometimes written defectively {{GHGheb|text=־ִ}}; cf. {{GHGpar|9|g}}. Similarly in the infinitive construct {{GHGheb|text=הַקְטִיל}}, and in the imperfect and participle {{GHGheb|text=יַקְטִיל}} and {{GHGheb|text=טַקְטִיל}}, which are syncopated from {{GHGheb|text=יְהַקְטִיל}} and {{GHGheb|text=מְהַקְטִיל}}; {{GHGpar|23|k}}. The corresponding Arabic forms (''juqtĭl'' and ''muqtĭl'') point to an original ''ĭ'' in the second syllable of these forms. In Hebrew the regular lengthening of this ''ĭ'' to ''ē'' appears in the strong verb at least in the {{GHGterm|jussive}} and in the {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}} (see n), as also in the {{GHGterm|imperative}} of the 2nd sing. masc. (see m); on {{GHGheb|text=הַקְטֵ֫לְנָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּקְטֵ֫לְנָה}} cf. {{GHGpar|26|p}}. On the return of the original ''ă'' in the second syllable of the ''Imperat., Jussive'', &c, under the influence of a guttural, cf. {{GHGpar|65|f}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|b}}
In the {{GHGterm|passive}} ({{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}) the preformative is pronounced with an obscure vowel, whilst the second syllable has ''ă'' (in pause ''ā''), as its characteristic, thus:—''Perf.'' {{GHGheb|text=הָקְטַל}} or {{GHGheb|text=הֻקְטַל}}, ''Imperf.'' {{GHGheb|text=יָקְטַל}} (syncopated from {{GHGheb|text=יְהָקְטַל}}) or {{GHGheb|text=יֻקְטַל}}, ''Part.'' {{GHGheb|text=מָקְטָל}} or {{GHGheb|text=מֻקְטָל}} (from {{GHGheb|text=מְהָקְטָל}}); but the {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} has the form {{GHGheb|text=הָקְטֵל}}.

Thus the characteristics of both conjugations are the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} preformative in the ''perfect, imperative'', and {{GHGterm|infinitive}}; in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} and {{GHGterm|participle Hiphʿîl}}, Pathaḥ under the preformatives, in the ''Hophʿal ŏ'' or ''ŭ''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|c}}
'''2.''' The ''meaning'' of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} is primarily, and even more frequently than in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} ({{GHGpar|52|g}}), ''causative'' of {{GHGterm|Qal}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יָצָא|translate=to go forth}}, Hiph. ''to bring forth, to lead forth, to draw forth''; {{GHGheb|text=קָדַשׁ|translate=to be holy}}, Hiph. ''to sanctify''. Under the ''causative'' is also included (as in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}) the ''declarative'' sense, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִצְדִּיק|translate=to pronounce just}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִרְשִׁיעַ|translate=to make one an evil doer}} (''to pronounce guilty''); cf. {{GHGheb|text=עקשׁ}}, in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=20}}, ''to represent as perverse''. If Qal has already a transitive meaning, {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} then takes two accusatives (see {{GHGpar|117|cc}}). In some verbs, {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} occur side by side in the same sense, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אָבַד|translate=periit}}, Piʿēl and Hiphʿîl, ''perdidit''; as a rule,<section end=par53 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

169.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par53 />however, only one of these two conjugations is in use, or else they differ from one another in meaning, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כָּבֵד|translate=gravem esse}}, Piʿēl ''to honour'', Hiphʿîl ''to bring to honour'', also ''to make heavy''. Verbs which are intransitive in {{GHGterm|Qal}} simply become transitive in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נָטָה|translate=to bow oneself}}, Hiph. ''to bow, to bend''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|d}}
Among the ideas expressed by the ''causative'' and ''transitive'' are included, moreover, according to the ''Hebrew'' point of view (and that of the Semitic languages in general, especially Arabic), a series of actions and ideas, which ''we'' have to express by periphrasis, in order to understand their being represented by the Hiphʿîl-form. To these ''inwardly transitive'' or ''intensive'' Hiphʿîls belong: (''a'') Hiphʿîl stems which express the obtaining or receiving of a concrete or abstract quality. (In the following examples the {{GHGterm|Qal}} stems are given, for the sake of brevity, with the addition of the meaning which—often together with other meanings—belongs to the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}.) Thus {{GHGheb|text=אהל}}, {{GHGheb|text=זהר}}, {{GHGheb|text=יפע}}, {{GHGheb|text=צוץ|translate=to be bright, to shine}} (to give forth brightness); opposed to {{GHGheb|text=חשׁךְ|translate=to become dark}}; {{GHGheb|text=אמץ}}, {{GHGheb|text=גבר}}, {{GHGheb|text=חזק|translate=to be strong}} (to develop strength), {{GHGheb|text=עטף|translate=to be weak}}; {{GHGheb|text=ארךְ|translate=to be long}} (to acquire length); {{GHGheb|text=גבהּ|translate=to be high}}; {{GHGheb|text=הום|translate=to be in tumult}}, {{GHGheb|text=זעק|translate=to cry out}}, {{GHGheb|text=רוע}}, {{GHGheb|text=רנן|translate=to make a noise, to exult}}; {{GHGheb|text=חלף|translate=to sprout}} (to put forth shoots), cf. {{GHGheb|text=פרח|translate=to bloom}}, {{GHGheb|text=עדף}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׁוק|translate=to overflow}}; {{GHGheb|text=חרשׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=חשׁה}}, {{GHGheb|text=סכת}}, {{GHGheb|text=צמת|translate=to be silent}} (silentium facere, Pliny); {{GHGheb|text=מתק|translate=to be sweet}}; {{GHGheb|text=צלח|translate=to have success}}; {{GHGheb|text=שׁפל|translate=to be low}}; {{GHGheb|text=אדם|translate=to become red}}, {{GHGheb|text=לבן|translate=to become white}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|e}}
(''b'') Stems which express in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} the entering into a certain condition and, further, the being in the same: {{GHGheb|text=אמן|translate=to become firm, to trust in}}; {{GHGheb|text=באשׁ|translate=to become stinking}}; {{GHGheb|text=זוד|translate=to become boiling, to boil over}}; {{GHGheb|text=חלה|translate=to become ill}}; {{GHGheb|text=הסר|translate=to come to want}}; {{GHGheb|text=חרה|translate=to become hot}}; {{GHGheb|text=יבשׁ|translate=to become dry, to become ashamed}}; {{GHGheb|text=יתר|translate=to attain superiority}}; {{GHGheb|text=סכן|translate=to become familiar}}; {{GHGheb|text=עור}}, {{GHGheb|text=קוץ|translate=to become awake}}; {{GHGheb|text=קשׁה|translate=to become hard}}; {{GHGheb|text=רגע}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׁקט|translate=to become quiet}} (to keep quiet); {{GHGheb|text=שׁמם|translate=to be astonished}}. The Hiphʿîl forms of some verbs of motion constitute a variety of this class: {{GHGheb|text=נגשׁ|translate=to draw near}}; {{GHGheb|text=קרב|translate=to come near}}; {{GHGheb|text=רחק|translate=to withdraw far off}} (all these three are besides used as causatives); {{GHGheb|text=קדם|translate=to come before}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|f}}
(''c'') Stems which express action in some particular direction: {{GHGheb|text=חטא|translate=to err}}; {{GHGheb|text=חלק|translate=to flatter}} (to act smoothly); {{GHGheb|text=יטב|translate=to act well, to do good}}; {{GHGheb|text=סכל|translate=to act foolishly}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׂכל|translate=to act wisely}}; {{GHGheb|text=ערם|translate=to act craftily}}; {{GHGheb|text=צנע|translate=to act submissively}}; {{GHGheb|text=רעע}}, {{GHGheb|text=רשׁע|translate=to act wickedly, godlessly}}; {{GHGheb|text=שׁחת}}, {{GHGheb|text=תעב|translate=to act corruptly, abominably}}; {{GHGheb|text=שׁלם|translate=to act peacefully, to be at peace, to be submissive}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|g}}
Further, there are in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} a considerable number of ''denominatives'' which express the ''bringing out'', the ''producing'' of a thing, and so are properly regarded as causatives,<ref>The same ideas are also paraphrased by the verb {{GHGheb|text=עָשָׂה}} (''to make''), e.g. ''to make fat'', for, to produce fat upon his body, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=27}}; ''to make fruit, to make branches'', for, to put forth, to yield, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=14|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=8|verse=7}}, cf. the Lat. ''corpus, robur, sobolem, divitias facere'', and the Ital. ''far corpo, far forze, far frutto''.</ref> e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אצר|translate=to set over the treasury}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=13|verse=13}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=וָאְַֽצַוֶּה}} is to be read, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=7|verse=2}}); {{GHGheb|text=בכר|translate=to bring forth a firstborn}}; {{GHGheb|text=גשׁם|translate=to cause to rain}}; {{GHGheb|text=זרע|translate=to produce seed}}; {{GHGheb|text=ימן}} ({{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵימִין}}) ''to go to the right'', cf. {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׂמְאִיל|translate=to go to the left}}; {{GHGheb|text=פרס|translate=to get}} or ''to have hoofs''; {{GHGheb|text=קרן|translate=to get}} or ''to have horns''; {{GHGheb|text=שׁכל|translate=to produce abortion}}; {{GHGheb|text=שׁלג|translate=to become snow-white}}; {{GHGheb|text=שׁמן|translate=to grow fat}}; {{GHGheb|text=שׁרשׁ|translate=to put forth roots}}, &c.; so also according to the ordinary acceptation {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽאֶזְנִ֫יחוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=6}}, ''they have become stinking'', from {{GHGheb|text=אֶזְנָח|translate=stinking}} or ''stench'', with retention of the {{GHGheb|text=א}} prosthetic, {{GHGpar|19|m}} (but see below, p).<section end=par53 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

170.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par53" />Of a different kind are the ''denominatives'' from: {{GHGheb|text=אזן}} (scarcely ''to prick up the ears'', but) ''to act with the ears, to hear''; cf. {{GHGheb|text=לשׁן|translate=to move the tongue, to slander}}, and the German ''äugeln'' (to make eyes), ''füsseln, näseln, schwänzeln''; {{GHGheb|text=שׁבר|translate=to sell corn}}; {{GHGheb|text=שׁכם|translate=to set out early}} (to lead the back [of the camel, &c.]?); opposed to {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽעֱרִיב}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|h}}
'''3.''' The meaning of {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} is (''a'') primarily that of a {{GHGterm|passive}} of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁלִיךְ|translate=proiecit}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָשְׁלַךְ}} or {{GHGheb|text=הֻשְׁלַךְ|translate=proiectus est}}; (''b'') sometimes equivalent to a passive of {{GHGterm|Qal}}, as {{GHGheb|text=נָקַם|translate=to avenge}}, Hoph. ''to be avenged'' (but see below, u).

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|i}}
Rem. 1. The ''î'' of the 3rd sing. masc. perf. {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} remains, without exception, in the 3rd fem. (in the tone-syllable). That it was, however, only lengthened from a short vowel, and consequently is changeable, is proved by the forms of the {{GHGterm|imperative}} and {{GHGterm|imperfect}} where ''ē'' (or, under the influence of gutturals, ''ă'') takes its place. In an open syllable the ''î'' is retained almost throughout; only in very isolated instances has it been weakened to {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} (see n and o).

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|k}}
2. The {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} commonly has {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} without ''Yodh'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַקְדֵּשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=17|verse=3}}; less frequently it takes {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַשְׁמֵיד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=9|verse=8}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=15|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=32|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=44|verse=25|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=35}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=10|verse=10}}. With {{GHGheb|text=א}} instead of {{GHGheb|text=ה}} (probably a mere scribal error, not an Aramaism) we find {{GHGheb|text=אַשְׁכֵּים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=25|verse=3}}. Rare exceptions, where the form with {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} stands for the {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}}, are, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=8}} (Sam; {{GHGheb|text=בְּהַנְחִיל}}; read perhaps {{GHGheb|text=בְּהַנְחִל}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=44|verse=19.25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=3}} (?); on the other hand, for {{GHGheb|text=לַעְשְׂר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=26|verse=12}} (which looks like an infinitive Hiphʿîl with elision of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, for {{GHGheb|text=לְהַֽעֲשִׂיר}}) the right reading is simply {{GHGheb|text=לְעַשֵּׂר}}, since elsewhere the Piʿēl alone occurs with the meaning ''to tithe''; for {{GHGheb|text=בַּעְשֵׂר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=10|verse=39}} perhaps the inf. Qal ({{GHGheb|text=בַּעְשׂר}}) was intended, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=8|verse=15.17}} (=''to take the tithe''). At the same time it is doubtful whether the present punctuation does not arise from a conflation of two different readings, the Qal and the Piʿēl.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|l}}
Instead of the ordinary form of the {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} {{GHGheb|text=הַקְטִיל}} the form {{GHGheb|text=הִקְטִיל}} sometimes occurs, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁמִיד|translate=to destroy}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=7|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=48|hidebook=1}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=14|verse=46}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=11|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=50|verse=34}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=51|verse=33|hidebook=1}} and {{GHGheb|text=הִקְצוֹת}} for {{GHGheb|text=הַקְצוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=14|verse=43}} from {{GHGheb|text=קָצָה}}; scarcely, however, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=7|verse=35}} (see {{GHGpar|155|l}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=22|verse=1}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=1}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=16}} (after {{GHGheb|text=עַד}}), and in the passages so explained by König (i. 276) where {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁאִיר}} appears after prepositions<ref>As to the doubtfulness, on general grounds, of this form of the Inf. Hiph., see Robertson Smith in the {{GHGcite|title=Journ. of Philol.}}, xvi. p. 72 f.</ref>; [cf. Driver on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=3|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=15|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=7|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=55|hidebook=1}}].

With ''ă'' in the second syllable there occurs {{GHGheb|text=הַזְכַּרְכֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=29}} (cf. the substantival infin. {{GHGheb|text=הַפְצַ֑ר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=23}}).—In the Aram. manner {{GHGheb|text=לְהַשְׁמָעוּת}} is found in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=24|verse=26}} (as a construct form) for the {{GHGterm|infinitive Hiphʿîl}} (cf. the {{GHGterm|infinitive Hithpa‛el}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=11|verse=23}}). On the elision of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} after prefixes, see q.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|m}}
3. In the {{GHGterm|imperative}} the ''î'' is retained throughout in the open syllable, according to ''i'', and consequently also before suffixes (see {{GHGpar|61|g}}) and {{GHGheb|text=־ָה|translate=paragogic}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַקְשִׁ֫יבָה|translate=attend to}}, {{GHGheb|text=הוֹשִׁ֫יעָה נָּא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=25}}, as in ed. Mant., Jabl;, Baer, not {{GHGheb|text=הוֹשִׁיעָ֫ה נָּא}} as Ginsb. and Kittel; with the tone at the end only {{GHGheb|text=הַצְלְיחָה}} ibid. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=25b|hidebook=v}}. On the other hand, in the 2nd sing. masc. the original ''ĭ'' (cf. Arabic ''’áqtĭl'') is lengthened to ''ē'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַשְׁמֵן|translate=make fat}}, and becomes ''Se<sup>e</sup>ghôl'' before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַסְכֶּן־נָא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=21}}.—The form {{GHGheb|text=הַקְטִיל}} for {{GHGheb|text=הַקְטֵל}} appears anomalously a few times: {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=94|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=18}} (cf. {{GHGpar|69|v}} and {{GHGpar|72|y}}); elsewhere the Masora has preferred the punctuation {{GHGheb|text=הַקְטֵיל}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=8|verse=6}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=142|verse=5}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=5|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=הַבִּ֫יטָה}} is required by the {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} for {{GHGheb|text=הביט}}.<section end="par53" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

171.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par53 />{{GHGmargin-letter|53|n}}
4. In the {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} the ''shorter'' form with {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} prevails for the jussive in the 3''rd masc.'' and {{GHGterm|fem.}} and 2''nd masc. sing.'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תַּגְדֵּל|translate=make not great}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ob|chapter=1|verse=12}}; {{GHGheb|text=יַכְרֵת|translate=let Him cut off!}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=12|verse=4}}; even incorrectly {{GHGheb|text=תַּגֵּיד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=19|verse=3}} and {{GHGheb|text=יַגֵּיד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=10|verse=20}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=יַבְעֶר־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=22|verse=4}}, where the jussive form is to be explained according to {{GHGpar|109|h}}, and {{GHGheb|text=יַֽאֲבֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=39|verse=26}} before the principal pause. Similarly, after {{GHGheb|text=ו}} consec., e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּבְדֵּל|translate=and He divided}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=4}}. On the other hand, ''î'' is almost always retained in the 1st sing., e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וָאַֽשְׁמִיד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=2|verse=9}} (but generally without {{GHGheb|text=י}}, as {{GHGheb|text=וָאַֽסְתִּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=39|verse=23}} f., &c.); cf. {{GHGpar|49|e}} and {{GHGpar|74|l}}, but also {{GHGpar|72|aa}}; in 1st plur. only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=4|verse=3}}; in the 3rd sing. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=105|verse=28}}. With ''ă'' in the principal pause {{GHGheb|text=וַתּוֹתַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=14}}, and in the lesser pause, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=4}}; before a sibilant (see {{GHGpar|29|q}}) {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּגַּשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=19}}; in the lesser pause {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּקַּף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=3|verse=5}}. Before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} the Ṣere becomes {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּֽחֲזֶק־בּוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=4}}. In the plural again, and before suffixes, ''î'' remains in the forms {{GHGheb|text=יַקְטִ֫ילוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּקְטִ֫ילוּ}}, even in the jussive and after {{GHGheb|text=ו}} consecutive, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּדְבִּ֫יקוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=18|verse=22}}. The only exceptions, where the ''î'' is weakened to {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, are {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּדְרְכוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּדְבְּקוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=31|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=10|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעַבְרוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=11|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאוֹצְרָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=13|verse=13}}, if it is {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} of {{GHGheb|text=אצר}}, but probably {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֲצַוֶּה}} is to be read, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=7|verse=2|hidebook=1}}; perhaps also {{GHGheb|text=תַּהְכְּרוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=3}} (according to others, {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}}). The same weakening occurs also in the imperfect in 3rd and masc. sing. before suffixes, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=65|verse=10}}, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=20}}, unless the form be {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}={{GHGheb|text=וַיְעַקְשֵׁנִי}}, since the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} is not found elsewhere. It is hardly likely that in these isolated examples we have a trace of the ground-form, ''yaqtĭl'', or an Aramaism. More probably they are due partly to a misunderstanding of the defective writing, which is found, by a purely orthographic licence, in numerous other cases (even in 3rd sing. {{GHGheb|text=יַשְׁלִ֑ם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=44|verse=28}}), and partly are intended, as ''formae mixtae'', to combine the forms of {{GHGterm|Qal}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}. Instead of the firmly closed syllable, the Masora requires in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=תַּֽדְשֵׁא}}, with euphonic Ga‛ya (see {{GHGpar|16|h}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|o}}
5. In the {{GHGterm|participle}}, {{GHGheb|text=מ֫וֹצֵא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=135|verse=7}} appears to be traceable to the ground-form, ''maqtĭl''; yet the Ṣere may also possibly be explained by the retraction of the tone. The Masora appears to require the weakening of the vowel to {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} (see above, n) in {{GHGheb|text=מַהְלְכִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=3|verse=7}} (probably, however, {{GHGheb|text=מַֽהֲלָכִים}} should be read), also in {{GHGheb|text=מַחְלְמִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=29|verse=8}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַעְזְרִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=28|verse=23}} (but as {{GHGheb|text=ם}} precedes, and accordingly dittography may well have taken place, the participle Qal is probably to be read in both places; the reading of the text is perhaps again intended to combine {{GHGterm|Qal}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, see above, n), and in the {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} {{GHGheb|text=מַחְצְרִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=15|verse=24}} &c. (where the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} {{GHGheb|text=מַֽחֲצֹֽצְרִים}} is better).—The fem. is ordinarily pointed as {{GHGheb|text=מַזְכֶּ֫רֶת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=15}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַשֶּׂגֶת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=14|verse=21}}; in pause {{GHGheb|text=מַשְׂכָּֽלֶת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=19|verse=14}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|p}}
6. In the {{GHGterm|perfect}} there occur occasionally such forms as {{GHGheb|text=הֶכְלַ֫מְנוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=7}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=17|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=29|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=6|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=7}}; with the original ''ă'' in the first syllable {{GHGheb|text=וְהַרְאֵיתִ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=5}}.—In {{GHGheb|text=אֶגְאָֽלְתִּי}}<ref>Most probably, however, {{GHGheb|text=גֵּאָ֫לְתִּי}} ({{GHGterm|perfect Piʿēl}}) is to be read, and the {{GHGheb|text=א}} is only an indication of the change of the {{GHGterm|perfect}} into the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}, as also previously, by a change of punctuation, {{GHGheb|text=וְאדרכם}} and {{GHGheb|text=וְיֵז}} (instead of {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֶדְ׳}} and {{GHGheb|text=וָיֵּז}}) are made future instead of past. Jewish exegesis applied these Edomoracles to the Roman (i.e. Christian) empire. So G. Moore in ''Theol. Literaturzeitung'', 1887, col. 292.</ref> ''I have stained'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=63|verse=3}}, {{GHGheb|text=א}} stands at the beginning instead of {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, cf. above, k, on {{GHGheb|text=אַשְׁכֵּים}}. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=וְהֶֽאֶזְנִ֫יחוּ}}<section end=par53 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

172.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par53 />{{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=6}} (see above, g) is a mere error of the scribe, who had the Aramaic form in mind and corrected it by prefixing {{GHGheb|text=ה}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|q}}
7. In the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} and {{GHGterm|participle}} the characteristic {{GHGheb|text=ה}} is regularly elided after the preformatives, thus {{GHGheb|text=יַקְמִיל}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַקְמִיל}}; but it is retained in the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} after prepositions, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לְהַקְמִיל}}. The exceptions are in the imperfect, {{GHGheb|text=יְהוֹשִׁיעַ|translate=He will save}} for {{GHGheb|text=יוֹשִׁיעַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=47}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=116|verse=6}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}}); {{GHGheb|text=יְהוֹדֶה|translate=He will praise}} for {{GHGheb|text=יוֹדֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=11|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=28|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=45|verse=18|hidebook=1}} (cf. the proper name {{GHGheb|text=יְהוּכַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=37|verse=3}}, for which {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=38|verse=1|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=יוּכַל}} [and {{GHGheb|text=יְהוֹסֵף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=81|verse=6}}); [{{GHGheb|text=יְהֵילִילוּ}} ({{GHGpar|70|d}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=52|verse=5}}, {{GHGheb|text=יְהָתֵ֫לּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=4}}, {{GHGheb|text=תְּהָתֵ֫לּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=9}}] and {{GHGheb|text=מְהֻקְצָעוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=46|verse=22}}; in the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} (where, however, as in {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, {{GHGpar|51|l}}, the {{GHGterm|infinitive Qal}} is generally to be read) {{GHGheb|text=לַסְתִּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=15}} for {{GHGheb|text=לְהַסְתִּיר}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַנְפִּל}} and {{GHGheb|text=לַצְבּוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַֽעֲבִיר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַֽהֲלִק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=37|verse=12}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַֽחֲטִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=5|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַלְבֵּן}} (doubly anomalous for {{GHGheb|text=לְהַלְבִּין}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=11|verse=35}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַשְׁמִעַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=26|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַֽאֲדִיב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=33}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַשְׁמִד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=וְלַשְׁבִּית}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=8|verse=4}} (certainly corrupt); {{GHGheb|text=בָּעִיר}} for {{GHGheb|text=בְּהָעִיר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=20}} (but ''in the city'' is probably meant); {{GHGheb|text=לָבִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=39|verse=7}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=31|verse=10}}); {{GHGheb|text=לַמְרוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=78|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַנְחוֹתָם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=13|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=כַּנְּלוֹת}} (see, however, {{GHGpar|20|h}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַרְאֹֽתְכֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=33}}: cf. further, from verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=27|verse=20}}; on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=26|verse=12}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=10|verse=39}}, see above, k; for {{GHGheb|text=לַמְחוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=31|verse=3}} read {{GHGheb|text=לְמֹחוֹת}} or {{GHGheb|text=לִמְמַחוֹת}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|r}}
8. With regard to the tone it is to be observed that the afformatives {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} in Hiphʿîl have ''not'' the tone, even in the {{GHGterm|perfect}} with ''waw consecutive'' (except in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=33}} before {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=15|verse=29}} before {{GHGheb|text=א}}, to avoid a hiatus); but the plural ending {{GHGheb|text=וּן}} (see {{GHGpar|47|m}}) always has the tone, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תַּקִרִב֫וּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=17}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|s}}
9. The passive (Hophʿal) has ''ŭ'' instead of Qameṣ ḥaṭuph in the first syllable ({{GHGheb|text=הֻקְטַל}}), in the strong verb less frequently in the perfect and infinitive, but generally in the participle, through the influence of the initial {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}} (but cf. {{GHGheb|text=מָשְׁחָת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=26}}); e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֻשְׁכַּב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=32|verse=32}} (beside {{GHGheb|text=הָשְׁכְּבָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=32|verse=19|hidebook=1}}); {{GHGheb|text=הֻשְׁלַךְ}} {{GHGterm|impf.}} {{GHGheb|text=יֻשְׁלַךְ}}, ''part.'' {{GHGheb|text=מֻשְׁלָךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=21}} (beside {{GHGheb|text=הָשְׁלַכְתָּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=19}}) {{GHGheb|text=הֻמְלַ֫חַתְּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=4}}; in the partic. Hoph. without elision of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}}: {{GHGheb|text=מְהֻקְצָעוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=46|verse=22}}; on the other hand, verbs {{GHGheb|text=פּ״ן}} always have ''ŭ'' (in a sharpened syllable): {{GHGheb|text=הֻגַּד}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֻגַּד}} (cf. {{GHGpar|9|n}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|t}}
10. The {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} has in {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} (as in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}) {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} in the last syllable, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הָחְתֵּל}} and {{GHGheb|text=הָמְלֵחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֻגֵּד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=9|verse=24}}. An {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} does not occur in the strong verb.

11. With regard to the {{GHGterm|imperative Hophʿal}}, see above, {{GHGpar|46|a}}, note.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|u}}
12. According to Böttcher ({{GHGcite|title=Ausführliches Lehrbuch}}, § 906) and Barth (see above, {{GHGpar|52|e}}) a number of supposed imperfects Hophʿal are, in fact, imperfects of the passive of {{GHGterm|Qal}}. As in the case of the perfects passive of Qal (see above, {{GHGpar|52|e}}) the question is again of verbs of which neither the corresponding causative (i.e. here the Hiphʿîl), nor the other tense of the same conjugation (i.e. here the perfect Hophʿal) is found; so with {{GHGheb|text=יֻקַּם}} (for {{GHGheb|text=יֻנְקַם}}, cf. ''yuqtălŭ'' as imperfect Qal in Arabic) and {{GHGheb|text=יֻתַּן}}, from {{GHGheb|text=נָקַם}} and {{GHGheb|text=נָתַן}}; {{GHGheb|text=יֻקַּח}} from {{GHGheb|text=לָקַח}} (cf. {{GHGpar|66|g}}); {{GHGheb|text=יוּאָר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=6}} from {{GHGheb|text=אָרַר}}; {{GHGheb|text=יֻחַן}} from {{GHGheb|text=חָנַן}}; {{GHGheb|text=יוּשָּׁ֑ד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=10|verse=14}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=1}}) from {{GHGheb|text=שָׁדַד}}; Barth adds the verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}}: {{GHGheb|text=תֻּתַּשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=19|verse=12}} from {{GHGheb|text=נתשׁ}}; {{GHGheb|text=יֻתָּץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lev|chapter=11|verse=35}} from {{GHGheb|text=נתץ}}; the verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}: {{GHGheb|text=יֻחָ֫קוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=23}} from {{GHGheb|text=חקק}}; {{GHGheb|text=יֻכַּת}} &c. from {{GHGheb|text=כּתת}}; the verb {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}: {{GHGheb|text=יוּדַשׁ}} from {{GHGheb|text=דּוּשׁ}}; the verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״י}}: {{GHGheb|text=יוּחָ֫ל}}, {{GHGheb|text=יוּשַׁר}}, {{GHGheb|text=יוּשַׁת}} from {{GHGheb|text=חִיל}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁיר}} and {{GHGheb|text=שִׁית}}. On {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫ישֶׂם}} &c., {{GHGpar|73|f}}. In point of fact it would be very strange, especially in the case of {{GHGheb|text=יֻתַּן}} and {{GHGheb|text=יֻקַּח}}, that of these frequently used verbs,<section end=par53 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

173.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par53 />amongst all the forms of Hiphʿîl and Hophʿal, only the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} Hophʿal should have been preserved. A passive of Qal is also indicated in the Tellel-Amarna letters, according to Knudtzon, by a number of imperfect forms, which are undoubtedly due to Canaanite influence, cf. ''Beitr. zur Assyriologie'', iv. 410.<section end=par53 />

<section begin=par54 />{{GHGpar-heading|54|Hithpaʿēl}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|54|a}}
'''1.''' The {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}}<ref>A. Stein, {{GHGcite|title=Der Stamm des Hithpael im Hebr.}} pt. 1, Schwerin, 1893, gives alphabetical statistics of the 1151 forms.</ref> is connected with {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, being formed by prefixing to the {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}-stem (''qaṭṭēl, qaṭṭal'') the syllable {{GHGheb|text=הִתְ}} (Western Aramaic {{GHGheb|text=אִתְ}}, but in Biblical Aramaic {{GHGheb|text=הִתְ}}; Syr. ''’et''<ref>So also in Hebrew {{GHGheb|text=אֶתְחַבַּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=20|verse=35}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=76|verse=6}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֶשְׁתּוֹלְלוּ}}).</ref>
). Like the preformative {{GHGheb|text=(הִנְ‍) נ‍}} of {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִתְ}} has also a reflexive force.

{{GHGmargin-letter|54|b}}
'''2.''' The {{GHGheb|text=ת}} of the prefix in this conjugation, as also in {{GHGterm|Hothpaʿal}} (see h), ''Hithpôēl, Hithpa‛lēl'' and ''Hithpalpel'' (§ 55), under certain circumstances, suffers the following changes:

(''a'') When the stem begins with one of the harder sibilants {{GHGheb|text=ס}}, {{GHGheb|text=צ‍}}, or {{GHGheb|text=ש}}, the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} and the sibilant change places (cf. on this ''metathesis'', {{GHGpar|19|n}}), and at the same time the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} after a {{GHGheb|text=צ‍}} becomes the corresponding emphatic {{GHGheb|text=ט}}: thus {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁתַּמֵּר|translate=to take heed to oneself}}, for {{GHGheb|text=הִתְשַׁמֵּר}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִסְתַּבֵּל|translate=to become burdensome}}, for {{GHGheb|text=הִתְסַבֵּל}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִצְטַדֵּק|translate=to justify oneself}}, from {{GHGheb|text=צָדַק}}. The only exception is in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=3}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְהִתְשׁוֹטַ֫טְנָה}}, to avoid the cacophony of three successive ''t''-sounds.

{{GHGmargin-letter|54|c}}
(''b'') When the stem begins with a ''d''- or ''t''-sound ({{GHGheb|text=ד}}, {{GHGheb|text=ט}}, {{GHGheb|text=ת}}), the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} of the preformative is assimilated to it ({{GHGpar|19|d}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מִדַּבֵּר|translate=speaking, conversing}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִדַּכָּא|translate=to be crushed}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִטַּהֵר|translate=to purify oneself}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִטַּמֵּא|translate=to defile oneself}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִתַּמֵּם|translate=to act uprightly}}. (An exception occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=22}}.) The assimilation of the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} occurs also with {{GHGheb|text=נ‍}} and {{GHGheb|text=כ‍}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִנַּבֵּא|translate=to prophesy}}, as well as {{GHGheb|text=הִתְנַבֵּא}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=24|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=5|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=11|verse=14}}); {{GHGheb|text=תִּכַּוֹנֵן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=27}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=54|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=59|verse=5}}); {{GHGheb|text=תִּכַּסֶּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=26|verse=26}}; with {{GHGheb|text=שׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=7|verse=16}} with {{GHGheb|text=ר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=10}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|54|d}}
Rem. Metathesis would likewise be expected, as in the cases under ''b'', when {{GHGheb|text=ת}} and {{GHGheb|text=ז}} come together, as well as a change of {{GHGheb|text=ת}} to {{GHGheb|text=ד}}. Instead of this, in the only instance of the kind ({{GHGheb|text=הִזַּכּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=16}}) the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} is assimilated to the {{GHGheb|text=ז}}, —unless indeed {{GHGheb|text=הִזַּ֫כּוּ}}, {{GHGterm|imperative Niphʿal}} of {{GHGheb|text=זכך}}, is intended.

'''3.''' As in form, so also in meaning, {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} is primarily (''a'') {{GHGterm|reflexive}} of ''Piēl'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִתְאַזֵּר|translate=to gird oneself}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִתְקַדֵּשׁ|translate=to sanctify oneself}}. Although in these examples the intensive meaning is not distinctly marked, it is so in other cases, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִתְנַקֵּם|translate=to how oneself revengeful}} (''Niph.'' simply ''to take revenge''), and in the numerous instances where the {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} expresses ''to make oneself'' that which is predicated by the stem, ''to conduct oneself'' as such, ''to show oneself, to imagine oneself, to ''<section end=par54 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

174.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par54 />''affect'' to be of a certain character. E.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִתְנַּדֵּל|translate=to make oneself great, to act proudly}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְחַכֵּם|translate=to show oneself wise, crafty}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְחַלָּה|translate=to pretend to be ill}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְעַשֵּׁר|translate=to make}}, i.e. ''to feign oneself rich''; {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׂתָּרֵר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=16|verse=13}}, ''to make oneself a prince''; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְנַבֵּא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=10}}, ''to act in an excited manner like a prophet, to rave''. The meaning of {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} sometimes coincides with that of {{GHGterm|Qal}}, both forms being in use together, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אָבַל|translate=to mourn}}, in Qal only in poetic style, in {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} in prose. On the accusative after Hithpaʿēl (regarded as a transitive verb), see {{GHGpar|117|w}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|54|f}}
(''b'') It expresses ''reciprocal'' action, like {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, {{GHGpar|51|d}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִתְרָאָה|translate=to look upon one another}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=1}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=41|verse=8}}; —but

(''c'') It more often indicates an action less directly affecting the subject, and describes it as performed ''with regard to'' or ''for'' oneself, in one’s own special interest (cf. {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, {{GHGpar|51|e}}).
