Hithpaʿēl in such cases readily takes an accusative, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִתְפָּרֵק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=3}} and {{GHGheb|text=הִתְנַצֵּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=6}} ''to tear off from oneself''; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְפַּשֵּׁט|translate=exuit sibi}} (''vestem''), {{GHGheb|text=הִתְפַּתַּח|translate=solvit sibi}} (''vincula''); {{GHGheb|text=הִצְטַיֵּד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=9|verse=12}}, ''to take'' (''something'') ''as one’s provision''; without an accusative, {{GHGheb|text=הִתְהַלֵּךְ|translate=to walk about for oneself}} (''ambulare''); {{GHGheb|text=הִתְפַּלֵּל|translate=sibi intercedere}} (see Delitzsch on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=15}}); {{GHGheb|text=הִתְחַקָּה|translate=to draw a line for oneself}}, Job {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=13|verse=27|hidebook=1}}; on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=2}}, see § 57, note.

{{GHGmargin-letter|54|g}}
(''d'') Only seldom is it {{GHGterm|passive}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִיא תִתְהַלָּֽל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=31|verse=30}} ''she shall be praised''; {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁתַּכַּח|translate=to be forgotten}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=8|verse=10}}, where the reflexive sense (''to bring oneself into oblivion'') has altogether disappeared. Cf. Niphʿal, {{GHGpar|51|f}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|54|h}}
The passive form {{GHGterm|Hothpaʿal}} is found only in the few following examples: {{GHGheb|text=הֻטַּמָּא|translate=to be defiled}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=24|verse=4}}; {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=הֻכַּבֵּס|translate=to be washed}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=13|verse=55.56}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֻדַּ֫שְׁנָה}} (for {{GHGheb|text=הֻתְדַּשְׁנָה}}, the {{GHGheb|text=נָה}} being treated as if it were the afformative of the ''fem. plur.'') ''it is made fat'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=34|verse=6}}. On {{GHGheb|text=הָתְפָּֽקְדוּ}}, see l.

{{GHGmargin-letter|54|i}}
Denominatives with a reflexive meaning are {{GHGheb|text=הִתְיַהֵד|translate=to embrace Judaism}}, from {{GHGheb|text=(יְהוּדָה) יְהוּד|translate=Judah}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִצְטַיֵּד|translate=to provision oneself for a journey}}, from {{GHGheb|text=צֵידָה|translate=provision for a journey}} (see {{GHGpar|72|m}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|54|k}}
Rem. 1. As in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, so in {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}}, the perfect very frequently (in stems ending in {{GHGheb|text=ג}}, {{GHGheb|text=ק}}, {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}}, {{GHGheb|text=פ}}) has retained the original {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} in the final syllable (while in the ordinary form it is attenuated, as in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, to ''ĭ'' and then lengthened to ''ē''), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִתְאַנַּף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=21}}, &c.; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=13|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=15|verse=8|hidebook=1}}; with {{GHGheb|text=וְ|translate=consecutive}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=21}}; so also in the imperfect and imperative, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תִּתְחַכַּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=7|verse=16}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=9|verse=8.18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=10|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=55|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=58|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=64|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=55|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְחַזַּק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=37|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=5|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=וָאֶֽתְאַפַּק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=12}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=11|verse=44}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=20|verse=7|hidebook=1}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=38|verse=23}}, ''ĭ'' takes the place of ''ă'' in the final syllable of the stem before {{GHGheb|text=שׁ}} (cf. {{GHGpar|44|d}}), and in the last passage before {{GHGheb|text=ל}}. In the ''perfect, imperfect'' (with the exception of {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=7|verse=16}}), and {{GHGterm|imperative}} of {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} (as well as of ''Hithpô‛ēl, Hithpa‛lēl, Hithpalpēl'', § 55) the original ''ă'' always returns in {{GHGterm|pause}} as {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִתְאַזָּרָ֑}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=93|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִתְאַבָּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=7|verse=27}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִתְהַלָּךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=18|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִתְלַכָּֽדוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=30|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְקַדָּ֑שׁוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=3|verse=5}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=33|verse=5}} and {{GHGpar|74|b}}.—The ''ā'' also appears before the fuller ending {{GHGheb|text=וּן}} in the plural of the imperfect (cf. {{GHGpar|47|m}}) in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=12|verse=9}}, Jb<section end=par54 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

175.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par54" />9:6, 16:10.—Like the {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=תְּקַטַּ֫לְנָה}} ({{GHGpar|52|n}}), forms occur in {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} like {{GHGheb|text=תִּתְהַלַּ֫כְנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=6|verse=7}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=8|verse=13}}, and so in ''Hithpoʿēl'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=9|verse=13}}; with ''ē'' only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=4|verse=1}}.—In the Aramaic manner an {{GHGterm|infinitive Hithpaʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִתְחַבְּרוּת}} occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=11|verse=23}} (cf. the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} inf. {{GHGheb|text=הַשְׁמָעוּת}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=24|verse=26}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|54|l}}
2. As instances of the {{GHGterm|reflexive}} {{GHGheb|text=הִתְקַטֵּל}} (connected with {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}) a few reflexive forms of the verb {{GHGheb|text=פָּקַד}} (''to examine'') are also probably to be reckoned. Instead of a {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} in a sharpened syllable after the first radical, these take {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} in an open syllable, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִתְפָּֽקְדוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=15.17}}, {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יִתְפָּקֵד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=15|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=21|verse=9|hidebook=1}}. The corresponding passive form {{GHGheb|text=הָתְפָּֽקְדוּ}} also occurs four times, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=1|verse=47}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=2|verse=33|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=26|verse=62|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=27}}. According to others, these forms are rather reflexives of {{GHGterm|Qal}}, in the sense of ''to present oneself for review, to be reviewed'', like the Aramaic ''ʾIthpeʿēl'' (Western Aramaic {{GHGheb|text=אִתְקְטֵל}}, Syr. {{GHGheb|text=אֶתְקְטֵל}}) and the Ethiopic ''taqat<sup>e</sup>la'', Arab. ''ʾiqtatala'', the last with the ''t'' always placed after the first radical (cf. above, b); but they are more correctly explained, with König, as {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} forms, the doubling of the {{GHGheb|text=ק}} being abnormally omitted.—Such a reflexive of {{GHGterm|Qal}}, with the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} transposed, occurs in {{GHGheb|text=הלתחם}} (on the analogy of O.T. Hebrew to be pronounced {{GHGheb|text=הִלְתַּחֵם}}) in the inscription of the Moabite king ''Mêšaʿ'', with the meaning of the O.T. {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נִלְחַם|translate=to fight, to wage war}}: see the inscription, lines 11, 15, 19, and 32; in the first two places in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} with {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֶלְתַּחֵם}}; in line 19 in the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} with suffix, {{GHGheb|text=בְּהִלְתַּֽחֲמֹה בִי|translate=in his fighting against me}}.
<section end="par54" />
<section begin="par55" />{{GHGpar-heading|55|Less Common Conjugations}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|55|a}}
Of the less common conjugations ({{GHGpar|39|g}}) some may be classed with {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, others with {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}. To the former belong those which arise from the lengthening of the vowel or the repetition of one or even two radicals, in fact, from an internal modification or development of the stem; to the latter belong those which are formed by prefixing a consonant, like the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}. Amongst the conjugations analogous to {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} are included the {{GHGterm|passive}} forms distinguished by their vowels, as well as the reflexives with the prefix {{GHGheb|text=הִתְ}}, on the analogy of {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|55|b}}
The following conjugations are related to {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, as regards their inflexion and partly in their meaning:

1. {{GHGterm|Pôʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=קוֹטֵל}}, passive ''Pôʿal'' {{GHGheb|text=קוֹטַל}}, reflexive ''Hithpôʿēl'' {{GHGheb|text=הִתְקוֹטֵל}}, corresponding to the Arabic conj. iii. ''qâtălă'', pass. ''qûtĭlă'', and conj. vi. reflexive ''tăqâtălă''; {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יְקוֹטֵל}}, {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=מְקוֹטֵל}}, {{GHGterm|imperfect passive}} {{GHGheb|text=יְקוֹטַל}} &c. Hence it appears that in Hebrew the ''ô'' of the first syllable is in all the forms obscured from ''â'', while the passive form is distinguished simply by the ''a''-sound in the second syllable. In the strong verb these conjugations are rather rare. Examples: {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=מְשֹֽׁפְטִי|translate=mine adversary, who would contend with me}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=טְלֽוֹשְׁנִי}} (denominative from {{GHGheb|text=לָשׁוֹן|translate=the tongue}}) ''slandering'' (as if ''intent on injuring with the tongue'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=101|verse=5}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} (The ''Q<sup>e</sup>ré'' requires {{GHGheb|text=מְלָשְׁנִי}} ''m<sup>e</sup>lŏšnî'' as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=1|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=וּגְדָול־}}); {{GHGheb|text=זֽׄרְמוּ|translate=they have poured out}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=77|verse=18}} (if not rather {{GHGterm|Puʿal}}); {{GHGheb|text=יוֹדַ֫עְתִּי|translate=I have appointed}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=3}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=הוֹדַ֫עְתִּי}} should be read); {{GHGheb|text=יְסֹעֵר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=13|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁרֵשׁ|translate=to take root}}, passive<section end="par55" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

176.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par55 />{{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹרַשׁ}}, ''denominative'' from {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁ֫רֶשׁ|translate=root}} (but {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁרֵשׁ|translate=to root out}}); in Hithpôʿēl {{GHGheb|text=הִתְגּֽׄעֲשׁוּ|translate=they shall be moved}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=25|verse=16}}; imperf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=46|verse=8|hidebook=1}}; from a verb {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹשֵׂ֫תִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=13}}. The {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=מִנֹּאָץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=52|verse=5}} is probably a ''forma mixta'' combining the readings {{GHGheb|text=מְנֹאָץ}} and {{GHGheb|text=מִתְנֹאֵץ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|55|c}}
''Poʿel'' proper (as distinguished from the corresponding conjugations of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} {{GHGpar|67|l}} and {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} {{GHGpar|72|m}}, which take the place of the ordinary causative {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}) expresses an aim or endeavour to perform the action, especially with hostile intent, and is hence called, by Ewald, the stem expressing ''aim'' (Zielstamm), ''endeavour'' (Suche-stamm) or ''attack'' (Angriffs-stamm); cf. the examples given above from {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=101|verse=5}}, and {{GHGheb|text=עוֹיֵן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=9}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} (probably for {{GHGheb|text=מְעוֹיֵן}}, cf. {{GHGpar|52|s}}; {{GHGpar|55|f}}: ''seeking to cast an evil eye'').

With {{GHGheb|text=קוֹטֵל}} is connected the formation of quadriliterals by the insertion of a consonant between the first and second radicals ({{GHGpar|30|p}}, § 56).

{{GHGmargin-letter|55|d}}
2. ''Paʿlēl'', generally with the ''ă'' attenuated to ''ĭ''=''Piʿlēl''<ref>Cf. Wolfensohn, ‘The Piʿlel in Hebrew,’ ''Amer. Journ. of Or. Studies'', xxvii (1907), p. 303 ff.</ref> (''Piʿlal''), {{GHGheb|text=קִטְלֵל}} and {{GHGheb|text=קִטְלַל}}; the ''ē'' in the final syllable also arises from ''ĭ'', and this again from ''ă''; passive ''Puʿlal'' {{GHGheb|text=קֻטְלַל}}, reflexive ''Hithpaʿlēl'' {{GHGheb|text=הִתְקַטְלֵל}}, like the Arabic conjugations ix. ''ʾiqtăllă'' and xi. ''ʾiqtâllă'', the former used of permanent, the latter of accidental or changing conditions, e.g. of colours; cf. {{GHGheb|text=שַֽׁאֲנַן|translate=to be at rest}}, {{GHGheb|text=רַֽעֲנַן|translate=to be green}}, passive {{GHGheb|text=אֻמְלַל|translate=to be withered}}, all of them found only in the {{GHGterm|perfect}} and with no corresponding {{GHGterm|Qal}} form. (For the barbarous form {{GHGheb|text=צִמְּתֻת֫וּנִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=88|verse=17}} read {{GHGheb|text=צִמְתָֽתְנִי}}; for {{GHGheb|text=נִפְלַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=28|verse=23}}, which has manifestly arisen only from confusion with the following {{GHGheb|text=חלל}}, read {{GHGheb|text=נָפַל}}). These forms are more common in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, where they take the place of {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} ({{GHGpar|72|m}}). Cf. also {{GHGpar|75|kk}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|55|e}}
3. ''P<sup>e</sup>ʿalʿal'': {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְטַל}} with repetition of the last two radicals, used of movements repeated in quick succession; e.g. {{GHGheb|text=סְחַרְחַר|translate=to go about quickly, to palpitate}} (of the heart) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=38|verse=11}}, from {{GHGheb|text=סָחַר|translate=to go about}}; passive {{GHGheb|text=חֳמַרְמַר|translate=to be in a ferment, to be heated, to be red}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=2|verse=11|hidebook=1}}. Probably this is also the explanation of {{GHGheb|text=חֲצוֹצַר}} (denom. from {{GHGheb|text=חֲצֽוֹצְרָה|translate=a trumpet}}, but only in the {{GHGterm|participle}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=15|verse=24}} &c. {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}) for {{GHGheb|text=חֲצַרְצַר}}, by absorption of the first {{GHGheb|text=ר}}, lengthening of ''ă'' in the open syllable, and subsequent obscuring of ''ā'' to ''ô''. On the other hand, for the meaningless {{GHGheb|text=אָֽהֲבוּ הֵב֫וּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=4|verse=18}} (which could only be referred to this conjugation if it stood for {{GHGheb|text=אֲהַבְהֲבוּ}}) read {{GHGheb|text=אָֽהֲבוּ}}, and for the equally meaningless {{GHGheb|text=יָפְיָפִ֫יתָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=45|verse=3}} read {{GHGheb|text=יָפִ֫יתָ}}. In both these cases a scribal error (''dittography'') has been perpetuated by the punctuation, which did not venture to alter the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}. On the employment of ''P<sup>e</sup>ʿalʿal'' in the formation of nouns, cf. {{GHGpar|84|n|b}}. Closely related to this form is—

{{GHGmargin-letter|55|f}}
4. ''Pilpēl'' (pass. ''Pŏlpal''), with a strengthening of the two essential radicals in stems {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, and {{GHGheb|text=ע״י}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גִּלְגֵּל|translate=to roll}}, from {{GHGheb|text=גַּל}}={{GHGheb|text=גָּלַל}}; {{GHGterm|reflexive}} {{GHGheb|text=הִתְגַּלְגֵּל|translate=to roll oneself down}}; {{GHGheb|text=כִּלְכֵּל}} from {{GHGheb|text=כּוּל}}, {{GHGterm|passive}} {{GHGheb|text=כָּלְכַּל}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=טֵאטֵא}} (so Baer and Ginsb. after Qimḥi; others {{GHGheb|text=טִאטֵא}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=23}}, and with ''ă'' in both syllables owing to the influence of {{GHGheb|text=ר}}, {{GHGheb|text=קַרְקַר}} from {{GHGheb|text=קוּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=24|verse=17}} (cf. however, in the parallel passage, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=45}} {{GHGheb|text=קָדְקֹד}}) and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=5}}, in the {{GHGterm|participle}}; {{GHGheb|text=שִׂגְשֵׂג}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=11}} ''to hedge in'', acc. to others ''make to grow''. Probably to this form also belongs {{GHGheb|text=יְלַעְלְעוּ}}, the emended reading of {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=39|verse=30}} instead of the impossible {{GHGheb|text=יְעַלְעוּ}}; also<section end=par54 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

177.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par55" />{{GHGheb|text=סַאסְּאָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=8}}, if that form is to be referred to an {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=סַאְסֵא}}; perhaps also {{GHGheb|text=שִׁשֵּׁא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=39|verse=2}} for {{GHGheb|text=שׁאשׁא}}. This form also commonly expresses rapidly repeated movement, which all languages incline to indicate by a repetition of the sound,<ref>Cf. Lat. {{GHGtranslate|tinnio, tintinno}}, our {{GHGtranslate|tick-tack, ding-dong}}, and the German {{GHGtranslate|wirrwarr, klingklang|lang=de}}. The repetition of the radical in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} also produces this effect; as in {{GHGheb|text=לָקַק|translate=to lick}}, {{GHGheb|text=דָּקַק|translate=to pound}}, {{GHGheb|text=טָפֵף|to trip along}}. The same thing is expressed also by {{GHGterm|diminutive}} forms, as in Latin by the termination ''-illo'', e.g. ''cantillo'', in German by ''-eln, -ern'', e.g. ''flimmern, trillern, tröpfeln, to trickle''.</ref> e.g. {{GHGheb|text=צִפְצֵף|translate=to chirp}}; cf. in the Lexicon the nouns derived from {{GHGheb|text=גָּרַר}}, {{GHGheb|text=עוּף}}, and {{GHGheb|text=צָלַל}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|55|g}}
As {{GHGterm|Hithpalpel}} we find {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁתַּקְשְׁקוּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=2|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּתְחַלְחַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=4|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּתְמַרְמַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=8|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=11|verse=11|hidebook=1}}. Of the same form is {{GHGheb|text=אֶדַּדֶּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=38|verse=15}}, if contracted from {{GHGheb|text=אֶתְדַּוְדֶּה}} or {{GHGheb|text=אתדידה}} from the root {{GHGheb|text=דו}} or {{GHGheb|text=די}}), and also {{GHGheb|text=הִתְמַהְמְהוּ|translate=tarry ye}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=9}} (but read probably {{GHGheb|text=הִתַּמְּהוּ}}), {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּתְמַהְמָהּ}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=16}}, &c., if it is to be derived from {{GHGheb|text=מָהַהּ}}, and not Hithpaʿel from {{GHGheb|text=מַהְמַהּ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|55|h}}
Only examples more or less doubtful can be adduced of—

5. {{GHGterm|Tiphʿēl}} (properly {{GHGterm|Taphʿēl}}<ref>The existence of a {{GHGterm|Taphʿēl}} is contested on good grounds by Barth, {{GHGcite|title=Nominalbildung}}, p. 279.</ref>): {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטֵל}}, with {{GHGheb|text=ת}} prefixed, cf. {{GHGheb|text=תִּרְגַּ֫לְתִּי|translate=to teach to walk, to lead}} (denominative from {{GHGheb|text=רֶ֫גֶל|a foot?}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=11|verse=3}}; from a stem {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יְרַֽחֲרֶה|translate=to contend with}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=12|verse=5}}; {{GHGterm|participle}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=15|hidebook=1}} (from {{GHGheb|text=חָרָה|translate=to be hot, eager}}). Similarly in Aramaic, {{GHGheb|text=תַּרְגֵּם|translate=to interpret}}, whence also in Hebrew the ''passive participle'' {{GHGheb|text=מְתֻרְגָּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=4|verse=7}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|55|i}}
6. ''Šaphʿēl'': {{GHGheb|text=שַׁקְטֵל}}, frequent in Syriac, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שַׁלְהֵב}} from {{GHGheb|text=להב|translate=to flame}}; whence in Hebrew {{GHGheb|text=שַׁלְהֶ֫בֶת|translate=flame}}. Perhaps of the same form is {{GHGheb|text=שַׁבְּלוּל|translate=a snail}} (unless it be from the stem {{GHGheb|text=שׁבל}}), and {{GHGheb|text=שְׁקַעֲרוּרֹת|hollow strakes}}, cf. {{GHGpar|85}}, No. 50. This conjugation is perhaps the original of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, in which case the {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, by a phonetic change which may be exemplified elsewhere, is weakened from a sibilant.

{{Asterism}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|55|k}}
Forms of which only isolated examples occur are:—

7. {{GHGheb|text=קִטְלַט}}, {{GHGterm|passive}} {{GHGheb|text=קֻטְלַט}}; as {{GHGheb|text=מְחֻסְפָּס|peeled off, like scales}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=14}}, from {{GHGheb|text=חָסַף}}, {{GHGheb|text=חָשַׂף|translate=to peel, to scale}}.

8. {{GHGheb|text=קַטְקַל}}, in {{GHGheb|text=זַרְזִיף|a rain-storm}}, from {{GHGheb|text=זָרַף}}.

9. {{GHGheb|text=נִתְקַטֵּל}} (regularly in Mishnic Hebrew<ref>[See Segal, {{GHGcite|title=Mišnaic Hebrew}}, Oxf. 1909, p. 30 ff.]</ref>) a form compounded of {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} and {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}}; as {{GHGheb|text=וְנִוַּסְּרוּ}} for {{GHGheb|text=וְנִתְוַסְּרוּ|translate=that they may be taught}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=23|verse=48}}; {{GHGheb|text=נִכַּפֵּר}} probably an error for {{GHGheb|text=הִתְכַּפֵּר|to be forgiven}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=21|verse=8}}. On {{GHGheb|text=נִשְׁתָּֽוָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=27|verse=15}}, see {{GHGpar|75|x}}.
<section end="par55" />
<section begin="par56" />{{GHGpar-heading|56|Quadriliterals}}

On the origin of these altogether secondary formations cf. {{GHGpar|30|p}}. While quadriliteral {{GHGterm|nouns}} are tolerably numerous, only the following examples of the verb occur:
<section end="par56" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

178.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par56" />(''a'') On the analogy of {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}: {{GHGheb|text=כִּרְסֵם|translate=imperfect}}, {{GHGheb|text=יְכַרְסְמֶ֫נָּה|he doth ravage it}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=80|verse=14}} from {{GHGheb|text=כָּסַם}}, cf. {{GHGheb|text=גָּזַם}}. {{GHGterm|Passive}} {{GHGheb|text=רֻֽטֲפַשׁ|to grow fresh again}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=33|verse=25}}. {{GHGterm|Participle}} {{GHGheb|text=מְכֻרְבָּל|girt, clothed}} (cf. Aramaic {{GHGheb|text=כְּבַל|to bind}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=15|verse=27}}. It is usual also to include among the quadriliterals {{GHGheb|text=פַּרְשֵׁז}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=26|verse=9}}, as a {{GHGterm|perfect}} of Aramaic form with {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} not attenuated. It is more correctly, however, regarded, with Delitzsch, as the {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} of a ''Piʿlel'' formation, from {{GHGheb|text=פָּרַשׂ|to spread out}}, with euphonic change of the first {{GHGheb|text=שׂ}} to {{GHGheb|text=שׁ}}, and the second to {{GHGheb|text=ז}}. Moreover, the reading {{GHGheb|text=פַּרְשֵׂז}} also is very well attested, and is adopted by Baer in the text of Job; cf. the Rem. on p. 48 of his edition.

(''b'') On the analogy of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}: {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׂמְאִיל}}, by syncope {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׂמִאיל}} and {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׂמִיל|translate=to turn to the left}} (denom. from {{GHGheb|text=שְׂמֹאל}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=13|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=21}}, &c. On {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽאֶזְנִ֫יחוּ}} cf. {{GHGpar|53|p}}.
<section end="par56" />
<section begin="par57" />{{center|C. Strong Verb with Pronominal Suffixes.<ref>This subject of the verbal suffixes is treated here in connexion with the strong verb, in order that both the forms of the suffixes and the general laws which regulate their union with verbal forms may be clearly seen. The rules which relate to the union of the suffixes with weak verbs will be given under the several classes of those verbs.</ref>}}

{{GHGpar-heading|57}}

The accusative of the personal pronoun, depending on an active verb,<ref>An accusative suffix occurs with {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=109|verse=3}} (since {{GHGheb|text=נִלְחַם}} is used in the sense of {{GHGtranslate|to attack}}), and according to some, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=44|verse=21}}; with {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=2}} ({{GHGheb|text=הִתְנַחֵל}} to appropriate somebody {{GHGtranslate|to oneself as a possession}}); cf. above, {{GHGpar|54|f}}, and {{GHGpar|117|w}}.</ref> may be expressed (1) by a separate word, {{GHGheb|text=אֵת}} the accusative sign (before a suffix {{GHGheb|text=אֶת}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֹת}}) with the pronominal suffix, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קָטַל אֹתוֹ|translate=he has killed him}}; or (2) by a mere suffix, {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלָ֫הוּ}} or {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלוֹ|translate=he has killed him}}. The latter is the usual method ({{GHGpar|33}}), and we are here concerned with it alone.<ref>On the cases where {{GHGheb|text=אֵת}} is necessary, see {{GHGpar|117|e}}.</ref> Neither of these methods, however, is employed when the accusative of the pronoun is {{GHGterm|reflexive}}. In that case a reflexive verb is used, viz. Niphʿal or Hithpaʿēl ({{GHGpar|51|doublesign=1}} and {{GHGpar|54|nosign=1}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִתְקַדֵּשׁ|translate=he sanctified himself}}, not {{GHGheb|text=קִדְּשׁוֹ}}, which could only mean {{GHGtranslate|he sanctified him}}.<ref>The exceptions in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=7|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=34|verse=2.8.10}} are only apparent. In all these instances the sharp antithesis between {{GHGheb|text=אֹתָם}} ({{GHGtranslate|themselves}}) and another object could only be expressed by retaining the same verb; also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=5|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=אֹתָם}} after an active verb serves to emphasize the idea of {{GHGtranslate|themselves}}.</ref>

Two points must be specially considered here: the form of the suffix itself ({{GHGpar|58}}), and the form which the verb takes when suffixes are added to it ({{GHGpar|59|doublesign=1}}–{{GHGpar|61|nosign=1}}).<section end="par57" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

179.text:
{{GHGpar-heading|58|The Pronominal Suffixes of the Verb}} Cf. the statistics collected by H. Petri, {{GHGcite|title=Das Verbum mit Suffixen im Hebr.}}, part ii, in the {{GHGheb|text=נביאים ראשנים}}, Leipzig, 1890. W. Diehl, ''Das Pronomen pers. suff.''... des Hebr., Giessen, 1895. J. Barth, ‘Beiträge zur Suffixlehre des Nordsem.,’ {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|AJSL.|American Journal of Semitic Languages.}}}} xvii (1901), p. 205 f. Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Semit. Sprachwiss.}}, i. 159 f.; {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, p. 638 ff. {{GHGmargin-letter|58|a}} '''1.''' The ''pronominal suffixes'' appended to the verb express the accusative of the ''personal pronoun''. They are the following:—

{{GHGmargin-letter|58|b}} '''2.''' That these suffixes are connected with the corresponding ''forms of the personal pronoun'' (§ 32) is for the most part self-evident, and only a few of them require elucidation. {{GHGmargin-letter|58|c}} The suffixes {{GHGheb|text=נִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=נוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=הוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָ}} (and {{GHGheb|text=ךָ}}, when a long vowel in an open syllable precedes) never have the tone, which always rests on the preceding syllable; on the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=כֶם}} and {{GHGheb|text=הֶם}} always take the tone. {{GHGmargin-letter|58|d}} In the 3rd pers. masc. {{GHGheb|text=־ָ֫ הוּ}}, by contraction of ''a'' and ''u'' after the rejection of the weak {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, frequently gives rise to ''ô'' ({{GHGpar|23|k}}), ordinarily written {{GHGheb|text=וֹ}}, much less frequently {{GHGheb|text=הֹ}} (see {{GHGpar|7|c}}). In the ''feminine'', the suffix {{GHGheb|text=הָ}} should be pronounced with a preceding ''a'' (cf. below, f, note), as {{GHGheb|text=־ָ֫ הָ}} or {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ הָ}}, on the analogy of ''āhû''; instead of {{GHGheb|text=־ָ֫ הָ}}, however, it was simply pronounced {{GHGheb|text=־ָהּ}}, with the rejection of the final vowel,

180.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par58 />and with ''Mappiq'', since the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} is consonantal; but the weakening to {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} is also found, see below, g.

{{GHGmargin-letter|58|e}}
'''3.''' The ''variety'' of the suffix-forms is occasioned chiefly by the fact that they are modified differently according to the form and tense of the verb to which they are attached. For almost every suffix three forms may be distinguished:

(''a'') One beginning with a consonant, as {{GHGheb|text=־֫נִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=־֫הוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=ו}} (only after ''î''), {{GHGheb|text=־֫נוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=ם (הֶם)}}, &c. These are attached to verbal forms which end with a vowel, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִקְטְל֫וּנִי}}; {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתִּ֫יהוּ}}, for which by absorption of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} we also get {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתִּיו}}, pronounced ''q<sup>e</sup>ṭaltîu''; cf. {{GHGpar|8|m}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|58|f}}
(''b'') A second and third with what are called ''connecting vowels''<ref>We have kept the term ''connecting'' vowel, although it is rather a superficial description, and moreover these vowels are of various origin. The connective ''a'' is most probably the remains of the old verbal termination, like the ''i'' in the 2nd pers. {{GHGterm|fem.}} sing. {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתִּ֫יהוּ}}. Observe e.g. the Hebrew form ''q<sup>e</sup>ṭāl-ani'' in connexion with the Arabic ''qatala-ni'', contrasted with Hebrew ''q<sup>e</sup>ṭālat-ni'' and Arabic ''qatalat-ni''. König accordingly prefers the expression ‘vocalic ending of the stem’, instead of ‘connecting syllable’. The connective ''ē'', aŒ¬, as Prätorius ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 55, 267 ff.) and Barth (ibid. p. 205 f.) show by reference to the Syriac connective ''ai'' in the imperf. of the strong verb, is originally due to the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״י}} ({{GHGheb|text=מְחֵנִי}} = {{GHGheb|text=מְחֵינִי}} from ''m<sup>e</sup>ḥainî''), in which the final ''ê'' was used as a connecting vowel first of the imperat., then of the impf. (besides many forms with ''a'', {{GHGpar|60|d}}), and of the infin. and participle.</ref> ({{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫ נִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ נִי}}), used with verbal forms ending with a consonant (for exceptions, see {{GHGpar|59|g}} and {{GHGpar|60|e}}). This ''connecting vowel'' is ''a'' with the forms of the perfect, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלַ֫נִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלָ֫נוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלָם}} (on {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלֵךְ}}, the ordinary form of the 3rd masc. perf. with the 2nd fem. suffix, cf. below, g); and ''e'' (less frequently ''a'') with the forms of the imperfect and imperative, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִקְטְלֵ֫הוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=קָטְלֵם}}; also with the infinitive and participles, when these do not take noun-suffixes (cf. {{GHGpar|61|a}} and h). The form {{GHGheb|text=וֹ}} also belongs to the suffixes of the perfect, since it has arisen from {{GHGheb|text=־ָ֫ הוּ}} (cf., however, {{GHGpar|60|d}}). With {{GHGheb|text=ךָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=כֶם}}, the connecting sound is only a vocal {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, which has arisen from an original short vowel, thus {{GHGheb|text=־ְךָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ְכֶם}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קְטָֽלְךָ}} (''q<sup>e</sup>ṭāl<sup>e</sup>khā''), or when the final consonant of the verb is a guttural, {{GHGheb|text=־ֲךָ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלָֽחֲךָ}}. In {{GHGterm|pause}}, the original short vowel (''ă'') reappears as {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} with the tone {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ ךָ}} (also {{GHGheb|text=־ָ֫ ךְ}}, see g). On the appending of suffixes to the final {{GHGheb|text=וּן}} of the imperfect ({{GHGpar|47|m}}), see {{GHGpar|60|e}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|58|g}}
Rem. 1. As ''rare'' forms may be mentioned ''sing.'' 2nd pers. {{GHGterm|masc.}} {{GHGheb|text=־ְכָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=18|verse=44}}, &c., in {{GHGterm|pause}} also {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ כָּה}} (see below, i); {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=כִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ כִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=103|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=137|verse=6|hidebook=1}}. Instead of the form {{GHGheb|text=־ֵךְ}}, which is usual even in the perfect (e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=27|verse=26}}), {{GHGheb|text=־ָךְ}} occurs as {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=60|verse=9}} (as {{GHGterm|masc.}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=6|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=45|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=55|verse=5|hidebook=1}} always in {{GHGterm|pause}}); with {{GHGterm|Munaḥ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=54|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=37}}.—In the 3''rd masc.'' {{GHGheb|text=הֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=8}}; in the 3''rd fem.'' {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} without {{GHGterm|Mappîq}} (cf. {{GHGpar|91|e}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=44|verse=19}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=1|verse=11}}, with<section end=par58 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

181.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par58" />retraction of the tone before a following tone-syllable, but read certainly {{GHGheb|text=שָׁמַר לָנֶ֫צַח}}.—The forms {{GHGheb|text=־֫מוֹ}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ָ֫ מוֹ}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ מוֹ}} occur 23 times, all in poetry<ref>Thus in Ps 2 {{GHGheb|text=־מוֹ}} occurs five times [four times attached to a noun or preposition, {{GHGpar|91|f|doublesign=1}}, {{GHGpar|103|c|nosign=1}}], and {{GHGheb|text=־ֵם}} only twice.</ref> (except {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=31}}) [viz. with the perfect {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=31|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=6}}; with the imperfect {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=5}} ({{GHGheb|text=מוּ}} for {{GHGheb|text=מוֹ}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=7.9.9.12.15.17.17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=21|verse=10.13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=22|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=45|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=80|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=140|verse=10|hidebook=1}}; with the imperative {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=59|verse=12.12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=83|verse=12|hidebook=1}}]. On the age of these forms, see {{GHGpar|91|l}} 3; on {{GHGheb|text=־ַן}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ָן}} as suffixes of the 3rd fem. plur. of the imperfect, {{GHGpar|60|d}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=48|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=קָֽחֶם־נָא}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּכֶּם־שָׁם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=14|verse=11}} according to Baer), {{GHGheb|text=־ֵם}} has lost the tone before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} and so is shortened to {{GHGheb|text=־ֶם}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=44|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּשִׂימוּן}} is probably only an error for {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּשִׂימוּם}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|58|h}}
2. From a comparison of these verbal suffixes with the noun-suffixes (§ 91) we find that (''a'') there is a greater variety of forms amongst the verbal than amongst the noun-suffixes, the forms and relations of the verb itself being more various;—(''b'') the verbal suffix, where it differs from that of the noun, is longer; cf. e.g. {{GHGheb|text=־֫נִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫ נִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ נִי}} (''me'') with {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} (''my''). The reason is that the pronominal object is less closely connected with the verb than the possessive pronoun (the genitive) is with the noun; consequently the former can also be expressed by a separate word ({{GHGheb|text=את}} in {{GHGheb|text=אֹתִי}}, &c.).

{{GHGmargin-letter|58|i}}
'''4.''' A verbal form with a suffix gains additional strength, and sometimes intentional emphasis, when, instead of the mere connecting vowel, a special connecting-syllable<ref>It is, however, a question whether, instead of a connecting syllable, we should not assume a special verbal form, analogous to the Arabic ''energetic mood'' (see l, at the end) and probably also appearing in the Hebrew cohortative (see the footnote on {{GHGpar|48|c}}).—As M. Lambert has shown in {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} 1903, p. 178 ff. (‘De l’emploi des suffixes pronominaux...’), the suffixes of the 3rd pers. with the impf. without ''waw'' in prose are {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נּוּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נָּה}}, but with ''waw consec.'' {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ הוּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ הָ}} or {{GHGheb|text=־ָהּ}}; with the jussive in the 2nd and 3rd pers. always {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ הוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ ההָ}}, the 1st pers. more often {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נּוּ}} than {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ הוּ}}, and always {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נָּה}}.</ref> (''ăn'')<ref>According to Barth ‘n-haltige Suffixe’ in {{GHGcite|title=Sprachwiss. Untersuchungen}}, Lpz. 1907, p. 1 ff., the connecting element, as in Aramaic, was originally ''in'', which in Hebrew became ''en'' in a closed tone-syllable.</ref> is inserted between the suffix and the verbal stem. Since, however, this syllable always has the tone, the ''ă'' is invariably (except in the 1st pers. sing.) modified to tone-bearing {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}. This is called the ''Nûn energicum''<ref>So König, {{GHGcite|title=Lehrgeb.}}, i. p. 226.</ref> (less suitably ''demonstrativum'' or ''epentheticum''), and occurs principally (see, however, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=10}} ''bis'') in pausal forms of the imperfect, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יְבָֽרֲכֶֽנְהוּ|translate=he will bless him}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=72|verse=15}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=22}}), {{GHGheb|text=אֶתְּקֶ֫נְךָּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=24}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְכַ֫בְּדָ֥נְנִי|translate=he will honour me}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=50|verse=23}}) is unusual; rarely in the perfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=24|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=בֵּֽרְכֶךָּ}}. On examples like {{GHGheb|text=דָּנַ֫נִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=6}}, cf. {{GHGpar|26|g}}, {{GHGpar|59|f}}. In far the greatest number of cases, however, this ''Nûn'' is assimilated to the following consonant ({{GHGheb|text=נ‍}}, {{GHGheb|text=כ‍}}), or the latter is lost in pronunciation (so {{GHGheb|text=ה}}), and the ''Nûn'' consequently sharpened. Hence we get the following series of suffix-forms:—<section end="par58" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

182.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par58 />1''st pers.'' {{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫ נִּי}} (even in pause, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=14}}, &c.), {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נִּי}} (for {{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫ נְנִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נְנִי}}).

2''nd pers.'' {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ ךָּ}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=24}} in pause {{GHGheb|text=־ֶנְךָּ}}) and, only orthographically different,

{{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ כָּה}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=2|verse=11}} in {{GHGterm|pause}}).

3''rd pers.'' {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נּוּ}} (for {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נְהוּ}}),<ref>On {{GHGheb|text=נוֹ}} = {{GHGheb|text=־ֶנּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=13}}, see {{GHGpar|67|o}}.</ref> {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נָּה}} for {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נְהָ}}.

[1''st pers. plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נּוּ}} (for {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נְנוּ}}), see the Rem.]

In the other persons Nûn energetic does not occur.

{{GHGmargin-letter|58|k}}
Rem. The uncontracted forms with ''Nûn'' are rare, and occur only in poetic or elevated style ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=10}} [''bis''], {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=24|hidebook=1}}); they are never found in the 3''rd fem. sing.'' and 1''st plur.'' On the other hand, the contracted forms are tolerably frequent, even in prose. An example of {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נּוּ}} as 1''st plur.'' occurs perhaps in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=15}} [but read {{GHGheb|text=־ֵנוּ}} and cf. {{GHGpar|72|cc}}], hardly in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=12|verse=5}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=הִנֶּ֫נּוּ|translate=behold us}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=50|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=40}} for {{GHGheb|text=הִנְנוּ}} (instead of {{GHGheb|text=הִנְּנוּ}}; see {{GHGpar|20|m}}).—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=4|verse=12}} the Masora requires {{GHGheb|text=תְּעֻגֶ֫נָה}}, without Dageš in the Nûn.

{{GHGmargin-letter|58|l}}
That the forms with ''Nûn energicum'' are intended to give greater emphasis to the verbal form is seen from their special frequency in {{GHGterm|pause}}. Apart from the verb, however, ''Nûn energicum'' occurs also in the union of suffixes with certain particles ({{GHGpar|100|o}}).

This Nûn is frequent in Western Aramaic. In Arabic the corresponding forms are the two ''energetic moods'' (see {{GHGpar|48|b}}) ending in ''an'' and ''anna'', which are used in connexion with suffixes (e.g. ''yaqtulan-ka'' or ''yaqtulanna-ka'') as well as without them.<section end=par58 />

<section begin=par59 />{{GHGpar-heading|59|The Perfect with Pronominal Suffixes}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|59|a}}
'''1.''' The endings (''afformatives'') of the perfect occasionally vary somewhat from the ordinary form, when connected with pronominal suffixes; viz.:—

(''a'') In the 3''rd sing. fem.'' the original feminine ending {{GHGheb|text=־ַת}} or {{GHGheb|text=־ָת}} is used for {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}.

(''b'') In the 2''nd sing. masc.'' besides {{GHGheb|text=תָּ}} we find {{GHGheb|text=תּ}}, to which the connecting vowel is directly attached, but the only clear instances of this are with {{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫ נִי}}.<ref>On the ''ă'' as an original element of the verbal form, see {{GHGpar|58|f}}, note.</ref>

(''c'') In the 2''nd sing. fem.'' {{GHGheb|text=תִּי}}, the original form of {{GHGheb|text=תְּ}}, appears; cf. {{GHGheb|text=אַתִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=קָטַ֫לְתִּי}}, {{GHGpar|32|f}}; {{GHGpar|44|g}}. This form can be distinguished from the 1st pers. only by the context.

(''d'') 2''nd plur. masc.'' {{GHGheb|text=תּוּ}} for {{GHGheb|text=תֶּם}}. The only examples are {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=20|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=7|verse=5}}. The {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתֶּן}} never occurs with suffixes; probably it had the same form as the masculine.

{{GHGmargin-letter|59|b}}
We exhibit first the forms of the perfect {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, as used in connexion with suffixes, since here no further changes take place in the stem itself, except as regards the tone (see c).<section end=par59 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

183.text:
{| cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" border="0" | ''Singular''. | ''Plural''. |- | 3. ''m.'' {{GHGheb|text=הִקְטִיל}} | 3. ''c.'' {{GHGheb|text=הִקְטִילוּ}} |- | 3. ''f.'' {{GHGheb|text=הִקְטִילַת}} | |- | 2. ''m.'' {{GHGheb|text=הִקְטַלְתָּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִקְטַלְתּ}} | 2. ''m.'' {{GHGheb|text=הִקְטַלְתּוּ}} |- | 2. ''f.'' {{GHGheb|text=הִקְטַלְתִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִקְטַלְתּ}} | |- | 1. ''c.'' {{GHGheb|text=הִקְטַלְתִּי}} | 1. ''c.'' {{GHGheb|text=הִקְטַלְנוּ}} |}
The beginner should first practise connecting the suffixes with these {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} forms and then go on to unite them to the {{GHGterm|Perfect Qal}} (see d). {{GHGmargin-letter|59|c}} '''2.''' The addition of the suffix generally causes the tone to be thrown forward towards the end of the word, since it would otherwise fall, in some cases, on the ante-penultima; with the ''heavy'' suffixes (see e) the tone is even transferred to the suffix itself. Considerations of tone, especially in the Perfect {{GHGterm|Qal}}, occasion certain vowel changes: (''a'') the {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} of the first syllable, no longer standing ''before'' the tone, always becomes vocal {{GHGterm|Šewâ}}; (''b'') the original {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} of the second syllable, which in the 3''rd sing. fem.'' and 3''rd plur.'' had become {{GHGterm|Šewâ}}, reappears before the suffix, and, in an open syllable before the tone, is lengthened to {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}}; similarly original ''ĭ'' (as in the 3''rd sing. masc. without'' a suffix) is lengthened to ''ē'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֲהֵב֫וּךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=19|verse=7}}. {{GHGmargin-letter|59|d}} The forms of the perfect of Qal consequently appear as follows:—
{| cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" border="0" | ''Singular''. | ''Plural''. |- | 3. ''m.'' {{GHGheb|text=קְטָל}} | 3. ''c.'' {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלוּ}} |- | 3. ''f.'' {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלַת}} ({{GHGheb|text=קְטָלָת}}, see g) | |- | 2. ''m.'' {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתָּ}} ({{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתּ}}, see h) | 2. ''m.'' {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתּוּ}} |- | colspan="2" | 2. ''f.'' {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתִּי}} ({{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתּ}}, see h) |- | 1. ''c.'' {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתִּי}} | 1. ''c.'' {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְנוּ}} |}
The connexion of these forms with all the suffixes is shown in ''Paradigm C.'' It will be seen there also, how the {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} in the Perfect {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} changes sometimes into {{GHGterm|Seghôl}}, and sometimes into {{GHGterm|vocal Šewâ}}. {{GHGmargin-letter|59|e}} Rem. 1. The suffixes of the 2nd and 3rd pers. plur. {{GHGheb|text=כֶם}} and {{GHGheb|text=הֶם}}, since they end in a consonant and also always have the tone, are distinguished as ''heavy'' suffixes (''suffixa gravia'') from the rest, which are called ''light'' suffixes. Compare the connexion of these (and of the corresponding feminine forms {{GHGheb|text=כֶן}} and {{GHGheb|text=הֶן}}) with the ''noun'', § 91. With a perfect {{GHGheb|text=כֶם}} alone occurs, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=26}}. The form {{GHGheb|text=קְטַל}} which is usually given as the connective form of the 3rd sing. masc. before {{GHGheb|text=כֶם}} and {{GHGheb|text=כֶן}} is only formed by analogy, and is without example in the O.T. {{GHGmargin-letter|59|f}} 2. In the 3''rd sing. masc.'' {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלָ֫הוּ}} (especially in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}; in the strong verb only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=20|verse=15}} in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}) is mostly contracted to {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלוֹ}}, according to {{GHGpar|23|k}}; likewise in the 2nd sing. masc. {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתָּ֫הוּ}} to {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתּוֹ}}.—As a suffix of the 1st sing. {{GHGheb|text=־ָ֫ נִי}} occurs several times with the 3rd sing. masc. perf. Qal of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, not only in {{GHGterm|pause}} (as {{GHGheb|text=עָנָ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=קָנָ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=22}} with {{GHGterm|Deḥi}}), but even with a {{Hyphenated word start|con|conjunctive}}

184.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par59 />{{Hyphenated word end|junctive|conjunctive}} accent, as {{GHGheb|text=הֹרָ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=עָנָ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=15}} (where, however, the reading {{GHGheb|text=עָנַ֫נִי}} is also found). With a sharpened {{GHGheb|text=נ‍}}: {{GHGheb|text=דָּנַ֫נִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=6}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִסְרַ֫נִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=18}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|59|g}}
3. The 3''rd sing. fem.'' {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלַת}} (={{GHGheb|text=קָֽטְלָה}}) has the twofold peculiarity that (''a'') the ending ''ath'' always takes the tone,<ref>{{GHGheb|text=חִבְּלָֽתְךָ֣}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=8|verse=5}} is an exception. {{GHGheb|text=כֶם}} would probably even here have the tone (see e); but no example of the kind occurs in the O.T. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=2}} the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} is used instead of the {{GHGterm|perfect}} with a suffix.</ref> and consequently is joined to those suffixes which form a syllable of themselves ({{GHGheb|text=נִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=ךָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=הוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=נוּ}}), without a connecting vowel, contrary to the general rule, {{GHGpar|58|f}}; (''b'') before the other suffixes the connecting vowel is indeed employed, but the tone is drawn back to the ''penultima'', so that they are pronounced with shortened vowels, viz. {{GHGheb|text=־֫ ־ֶךְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=־֫ ־ַם}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֲהֵבָ֫תֶךְ|translate=she loves thee}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=4|verse=15}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=גְּנָבָ֫תַם|translate=she has stolen them}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=32}}; {{GHGheb|text=שְׂרָפָּ֫תַם|translate=it burns them}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=2|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=48|verse=7}}. For {{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫ תְנִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫ תְךָ}} &c., in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=־ָֽ תְנִי}} is found, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=8|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=69|verse=10}}, and {{GHGheb|text=־ָֽ תְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=8|verse=5}}; and also without the {{GHGterm|pause}} for the sake of the assonance {{GHGheb|text=חִבְּלָֽתְךָ}}, ''she was in travail with thee'', ibid. The form {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלַ֫תּוּ}} (e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=4|verse=15}}) has arisen, through the loss of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} and the consequent sharpening of the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} (as in {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נּוּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נָּה}} for {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נְהוּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ נְהָ}}, cf. {{GHGpar|58|i}}), from the form {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלַ֫תְהוּ}}, which is also found even in {{GHGterm|pause}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֲהֵבַֽתְהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=28}}; elsewhere it takes in {{GHGterm|pause}} the form {{GHGheb|text=סְמָכָֽתְהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=16}}); so {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלַ֫תָּה}} from {{GHGheb|text=קֵטָלַ֫תְהָ}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=34|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=3|verse=6}}; in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=14|verse=15}}, always, on the authority of Qimḥi, without {{GHGterm|Mappîq}} in the {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, which is consequently always a more vowel-letter.

{{GHGmargin-letter|59|h}}
4. In the 2''nd sing. masc.'' the form {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתָּ}} is mostly used, and the suffixes have, therefore, no connecting vowel, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=זְנַחְתָּ֫נוּ פְרַצְתָּ֑נוּ|translate=thou hast cast us off, thou hast broken us down}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=60|verse=3}}; but with the suff. of the 1st sing. the form {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתַּ֫נִי}} is used, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חֲקַרְתַּ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=1}}; in {{GHGterm|pause}}, however, with {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עֲזַבְתָּ֑נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=22|verse=2}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=1|verse=15}} (with {{GHGterm|Zaqeph qaṭon}}); but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=צְרַפְתָּ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=17|verse=3}} with ''Mer<sup>e</sup>kha''.—In the 2''nd sing. fem.'' {{GHGheb|text=־תִּי}}— is also written defectively, {{GHGheb|text=רִמִּיתִ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=35}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=15|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=4|verse=9}}. Occasionally the suffix is appended to the ordinary form {{GHGheb|text=־ְתּ}}, viz. {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁבַּעְתָּ֫נוּ|translate=thou}} ({{GHGterm|fem.}}) ''dost adjure us'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=5|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=17.20}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=27}}, and, quite abnormally, with {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} {{GHGheb|text=הוֹרַדְתֵּ֫נוּ|translate=thou}} ({{GHGterm|fem.}}) ''didst let us down'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=18}}, where {{GHGheb|text=הוֹרַדְתִּ֫נוּ}} would be expected. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=וְיִסְּרֵ֫נִי}} is probably intended as an {{GHGterm|imperfect}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|59|i}}
5. In verbs ''middle ē'', the ''ē'' remains even before suffixes (see above, c), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֲהֵֽבְךָ֫}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=15|verse=16}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲהֵבַ֫תְהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=28}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=22|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְרֵא֫וּהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=37|verse=24}}. From a verb ''middle ō'' there occurs {{GHGheb|text=יְכָלְתִּיו|translate=I have prevailed against him}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=13|verse=5}}, from {{GHGheb|text=יָכֹל}} with ''ŏ'' instead of ''ō'' in a syllable which has lost the tone ({{GHGpar|44|e}}).<section end=par59 />

<section begin=par60 />{{GHGpar-heading|60|Imperfect with Pronominal Suffixes}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|60|a}}
In those forms of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} Qal, which have no afformatives, the vowel ''ō'' of the second syllable mostly becomes {{GHGheb|text=־ְ}} (simple {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ mobile}}), sometimes {{GHGheb|text=־ֳ}}; thus in the principal {{GHGterm|pause}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=35|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=62|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=35|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=10|verse=10}}; before the principal {{GHGterm|pause}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=33}}; before a secondary {{GHGterm|pause}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=17|verse=23}}; even before a conjunctive accent, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=23|verse=5}}. Before {{GHGheb|text=־ְךָ}},<section end=par60 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

185.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par60" />{{GHGheb|text=־ְכֶם}}, however, it is shortened to {{GHGterm|Qameṣ ḥaṭuph}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁמָרְךָ}} (but in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁמְרֶ֫ךָ}} or {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁמְרֶ֫ךָּ}}; with ''Nûn energicum'', see {{GHGpar|58|i}}), {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁמָרְכֶם}}, &c. Instead of {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטֹ֫לְנָה}}, the form {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְטְלוּ}}<ref>This form is also found as feminine without a suffix, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=37|verse=7}}. In the latter passage {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּקְרְבוּ}} is probably to be regarded, with König, as a clumsy correction of the original {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּק׳}}, intended to suggest the reading {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּקְרַ֫בְנָה}}, to agree with the usual gender of {{GHGheb|text=עֲצָמוֹת}}.</ref> is used for the 2nd and 3rd ''fem. plur''. before suffixes in three places: {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=6}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|60|b}}
Rem. 1. {{GHGheb|text=יְחָבְרְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=94|verse=20}} is an anomalous form for {{GHGheb|text=יַחְבָּרְךָ}} (cf. the analogous {{GHGheb|text=יָחְנְךָ}} {{GHGpar|67|n}}) and {{GHGheb|text=יִֽפְגָֽשְׁךָ}} (so Baer; others {{GHGheb|text=יִפְגָּֽשְׁךָ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=18}} for {{GHGheb|text=יִפְגָּֽשֲׁךָ}}. To the same category as {{GHGheb|text=יְחָבְרְךָ}} belong also, according to the usual explanation, {{GHGheb|text=תָּֽעָבְדֵם}} (from {{GHGheb|text=תַּֽעֲבֹד}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=5|verse=9}}, and {{GHGheb|text=נָֽעָב׳}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=13|verse=3}}. As a matter of fact, the explanation of these forms as imperfects of {{GHGterm|Qal}} appears to be required by the last of these passages; yet why has the retraction of the ''ŏ'' taken place only in these examples (beside numerous forms like {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעַבְדֵ֫נִי}})? Could the Masora in the two Decalogues and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=24}} (on the analogy of which {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=13|verse=3}} was then wrongly pointed) have intended an imperfect {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} with the suffix, meaning {{GHGtranslate|thou shalt not allow thyself to be brought to worship them}}?

{{GHGmargin-letter|60|c}}
Verbs which have ''a'' in the second syllable of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}, and imperative, {{GHGterm|Qal}} (to which class especially {{GHGterm|verba tertiae}} and {{GHGterm|mediae gutturalis}} belong, {{GHGpar|64}} and {{GHGpar|65}}) do ''not'', as a rule, change the {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} (nor of the imperative, see {{GHGpar|61|g}}) into {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} before suffixes; but the Pathaḥ, coming to stand in an open syllable before the tone, is lengthened to {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּלְבָּשֵׁ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִגְאָל֫וּהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=5|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּשְׁלָחֵם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=8|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרָאֻ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=145|verse=18}}; but {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרְאוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=6}}, is probably a {{GHGterm|forma mixta|en=mixed form}} combining the readings {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרָאוֹ}} and {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרְאוּ}}, cf. {{GHGpar|74|e}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|60|d}}
2. Not infrequently suffixes with the connecting vowel ''a'' are also found with the imperfect, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תִּדְבָּקַ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=19}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=32|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=24}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=56|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=18}}; also {{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫נִּי}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=19.31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=34|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=21|hidebook=1}} (in principal {{GHGterm|pause}}); {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּכִּירָהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=33}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=11|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=28|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=20|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=יַכִּירָ֑נוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=63|verse=16}} (manifestly owing to the influence of the preceding {{GHGheb|text=יְדָעָ֫נוּ}}); {{GHGheb|text=יִלְבָּשָׁם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=29|verse=30}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=7|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=74|verse=8}}; even {{GHGheb|text=אֲמִילַֽם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=10–12|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיּֽוֹשִׁיעָן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=17}}, and {{GHGheb|text=יְחִיתַֽן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=2|verse=17}} (where, however, the ancient versions read {{GHGheb|text=יְחִתֶּ֫ךָ}}); even {{GHGheb|text=יִרְדְּפוֹ}} (''ô'' from ''āhu'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=8|verse=3}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=22|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=4}} (but read {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּצְפְּנֵם}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=1}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=14|hidebook=1}} (where, however, the text is corrupt); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=6}} (where read with the old versions {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּךְ}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=6}} (see {{GHGpar|74|e}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=4|verse=12}}.—On pausal {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} for {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} in {{GHGheb|text=וַֽאֲבָֽרֲכָֽם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=48|verse=9}} and {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּאַֽלֲצֶ֑הוּ}} (so Baer, but ed. Mant., Ginsb. {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּאַלְצֵ֑הוּ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=16}}, see {{GHGpar|29|q}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|60|e}}
3. Suffixes are also appended in twelve passages to the plural forms in {{GHGheb|text=וּן}}, viz. {{GHGheb|text=תְּדַכְּאוּנַ֫נִי}}, {{GHGtranslate|will ye break me in pieces}}? {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְשָֽׁרְת֑וּנֶךְ}} (here necessarily with a connecting vowel) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=60|verse=7.10}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=5|verse=22}} ({{GHGheb|text=וֹ}} but probably corrupt); elsewhere always without a connecting vowel; {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרָאֻ֫נְנִי}} with two other examples {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=5|verse=15}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=־֫וּנְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=63|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=91|verse=12|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=־ֻ֫נְהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=־֫וּנְהָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=24}}, all in principal pause. [See Böttcher, ''Lehrb.'', § 1047 f.]

{{GHGmargin-letter|60|f}}
4. In {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, {{GHGterm|Pôʿēl}}, and {{GHGterm|Poʿlēl}}, the {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} of the final syllable, like the ''ō'' in Qal, becomes vocal {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}; but before the suffixes {{GHGheb|text=־ְךָ}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ְכֶם}} it is shortened to {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יְקַבֶּצְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=30|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=34|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=2}}. With a final guttural, however, {{GHGheb|text=אֲשַׁלֵּֽחֲךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=27}}; also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=4|verse=8}}, where with Qimḥi {{GHGheb|text=תְּכַבֵּ֫דְךָ}} is to be read. ''ē'' is<section end="par60" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

186.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par60 />retained in the tone-syllable; an analogous case in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} is {{GHGheb|text=וְיַגֵּ֫דְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=7}}. Less frequently {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} is sharpened to {{GHGterm|Ḥireq}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֲאַמִּצְכֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=5}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=31|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=52|verse=12|hidebook=1}}; so in ''Poʿlēl'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=25|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=30|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=37|verse=34|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=145|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, and probably also in {{GHGterm|Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽסִפְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=6}}; cf. {{GHGpar|68|h}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|60|g}}
5. In {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} the ''î'' remains, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תַּלְבִּישֵׁ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=10|verse=11}} (after {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} it is often written defectively, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּלְבִּשֵׁם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=21}} and ofton); but cf. above, {{GHGpar|60|f|nonumber=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=7}}. Forms like {{GHGheb|text=תַּעְשְׁרֶ֫נָּה|translate=thou enrichest it}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=65|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=25}}, are rare. Cf. {{GHGpar|53|n}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|60|h}}
6. Instead of the suffix of the 3rd plur. fem. ({{GHGheb|text=ן}}), the suffix of the 3rd plur. masc. ({{GHGheb|text=ם}}) is affixed to the afformative {{GHGheb|text=וּ}}, to avoid a confusion with the personal ending {{GHGheb|text=וּן}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=וַיְמַלְאוּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=15}} (previously also with a perf. {{GHGheb|text=סִתְּמוּם}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=17}} (where {{GHGheb|text=וַיּֽוֹשִׁעָן}} occurs immediately after); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=39|verse=18.20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=10}} (where also {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵיהֶם}} is for {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵיהֶן}}, a neglect of gender which can only be explained by {{GHGpar|135|o}}).—For {{GHGheb|text=יַֽהַרְגֻן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=11|verse=5}} read perhaps {{GHGheb|text=יַֽהַרְגֵן}} with M. Lambert.<section end=par60 />

<section begin=par61 />{{GHGpar-heading|61|Infinitive, Imperative and Participle with Pronominal Suffixes}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|61|a}}
'''1.''' The {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} of an ''active verb'' may be construed with an accusative, and therefore can also take a {{GHGterm|verbal suffix}}, i.e. the ''accusative'' of the personal pronoun. The only undoubted instances of the kind, however, in the O.T. are infinitives with the verbal suffix of the 1st pers. sing., e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לְדָרְשֵׁ֫נִי|translate=to inquire of me}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=37|verse=7}}. As a rule the infinitive (as a ''noun'') takes ''noun''-suffixes (in the ''genitive'', which may be either subjective or objective, cf. {{GHGpar|115|c}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עָבְרִי|translate=my passing by}}; {{GHGheb|text=מָלְכוֹ|translate=his reigning}}, see {{GHGpar|115|a}} and {{GHGpar|115|e|nonumber=1}}. The infinitive {{GHGterm|Qal}}, then, usually has the form ''qŏṭl'', retaining the original short vowel under the first radical (on the probable ground-form ''qŭṭŭl'', see {{GHGpar|46|a}}). The resulting syllable as a rule allows a following B<sup>e</sup>gadk<sup>e</sup>phath to be spirant, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בְּכָתְבוֹ|translate=in his writing}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=45|verse=1}}; cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=הָפְכִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=נָגְפּוֹ}} (so ed. Mant.; others {{GHGheb|text=נָגְפוֹ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=27}}; {{GHGheb|text=עָצְבִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=4|verse=10}}; before {{GHGheb|text=־ְךָ}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ְכֶם}} also the syllable is completely closed, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בְּאָסְפְּךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=23|verse=39}} (but in pause {{GHGheb|text=לְהָרְגֶֽ֫ךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=42}}), unless the vowel be retained in the second syllable; see {{GHGpar|60|d|nonumber=1}}. With the form {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹל}} generally, compare the closely allied nouns of the form {{GHGheb|text=קֹ֫טֶל}} (before a suffix {{GHGheb|text=קָטְל}} or {{GHGheb|text=קֻטְל}}), {{GHGpar|84|a|a}}; {{GHGpar|93|q}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|61|b}}
Rem. 1. The infin. of verbs which have ''ō'' in the last syllable of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} of {{GHGterm|Qal}}, sometimes takes the form ''qiṭl'' before suffixes, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בְּבִגְדוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=מִכְרָם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=2|verse=6}} (but {{GHGheb|text=מָכְרָהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=8}}) {{GHGheb|text=נִפְלוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=1|verse=10}} (but {{GHGheb|text=נָפְלוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=29|verse=3}}), {{GHGheb|text=לשִׂטְנוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=3|verse=1}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁבְרִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=30|verse=18}} &c. According to Barth (see above, {{GHGpar|47|i}} with the note) these forms with ''i'' in the first syllable point to former ''i''-imperfects.

{{GHGmargin-letter|61|c}}
Infinitives of the form {{GHGheb|text=קְטַל}} ({{GHGpar|45|c}}) in verbs middle or third guttural (but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=שִׁכְבָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=33.35}}—elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=שָׁכְבְּךָ}} and {{GHGheb|text=שָׁכְבוֹ}}) before suffixes sometimes take the form ''qaṭl'', as {{GHGheb|text=זַעְפּוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jon|chapter=1|verse=15}} (and, with the syllable loosely closed.<section end=par61 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

187.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par61 />{{GHGheb|text=פַּֽעֲמוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=25}}), {{GHGheb|text=מַחְאֲךָ}} and {{GHGheb|text=רַקְעֲךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=25|verse=6}}; sometimes ''qiṭl'', with the ''a'' attenuated to ''i'', especially in verbs third guttural; as {{GHGheb|text=בִּטְחֵךְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=בִּלְעִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=בִּקְעָם}}, {{GHGheb|text=פִּגְעוֹ}}, {{GHGheb|text=פִּתְחִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=רִבְעָהּ}}—Contrary to {{GHGpar|58|f}} {{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫נִי}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=12|verse=17}}) and {{GHGheb|text=־ָ֫נוּ}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=14|verse=11}}) are sometimes found with the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} instead of {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ נִי}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ נוּ}}. On {{GHGheb|text=רדופי|translate=my following}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=38|verse=21}} (but {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} {{GHGheb|text=רָדְפִי}}), cf. the analogous examples in {{GHGpar|46|e}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|61|d}}
2. With the suffixes {{GHGheb|text=־ְךָ}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ְכֶם}}, contrary to the analogy of the correspending nouns, forms occur like {{GHGheb|text=אֲכָלְךָ|translate=thy eating}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֲכָלְכֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=עֲמָדְךָ}} (others {{GHGheb|text=עֲמָֽדְךָ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ob|chapter=1|verse=11}}, i.e. with ''ō'' shortened in the same way as in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}, see {{GHGpar|60}}. But the analogy of the nouns is followed in such forms as {{GHGheb|text=קֻצְרְכֶם|translate=your harvesting}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=19|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=23|verse=22|hidebook=1}} (with retention of the original ''ŭ''), and {{GHGheb|text=מָֽאָסְכֶם}} (read ''mŏʾŏs<sup>e</sup>khèm'') ''your despising'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=12}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=20|verse=2}}; on {{GHGheb|text=בְּמֹצַֽאֲכֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=20}} (for {{GHGheb|text=בְּמָצְ׳}}), see {{GHGpar|74|h}}.—Very unusual are the infinitive suffixes of the 2nd sing. masc. with {{GHGheb|text=נ|translate=energicum}} (on the analogy of suffixes with the imperfect, {{GHGpar|58|i}}), as {{GHGheb|text=יַסְּרֶ֑ךָּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=36}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=23|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=33|verse=32}}, all in principal pause.

{{GHGmargin-letter|61|e}}
Examples of the {{GHGterm|infinitive Niphʿal}} with suffixes are, {{GHGheb|text=הִכָּֽבְדִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=14|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִשָּֽׁמֶדְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=20}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִשָּֽׁמְדָֽךְ}} verse 24); {{GHGheb|text=הִשָּֽׁפְטוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=37|verse=33}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִזָּֽכֶרְכֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=29}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִשָּֽׁמְדָם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=7|verse=23}}. In the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} of {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} (as also in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}, see {{GHGpar|60|f}}) the ''ē'' before the suff. {{GHGheb|text=־ְךָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ְכֶם}} becomes {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=דַּבֶּ֫רְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=4|verse=10}}, and with a sharpening to ''ĭ'' {{GHGheb|text=פָּֽרִשְׂכָם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=15}} (see {{GHGpar|60|f}}). In the {{GHGterm|infinitive Pôʿēl}}, {{GHGheb|text=בּֽוֹשַׁסְכָם}} occurs (with ''a'' for ''ĕ'' or ''ĭ'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=11}}, but probably {{GHGheb|text=בּֽוּסְכָם}}, with Wellhausen, is the right reading; the correction {{GHGheb|text=ס}} has crept into the text alongside of the {{GHGtranslate|corrigendum|en=to be translated}} {{GHGheb|text=ש}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|61|f}}
'''2.''' The leading form of the {{GHGterm|imperative Qal}} before ''suffixes'' ({{GHGheb|text=קָטְל}}) is due probably (see {{GHGpar|46|d}}) to the retention of the original short vowel of the first syllable (ground-form ''qŭṭŭl''). In the {{GHGterm|imperative}} also ''ŏ'' is not followed by {{GHGterm|Dageš lene}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כָּתְבֵם|pron=kŏthbhēm}} (not ''kŏthbēm''), &c.<ref>{{GHGheb|text=שָֽׁמְרֵ֫נִי}} ''šām<sup>e</sup>rēnî'' required by the Masora in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=16|verse=1}} (also {{GHGheb|text=שָֽׁמְרָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=86|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=167|hidebook=1}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=38|verse=14}} and {{GHGheb|text=עֲמָֽדְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ob|chapter=1|verse=11}}), belongs to the disputed cases discussed in {{GHGpar|9|v}} and {{GHGpar|48|i}} note.</ref> As in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} ({{GHGpar|60|d}}) and {{GHGterm|infinitive}} (see above, {{GHGpar|61|c}}), so also in the {{GHGterm|imperative}}, suffixes are found united to the stem by an ''a''-sound; e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כָּתְבָהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=8}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=28}}.—The forms {{GHGheb|text=קִטְלִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=קִטְלוּ}}, which are not exhibited in Paradigm C, undergo no change. Instead of {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹ֫לְנָה}}, the masc. form ({{GHGheb|text=קִטְלוּ}}) is used, as in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|61|g}}
In verbs which form the {{GHGterm|imperative}} with ''a'', like {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלַח}} (to which class belong especially verbs ''middle'' and ''third guttural'', {{GHGpar|64|doublesign=1}} and {{GHGpar|65|nosign=1}}), this ''a'' retains its place when pronominal suffixes are added, but, since it then stands in an open syllable, is, as a matter of course, lengthened to {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} (just as in ''imperfects Qal'' in a, {{GHGpar|60|c}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלָחֵ֫נִי|translate=send me}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=8}}, {{GHGheb|text=בְּחָנֵ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=26|verse=2}}, {{GHGheb|text=קְרָאֵ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=50|verse=15}}, {{GHGheb|text=שְׁמָע֫וּנִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=23|verse=8}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=9|verse=1}}, {{GHGheb|text=בְּצָ֫עַם}} (so ed. Mant., Baer, Ginsb., instead of the ordinary reading {{GHGheb|text=בְּצַ֫עְם}}) is to be explained, with Margolis, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|AJSL.|American Journal of Semitic Languages.}}}} xix, p. 45 ff., from an original {{GHGheb|text=בְּצַעְמוֹ}}, as {{GHGheb|text=וַֽהֲרָגָ֑תַם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=9|verse=4}} from original {{GHGheb|text=וַֽהֲרָגָ֑תְמוֹ}}.—In the imperative {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, the form used in conjunction with suffixes is not the 2nd ''sing. masc.''<section end=par61 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

188.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par61 />{{GHGheb|text=חַקְטֵל}}, but {{GHGheb|text=הַקְטִיל}} (with ''î'' on account of the open syllable, cf. {{GHGpar|60|g}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַקְרִיבֵ֫הוּ|translate=present it}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mal|chapter=1|verse=8}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|61|h}}
'''3.''' Like the infinitives, the participles can also be united with either verbal or noun-suffixes; see {{GHGpar|116|f}}. In both cases the vowel of the participles is shortened or becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} before the suffix, as in the corresponding noun-forms, e.g. from the form {{GHGheb|text=קֹטֵל}}: {{GHGheb|text=רֹֽדְפִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=רֹֽדְפוֹ}}, &c.; but before {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ mobile}} {{GHGheb|text=יֹֽצֶרְךָ}}, &c., or with the original ''ĭ'', {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽיִבְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=4}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽסִפְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=22|verse=20}} (coinciding in form with the 1st ''sing. imperfect Qal'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=6}}; cf. {{GHGpar|68|h}}); with a middle guttural ({{GHGheb|text=גֹּֽאֲלִי}}), {{GHGheb|text=גֹּֽאַלְךָ}}; with a third guttural, {{GHGheb|text=בֹּרַֽאֲךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=1}}, but {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁלֵֽחֲךָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְשַׁלֵּֽחֲךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=28|verse=16}}, cf. {{GHGpar|65|d}}. The form {{GHGheb|text=מְקַטֵּל}}, with suffix {{GHGheb|text=מְקַטְּלִי}}; before {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} sometimes like {{GHGheb|text=מְלַמֶּדְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=48|verse=17}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְנַחֶמְכֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, sometimes like {{GHGheb|text=מְאַסִּפְכֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=52|verse=12|hidebook=1}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=רֹאָ֫נִי}} is irregular for {{GHGheb|text=רֹאֵ֫נִי}}; instead of the meaningless {{GHGheb|text=כֻּלֹּה מְקַלְלַֽוְנִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=15|verse=10}} read {{GHGheb|text=כֻּלְּהֶם קִלְל֫וּנִי}}.

Also unusual (see above, {{GHGpar|61|d|nonumber=1}}) with participles are the suffixes of the 2nd sing. masc. with {{GHGheb|text=נ‍|translate=energicum}}, as {{GHGheb|text=עוֹנֶ֫ךָּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=1}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=8|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=12|verse=14.28|hidebook=1}}.<section end=par61 />

<section begin=par62 />{{GHGpar-heading|62|Verbs with Gutturals}}

{{center|Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, p. 584 ff.}}

Verbs which have a guttural for one of the three radicals differ in their inflexion from the ordinary strong verb, according to the general rules in {{GHGpar|22}}. These differences do not affect the consonantal part of the stem, and it is, therefore, more correct to regard the guttural verbs as a subdivision of the strong verb. At the most, only the entire omission of the strengthening in some of the verbs ''middle guttural'' (as well as in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Niphʿal}} of verbs ''first guttural'') can be regarded as a real weakness ({{GHGpar|63|h|doublesign=1}}, {{GHGpar|64|e|nosign=1}}). On the other hand, some original elements have been preserved in guttural stems, which have degenerated in the ordinary strong verb; e.g. the ''ă'' of the initial syllable in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}}, as in {{GHGheb|text=יַחְמֹד}}, which elsewhere is attenuated to ''ĭ'', {{GHGheb|text=יִקְטֹל}}.—In guttural verbs {{GHGheb|text=א}} and {{GHGheb|text=ה}} are only taken into consideration when they are actual consonants, and not vowel-letters like the {{GHGheb|text=א}} in some verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״א}} ({{GHGpar|68}}), in a few {{GHGheb|text=ע״א}} ({{GHGpar|73|g}}), and in most {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}} ({{GHGpar|74}}). In all these cases, however, the {{GHGheb|text=א}} was at least originally a full consonant, while the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} was never anything but a vowel letter, cf. {{GHGpar|75}}. The really consonantal {{GHGheb|text=ה}} at the end of the word is marked by {{GHGterm|Mappîq}}.—Verbs containing a {{GHGheb|text=ר}} also, according to {{GHGpar|22|q}}, {{GHGpar|22|r|nonumber=1}}, share some of the peculiarities of the guttural verbs. For more convenient treatment, the cases will be distinguished, according as the guttural is the first, second, or third radical. (Cf. the Paradigms D, E, F, in which only those conjugations are omitted which are wholly regular.)<section end=par62 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

189.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude>
<section begin=par63/>{{GHGpar-heading|63|Verbs First Guttural, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עָמַד}} to stand}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|63|a}}
In this class the deviations from the ordinary strong verb may be referred to the following cases:—
