'''1.''' Instead of a {{GHGterm|simple Š<sup>e</sup>wâ mobile}}, the initial guttural takes a {{GHGterm|compound Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} ({{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph}}, {{GHGpar|10|f}}, {{GHGpar|22|l}}). Thus the {{GHGterm|infinitives}} {{GHGheb|text=עֲמֹד}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֱכֹל|translate=to eat}}, and the {{GHGterm|perfects, 2nd plur. masc.}} {{GHGheb|text=עֲמַדְתֶּם}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֲפַצְתֶּם}} from {{GHGheb|text=חָפֵץ|translate=to be inclined}}, correspond to the forms {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹל}} and {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתֶּם}}; also {{GHGheb|text=אֲכָלוֹ}} to {{GHGheb|text=קְטָלוֹ}}, and so always with initial {{GHGheb|text=־ֲ}} before a suffix for an original ''ă'', according to {{GHGpar|22|o}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|63|b}}
'''2.''' When a preformative is placed before an initial guttural, either the two may form a closed syllable, or the vowel of the preformative is repeated as a {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph}} under the guttural. If the vowel of the preformative was originally ''a'', two methods of formation may again be distinguished, according as this ''a'' remains or passes into S<sup>e</sup>ghôl.

{{GHGmargin-letter|63|c}}
Examples: (''a'') of firmly closed syllables after the original vowel of the preformative (always with ''ō'' in the second syllable, except {{GHGheb|text=וַתַּעְגַּב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=23|verse=5}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּעְדֶה}} &c. from {{GHGheb|text=עָדָה|translate=to adorn oneself}}, and {{GHGheb|text=יַעְטֶה}}; but cf. {{GHGpar|63|e|nonumber=1}}): {{GHGheb|text=יַחְמֹד}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַחְמֹל}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַהְשֹׁב}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַהְשֹׁךְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַעְקֹב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=3}} (probably to distinguish it from the name {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעֲקֹב}}, just as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=10|verse=19}}, &c., the participle fem. Niphʿal of {{GHGheb|text=חָלָה}} is {{GHGheb|text=נַחְלָה}} to distinguish it from {{GHGheb|text=נַֽחֲלָה}}), &c., and so generally in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} of stems beginning with {{GHGheb|text=ח}}, although sometimes parallel forms exist, which repeat the ''ă'' as a {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יַֽחֲשֹׁב}}, &c. The same form appears also in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=יַחְסִיר}}, &c. Very rarely the original ''ă'' is retained in a closed syllable under the preformative {{GHGheb|text=נ‍}} of the {{GHGterm|perfect Niphʿal}}: {{GHGheb|text=נַחְבֵּ֫אתָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=27}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=16}}; also the {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} {{GHGheb|text=נַחְתּוֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=8|verse=8}}, {{GHGheb|text=נַעְתּוֹר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=5|verse=20}}, and the {{GHGterm|participle fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=נַחְלָה}} (see above), {{GHGterm|plur.}} {{GHGheb|text=נַעְתָּרוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=27|verse=6}}. In these forms the original ''ă'' is commonly kept under the preformative and is followed by {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Pathaḥ}}; thus in the {{GHGterm|perfect}} of some verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נַֽעֲשָׂה}}, &c.; in the {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}}, {{GHGheb|text=נַֽהֲפוֹךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=9|verse=1}}; in the {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=נַֽעֲרָץ}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=89|verse=8}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|63|d}}
(''b'') Of the corresponding {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph}} after the original vowel: {{GHGheb|text=יַֽחֲבשׁ}} (but {{GHGheb|text=יֶחְבָּֽשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=18}} in pause), {{GHGheb|text=יֽחֲלֹם}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעֲמֹד}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַֽהֲרֹס}}, and so almost always with {{GHGheb|text=ע}} and often with {{GHGheb|text=ה}} in the ''imperfects'' of {{GHGterm|Qal}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}; in {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָֽעֳמַד}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָֽעֳמַד}}; but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=הָחְבָּ֑אוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=22}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָחְתֵּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=4}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|63|e}}
The ''ă'' of the preformative before a guttural almost always ({{GHGpar|22|i}}, cf. {{GHGpar|27|p}}) becomes {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} (cf., however, {{GHGpar|63|q|nonumber=1}}). This {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} again appears sometimes

(''c'') in a closed syllable, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יֶחְבַּשׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֶחְסַד}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֶעְתַּד}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֶאְשַׁם}}, always with ''ă'' in the second syllable, corresponding to the imperfects of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}},
<section end=par63/><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

190.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par63 />with original ''ĭ'' in the first and ''ă'' in the second syllable, {{GHGpar|67|n}}, and also to the imperfects of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, {{GHGpar|72|h}}; but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=יֶאְפֹּד}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֶאְסֹר}}, and {{GHGheb|text=יֶהְדֹּף}}; in ''Niph.'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נֶהְפַּךְ}}; {{GHGheb|text=נֶחְלוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=6|verse=6}}, &c.; in ''Hiph.'' {{GHGheb|text=הֶחְסִיר}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֶעְלִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=4|verse=7}} &c.: sometimes

(''d'') followed by {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יֶֽחֱזַק}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֶֽאֱסֹף}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֶֽחֱשׂף}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֶעֱרַב}} in {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽעֱמִיד}} {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}; {{GHGheb|text=נֶֽעֱנַשׁ}} {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|63|f}}
Rem. With regard to the above examples the following points may also be noted: (1) The forms with a firmly closed syllable (called the hard combination) frequently occur in the same verb with forms containing a loosely closed syllable (the soft combination). (2) In the 1st ''sing. imperfect Qal'' the preformative {{GHGheb|text=א}} invariably takes {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, whether in a firmly or loosely closed syllable, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֶֽחֱבשׁ}} (with the cohortative {{GHGheb|text=אֶחְבְּשָׁה}}), {{GHGheb|text=אֶחְסָר}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}}), &c. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=32|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=אַֽעֲנֶה}} must unquestionably be {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, since elsewhere the pointing is always {{GHGheb|text=אֶֽעֱ׳}}. Cohortatives like {{GHGheb|text=אַֽהַרְגָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=41}} and {{GHGheb|text=אַחְדְּלָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=6}}, are explained by the next remark. (3) The shifting of the tone towards the end frequently causes the {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} of the preformative to change into {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, and vice versa, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נַֽעֲשָׂה}}, but {{GHGheb|text=נֶֽעֶשְׂתָה}} 3rd ''sing. fem.''; {{GHGheb|text=יֶֽאֱסֹף}}, but {{GHGheb|text=תַּֽאַסְפִי}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽעֱמִיד}}, but with {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} {{GHGheb|text=וְהַֽעֲמַדְתָּ֫}}, &c.; so {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּחְסְרוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=3}} the plur. of {{GHGheb|text=וַיֶּחְסַר}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=11|verse=8}}; and thus generally a change of the stronger {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} group ({{GHGheb|text=־ֶֽ־ֱ }}) into the lighter {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Pathaḥ}} group takes place whenever the tone is moved one place toward the end (cf. {{GHGpar|27|v}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|63|g}}
'''3.''' When in forms like {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעֲמֹד}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֶֽעֱמַד}}, the vowel of the final syllable becomes a {{GHGterm|vocal Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} in consequence of the addition of an afformative ({{GHGheb|text=וּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}) or suffix, the {{GHGterm|compound Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} of the guttural is changed into the corresponding short vowel, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעֲמֹד}}, ''plur''. {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעַמְדוּ}} (''ya-ʿa-m<sup>e</sup>-dhû'' as an equivalent for ''yaʿ-m<sup>e</sup>-dhû''); {{GHGheb|text=נֶֽעֶזְבָה|translate=she is forsaken}}. But even in these forms the hard combination frequently occurs, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יַחְבְּלוּ|translate=they take as a pledge}} (cf. in the ''sing.'' {{GHGheb|text=תַּחְבֹּל}}, also {{GHGheb|text=יַֽחֲבֹל}}); {{GHGheb|text=יֶחְזְקוּ}} (also {{GHGheb|text=יֶֽחֶזְקוּ}}) ''they are strong''. Cf. {{GHGpar|22|m}} and, in general, {{GHGpar|63|m|nonumber=1}}, {{GHGpar|28|c}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|63|h}}
'''4.''' In the ''infinitive, imperative, and imperfect Niphʿal'', where the first radical should by rule be strengthened ({{GHGheb|text=הִקָּטֵל}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִקָּטֵל}}), the strengthening is always omitted, and the vowel of the preformative lengthened to {{GHGterm|Ṣere}}; {{GHGheb|text=יֵֽעָמֵד}} for ''yiʿʿāmēd'',<ref>{{GHGheb|text=אֶֽעָנֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=7}} (so even the Mantua ed.) is altogether abnormal: read {{GHGheb|text=אֵֽעָנֶה}}, with Baer, Ginsb.</ref> &c. Cf. {{GHGpar|22|c}}—For {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽיעָשֶׂה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=25|verse=31}} (according to Dillmann, to prevent the pronunciation {{GHGheb|text=תַּֽעֲשֶׂה}}, which the LXX and Samaritan follow) read {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽעָשֶׂה}}.

{{center|Remarks

I. ''On Qal''.}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|63|i}}
1. In verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״א}} the {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} and ''imperative take Ḥaṭeph-S<sup>e</sup>ghôl'' in the first syllable (according to {{GHGpar|22|o}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֱזֹר|translate=gird thou}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=3}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֱהַב|translate=love thou}},<section end=par63 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

191.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par63 />{{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=3|verse=1}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֱחֹז|translate=seize thou}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=4|verse=4}} (on {{GHGheb|text=אֵפוּ|translate=bake ye}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=23}}, see {{GHGpar|76|d}}); {{GHGheb|text=אֱכֹל|translate=to eat}}; infinitive with a prefix {{GHGheb|text=לֶֽאֱחֹז}}, {{GHGheb|text=לֶֽאֱכֹל}}, {{GHGheb|text=כֶּֽאֱכֹל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=24}}; {{GHGheb|text=לֶֽאֱהֹב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=3|verse=8}}. Sometimes, however, {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Pathaḥ}} is found as well, e.g. {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=אֲחֹז}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=6|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽאֲכֹל הָאֵשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=26|verse=10}} (before a suffix {{GHGheb|text=אֲכָלְךָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲמָרְךָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲכָלְכֶם}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲמָרְכֶם}} {{GHGpar|61|d}}); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=7|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=12|verse=23|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=25|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=102|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=7}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֲמָר־לְךָ}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=18}}, always in close connexion with the following word. With a firmly closed syllable after {{GHGheb|text=ל}} cf. {{GHGheb|text=לַחְסוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַחְפֹּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=2}} f. (on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=2|verse=20}}, cf. {{GHGpar|84|n|b}}); {{GHGheb|text=לַחְתּוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=2|verse=16}}; {{GHGheb|text=לַחְשֹׁב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=31|verse=4}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=לַעְזֹר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=3}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}, but also {{GHGheb|text=בֶּֽעְזׄר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=15|verse=26}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|63|k}}
{{GHGheb|text=הֶֽחֳדַ֫לְתִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=9.11.13}} is altogether anomalous, and only a few authorities give {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽחֱדַלְתִּי}} (Hiphʿil), adopted by Moore in Haupt’s Bible. According to Qimḥi, Olshausen, and others, the Masora intended a {{GHGterm|perfect Hophʿal}} with syncope of the preformative after the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} interrogative = {{GHGheb|text=הֶהָֽחֳדַ֫לְתִּי}}, or (according to Olshausen) with the omission of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} interrogative. But since the ''Hiphʿil'' and {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} of {{GHGheb|text=חָדֵל}} nowhere occur, it is difficult to believe that such was the intention of the Masora. We should expect the {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽחָדַ֫לְתִּי}}. But the {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} under the {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, falling between the tone and counter-tone, was naturally less emphasized than in {{GHGheb|text=חָדַ֫לְתִּי}}, without the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} interrogative. Consequently it was weakened, not to simple {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, but to {{GHGheb|text=־ֳ}}, in order to represent the sound of the {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} (likewise pronounced as ''å'') at least in a shortened form. The {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} interrogative is explained, in any case, from {{GHGpar|100|n}} (cf. the similar pointing of the article, e.g. in {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽחֳדָשִׁים}}, {{GHGpar|35|k}}). For the accusative after {{GHGheb|text=חָדֵל}}, instead of the usual {{GHGheb|text=מִן}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=17}} affords sufficient evidence.

{{GHGmargin-letter|63|l}}
Also in the other forms of the {{GHGterm|imperative}} the guttural not infrequently influences the vowel, causing a change of ''ĭ'' (on this ''ĭ'' cf. {{GHGpar|48|i}}) into {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֶסְפָה|translate=gather thou}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=16}}; {{GHGheb|text=עֶרְכָה|translate=set in order}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=33|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=חֶשְׂפִּי|translate=strip off}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=2}} (on this irregular {{GHGterm|Dageš}} cf. {{GHGpar|46|d}}), especially when the second radical is also a guttural, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֶֽהֱבוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=31|verse=24}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=8|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֶֽחֱזוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=2|verse=15}}; cf. also in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֱנוּ|translate=sing ye}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=147|verse=7}} (compared with {{GHGheb|text=עֲנוּ|translate=answer ye}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=12|verse=3}}) and {{GHGheb|text=אֱלִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=1|verse=8}}.—{{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} occurs in {{GHGheb|text=חַבְלֵ֫הוּ|translate=hold him in pledge}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=20|verse=16}}, and probably also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=9|verse=14}} ({{GHGheb|text=חַֽנְנֵ֫נִי}}).—As a pausal form for {{GHGheb|text=חָרְבִי}} (cf. the ''plur.'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=12}}) we find in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=44|verse=27}} {{GHGheb|text=חֳרָ֑בִי}} (cf. the ''imperf''. {{GHGheb|text=יֶֽחֱרַב}}) with the ''ŏ'' repeated in the form of a {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Qameṣ}}. For other examples of this kind, see {{GHGpar|10|h}} and {{GHGpar|46|e}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|63|m}}
2. The pronunciation (mentioned above, No. 2) of the imperfects in ''ă'' with {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} under the preformative in a firmly closed syllable (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יֶחְדַּל}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֶחְכַּם}}) regularly gives way to the soft combination in verbs which are at the same time {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יֶֽחֱזֶה}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֶֽחֱצֶה}} &c. (but cf. {{GHGheb|text=יֶהְגֶּה}} &c., {{GHGheb|text=יַחְתֶּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=6|verse=27}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֶעְשֶׂה}} ed. Mant., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=20}}). Even in the strong verb {{GHGheb|text=וַיֶּֽחֱזַק}} is found along with {{GHGheb|text=יֶחְזַק}}. Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=וַתַּעְגַּב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=23|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּעְקְבֵנִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=36}} (so Ben-Asher; but Ben-Naphtali {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּֽעַקְ׳}}); {{GHGheb|text=וַתַּחְלְקֵם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=9|verse=22}}, and so always in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} of {{GHGheb|text=עָזַר}} with suffixes, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=25}}, &c.—{{GHGheb|text=תְּאֵֽהֲבוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=22}} is to be explained from the endeavour to avoid too great an accumulation of short sounds by the insertion of a long vowel, but it is a question whether we should not simply read {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽאהֲבוּ}} with Haupt in his Bible, ''Proverbs'', p. 34, 1. 44 ff.; cf. the analogous instances under {{GHGpar|63|p|nonumber=1}}, and<section end=par63 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

192.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par63" />such nouns as {{GHGheb|text=בְּאֵר}}, {{GHGheb|text=זְאֵב}}, {{GHGpar|93|t}}.—On {{GHGheb|text=יְחָבְרְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=94|verse=20}} for {{GHGheb|text=יַחְבָּרְךָ}} (according to Qimḥi, and others, rather {{GHGterm|Puʿal}}) cf. {{GHGpar|60|b}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|63|n}}
{{GHGheb|text=יַאְטֵם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=58|verse=5}} and {{GHGheb|text=יַעְרִם|translate=to deal subtilly}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=23|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=15|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=19|verse=25|hidebook=1}}, may be explained with Barth ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1889, p. 179) as ''i''-imperfects (see above, {{GHGpar|47|i}}),—the latter for the purpose of distinction from the causative {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעֲרִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=83|verse=4}}.—Instead of the unintelligible form {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּחָֽלְקֵם}} (so ed. Mant.; Baer and Ginsb. as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=24|verse=3|hidebook=1}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=23|verse=6}} and {{GHGheb|text=וַיֶּֽחָ׳}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=24|verse=3|hidebook=1}} (partly analogous to {{GHGheb|text=תָּֽעָבְדֵם}} {{GHGpar|60|b}}) the Qal {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּחְלְקֵם}} is to be read. The form {{GHGheb|text=יִֽרַדֹּף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=7|verse=6}} which is, according to Qimḥi (in {{GHGcite|title=Mikhlol}}; but in his Lexicon he explains it as {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}}), a composite form of {{GHGterm|Qal}} ({{GHGheb|text=יִרְדֹּף}}) and {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} ({{GHGheb|text=יְרַדֵּף}}), can only be understood as a development of {{GHGheb|text=יִֽרְדֹף}} (cf. {{GHGpar|64|h}} on {{GHGheb|text=יִֽצֲחַק}}, and {{GHGpar|69|x}} on {{GHGheb|text=תִּֽהֲלַךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=9}}). Pathaḥ has taken the place of {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Pathaḥ}}, but as a mere helping-vowel (as in {{GHGheb|text=שָׁמַעַתְּ}} {{GHGpar|28|e}}, note 2) and without preventing the closing of the syllable. It is much simpler, however, to take it as a ''forma mixta'', combining the readings {{GHGheb|text=יִרְדֹּף}} (impf. Qal) and {{GHGheb|text=יְרַדֵּף}} (impf. Piʿel).

{{center|II. ''On Hiphʿîl and Hophʿal.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|63|o}}
3. The above-mentioned ({{GHGpar|63|f|nonumber=1}}, 3) change of {{GHGheb|text=־ֶֽ־ֱ}} to {{GHGheb|text=־ַֽ־ֲ}} occurs in the {{GHGterm|perfect Hiphʿîl}}, especially when {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} precedes, and the tone is in consequence thrown forward upon the afformative, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽעֱמַ֫דְתָּ}}, but {{GHGheb|text=וְהַֽעֲמַדְתָּ֫}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=3|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=8|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=27|verse=19|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽעֱבַ֫רְתִּי}}, but {{GHGheb|text=וְהַֽעֲבַרְתִּ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=15|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=20|verse=37}}; even in the 3rd ''sing.'' {{GHGheb|text=וְהַֽאֲוִין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=77|verse=2}}.—On the contrary {{GHGheb|text=־ֶֽ־ֱ}} occurs instead of {{GHGheb|text=־ַֽ־ֲ}} in the {{GHGterm|imperative Hiphʿil}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=8.30}}; and in the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=32}}. The preformative of {{GHGheb|text=עתר}} in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} always takes ''a'' in a closed syllable: {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=8|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=הַעְתִּ֫ירוּ}}; verse 5 {{GHGheb|text=אַעְתִּיר}}; also verse 25 and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=27}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|63|p}}
4. In the {{GHGterm|perfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=־ֶֽ־ֱ}} is sometimes changed into {{GHGheb|text=־ֵֽ־ֲ}}, and in {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=־ֶֽ־ֳ}} into {{GHGheb|text=־ֽׄ־ֲ}} (cf. {{GHGpar|23|h}}); {{GHGheb|text=הֵֽעֲבַ֫רְתָּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=7|verse=7}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵֽעֲלָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=1|verse=15}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֹֽעֲלָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=20|verse=34}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=2|verse=8}}, always before {{GHGheb|text=ע}}, and hence evidently with the intention of strengthening the countertone-syllable ({{GHGheb|text=הֵֽ}} or {{GHGheb|text=הֹֽ}}) before the guttural. On a further case of this kind ({{GHGheb|text=זֹֽעֲמָה}}) see {{GHGpar|64|c}}. Something similar occurs in the formation of segholate nouns of the form ''qŏṭl''; cf. {{GHGpar|93|q}}, and (on {{GHGheb|text=אֵמוּן}} &c. for {{GHGheb|text=אֱמוּן}}) {{GHGpar|84|q|a}}.—In the imperfect consecutive {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּֽחֲזֶק בּוֹ}} the tone is thrown back on to the first syllable. On the {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=תָּֽעָבְדֵם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=5}}, &c., see {{GHGpar|60|b}}.

{{center|III. {{GHGheb|text=הָיָה}} <!-- not a translation --> ''and'' {{GHGheb|text=חָיָה}}.}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|63|q}}
5. In the verbs {{GHGheb|text=הָיָה|translate=to be}}, and {{GHGheb|text=חָיָה|translate=to live}}, the guttural hardly ever affects the addition of preformatives; thus {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=יִֽהְיֶה}} and {{GHGheb|text=יִֽחְיֶה}}, {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נִֽהְיָה}}); but in the {{GHGterm|perfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽחֱיָה}} (2nd ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=וְהַֽחֲיִתֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=13}}, and even without {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=19}}). Initial {{GHGheb|text=ה}} always has {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} instead of {{GHGterm|vocal Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֱיֵה}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֱיוֹת}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֱיוֹתָם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=7}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֱיִיתֶם}} (except {{GHGheb|text=הֲיִי|translate=be thou!}} {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=60}}). The 2nd ''sing. fem. imperative'' of {{GHGheb|text=חָיָה}} is {{GHGheb|text=חֲיִי|translate=live thou}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=6}}; the infinitive, with suffix, {{GHGheb|text=חֲיוֹתָם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=5|verse=8}}. After the prefixes {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=בְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=כְ‍}}, {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִ‍}} (={{GHGheb|text=מִן}}) both {{GHGheb|text=ה}} and {{GHGheb|text=ח}} retain the ''simple'' Š<sup>e</sup>wâ ({{GHGpar|28|b}}) and the prefix takes ''ĭ'', as elsewhere before strong consonants with {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}; hence in the {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=וִֽהְיִיתֶם}}, {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=וִֽהְיוּ}}, {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=לֽהְיוֹת}}, {{GHGheb|text=בִּֽהְיוֹת}} &c. (cf. {{GHGpar|16|f}}, ε). The only exception is the 2nd ''sing. masc.'' of the {{GHGterm|imperative}} after {{GHGterm|wāw}}; {{GHGheb|text=וֶֽהְיֵה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=2}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=וֶֽחְיֵה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=20|verse=7}}.<section end="par63" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

193.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par64" />{{GHGpar-heading|64|Verbs Middle Guttural, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שָׁחַט}} to slaughter}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|64|a}}
The slight deviations from the ordinary inflexion are confined chiefly to the following<ref>{{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}, which is not exhibited in the paradigm, follows the analogy of {{GHGterm|Qal}}; {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} is regular.</ref>:—

'''1.''' When the guttural would stand at the beginning of a syllable with simple {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, it necessarily takes a {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph}}, and almost always {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Pathaḥ}}, e.g. {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=שָֽׁחֲטוּ}}, {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁחֲטוּ}}, {{GHGterm|imperative Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=הִשָּֽׁחֲטוּ}}. In the {{GHGterm|imperative Qal}}, before the afformatives ''î'' and ''û'', the original {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} is retained in the first syllable, and is followed by {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Pathaḥ}}, thus, {{GHGheb|text=זַֽעֲקִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=זַֽעֲקוּ}}, &c.; in {{GHGheb|text=אֶֽהֱבוּ}} the preference of the {{GHGheb|text=א}} for {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} (but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=יֹֽאחֱזוּךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=21}}) has caused the change from ''ă'' to ''ĕ''; in {{GHGheb|text=שִֽׁחֲדוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=22}}, even ''ĭ'' remains before a ''hard'' guttural.

So in the ''infinitive Qal fem.'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אַֽהֲבָה|translate=to love}}, {{GHGheb|text=דַּֽאֲבָה|translate=to pine}}; and in the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} with a suffix {{GHGheb|text=לְסַֽעֲדָהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=9|verse=6}}; the doubtful form {{GHGheb|text=שַֽׁחֲטָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=5|verse=2}}, is better explained as {{GHGterm|infinitive Piʿēl}} (= {{GHGheb|text=שַֽׁחֲתָה}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|64|b}}
'''2.''' Since the preference of the gutturals for the ''a''-sound has less influence on the following than on the preceding vowel, not only is {{GHGterm|Ḥolem}} retained after the middle guttural in the {{GHGterm|infinitive Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=שְׁחֹט}} (with the fem. ending and retraction and shortening of the ''o'' {{GHGheb|text=רָחְצָה}} and {{GHGheb|text=רָֽחֳקָה}} cf. {{GHGpar|45|b}}), but generally also the {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Niphʿal}} and {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִלָּחֵם|translate=he fights}}, {{GHGheb|text=יְנַחֵם|translate=he comforts}}, and even the more feeble {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} after {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} in such forms as {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּלָּ֫חֶם}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּפָּ֫עֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=8}} (cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּוָּעַ֫ץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=12|verse=6}}, &c.). But in the {{GHGterm|imperative}} and {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}}, the final syllable, through the influence of the guttural, mostly takes {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}}, even in transitive verbs, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שְׁחַט}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁחַט}}; {{GHGheb|text=זְעַק}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִזְעַק}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּחַר}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִבְחַר}}; with ''suffixes'' (according to {{GHGpar|60|c}}), {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּחָנֵ֫נִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=שְׁאָל֫וּנִי}}, {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יִגְאָלוּ֫הוּ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|64|c}}
With ''ō'' in the {{GHGterm|imperative Qal}}, the only instances are {{GHGheb|text=נְעֹל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֱחֹז}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=4|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=21}}, {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶֽחֳזִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=3|verse=15}} (with the unusual repetition of the lost ''ō'' as {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Qameṣ}}; 2nd ''plur. masc.'' in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=אֱחֹ֑זוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=7|verse=3}}; without the {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶֽחֱזוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=2|verse=15}}); {{GHGheb|text=סְעָד־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=8}}.<ref>Also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=5}} (where Qimḥi would read ''s<sup>e</sup>ʿād''), read ''s<sup>e</sup>ʿŏd'', and on the use of the conjunctive accent (here ''Darga'') as a substitute for Metheg, at. {{GHGpar|9|u}} (c) and {{GHGpar|16|b}}.</ref> Finally {{GHGheb|text=זֹֽעֲמָה}} for {{GHGheb|text=זָֽעֳמָה}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=7}}, is an example of the same kind, see {{GHGpar|63|p}}. Just as rare are the imperfects in ''ō'' of verbs ''middle guttural'', as {{GHGheb|text=יִנְהֹם}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֶֽאֱחֹז}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּמְעֹל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=27}} (but {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּמְעַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=26|verse=16}}); cf. {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּשְׁחֳדִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=33}}; {{GHGheb|text=תִּפְעָל־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=35|verse=6}}. Also in the ''perfect Piʿēl, Pathaḥ'' occurs somewhat more frequently than in the strong verb, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נִחַם|translate=to comfort}} (cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=כִּהֵן}}, {{GHGheb|text=כִּחֵד}}, {{GHGheb|text=כִּחֵשׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁחֵת}});<section end="par64" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

194.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par64"/>but {{GHGheb|text=א}} and {{GHGheb|text=ע}} always have ''ē'' in 3rd ''sing''.—On the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} with suffixes, cf. {{GHGpar|61|b}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|64|d}}
'''3.''' In {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, {{GHGterm|Puʿal}}, and {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}}, the {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}} being inadmissible in the middle radical, the preceding vowel, especially before {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, {{GHGheb|text=ח}} and {{GHGheb|text=ע}}, nevertheless, generally remains short, and the guttural is consequently to be regarded as, at least, ''virtually'' strengthened, cf. {{GHGpar|22|c}}; e.g. {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=שִׂחַק}}, {{GHGheb|text=נִֽחֲלוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=14|verse=1}}, {{GHGheb|text=וּבִֽעַרְתִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=10}}, {{GHGheb|text=נִהַג}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=13}} (cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=אֵחַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=נֵהַ֫לְתָּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=13}}, but in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} and {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=יְנַהֵל}}, &c.; in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=רֵעָה}}), {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=שַׂחֵק}}, {{GHGterm|Puʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=רֻחַץ}} (but cf. {{GHGheb|text=דֹּחוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=36|verse=13}} from {{GHGheb|text=דָּחָה}}, also the unusual position of the tone in {{GHGheb|text=בֹּ֫חַן}}<ref>{{GHGheb|text=בֹּ֫חַן}} is explained by Abulwalîd as the 3rd pers. {{GHGterm|perfect Puʿal}}, but by Qimḥi as a noun.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=18}}, and in the {{GHGterm|perfect Hithpaʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִתְרָחַ֫צְתִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=30}}); ''Hithpaʿēl perfect'' and {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=הִטַּֽהֲרוּ}}, &c.; in {{GHGterm|pause}} (see {{GHGpar|22|c|doublesign=1}}, {{GHGpar|27|q|nosign=1}}, {{GHGpar|29|v|nosign=1}}, {{GHGpar|54|k|nosign=1}}) {{GHGheb|text=הִטֶּהָֽרוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=8|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=30|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִתְנֶחָם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=19}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|64|e}}
The complete omission of the strengthening, and a consequent lengthening of the preceding vowel, occurs invariably only with {{GHGheb|text=ר}} ({{GHGheb|text=כָּרַּת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=4}} is an exception; {{GHGheb|text=כֹּרָ֑תָה}} also occurs, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=28}}), e g. {{GHGheb|text=בֵּרַךְ}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=בֵּרֵךְ}}), {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יְבָרֵךְ}}, {{GHGterm|Puʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=בֹּרַךְ}}. Before {{GHGheb|text=א}} it occurs regularly in the stems {{GHGheb|text=בֵּאֵר}}, {{GHGheb|text=גֵּאֵל}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֵאֵן}}, {{GHGheb|text=פֵּאֵר}}, and in the {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} of {{GHGheb|text=באשׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=ראה}}, and {{GHGheb|text=שׁאה}}; on the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=א}} is ''virtually'' strengthened in the ''perfects'', {{GHGheb|text=נִאֵף}} (once in the imperfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=29|verse=23}}) ''to commit adultery'', {{GHGheb|text=נִאֵץ|translate=to despise}} (in the {{GHGterm|participle}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=60|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=17}}; according to Baer, but not ed. Mant., or Ginsb., even in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יְנַאֵץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=74|verse=10}}), {{GHGheb|text=נִאֵר|translate=to abhor}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=2|verse=7}} (also {{GHGheb|text=נֵאַ֫רְתָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=89|verse=40}}) and {{GHGheb|text=שִׁאֵל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=109|verse=10}}; moreover, in the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=יַאֵשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=2|verse=20}}, according to the best reading. On the {{GHGterm|Mappîq}} in the {{GHGterm|Puʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=רֻאִ֫וּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=33|verse=21}}, cf. {{GHGpar|14|d}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|64|f}}
Rem. 1. In the verb {{GHGheb|text=שָׁאַל|translate=to ask, to beg}}, some forms of the {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} appear to be based upon a secondary form ''middle e'', which is {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} when the vowel of the {{GHGheb|text=א}} stands in an open syllable, cf. {{GHGheb|text=שְׁאֵֽלְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=20}}; {{GHGheb|text=שְׁאֵל֫וּנִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=137|verse=3}}; but in a closed syllable, even without a suffix, {{GHGheb|text=שְׁאֶלְתֶּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=12|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=29}}; {{GHGheb|text=שְׁאִלְתִּ֫יהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=20}}. Cf., however, similar cases of attenuation of an original ''ă'', {{GHGpar|69|s}}, and especially {{GHGpar|44|d}}. In the first three examples, if explained on that analogy, the ''ĭ'' attenuated from ''ă'' would have been lengthened to ''ē'' (before the tone); in the next three ''ĭ'' would have been modified to ''ĕ''. Also in the ''Hiphʿil''-form {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁאִלְתִּ֫יהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=28}} the {{GHGheb|text=אִ}} is merely attenuated from {{GHGheb|text=אַ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|64|g}}
2. In {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} the lengthening of the vowel before the guttural causes the tone to be thrown back upon the penultima, and consequently the {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} of the ultima to be shortened to {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}. Thus (''a'') before monosyllables, according to {{GHGpar|29|e}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לְשָׁ֫רֶת שָׁם|translate=to minister there}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=17|verse=12}}, even in the case of a guttural which is ''virtually'' strengthened, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=8|verse=18}} (see {{GHGpar|29|g}}). (''b'') after {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=רַיְבָ֫רֶךְ|translate=and he blessed}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=22}} and frequently, {{GHGheb|text=וַיְגָ֫רֶשׁ|translate=and he drove out}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=11}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּתפָּ֫עֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=2|verse=1}}.
<section end="par64"/><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

195.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par64" />{{GHGmargin-letter|64|h}}
3. The following are a few rarer anomalies; in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=יִֽצֲחַק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=6}} (elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=תִּצְחַק}}, &c., in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=יִצְחָק}}, cf. {{GHGpar|10|g}} (c) and {{GHGpar|63|n}}); {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֵחַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=5}} (for {{GHGheb|text=וָאֶֽאֱחַר}}); in the {{GHGterm|perfect Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶֽחֱרוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=28}} (perhaps primarily for {{GHGheb|text=אִֽחֲרוּ}}; according to {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=אֵֽחֲרוּ}} would be expected), and similarly {{GHGheb|text=יֶחֱֽמַ֫תְנִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=51|verse=7}} for {{GHGheb|text=יִחֲֽמַ֫תְנִי}}; in the {{GHGterm|imperative Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=קָרַב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=37|verse=17}} (cf. above, {{GHGpar|52|n}}); finally, in the {{GHGterm|imperative Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הַרְחַק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=21}} and {{GHGheb|text=הַמְעַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=69|verse=24}}, in both cases probably influenced by the closing consonant, and by the preference for ''Pathaḥ'' in {{GHGterm|pause}} (according to {{GHGpar|29|q}}); without the pause {{GHGheb|text=הַרְחֵק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=4|verse=24}}, &c.; but also {{GHGheb|text=הַנְחַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=4|verse=11}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|64|i}}
4. As {{GHGterm|infinitive Hithpaʿēl}} with a suffix we find {{GHGheb|text=הִתְיַחְשָׂם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=8|verse=1}}, &c., with a firmly closed syllable, also the {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=מִתְיַחְשִׂים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=7|verse=64}}; Baer, however, reads in all these cases, on good authority, {{GHGheb|text=הִתְיַֽחֲשָׂם}} &c.—The quite meaningless {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} {{GHGheb|text=ונאשאר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=9|verse=8}} (for which the {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} requires the equally unintelligible {{GHGheb|text=וְנֵֽשֲׁאַר}}) evidently combines two different readings, viz. {{GHGheb|text=וְנִשְׁאָר}} (''part. Niph.'') and {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֶשָּׁאֵר}} (''imperf. consec.''); cf. König, {{GHGcite|title=Lehrgebäude}}, i. p. 266 f.—In {{GHGheb|text=יְתָֽאֳרֵ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=44|verse=13}} (also {{GHGheb|text=יְתָֽאֲרֵ֫הוּ}} in the same verse) an {{GHGterm|imperfect Pôʿēl}} appears to be intended by the Masora with an irregular shortening of the ''ô'' for {{GHGheb|text=יְתֹֽאֲר׳}}; cf. {{GHGpar|55|b}} {{GHGheb|text=מְלָשְׁנִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=101|verse=5}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}; on the other hand Qimḥi, with whom Delitzsch agrees, explains the form as {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, with an irregular {{GHGheb|text=־ֳ}} for {{GHGheb|text=־ֲ}}, as in the reading {{GHGheb|text=אֲלַקֳּטָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=2.7}}; cf. {{GHGpar|10|h}}.

5. A few examples in which {{GHGheb|text=א}}, as middle radical, entirely loses its consonantal value and quiesces in a vowel, will be found in {{GHGpar|73|g}}.
<section end="par64" />
<section begin="par65" />{{GHGpar-heading|65|Verbs Third Guttural, ''e.g.'' {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלַח}} to send||<ref>Verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} in which the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} is ''consonantal'' obviously belong also to this class, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גָּבַהּ|translate=to be high}}, {{GHGheb|text=תָּמַהּ|translate=to be astonished}}, {{GHGheb|text=מָהַהּ}} (only in ''Hithpalpel'') ''to delay''.</ref>}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|65|a}}
'''1.''' According to {{GHGpar|22|d}}, when the last syllable has a vowel incompatible with the guttural (i.e. ''not'' an ''a''-sound), two possibilities present themselves, viz. either the regular vowel ''remains'', and the guttural then takes ''furtive Pathaḥ'', or {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} (in pause {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}}) takes its place. More particularly it is to be remarked that—

(''a'') The unchangeable vowels {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=וֹ}}, {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} ({{GHGpar|25|b}}) are always retained, even under such circumstances; hence ''inf. abs. Qal'' {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלוֹחַ}}, ''part. pass.'' {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלוּחַ}}, ''Hiph.'' {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁלִיחַ}}, ''imperf.'' {{GHGheb|text=יַשְׁלִיחַ}}, ''part.'' {{GHGheb|text=מַשְׁלִיחַ}}. So also the less firm ''ō'' in the ''inf. constr.'' {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלֹח}} is almost always retained: cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלַח}}, in close connexion with a substantive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=58|verse=9}}, and {{GHGheb|text=גְּוַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=20|verse=3}}. Examples of the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} with suffixes are {{GHGheb|text=בְּבָרְחֲךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=35|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּפִגְעוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=35|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=לְרִבְעָהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=18|verse=23}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|65|b}}
(''b'') The {{GHGterm|imperfect}} and {{GHGterm|imperative Qal}} almost always have ''ă'' in the second syllable, sometimes, no doubt, due simply to the influence of the guttural (for a tone-long ''ō'', originally ''ŭ''), but sometimes as being the original vowel, thus {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁלַח}}, {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלַח}}, &c.; with suffixes {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁלָחֵ֫נִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלָחֵ֫נִי}}, see {{GHGpar|60|c}}.<section end="par65" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

196.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par65"/>Exceptions, in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=אסלוח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=7}}, {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֶסְלַח}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}); in the {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=טְבֹחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=16}}. On such cases as {{GHGheb|text=אֶפְשֳׂעָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=4}}, cf. {{GHGpar|10|h}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|65|c}}
(''c'') Where {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} would be the regular vowel of the final syllable, both forms (with ''ē<sup>a</sup>'' and ''ă'') are sometimes in use; the choice of one or the other is decided by the special circumstances of the tone, i.e.:—

{{GHGmargin-letter|65|d}}
Rem. 1. In the {{GHGterm|absolute state}} of the {{GHGterm|participle Qal}}, {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}}, the forms {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁלֵחַ}} (with suff. {{GHGheb|text=שֹֽׁלְחִי}}, but {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁלֵֽחֲךָ}}), {{GHGheb|text=מְשַׁלֵּחַ}} (with suff. {{GHGheb|text=מְשַׁלּֽחֲךָ}}), and {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁתַּגֵּעַ}} are used exclusively; except in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ע}} where we find, in close connexion, also {{GHGheb|text=נֹטַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=94|verse=9}}, {{GHGheb|text=רֹגַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=35}}, {{GHGheb|text=רֹקַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=44|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGheb|text=רוֹקַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=136|verse=6}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁסָע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=11|verse=7}}, all with the tone on the last syllable.—The part. Puʿal is {{GHGheb|text=מְרֻבַּע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=45|verse=2}} according to the best authorities (Kittel {{GHGheb|text=מְרֻבָּע}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|65|e}}
2. Similarly, in the ''imperf.'' and ''inf. Niphʿal'', and in the ''perf. inf.'' and ''imperf. Piʿēl'' the (probably more original) form with ''ă'' commonly occurs in the body of the sentence, and the fuller form with ''ē<sup>a</sup>'' in {{GHGterm|pause}} (and even with the lesser distinctives, e.g. with ''D<sup>e</sup>hi'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=86|verse=4}} in the {{GHGterm|imperative Piʿēl}}; with {{GHGterm|Ṭiphḥa}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=12|verse=32}} in the {{GHGterm|infinitive Piʿēl}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=4|verse=31}} {{GHGterm|imperfect Hithpaʿēl}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=16|verse=6}} {{GHGterm|imperfect Niphʿal}}), cf. e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִגָּרַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=27|verse=4}}, with {{GHGheb|text=יִגָּרֵעַֽ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=36|verse=3|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּשָּׁבַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=34}}, even with retraction of the tone in the ''inf. abs. Niphʿal'' {{GHGheb|text=הִשָּׁבַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=30|verse=3}} (elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=הִשָּׁבֵעַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=7|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=12|verse=16|hidebook=1}} twice, in each case without the pause); {{GHGheb|text=תְּבַקַּע־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=3|verse=9}}, with {{GHGheb|text=תְּבַקֵּֽעַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=בַּלַּע|translate=to devour}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=1|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=4|verse=20}} with {{GHGheb|text=בַּלֵּ֑עַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=2|verse=8}}; for {{GHGterm|infinitive Hithpaʿēl}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=20}}. The ''infinitive absolute Piʿē̇l'' has the from {{GHGheb|text=שַׁלֵּחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=22|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=22}}; the {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}}, on the other hand, when without the pause is always as {{GHGheb|text=שַׁלַּח}} except {{GHGheb|text=לְשַׁלֵּחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=4}}.— {{GHGheb|text=יְזַבֵּחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=1|verse=16}} has ''ē'', though not in {{GHGterm|pause}}, and even {{GHGheb|text=וַיְזַבֵּחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=16|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=28|verse=4}}; but ''a'' in {{GHGterm|pause}} in the {{GHGterm|imperative Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵֽאָנַ֑ח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=11}}; ''jussive Piʿēl'' {{GHGheb|text=תְּאַחַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=40|verse=18}}; cf. {{GHGpar|52|n}}. An example of ''ă'' in the {{GHGterm|imperative Piʿēl}} under the influence of a final {{GHGheb|text=ר}} is {{GHGheb|text=כַּתַּר־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=36|verse=2}}, in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=וָתֵּֽעָצַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=13}}, &c.—In {{GHGheb|text=יַפְרִחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=14|verse=9}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=92|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=14|verse=11}}), Barth (see above, {{GHGpar|63|n}}) finds an ''i-imperfect'' of {{GHGterm|Qal}}, since the intransitive meaning is only found in {{GHGterm|Qal}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|65|f}}
3. In the 2nd ''sing. masc.'' of the {{GHGterm|imperative}}, and in the forms of the {{GHGterm|jussive}} and {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}} of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} which end in gutturals, ''a'' alone occurs, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַצְלַח|translate=prosper thou}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַבְטַח|translate=let him make to trust}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּצְמַח|translate=and he made to grow}} (so in ''Hithpalpel'' {{GHGheb|text=יִחְמַהְמַהּ}}, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=2|verse=3}}); even in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּצְלַ֑ח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=29|verse=23}}, and, with the best authorities, {{GHGheb|text=וְיוֹכָֽח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=12|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=וְישַֽׁעֲכֶ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=35|verse=4}} is perhaps to be emended into {{GHGheb|text=וְישִֽׁעֲ׳}} (={{GHGheb|text=וְיוֹשִׁיע׳}}).—In the ''infinitive absolute Ṣere'' remains, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַגְבֵּהַּ|translate=to make high}}; as {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} {{GHGheb|text=חוֹכַח}} also occurs in close connexion ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=26}}); on {{GHGheb|text=הוֹשֵׁעַ}} as {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=26.33}}), cf. {{GHGpar|53|k}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|65|g}}
'''2.''' When the guttural with {{GHGterm|quiescent Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} stands at the end of a syllable, the ordinary strong form remains when not connected with suffixes, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלַ֫חְתָּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלַ֫חְתִּי}}. But in the 2nd ''sing. fem. perfect'' a ''helping-Pathaḥ'' takes the place of the {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁכַ֫חַתְּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=25}} ({{GHGpar|28|e}}); also in, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=3}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָקַ֫חַתְּ}} is to be read, not {{GHGheb|text=לָקַחְתְּ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|65|h}}
Rem. The soft combination with {{GHGterm|compound Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} occurs only in the 1st ''plur. perfect'' with suffixes, since in these forms the tone is thrown one place farther forward, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יְדַֽעֲנ֫וּךָ|translate=we know thee}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=8|verse=2}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=44|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=132|verse=6|hidebook=1}}). Before the ''suffixes'' {{GHGheb|text=ךָ}} and {{GHGheb|text=בֶם}}, the guttural must have {{GHGheb|text=־ֲ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֶשְׁלָֽחֲךָ|translate=I will send thee}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֲשַׁלֵּֽחֲךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=27}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַשְׁמִֽיעֲךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=18|verse=2}}.

On the weak verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}}, see especially § 74.<section end="par65"/><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

197.text:
{{center|II. The Weak Verb.Cf. the summary, {{GHGpar|41}}.}} {{GHGpar-heading|66|Verbs Primae Radicalis Nûn ({{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}}), e.g|| {{GHGheb|text=נָגַשׁ|translate=to approach}} }}
Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Semit. Sprachwiss.}}, p. 138 ff.; {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, p. 595 ff.
{{GHGmargin-letter|66|a}} The weakness of initial {{GHGheb|text=נ‍}} consists chiefly in its suffering ''aphaeresis'' in the {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} and {{GHGterm|imperative}} in some of these verbs (cf. {{GHGpar|19|h}}). On the other hand, the ''assimilation'' of the {{GHGheb|text=נ‍}} (see below) cannot properly be regarded as weakness, since the triliteral character of the stem is still preserved by the strengthening of the second consonant. The special points to be noticed are— {{GHGmargin-letter|66|b}} '''1.''' The ''aphaeresis'' of the Nûn (''a'') in the {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}}. This occurs only (though not necessarily) in those verbs which have ''a'' in the second syllable of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}. Thus from the stem {{GHGheb|text=נגשׁ}}, {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יִגַּשׁ}}, {{GHGterm|infinitive}} properly {{GHGheb|text=גַּשׁ}}, but always lengthened by the feminine termination {{GHGheb|text=ת}} to the segholate form {{GHGheb|text=גֶּ֫שֶׁת}}The law allowing the addition of the feminine termination to the unlengthened form, instead of a lengthening of the vowel, is suitably called by Barth ‘the law of compensation’ ({{GHGcite|title=Nominalbildung}}, p. xiii).; with ''suffix'' {{GHGheb|text=גִּשְׁתּוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=3}}; with the concurrence of a guttural {{GHGheb|text=נָגַע|translate=to touch}}, imperfect {{GHGheb|text=יִגַּע}}, infinitive {{GHGheb|text=גַּ֫עַת}}{{GHGcritic|In the printed book {{GHGheb|text=גַּעַ֫ת}}, but {{GHGheb|text=גַּ֫עַת}} is definitely correct.|Amire80}} (also {{GHGheb|text=נְגֹעַ}}, see below); {{GHGheb|text=נָטַע|translate=to plant}}, infinitive {{GHGheb|text=טַ֫עַת}} (also {{GHGheb|text=נְטֹעַ}}, see below); on the verb {{GHGheb|text=נָתַן|translate=to give}}, see especially {{GHGpar|66|h|nonumber=1}} and {{GHGpar|66|i|nonumber=1}}. On the other hand, ''aphaeresis'' does not take place in verbs which have ''ō'' in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נָפַל|translate=to fall}}, imperfect {{GHGheb|text=יִפֹּל}}, infinitive {{GHGheb|text=נְפֹל}}, with ''suffix'' {{GHGheb|text=נָפְלוֹ}}, also {{GHGheb|text=נִפְלוֹ}}; {{GHGheb|text=לִנְדֹּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=6|verse=2}}, &c.; cf., moreover, {{GHGheb|text=לִנְגֹּעַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=20|verse=6}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=וּנְגֹעַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=19|verse=12}} (even {{GHGheb|text=לִנְגּוֹעַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=7}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=1|verse=10}}); with ''suffix'' {{GHGheb|text=בְּנָגְעוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=15|verse=23}}. Also {{GHGheb|text=לִנְטֹעַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=16}} (but {{GHGheb|text=לָטַ֫עַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=3|verse=2}}); {{GHGheb|text=נְשׂא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=18|verse=3|hidebook=1}}; with ''suffix'' {{GHGheb|text=בְּנָשְׂאִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=28|verse=2}} (elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=שְׂאֵת}}, cf. {{GHGpar|74|i}} and {{GHGpar|76|b}}), {{GHGheb|text=לִנְשָׁק־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=9}}. {{GHGmargin-letter|66|c}} (''b'') In the {{GHGterm|imperative}}. Here the ''Nûn'' is always dropped in verbs with ''a'' in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נגשׁ}}, {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=גַּשׁ}} (more frequently with {{GHGterm|paragogic ā}}, {{GHGheb|text=גְּשָׁה}}; before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} also {{GHGheb|text=גֶּשׁ־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=9}}), ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=גְּשׁוּ}}, &c. Parallel with these there are the curious forms with ''ō'', {{GHGheb|text=גּ֫שִֽׁי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=14}} (with {{GHGterm|retarding}} Metheg in the second syllable, and also {{GHGterm|nasog ʾaḥor}}, according to {{GHGpar|29|e}}, before {{GHGheb|text=הֲלֹם}}) and {{GHGheb|text=גּ֫שׁוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=3|verse=9}} (before {{GHGheb|text=ה֫נָּה}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=38}} (before {{GHGheb|text=הֲלֹם}}) and {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=29|verse=31}}; in all these cases without the {{GHGterm|pause}}. With ''Nûn'' retained, as if in a strong verb, {{GHGheb|text=נְהַג|translate=drive}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=4|verse=24}} ({{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יִנְהַג}}, without assimilation of the ''Nûn''), {{GHGheb|text=וְנִטְעוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=19|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=29|verse=5.28}}; cf. also the verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, which are at the same time {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}}; {{GHGheb|text=נְהֵה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=32|verse=18}}, {{GHGheb|text=נְחֵה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=34}}, {{GHGheb|text=נְטֵה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=8|verse=1}}, &c.; the verb {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}}, {{GHGheb|text=נְשָׂא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=10|verse=12}} (usually {{GHGheb|text=שָׂא}}); cf. {{GHGpar|76|b}}. But, as in the infinitive, the ''aphaeresis'' never takes place in verbs which have ''ō'' in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נְצֹר}}, {{GHGheb|text=נְתֹץ}}, &c.

198.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par66 />{{GHGmargin-letter|66|d}}
'''2.''' When, through the addition of a {{GHGterm|preformative}}, ''Nûn'' stands at the end of a syllable, it is readily assimilated to the second radical ({{GHGpar|19|c}}); thus in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}},<ref>Cf. Mayer Lambert, ‘Le futur qal des verbes {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}}, {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}}, {{GHGheb|text=פ״א}}’, in the {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} xxvii, 136 ff.</ref> e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִפֹּל}} for {{GHGpron|yinpōl}}, {{GHGtranslate|he will fall}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִגַּ֫שׁ}} for {{GHGpron|yingaš}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִתֵּן}} for {{GHGpron|yintēn}}, {{GHGtranslate|he will give}} (on this single example of an {{GHGterm|imperfect}} with original ''i'' in the second syllable, cf. h)<ref>An imperfect in ''a'' ({{GHGheb|text=יִגַּשׁ}}) is given in the Paradigm, simply because it is the actual form in use in this verb.</ref>; also in the {{GHGterm|perfect Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נִגַּשׁ}} for {{GHGpron|ningaš}}; throughout {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} ({{GHGheb|text=הִגִּישׁ}}, &c.) and {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} (which in these verbs always has {{GHGterm|Qibbuṣ}}, in a sharpened syllable, cf. {{GHGpar|9|n}}) {{GHGheb|text=הֻגַּשׁ}}.

The other forms are all quite regular, e.g. the {{GHGterm|perfect}}, {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} and {{GHGterm|participle Qal}}, all {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, {{GHGterm|Puʿal}}, &c.

In Paradigm H, only those conjugations are given which differ from the regular form.

{{GHGmargin-letter|66|e}}
The ''characteristic'' of these verbs in all forms with a preformative is {{GHGterm|Dageš}} following it in the second radical. Such forms, however, are also found in certain verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}} ({{GHGpar|71}}), and even in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} ({{GHGpar|67}}). The {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=גֶּ֫שֶׁת}} and the {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=גַּשׁ}}, also {{GHGheb|text=גֶשׁ־}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=9}}) and {{GHGheb|text=תֵּן}}, resemble the corresponding forms of verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} ({{GHGpar|69}}).—On {{GHGheb|text=יִקַּח}}, {{GHGheb|text=קַח}}, and {{GHGheb|text=קַ֫חַת}}, from {{GHGheb|text=לָקַח|translate=to take}}, see {{GHGpar|66|g|nonumber=1}}.—In {{GHGheb|text=יִקּוֹם}} ({{GHGterm|imperfect Niphʿal}} of {{GHGheb|text=קוּם}}), and in similar forms of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} ({{GHGpar|72}}), the {{GHGterm|full}} writing of the ''ô'' indicates, as a rule, that they are not to be regarded as {{GHGterm|imperfects Qal}} of {{GHGheb|text=נָקַם}}, &c.—Also {{GHGheb|text=אֶסַּק}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=8}}) is not to be derived from {{GHGheb|text=נסק}}, but stands for {{GHGheb|text=אֶסְלַק}} (with a sharpening of the {{GHGheb|text=ס}} as compensation for the loss of the {{GHGheb|text=ל}}), from {{GHGheb|text=סָלַק|translate=to ascend}}, see {{GHGpar|19|f}}, and Kautzsch, {{GHGcite|title=Gramm. des Bibl.-Aram.}}, § 44. Similarly the ''Hiphʿil''-forms {{GHGheb|text=הִשִּׂיקוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=39|verse=9}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַשִּׂיק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=44|verse=15}}, and the Niphʿal {{GHGheb|text=נִשְּׂקָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=78|verse=21}} are most probably from a stem {{GHGheb|text=שֹלק}}, not {{GHGheb|text=נשֹק}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|66|f}}
Rem. 1. The instances are comparatively few in which the forms retain their ''Nûn'' before a firm consonant, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נָטַר}}, imperfect {{GHGheb|text=יִנְטֹר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=5}} (elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=יִטֹּר}}); also from {{GHGheb|text=נָצַר}} the pausal form is ''always'' {{GHGheb|text=יִנְצֹ֫רוּ}} (without the {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=יִצְּרוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=20|verse=28}}); similarly in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=58|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=61|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=3|hidebook=1}} (where, however, {{GHGheb|text=תִּנָּדֵף}} is intended), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=140|verse=2.5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=2|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=40|verse=24}}, the retention of the ''Nûn'' is always connected with the {{GHGterm|pause}}. In {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} this never occurs (except in the irregular {{GHGterm|inf.}} {{GHGheb|text=כְּהִנְדֹּף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=3}}, cf. {{GHGpar|51|k}}), in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} and {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} very seldom; e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לְהַנְתִּיךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=22|verse=20}}, {{GHGheb|text=תָנְתְּקוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=31}}; for {{GHGheb|text=לַנְפִּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=22}} read {{GHGheb|text=לִנְפֹּל}}, according to {{GHGpar|53|q}}. On the other hand, the ''Nûn'' is regularly retained in all verbs, of which the second radical is a guttural, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִנְחַל|translate=he will possess}}, although there are rare cases like {{GHGheb|text=יֵחַת}} (also {{GHGheb|text=יִנְחַת}}) {{GHGtranslate|he will descend}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=21|verse=13}} (even {{GHGheb|text=תֵּ֫חַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=17|verse=10}}; without apparent reason accented as ''Milʿēl''), {{GHGterm|plur.}} {{GHGheb|text=יֵחַ֫תּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=13}} (cf. {{GHGpar|20|i}}; the Masora, however, probably regards {{GHGheb|text=יֵחַת}} and {{GHGheb|text=יֵחַ֫תּוּ}} as {{GHGterm|imperfect Niphʿal}} from {{GHGheb|text=חָתַת}}); {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נִחַם}} for {{GHGheb|text=נִנְחַם|translate=he has grieved}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|66|g}}
2. The {{GHGheb|text=ל}} of {{GHGheb|text=לָקַח|translate=to take}} is treated like the ''Nûn'' of verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}} ({{GHGpar|19|d}}). Hence {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=יִקַּח}}, cohortative ({{GHGpar|20|m}}) {{GHGheb|text=אֶקְחָה}}, {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=קַח}}, in {{GHGterm|pause}} and<section end=par66 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

199.text:
{{GHGcorrected}}
before {{GHGterm|suffixes}} {{GHGheb|text=קָח}} (on {{GHGheb|text=קָֽחֶם־נָא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=48|verse=9}}, see {{GHGpar|61|g}}), {{GHGterm|paragogic}} form {{GHGheb|text=קְחָת}}; {{GHGheb|text=קְחִי}}, &c. (but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=לְקַח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=29|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=37|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=20|verse=16}}, {{GHGheb|text=לִקְחִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=17|verse=11}}, perhaps a mistake for {{GHGheb|text=לָהּ קְחִי}}, cf. LXX and Lucian); {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} {{GHGheb|text=קַ֫חַת}} (once {{GHGheb|text=קְחַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=12|verse=9}}, cf. {{GHGpar|93|h}}); with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָקַ֫חַת}}; with {{GHGterm|suffix}} {{GHGheb|text=קַחְתִּי}}; {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} (cf., however, {{GHGpar|53|u}}) {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יֻקַּח}}; {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, however, is always {{GHGheb|text=נִלְקַח}}.—The meaningless form {{GHGheb|text=קָח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=17|verse=5}} is a mistake; for the equally meaningless {{GHGheb|text=קָחָם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=11|verse=3}} read {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֶקָּחֵם}}. {{GHGmargin-letter|66|h}} 3. The verb {{GHGheb|text=נָתַן|translate=to give}}, mentioned above in {{GHGpar|66|d|nonumber=1}}, is the only example of a verb {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}} with {{GHGterm|imperfect}} in ''ē'' ({{GHGheb|text=יִתֵּן}} for {{GHGpron|yintēn}}; {{GHGheb|text=נִתַּן־}}P. Haupt on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=5}} in his Bible, compares the form of the Assyrian imperfect {{GHGpron|iddan}} or {{GHGpron|ittan}} (besides {{GHGpron|inádin}}, {{GHGpron|inámdin}}) from {{GHGpron|nadânu}} = {{GHGheb|text=נתן}}. But could this one passage be the only trace left in Hebrew of an imperf. in ''a'' from {{GHGheb|text=נתן}}? only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=5}}, elsewhere before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} {{GHGheb|text=יִתֶּן־}}, &c.), and a corresponding {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=תֵּן}} or (very frequently) {{GHGheb|text=תְּנָה}} (but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=8|verse=2}} the very strange reading {{GHGheb|text=תְּנָה}} is no doubt simply meant by the Masora to suggest {{GHGheb|text=נָֽתְנָה}}); before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} {{GHGheb|text=תֶּן־}}, {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=תְּנִי}}, &c. Moreover, this very common verb has the peculiarity that its final ''Nûn'', as a weak nasal, is also assimilated; {{GHGheb|text=נָתַ֫תִּי}} for {{GHGpron|nāthántī}}, {{GHGheb|text=נָתַ֫תָּ}} or, very frequently, {{GHGheb|text=נָתַ֫תָּה}}, with a kind of orthographic compensation for the assimilated ''Nûn'' (cf. {{GHGpar|44|g}}); {{GHGterm|Niphʿal perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=נִתַּתֶּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=9|verse=7}}. {{GHGmargin-letter|66|i}} In the {{GHGterm|infinitive construct Qal}} the ground-form {{GHGpron|tint}} is not lengthened to {{GHGpron|tèneth}} (as {{GHGheb|text=גֶּ֫שֶׁת}} from {{GHGheb|text=נָגַשׁ}}), but contracted to {{GHGpron|titt}}, which is then correctly lengthened to {{GHGheb|text=תֵּת}}, with the omission of {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}} in the final consonant, see {{GHGpar|20|l}}; but with suffixes {{GHGheb|text=תִּתִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּתּוֹ}}, &c.; before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} with the prefix {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} = {{GHGheb|text=לָֽתֶת־}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=5|verse=21}}, and even when closely connected by other means, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=7}}. However, the strong formation of the {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} also occurs in {{GHGheb|text=נְתֹן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=20|verse=21}} and {{GHGheb|text=נְתָן־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=9}}; cf. {{GHGpar|69|m}}, note 2. On the other hand, for {{GHGheb|text=לְתִתֵּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=6|verse=19}} read either {{GHGheb|text=לְתִתּוֹ}} or simply {{GHGheb|text=לָתֵת}}, just as the {{GHGterm|Qerê}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=17|verse=14}}, requires {{GHGheb|text=תֵּת}} for {{GHGheb|text=תתן}}. {{GHGmargin-letter|66|k}} In other stems, the {{GHGheb|text=נ‍}} is retained as the third radical, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שָׁכַ֫נְתָּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=זָקַ֫נְתִּי}} cf. {{GHGpar|19|c}} and {{GHGpar|44|o}}. On the entirely anomalous aphaeresis of the ''Nûn'' with a strong vowel in {{GHGheb|text=תַּ֫תָּה}} (for {{GHGheb|text=נָתַ֫תָּ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=22|verse=41}}, cf. {{GHGpar|19|i}}.—On the {{GHGterm|passive imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יֻתַּן}}, cf. {{GHGpar|53|u}}.
{{GHGpar-heading|67|Verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=סָבַב}} to surround}}
Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Semit. Sprachwiss.}}, p. 155 ff.; {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, p. 632 ff. {{:Gesenius' Hebrew Grammar/Additions and Corrections/175}}
{{GHGmargin-letter|67|a}} '''1.''' A large number of Semitic stems have verbal forms with only two radicals, as well as forms in which the stem has been made triliteral by a ''repetition of the second radical'', hence called verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}. Forms with two radicals were formerly explained as being due to contraction from original forms with three radicals. It is more correct

200.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par67 />to regard them as representing the original stem (with two radicals), and the forms with the second radical repeated as subsequently developed from the monosyllabic stem.<ref>So (partly following Ewald and Böttcher) A. Müller, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} xxxiii. p. 698 ff.; Stade, ''Lehrbuch'', {{GHGpar|385|b}}, c; Nöldeke, and more recently Wellhausen, ‘''Ueber einige Arten schwacher Verba im Hebr.''’ (''Skizzen u. Vorarb.'' vi. 250 ff.). Against Böttcher see M. Lambert, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} xxxv. 330 ff., and Brockelmann, as above.</ref> The appearance of a general contraction of triliteral stems is due to the fact that in biliteral forms the second radical regularly receives {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}} before afformatives, except in the cases noted in {{GHGpar|22|b}} and q. This points, however, not to an actual doubling, but merely to a strengthening of the consonant, giving more body to the monosyllabic stem, and making it approximate more to the character of triliteral forms.

The development of biliteral to triliteral stems ({{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}) generally takes place in the 3rd ''sing. masc.'' and {{GHGterm|fem.}} and 3rd ''plur. perfect Qal'' of ''transitive'' verbs, or at any rate of verbs expressing an activity, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=סָבַב}}, {{GHGheb|text=סָֽבְבָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=סָֽבְבוּ}}: {{GHGheb|text=חָנַן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=5}} (but with suffix {{GHGheb|text=חַנַּ֫נִי}}, ver. 11); sometimes with an evident distinction between transitive and intransitive forms, as {{GHGheb|text=צָרַר|translate=to make strait}}, {{GHGheb|text=צַר|translate=to be in a strait}}; see further details, including the exceptions, in aa. The development of the stem takes place (''a'') necessarily whenever the strengthening of the 2nd radical is required by the character of the form (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חִלֵּל}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֻׁדֵּד}}), and (''b'') as a rule, whenever the 2nd radical is followed or preceded by an essentially long vowel, as, in Qal, {{GHGheb|text=סָבוֹב}}, {{GHGheb|text=סָבוּב}}, in Pôʿl and Pôʿal, {{GHGheb|text=סוֹבֵב}}, {{GHGheb|text=סוֹבַב}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|b}}
'''2.''' The biliteral stem always (except in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} and the {{GHGterm|imperfect Niphʿal}}, see below) takes the vowel which would have been required between the ''second'' and ''third'' radical of the ordinary strong form, or which stood in the ground-form, since that vowel is characteristic of the form ({{GHGpar|43|b}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תַּם}} answering to {{GHGheb|text=קָטַל}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּ֫מָּה}} to the ground-form ''qăṭălăt'', {{GHGheb|text=תַּ֫מּוּ}} to the ground-form ''qăṭălû''; {{GHGterm|infinitive}}, {{GHGheb|text=סֹב}} to {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹל}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|c}}
'''3.''' The insertion of {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}} (mentioned under a), for the purpose of strengthening the second radical, never takes place (see {{GHGpar|20|l}}) in the final consonant of the word, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תַּם}}, {{GHGheb|text=סֹב}}, not {{GHGheb|text=תַּםּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=סֹבּ}}; but it appears again on the addition of afformatives or suffixes, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תַּמּ֫וּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=סֹ֫בּוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=סַבּ֫וּנִי}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|d}}
'''4.''' When the afformative begins with a consonant ({{GHGheb|text=נ‍}}, {{GHGheb|text=ת}}), and hence the strongly pronounced second radical would properly come at the end of a closed syllable, a ''separating vowel'' is inserted between the stem-syllable and the afformative. In the {{GHGterm|perfect}} this vowel is {{GHGheb|text=וֹ}}, in the {{GHGterm|imperative}} and {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=־ֶי}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=סַבּ֫וֹתָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=סַבּ֫וֹנוּ}}, {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=תְּסֻבֶּ֫ינָה}} (for ''sabb-tā, sabb-nû, tasōbb-nā''). The artificial opening of the syllable<section end=par67 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

201.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" />{{GHGcorrected}}</noinclude><section begin="par67"/>by this means is merely intended to make the strengthening of the second radical audible.<ref>Of all the explanations of these separating vowels the most satisfactory is that of Rödiger, who, both for the {{GHGterm|perfect}} and {{GHGterm|imperfect}} (Ewald and Stade, for the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} at least), points to the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}. We must, however, regard {{GHGheb|text=סַבּ֫וֹתָ}} as formed on the analogy not of {{GHGheb|text=גָּלִ֫יתָ}}, but (with P. Haupt) of a form {{GHGheb|text=גָּל֫וֹתָ}} (= ''gālautā'', cf. Arab. ''ġazauta''), while {{GHGheb|text=תְּסֻבֶּינָה}} follows the analogy of {{GHGheb|text=תִּגְלֶינָה}}. [See also Wright, ''Comp. Gr.'', 229 f.]</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|e}}
The {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=תַּ֫מְנוּ}} (for {{GHGheb|text=תַּמּ֫וֹנוּ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=64|verse=7}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=44|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=תָּֽמְנוֹ}} with ''Silluq''), owing to omission of the separating vowel, approximates, if the text is right, to the form of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=קַ֫מְנוּ}} from {{GHGheb|text=קוּם}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|f}}
'''5.''' Since the preformatives of the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}}, of the {{GHGterm|perfect Niphʿal}}, and of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} and {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} throughout, before a monosyllabic stem form an open syllable, they take a ''long'' vowel before the tone (according to {{GHGpar|27|e}}), e.g. {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=יָסֵב}} for ''yă-sēb'', {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=הָסֵב}} for ''yă-sēb'', &c. Where the preformatives in the strong verb have ''ĭ'', either the original ''ă'' (from which the ''ĭ'' was attenuated) is retained and lengthened, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יָסֹב}} in {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} for ''yă-sōb'', or the ''ĭ'' itself is lengthened to ''ē'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֵסֵב}} {{GHGterm|perfect Hiphʿîl}} for ''hĭ-sēb'' (see further under h). The vowel thus lengthened can be maintained, however, only before the tone (except the ''û'' of the {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}, {{GHGheb|text=הוּסַב}} for ''hŭ-săb''); when the tone is thrown forward it becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, according to {{GHGpar|27|k}} (under {{GHGheb|text=א}} and {{GHGheb|text=ה}} {{GHGterm|compound Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תָּסֹב}}, but {{GHGheb|text=תְּסֻבֶּ֫ינָה}}; {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=תָּסֵב}}, but {{GHGheb|text=תְּסִבֶּ֫ינָה}}; {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=הֲסִבֹּתִי}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|g}}
Besides the ordinary form of the imperfects, there is another (common in ''Aramaic''), in which the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} is pronounced {{GHGheb|text=יִסֹּב}} or {{GHGheb|text=יִסַּב}}, the ''first'' radical, not the second, being strengthened by {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}}, cf. {{GHGheb|text=יִשֹּׁם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=9|verse=8}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּקֹּד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=26}}; with ''a'' in the second syllable, {{GHGheb|text=יִגָּ֑ר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=11|verse=7}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִדַּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=4}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּשַּׁח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=2|verse=9}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=יִדֹּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=13}} and frequently, {{GHGheb|text=וָאֶֽכֹּת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=9|verse=21}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=יִסֹּב}} (''turn'' intrans.) {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=5|verse=8}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּקֹּב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=24|verse=11}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִתֹּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=47|verse=12}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=יִחַם}} (with ''Dageš forte implicitum'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=1|verse=1}}; in the plural, {{GHGheb|text=יִתַּ֫מּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=35}}, &c. (in pause {{GHGheb|text=יִתָּ֫מּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=102|verse=28}}); perhaps also {{GHGheb|text=יִמַּל}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִמַּךְ}} (unless these forms are rather to be referred to {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, like {{GHGheb|text=יִדָּ֑מּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִמָּֽלוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=24}}); with suffix {{GHGheb|text=תִּקֳּבֶ֫נּוּ}} occurs (cf. {{GHGpar|10|h}}) in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=25}}; {{GHGterm|Imperfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=יַתֵּם}}, {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=יֻבַּת}}, &c. The vowel of the preformative (which before {{GHGterm|Dageš}} is, of course, short) follows the analogy of the ordinary strong form (cf. also u and y). The same method is then extended to forms with afformatives or suffixes, so that even before these additions the second radical is not strengthened, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּקְּד֫וּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=28}}, &c., for {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּקֹ֫דּוּ|translate=and they bowed the head}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּכְּתוּ|translate=and they beat down}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=44}} (from {{GHGheb|text=כָּתַת}}); {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּתְּמוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִדְּמוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=21}} (cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּסֵּ֫בּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=18|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=5|verse=8}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֻכַּ֫תּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=46|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=20}}). To the same class of apparently strong formations belongs {{GHGheb|text=תִּצַּ֫לְנָה}} (without the separating vowel, for {{GHGheb|text=תְּצִ֫לָּינָה}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=11}} and below, p) ''they shall tingle'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=21|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=19|verse=3}}.—On the various forms of the {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, see under t.

{{:Gesenius' Hebrew Grammar/Additions and Corrections/177}}
<section end="par67"/><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

202.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par67" />{{GHGmargin-letter|67|h}}
'''6.''' The original vowel is retained, see f, (''a'') in the preformative of the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=יָסֹב}} for ''yă-sōb'' (cf. {{GHGpar|47|b|doublesign=1}}, {{GHGpar|63|b|nosign=1}}, and for verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} § 72); (''b'') in the {{GHGterm|perfect Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נָסַב}} for ''nă-săb'' ({{GHGpar|51|a}}); (''c'') in {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=הוּסַב}}, with irregular lengthening (no doubt on the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}}) for ''hōsăb'' from ''hŭ-sab'', imperfect {{GHGheb|text=יוּסַב}} from ''yŭ-sab'', &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|i}}
On the other hand, an already attenuated vowel (''i'') underlies the intransitive ''imperfects Qal'' with ''ă'' in the second syllable (probably for the sake of dissimilating the two vowels), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יֵמַר}} for ''yĭ-măr'' (see p); and in the preformative of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵסֵב}} from ''hĭ-sēb'' (ground-form {{GHGheb|text=הַקְטֵל}}, {{GHGpar|53|a}}), as well as of the participle {{GHGheb|text=מֵסֵב}} (ground-form {{GHGheb|text=מַקְטֵל}}), on the analogy of the perfect. In the second syllable of the Perf. the underlying vowel is ''ĭ'', attenuated from an original ''ă'', which in the strong verb is abnormally lengthened to ''î'' ({{GHGpar|53|a}}). The lengthened from ''ĭ'' is, of course, only tone-long, and hence when without the tone and before {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}} we have e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֲסִבּ֫וֹתָ}}. On the retention of the original ''ă'' in the second syllable, cf. v.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|k}}
'''7.''' The ''tone'', as a general rule, tends to keep to the stem-syllable, and does not (as in the strong verb) pass to the afformatives {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} (2nd ''sing. fem. imperfect''); e.g. 3rd ''sing. fem. perfect'' {{GHGheb|text=חַ֫תָּה}}, in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=חָ֫תָּה}}; with {{GHGheb|text=ר}} and gutturals {{GHGheb|text=מָ֫רָה}} (for {{GHGheb|text=מַ֫רָּה}}), {{GHGheb|text=שָׁ֫חָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=44|verse=26}}; on the other hand, with {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} {{GHGheb|text=וְרַבָּ֫ה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=12}} (but {{GHGheb|text=וָחָֽיָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=16}}). In the 3rd ''plur. perfect'' the tone-syllable varies; along with {{GHGheb|text=דַּ֫לּוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=קַ֫לּוּ}}, we also find {{GHGheb|text=דַּלּ֫וּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=קַלּ֫וּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=רַבּ֫וּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=12}}, {{GHGheb|text=שַׁח֫וּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=3|verse=6}}, &c.; but in {{GHGterm|pause}} always {{GHGheb|text=חָ֫תּוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=תָּ֫מּוּ}}, &c. The tone likewise remains on the stem-syllable in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} in {{GHGheb|text=תָּסֹ֫בִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָסֹ֫בּוּ}}; {{GHGterm|perfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵסֵ֫בָּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵסֵ֫בּוּ}}; {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=תָּסֵ֫בִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָ֫סֵבּוּ}} &c. In the forms with separating vowels, the tone is moved forward to these vowels (or to the final syllable, cf. ee), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=סַבּ֫וֹתָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=תְּסֻבֶּ֫ינָה}}, &c.; except before the endings {{GHGheb|text=תֶם}} and {{GHGheb|text=תֶן}} in the {{GHGterm|perfect}}, which always bear the tone. This shifting of the tone naturally causes the shortening of the merely tone-long vowels ''ē'' and ''ō'' to ''ĭ'' and ''ŭ'' (or ''ŏ'', see n), hence {{GHGheb|text=הֲסִבּ֫וֹתָ}} from {{GHGheb|text=הֵסֵב}}, {{GHGheb|text=תֲּסֻבּ֫ינָה}} from {{GHGheb|text=יָסֹב}}; on cases in which the vowel of the preformative becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, see above, f

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|l}}
'''8.'''
