In several verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, instead of {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, {{GHGterm|Puʿal}} and {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}}, the less frequent conjugation {{GHGterm|Pôʿēl}}, with its passive and reflexive, occurs (most probably on the analogy of the corresponding forms of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, cf. {{GHGpar|72|m}}), generally with the same meaning,<ref>Sometimes both {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and {{GHGterm|Pôʿēl}} are formed from the same stem, though with a difference of meaning, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=רִצֵּץ|translate=to break in pieces}}, {{GHGheb|text=רֹצֵץ|translate=to oppress}}; {{GHGheb|text=חִנֵּן|translate=to make pleasing}}, {{GHGheb|text=חוֹנֵן|translate=to have pity}}; {{GHGheb|text=סִבֵּב|translate=to turn, to change}}, {{GHGheb|text=סוֹבֵב|translate=to go round, to encompass}}.</ref> e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עוֹלֵל|translate=to ill-treat}}, passive {{GHGheb|text=עוֹלַל}}, reflexive {{GHGheb|text=הִתְעוֹלֵל}} (from {{GHGheb|text=עָלַל}}; cf. the ''Hithpôʿēl'' from {{GHGheb|text=רָעַע}}<section end="par67" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

203.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par67" />and {{GHGheb|text=פַּרַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=19}} f.); in a few verbs also ''Pilpēl'' ({{GHGpar|55|f}}) is found, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גִּלְגֵּל|translate=to roll}}, ''Hithpalpēl'' {{GHGheb|text=הִתְגַּלְגֵּל|translate=to roll oneself}} (from {{GHGheb|text=גָּלַל}}); imperative with suffix {{GHGheb|text=סַלְסְלֶהָ|translate=exalt her}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=4|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=שִֽׁעֲשַׁע|translate=to comfort, to delight in}}; passive {{GHGheb|text=שָֽׁעֳשַׁע|translate=to be caressed}} (from {{GHGheb|text=שָׁעַע}}). These forms cannot appear in a biliteral form any more than {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, {{GHGterm|Puʿal}}, and {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=עִוְעִים}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=14}}) and {{GHGheb|text=קַוְקָו}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=18|verse=2.7}}).—For {{GHGheb|text=תִּתָּבָר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=22|verse=27}} read, according to {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=27}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּתְבָּרָר}}.

{{center|{{Small-caps|Remarks}}

I. ''On Qal.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|m}}
1. In the {{GHGterm|perfect}}, isolated examples are found with ''ō'' in the first syllable, which it is customary to refer to triliteral stems with middle ''ō'' (like {{GHGheb|text=יָכֹל}}, {{GHGpar|43|a}}); viz. {{GHGheb|text=רֹ֫מּוּ|translate=they are exalted}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=24}} to {{GHGheb|text=רָמֹם}}; {{GHGheb|text=רֹ֫בּוּ|translate=they shot}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=23}} to {{GHGheb|text=רָבֹב}}; {{GHGheb|text=זֹ֫רוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=6}} to {{GHGheb|text=זָרֹר}}. But this explanation is very doubtful: {{GHGheb|text=זֹ֫רוּ}} especially is rather to be classed among the passives of Qal mentioned in {{GHGpar|52|e}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|n}}
2. ''Imperfects Qal'' with ''ō'' in the second syllable keep the original ''a'' in the preformative, but lengthen it to ''ā'', as being in an open syllable, hence {{GHGheb|text=יָחֹן}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָמֹד}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָעֹז}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָרֹן}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָרֹעַ}} (trans. ''he breaks in pieces'', but {{GHGheb|text=יֵרַע}} intrans.= ''he is evil''); imperfects with ''ă'' have, in the preformative, an ''ē'', lengthened from ''ĭ''. See the examples below, under p, {{GHGpar|63|c}} and e, {{GHGpar|72|h}}, and specially Barth in {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1894, p. 5 f.

The ''Ḥōlĕm'' of the ''infinitive, imperative'', and {{GHGterm|imperfect}} ({{GHGheb|text=סֹב}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָסֹב}}) is only tone-long, and therefore, as a rule, is written defectively (with a few exceptions, chiefly in the later orthography, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=צוֹר|translate=bind up}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=16}}; {{GHGheb|text=גּוֹל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=37|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=דּוֹם}} ver. 7; {{GHGheb|text=לָבֽוֹז}} for {{GHGheb|text=לָבֹז|translate=to plunder}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=3|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=8|verse=11|hidebook=1}}). When this ''ō'' loses the tone, it becomes in the final syllable ''ŏ'', in a sharpened syllable ''ŭ'', or not infrequently even ''ŏ'' (see above, k). Examples of ''ŏ'' are: (''a'') in a toneless final syllable, i.e. before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} or in the {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}}, {{GHGheb|text=רָן־}} (''rŏn'') ''to rejoice'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיָ֫סָב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=18}} (once even with ''ŭ'' in a toneless final syllable, {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫רֻם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=20}}); on the other hand, in the ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּסֹ֫בּוּ}}, {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּסֻבֶּ֫ינָה}}; (''b'') before a tone-bearing ''afformative'' or ''suffix'', e.g. ''imperative 2nd sing. fem.'' {{GHGheb|text=רָנִּ֫י}}, {{GHGheb|text=גָּזִּ֫י}} (cf. ff); {{GHGheb|text=חָנֵּ֫נִי|translate=pity me}}; {{GHGheb|text=סָלּ֫וּהָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=50|verse=26}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְשָׁדֵּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=11|verse=3}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}; {{GHGheb|text=תְּחָגֻּֽהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=14}} (for the defective writing, cf. {{GHGheb|text=יְסֻבֻּ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=40|verse=22}}). In {{GHGheb|text=יָחְנְךָ֫}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=19}} (for {{GHGheb|text=יִחָנְךָ}}) this ''ŏ'' is thrown back to the preformative.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|o}}
On the 2nd plur. fem. imperat. {{GHGheb|text=עֹ֫רָה|translate=make yourselves naked}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=32|verse=11}}, cf. the analogous forms in {{GHGpar|48|i}}.-Quite abnormal is the {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} {{GHGheb|text=רֹ֫עָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=19}} (as {{GHGheb|text=ה}} follows, probably only a case of dittography for {{GHGheb|text=רֹעַ}}, cf. {{GHGheb|text=קֹב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=25}} and {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=16}}); so also are the ''imperatives'' {{GHGheb|text=קָֽבָה־לִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=11.17}}, and {{GHGheb|text=אָֽרָה־לִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, with {{GHGheb|text=ה|translate=paragogic}}. We should expect {{GHGheb|text=קֻ֫בָּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֹ֫רָה}}. If these forms are to be read ''qŏballî, ʾŏrallî'', they would be analogous to such cases as {{GHGheb|text=מִדְבַּ֫רָה}} ({{GHGpar|90|i}}), the addition of the {{GHGterm|paragogic}} {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} causing no change in the form of the word ({{GHGheb|text=קָב־}} like {{GHGheb|text=רָן־}} above). If, however, as Jewish tradition requires, they are to be read ''qāballî, ʾārallî'', then in both cases the {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} must be explained, with<section end="par67" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

204.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par67" />Stade, as the equivalent of ''ō'' ({{GHGheb|text=קֹֽבָה־לִּי}}, &c.; cf. {{GHGpar|9|v}}). Still more surprising is {{GHGheb|text=קָבְנוֹ|translate=curse him}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=13}}, for {{GHGheb|text=קֻבֶּ֫נּוּ}} or {{GHGheb|text=קָבּ׳}}.<ref>For {{GHGheb|text=נוֹ}} as suffix of the 3rd person a parallel might be found in {{GHGheb|text=יֶשְׁנוֹ}}, {{GHGpar|100|o}}, and probably also in the ''Nûn'' of the Phoenician suffix {{GHGheb|text=נם}}: cf. Barth, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} xli. p. 643, and the note on {{GHGpar|100|o}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|p}}
3. Examples with ''Pathaḥ'' in the ''infinitive, imperative'', and {{GHGterm|imperfect}} are {{GHGheb|text=בַּר}} (in {{GHGheb|text=לְבָרָם|translate=to prove them}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=3|verse=18}}); {{GHGheb|text=רָד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=45|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=שַׁךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=26}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּשַׁגָּם|translate=in their error}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=3}} (so ed. Mant., but there is also good authority for {{GHGheb|text=בְּשַׁגַּם}}, from {{GHGheb|text=שַׁ·}} = {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ·}} = {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} and {{GHGheb|text=גַּם}} also; so Baer and Ginsburg). Also {{GHGheb|text=גַּל|translate=take away}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=22}}; and the ''imperfects'' {{GHGheb|text=יֵחַם|translate=it is hot}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=19|verse=6}}, &c. (on the ''ē'' of the preformative cf. n); {{GHGheb|text=יֵמַר|translate=it is bitter}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=יֵצַר|translate=it is straitened}}; {{GHGheb|text=יֵרַךְ|translate=it is soft}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=תֵּשַׁם|translate=it is desolate}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=12|verse=19}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=תֵּשָֽׁם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=19}}); {{GHGheb|text=וַתֵּקַ֫ל|translate=she was despised}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=4}} (but elsewhere in the ''impf. consec.'' with the tone on the penultima, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּ֫צֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=8}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּ֫רַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=11}}, &c., cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=19|verse=7}}); in the 1st ''sing. imperfect'' {{GHGheb|text=אֵיתָ֑ם}}<ref>Also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=6|verse=6}}, instead of {{GHGheb|text=תִּישָׁ֑מְנָה}}, which could only come from {{GHGheb|text=ישׁם}}, {{GHGheb|text=תֵּי֚שׁ׳}} is intended, and {{GHGheb|text=יֶאְשְׁמוּ}} in the same verse is probably only an error for {{GHGheb|text=יֵשַׁ֫מּוּ}}.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=19|verse=14}}, abnormally written fully for {{GHGheb|text=אֵתָם}}, unless {{GHGheb|text=אֶתָּם}} is to be read, as in some MSS., on the analogy of the 3rd sing. {{GHGheb|text=יִתֹּם}}.—In the ''impf. Qal'' of {{GHGheb|text=שׁלל}} the reading of {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=2|verse=8}} varies between {{GHGheb|text=יְשַׁלּ֫וּךָ}} (Baer, Ginsb.) and {{GHGheb|text=יְשָׁלּ֫וּךָ}} (ed. Mant., {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|Jabl.|Biblia Hebraica ex recensione D. E. Jablonski, Berolini, 1699.}}}}).— The following forms are to be explained with Barth ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} xliii, p. 178) as imperfects Qal with original ''ĭ'' in the second syllable, there being no instances of their Hiphʿîl in the same sense: {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫גֶל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָגֵן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=31|verse=5}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּסֶךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=40|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=91|verse=4}}, &c.; perhaps also {{GHGheb|text=תְּצִלֶּ֫ינָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=11}} and {{GHGheb|text=יָהֵל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Job|chapter=31|verse=26}}, &c.; in accordance with this last form, {{GHGheb|text=(בְּ)הִלּוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Job|chapter=29|verse=3}} would also be an {{GHGterm|infinitive Qal}}, not Hiphʿîl (for {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽהֲהִלּוֹ}}), as formerly explained below, under w. Finally the very peculiar form {{GHGheb|text=וַתָּ֫רִץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=53}} may probably be added to the list.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|q}}
Imperfects, with an original ''u'' in the second syllable, are also found with this ''ŭ'' lengthened to ''û'' (instead of ''ō''), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יָרוּן}}, if the text is correct, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=29|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָשׁוּד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=91|verse=6}} (unless it be simply an imperfect from {{GHGheb|text=שׁוּד|translate=to be powerful, to prevail}}); {{GHGheb|text=יָרוּץ}} (if from {{GHGheb|text=רצץ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=4}}, &c. (also defectively {{GHGheb|text=אָרֻץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=30}}; but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=6}}, according to Baer, {{GHGheb|text=וְתָרוּץ}}); {{GHGheb|text=תִּתֻּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=24|verse=11}} (on the sharpening of the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} cf. g above).<ref>According to Stade, {{GHGcite|title=Grammatik}}, § 95, Rem., the pronunciation with ''û'', since it also appears in Neo-Punic [and in Western Syriac, see Nöldeke, {{GHGcite|title=Syr. Gramm.}}, § 48], was that of everyday life.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|r}}
A similar analogy with verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} is soon in the infinitives {{GHGheb|text=לָבוּר}} (for {{GHGheb|text=בֹּר}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=9|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּחֻקוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=27}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=בְּחוּקוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=29}}) for {{GHGheb|text=בְּחֻקּוֹ}}, and in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=אֲמֻֽשְׁךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=21}}. (The forms {{GHGheb|text=חַנּוֹת}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=77|verse=10}}, {{GHGheb|text=שַׁמּוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=36|verse=3}}, {{GHGheb|text=חַלּ֫וֹתִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=77|verse=11}}, formerly treated here as infinitives from {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} stems, are rather to be referred to {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} stems, with Barth, ''Wurzeluntersuchungen'', Lpz. 1902, p. 21.) On other similar cases, see below, under ee. For examples of the ''aramaïzing imperfect'', see above, g.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|s}}
4. In the {{GHGterm|participle}}, the aramaïzing form {{GHGheb|text=שֹֽׁאֲסַ֫יִךְ}} for {{GHGheb|text=שֹֽׁסְסַ֫יִךְ}} occurs in {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=30|verse=16}} (the {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} indicates a {{GHGterm|participle}} from {{GHGheb|text=שָׁסָה}}); {{GHGheb|text=רֹעָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=19}} appears to be a contraction from {{GHGheb|text=רֹֽעֲעָה}}, ''part. fem.'' = ''breaking in pieces.''<section end="par67" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

205.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par67 />{{center|II. ''On Niphʿal.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|t}}
5. Besides the ordinary form of the {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=נָסַב}} with {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=נָסָב}}) and the {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=נָסָב}} with {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} in the second syllable, there is also another with {{GHGterm|Ṣere}}, and a third with {{GHGterm|Ḥolem}}, e.g. {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=נָמֵס|translate=it melts}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=22|verse=15|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=נָסֵ֫בָּה}} (for {{GHGheb|text=נָסַבָּה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=2}}; ''part''. {{GHGheb|text=נָמֵס|translate=molten}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=2|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=נָקֵל|translate=it is a light thing}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=20|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=6}} (''perf.'' {{GHGheb|text=נָקַל}}); with ''ō'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נָגֹ֫לּוּ|translate=they are rolled together}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=34|verse=4}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=63|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=64|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=3|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=1|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=6}}b. In the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} with ''ō'' in the second syllable, on the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} (from which König would also explain the ''perfects'' with ''ō''), we find {{GHGheb|text=תִּדֹּ֫מִּי|translate=thou shalt be brought to silence}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=2}} (unless this form should be referred to {{GHGterm|Qal}} with Qimḥi, Olshausen, König); {{GHGheb|text=יֵרוֹעַ|translate=he suffers hurt}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=11|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=13|verse=20|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=תֵּרוֹץ}} (for ''tirrōṣ'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=29|verse=7}}; with ''ē'' in the second syllable {{GHGheb|text=תֵּחֵל|translate=she profanes herself}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=21|verse=9}}, but {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֵחַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=22|verse=26}}, and {{GHGheb|text=יֵחָ֑ל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=48|verse=11}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֵחַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=8}}, &c. For ''infinitives'', cf. {{GHGheb|text=הִמֵּס|translate=to melt}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=3}} (as ''inf. constr.''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=10}} as ''inf. absol.''); again, with compensatory lengthening in the first syllable, {{GHGheb|text=הֵחֵל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=20|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=14|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, but with suffix {{GHGheb|text=הֵֽחַלּוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=21|verse=4}}; also {{GHGheb|text=הִבּוֹז|translate=to be plundered}}, and {{GHGheb|text=הִבּוֹק|translate=to be emptied}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=3}}; in the {{GHGterm|imperative}}, only {{GHGheb|text=הִבָּ֫רוּ|translate=be ye clean}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=52|verse=11}}. On {{GHGheb|text=הֵרֹ֫מּוּ|translate=get you up}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=10}}, and the corresponding ''imperf.'' {{GHGheb|text=יֵרֹ֫מּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=10|verse=17}}, &c., cf. dd.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|u}}
Examples of the {{GHGterm|perfect Niphʿal}} with sharpening of the initial syllable are, {{GHGheb|text=נִחַל|translate=it is profaned}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=22|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=25|verse=3|hidebook=1}} (from {{GHGheb|text=חָלַל}}); {{GHGheb|text=נִחַר}} (from {{GHGheb|text=חָרַר}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=69|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=102|verse=4|hidebook=1}} (also {{GHGheb|text=נָחַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=29}}); {{GHGheb|text=נִחַת|translate=fractus est}} (from {{GHGheb|text=חָתַת}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mal|chapter=2|verse=5}}; cf. with this in the {{GHGterm|participle}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֵֽחָמִים}} (for ''niḥḥāmîm'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=57|verse=5}}, and {{GHGheb|text=נֵֽאָרִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mal|chapter=3|verse=9}}: in the {{GHGterm|imperative}} and {{GHGterm|infinitive Niphʿal}} such a virtual strengthening of the guttural after preformatives never occurs.—The occurrence of ''u'' instead of ''ô'' as a separating vowel in the {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=נְשַׁדֻּ֫נוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mic|chapter=2|verse=4}} is abnormal.

{{center|III. ''On Hiphʿîl and Hophʿal.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|v}}
6. The second syllable in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} sometimes has {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} instead of {{GHGterm|Ṣere}}, especially under the influence of {{GHGheb|text=ר}} and the gutturals, e.g. {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵמַר|translate=he made bitter}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵשַׁח|translate=he bowed}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵפַר|translate=he hath broken}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=14}}, in {{GHGterm|pause}}, cf. {{GHGpar|29|q}}; otherwise {{GHGheb|text=הֵפֵר}}, ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=הֵפֵ֫רוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=5}}. In {{GHGheb|text=הֵפִיר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=33|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=17|verse=19}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=89|verse=34}}, and in {{GHGheb|text=הֵשׂ֫ירוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=8|verse=4}} (perhaps also in {{GHGheb|text=יְחִיתַן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hab|chapter=2|verse=17}}, but cf. {{GHGpar|20|n}}) there is an assimilation to the corresponding forms of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, see z. Also {{GHGheb|text=הֵצַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=52}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵתַז}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=18|verse=5}}; ''inf.'' {{GHGheb|text=לְהָבַֽר|translate=to cleanse}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=4|verse=11}}, in {{GHGterm|pause}}. But also with other consonants, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֵדַק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=23|verse=15}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵקַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=23}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֵרַךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=23|verse=16}}; ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=הֵסַ֫בּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=5|verse=9.10}} (and so usually in the 3rd ''plur. perf'', except before {{GHGheb|text=ר}} and gutturals, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֵרֵ֫עוּ}}); ''imper.'' {{GHGheb|text=הָשַׁ֑ע|translate=besmear}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=10}}; ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=הָשַׁ֑מּוּ|translate=be astonished}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=5}}; {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=תָּרַ֫ע}} ''Thou dost afflict; part.'' {{GHGheb|text=מֵצַל}} (on ''ē'' in the first syllable, see under i) ''shadowing'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=31|verse=3}} (but {{GHGheb|text=מֵסִיךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=3|verse=24}} is assimilated to the form of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, unless, with Moore, we simply read {{GHGheb|text=מֵסֵךְ}}, or, with incorrect spelling, {{GHGheb|text=מֵסֵיךְ}}. So in the {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=הֲמִישֵׁ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=26}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}, and in the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=הֲתִֽמְךָ}} is {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=33|verse=1|hidebook=1}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|w}}
The ''ē'' of the second syllable, when without the tone, may become ''ĕ'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫תֶל בִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=7}} (see also x). It is unusual (cf. {{GHGpar|53|k}}) to find the ''ē'' written fully as in the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=לְהָפֵיר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=11|verse=10}}. Instead of {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Pathaḥ}} a {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}<section end=par67 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

206.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par67 /><noinclude>{{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} </noinclude><section begin=par /><!-- no section needed -->is found under the preformative in {{GHGheb|text=הֱקִלֹּתַ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=44}}, and a {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} occurs before {{GHGheb|text=ח}} (with a virtual sharpening of the {{GHGheb|text=ח}}) in such forms as {{GHGheb|text=הַֽחִתֹּ֫תָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=9|verse=3}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=11|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=3|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=22|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=6|verse=13}}—in all these cases before {{GHGheb|text=חִ}}.—On {{GHGheb|text=בְּהִלּוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=3}}, see above, p: on {{GHGheb|text=וְהַחְתַּתִּ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=37}}, see below, dd.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|x}}
7. In the {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}} of verbs whose second radical is a guttural, ''ă'' is retained ({{GHGpar|22|d}}) in the second syllable instead of ''ĕ'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫רַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=16|verse=25}}: so also with {{GHGheb|text=ר}}, as {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫צַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=28|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=9}}—but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫פֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=4|verse=9}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|y}}
8. Aramaïzing forms (but cf. Rem. {{GHGpar|67|g}}) in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} and {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} are, {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּסֵּב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=13|verse=18}}, &c.; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju.|chapter=18|verse=23}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תַּמֵּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=21}}, but read {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תֶּ֫מֶר}} from {{GHGheb|text=מָרָה}}: {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּכְּתוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=44}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=45}}), but {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּסֵּ֫בּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=18|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=5|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=29|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַחֵל|translate=profanabo}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=39|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=תַּתֵּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=3}}; without elision of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} (cf. {{GHGpar|53|q}}), {{GHGheb|text=וַיְהַתֵּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=18|verse=27}}, but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=יְהָתֵ֫לוּ}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=תְּהָתֵ֫לּוּ}}; with ''î'' in the second syllable {{GHGheb|text=יַשִּׁים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=50|verse=45|hidebook=1}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=וַנַּשִּׁים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=30}}; in the {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=הִזִּי֫לוּהָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=8}}. In {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֻמְּכוּ|translate=they are brought low}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=יֻכַּת|translate=he is smitten}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=12}} (''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=יֻכַּ֫תּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=46|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=1|verse=7}}); in {{GHGterm|pause}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֻחָֽקוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=23}}, but also {{GHGheb|text=יֻכַּ֑תּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=20}} (so Baer, Ginsb., but ed. Mant., Jabl. {{GHGheb|text=יֻכָּתּוּ}}); with ''ŏ'' in the initial syllable, {{GHGheb|text=הָשַּׁמָּהֿ}} ({{GHGterm|infinitive}} with ''suffix'' = {{GHGheb|text=הָשַּׁמָּהּ}}, cf. {{GHGpar|91|e}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=34}} f., cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=36|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=בָּהְשַׁמָּה}}, with irregular syncope for {{GHGheb|text=בְּהָשַּׁ׳}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=43}}.

{{center|IV. ''In General.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|z}}
9. Verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} are most closely related as regards inflexion to verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} (§ 72). The form of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} is generally the shorter (cf. e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יָסֹב}} and {{GHGheb|text=יָקוּם}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵסֵב}} and {{GHGheb|text=הֵקִים}}); in a few cases, however, the two classes exactly coincide, e.g. in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} with {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}}, in {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} and in the less common conjugations (see above, l).

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|aa}}
10. The developed forms (with three radicals), as mentioned in ''a'', are especially frequent in the 3rd ''sing. masc.'' and {{GHGterm|fem.}}, and the 3rd ''plur. perf. Qal'' (i.e. in forms without an afformative or with an afformative beginning with a vowel) of transitive verbs, or verbs, at any rate, expressing action, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=סָבַב}}, {{GHGheb|text=סָֽבְבוּ}} (but before a suffix also {{GHGheb|text=סַבּ֫וּנִי}}, as well as {{GHGheb|text=סְבָב֫וּנִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=שַׁדּ֫וּנִי}} &c.); {{GHGheb|text=זָמַם}}, {{GHGheb|text=זָֽמֲמָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=אָֽפֲפוּ}}, &c. Sometimes the contracted, ''as well as'' the uncontracted form, is found, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בָּזַז|translate=to plunder, plur.}} {{GHGheb|text=בָּֽזְזוּ}}; in other parts, only {{GHGheb|text=בָּזַ֫זְנוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=35}}, as well as {{GHGheb|text=בַּזּ֫וֹנוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=3|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=זָמַ֫מְתִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=8|verse=14.15}} and {{GHGheb|text=זַמֹּ֫תִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=4|verse=28}}. Other examples of biliteral forms in 2nd ''sing. masc.'' are {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=25|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=32}}; in 1st ''sing.'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=5|verse=9}}. A part from Qal the only example of a developed form is {{GHGheb|text=וְהַחְתַּתִּ֫יּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=37}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|bb}}
On the other hand, the biliteral forms are the more common in the 3rd ''sing.'' and ''plur.'' of perfects which are ''intransitive'', and express a state; cf. {{GHGheb|text=דַּק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=9|verse=21}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=דָּ֑ק}}; elsewhere always a transitive verb); {{GHGheb|text=חַת}}, {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=חַ֫תָּה}}; {{GHGheb|text=מַר}}, {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=מָ֫רָה}} (for ''marrā''); {{GHGheb|text=צַר}}, {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=צָ֫רָה}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=וְחָ֫רָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=24|verse=11}}); {{GHGheb|text=רַךְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=שַׁח}}, {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=שַׁ֫חָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּם}} &c.; ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=חַ֫תּוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּ֫מּוּ}} &c. (but on the tone, cf. ee below). Exception, {{GHGheb|text=עָֽשְׁשָׁה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=6|verse=8}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|cc}}
The intransitive but developed perfects {{GHGheb|text=דָּֽלֲלוּ}} (also {{GHGheb|text=דַּ֫לּוּ}}), {{GHGheb|text=חָלַל}}, {{GHGheb|text=נָֽדְדָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=נָֽדְדוּ}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=נָדָ֫דוּ}}), {{GHGheb|text=סָרַר}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָֽשֲׁשָׁה}} (''plur.'' in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=עָשֵֽׁשׁוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=31|verse=11}}), {{GHGheb|text=צָֽלֲלוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָֽׁחֲחוּ}} (also {{GHGheb|text=שַׁ֫חוּ}}), almost all have, as Mayer Lambert observes, at least an active, not a stative meaning. Triliteral forms of the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} after {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} are {{GHGheb|text=לִסְבֹּב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=לִשְׁדוֹד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=47|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=לִגְזׄז}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=19}} (also {{GHGheb|text=לָגֹז}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=13}}); cf. also {{GHGheb|text=לַחְמָם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=14}}, in ''subordinate pause'', for {{GHGheb|text=לַֽחֲמַם}}; with ''suffix'' {{GHGheb|text=לַֽחֲנַנְכֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=18}}, and, from the same<section end=par67 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

207.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par67 />form {{GHGheb|text=חֲנַן}}, with retraction and modification of the vowel, {{GHGheb|text=לְחֶנְנָהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=102|verse=14}}; also {{GHGheb|text=שְׂחוֹחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=60|verse=14}}, {{GHGheb|text=בִּגְזׄז}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=2}}, {{GHGheb|text=כִּמְסֹס}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=18}}, {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽעֲזוֹז}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=28}}, {{GHGheb|text=בִּצְרוֹר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=26|verse=8}}.—{{GHGterm|Imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=שָׁדְדוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=28}} (cf. {{GHGpar|20|b}}, and ibid. also on {{GHGheb|text=חַֽנְנֵ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=9|verse=14}}); in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִדּוֹד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=7}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=13}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=40}}) from {{GHGheb|text=נדד}}; the strong form here, after the assimilation of the ''Nûn'', was unavoidable. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=יְשָׁדְדֵם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=6}} is anomalous for {{GHGheb|text=יְשְׁדֵּם}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=11|verse=3}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}; the eastern school read the Poʿēl {{GHGheb|text=ישׁודדם}} in the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}); the strengthening of the second radical has been afterwards resolved by the insertion of a {{GHGterm|vocal Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}. Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=יֶֽחֱנַן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=15}} (elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=יָחֹן}}). In {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, the triliteral form {{GHGheb|text=יִלָּבֵב}} is found, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=11|verse=12}}; in ''Hiphʿil'', all the forms of {{GHGheb|text=רנן}}, thus {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=הַרְנִ֫ינוּ}}, {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=תַּרְנִין}}; {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=הַשְׁמֵם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=6|verse=13}}; {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=מַשְׁמִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=3|verse=15}}. That the developed (triliteral) forms possess a certain emphasis is seen from their frequent use in {{GHGterm|pause}}, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=11}} after a biliteral form ({{GHGheb|text=סַבּ֫וּנִי גַם־סְבָב֫וּנִי}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|dd}}
11. The above-mentioned (see g) neglect of the strengthening in aramaïzing forms, such as {{GHGheb|text=יִדְּמוּ}} and the like, occurs elsewhere tolerably often; in the {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=תַּ֫מְנוּ}} for {{GHGheb|text=תַּמּ֫וֹנוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=28}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=44|verse=18}}; cf. above, e); {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=נָבֹ֫זָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=36}} ({{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} {{GHGterm|parag.}} without any influence on the form, cf. o); even with the firm vowel reduced to ''vocal Š<sup>e</sup>wâ;'' {{GHGheb|text=נָֽבְלָ֫ה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=11|verse=7}} for {{GHGheb|text=נָבֹ֫לָּה}} (cohortative from {{GHGheb|text=בָּלַל}}); {{GHGheb|text=יָֽזְמ֫וּ}} for {{GHGheb|text=יָזֹ֫מּוּ}} ibid. ver. 6, ''they purpose''; following the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲמֻֽשְׁךָ}} (see above, r); from ''intransitive imperfects Qal'', {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽצְרִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=19}} (''plur. masc.'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=18|verse=7}}); {{GHGheb|text=יֵֽרְעוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=2|verse=3}}; also {{GHGheb|text=תִּישָׁ֑מְנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=6|verse=6}} (for which read {{GHGheb|text=תֵּישׁ׳}}={{GHGheb|text=תֵּשׁ׳}}) might be explained in the same way.—{{GHGterm|Perfect Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נָֽסְבָ֫ה}} for {{GHGheb|text=נָסַ֫בָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=41|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=נָֽזְלוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=5}} for {{GHGheb|text=נְמַלְתֶּם ;נָזֹ֫לּוּ}} for {{GHGheb|text=נְמַלֹּתֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=11}} (as if from {{GHGheb|text=מָלַל}} not {{GHGheb|text=מוּל|translate=to circumcise}}), cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=8|verse=14}}; {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=תִּמַּ֫קְנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=14|verse=12}}; {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=נֵֽחָמִים}}, cf. u. So also {{GHGheb|text=נָפַץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=11}}, {{GHGheb|text=נָֽפְצָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=19}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=3}}), are perfects {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} from {{GHGheb|text=פצץ}} (= {{GHGheb|text=פּוּץ}}), not {{GHGterm|Qal}} from {{GHGheb|text=נָפַץ}}.—In {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵתַ֫לְתָּ}} (for {{GHGheb|text=הֲתִלֹּ֫תָ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=10}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=34}}); {{GHGheb|text=הֵעֵ֫זָה}} for {{GHGheb|text=הֵעֵ֫וָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=7|verse=13}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=6|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=7|verse=13|hidebook=1}}).

No less irregular is the suppression of the vowel of the stem-syllable in {{GHGheb|text=לְהַפְרְכֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=15}}.—On the perfect {{GHGheb|text=דַּלְיוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=26|verse=7}}, cf. {{GHGpar|75|u}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|ee}}
12. Cases in which the tone is thrown forward on the afformatives (see k) are (''a'') in the {{GHGterm|perfect}}, the 1st ''sing.'' regularly (but cf. {{GHGheb|text=וַֽהֲצֵרֹ֫תִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=10|verse=18}} before {{GHGheb|text=לָהֶם}}) after {{GHGheb|text=ו}} {{GHGterm|consec.}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=19.22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=19|verse=34}}, &c., also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=44|verse=16}} ({{GHGheb|text=חַמּוֹתִ֖י}} before {{GHGheb|text=ר}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=92|verse=11}} (but the text is certainly corrupt; see the Lexicon), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=116|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, perhaps also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=17}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְחַנֹּתִֹי}} (though in this passage, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=17|verse=3}}, the form might be an {{GHGterm|infinitive}} in ''ôth;'' see Delitzsch on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=17}}); in the 2nd ''sing.'' {{GHGheb|text=וְקַצֹּתָ֫ה}} (before {{GHGheb|text=א}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=25|verse=12}}; in the 3rd ''plural'', {{GHGheb|text=רַבּ֫וּ|translate=multi sunt}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=3|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=רַכּ֫וּ|translate=they are soft}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=55|verse=22}} {{GHGheb|text=קַלּ֫וּ|translate=they are swift}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=4|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=1|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=זַכּ֫וּ|translate=they are pure}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=25|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=4|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=שַׁח֫וּ|translate=they did bow}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=3|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=חָר֫וּ|translate=they are burned}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=6}}. A by form of {{GHGheb|text=שָׁתוּ}} ({{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, cf. {{GHGpar|72|dd}}) is {{GHGheb|text=שַׁתּ֫וּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=49|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=9|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|ff}}
(''b'') In the {{GHGterm|imperative}} (a command in an emphatic tone) {{GHGheb|text=רָנִּ֫י|translate=sing}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=54|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=3|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=2|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=רָנּ֫וּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=44|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=7}} (but {{GHGheb|text=רֹ֫נִּי|translate=lament}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=2|verse=19}}), {{GHGheb|text=חָגִּ֫י|translate=keep}} (''thy feasts''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=2|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=7|verse=29}}; {{GHGheb|text=עוּזָּ֫ה}} (= {{GHGheb|text=עֻזָּה}}) before {{GHGheb|text=א}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=29}}. On the retention of the short vowels ''ŭ'' (''ŏ'') and ''ĭ'' before {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}}, in place of the tone-long ''ō'' and ''ē'', see above, k'';'' on the change of the vowel of the preformative into {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, when it no longer stands before the tone, see g.<section end=par67 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

208.text:
{{center|{{Small-caps|The Weakest Verbs}} ({{GHGterm|Verba Quiescentia}}).}} {{GHGpar-heading|68|Verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״א}} e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אָכַל}} to eat}}
Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Semit. Sprachwiss.}}, p. 140 ff.; {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, p. 589 ff.
{{GHGmargin-letter|68|a}} So far as {{GHGheb|text=א}} retains its full consonantal value as a guttural, these verbs share all the peculiarities of verbs ''primae gutturalis'', mentioned in § 63. They are, however, to be treated as ''weak'' verbs, when the {{GHGheb|text=א}} loses its value as a consonant, and coalesces with the preceding vowel (originally short) to form one long syllable. This takes place only in the following very common verbs and forms, as if through phonetic decay:— {{GHGmargin-letter|68|b}} '''1.''' In the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}}, five verbs (viz. {{GHGheb|text=אָבַד|translate=to perish}}, {{GHGheb|text=אָבָה|translate=to be willing}}, {{GHGheb|text=אָכַל|translate=to eat}}, {{GHGheb|text=אָמַר|translate=to say}}, {{GHGheb|text=אָפָה|translate=to bake}}) regularly make the {{GHGheb|text=א}} quiesce in a long ''ô'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יֹאכַל}}.So in the modern vulgar Arabic of South Palestine, ''yaʾkul'' (''he eats'') becomes ''yôkul''. In a few others the ordinary (strong) form is also in use, as {{GHGheb|text=יֹאחֵז}} (18 times) and {{GHGheb|text=יֶֽאֱחֹז}} (3 times) ''he takes hold''; {{GHGheb|text=יׄסֵף}} (see h), also {{GHGheb|text=יֶֽאֱסֹף}}, ''he collects''. This ''ô'' has primarily arisen from an obscuring of ''ô'' ({{GHGpar|9|q}}), and the ''â'' from {{GHGheb|text=־ַאְ}}, the weak consonant {{GHGheb|text=א}} coalescing with ''ă'' to ''â''; cf. {{GHGpar|23|a}}. {{GHGmargin-letter|68|c}} In the second syllable ''ō'' (for original ''ŭ'') never appears, but either ''ē''On this ''ē'' (originally ''ĭ'') as a dissimilation from ''ō'' (originally ''ŭ''), cf. {{GHGpar|27|w}}, and F. Philippi, in the {{GHGcite|title=Zeitschrift für Völkerpsychologie und Sprachwissenschaft}}, xiv. 178. The latter rightly observes that the existence of an original ''u'' in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} of {{GHGheb|text=אָכַל}} is indicated by the form of the {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=אֱכֹל}}, the Arabic ''yaʾkul'' and the Aramaic {{GHGheb|text=יֵאכֻל}}, as well as by the fact that {{GHGheb|text=יֶֽאֱחֹז}} and {{GHGheb|text=יֶֽאֱסֹף}} are found along with {{GHGheb|text=יֹאחֵז}} and {{GHGheb|text=יֹאסֵף}}. or ''ă''; and in {{GHGterm|pause}} almost always ''ē'', even before the tone-bearing ''heavy'' afformative {{GHGheb|text=וּן}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יֽאֹכֵלוּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=18|verse=1}}, without the pause {{GHGheb|text=יֹֽאכְלוּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=28}}. In the 3rd ''sing. masc.'' and 1st ''sing.'' of {{GHGheb|text=אָמַר}}, however, ''ă'' is always retained in pause, {{GHGheb|text=יֹאמַ֫ר}} and {{GHGheb|text=אֹמַ֫ר}}; but in the 2nd {{GHGterm|masc.}} {{GHGheb|text=תֹּאמֵ֑ר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=5|verse=20}}, in the 3rd {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=תֹּאמַֽר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=21}}; in the ''plural'' {{GHGheb|text=יֹאמֵ֑רוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=145|verse=6.11}}, {{GHGheb|text=תֹּאמֵ֫רוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=38}}, with ''Segolta''; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=תּאֹכַֽל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=7}}, &c. But with conjunctive accents in the body of the sentence, ''ă'' (as being a lighter vowel) is used, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תֹּאבַ֖ד לָעַֽד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=9|verse=19}}, but in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=תּאֹבֵֽד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=1|verse=6}}; cf. a similar interchange of ''ē'' and ''ă'' in {{GHGpar|65|c}}. The 3rd ''fem. plur. impf.'' always has the form {{GHGheb|text=תֹּאכַ֫לְנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=11|verse=9}}. {{GHGmargin-letter|68|d}} When the tone moves back, the final syllable of the ''imperfects'' of {{GHGheb|text=אָבַד}} and {{GHGheb|text=אָכַל}}, with a conjunctive accent, also always takes {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יֹ֣אבַד יוֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=3}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיּ֫אֹכַל|translate=and he did eat}}; in {{GHGheb|text=אָמַר}} the loss of the tone from the final syllable only occurs in the form with {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}}

209.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par68 />(but never in the 1st ''sing.'' {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֹמַר}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֹכַל}}), and then the final syllable, if without the {{GHGterm|pause}}, always takes {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַ֫יֹּאמֶר|translate=and he said}} (except {{GHGheb|text=וַתֹּ֫אמַר לוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=7|verse=13}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|68|e}}
In {{GHGterm|pause}}, however, the {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}} (except the 1st pers. of {{GHGheb|text=אָכַל}}, see below) always has the form {{GHGheb|text=וַיֹּאכַ֫ל}} (but ''plur.'' always {{GHGheb|text=יֹאכֵ֫לוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיֹּאכֵ֫לוּ}}), {{GHGheb|text=וַיֹּאמַ֫ר}}; except {{GHGheb|text=וַיֹּ֫אמַר}} in the poetic portion of the book of Job, as 3:2, 4:1, &c., but not in 32:6, in the middle of the verse. The weak {{GHGterm|imperfect}} of {{GHGheb|text=אָחַז}} is always {{GHGheb|text=יֹאחֵז}} and {{GHGheb|text=וַיֹּאחֶז}}, but in the 1st ''sing.'', according to {{GHGpar|49|e}}, {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֹחֵ֫ז}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=6}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֹכֵ֫ל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn.|chapter=3|verse=12.13}} in {{GHGterm|pause}}.—{{GHGheb|text=אָבָה}} and {{GHGheb|text=אָפָה}} are, at the same time, verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, hence {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יֹּאבֶה}} ({{GHGpar|75|c}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|68|f}}
Before ''light'' suffixes the vowel of the second syllable becomes vocal Šewâ, as {{GHGheb|text=יֹֽאכְלֵם}}, {{GHGheb|text=תֹּֽאכְלֶ֫נּוּ}} but {{GHGheb|text=תֹּֽאכַלְכֶם}}.—In a few cases, instead of the ''ô'' in the first syllable an ''ê'' is found, which is due to contraction from the group {{GHGheb|text=־ֶֽ ־ֱ}} (or {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ ־ְ}}) in place of {{GHGheb|text=־ַ ־ְ }}; e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תֵּאתֶה|translate=it shall come}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=4|verse=8}}, from {{GHGheb|text=תֶּֽאֱתֶה}} (from {{GHGheb|text=אָתָה}}); {{GHGheb|text=אֵהָ֑ב}} (for {{GHGheb|text=אֵהַב}}) ''I love'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=17}}, also (four times) {{GHGheb|text=אֹהַב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mal|chapter=1|verse=2}}, &c., with suffixes {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽהֲבֵ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=11|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=14|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, &c. (but only in 1st ''sing.'', otherwise {{GHGheb|text=יֶֽאֱהַב}}, &c., from {{GHGheb|text=אָהֵב}}, {{GHGheb|text=אָהַב}}); {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֵחַ֫ר|translate=and I stayed}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=5}}. The {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} of {{GHGheb|text=אָמַר}} with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} is always {{GHGheb|text=לֵאמֹר|translate=dicendo}}, for {{GHGheb|text=לֶֽאֱמֹר}}.—According to Barth ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1889, p. 179) {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫אצֶל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=25}} is to be regarded as an {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}}, without the obscuring of {{GHGheb|text=־ָא}} to ''ô'', not as {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}}, since {{GHGheb|text=אצל}} elsewhere occurs only in the {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} and {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}; on the original ''i'' in the second syllable, see above, {{GHGpar|67|p}}. For {{GHGheb|text=תְּאָכְ֫לֵהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=20|verse=26}} we should simply emend {{GHGheb|text=תֹּֽאכְל׳}}; the view that it is {{GHGterm|imperfect Pôʿēl}} (which nowhere else occurs) can, as regards the change of ''ô'' to ''ŏ'', be supported only by the very doubtful analogies of {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=62|verse=4}} (see {{GHGpar|52|q}}) and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=101|verse=5}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} (see {{GHGpar|55|b}}), while the view that it is {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} ({{GHGheb|text=תְּאָכְ׳}}={{GHGheb|text=תְּאָֽכְ׳}}={{GHGheb|text=תְּאַכְּ׳}}) rests on no analogy whatever. It would be more admissible to suppose that {{GHGheb|text=תְּאָכְ׳}} stands for {{GHGheb|text=תְּאֻכְּ׳}}, {{GHGterm|Puʿal}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=אֲכֶלְךָ}} for {{GHGheb|text=אֲכַלְּךָ}}, {{GHGpar|27|q}}); but no reason has been discovered for this departure from the natural punctuation {{GHGheb|text=תֹּאכְ׳}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|68|g}}
'''2.''' In the 1st ''pers. sing. imperfect'', where two {{GHGheb|text=א}}’s would ordinarily come together, the second (which is radical) is regularly dropped ({{GHGpar|23|f}}), as {{GHGheb|text=אֹמַר}}<ref>The regularity of this orthography indicates that the contraction of {{GHGheb|text=אַאְ}} to ''â'' in this 1st pers. occurred at a time when in the 3rd and 2nd persons the {{GHGheb|text=א}} was still audible as a consonant (which accordingly was almost always retained in writing). Nöldeke ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} xxxii. 593) infers this from the fact that also in Arabic the 3rd and 2nd persons are still written ''yăʾkŭlŭ, tăʾkŭlŭ'', but the 1st pers. ''ʾâkūlŭ'', not ''ʾăʾkŭlŭ''.</ref> (for {{GHGheb|text=אֹאמַר}}), &c., and even {{GHGterm|plene}} {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאוֹמַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=2|verse=7}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=אֽוֹמְרָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=42|verse=10}}. In the other cases, also, where the {{GHGheb|text=א}} is ordinarily regarded as ''quiescing'' in ''ô'' or ''ê'', it is only retained orthographically, and on etymological grounds. Hence the possibility of its being dropped in the following cases:—

{{GHGmargin-letter|68|h}}
Always in the contracted forms of {{GHGheb|text=אָסַף}}, as {{GHGheb|text=תֹּסֵף}} for {{GHGheb|text=תֹּאסֵף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=29}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיֹּ֫סֶף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=6|verse=1}} (but for {{GHGheb|text=יֵאָֽסֵף}}{{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=19}} read {{GHGheb|text=יֹאסִף}}={{GHGheb|text=יוֹסִף}} with the LXX); cf. also in <section end=par68 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

210.text:
the 1st ''pers.'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=4|verse=6}} and {{GHGheb|text=אֹסִֽפְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=6}}, which is apparently (from the {{GHGterm|Metheg}} with the ''i''), intended for an {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}}: instead of it, however, read, with the Mantua edition, {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽסִפְךָ}} (with ''ĭ'', according to {{GHGpar|60|f}}). But {{GHGheb|text=תֹּֽאסִפוּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=5|verse=7}} (for {{GHGheb|text=תּֽוֹס׳}}), {{GHGheb|text=וַיֹּ֫אסֶף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=29}} (for {{GHGheb|text=וַיּ֫וֹסֶף}}), and {{GHGheb|text=יאסף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=19}} (see above) are due to a mistake, since all three forms must be derived from the stem {{GHGheb|text=יָסַף}}. Furthermore, {{GHGheb|text=יֽׄמְר֫וּךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=20}} (where certainly {{GHGheb|text=יַמְר׳}} is to be read); {{GHGheb|text=תֹּבֵא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=10}} (cf. {{GHGpar|75|hh}}); {{GHGheb|text=וַתֹּפֵ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=24}}; {{GHGheb|text=יוֹכְלוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=42|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=תֹּֽמְרוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַתֹּ֫חֶז}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽוְלִי|translate=thou gaddest about}} (from {{GHGheb|text=אָזַל}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=36}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּ֫תֵא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=21}} (for {{GHGheb|text=יֶֽאֱתֶה}}), according to other readings (on the analogy of the cases mentioned in {{GHGpar|75|p}}) {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵתֵ֫א}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּ֫תֶא}} or {{GHGheb|text=וַיֶּ֫תֶא}}. Paradigm I shows the weak forms of the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}}, and merely indicates the other conjugations, which are regular. {{GHGmargin-letter|68|i}} Rem. 1. In the derived conjugations only isolated weak forms occur: {{GHGterm|Perfect Niphal}} {{GHGheb|text=נֹֽאחֲזוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=32|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=22|verse=9}}; ''Hiph.'' {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫אצֶל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=25}} (but the statement in verse 17 is {{GHGheb|text=וְאָֽצַלְתִּי}}, therefore Qal); equally doubtful is the punctuation of {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫רֶב}} (for {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּֽאֲרֵב}}?) ''and he laid wait'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=5}}, and {{GHGheb|text=אָזִין|translate=I listen}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=32|verse=11}} (on the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}); cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אוֹכִיל}} (''ô'' from ''â'') ''I give to eat'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hos|chapter=11|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֹבִ֫ידָה}} (''ô'' from ''â'') ''I will destroy'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=46|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיּוֹחֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=5}} {{GHGterm|Qerê}} (for {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּאח׳}}); the {{GHGterm|Kethîbh}} appears to require the {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיְיַחֵר}}, from {{GHGheb|text=יחר}} as a secondary form of {{GHGheb|text=אחר}}; but {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּיחַר}}={{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּאחַר}} for {{GHGheb|text=וַיֶּֽאֱחַר}} as {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} is not impossible. On {{GHGheb|text=וָאֽוֹצְרָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=13|verse=13}}, cf. {{GHGpar|53|n}}.—{{GHGterm|Infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=לְהָכִיל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=33}} (={{GHGheb|text=לְהַֽאֲכ׳}} unless it is rather ''infin. Hiph.'' from {{GHGheb|text=כּוּל}}); {{GHGterm|Participle}} {{GHGheb|text=מֵזִין|translate=giveth ear}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=17|verse=4}} (clearly by false analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, for {{GHGheb|text=מַֽאֲזִין}}); {{GHGterm|Imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵתָ֫יוּ|translate=bring}} (from {{GHGheb|text=אָתָה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=12|verse=9}}. (On the same form used for the {{GHGterm|perfect}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=14}}, cf. {{GHGpar|76|d}}.) {{GHGmargin-letter|68|k}} 2. In the {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} the {{GHGheb|text=א}} is sometimes elided (like {{GHGheb|text=ה}} in {{GHGheb|text=יְהַקְטִיל}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַקְטִיל}}), thus {{GHGheb|text=מַלֵּף}} (as in Aramaic and Samaritan) ''teaching'', for {{GHGheb|text=מְאַלֵּף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=35|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=יַהֵל}} (if not a mere scribal error) for {{GHGheb|text=יְאַהֵל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=13|verse=20}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַתַּזְרֵ֫נִי|translate=thou hast girded me}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=22|verse=40}}, for {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּאַזְּרֵ֫נִי}} as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=40}}; {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאַבֶּדְּךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=28|verse=16}}; cf. {{GHGpar|23|c}}.
{{GHGpar-heading|69|Verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}}. First Class, or Verbs originally {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}}, ''e.g.'' {{GHGheb|text=יָשַׁב}} to dwell}}
Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Semit. Sprachwiss.}}, p. 141 f.; {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, p. 596 ff.
{{GHGmargin-letter|69|a}} Verbs which at present begin with Yôdh when without preformatives are divided into two classes according to their origin and consequent inflexion: (''a'') Verbs which (as still in Arabic and Ethiopic) originally began with {{GHGterm|Wāw}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יָלַד|translate=to give birth to}}, Arab. and Eth. ''wălădă''. In consequence of a phonetic change which prevails also with few exceptions in the noun, this {{GHGterm|Wāw}} in Hebrew and Aramaic always becomes a {{GHGterm|Yôdh}}, at least when it is the initial consonant; but after preformatives it either reappears, or is again changed into

211.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par69 />{{GHGterm|Yôdh}}, or, lastly, is altogether elided; (''b'') Verbs which (as in Arabic) originally began with {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} (called ''Verba cum Iod originario'', see § 70). A few verbs again (some with original {{GHGterm|Yôdh}}, and some with original {{GHGterm|Wāw}}) form a special class, which in certain forms assimilates the {{GHGterm|Wāw}} or ''Yâdh'' to the following consonant on the analogy of the ''Nûn'' in verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}} (see § 71).

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|b}}
With regard to verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} (i.e. {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}} with original {{GHGterm|Wāw}}) it is to be noticed that—

'''1.''' In the ''imperfect, imperative'' and ''infinitive construct Qal'' there is a twofold inflexion, according as the {{GHGterm|Wāw}} is wholly rejected or only changed into {{GHGterm|Yôdh}}. The complete rejection (or ''elision'') takes place regularly in eight verbs (see h) in the following manner:

A. {{GHGterm|Imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יֵשֵׁב}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֵדַע}} with an unchangeable<ref>The ''e'' of the first syllable is really ''ê'', not tone-long ''ē'', since it is retained not merely before the tone, and in the counter-tone (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וְיֵדָֽעֵם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=14|verse=10}}), but also in {{GHGheb|text=אֵדָֽעֲךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=13.17}}. It is no objection to this view that the ''scriptio plena'' of this ''ê'' occurs (with the exception of {{GHGheb|text=יֵיקַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=72|verse=14}}, elsewhere pointed {{GHGheb|text=יִיקַר}}) only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=1|verse=8}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=35|verse=9}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=138|verse=6}} the Masora prefers to point {{GHGheb|text=יְיֵדָע}}.—Of the various explanations of the ''ê'' the most satisfactory is that of Philippi ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} xl. p. 653) that an original ''yălĭd'', for example (see above), became ''yilid'' by assimilation of the vowel of the first syllable to that of the second; this then became ''yêlēd'' instead of ''yēlēd'', in an attempt to raise the word again in this way (by writing ''ê'' instead of ''ē'') to a triliteral form.</ref> {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} in the first syllable and original ''ĭ'' in the second, which in the tone-syllable (according to {{GHGpar|27|c}}) becomes ''ē'' (thus {{GHGheb|text=יֵלֵד}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֵצֵא}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֵלֵךְ ;יֵרֵד}}, see x), or, under the influence of a guttural, with ''ă'' in the second ({{GHGheb|text=יֵדַע}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֵקַע}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֵחַד}}).

The tone-long ''ē'' of the second syllable is of course liable to be shortened or to become {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּ֫שֶׁב}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֵֽשְׁבוּ}}, &c.; in the same way ''ă'' becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} in such cases as {{GHGheb|text=יֵֽדְעוּ}}, &c., but is lengthened to {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} in {{GHGterm|pause}} ({{GHGheb|text=יֵדָ֫עוּ}}) and before suffixes ({{GHGheb|text=יֵֽדָעֵם}}).

B. {{GHGterm|Imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁב}} with ''aphaeresis'' of the {{GHGterm|Wāw}} and with tone-long ''ē'', from ''ĭ'', as in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}.

C. {{GHGterm|Infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫בֶת}} from original ''šibh'', by addition of the feminine ending ({{GHGheb|text=ת}}) lengthened to a ''segholate'' form; as in verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}} (cf. {{GHGpar|66|b}}) this lengthening affords a certain compensation for loss of the initial consonant.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|c}}
Rem. Since the infinitives {{GHGheb|text=דֵּעָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=לֵדָה}} (see below, m) point to a ground-form ''diʿat, lidat'', we must, with Philippi ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} xxxii. 42) and Barth (ibid. xli. 606), assign to {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫בֶת}}, &c., the ground-form ''šibt'' (which, therefore, reappears in {{GHGheb|text=שִׁבְתִּי}}, &c.); the apparent ground-form ''šabt'' rests upon the law that the ''ĭ'' of the stem-syllable is changed into ''a'' whenever the syllable becomes doubly closed by the addition of the vowelless feminine ending.<section end=par69 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

212.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par69 />{{GHGmargin-letter|69|d}}
In more than half the number of verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} the original {{GHGterm|Wāw}} in the above-mentioned forms gives place to {{GHGterm|Yôdh}}, which, unless it suffers aphaeresis (see f), appears:—

in the ''imperatives'' {{GHGheb|text=יְצֹק}}, {{GHGheb|text=יְרַשׁ}} and ''infinitives'' {{GHGheb|text=יְסֹד}}, {{GHGheb|text=יְרֹא}}, as a strong consonant, but

in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יִירַשׁ}}, properly ''yiyrăš'', merges with the preceding ''ĭ'' into ''î''.

In the second syllable ''imperfects'' of this form regularly have ''ă''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|e}}
(''a'') That the latter forms are derived from verbs with an original {{GHGterm|Wāw}} (not {{GHGterm|Yôdh}}) is shown partly by the inflexion of these verbs in {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, and {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} (where the original {{GHGterm|Wāw}} reappears throughout), and partly by the Arabic, in which verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} likewise exhibit a twofold formation; cf. ''wălădă'', imperf. ''yălĭdu'', with elision of the {{GHGterm|Wāw}}, and ''wăǵĭlă, yauǵalu'', with retention of the {{GHGterm|Wāw}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|f}}
(''b'') Sometimes both forms, the weaker and the stronger, occur in the same verb; cf. {{GHGheb|text=צַק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=4|verse=41}} and {{GHGheb|text=יְצֹק|translate=pour}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=24|verse=3}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=יִֽצְקוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=18|verse=34}} and the ''infin.'' {{GHGheb|text=צֶ֫קֶת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=38|verse=27}}); {{GHGheb|text=רֵשׁ|translate=take possession}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=15}} (but cf. s), {{GHGheb|text=רָשׁ}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}} for {{GHGheb|text=רַשׁ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=24.31}}; ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=רְשׁוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=9|verse=23|hidebook=1}}, but also, with {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} {{GHGterm|paragogic}}, {{GHGheb|text=יְרָ֫שָׁה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=23}}. In the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יִיקַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=22}} and {{GHGheb|text=יֵקַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=16}} ''it shall be kindled''; {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּיקַר|translate=it was precious}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=30}} and {{GHGheb|text=יֵקַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=49|verse=9}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=יֵיקַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=72|verse=14}}).—The form {{GHGheb|text=וַֽיֱּחֶמוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=39}}, for {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּֽחֲמוּ}}, beside {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּחַ֫מְנָה}} verse 38, is remarkable; cf. {{GHGpar|47|k}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|g}}
(''c'') On {{GHGheb|text=רַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=11}} for {{GHGheb|text=י֖רַד}} and {{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=42|verse=10}} for the {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} {{GHGheb|text=יָשׁוֹב}}, cf. {{GHGpar|19|i}}.—But {{GHGheb|text=יְרַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=13}} (twice) is not intended by the Masora either as {{GHGterm|perfect}} (for {{GHGheb|text=יָרַד}}, which really should be restored) or as {{GHGterm|imperative}} of {{GHGheb|text=יָרַד}}, but as an apocopated {{GHGterm|imperfect Piʿēl}} from {{GHGheb|text=רָדָה}} (={{GHGheb|text=יְרַדֶּה}}) ''to have dominion''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|h}}
(''d'') The eight verbs,<ref>A ninth {{GHGheb|text=יָסַף|translate=to add}}, is also to be included. In the ''Mêšaʿ''-inscription, l. 21, the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} is written {{GHGheb|text=לספת}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=יספתי}}, l. 29); hence read in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=1}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=32|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=29|verse=18}}) {{GHGheb|text=סֶ֫פֶת}} for {{GHGheb|text=סְפוֹת}}. The 2nd ''plur. masc. imperative'' {{GHGheb|text=סְפוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=7|verse=21}} corresponds to {{GHGheb|text=שְׁבוּ}}; thus in proof of a supposed {{GHGheb|text=סָפָה|translate=addere}}, there remains only {{GHGheb|text=אַסְפֶּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=23}}, for which, according to {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=8}}, read {{GHGheb|text=אֹסִ֫פָה}}.</ref> of which the initial consonant in the above-mentioned forms always suffers elision or aphaeresis, are {{GHGheb|text=יָלַד|translate=to bring forth}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָצָא|translate=to go forth}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָשַׁב|translate=to sit, to dwell}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָרַד|translate=to descend}}, also {{GHGheb|text=הָלַךְ|translate=to go}} (cf. below, x); and with ''ă'' in the second syllable of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָדַע|translate=to know}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָחַד|translate=to be united}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָקַע|translate=to be dislocated}}. Examples of the other formation ({{GHGheb|text=יִיוַשׁ}}, &c.) are {{GHGheb|text=יָעֵף|translate=to be wearied}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָעַץ|translate=to counsel}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָשֵׁן|translate=to sleep}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָרֵא}} ({{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יִירָא}}, {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=יְרָא}}) ''to fear''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|i}}
'''2.''' The original {{GHGterm|Wāw}} is retained as a firm consonant: (''a'') in the ''infinitive, imperative'', and {{GHGterm|imperfect Niphʿal}}, being protected by the strengthening, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִוָּשֵׁב}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִוָּשֵׁב}}, which are consequently strong forms like {{GHGheb|text=הִקָּטֵל}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִקָּטֵל}}; (''b'') in the ''Hithpaʿel'' of some verbs, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִתְוַדַּע}} from {{GHGheb|text=יָדַע}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִתְוַכַּח}} from {{GHGheb|text=יָכַח}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִתְוַדָּה}} from {{GHGheb|text=יָדָה}}; otherwise a radical {{GHGterm|Wāw}} at the beginning of a word is now found only in a few nouns, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וָלָד|translate=off spring}} from {{GHGheb|text=יָלַד|translate=to bear}}. At the end of a syllable {{GHGterm|Wāw}} with the homogeneous<section end=par69 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

213.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par69 />vowel ''ŭ'' coalesces into ''ǔ''; so throughout {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הוּשַׁב}} for ''hŭwšabh''; but with a preceding ''a'' the {{GHGterm|Wāw}} is contracted into ''ô'' ({{GHGheb|text=וֹ}}); so in the {{GHGterm|perfect}} and {{GHGterm|participle Niphʿal}} and throughout {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נוֹשַׁב}} from an original ''năwšăbh'', {{GHGheb|text=הוֹשִׁיב}} from an original ''hăwšîbh''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|k}}
The first radical always appears as {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} in the {{GHGterm|perfect}} and {{GHGterm|participle Qal}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָשַׁב}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=ישֵׁב}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָשׁוּב}}, even when {{GHGheb|text=וְ}} precedes, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וְיָשַׁב}} (but {{GHGheb|text=וִיֽשַׁבְתֶּם}}, according to {{GHGpar|24|b}}), also throughout {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and {{GHGterm|Puʿal}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִחֵל|translate=to wait}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֻלַּד|translate=to be born}}, and in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} and {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=יְיַחֵל}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְיֻדָּע|translate=known}} (from {{GHGheb|text=יָדַע}}), and, as a rule, also in ''Hithpaʿel'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִתְיַלֵּד}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִתְיַצֵּב}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִתְיַחֵשׂ}} (as against {{GHGheb|text=הִתְוַדַּע}}, &c., with {{GHGterm|Wāw}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|l}}
The beginner may recognize verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} partly by the {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} under the preformatives; in {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} by the {{GHGterm|Wāw}} ({{GHGheb|text=ו}}, {{GHGheb|text=וֹ}}) before the second radical. (The defective writing, as in {{GHGheb|text=הֹלִיד}}, is rare.) Verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} have forms like {{GHGheb|text=(דַּע) שֵׁב}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫בֶת}}, in common with verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}}. Similarly {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} has the same form as in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} and {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|m}}
Rem. 1. The {{GHGterm|infinitive Qal}} of the weaker form ({{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫בֵת}}, ground-form ''šibt'', {{GHGheb|text=רֶ֫שֶׁת}}; cf. above, c) with suffixes is pointed as {{GHGheb|text=שִׁבְתִּי}},<ref>{{GHGheb|text=וְשַׁבְתִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=23|verse=6}} can hardly be intended for an ''infin.'' with suffix from {{GHGheb|text=יָשַׁב}}, but rather for a ''perf. consec.'' from {{GHGheb|text=שׁוּב}}; but read {{GHGheb|text=וְיָֽשַׁבְתִּי}}.</ref> {{GHGheb|text=רִשְׁתּוֹ}} (the strong form only in {{GHGheb|text=לְיָרְשֵׁ֫נוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=15}}). The masculine form is very rare, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=דֵּעַ|translate=to know}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=32|verse=6.10}}, as also the feminine ending {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=דֵּעָ֫ה}}<ref>The infinitives {{GHGheb|text=דֵּעָה}} and {{GHGheb|text=רְדָה}} belong to the source marked E (Dillmann’s B) in the modern criticism of the Pentateuch. The same document also has {{GHGheb|text=נְתֹן|translate=to give}}, for {{GHGheb|text=תֵּת}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֲלֹךְ|translate=to go}}, for {{GHGheb|text=לֶ֫כֶת}}; and {{GHGheb|text=עֲשׂה|translate=to make}}, for {{GHGheb|text=עֲשׂוֹת}}. See Dillmann, {{GHGcite|title=Die BB. Num., Deut., Jos.}}, p. 618.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=4}}, {{GHGheb|text=לֵדָ֫ה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=3}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=19|verse=3}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=9|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=מֵֽרְדָה}}<sup>2</sup> ''to descend'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=46|verse=3}}, where the change of the ''ē'' into vocal {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} is to be explained, with König, from its position between the principal and secondary tone. From {{GHGheb|text=יָדַע}}, under the influence of the guttural, {{GHGheb|text=דַּ֫עַת}} is formed, with ''suff.'' {{GHGheb|text=דַּעְתִּי}}, &c.; but from {{GHGheb|text=יצא}}, {{GHGheb|text=צֵאת}}. From {{GHGheb|text=יָרַד}} there occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=30|verse=4}} in {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} {{GHGheb|text=מִיָּרְדִי}} (the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} requires {{GHGheb|text=מִיּֽוֹרְדֵי}}) a very remarkable case of the strong form (for {{GHGheb|text=מֵֽרִדְתִּי}}). For {{GHGheb|text=לַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=19}} (generally explained as a case of assimilation of {{GHGheb|text=ד}} to {{GHGheb|text=ת}} in the supposed ground-form ''ladt''; according to Mayer Lambert pausal of {{GHGheb|text=לֵת}}=''lidt'', see above, c) read simply {{GHGheb|text=לֶ֫דֶת}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|n}}
Examples of the strong form of the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} are {{GHGheb|text=יְרֹא|translate=to fear}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=22|verse=25}}, with preposition {{GHGheb|text=לִיסֹד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=16}} (but {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=31|verse=7}} according to Ben Naphtali {{GHGheb|text=לִיסֹּד}}, where the {{GHGheb|text=י}} is only retained orthographically, but is really assimilated to the {{GHGheb|text=ס}}; the reading of Ben Asher, {{GHGheb|text=לְיִסּוֹד}}, accepted by Baer, is meaningless); {{GHGheb|text=לִישׁוֹן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=5|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=לֵרֹא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=29}} is irregular, but probably {{GHGheb|text=לִרֹא}} (for {{GHGheb|text=לִירֹא}}) is intended. With ''suff.''. {{GHGheb|text=בְּיָסְדִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=4}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=3|verse=12}}; with {{GHGheb|text=ת}} {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=יְכֹ֫לֶת|translate=to be able}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=16}}. On {{GHGheb|text=יְב֫שֶׁת}}, which is likewise usually referred to this class, cf. the note on {{GHGpar|70|a}}.
<section end=par69 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

214.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par69 />{{GHGmargin-letter|69|o}}
2. The {{GHGterm|imperative Qal}} frequently has the lengthening by {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שְׁבָה|translate=sit thou}}, {{GHGheb|text=רְדָה|translate=descend thou}}. From {{GHGheb|text=יָהַב|translate=to give}}, Arab. ''wăhăbă'', only the {{GHGterm|imperative}} is used in Hebrew; it has the form {{GHGheb|text=הַב|translate=give}}, lengthened {{GHGheb|text=תָ֫בָה}} generally with the meaning ''age, go to'', hence in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=11|verse=3.4}} even addressed to several persons ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=21}} {{GHGheb|text=הָבָ֫ה}} before {{GHGheb|text=א}} to avoid the hiatus); {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=הָבִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=3|verse=15}}, {{GHGterm|Milraʿ}} on the analogy of the plural {{GHGheb|text=הָב֫וּ}} (once in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=22}} {{GHGheb|text=הָ֫בוּ}} before the tone-syllable; but cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=3}}), whilst, on the analogy of other ''imperatives Qal'' of verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֲבִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֲבוּ}} would be expected.—On {{GHGheb|text=דְּעֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=14}}, cf. {{GHGpar|48|l}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|p}}
3. The {{GHGterm|imperfect}} with {{GHGheb|text=ו}} elided takes ''ă'' in the second syllable, besides the cases mentioned above (under f), also in {{GHGheb|text=תֵּרַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=17}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=3|verse=48}}) and in the pausal form {{GHGheb|text=יֵלַךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=21}}, &c. (from {{GHGheb|text=הָלַךְ}}, see x); on {{GHGheb|text=יֵקַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=16}} see above, f. The ''ă'' in the second syllable, when followed by the afformative {{GHGheb|text=נָה}} ({{GHGheb|text=תֵּרַ֫דְנָה}} &c.), is in accordance with the law mentioned above (under c), by which ''ă'' takes the place of ''ĭ'' in a doubly closed syllable. Forms with ''ē'' in the second syllable shorten the ''ē'' to {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, when the tone is drawn back (before a tone-syllable or after {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יֵֽשֶׁב־נָא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=33}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּ֫רֶד}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיּ֫שֶׁב}}; but ''ē'' is retained in an open syllable, even with Milʿel-tone, in {{GHGheb|text=יֵ֫צֵא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=39}}, in both cases with ''nasog ʾaḥor'', {{GHGpar|29|e}}. The ''pausal'' is either of the form {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּשֵׁב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=4|verse=1}} or {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּרַ֑ד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=10}}; the 1st pers. sing., whether in or out of pause, is {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֵרֵד}}, {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֵלֵד}} &c., except {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֵלַ֑ךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=10}}, see x.—For {{GHGheb|text=יְיֵדָֽע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=138|verse=6}} (cf. the note above, on b and the analogous cases in {{GHGpar|70|d}}) {{GHGheb|text=יֵידָֽע}} is intended.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|q}}
The {{GHGterm|imperfect}} of the form {{GHGheb|text=יִירַשׁ}} is frequently (especially before afformatives) written defectively, in which case the ''î'' can always be recognized as a long vowel by the {{GHGterm|Metheg}} (see {{GHGpar|16|f}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִֽעֲפוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=30}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִֽגְעוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=65|verse=23}}; and so always {{GHGheb|text=יִֽרְאוּ|translate=they fear}}, as distinguished from {{GHGheb|text=יִרְאוּ|translate=they see}} (''imperf. Qal'' of {{GHGheb|text=רָאָה}}).—On {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫ישֶׂם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=50|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=33|hidebook=1}} ''K<sup>e</sup>th'', and {{GHGheb|text=יִיסָךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=30|verse=32}}, see {{GHGpar|73|f}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|r}}
From {{GHGheb|text=יָכֹל|translate=to prevail, to be able}}, the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} is {{GHGheb|text=יוּכַל}}, which can only have arisen through a depression of the vowel from {{GHGheb|text=יוֹכַל}} (ground-form ''yaukhal''=''yawkhal''), to distinguish it, according to Qimḥi, from {{GHGheb|text=אוֹכַל}}, just as, according to {{GHGpar|47|b}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֶקְטֹל}} is differentiated from {{GHGheb|text=יִקְטֹל}}. Cf. the Arabic ''yauruʿu'' (''yôruʿu'') from ''waruʿa, yauǵalu'' (''yôǵalu'') from ''waǵila'', as also the vulgar Arabic (among towns-people) ''yûṣal'', &c., from ''waṣala''. Others regard {{GHGheb|text=יוּכַל}} as an {{GHGterm|imperfect Hophʿal}} (''he is enabled=he can''), always used instead of the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}}; cf., however, {{GHGpar|53|u}}.—{{GHGheb|text=וַתּוּכָֽל}} occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=5}} as 2nd ''sing. fem.'' for {{GHGheb|text=וַתּוּכָֽלִי}}, according to König because the 2nd {{GHGterm|fem.}} had been sufficiently indicated previously.—Further {{GHGheb|text=יוֹרֶה}} or {{GHGheb|text=יֹרֶה}} is to be regarded with M. Lambert ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} xxxvii, no. 73) as ''impf. Qal'' (not ''Hiphʿil'') of {{GHGheb|text=יָרָה|translate=to throw, shoot}} (the supposed ''impf. Qal'' {{GHGheb|text=וַנִּירָם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=30}} is critically very doubtful). This is shown especially by the passages in which the {{GHGterm|impf.}} {{GHGheb|text=יוֹרֶהּ}} is immediately preceded by the ''imperat. Qal'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=13|verse=17}}) or ''infin. Qal'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=64|verse=5}}), or is followed by the {{GHGterm|participle Qal}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=35|verse=23}}; but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=11|verse=24}} by the {{GHGterm|participle Hiphʿil}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|s}}
4. The attenuation of ''ă'' to ''ĭ'' in the {{GHGterm|perfect}} (in a toneless, closed syllable) which is discussed in {{GHGpar|44|d}} (cf. {{GHGpar|64|f}}) occurs in verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} in a few forms of {{GHGheb|text=יָלַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=7}}, &c. (always after {{GHGheb|text=יְ}}), as well as of {{GHGheb|text=יָרַשׁ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וִֽירִשְׁתֶּם}}, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=8|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=17|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=19|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=26|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=31|verse=3|hidebook=1}} (always after {{GHGheb|text=וִי}} for {{GHGheb|text=וְיְ}}). In both cases the attenuation might be explained from the tendency to assimilate the vowels, especially if the initial {{GHGheb|text=יְ}} was pronounced, as in Syriac, like ''i'' ({{GHGpar|47|b}}). In the case of {{GHGheb|text=יָרַשׁ}}, however, a secondary form {{GHGheb|text=יַרֵשׁ}} (cf. {{GHGpar|44|d}}) is probably to be assumed, since in Arabic also the verb is ''wărĭṯă''. The forms<section end=par69 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

215.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par69 />{{GHGheb|text=וִֽירֵשׁ֫וּךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=36|verse=12}} and {{GHGheb|text=וִֽירֵשׁ֫וּהָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=69|verse=36}}, &c., are most simply explained from the return of this ''ĭ''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|t}}
5. As an exception, the {{GHGterm|imperfect Niphʿal}} sometimes has a {{GHGheb|text=י}} instead of the {{GHGheb|text=ו}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּיָּ֫חֶל|translate=and he stayed}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=12}} (unless the {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} or {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּחֶל}}, as in ver. 10, is to be read), cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=19|verse=13}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=8}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}.—The first person always has the form {{GHGheb|text=אִוָּשֵׁב}}, not {{GHGheb|text=אֶוָּשֵׁב}}, cf. {{GHGpar|51|p}}.—In the {{GHGterm|participle}} the plural {{GHGheb|text=נוּגֵי}} (from {{GHGheb|text=יָגָה}}, with depression of ''ô'' to ''û'', cf. {{GHGpar|27|n}}) is found in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=3|verse=18}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=4}}. While in these cases some doubt may be felt as to the correctness of the Masoretic pointing, much more is this so in the perfect {{GHGheb|text=נוּלְּדוּ}} ''null<sup>e</sup>dhû'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=3|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=20|verse=8|hidebook=1}}, for {{GHGheb|text=נֽוֹלְדוּ}} which appears to be required by the {{GHGterm|wāw}} in the initial syllable.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|u}}
6.
