In the {{GHGterm|imperfect Piʿēl}} elision of the first radical ({{GHGheb|text=י}}) sometimes takes place after {{GHGterm|wāw consec.}} (as in the case of {{GHGheb|text=א}}, {{GHGpar|68|k}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּגֶּה}} for {{GHGheb|text=וַיְיַגֶּה|translate=and he has grieved}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=3|verse=33}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּדּוּ}} for {{GHGheb|text=וַיְיַדּוּ|translate=and they have cast}}, verse 53, from {{GHGheb|text=ידה}}, which may also be a true verb {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}} (on the other hand, in {{GHGheb|text=יַדּוּ גוֹרָל|translate=they have east lots}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=4|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ob|chapter=1|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=10}}, a {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} of {{GHGheb|text=יָדַד}} is required by the context; but as this, being a ''transitive'' perfect, ought to have the form {{GHGheb|text=יָֽדְדוּ}} according to {{GHGpar|67|a}}, perhaps we should read {{GHGheb|text=יִדּוּ}}). So from a verb {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}}, of the second class, {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּבְּשֵׁ֫הוּ}} for {{GHGheb|text=וַיְיַבְּשֵׁ֫הוּ|translate=and he made it dry}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=1|verse=4}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּשְּׁרֵם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=32|verse=30}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} (the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} points either to {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיְיַשְּׁרֵם}} or {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּיְשִׁרֵם}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|v}}
7. The {{GHGterm|imperative Hiphʿîl}}, instead of the usual form {{GHGheb|text=הוֹשֵב}}, sometimes has ''î'' in the second syllable; {{GHGheb|text=הוֹצִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=הוֹפִיעַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=94|verse=1}} (before {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, hence probably a mere mistake for {{GHGheb|text=הוֹפִ֫יעָה}}). On the uncertainty of the tone in {{GHGheb|text=הוֹשִׁיעָה־נָּא}} see {{GHGpar|53|m}}. When closed by a guttural the second syllable generally has ''ă'', as {{GHGheb|text=הוֹדַע}}, {{GHGheb|text=הוֹשַׁע}}, cf. also {{GHGheb|text=הֹקַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=17}} (as in the ''infin. constr.'' {{GHGheb|text=הוֹכַח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=26}}; see {{GHGpar|65|f}}). On the other hand, ''î'' always appears when the syllable is open, thus {{GHGheb|text=הוֹשִׁ֫יבָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=הוֹשִׁ֫יבִי}}, and so also before suffixes ({{GHGpar|61|g}}). {{GHGheb|text=הַיְצֵא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=17}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} ({{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} {{GHGheb|text=הוֹצֵא}}, see {{GHGpar|70|b}}) is irregular.—The {{GHGterm|jussive}} and the ''imperfect consecutive Hiphʿîl'' when the tone is drawn back take {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} in the second syllable, as in {{GHGterm|Qal}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=י֫וֹסֶף|translate=that he may increase}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=5}}, before {{GHGheb|text=לֶ֫קַח}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=28}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=3|verse=26}} after {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיֹּ֫סֶף}} ({{GHGheb|text=תּ֫וֹסְףְּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=6}} is anomalous); in {{GHGterm|pause}}, however, also {{GHGheb|text=תּוֹסַף}} as {{GHGterm|jussive}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=40|verse=32}} (usual {{GHGterm|jussive}} in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=יוֹשֵׁב}}, &c., which occurs even without the pause after {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=24|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=8|verse=4}}, &c.). With a final guttural {{GHGheb|text=יֹדַ֫ע}} and {{GHGheb|text=יוֹכַ֫ח}} ({{GHGterm|jussive}}) and {{GHGheb|text=וַיּוֹכַה}} &c.; with a final {{GHGheb|text=ר}} in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=וַתֹּתַֽר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=14}}: on {{GHGheb|text=וְישַֽׁעֲכֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=35|verse=4}}, cf. {{GHGpar|65|f}}).—On forms like {{GHGheb|text=יְהוֹשִׁיעַ}}, see {{GHGpar|53|q}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|w}}
In ''Hophʿal ô'' stands instead of {{GHGheb|text=וּ}}, in {{GHGheb|text=הוֹדַע}} (for {{GHGheb|text=הוּדַע}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=4|verse=23.28}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֹגָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=13}}, and perhaps in {{GHGheb|text=יוֹרֶא}} (for {{GHGheb|text=יוּרֶה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=11|verse=25}}; but cf. Delitzsch on the passage.—''Ptcp.'' {{GHGheb|text=מוּדַ֫עַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=12|verse=5}} ''Q<sup>e</sup>re'' ({{GHGheb|text=מְיֻדַּ֫עַת}} ''K<sup>e</sup>th'').—An {{GHGterm|infinitive Hophʿal}} with feminine ending occurs in {{GHGheb|text=הֻלֶּ֫דֶת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=20}}, for {{GHGheb|text=הֻלֶ֫דֶת}}={{GHGheb|text=הוּל׳}}; cf. above, t, on {{GHGheb|text=נוּלְּדוּ}}, and § 71 at the end.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|x}}
8. The verb {{GHGheb|text=הָלַךְ|translate=to go}}, also belongs in some respects to the {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} class, since it forms (as if from {{GHGheb|text=וָלַךְ}}) {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יֵלֵךְ}}, with {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּ֫לֶךְ}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּלַֽךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=61}}, &c.), 1st sing. {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֵלֵךְ}} (but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֵלַ֑ךְֹ}}); {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} {{GHGheb|text=לֶ֫כֶת}} with suff. {{GHGheb|text=לֶכְתִּי}} ({{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} under the influence of the following palatal, as in {{GHGheb|text=נֶכְדִּי}}, cf. also {{GHGheb|text=נֶגְדִּי}}); {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=לֵךְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=לֶךְ־}}, in the lengthened form {{GHGheb|text=לְכָה}} (as an interjection referring even to a ''feminine'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=32}}, or a ''plural'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=44}}) and {{GHGheb|text=לְךָ}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=25|verse=17}}); ''Hiph.'' {{GHGheb|text=הוֹלִיךְ}} (also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=הוֹלִ֫יכִי}} 2nd ''fem. imperative'' is to be read for {{GHGheb|text=הֵילִ֫יכִי}}, which probably arose merely through<section end=par69 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

216.text:
confusion with the following {{GHGheb|text=הֵינִקִ֫הוּ}}); {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יוֹלִיךְ}}, but in the 1st sing. of the {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}} always {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאוֹלֵךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=2|verse=10}}, &c. Rarely, and almost exclusively late or in poetry, the regular inflexions of {{GHGheb|text=הָלַךְ}} are also found: ''imperf.'' {{GHGheb|text=יַֽהֲלֹךְ}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=58|verse=9}}, &c.; but {{GHGheb|text=תִּֽהֲלַךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=9}}; cf. {{GHGpar|64|a}} and h); {{GHGheb|text=אֶֽהֱלֹךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=22}}, also Mêšaʿ inscription, line 14, {{GHGheb|text=אהלך}}; ''infin.'' {{GHGheb|text=הֲלֹךְ}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=13}} f.16,Cf. above, m, note 2. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=6|verse=8.9}}); {{GHGterm|imperative plur.}} {{GHGheb|text=הִלְכוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=51|verse=50}}. On the other hand, the {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} is always {{GHGheb|text=הָלַךְ}}, {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=הֹלֵךְ}}, {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} {{GHGheb|text=הָלוֹךְ}}, {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נֶֽהֱלַךְ}}, {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִלֵּךְ}}, {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִתְהַלֵּךְ}}, so that a {{GHGheb|text=י}} never arrears unmistakably as the first radical. The usual explanation of the above forms is nevertheless based on a supposed obsolete {{GHGheb|text=יָלַךְ}}. It is, however, more correct to regard the apparent {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} forms of {{GHGheb|text=הלך}} with Praetorius ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZAW.|Zeitschrift für die alttestamentliche Wissenschaft, ed. by B. Stade, Giessen, 1881 ff., and since 1907 by K. Marti.}}}} ii. 310 ff.) as originating with the Hiphʿîl, of which the ground-form ''hahlîkh'' became ''hâlîkh'', and this again, on the analogy of the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} of verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״א}}, ''hôlîkh''. This ''hôlîkh'' being referred to a supposed ''haulîkh'' (properly ''hawlîkh'') gave rise to new formations after the manner of verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}}.
{{GHGpar-heading|70|Verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}}. Second Class, or Verbs properly {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}}, ''e.g.'' {{GHGheb|text=יָטַב}} to be good. Paradigm L}}
Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Semit. Sprachwiss.}}, p. 143 ff.; {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, p. 603 ff.
Verbs properly {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}} differ from verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} in the following points: {{GHGmargin-letter|70|a}} '''1.''' In {{GHGterm|Qal}} the initial Yôdh never suffers aphaeresis or elision; hence the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} has the form {{GHGheb|text=יְבשׁ}},This may be inferred from {{GHGheb|text=בִּיבשׁ}} (={{GHGheb|text=בִּיְ׳}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=11}}, which with its fem. {{GHGheb|text=יְב֫שֶׁת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=7}}, is the only example of an infinitive ''construct Qal'' of these verbs. No example of the {{GHGterm|imperative Qal}} is found: consequently the forms {{GHGheb|text=יְטַב}}, &c. (in Paradigm L of the earlier editions of this Grammar), are only inferred from the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}. the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יִיטַב}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִיקַץ}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִינַק}}. (in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=יִינָק}}.), also written {{GHGheb|text=יִטַב}}, &c.; and so always with a tone-bearing ''ă'' in the second syllable, even after {{GHGterm|wāw consec.}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּיקַ֫ץ}}, except {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫יקֶץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=24}}, and {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫יצֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=7.19}}, unless {{GHGheb|text=יָצַר}} is to be included among verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=נוֹצַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=10}}). {{GHGmargin-letter|70|b}} '''2.''' In {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} the original form {{GHGheb|text=הַיְטִיב}} is regularly contracted to {{GHGheb|text=הֵיטִיב}} (rarely written {{GHGheb|text=הֵטִיב}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵיטִב}}, &c.); {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יֵיטִיב}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּ֫יטֶב}}. Instances of the uncontracted form are {{GHGheb|text=יַיְשִׁ֫רוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=4|verse=25}}, according to Barth (see above, {{GHGpar|67|p}}), an example of an ''i-imperfect'' of {{GHGterm|Qal}}, since the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} is otherwise always ''causative''; {{GHGheb|text=הַיְשַׁר}} ({{GHGterm|imperative}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=9}} {{GHGterm|Qerê}} (the {{GHGterm|Keth.}} requires {{GHGheb|text=הושׁר}} according to the form of verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=45|verse=2}}, {{GHGheb|text=אושׁר}} {{GHGterm|Keth.}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲיַשֵּׁר}} {{GHGterm|Qerê}}), cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=17}} {{GHGterm|Qerê}}; {{GHGheb|text=מַיְמִינִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=12|verse=2}}, to be explained as a denominative from {{GHGheb|text=יָמִין}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַיְסִירֵם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=7|verse=12}} ({{GHGpar|24|f}}, note), but perhaps the punctuation here is only intended to suggest another reading {{GHGheb|text=אֲיַסְּרֵם}}.

217.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" />{{GHGcorrected}}</noinclude><section begin="par70" />{{GHGmargin-letter|70|c}}
Rem. 1. The only verbs of this kind are: {{GHGheb|text=יָטַב|translate=to be good}} (only in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} and in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}; in the {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=טוֹב}}, a verb {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, is used instead), {{GHGheb|text=יָנַק|translate=to suck}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָקַץ|translate=to awake}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָצַר|translate=to form}} (but see above, a), {{GHGheb|text=יָלַל}} only in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵילִיל|translate=to bewail}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָשַׁר|translate=to be straight, right}}, also {{GHGheb|text=יָבֵשׁ}} (Arabic ''yăbĭsă'') ''to be dry'' (but {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הוֹבִישׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=6}}, on the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}}; on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=5}}, cf. {{GHGpar|72|x}}), and the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵימִין}} (denominative from {{GHGheb|text=יָמִין}}), infin. {{GHGheb|text=לְהֵמִין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=19}} ''to go to the right''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|70|d}}
2. In some examples of the {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} the preformative has been subsequently added to the contracted form: {{GHGheb|text=יְיֵטִיב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְיֵלִיל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=15|verse=2.3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=16|verse=7|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֲיֵלִיל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=31}}; plur. {{GHGheb|text=יְיֵלִ֫ילוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=7|verse=14}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=65|verse=14}}. Qimḥi and others explain the above forms from a phonetic interchange of {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} and ''He'', arising from the unsyncopated forms {{GHGheb|text=יְהֵילִיל}}, &c. (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=52|verse=5}}). It is, perhaps, more correct to suppose that the regular forms ({{GHGheb|text=יֵיטִיב}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֵילִיל}}) were originally intended, but that in the later pronunciation the syllable was broken up in order to restore artificially the preformative which had become merged in the first radical.

{{GHGmargin-letter|70|e}}
Isolated anomalies are: {{GHGterm|perfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=וְהֵיטִֽבֹתִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=36|verse=11}} with separating vowel (for {{GHGheb|text=הֵיטַ֫בְתִּי}}) on the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}; {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יֵיטֵיב}} for {{GHGheb|text=יֵיטִיב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=1|verse=47}}; {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽיטְבִי}} ({{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} for {{GHGheb|text=תִּיטְבִי}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּנִיקֵ֫הוּ}} {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=9}}, either an error for {{GHGheb|text=וַתֵּֽינִק׳}}, or an irregular shortening of the first syllable, caused by the forward movement of the tone. Similarly, the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵקִיץ}} (from {{GHGheb|text=קוּץ}}) is always used instead of {{GHGheb|text=הֵיקִיץ}} from {{GHGheb|text=יָקַץ}}; hence also {{GHGheb|text=הֲקִיצ֫וֹתָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֱקִיצֹ֫תִי}}, ''imperat.'' {{GHGheb|text=הָקִ֫יצָה}}, ''infin.'' {{GHGheb|text=הָקִיץ}}.—On {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּבְּשֵׁ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=1|verse=4}}, see {{GHGpar|69|u}}).
<section end="par70" />
<section begin="par71" />{{GHGpar-heading|71|Verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}}. Third Class, or Verbs with Yôdh assimilated}}

In some verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}}, the {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} (or the original {{GHGterm|Wāw}}) does not quiesce in the preceding vowel, but is regarded as a full consonant, and, like ''Nûn'',<ref>These verbs, like verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} (cf. above, note on {{GHGpar|67|g}}), may perhaps have been influenced by the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}}.</ref> is assimilated to the following consonant. These forms, therefore, belong properly to the class of strong verbs. Assimilation invariably takes place in {{GHGheb|text=יָצַע}} (prop. {{GHGheb|text=וצע}}) ''to spread under''; {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִצִּיעַ}}, {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=הֻצַּע}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָצַת|translate=to burn}}, imperfect {{GHGheb|text=יִצַּת}}, {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נִצַּת}}, {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִצִּית}} (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=4}} also {{GHGheb|text=אַצִּיתֶ֫נָּה}} is to be read with König; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=30}} the Masora has rightly emended the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} {{GHGheb|text=והוציתיה}}, which could only be the 1st sing. perf. of a verb {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}}, to the imperative {{GHGheb|text=וְהַצִּית֫וּהָ}} in agreement with the context and all the early versions); {{GHGheb|text=יָצַג}}, {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִצִּיג|translate=to place}}, {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=הֻצַּג}}; and probably also in the forms ordinarily derived from {{GHGheb|text=נָצַב}}, viz. {{GHGheb|text=נִצַּב}} ({{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}), {{GHGheb|text=הִצִּיב}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַצִּיב}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֻצַּב}}; at any rate a stem {{GHGheb|text=יָצַב}} is implied by the {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִתְיַצֵּב}}; instead of the anomalous {{GHGheb|text=וַתֵּֽתַצַּב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=4}} read with the Samaritan {{GHGheb|text=ותתיצב}}, i.e. {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּתְיַצֵּב}}. Besides the common form we find once {{GHGheb|text=אֶצֹּק}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=44|verse=3}} (from {{GHGheb|text=יָצַק|translate=to pour}}) with a ''transitive'' meaning, beside {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּ֫צֶק}} i''ntransitive'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=35}}. Elsewhere the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}<section end="par71" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

218.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par71 />{{GHGterm|consecutive}} has the form {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּצֹק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=28|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=35|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, &c., cf. {{GHGpar|69|f}}, where also other forms of {{GHGheb|text=יָצַק}} are given; {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫יצֶר}} and {{GHGheb|text=יִּצֹּר}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=44|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=8|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=1|verse=5}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}), from {{GHGheb|text=יָצַר|translate=to form}}, are, however, used in the same sense. Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אֶסֳּרֵם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=10|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּשַּׁ֫רְנָה}} (for {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּ׳}} according to {{GHGpar|47|k}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=12}}; {{GHGheb|text=לִיסֹּד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=31|verse=7}} (cf. {{GHGpar|69|n}}) and {{GHGheb|text=מוּסָּד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=16}}. This assimilation is found always with sibilants (most frequently with {{GHGheb|text=צ‍}}) except in the case of {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּקַּץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=3|verse=15}} (so ed. Mant., Ginsb., Kittel; but {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|Jabl.|Biblia Hebraica ex recensione D. E. Jablonski, Berolini, 1699.}}}}, Baer {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּקַץ}}) and in {{GHGheb|text=הֻ֫לֶּדֶת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=5}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=הוּלֶּדֶת}} verse 4), {{GHGterm|infinitive Hophʿal}} of {{GHGheb|text=יָלַד}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=נוּלְּדוּ}} {{GHGpar|69|t}}).<section end=par71 />

<section begin=par72 />{{GHGpar-heading|72|Verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} (vulgo {{GHGheb|text=ע״ו}}), ''e.g.'' {{GHGheb|text=קוּם}} to rise up. Paradigm M}}

Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Semit. Sprachwiss.}}, p. 144 ff.; {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, p. 605 ff.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|a}}
'''1.''' According to {{GHGpar|67|a}} a large number of monosyllabic stems were brought into agreement with the triliteral form by a strengthening, or repetition, of the second radical, i.e. of the ''consonantal'' element in the stem. In another large class of stems the same object has been attained by strengthening the ''vocalic'' element. The ground-form used for these verbs is not, as in other cases ({{GHGpar|39|a}}), the 3rd ''sing. mast. perfect'', but always the {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} form ({{GHGpar|39|b}}), the ''û'' of which is characteristic also of the {{GHGterm|imperative}} and of the ''imperfect indicative Qal''. These stems are consequently termed verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ו}} or more correctly (see below) {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}.<ref>The term {{GHGheb|text=ע״ו}} was consequent on the view that the {{GHGterm|Wāw}} (or {{GHGheb|text=י}} in the case of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ו}}) in these stems was originally consonantal. This view seemed especially to be supported by the return of the {{GHGterm|Wāw}} in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} ({{GHGheb|text=עִוֵּד}}, the {{GHGheb|text=ו}} usually passing into {{GHGheb|text=י}} as in {{GHGheb|text=קִיַּם}}, cf. Arabic ''qáwwămă''), and by certain forms of the {{GHGterm|absolute state}} of the nouns of such stems, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מֶ֫וֶת|translate=death}}, compared with {{GHGheb|text=מוּת|translate=to die}}. Hence in explaining the verbal forms a supposed stem ''qawam'' (in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״י}} e.g. ''šayat'') was always assumed, and {{GHGheb|text=יָקוּם}} was referred to an original ''yaqwŭm'', the {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} {{GHGheb|text=קוֹם}} to original ''qawôm'', the {{GHGterm|participle passive}} {{GHGheb|text=קוּם}} to original ''qawûm''. It must, however, be admitted: (1) that forms like {{GHGheb|text=עִוֵּד}}, {{GHGheb|text=קִים}} (see m) are only to be found in the latest books, and are hence evidently secondary as compared with the pure Hebrew forms {{GHGheb|text=קוֹמֵם}}, &c.; (2) that to refer the verbal forms invariably to the stem {{GHGheb|text=קָוַם}}, leads in many cases to phonetic combinations which are essentially improbable, whereas the assumption of original ''middle-vowel'' stems renders a simple and natural explanation almost always possible. These {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} stems are therefore to be rigidly distinguished from the real {{GHGheb|text=ע״ו}} stems of the strong forms, such as {{GHGheb|text=רָוַח}}, {{GHGheb|text=גָּוַע}}, &c. (see below, gg).—As early as the eleventh century the right view with regard to {{GHGheb|text=״וּ}} stems was taken by Samuel Hannagîd (cf. Bacher, ''Leben und Werke des AbulwaléÆd'', p. 16); recently by Böttcher (''Lehrbuch'', § 1112), and (also as to {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} stems) especially by Müller, Stade, and Wellhausen (see above, {{GHGpar|67|a}}, note). On the other hand, the old view of {{GHGheb|text=ו}} and {{GHGheb|text=י}} as consonants has been recently revived by Philippi, Barth, M. Lambert, and especially Brockelmann (op. cit.).</ref>
<section end=par72 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

219.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par72 />{{GHGmargin-letter|72|b}}
'''2.''' As in the case of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, the monosyllabic stem of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} generally takes the vowel which would have been required in the ''second'' syllable of the ordinary strong form, or which belonged to the ground-form, since this is essentially characteristic of the verbal form ({{GHGpar|43|b}}; {{GHGpar|67|b}}). However, it is to be remarked: (''a'') that the vowel, short in itself, becomes of necessity long in an open syllable as well as in a tone-bearing closed ''ultima'' (except in {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}, see d), e.g. 3rd ''sing. mast. perf.'' {{GHGheb|text=קָם}}, {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=קָ֫מָה}}, ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=קָ֫מוּ}}, but in a closed ''penultima'' {{GHGheb|text=קַ֫מְתָּ}}, &c.<ref>In Aramaic, however, always {{GHGheb|text=קָ֫מְתָּ}}; also in Hebrew grammars before Qimḥi {{GHGheb|text=קָ֫מְתָּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=קָ֫מְתִּי}}, &c., are found, but in our editions of the Bible this occurs only in {{GHGterm|pause}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קָ֑מְתִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=8}}, {{GHGheb|text=מָ֫תְנוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=7|verse=3.4}}.</ref>; (''b'') that in the forms as we now have them the lengthening of the original short vowel sometimes takes place irregularly. Cf. f.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|c}}
Intransitive verbs ''middle e'' in the {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} have the form {{GHGheb|text=מֵת|translate=he is dead}}; verbs ''middle o'' have the form {{GHGheb|text=אוֹר|translate=he shone}}, {{GHGheb|text=בּשׁ|translate=he was ashamed}}, {{GHGheb|text=מוֹב|translate=he was good}}.<ref>According to Stade ({{GHGcite|title=Grammatik}}, {{GHGpar|385|e}} and f) the ''e'' in {{GHGheb|text=מֵת}} is of the nature of a diphthong (from ''ai'', which arose from the union of the vowel ''ĭ'', the sign of the intransitive, with the ''ă'' of the root), and likewise the ''o'' in {{GHGheb|text=אוֹר}}, &c. (from ''au''). But ''ô'' (from ''au'') could not, by {{GHGpar|26|p}}, remain in a closed penultima ({{GHGheb|text=בּ֫שְׁתָּ}}, &c.); consequently the ''o'' of these forms can only be tone-long, i.e. due to lengthening of an original ''ŭ'', and similarly the ''ē'' of {{GHGheb|text=מֵת}} to lengthening of an original ''ĭ''. This is confirmed by the fact that the ''ō'' in {{GHGheb|text=בּשְׁתְּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=בּ֫שְׁתִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=בּ֫שְׁנוּ}} is always, and in {{GHGheb|text=בּ֫שׁוּ}}, 3rd ''plur. perfect'', nearly always (the instances are 11 to 2), written defectively. Forms like {{GHGheb|text=בּ֫וֹשָׁה}}, {{GHGheb|text=בּ֫וֹשׁוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=א֫וֹרוּ}}, &c., are therefore due to orthographic licence.</ref> Cf. n–r.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|d}}
'''3.''' In the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}}, {{GHGterm|perfect Niphʿal}}, and throughout {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} and {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} the short vowel of the preformatives in an open syllable before the tone is changed into the corresponding tone-long vowel. In {{GHGterm|Qal}} and {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} the original ''ă'' is the basis of the form and not the ''ĭ'' attenuated from ''ă'' ({{GHGpar|67|h}}; but cf. also h below, on {{GHGheb|text=יֵבוֹשׁ}}), hence {{GHGheb|text=יָקוּם}}, for ''yăqûm''; {{GHGheb|text=נָקוֹם}} for ''năqôm''; on the other hand, in the {{GHGterm|perfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵקִים}} for ''hĭqîm''; {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=מֵקִים}} (on the Ṣere cf. z); {{GHGterm|perfect Hophʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=הוּקַם}} for ''hŭqam''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|e}}
A vowel thus lengthened before the tone is naturally changeable and becomes {{GHGterm|vocal Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} when the tone is moved forward, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יְמִיתֶ֫נּוּ|translate=he will kill him}}; so also in the 3rd ''plur. imperfect Qal'' with ''Nûn paragogic''; {{GHGheb|text=יְמוּת֫וּן}} (without ''Nûn'' {{GHGheb|text=יָמ֫וּתוּ}}). The wholly abnormal ''scriptio plena'' of ''ē'' in {{GHGheb|text=הַֽהֵימִיר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=11}} (beside {{GHGheb|text=הֵמִיר}} in the same verse) should, with König, be emended to {{GHGheb|text=הֲיָמִיר}}; the incorrect repetition of the interrogative necessarily led to the pointing of the form as {{GHGterm|perfect}} instead of {{GHGterm|imperfect}}.—But in {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} the ''û'' is retained throughout as an unchangeable vowel, when it has been introduced by an abnormal lengthening for the tone-long ''ō'' (as in the {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}).
<section end=par72 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

220.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par72 />{{GHGmargin-letter|72|f}}
'''4.''' The cases of unusual vowel lengthening mentioned in ''b'' are: {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=יָקוּם}} (also in Arabic ''yăqûmu''), but {{GHGterm|jussive}} with normal lengthening ({{GHGpar|48|g}}), {{GHGheb|text=יָקֹם}}, with retraction of the tone {{GHGheb|text=יָ֫קָם}} (''yāqŏm''), {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫קָם}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫קֹם}}); {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=קוּם}}, with normal lengthening of the ''ŭ'' in the 2nd ''plur. fem.'' {{GHGheb|text=קֹ֫מְנָה}}, since, according to {{GHGpar|26|p}}, the ''û'' cannot be retained in a closed penultima; {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} {{GHGheb|text=קוּם}}. In {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} the original ''ĭ'' is naturally lengthened to ''î'' ({{GHGheb|text=הֵקִים}}, {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יָקִים}}, {{GHGterm|jussive}} {{GHGheb|text=יָקִם}}, with retraction of the tone {{GHGheb|text=יָ֫קֶם}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫קֶם}}); on the transference of this ''î'' to the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} of the strong verb, cf. {{GHGpar|53|a}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|g}}
The following forms require special consideration: the {{GHGterm|participle Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=קָם}} is to be traced to the ground-form with ''â'' unobscured, Arab. ''qâtĭl'', {{GHGpar|9|q}}, and {{GHGpar|50|b}}. On this analogy the form would be ''qâĭm'',<ref>So in Arabic, prop. ''qâʾĭm'', since the two vowels are kept apart by the insertion of an {{GHGheb|text=א}}, cf. Aram. {{GHGheb|text=קָאֵם}}; but also contracted, as ''šâk'', ''hâr'', for ''šâʾĭk'', &c. (cf. Wright’s ''Gramm. of the Arabic Language'', 2nd ed. vol. i. p. 164).</ref> which after absorption of the ''ĭ'' became {{GHGheb|text=קָם}}, owing to the predominating character of the ''â''. The unchangeableness of the ''â'' (''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=קָמִים}}, {{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=קָמֵי}}, &c.) favours this explanation.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|h}}
In the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}}, besides the forms with original ''ŭ'' (now ''û'') there are also forms with original ''ă''. This ''ă'' was lengthened to ''ā'', and then further obscured to ''ô''; hence especially {{GHGheb|text=(יָבֹא) יָבוֹא}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּבֹא}}, &c., from the {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=בָּא|translate=he has come}}. In the ''imperfects'' {{GHGheb|text=יֵאוֹר}} (but cf. {{GHGheb|text=וַתָּאֹ֫רְנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=27}}) and {{GHGheb|text=יֵבוֹשׁ}} from the ''intransitive perfects'' {{GHGheb|text=אוֹר}}, {{GHGheb|text=בּשׁ}} (see above, c), most probably also in {{GHGheb|text=יֵאֹ֫תוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=12|verse=9}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֵאוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=15}} from an unused {{GHGheb|text=אות|translate=to consent}}, and perhaps in {{GHGheb|text=וַתֵּהֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=5}}, &c., as in the cases noticed in {{GHGpar|63|e}} and especially {{GHGpar|67|n}}, the ''ē'' of the preformative is lengthened from ''ĭ'' (which is attenuated from original ''ă'') and thus ''yĭ-băš'' became ''yĭ-bāš'', and finally ''yē-bôš''. Finally the ''Niph.'' {{GHGheb|text=נָקוֹם}} (''nă-qām''), {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יִקּוֹם}} from ''yiqqām'', originally ({{GHGpar|51|m}}) ''yinqăm'', arises in the same way from the obscuring of ''ā'' lengthened from ''ă''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|i}}
'''5.''' In the {{GHGterm|perfect Niphʿal}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} a {{GHGheb|text=וֹ}} is inserted before the afformatives beginning with a consonant in the 1st and 2nd persons, and {{GHGheb|text=־ֶי}} regularly (but see Rem.) in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}}, sometimes also in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} (as in {{GHGheb|text=תְּבִיאֶ֫ינָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=7|verse=30}}, cf. {{GHGheb|text=תְּהִימֶ֫נַּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=2|verse=12}}), before the termination of {{GHGheb|text=נָה}}. As in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} ({{GHGpar|67|d}} and note) these ''separating vowels'' serve as an artificial opening of the preceding syllable, in order to preserve the long vowel; in the {{GHGterm|perfect Hiphʿîl}}, however, before the {{GHGheb|text=וֹ}}, instead of the ''î'' an ''ē'' is somewhat often found<ref>{{GHGheb|text=וַֽהֲשֵֽׁיבֹתֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=7}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=6|verse=25}}) could only be an orthographic licence for {{GHGheb|text=והשֵֽׁב׳}}; perhaps, however, {{GHGheb|text=והשִֽׁיב׳}} was originally intended.</ref> (as a normal lengthening of the original ''ĭ''), especially after ''wāw {{hyphenated word start|con|consecutive}}''<section end=par72 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

221.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par72 />''{{hyphenated word end|secutive|consecutive}}'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=39}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=30|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, as well as before the afformatives {{GHGheb|text=תֶם}} and {{GHGheb|text=תֶן}} or before suffixes, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=22|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=34}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=34|verse=4}}. For in all these cases the tone is removed from the {{GHGheb|text=וֹ}} to the following syllable, and this forward movement of the tone produces at the same time a weakening of the ''î'' to ''ē''; thus {{GHGheb|text=הֵקִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֲקִימ֫וֹתָ}} (or {{GHGheb|text=הֱק׳}}; on {{GHGheb|text=הַֽעֵדֹ֫תָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=19|verse=23}}, cf. x), but {{GHGheb|text=וַֽהֲקֵֽמֹתָ}}, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=30}}, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=39}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=18|verse=26}} (cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=וַֽהֲקֵמֹנ֫וּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=5|verse=4}}). In the same way in the 1st ''pers. sing.'' of the {{GHGterm|perfect Niphʿal}}, the ''ô'' before the separating vowel is always modified to ''û'' ({{GHGheb|text=נְקוּמ֫וֹתִ׳}}); cf. v. In the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} the separating vowel {{GHGheb|text=־ֶי}} always bears the tone ({{GHGheb|text=תְּקוּמֶ֫ינָה}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|k}}
Without the separating vowel and consequently with the tone-long ''ō'' and ''ē'' instead of ''û'' and ''î'' we find in {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=תָּבֹ֫אנָה}} (see {{GHGpar|76|g}}); {{GHGheb|text=תָּשֹׁ֫בְןָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=55}} (also {{GHGheb|text=תְּשׁוּבֶ֫ינָה}} in the same verse); {{GHGheb|text=וַתָּשֹׁ֫בְנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=7|verse=14}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=35|verse=9}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}; on the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} {{GHGheb|text=תֵּישַׁ֫בְנָה}} cf. above, note on {{GHGpar|69|b}}); {{GHGheb|text=וַתָּאֹ֫רְנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=27}}, from {{GHGheb|text=אוֹר}} ({{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּרְאֶ֫נָה|translate=and they saw}}, see {{GHGpar|75|w}}); in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֵנַ֫פְתָּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=25}}, also {{GHGheb|text=הֲנִיפ֫וֹתִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=וְהֵֽטַלְתִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=26}}; {{GHGheb|text=תָּשֵׁ֫בְנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=20|verse=10}}; with a separating vowel, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תְּבִיאֶ֫ינָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv.|chapter=7|verse=30}} from {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹא}}. {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} without {{GHGheb|text=י}} occurs in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} in {{GHGheb|text=תְּמוּתֶ֫נָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=1|verse=17}}; and in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=2|verse=12}}: the Dageš in the ''Nûn'' is, with Baer, to be rejected in all three cases according to the best authorities. Wholly abnormal is {{GHGheb|text=תָּקִ֫ימְנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=44|verse=25}}, probably an erroneous transposition of {{GHGheb|text=ימ‍}} (for {{GHGheb|text=תְּקִמֶ֫ינָה}}), unless it originates from an incorrect spelling {{GHGheb|text=תָּקֵ֫ימְנָה}} or {{GHGheb|text=תְּקִימֶ֫נָה}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|l}}
'''6.''' The tone, as in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} (cf. {{GHGpar|67|k}}), is also generally retained on the stem-syllable in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} before the afformatives {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=וּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}}; thus {{GHGheb|text=קָ֫מָה}} (but also {{GHGheb|text=בָּזָ֫ה לְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=19|verse=21}}, probably for the sake of rhythmical uniformity with the following {{GHGheb|text=לָֽעֲגָה לְךָ}}; after {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} {{GHGheb|text=וְשָׁבָ֫ה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=17}}); {{GHGheb|text=קָ֫מוּ}} (but also {{GHGheb|text=קָמ֫וּ}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=76|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=5|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=4|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=וְרָצ֫וּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=8|verse=11}}; so especially before a following {{GHGheb|text=א}}, cf. {{GHGpar|49|l}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=13|verse=32}}; {{GHGheb|text=וְנָע֫וּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=1}}; before {{GHGheb|text=ע}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=131|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=4|verse=14}}); {{GHGheb|text=תָּק֫וּמִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָק֫וּמוּ}}, but before a ''suffix'' or with ''Nûn paragogic'' {{GHGheb|text=וַיְסֻכ֫וּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=28|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְקוּמ֫וּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=11}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|m}}
'''7.''' The formation of the conjugations {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, {{GHGterm|Puʿal}}, and {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} is, strictly speaking, excluded by the nature of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}. It is only in the latest books that we begin to find a few secondary formations, probably borrowed from Aramaic, on the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ו}} (with consonantal {{GHGheb|text=ו}}, see below, gg); e.g. the {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=עִוֵּד|translate=to surround}}, only in {{GHGheb|text=עִוְּדֻ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=61}}; and with change of {{GHGheb|text=ו}} to {{GHGheb|text=י}}, {{GHGheb|text=קִיַּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=9|verse=31}}, {{GHGheb|text=קִיְּמוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=9|verse=27}}, {{GHGterm|impf.}} {{GHGheb|text=וָאֲֽקַיֵ֫מָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=106}}, ''infin.'' {{GHGheb|text=קַיֵּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=4|verse=7}} &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=9|verse=21}} &c., ''imperat.'' {{GHGheb|text=קַיְּמֵ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=28}}; {{GHGheb|text=וְחִיַּכְתֶּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=1|verse=10}} from {{GHGheb|text=חוּב|translate=to be guilty}}. The {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִצְטַיֵּד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=9|verse=12}}, which belongs to the older language, is probably a denominative from {{GHGheb|text=צַ֫יִד}}. On the other hand the otherwise less common conjugation ''Pôlēl'' (see {{GHGpar|55|c}}), with its passive and reflexive, is usually<section end=par72 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

222.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par72" />employed in the sense of {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and as a substitute for it, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קוֹמֵם|translate=to set up}} from {{GHGheb|text=קוּם}}; {{GHGheb|text=מוֹתֵת|translate=to slaughter}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=51|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=1|verse=9}}, from {{GHGheb|text=מוּת}}; {{GHGheb|text=רוֹמֵם|translate=to exalt}}, passive {{GHGheb|text=רוֹמַם}}, from {{GHGheb|text=רוּם}}; reflexive {{GHGheb|text=הִתְעוֹרֵר|translate=to stir up oneself}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=יִתְעֹרָֽר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=17|verse=8}} in {{GHGterm|pause}}) from {{GHGheb|text=עוּר}}; reciprocal {{GHGheb|text=הִתְבּשֵׁשׁ|translate=to be ashamed before one another}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=25}}. The conjugation ''Pilpēl'' ({{GHGpar|55|f}}), on the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, is less common, e.g., {{GHGheb|text=טִלְטֵל|translate=to hurl away}} from {{GHGheb|text=טוּל}}; {{GHGheb|text=כִּלְכֵּל|translate=to contain}} from {{GHGheb|text=כּוּל}}; {{GHGheb|text=קַרְקַר|translate=to destroy}} from {{GHGheb|text=קוּר}}.

{{center|{{Small-caps|Remarks}}

I. ''On Qal.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|n}}
1. Of verbs ''middle e'' and ''o'', in which, as in the strong verb, the {{GHGterm|perfect}} and {{GHGterm|participle}} have the same form ({{GHGpar|50|b}}<!-- the text says 50. 2, but the link is to 50b -->), the following are the only examples: {{GHGheb|text=מֵת|translate=he is dead, fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=מֵ֫תָה}}, 2nd {{GHGterm|masc.}} {{GHGheb|text=מַ֫תָּה}} (cf. {{GHGpar|44|g}}; {{GHGpar|66|h}}); 1st ''sing.'' {{GHGheb|text=מַ֫תִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=וָמַ֫תִּי}} (even in {{GHGterm|pause}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=19}}); ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=מֵ֫תוּ}}, 1st ''pers.'' {{GHGheb|text=מַ֫תְנוּ}}, in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=מָ֫תְנוּ}}; {{GHGheb|text=בּשׁ|translate=he was ashamed}}, {{GHGheb|text=בּשְׁתְּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=בּ֫שְׁתִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=בּ֫שְׁנוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=בּ֫שׁוּ}}; {{GHGheb|text=אוֹר|translate=it has shone, plur.}} {{GHGheb|text=א֫וֹרוּ}}; {{GHGheb|text=טוֹב|translate=to be good}}, {{GHGheb|text=טֹ֫בו}}. {{GHGterm|Participles}} {{GHGheb|text=מֵת|translate=a dead man}} (''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=מֵתִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֵתֵי}}); {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹשִׁים|translate=ashamed}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=32|verse=30}}. For {{GHGheb|text=נֵד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=11}} read {{GHGheb|text=נָד}}, or, with LXX, {{GHGheb|text=עַד}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|o}}
Isolated anomalies in the {{GHGterm|perfect}} are: {{GHGheb|text=וְשָׁבַ֫ת}} (with the original ending of the {{GHGterm|fem.}} for {{GHGheb|text=וְשָׁבָ֫ה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=46|verse=17}} (see {{GHGpar|44|f}}); {{GHGheb|text=צָקוּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=16}} (see {{GHGpar|44|l}}).—In {{GHGheb|text=בָּ֫נוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=8}} (for {{GHGheb|text=בָּאנוּ}} from {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹא}}) the {{GHGheb|text=א}} has been dropped contrary to custom. In {{GHGheb|text=בֹּ֫אוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=27|verse=18}} (instead of {{GHGheb|text=בָּ֫אוּ}}) the Masora seems to point to the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יָבֹא֫וּ}} which is what would be expected; as {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} precedes, it is perhaps simply a scribal error.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|p}}
The form {{GHGheb|text=קָם}} occurs (cf. {{GHGpar|9|b}}) with {{GHGheb|text=א}} in the {{GHGterm|perfect}}, {{GHGheb|text=קָאם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=10|verse=14}}, also in the {{GHGterm|participles}} {{GHGheb|text=לָאט|translate=softly}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=21}}, {{GHGheb|text=רָאשׁ|translate=poor}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=1.4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=10|verse=4}}, ''plur.'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=13|verse=23|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁאטִים|translate=doing despite unto}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=שֹֽׁאֲטִים}} is to be read, from a stem {{GHGheb|text=שׁאט}} whence {{GHGheb|text=שְׁאָט}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=25|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=36|verse=5|hidebook=1}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=28|verse=24.26}}; {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=57|hidebook=1}}; also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=14|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=רָאמָה}} is to be read with Ben-Naphtali for {{GHGheb|text=רָֽאֲטָה}}. On the analogy of participles of verbs ''middle ō'' (like {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹשִׁים}}, see above) {{GHGheb|text=קוֹמִים}} occurs for {{GHGheb|text=קָמִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=16|verse=7}} and even with a transitive meaning {{GHGheb|text=לוֹט|translate=occultans|en=covering}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=25|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹסִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=10|verse=5}}.—{{GHGterm|Participle passive}}, {{GHGheb|text=מוּל|translate=circumcised}}; but {{GHGheb|text=סוּג|translate=a backslider}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=14|verse=14}}, and {{GHGheb|text=סוּרָה|translate=put aside}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=21}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=13}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}), are verbal adjectives of the form ''qāṭûl'' ({{GHGpar|50|f}}), not passive participles. For {{GHGheb|text=חֻשִׁים|translate=hastening}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=32|verse=17}}, read {{GHGheb|text=חֲמֻשִׁים}} as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=13|verse=18}}; for {{GHGheb|text=שׁוּבֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=2|verse=8}} read {{GHGheb|text=שָׁבֵי}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|q}}
2. Imperfects in ''û'' almost always have the corresponding {{GHGterm|imperative}} and {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} in ''û'', as {{GHGheb|text=יָקוּם}}, {{GHGterm|imperative}} and {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=קוּם}} (also defectively written {{GHGheb|text=יָקֻם}}, {{GHGheb|text=קֻם}}); but {{GHGheb|text=יָדוּשׁ|translate=he threshes}} (''infin.'' {{GHGheb|text=דּוּשׁ}}), has {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=דּ֫וֹשִׁי}} ({{GHGterm|fem.}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=4|verse=13}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָמוּט|translate=it slippeth, infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=מוֹט}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=38|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=46|verse=3|hidebook=1}}); cf. {{GHGheb|text=נוֹחַ}} (also {{GHGheb|text=נוּחַ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=25}} and {{GHGheb|text=נוֹעַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=2}} (elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=נוּעַ}}) with the ''imperfects'' {{GHGheb|text=יָנוּחַ}} and {{GHGheb|text=יָנוּעַ}}; {{GHGheb|text=לָעוֹז}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=שוֹב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=16}}; {{GHGheb|text=רוֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=10|verse=17}} (verse 16 {{GHGheb|text=רוּם}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|r}}
Where the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} (always intransitive in meaning) has ''ô'' the {{GHGterm|imperative}} and {{GHGterm|infinitive}} also have it; thus {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=(יָבֹא) יָבוֹא}}, ''infin.'' and ''imper.'' {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹא}} or {{GHGheb|text=בֹּא}}<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=12}} ({{GHGheb|text=בְּבֹאָה}} before a genitive), the text is evidently corrupt: read with Klostermann after the LXX {{GHGheb|text=בְּבֹאֵךְ}}.</ref>; {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּאֹר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=32}}, {{GHGheb|text=א֫וֹרִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=א֫וֹרוּ}}; {{GHGheb|text=יֵבוֹשׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹשׁ}}, &c.—{{GHGheb|text=יָקוֹט}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=8|verse=14}} (if it be a verb at all and not rather a substantive) is formed on the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}},<section end="par72" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

223.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par72 />since the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} of {{GHGheb|text=קוּטֹ}} appears as {{GHGheb|text=אָקוּט}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=95|verse=10}}. On the other hand {{GHGheb|text=יְקשׁוּן}} (as if from {{GHGheb|text=קוֹשׁ}}, on the analogy of {{GHGheb|text=יָבוֹא}}, &c.) occurs as {{GHGterm|imperfect}} of {{GHGheb|text=יָקשׁ}} ({{GHGheb|text=פ״י}}). The {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יָדוֹן}}, with ''ô'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=3}}, probably in the sense of ''to rule'', has no corresponding {{GHGterm|perfect}}, and is perhaps intentionally differentiated from the common verb {{GHGheb|text=יָדִין|translate=to judge}} (from {{GHGheb|text=דִּין}}, {{GHGheb|text=ע״י}}). Or can {{GHGheb|text=יָדוֹן}} be a {{GHGterm|jussive}} after {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} (cf. {{GHGpar|109|d}})? Similarly {{GHGheb|text=לֹא תָחוֹס עֵינִי (עֵֽינְךָ)}} might be taken as a case of a jussive after {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}}, with irregular ''scriptio plena'' (as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=30}}), in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=7|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=13|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=19|verse=13.21|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=25|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=5|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=7|verse=4.9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=8|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=9|verse=10|hidebook=1}}. But perhaps in all these cases {{GHGheb|text=לֹא תָחוּס}} was originally intended, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=13|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=21|verse=7}}, while cases like {{GHGheb|text=יָחֹס}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=72|verse=13}} are to be explained as in {{GHGpar|109|k}}.—The {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} always has ''ô'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קוֹם יָק֫וּמוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=44|verse=29}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|s}}
3. In the {{GHGterm|imperative}} with afformatives ({{GHGheb|text=ק֫וּמִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=ק֫וּמוּ}}) the tone is on the stem syllable (cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=עוּרִ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=12}} intentionally varied from {{GHGheb|text=ע֫וּרִי}}; also {{GHGheb|text=עוּרִ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=13|verse=7}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=9}} beside {{GHGheb|text=ע֫וּרִי כִּ֣ימֵי}}; {{GHGheb|text=גִּילִ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=9|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=צוּרִ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=2}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׁוּבִ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=116|verse=7}}, likewise for rhythmical reasons). So also the lengthened form, as {{GHGheb|text=שׁ֫וּבָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=7|verse=8}}, and {{GHGheb|text=ע֫וּרָה}} verse 7. But if an {{GHGheb|text=א}} follows in close connexion, the lengthened {{GHGterm|imperative}} usually has the form {{GHGheb|text=קוּמָ֫ה}}, &c.,<ref>Cf. Delitzsch’s commentary on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=3|verse=8}}.</ref> in order to avoid a hiatus, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=82|verse=8}}; hence also before {{GHGheb|text=יְהֹוָה}}, ''Q<sup>e</sup>rê perpetuum'' {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנָי}} ({{GHGpar|17|c}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=3|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=7|verse=7|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=קוּמָ֫ה}} (cf., however, in the same verse {{GHGheb|text=ע֫וּרָה}} and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=40|verse=5}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֻׁ֫בָה}} before {{GHGheb|text=א}}), and so even before {{GHGheb|text=ר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=43|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=74|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, &c. ({{GHGheb|text=רִיבָ֫ה}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|t}}
4. In the {{GHGterm|jussive}}, besides the form {{GHGheb|text=יָקֹם}} (see above, f), {{GHGheb|text=יָקוֹם}} also occurs (as subjunctive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=נָסוֹג}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=80|verse=19}} may also, with Delitzsch, be regarded as a voluntative), incorrectly written {{GHGterm|plene}}, and {{GHGheb|text=יָקֻ֫ם}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=31}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=9|verse=4.16}}), which, however, is only orthographically different from {{GHGheb|text=יָקוּם}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=46|verse=6}}). In the {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}} ({{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫קָם}}, in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫קֹם}}, see above, f) if there be a guttural or {{GHGheb|text=ר}} in the last syllable, ''ă'' often takes the place of ''ŏ'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫נַח|translate=and he rested}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫נַע|translate=and it was moved}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫סַר|translate=and he turned aside}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=4|verse=1}} (distinguished only by the sense from {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫סַר|translate=and he removed}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=13}}); {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫צַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=17|verse=5|hidebook=1}} (but also {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫גָר}} from both {{GHGheb|text=גּוּר|translate=to sojourn}}, and {{GHGheb|text=גּוּר|translate=to fear}}); {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫עַף}} (to be distinguished from {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫עָף|translate=and he flew}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=6}}) ''and he was weary'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=28.31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=21|verse=15}}, but probably in all these cases {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּעַף}} for {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּיעַף}} from {{GHGheb|text=יָעֵף}} is intended. For {{GHGheb|text=ותלוש}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=8}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, the Q<sup>e</sup>rê rightly requires {{GHGheb|text=וַתָּ֫לָשׁ}}. On the other hand, in an open syllable always {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּק֫וּמוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּס֫וּרוּ}}, &c. On {{GHGheb|text=(וָאָֽקֻם) וָאָֽקוּם}}, see {{GHGpar|49|e}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|u}}
Examples of the full plural ending {{GHGheb|text=וּן}} with the tone (see above, l) are {{GHGheb|text=תְּמֻת֫וּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=3.4}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְנוּס֫וּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְרוּצ֫וּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=2|verse=4.7.9}}.

{{center|II. ''On Niphʿal''. }}

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|v}}
5. The form of the 1st ''sing. perf.'' {{GHGheb|text=נְקוּמ֫וֹתִי}}, which frequently occurs ({{GHGheb|text=נְסוּגֹ֫תִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=נְפוּגֹ֫תִי}}, cf. also the ''ptcp. plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=נְכוּכִים}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=14|verse=3}}), serves as a model for the 2nd ''sing.'' {{GHGheb|text=נְקוּמ֫וֹתָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=נְקוּמוֹת}}, and the 1st ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=נְקוּמ֫וֹנוּ}} given in the paradigm, although no instances of these forms are found; but of the 2nd ''plur.'' the<section end=par72 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

224.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" />{{GHGcorrected}}</noinclude><section begin=par72/>only examples found have ''ô'' (not ''û''), viz. {{GHGheb|text=נְפֽוֹצֹתֶם|translate=ye have been scattered}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=11|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=20|verse=34.41|hidebook=1}}, and {{GHGheb|text=וּנְקֹֽטֹתֶם|translate=and ye shall loathe yourselves}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=20|verse=43}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=36|verse=31|hidebook=1}}.—To the ''ĭ'' (instead of ''ă'') of the preformative may be traced the {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=נֵעוֹר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=2|verse=17}} (analogous to the {{GHGterm|perfect}} and {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=נִמּוֹל}}, see below, ee), {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יֵעוֹר}} for ''yiʿʿōr''.—The {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} {{GHGheb|text=הִדּוּשׁ}} occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=25|verse=10}}; in {{GHGheb|text=לֵאוֹר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=33|verse=30}}, the Masora assumes the elision of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} (for {{GHGheb|text=לִהֵאוֹר}}); but probably {{GHGheb|text=לָאוֹר}} ({{GHGterm|Qal}}) is intended (see {{GHGpar|51|l}}).—{{GHGheb|text=נַמוֹג}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=31}}, {{GHGheb|text=נָסוֹג}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=13}} are to be regarded as ''infinitives absolute''.

{{center|III. ''On Hiphʿîl, Hophʿal, and Piʿlēl''.}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|w}}
6. Examples of the {{GHGterm|perfect}} without a separating vowel (see above, k), are: {{GHGheb|text=הֵבֵ֫אתָ}}, &c. (see further, {{GHGpar|76|g}}); {{GHGheb|text=הֵמַ֫תָּה}} (from {{GHGheb|text=מוּת}}) for ''hēmáth-tā'' (cf. {{GHGpar|20|a}}); {{GHGheb|text=הֵכַ֫נּוּ}} 1st ''plur. perfect Hiphʿîl'' from {{GHGheb|text=כּוּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=29|verse=19}}, even {{GHGheb|text=הֲמִתֶּם}} ({{GHGpar|27|s}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=6}}, &c.; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=35}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=28}}, also {{GHGheb|text=וַֽהֲמִתֶּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=16}}, and {{GHGheb|text=וַֽהֲמִתִּ֫יהָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=2|verse=5}}; but elsewhere, with {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} {{GHGheb|text=וְהֵֽמַתִּ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=30}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=וְהֵֽמַלְתִּ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=16|verse=13}}, and {{GHGheb|text=וְהֵֽנַפְתָּ֫}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=29|verse=24}}, &c.—In these cases the ''ē'' of the first syllable is retained in the secondary tone; elsewhere in the second syllable before the tone it becomes {{GHGheb|text=־ֱ}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=15|verse=12}}, &c.) or more frequently {{GHGheb|text=־ֲ}}, and in the syllable before the antepenultima it is necessarily {{GHGheb|text=־ֲ}} (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַֽהֲקִֽמֹתִ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=18}}). Before a suffix in the 3rd ''sing. mase.'' (except {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=13}}) and {{GHGterm|fem.}}, and in the 3rd ''plur.'', the vowel of the initial syllable is {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, in the other persons always {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Pathaḥ}} (König); on {{GHGheb|text=הֲקֵֽמֹתוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=9|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=89|verse=44}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=19|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=31|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=39}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=22|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=27|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=30|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=34|verse=4}}, and above, ''i''. The 3rd ''fem. perf. Hiph.'' {{GHGheb|text=הֵסַ֫תָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=25}} is quite abnormal for {{GHGheb|text=הֵסִ֫יתָה}} from {{GHGheb|text=סוּת}} or {{GHGheb|text=סִית}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|x}}
As in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} with {{GHGheb|text=ח}} for their first radical ({{GHGpar|67|w}}), all the forms of {{GHGheb|text=עוּד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=19|verse=23}} (where against the rule given under ''i'' we find {{GHGheb|text=הַֽעֵדֹ֫תָה}} with ''ē'' instead of ''î''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=8|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=9|verse=34}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=42|verse=19}}, and {{GHGheb|text=עוּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=45|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, take Pathaḥ in these conjugations instead of {{GHGheb|text=־ֲ}}. The irregular {{GHGheb|text=וְהֽוֹשְׁבוֹתִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=10|verse=6}} has evidently arisen from a combination of two different readings, viz. {{GHGheb|text=וְהֽוֹשַׁבְתִּים}} (from {{GHGheb|text=יָשַׁב}}) and {{GHGheb|text=וַֽהֲשִֽׁבוֹתִים}} (from {{GHGheb|text=שׁוּב}}): the latter is to be preferred.—On {{GHGheb|text=הֵבִישׁ}} and {{GHGheb|text=הוֹבִישׁ}} as a (metaplastic) {{GHGterm|perfect Hiphʿîl}} of {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹשׁ}}, cf. {{GHGpar|78|b}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|y}}
7. In the {{GHGterm|imperative}}, besides the short form {{GHGheb|text=הָקֵם}} (on {{GHGheb|text=הָשַֽׁב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=22}} with Silluq, cf. {{GHGpar|29|q}}; but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=35}} for {{GHGheb|text=הָשַׁב}} read the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=הָשֵׁב}}) the lengthened form {{GHGheb|text=הָקִ֫ימָה}} is also found. With ''suffix'' {{GHGheb|text=הֲקִימֵ֫נִי}}, &c. The {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=הָבִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=18}} is irregular (for {{GHGheb|text=הָבֵא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=16}}); perhaps {{GHGheb|text=הָבֵיא}} (as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=40}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=8|verse=6}}) is intended, or it was originally {{GHGheb|text=הָבִ֫יאָה}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|z}}
In the {{GHGterm|infinitive}}, elision of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} occurs in {{GHGheb|text=לָבִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=39|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=31|verse=10}} (for {{GHGheb|text=לְהָבִיא}}); {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} {{GHGterm|fem.}} is added in {{GHGheb|text=לַֽהֲנָפָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=28}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=2|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=4|verse=14|hidebook=1}} and the analogous {{GHGterm|infinitive Haphʿel}} in biblical Aramaic, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=5|verse=20}}.—As {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} {{GHGheb|text=הָכִין}} occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=7|verse=14}} (perh. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=4|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=10|verse=23}}).—The {{GHGterm|participles}} have ''ē'', on the analogy of the {{GHGterm|perfect}}, as the vowel of the preformative, like verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} ({{GHGpar|67|i}}). On {{GHGheb|text=מֵבִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=5|verse=2}}, &c. (in {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}), see {{GHGpar|74|k}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|aa}}
On the shortened forms of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} ({{GHGheb|text=יָקֵם}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיַָּקֶם}}, but always {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּבֵ֫א}}; in the {{GHGterm|jussive}} also with retraction of the tone {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תָּ֫שֶׁב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=20}}) see above, f. With a guttural or {{GHGheb|text=ר}} the last syllable generally has {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} (as in {{GHGterm|Qal}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיָ֫עַד|translate=and he testified}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=17|verse=13}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָרַ֫ח|translate=let him smell}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=26|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫רַח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫סַר}}<section end=par72/><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

225.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par72" />''and he took away'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=13}}. The 1st ''sing.'' of the {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}} commonly has the form {{GHGheb|text=וָאָֽשִׁ֫יב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=2|verse=20}}, or, more often, defectively {{GHGheb|text=וָאָֽעִד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=42}}, less frequently the form {{GHGheb|text=וָאָֽשֵׁב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=14|verse=7}}.—For {{GHGheb|text=אָסֵף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=1|verse=2}} (after {{GHGheb|text=אָסֹף}}) and in verse 3, read {{GHGheb|text=אֹסֵף}} from {{GHGheb|text=אָסַף}}, on the analogy of {{GHGheb|text=אֹמֵד}} {{GHGpar|68|g}}: similarly in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=8|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽסְפֵם}} instead of {{GHGheb|text=אֲסִיפֵם}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|bb}}
In the {{GHGterm|imperfect Pôlēl}} the tone is moved backwards before a following tone-syllable, but without a shortening of the vowel of the final syllable; e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תְּד֫וֹמֵֽם נּ֑וֹי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=14|verse=34}}; {{GHGheb|text=תְּח֫וֹלֵֽל לְוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=35|verse=14}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=23}}, and acc. to Baer {{GHGheb|text=וַתּתְבֹּ֫נֵֽן בִּֽי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=20}} (ed. Mant., Ginsb. {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּתְבֹּנֶן בִּֽי}}), always in principal pause; on the {{GHGterm|Metheg}} with {{GHGterm|Ṣere}}, cf. {{GHGpar|16|f}} γ.—As ''Pôlal'' cf. {{GHGheb|text=יְרֹעָ֑ע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=16|verse=10}}.

As {{GHGterm|participle Hophʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=הַמּוּשַׁב}} occurs in close connexion, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=12}}; cf.{{GHGpar|65|d}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|cc}}
Peculiar contracted forms of ''Pôlēl'' (unless they are transitives in {{GHGterm|Qal}}) are {{GHGheb|text=וַיְכֻנֶ֫נּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=15}}, {{GHGheb|text=יְעוּרֶ֫נּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=41|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּמוּגֵ֫נוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=64|verse=6}} for {{GHGheb|text=וַיְכֹֽנְנֶ֫נּוּ}}, &c. [but read {{GHGheb|text=וַיְכֹנְנֵנוּ}} ({{GHGpar|58|k}}), {{GHGheb|text=יְעִירֶנּוּ}} or {{GHGheb|text=יְעוֹרְנֶנּוּ}}, and {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּמַגְּנֵנוּ}}]; also {{GHGheb|text=תְּרֹמֵם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=17|verse=4}}, for {{GHGheb|text=תְּדֹֽמְמֵם}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=15|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=יְעֹעֵ֫רוּ}} appears to have arisen from the ''Pilpel'' {{GHGheb|text=יְעַרְעֵָ֫רוּ}}, the ''ă'' after the loss of the {{GHGheb|text=ר}} having been lengthened to ''ā'', which has then been obscured to ''ô''.—For the strange form {{GHGheb|text=בִּֽתְקֽוֹמֲמֶ֫יךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=21}}, which cannot (according to {{GHGpar|52|s}}) be explained as a {{GHGterm|participle}} with the {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}} omitted, read {{GHGheb|text=בְּמִתְק׳}}.

{{center|IV. ''In General.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|dd}}
8. The verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} are primarily related to the verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} (§ 67), which were also originally biliteral, so that it is especially necessary in analysing them to pay attention to the differences between the inflexion of the two classes. Several forms are exactly the same in both, e.g. {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} with {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}}, the whole of {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}, the ''Piʿlēl'' of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, and the {{GHGterm|Pôʿēl}} of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}; see {{GHGpar|67|z}}. Owing to this close relation, verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} sometimes have forms which follow the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, e.g. {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=בַּז|translate=he has despised}} (from {{GHGheb|text=בּוּז}}, as if from {{GHGheb|text=בָּזַז}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=4|verse=10}}; {{GHGterm|perfect Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נָמָרֽ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=11}} (for {{GHGheb|text=נָמוֹר}} from {{GHGheb|text=מוּד}}, as if from {{GHGheb|text=מָרַר}}). The same explanation equally applies to {{GHGheb|text=נָֽקְטָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=10|verse=1}} for {{GHGheb|text=נָקַ֫טָּה}} (cf. § 67 dd) = {{GHGheb|text=נָק֫וֹטָה}} from {{GHGheb|text=קוּט}}, and {{GHGheb|text=נָ֫קֹטּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=6|verse=9}} (for {{GHGheb|text=נָק֫וֹטוּ}}); {{GHGheb|text=יֵר֫וֹמּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=10|verse=17}} and {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּדֹ֫מּוּ}} verse 15; {{GHGheb|text=הֵדֹ֫מּוּ}} ({{GHGterm|imperative}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִסַּג}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=2|verse=6}}; ''Hiphʿîl perfect'' {{GHGheb|text=הֵתַז}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=18|verse=5}} for {{GHGheb|text=הֵתֵז}} (cf. {{GHGpar|29|q}}), which is for {{GHGheb|text=הֵתִיז}} from {{GHGheb|text=תּוּז}}. On the other hand the ''imperfects'' {{GHGheb|text=יָמֵר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=48|verse=14}} (unless it be intended for {{GHGheb|text=יָמִר}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=15|verse=4}}) and {{GHGheb|text=יָפֵחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=2|verse=3}}, are to be regarded according to {{GHGpar|109|i}}, simply as rhythmically shortened forms of {{GHGheb|text=יָמִיר}} and {{GHGheb|text=יָפִיחַ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|ee}}
9. In common with verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} ({{GHGpar|67|g}}) verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} sometimes have in {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} the quasi-Aramaic formation, by which, instead of the long vowel under the preformative, they take a short vowel with ''Dages̆ forte'' in the following consonant; this variety is frequently found even along with the ordinary form, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִסִּית|translate=to incite}}, imperfect {{GHGheb|text=יַסִּית}} (also {{GHGheb|text=הֵסִית}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָסִית}}); {{GHGheb|text=הִסִּיג}}, imperfect {{GHGheb|text=יַסִּיג|translate=to remove}} (from {{GHGheb|text=סוּנ‍}}), also {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=הֻסַּג}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=14}} (on {{GHGheb|text=הֻ֣קַּם}} cf. {{GHGpar|29|g}}); sometimes with a difference of meaning, as {{GHGheb|text=הֵנִיחַ|translate=to cause to rest}},<ref>As the passive of this {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} we should expect the {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=הוּנַח}}, which is, no doubt, to be read for {{GHGheb|text=הוּנַּח}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=5|verse=5}}.</ref> but {{GHGheb|text=הִנִּיחַ}} ({{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יַנִּיחַ}}, {{GHGterm|consecutive}} {{GHGheb|text=וַתַּנִּ֫חַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=16}}; {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=חַנַּח}}, ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=הַנִּ֫יחוּ}}) ''to set down''; for {{GHGheb|text=וַהֻנִּ֫יחָה}} (Baer, Ginsburg {{GHGheb|text=וְהֻנִ׳}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=5|verse=11}} (which at any rate could only be explained as an isolated passive of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} on the analogy of the biblical Aramaic {{GHGheb|text=הֳקִימַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=7|verse=4}}) we should probably read {{GHGheb|text=וַהִנִּיחֻ֫הָ}} with
<section end="par72" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

226.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par72 /><section begin=par72 />Klostermann after the LXX. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=8|verse=11}} the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} {{GHGheb|text=הדים}} is intended for a {{GHGterm|perfect Hiphʿîl}}. There is also a distinction in meaning between {{GHGheb|text=יָלִין|translate=to spend the night, to remain}}, and {{GHGheb|text=יַלִּין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=7}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} ({{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} {{GHGheb|text=תּלּוֹנוּ}}; conversely, verse 2 {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} {{GHGheb|text=יַלִּ֫ינוּ}}, {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} {{GHGheb|text=יִלּ֫וֹנוּ}}), {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=מַלִּין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, ''to be stubborn, obstinate'': in the latter sense from the form {{GHGheb|text=יָלִין}} only {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫לֶן}} is found, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=17|verse=3}}. Other examples are {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נִמּוֹל|translate=he was circumcised}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=26}} f.; {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=22|hidebook=1}} (from {{GHGheb|text=מוּל}}, not {{GHGheb|text=נָמַל}}); {{GHGheb|text=נֵעוֹר|translate=he is waked up}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=2|verse=17}} (see above, v); {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִזִּיל֫וּהַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=יַלִּ֫יזוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=4|verse=21}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|ff}}
Perhaps the same explanation applies to some forms of verbs ''first guttural'' with ''Dageš forte implicitum'', which others derive differently or would emend, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַתַּ֫חַשׁ}} for {{GHGheb|text=וַתָּ֫חַשׁ|translate=and she hastened}} (from {{GHGheb|text=חוּשׁ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּ֫עַט}} (another reading is {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫עַט}}), {{GHGheb|text=וַתַּ֫עַט}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=14|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=32|hidebook=1}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}) from {{GHGheb|text=עוּט}} or {{GHGheb|text=עִיט|translate=to fly at anything}}. Both, as far as the form is concerned, would be correct ''apocopated imperfects'' from {{GHGheb|text=חָשָׁה}} and {{GHGheb|text=עָטָה}} ({{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}), but these stems only occur with a wholly different meaning.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|gg}}
10. Verbs with a consonantal {{GHGterm|Wāw}} for their second radical, are inflected throughout like the strong form, provided the first or third radical is not a weak letter, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חָוַר}}, {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יֶֽחֱוַר|translate=to be white}}; {{GHGheb|text=גָּוַע}}, {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יִגְוַע|translate=to expire}}; {{GHGheb|text=רָוַח|translate=to be wide}}; {{GHGheb|text=צָוַח|translate=to cry}}; {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=עִוֵּל}}, {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יְעַוֵּל|translate=to act wickedly}}; {{GHGheb|text=עִוֵּת|translate=to bend}}, {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִתְעַוֵּת|translate=to bend oneself}}; and this is especially the case with verbs which are at the same time {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=צָוָה}}, {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=צִוָּה|translate=to command}}, {{GHGheb|text=קִוָּה|translate=to wait}}, {{GHGheb|text=רָוָה|translate=to drink}}, {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=רִוָּה}} (on {{GHGheb|text=אֲרַיָּ֫וֶךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=16|verse=9}}, see {{GHGpar|75|dd}}) and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִרְוָה|translate=to give to drink}}, &c.<section end=par72 />

<section begin=par73 />{{GHGpar-heading|73|Verbs middle i (vulgo {{GHGheb|text=ע״י}}), ''e.g.'' {{GHGheb|text=בִּין}} to discern. Paradigm N}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|73|a}}
'''1.''' These verbs agree, as regards their structure, exactly with verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, and in contrast to them may be termed {{GHGheb|text=ע״י}}, or more correctly, ''ʿayin-î'' verbs, from the characteristic vowel of the ''impf., imper.'', and ''infin. constr''. This distinction is justified in so far as it refers to a difference in the pronunciation of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} and its kindred forms, the {{GHGterm|imperative}} and ''infin. constr.''—the {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} verbs having ''û'' lengthened from original ''ŭ'' and {{GHGheb|text=ע״י}} having ''î'' lengthened from original ''ĭ''. In other respects verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״י}} simply belong to the class of really monosyllabic stems, which, by a strengthening of their ''vocalic'' element, have been assimilated to the triliteral form<ref>That verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=ע״י}} are developed from biliteral roots at a period before the differentiation of the Semitic languages is admitted even by Nöldeke ({{GHGcite|title=Beiträge zur sem. Sprachwiss.}}, Strassburg, 1904, p. 34 ff.), although he contests the view that {{GHGheb|text=בִּינֹ֫תִי}} and {{GHGheb|text=רִיב֫וֹתָ}} are to be referred to {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} with the preformative dropped.</ref> ({{GHGpar|67|a}}). In the {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} the monosyllabic stem, as in {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, has ''ā'' lengthened from ''ă'', thus: {{GHGheb|text=שָׁת}} ''he has set; infinitive'' {{GHGheb|text=שִׁית}}, {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} {{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹת}}, {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=שִׁית}}, {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יָשִׁית}}, {{GHGterm|jussive}} {{GHGheb|text=יָשֵׁת}} ({{GHGpar|48|g}}), {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיָ֫שֶׁת}}.—The {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} of some verbs<section end=par73 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

227.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par73 />used to be treated as having a double set of forms, a regular series, and others like {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} without the preformative, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בִּין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=10|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=בִּינֹ֫תִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=9|verse=2}}, also {{GHGheb|text=בַּ֫נְתָּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=רִיב֫וֹתָ|translate=thou strivest}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=33|verse=13}}, also {{GHGheb|text=רַ֫בְתָּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=3|verse=58}}. The above ''perfects'' ({{GHGheb|text=בִּין}}, {{GHGheb|text=רִיב}}, &c.) might no doubt be taken as forms ''middle ē'' (properly ''ĭ''), the ''ĭ'' of which has been lengthened to ''î'' (like the ''ŭ'' lengthened to ''ŭ'' in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} of {{GHGheb|text=קוּם}}). It is more probable, however, that they are really shortened forms of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}. This is supported by the fact that, especially in the case of {{GHGheb|text=בִּין}}, the shortened forms are few and probably all late, while the corresponding unshortened forms with the same meaning are very numerous, e.g. {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵבִין}} (but {{GHGheb|text=בִּין}} only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=10|verse=1}}), {{GHGheb|text=הֲבִֽינוֹתֶם}}, {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=הָבִין}} (but ''infin. abs.'' {{GHGheb|text=בִּין}} only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=23|verse=1}}), {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=הָבֵן}} (only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=9|verse=23}} {{GHGheb|text=וּבִין}} immediately before {{GHGheb|text=וְהָבֵן}}, also {{GHGheb|text=בִּ֫ינוּ}} three times, and {{GHGheb|text=בִּ֫ינָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=2}}), {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=מֵבִין}}.<ref>Since {{GHGheb|text=בנת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=2}} might be intended for {{GHGheb|text=בִּנֹ֫תָ}}, there remains really no form of {{GHGheb|text=בין}} which must ''necessarily'' be explained as a Qal, except the ''ptcp. plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=בָּנִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=7}}. Nevertheless it is highly probable that all the above instances of Hiphʿîl-forms, parallel with Qal-forms of the same meaning, are merely due to a secondary formation from the ''imperfects Qal'' {{GHGheb|text=יָבִין}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָשִׂים}}, &c., which were wrongly regarded as ''imperfects Hiphʿîl'': so Barth, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} xliii. p. 190 f., and {{GHGcite|title=Nominalbildung}}, p. 119 f.</ref> Elsewhere {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}-forms are in use along with actual {{GHGterm|Qal}}-forms with the same meaning, thus: {{GHGheb|text=מֵרִיב}} (also {{GHGheb|text=רָב}}), {{GHGheb|text=מֵשִׂים|translate=placing}} (but only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=20}}, which, with the critically untenable {{GHGheb|text=הָשִׂ֫ימִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=21}}, is the only instance of {{GHGheb|text=שׂוּם}} in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}), {{GHGheb|text=מֵגִיחַ|translate=breaking forth}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=33}}, with ''infin. Qal'' {{GHGheb|text=גִּיתוֹ}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַחִ֫ישׁוּ|translate=they rushed forth}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=37}}, with {{GHGheb|text=תָשׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=חַ֫שְׁתּי}}; {{GHGheb|text=מֵצִיץ|translate=glancing}}, also in {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=צָץ}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֵקִיא|translate=he spat out}}, with ''imperat. Qal'' {{GHGheb|text=קְיוּ}}. As ''passives'' we find a few apparent ''imperfects Hophʿal'', which are really (according to {{GHGpar|53|u}}) ''imperfects passive'' of {{GHGterm|Qal}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יוּחַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=66|verse=8}} from {{GHGheb|text=חִיל|translate=to turn round}}, {{GHGheb|text=יוּשָׁר}} from {{GHGheb|text=שִׁיר|translate=to sing}}, {{GHGheb|text=יוּשַׁת}} from {{GHGheb|text=שִׁית|translate=to set}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|73|b}}
'''2.''' The above-mentioned {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}-forms might equally well be derived from verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}; and the influence of the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} is distinctly seen in the {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נָבוֹן}} (ground-form ''nabān''), ''Pôlēl'' {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹנֵן}}, and ''Hithpôlēl'' {{GHGheb|text=הִתְבּוֹנֵן}}. The very close relation existing between verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״י}} and {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} is evident also from the fact that from some stems both forms occur side by side in {{GHGterm|Qal}}, thus from {{GHGheb|text=תִיל|translate=to turn round, imperative}} also {{GHGheb|text=ח֫וּלִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=4|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=שִׂים|translate=to place, infinitive construct}} commonly {{GHGheb|text=שׂוּם}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=שׂים}} ''Q<sup>e</sup>re''), {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יָשִׂים}}, but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=4|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=יָשׂוּם}}. In other verbs one form is, at any rate, the more common, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גִּיל|translate=to exult}} ({{GHGheb|text=גּוּל}} only {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=23|verse=24}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}); from {{GHGheb|text=לוּן}} (perhaps denominative from {{GHGheb|text=לַ֫יִל}}) ''to spend the night'', {{GHGheb|text=לָלוּן}} occurs six times as {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָלִין}} only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=23}}; but the {{GHGterm|imperative}} is always {{GHGheb|text=לִין}}, &c.—Of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״י}} the most common are {{GHGheb|text=שִׁית|translate=to set}}, {{GHGheb|text=רִיב|translate=to strive}}, {{GHGheb|text=דִּין|translate=to judge}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׂישׂ|translate=to rejoice}}; cf. also {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=בָּל}} (''middle''<section end=par73 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

228.text:
