<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par73 />{{GHGterm|Yôdh}} in Arabic) ''to comprehend, to measure'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=12}}; {{GHGheb|text=עִיט}} (as in Arabic and Syriac) ''to rush upon'', and the denominative {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=קָץ}} (from {{GHGheb|text=קַ֫יִץ}}) ''to pass the summer'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=18|verse=6}}. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=וְדִיגוּם|translate=and they shall fish them}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=16|verse=16}}, generally explained as {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}}, denominative from {{GHGheb|text=דָּג|translate=fish}}, probably represents a denominative {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְדִיְגוּ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|73|c}}
Corresponding to verbs properly {{GHGheb|text=ע״ו}}, mentioned in {{GHGpar|72|gg}}, there are certain verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״י}} with consonantal {{GHGterm|Yôdh}}, as {{GHGheb|text=אָיַב|translate=to hate}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָיֵף|translate=to faint}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָיָה|translate=to become, to be}}, {{GHGheb|text=חָיָה|translate=to live}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|73|d}}
Rem. 1. In the {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} 3rd ''fem. sing.'' {{GHGheb|text=וְלָ֫נֶה}} occurs once, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=5|verse=4}}, for {{GHGheb|text=וְלָ֫נָה}}, with the weakening of the toneless ''ā'' to ''ĕ'' (as in the ''fem. participle'' {{GHGheb|text=זוּרֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=5}}); cf. the analogous examples in {{GHGpar|48|l}} and {{GHGpar|80|i}}.—2nd ''sing. masc.'' {{GHGheb|text=שַׁתָּ֫ה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=90|verse=8}}, {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} (before {{GHGheb|text=ע}}; cf. {{GHGpar|72|s}}); 1st ''sing.'' once {{GHGheb|text=שַׁתִּ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=28}}, ''milraʿ'', without any apparent reason; 1st ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=וְלַ֫נּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=13}} for ''lán-nû''. The lengthened {{GHGterm|imperative}} has the tone on the ultima before gutturals, {{GHGheb|text=רִיבָ֫ה יהוה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=1}}; see further, {{GHGpar|72|s}}.—Examples of the {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} are: {{GHGheb|text=רֹב|translate=litigando}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=40|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=שׂוֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=42|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁת|translate=ponendo}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=7}}. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=דִיב יָדִיב}} (for {{GHGheb|text=דֹב}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=50|verse=34}}, {{GHGheb|text=בִּין תָּבִין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=23|verse=1}}, {{GHGheb|text=חול תחיל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=30|verse=16}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, are irregular and perhaps due to incorrect ''scriptio plena''; for the last the {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} requires {{GHGheb|text=הוּל תָּחוּל}}, but read {{GHGheb|text=חוֹל}}; cf. {{GHGpar|113|x}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|73|e}}
2. The ''shortened imperfect'' usually has the form {{GHGheb|text=יָבֵן}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָשֵׂם}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָשֵׁת}}; more rarely, with the tone moved back, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יָ֫רֶב לוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=31}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=1}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תָּ֫שֶׁת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=20}}. So with {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיָ֫שֶׂם|translate=and he placed}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיָ֫בֶן|translate=and he perceived}}; with a middle guttural {{GHGheb|text=וַיָ֫עַט בָּהֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=14}} (see {{GHGpar|72|ee}}); with {{GHGheb|text=ר}} as 3rd radical, {{GHGheb|text=וַתָּ֫שַׁר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=1}}. As jussive of {{GHGheb|text=לִין}}, {{GHGheb|text=תָּלַ֫ן}} is found in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=20}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}}) and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=17|verse=2}}, for {{GHGheb|text=תָּלֵן}}.—For {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תָּרוֹב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=3|verse=30}} ''Keth.'' (''Q<sup>e</sup>re'' {{GHGheb|text=תָּרִיב}}) read {{GHGheb|text=תָּרֵב}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|73|f}}
3. As ''participle active Qal'' {{GHGheb|text=לֵן|translate=spending the night}}, occurs once, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=13|verse=21}}; {{GHGterm|participle passive}} {{GHGheb|text=שִׂים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=24|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ob|chapter=1|verse=4}}; ''feminine'' {{GHGheb|text=שׂוּמָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=32}}, in the {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}, even according to the reading of the Oriental schools (see p. 38, note 2): the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} has {{GHGheb|text=שִׂימָה}}. A {{GHGterm|passive}} of {{GHGterm|Qal}} (cf. above, {{GHGpar|52|e}} and s, and {{GHGpar|53|u}}) from {{GHGheb|text=שִׂים}} may perhaps be seen in {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫ישֶׂם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=50|verse=26}} (also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=33}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} {{GHGheb|text=ויישם}}, {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיּוּשָׂם}}; the Samaritan in both places has {{GHGheb|text=ויושם}}), and also in {{GHGheb|text=יִיסָךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=30|verse=32}}, Samaritan {{GHGheb|text=יוסך}}. Against the explanation of {{GHGheb|text=ייסך}} as a {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}-form from {{GHGheb|text=סוּךְ}}, Barth ({{GHGcite|title=Jubelschrift... Hildesheimer}}, Berlin, 1890, p. 151) rightly urges that the only example of a Hiphʿîl of {{GHGheb|text=סוּךְ}} is the doubtful {{GHGheb|text=וַיָ֫םֶךְ}}, which is probably an ''ĭ''-imperfect of {{GHGterm|Qal}}.—The explanation of {{GHGheb|text=יישם}}, &c., as a {{GHGterm|passive}} of {{GHGterm|Qal}} arising from ''yiysam'', &c. = ''yuysam'' (so Barth, ibid., note 1), is certainly also unconvincing, so that the correctness of the traditional reading is open to question.

{{center|<nowiki>* * * * * *</nowiki>}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|73|g}}
4. In verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״א}} the {{GHGheb|text=א}} always retains its censonantal value; these stems are, therefore, to be regarded as verbs ''middle Guttural'' (§ 64). An exception is {{GHGheb|text=יָנֵאץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=5}} if it be {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} of {{GHGheb|text=נאץ}} (for {{GHGheb|text=יַנְאֵץ}}); but if the form has really been correctly transmitted, it should rather be referred to {{GHGheb|text=נָצַץ}}, and regarded as incorrectly written for {{GHGheb|text=יָנֵץ}}. On {{GHGheb|text=נָאווּ}} (from {{GHGheb|text=נַֽאֲוָה}}), which was formerly treated here as {{GHGheb|text=ע״א}}, see now {{GHGpar|75|x}}.<section end=par73 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

229.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par74 />{{GHGpar-heading|74|Verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}}, ''e.g.'' {{GHGheb|text=מָצָא}} to find. Paradigm O}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|74|a}}
The {{GHGheb|text=א}} in these verbs, as in verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״א}}, is treated in some cases as a consonant, i.e. as a guttural, in others as having no consonantal value (as a quiescent or vowel letter), viz.:

'''1.''' In those forms which terminate with the {{GHGheb|text=א}}, the final syllable always has the regular vowels, if long, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מֹצֵא}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִצֵּא}}, {{GHGheb|text=מָצוּא}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִמְצִיא}}, i.e. the {{GHGheb|text=א}} simply quiesces in the long vowel, without the latter suffering any change whatever. It is just possible that after the altogether heterogeneous vowel ''û'' the {{GHGheb|text=א}} may originally have preserved a certain consonantal value. On the other band, if the final {{GHGheb|text=א}} quiesces in a preceding ''ă'' (as in the ''perfect, imperfect'', and {{GHGterm|imperative Qal}}, in the {{GHGterm|perfect Niphʿal}}, and in {{GHGterm|Puʿal}} and {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}) this ''ă'' is necessarily lengthened to ''ā'', by {{GHGpar|27|g}}, as standing in an open syllable; e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מָצָא}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִמְצָא}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|74|b}}
The {{GHGterm|imperfect}} and {{GHGterm|imperative Qal}} invariably have ''ā'' in the final syllable, on the analogy of verbs ''tertiae gutturalis''; cf., however, {{GHGpar|76|e}}.—In the ''imperfect Hithpaʿēl ā'' occurs in the final syllable not only (according to {{GHGpar|54|k}}) in the principal pause ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=31|verse=23}}), or immediately before it ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=10|verse=16}}), or with the lesser disjunctives ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=21|verse=1.4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=19|verse=13.20}}), but even out of pause with ''Mer<sup>e</sup>kha'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=6|verse=7}}, and even before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=19|verse=12}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|74|c}}
'''2.''' When {{GHGheb|text=א}} stands at the end of a syllable before an afformative beginning with a consonant ({{GHGheb|text=ת}}, {{GHGheb|text=נ‍}}), it likewise quiesces with the preceding vowel; thus in the {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} (and {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}, see below) quiescing with ''ă'' it regularly becomes ''Qumeṣ'' ({{GHGheb|text=מָצָ֫אתָ}} for {{GHGheb|text=מָצַ֫אְתָּ}}, &c.); but in the {{GHGterm|perfect}} of all the other active and reflexive conjugations, so far as they occur, it is preceded by ''S̥̥ere'' ({{GHGheb|text=נִמְצֵ֫אתָ}}, &c.), and in the {{GHGterm|imperative}} and {{GHGterm|imperfect}} by {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְצֶ֫אנָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּמְצֶאנָה}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|74|d}}
(''a'') The {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} of these forms of the imperfect and imperative might be considered as a modification, and at the same time a lengthening of an original ''ă'' (see {{GHGpar|8|a}}). In the same way the ''ē'' of the {{GHGterm|perfect}} forms in ''Piʿēl, Hithpaʿēl'', and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} might be traced to an original ''ĭ'' (as in other cases the ''ē'' and ''î'' in the final syllable of the 3rd ''sing. muse. perfect'' of these conjugations), although this ''ĭ'' may have only been attenuated from an original ''ă''. According to another, and probably the correct explanation, however, both the {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} and the {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} are due to the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} ({{GHGpar|75|f}}) in consequence of the close relation between the two classes, cf. {{GHGpar|75|nn}}.—No form of this kind occurs in {{GHGterm|Puʿal}}; in the {{GHGterm|perfect Hophʿal}} only the 2nd ''masc. sing.'' {{GHGheb|text=הֻבָ֫אתָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=40|verse=4}}, lengthened according to rule.

{{GHGmargin-letter|74|e}}
(''b'') Before suffixes attached by a connecting vowel (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרָאֵ֫נִי}}) the {{GHGheb|text=א}} retains its consonantal value; so before {{GHGheb|text=ךָ}} and {{GHGheb|text=בֶם}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֶמְצָֽאֲךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=8|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִבָּרַֽאֲךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=28|verse=13}} (cf. {{GHGpar|65|h}}), not {{GHGheb|text=אֶמְצָאךָ}}, &c., since these suffixes, by {{GHGpar|58|f}}, are likewise attached to the verb-form by a connecting vowel in the form of {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ mobile}}.—As {{GHGterm|infinitive Qal}} with suffix notice {{GHGheb|text=מַחְאֲךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=25|verse=6}}; {{GHGterm|participle}} with suffix {{GHGheb|text=בֹּדַֽאֲךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=1}}; {{GHGterm|infinitive Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּטַמַּֽאֲכֶם}}.—The doubly anomalous form {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרְאוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=6}} (for {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרָאֵ֫הוּ}} or {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרָאֶ֫נּוּ}}) is perhaps a ''forma mixta'' combining the readings {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרָאוֹ}} and {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרְאוּ}}.
<section end=par74 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

230.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par74 />{{GHGmargin-letter|74|f}}
'''3.''' When {{GHGheb|text=א}} begins a syllable (consequently before afformatives which consist of or begin with a vowel, as well as before suffixes) it is necessarily a firm consonant, and the form then follows the analogy of the strong verb, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מָֽצְאָה}} ''māṣ<sup>e</sup>ʿā'', {{GHGheb|text=מָֽצְאוּ}}, &c. (in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=מָצָ֫אָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=מָצָ֫אוּ}}).

{{center|{{Small-caps|Remarks.}}}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|74|g}}
1. Verbs ''middle e'', like {{GHGheb|text=מָלֵא|translate=to be full}}, retain the {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} also in the other persons of the {{GHGterm|perfect}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מָלֵ֫אתִי}} ({{GHGheb|text=מְלָאוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=7|verse=5}} has {{GHGheb|text=־ָ}} owing to its transitive use; for {{GHGheb|text=יְרָאתֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=4|verse=24}} read with Ewald {{GHGheb|text=יִרְאָתָם}}). Instead of {{GHGheb|text=מָֽצְאָה}} the form {{GHGheb|text=קָרָאת|translate=she names}}, on the analogy of the {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}-forms noticed in {{GHGpar|75|m}}, occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=14}} (from {{GHGheb|text=קָֽרְאַת}}, cf. {{GHGpar|44|f}}), and with a different meaning (''it befalls'') in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=31|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=44|verse=23}}, in both places before {{GHGheb|text=א}}, and hence, probably, to avoid a hiatus (on the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=וְחָטָאת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=5|verse=16}}, could only be the and ''sing. masc.''; the text which is evidently corrupt should probably be emended to {{GHGheb|text=וְחָטָאתָ לְעַמֶּ֫ךָ}} with the LXX); in {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נִפְלָאת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=23}}; in {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=הֻבָאת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=11}}.—The 2nd ''fem. sing.'' is written {{GHGheb|text=קָרָאתְ}} by Baer, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gen|chapter=16|verse=11}}, &c., according to early MSS.

{{GHGmargin-letter|74|h}}
2. The ''infin. Qal'' occurs sometimes on the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} ({{GHGheb|text=גְּלוֹת}}, &c., see {{GHGpar|75|nn}}) in the feminine form; so always {{GHGheb|text=מְלֹאת|translate=to fill}} (as distinguished from {{GHGheb|text=מְלֹא|translate=fullness}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=8|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=12|verse=4.6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=25|verse=30|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=29|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=5|verse=2}}, also written {{GHGheb|text=מְלֹאות}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=25|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=20|verse=22}}, &c., and {{GHGheb|text=מְלוֹאת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=1|verse=5}}. Cf. further, {{GHGheb|text=קְרֹאת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=שְׂנֹאת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=13}}; before suffixes, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=33|verse=12}}, and likewise in ''Niph.'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=13|verse=4}}; also in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=לְמַלֹּאת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=31|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=35|verse=33|hidebook=1}}, or {{GHGheb|text=לְמַלּאוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=9|verse=2}}, &c. {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}; with suffix {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=21|verse=2}}.—On the (aramaïzing) ''infinitives'' {{GHGheb|text=מַשָּׁא}} and {{GHGheb|text=מַשְׂאוֹת}}, see {{GHGpar|45|e}}; on {{GHGheb|text=לִקְרַאת|translate=obviam}}, {{GHGpar|19|k}}.—{{GHGheb|text=בְּמֹצַֽאֲכֶם|translate=when ye find}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=20}}, stands, according to {{GHGpar|93|q}}, for {{GHGheb|text=מָצְאֲכֶם}}. The tone of the lengthened {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=רְפָאָ֫ה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=41|verse=5}} as {{GHGterm|Mil<sup>e</sup>raʿ}} (before {{GHGheb|text=נַפְשִׁי}}) is to be explained on rhythmical grounds; cf. the analogous cases in {{GHGpar|72|s}}.—The and ''fem. plur. imperative'' in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=1|verse=9}} has, according to ''Qimḥi'', the form {{GHGheb|text=מְצֵ֫אןָ}} and in verse 20 {{GHGheb|text=קְרֵ֫אןָ}}; on the other hand, the Mantua edition and Ginsburg, on good authority, read {{GHGheb|text=מְצֶאןָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=קְרֶאןָ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|74|i}}
3. The {{GHGterm|participle fem.}} is commonly contracted, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מֹצְאת}} (for {{GHGheb|text=מֹצֶ֫אֶת}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=22}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=2|verse=15}}; so {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נִפְלְאה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=30|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=5|verse=7}} (but {{GHGheb|text=נִשָּׂאָת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=25}}), and {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=25}}; less frequent forms are {{GHGheb|text=מֽוֹצְאֵת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=8|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=נֽשְֹׁאֵת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=10|verse=22}} (cf. {{GHGpar|76|b}}, {{GHGheb|text=שְׂאֵת}} beside {{GHGheb|text=לָשֵׂאת}} as {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} from {{GHGheb|text=נָשָׂא}}) and without {{GHGheb|text=א}} (see k) {{GHGheb|text=יוֹצְת}} (from {{GHGheb|text=יָצָא}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=57}}. In the forms {{GHGheb|text=חֹטִאים|translate=sinning}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=33}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=99|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=בֹּדָאם|translate=feigning them}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=6|verse=8}}, the {{GHGheb|text=א}} is elided, and is only retained orthographically ({{GHGpar|23|c}}) after the retraction of its vowel; see the analogous cases in {{GHGpar|75|oo}}.—On the ''plur. masc. ptcp. Niph.'' cf. {{GHGpar|93|oo}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|74|k}}
4. Frequently an {{GHGheb|text=א}} which is quiescent is omitted in writing ({{GHGpar|23|f}}): (''a'') in the middle of the word, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בָּ֫נוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=מָצָ֫תִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=11}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=צָמֵ֫תִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=19}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=32|verse=18}}. In the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=תִּשֶּׂ֫נָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=5|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=1|verse=14}} (but the same form occurs with {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} pleonastic after the manner of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=23|verse=49}}, according to the common reading; cf. {{GHGpar|76|b}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=50|verse=20}}); in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=אַחַטֶּ֫נָּה}} (after elision of the {{GHGheb|text=א}}, cf. {{GHGpar|75|oo}} ) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=39}}; and also in {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נִטְמֵתֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=11|verse=43}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=16}}. (''b'') at the end of the word; {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּבוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=12|verse=12}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}; {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽחֱטִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=13|verse=6}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=53|verse=10}} ({{GHGheb|text=הֶֽחֱלִי}} for {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽחֱלִיא}} {{GHGterm|perfect Hiphʿîl}} of {{GHGheb|text=חָלָה}} formed<section end=par74 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

231.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par74 />after the manner of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}}); in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=יַשִּׁי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=55|verse=16}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָנִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=141|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=אָבִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=1|verse=15}}; in the {{GHGterm|infinitive}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=32|verse=35}}; in the {{GHGterm|participle}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=5|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=19|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=39|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, all in {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} ({{GHGheb|text=מֵבִי}}, always before {{GHGheb|text=א}}, hence perhaps only a scribal error).

{{GHGmargin-letter|74|l}}
5. In the ''jussive, imperfect consecutive'', and {{GHGterm|imperative Hiphʿîl}} a number of cases occur with ''î'' in the final syllable; cf. {{GHGheb|text=יַשִּׁא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=36|verse=14}} (in the parallel passages {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=18|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=32|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=יִשִּׁיא}}); {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּבִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=8|verse=2}} (before {{GHGheb|text=ע}}); {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּֽחֲטִא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=21|verse=11}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=16|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=22|hidebook=1}}); {{GHGheb|text=וַתַּתְבִּא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=6|verse=29}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיּוֹצִא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=11|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=78|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=105|verse=43|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=הָבִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=הוֹצִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=8}} (in both cases before {{GHGheb|text=ע}}). If the tradition be correct (which at least in the defectively written forms appears very doubtful) the retention of the ''î'' is to be attributed to the open syllable; while in the closed syllable of the 3rd ''sing. masc.'' and {{GHGterm|fem.}}, and the 2nd ''sing. masc.'' after {{GHGheb|text=ו}} {{GHGterm|consecutive}}, the ''î'' is always reduced to ''ē''. In the examples before {{GHGheb|text=ע}} considerations of euphony may also have had some influence (cf. {{GHGpar|75|hh}}).—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=40|verse=3}}, Baer reads with the Western school {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּבֵיא}}, while the Orientals read in the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} {{GHGheb|text=ויבוא}}, and in the {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּבֵא}}.

On the transition of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}} to forms of {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} see {{GHGpar|75|nn}}.<section end=par74 />

<section begin=par75 />{{GHGpar-heading|75|Verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, ''e.g.'' {{GHGheb|text=גָּלָה}} to reveal. Paradigm P}}

Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Semit. Sprachwiss.}}, p. 149 ff.; {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, p. 618 ff.—G. R. Berry, ‘Original Waw in {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} verbs’ in {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|AJSL.|American Journal of Semitic Languages.}}}} xx. 256 f.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|a}}
These verbs, like the verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}} ({{GHGpar|69|doublesign=1}}, {{GHGpar|70|nosign=1}}), belong to two different classes, viz. those originally {{GHGheb|text=ל״ו}} and those originally {{GHGheb|text=ל״י}},<ref>According to Wellheusen, ‘''Ueber einige Arten schwacher Verbs''‘ in his ''Skizzen'', vi. p. 255 ff., the {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} verbs, apart from some true {{GHGheb|text=ל״ו}} and some probable {{GHGheb|text=ל״י}}, are to be regarded as originally biliteral. To compensate for their arrested development they lengthened the vowel after the 2nd radical, as the {{GHGheb|text=ע״ו}} verbs did after the 1st radical. But although there is much to be said for this view, it fails to explain pausal forms like {{GHGheb|text=חָסָ֫יָה}} (see u). It seems impossible that these should all be ''late'' formations.</ref> which in Arabic, and even more in Ethiopic, are still clearly distinguished. In Hebrew, instead of the original {{GHGheb|text=ו}} or {{GHGheb|text=י}} at the end of the word, a {{GHGheb|text=ה}} always appears (except in the ''ptcp. pass. Qal'') as a purely orthographic indication of a final vowel ({{GHGpar|23|k}}); hence both classes are called {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גָּלָה}} for {{GHGheb|text=גָּלַי|translate=he has revealed}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלָה}} for {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלֵו|translate=he has rested}}. By far the greater number of these verbs are, however, treated as originally {{GHGheb|text=ל״י}}; only isolated forms occur of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ו}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|74|b}}
{{GHGheb|text=שָׁלָה|translate=to be at rest}} may be recognized as originally {{GHGheb|text=ל״ו}}, in the forms in which the {{GHGterm|Wāw}} appears as a strong consonant, cf. 1st ''sing. perfect Qal'' {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלַ֫וְתִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=26}}, the {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלֵו}} and the derivative {{GHGheb|text=שַׁלְוָה|translate=rest}}; on the other hand the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} is {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁלָ֫יוּ}}. (with {{GHGterm|Yôdh}}). In {{GHGheb|text=עָנָה}} (Arab. {{GHGheb|text=עני}}) ''to answer'', and {{GHGheb|text=עָנָה}} (Arab. {{GHGheb|text=ענו}})<ref>In the Mêšaʿ inscription, line 5, {{GHGheb|text=ויענו|translate=and he oppressed}} occurs as 3rd ''sing. masc. imperfect Piʿēl'', and in line 6, {{GHGheb|text=אענו|translate=I will oppress}} as 1st ''sing.''</ref> ''to be afflicted'', are to be seen two verbs originally distinct, which have been assimilated in Hebrew (see the Lexicon, s. v. {{GHGheb|text=עָנָה}}).<section end=par75 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

232.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par75 />Of quite a different class are those verbs of which the third radical is a ''consonantal'' {{GHGheb|text=ה}} (distinguished by {{GHGterm|Mappîq}}). These are inflected throughout like verbs ''tertiae gutturalis''. Cf. §65 note on the heading.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|c}}
The grammatical structure of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} (see Paradigm ''P'') is based on the following laws:—

'''1.''' In all forms in which the original {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} or {{GHGterm|Wāw}} would stand at the end of the word, it is dropped (cf. {{GHGpar|24|g}}) and {{GHGheb|text=ה}} takes its place as an orthographic indication of the preceding long vowel. Such an indication would have been indispensable, on practical grounds, in the still unvocalized consonantal text. But even after the addition of the vowel signs, the orthographic rule remained, with insignificant exceptions (see {{GHGpar|8|k}}, and ''ā'' in {{GHGheb|text=קָטַ֫לְתָּ}}, &c.), that a final vowel must be indicated by a vowel letter. In verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} which is here employed as a vowel letter is preceded by the same vowel in the same part of the verb throughout all the conjugations. Thus the endings are—

{{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} in all perfects, {{GHGheb|text=גָּלָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=נִגְלָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=גִּלָּה}}, &c.

{{GHGheb|text=־ֶה}} in all imperfects and participles, {{GHGheb|text=יִגְלֶה}}, {{GHGheb|text=גֹּלֶה}}, &c.

{{GHGheb|text=־ֵה}} in all imperatives, {{GHGheb|text=גְּלֵה}}, {{GHGheb|text=גַּלֵּה}}, &c.

{{GHGheb|text=־ֹה}} in the infinitive absolute ({{GHGheb|text=גָּלֹה}}, &c.), except in ''Hiphʿîl, Hophʿal'', and generally also ''Piēl'', see aa and ff.

The ''participle passive Qal'' alone forms an exception, the original {{GHGheb|text=י}} (or {{GHGheb|text=ו}}, see v) reappearing at the end, {{GHGheb|text=גָּלוּי}}; and so also some derived nouns ({{GHGpar|84|c|a}}, ε, &c.).

The {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} always has the ending {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} (with {{GHGheb|text=ת|translate=feminine}}); {{GHGterm|Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=גְּלוֹת}}, {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=גַּלּוֹת}}, &c.; for exceptions, see n and y.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|d}}
These forms may be explained as follows:—in the {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=גָּלָה}} stands, according to the above, for ({{GHGheb|text=י}}){{GHGheb|text=גָּלַ}}, and, similarly, in ''Niphʿal, Puʿal'', and {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}. The {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} may be based on the forms {{GHGheb|text=קִטַּל}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִתְקָטַּל}} ({{GHGpar|52|l}}; and {{GHGpar|54|k}}), and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} on the form {{GHGheb|text=הִקְטַל}}, on the analogy of the ''ă'' in the second syllable of the Arabic ''ʿáqtălă'' ({{GHGpar|53|a}}). Perhaps, however, the final''ā'' of these conjugations simply follows the analogy of the other conjugations.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|e}}
The explanation of the final tone-bearing {{GHGheb|text=־ֶה}} of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} is still a matter of dispute. As to the various treatments of it, see Barth, {{GHGcite|title=Nominalbildung}}, i. p. xxx ff, with § 136, Rem., and {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} xliv. 695 f., against Philippi’s objections in the ''Zeitschrift für Völkerpsychologie'', 1890, p. 356 f.; also {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} lvi. 244, where Barth appeals to the rule that, in the period before the differentiation of the North Semitic dialects, final ''iy'' becomes {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ}} ({{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=־ְה}}), not ''î''; M. Lambert, Journ. Asiat. 1893, p. 285; Prätorius, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} lv. 365. The most probable explanation now seems to be, first, that the uniform pronunciation of ''all'' imperfects and participles with {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} in the last syllable merely follows the analogy of the ''impf. Qal'', and secondly, that the {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} of the ''impf. Qal'' does perhaps ultimately represent a contraction of the original termination {{GHGheb|text=־ַי}} (= ''ai''), although elsewhere (e.g. in the {{GHGterm|imperative}} of {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}) ''ai'' is usually contracted to ''ê''.
<section end=par75 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

233.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par75 />{{GHGmargin-letter|75|f}}
'''2.''' When the original {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} stands at the end of the syllable before an afformative beginning with a consonant ({{GHGheb|text=ת}}, {{GHGheb|text=נ‍}}) there arises (''a'') in the ''perfects'', primarily the diphthong ''ai'' ({{GHGheb|text=־ַי}}). In the middle of the word this ought always to be contracted to ''ê'' ({{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}}), but this ''ê'' is only found consistently in the passive conjugations, whilst regularly in {{GHGterm|Qal}}, and frequently in the other active and reflexive conjugations (especially in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}), it appears as ''î'' (cf. x, z, ee). This ''î'', however, in the ''perf. Qal'' is not to be explained as a weakening of an original ''ê'', but as the original vowel of the ''intransitive'' form. It then became usual also in the ''transitive'' forms of {{GHGterm|Qal}} (and in some other conjugations on this analogy), whereas e.g. in Syriac the two kinds of forms are still carefully distinguished.—(''b'') In the ''imperfects'' and ''imperatives'', {{GHGheb|text=־ֶי}} with the tone always appears before the afformative {{GHGheb|text=נָה}}. On the most probable explanation of this {{GHGheb|text=־ֶי}}, see above, e.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|g}}
'''Summary.''' Accordingly before afformatives beginning with a consonant the principal vowel is—

In the perfect ''Qal î'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גָּ֫לִיתָ}};

In the perfects of the other active and reflexive conjugations, sometimes ''ê'', sometimes ''î'', {{GHGheb|text=גִּלֵּ֫יתָ}} and {{GHGheb|text=גִּלִּ֫יתָ}}; {{GHGheb|text=נִגְלֵ֫יתָ}} and {{GHGheb|text=נִגְ֫לִיתָ}};

In the perfects passive always ''ê'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גֻּלֵּ֫יתָ}};

In the imperfects and imperatives always {{GHGheb|text=־ֶי}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גְּלֶ֫ינָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּגְלֶ֫ינָה}}.

The diphthongal forms have been systematically retained in Arabic and Ethiopic; only as an exception and in the popular language is the diphthong contracted. In Aramaic the contracted forms predominate, yet the Syriac, for example, has in {{GHGterm|Qal}} 2nd ''pers. sing. g<sup>e</sup>lait'' (but 1st ''pers. sing.'' {{GHGheb|text=גְּלִית}}), and so too the Western Aramaic {{GHGheb|text=גְּלַיתָ}}, but also {{GHGheb|text=גְּלֵיתָ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|h}}
'''3.''' Before the vocalic afformatives ({{GHGheb|text=וּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}) the {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} is usually dropped altogether, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גָּלוּ}} (ground-form ''găl̆yû''), {{GHGheb|text=תִּגְלִי}}, {{GHGterm|participle fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=גֹּלָה}}, ''plur. masc.'' {{GHGheb|text=גֹּלִים}}; yet the old full forms also not infrequently occur, especially in {{GHGterm|pause}}, see u. The elision of the {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} takes place regularly before ''suffixes'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גָּֽלְךָ}} (see ll).

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|i}}
'''4.''' In the 3rd ''sing. fem. perfect'', the original feminine ending {{GHGheb|text=־ַת}} was appended to the stem; hence, after elision of the {{GHGterm|Yôdh}}, arose properly forms like {{GHGheb|text=גָּלָת}}, with ''ā'', in the final syllable with the tone, This form, however, has been but rarely preserved (see below, m). The analogy of the other forms had so much influence, that the common ending {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} was added pleonastically to the ending {{GHGheb|text=־ָת}}. Before the {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} the vowel of the ending {{GHGheb|text=־ָת}}, which thus loses the tone, becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, and thus there arise such forms as {{GHGheb|text=גָּֽלְתָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=נִגְלְתָה}}, &c. (but in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=גָּלָ֫תָה}}, &c.).

For similar cases see {{GHGpar|70|d}}; {{GHGpar|91|m}}.
<section end=par75 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

234.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par75 />{{GHGmargin-letter|75|k}}
'''5.''' Finally, a strongly-marked peculiarity of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} is the rejection of the ending {{GHGheb|text=־ֶה}} in forming the {{GHGterm|jussive}} and the {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}}. This shortening c curs in all the conjugations, and sometimes also involves further changes in the vocalization (see o, y, bb, gg). Similarly, in some conjugations a ''shortened imperative'' (cf. {{GHGpar|48|k}}) is formed by ''apocope'' of the final {{GHGheb|text=־ֵה}} (see cc, gg).

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|l}}
'''6.''' The ordinary form of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} with the ending {{GHGheb|text=־ֶה}} serves in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} to express the cohortative also ({{GHGpar|48|c}}); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=25|verse=17}}, &c. With a final {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} there occur only: in {{GHGterm|Qal}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֶשְׁעָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=117}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֶֽהֱמָ֑יָה}} (with the {{GHGheb|text=י}} retained, see below, u) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=77|verse=4}}; and in {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=וְנִשְׁתָּ֫עָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=23}} (with {{GHGterm|Ṭiphḥa}}, therefore in lesser pause).

{{center|{{Small-caps|Remarks.}}

I. ''On Qal .''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|m}}
1. The older form of the {{GHGterm|fem.}} of the 3rd ''sing. perf.'' {{GHGheb|text=גָּלָת}}, mentioned above, under i (cf. {{GHGpar|74|g}}), is preserved in {{GHGheb|text=עָשָׂת}} (before {{GHGheb|text=א}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=25|verse=21}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=9|verse=37}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}})<ref>In the Siloam inscription also (see above, {{GHGpar|2|d}}), line 3, {{GHGheb|text=הית}} may be read {{GHGheb|text=הָיָת}} quite as well as [{{GHGheb|text=ה}}]{{GHGheb|text=הָֽיְתָ}}.</ref>; likewise in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִרְצָת}} (before {{GHGheb|text=א}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=34}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֶלְאָ֑ת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=24|verse=12}}; and in {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=הָגְלָת}} (before {{GHGheb|text=יְ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=19}}.—The 2nd ''sing. fem.'' is also written {{GHGheb|text=־ִיתְ}}; thus in the textus receptus {{GHGheb|text=וְהָיִיתְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=2}}, and always in Baer’s editions (since 1872), as in most other verbs; {{GHGheb|text=חָזִיתְ}} and {{GHGheb|text=גִּלִּיתְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=57|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=עָשִׂיתְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=48}}, &c. (so {{GHGheb|text=וְהוֹצֵאתְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=17|verse=13}} from {{GHGheb|text=יָצָא}}). In the 3rd ''pers. plur.'' the tone, instead of keeping its usual place ({{GHGheb|text=גָּלוּ֫}}, &c.), is retracted in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=37|verse=20}}, {{GHGheb|text=כָּ֫לוּ}}, both on account of the {{GHGterm|pause}} and also in rhythmical antithesis to the preceding {{GHGheb|text=כָּלוּ֫}}; also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=16|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=תָּעוּ}} (according to Delitzsch for the sake of the assonance with {{GHGheb|text=נָגָ֫עוּ}}); and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=חָ֫זוּ}}.—On the tone of the {{GHGterm|perfect consecutive}} see {{GHGpar|49|k}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|n}}
2. The ''infin. absol.'' frequently has {{GHGheb|text=וֹ}} (probably a survival of the older orthography) for {{GHGheb|text=־ֹה}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הָיוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=עָשׂוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=4|verse=18}}, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=31|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=קָנוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=24|verse=24}}; {{GHGheb|text=רָאוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=9}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=12}}), &c., beside {{GHGheb|text=רָאֹה}}. The form {{GHGheb|text=שָׁתוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=13}} (beside {{GHGheb|text=שָׁתוֹ}} in the same verse) appears to have been chosen on account of its similarity in sound to {{GHGheb|text=שָׁחֹט}}; so in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=20}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=10|verse=4}}, {{GHGheb|text=אָלוֹת}} (unless it is a substantive, ''oaths'') and {{GHGheb|text=כָּדֹת}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=עָרוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=3|verse=13}}.—Conversely, instead of the {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} {{GHGheb|text=גְּלוֹת}} such forms are occasionally found as {{GHGheb|text=גְּלֹה}} or {{GHGheb|text=גְּלוֹ}}, cf. {{GHGheb|text=רְאֹה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=48|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=קְנֹה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=16|verse=16}}; {{GHGheb|text=עֲשׂה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=50|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=101|verse=3}}, also {{GHGheb|text=עֲשׂוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=28}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=31|verse=4}}), and even with the ''suffix'' {{GHGheb|text=הוּ}} the very remarkable form {{GHGheb|text=עֲשׂ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=18|verse=18}}.<ref>All these infinitives construct in ''ô'', in the Pentateuch, belong to the document called E; cf. {{GHGpar|69|m}}, second note.</ref>—The feminine form {{GHGheb|text=רַֽאֲוָה}} (for {{GHGheb|text=דְאוֹת}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=28|verse=17}}, analogous to nouns like {{GHGheb|text=גַּֽאֲוָה}} (cf. {{GHGpar|45|d}}), is strange, but {{GHGheb|text=הֱיֵה}} as ''infin.'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=15}} is quite inexplicable.—The forms {{GHGheb|text=הֹגוֹ}} and {{GHGheb|text=הֹרוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=13}} are perhaps to be regarded with Barth, {{GHGcite|title=Nominalbildung}}, {{GHGpar|51|a}}, as ''infinitives absolute'' of the {{GHGterm|passive}} of {{GHGterm|Qal}} (see above, {{GHGpar|53|u}}), not of {{GHGterm|Pôʿēl}}.—The 2nd ''sing. masc. imperative'' {{GHGheb|text=וֶחְֽיֶה}} occurs in the principal pause in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=4|verse=4}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=7|verse=2|hidebook=1}}; but<section end=par75 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

235.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="46.39.50.179" /></noinclude><section begin="par75" />probably these forms are simply to be attributed to a Masoretic school, which in general marked the difference between certain forms by the use of ''é'' for ''ē'', and conversely ''ē'' for ''é''; cf. the analogous examples in {{GHGpar|52|n}}, and especially {{GHGpar|75|hh}}, also Kautzsch, ''Grammatik des Bibl.-Aram.'', § 17, 2, Rem. 1.—On the reading {{GHGheb|text=וּֽרֲאֵ֫ינָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=3|verse=11}} (for {{GHGheb|text=וּֽרֲאֶ֫ינָה}}, on the analogy of the reading {{GHGheb|text=מְצֵ֫אנָה}}, &c., {{GHGpar|74|h}}), see Baer’s note on the passage.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|o}}
3. The ''shortening'' of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} (see above, k, and the note on hh) occasions in {{GHGterm|Qal}} the following changes:

(''a'') As a rule the first radical takes a helping {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, or, if the second radical is a guttural, a helping {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} (according to {{GHGpar|28|e}}). Thus {{GHGheb|text=יִ֫גֶל}} for {{GHGheb|text=יִגְלְ}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫בֶז|translate=and he despised}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=25|verse=34}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫בֶן|translate=and he built}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִ֫שַׁע|translate=he looks}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫מַח|translate=and he destroyed}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=23}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|p}}
(''b'') The ''ĭ'' of the preformative is then sometimes lengthened to ''ē'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יֵ֫רֶא|translate=he sees}}. This, however, mostly happens only after the preformative {{GHGheb|text=ת}}, whilst after {{GHGheb|text=י}} the homogeneous ''ĭ'' remains, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַתֵּ֫כֶל}} (but {{GHGheb|text=יִ֫כֶל}}), {{GHGheb|text=וַתֵּ֫פֶן}} (but {{GHGheb|text=יִ֫פֶן}}), {{GHGheb|text=וַתֵּ֫רֶב}} (but {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫רֶב}}); with middle guttural {{GHGheb|text=תֵּ֫תַע}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַתֵּ֫כַהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=17|verse=7}} (from {{GHGheb|text=כָּהָה}}). The unusual position of the tone in {{GHGheb|text=תֵּרֵ֫א}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=9|verse=5}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְתֵרֵ֫א}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=10}} (so Baer and Ginsb.; ed. Mant. {{GHGheb|text=יִרֶ֫א}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְיִרֶ֫א}}) is best explained (except in {{GHGheb|text=יֵרֶ֫א}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=33}}, before {{GHGheb|text=פ}}) on the analogy of {{GHGheb|text=קוּמָ֫ה}}, &c., {{GHGpar|72|s}}, as due to the following {{GHGheb|text=א}}. But cf. also hh

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|q}}
(''c'') The helping vowel is elsewhere not used under the circumstances mentioned in {{GHGpar|28|d}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּשְׁבְּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=41|verse=10}}, cf. {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּפְתְּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=27}}; on the other hand, with ''ĭ'' lengthened into ''ē'' (see p) {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּשְׁתְּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּבְךְּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּרְדְּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֵשְׂטְ}}. The form {{GHGheb|text=יֵ֫רֶא|translate=he sees}}, occurs parallel with {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּרְא|translate=and he saw}} (but 3rd {{GHGterm|fem.}} always {{GHGheb|text=וַתֵּ֫רֶא}}), the latter with the original {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} on account of the following {{GHGheb|text=ר}}, and identical with the 3rd ''sing. masc.'' of the ''imperf. consec. Hiphʿîl'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=11|verse=4}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|r}}
(''d'') Examples of verbs ''primae gutturalis'' (§ 63), and at the same time {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, are {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּ֫עַשׂ}}, in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫עַשׂ|translate=and he made}}, from {{GHGheb|text=עָשָׂה}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּ֫עַן|translate=and he answered}}, from {{GHGheb|text=עָנָה}} (always identical with the corresponding forms in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}), {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּ֫חַץ|translate=and he divided}}, from {{GHGheb|text=חצה}}. On some similar forms of {{GHGheb|text=פ״א}} see {{GHGpar|76|d}}.—In the following cases the initial (hard) guttural does not affect the form: {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫חַר|translate=and he was wroth}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫חַן|translate=and he encamped}} (3rd plur. {{GHGheb|text=וַיִַּֽחֲנוּ}}), {{GHGheb|text=יִ֫חַדְּ}} (with {{GHGterm|Dageš lene}} and {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}) ''let it rejoice'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=6}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=18|verse=9}}.—On {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּז}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְיֵז}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּט}} ({{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} as well as {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}}), &c., see {{GHGpar|76|b}}, c, f.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|s}}
(''e'') The verbs {{GHGheb|text=הָיָה|translate=to be}}, and {{GHGheb|text=חָיָה|translate=to live}}, of which the shortened imperfects ought to be ''yihy'' and ''yiḥy'', change these forms to {{GHGheb|text=יְהִי}} and {{GHGheb|text=יְחִי}}, the second {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} being resolved into ''î'' at the end of the word; but in {{GHGterm|pause}} ({{GHGpar|29|n}}) {{GHGheb|text=יֶ֫הִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֶ֫חִי}}, with the original ''ă'' modified to {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} with the tone (cf. also ''nouns'' like {{GHGheb|text=בְּכִי}} for ''bakhy''. in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=בֶּ֫כִי}}; {{GHGheb|text=עֳנִי}} for ''‛ŏny'', &c., {{GHGpar|84|c|a}}, and {{GHGpar|93|x}}). For {{GHGheb|text=תֶּ֫שִׁי}}, however, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=18}}, since no verb {{GHGheb|text=שָׁיָה}} exists, we must read either {{GHGheb|text=תֵּשׁ}}, or better {{GHGheb|text=תִּשֶּׁה}} (Samaritan {{GHGheb|text=תשא}}), as {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} of {{GHGheb|text=נָשָׁה|translate=to forget}}.—Analogous to {{GHGheb|text=יְהִי}} from {{GHGheb|text=הָיָה}}, there occurs once, from {{GHGheb|text=הָוָה|translate=to be}}, the form {{GHGheb|text=יְהוּא}} for {{GHGheb|text=יְהוּ|translate=he will be}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=11|verse=3}}, but no doubt {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} is the right reading.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|t}}
The ''full'' forms (without apocope of the {{GHGheb|text=־ֶה}}, cf. {{GHGpar|49|c}}) not infrequently occur after {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}}, especially in the 1st pers. and in the later books, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֶרְאֶה|translate=and I saw}}, twenty times, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=7|verse=21}} in {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}, but never in the Pentateuch ({{GHGheb|text=וָאֵ֫רֶא}} fifteen times, of which three are in the Pent.); also in the<section end="par75" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

236.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par75 />3rd pers. {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּרְאֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=18|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=42|verse=16}} ''Q<sup>e</sup>re''; {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּֽעֲשֶׂה|translate=and he made}}, four times (but {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּ֫עַשׂ}} over 200 times); cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=2}} ({{GHGheb|text=וַתִּזְנֶה}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=10|verse=29}} ({{GHGheb|text=וַתַּֽעֲלֶה}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=16}} ({{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֲצַוֶּה}}), and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=48}}. So also occasionally for the {{GHGterm|jussive}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=34|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=28|verse=6}}.—For the well attested, but meaningless {{GHGheb|text=תִּֽירְאוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=21}} (doubtless caused by the following {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּירָֽאוּ}}), read {{GHGheb|text=תִּרְאוּ|translate=ye see}}, with Ginsburg.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|u}}
4. The original {{GHGheb|text=י}} sometimes appears even before afformatives beginning with a vowel (cf. above, h and l), especially in and before the {{GHGterm|pause}}, and before the full plural ending {{GHGheb|text=־וּן}}, or where for any reason an emphasis rests on the word. {{GHGterm|Perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=חָסָ֫יָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=57|verse=2}}, {{GHGheb|text=חָסָ֫יוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=37}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=2}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}; {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּעָ֫יוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=12}}. {{GHGterm|Imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יֶאֱֽחָ֑יוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=14|hidebook=1}} (without the {{GHGterm|pause}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=32}}); {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁלָ֫יוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=122|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=12|verse=6}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=77|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִרְבְּיֻן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=8|verse=13}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=36|verse=9}}: more frequently like {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁתָּיוּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=78|verse=44}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=31|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=36|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=39|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=83|verse=3|hidebook=1}}; before a suffix, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=25}}. Also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=26|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=דָּֽלְיוּ}}, as ''perf. Qal'' from {{GHGheb|text=דָּלָה}}, was perhaps originally intended, but hardly {{GHGheb|text=דָּלָ֫יוּ}}, since these full forms, though they may stand out of pause, do not begin sentences; {{GHGheb|text=דַּ֫לְיוּ}} probably points to {{GHGheb|text=דַּ֫לּוּ}} from {{GHGheb|text=דָּלַל}} as the right reading, since the sense requires an intransitive verb. Cf. further, v, x, dd, gg.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|v}}
5. The {{GHGterm|participle active}} (cf. Vollers, ‘Das Qâtil-Partizipium,’ {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZA.|Zeitschrift für Assyriologie und verwandte Gebiete, ed. by C. Bezold. Lpz. 18S6 ff.}}}} 1903, p. 312 ff., and on the participles of {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, ''ibid.'', p. 316 ff.), besides feminine forms like {{GHGheb|text=עֹלָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=31}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=רֹאָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=20|verse=12}}, has also a ''feminine'' which retains the 3rd radical {{GHGheb|text=י}}, viz. {{GHGheb|text=בּֽוֹכִיָּה}} ( ={{GHGheb|text=בֹּכָה}}) ''weeping'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=16}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֽוֹמִיָּה|translate=tumultuous}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=2}} (''plur.'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=21}}); {{GHGheb|text=צֽוֹפִיָּה|translate=spying}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=31|verse=27}}, {{GHGheb|text=פֹּֽרִיָּה|translate=fruitful}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=128|verse=3}}, ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽתִיּוֹת|translate=the things that are to come}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=23}}. With the ordinary strong inflexion {{GHGheb|text=י}} appears in {{GHGheb|text=עֹֽטְיָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=7}}, but perhaps there also {{GHGheb|text=עֹֽטִיָּה}} was intended, unless it should be {{GHGheb|text=טֹֽעִיָּה|translate=a wanderer}}. For {{GHGheb|text=רֹאָ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=10}}, {{GHGheb|text=רֹאֵ֫נִי}} is to be read.—On {{GHGheb|text=עשֵֹׁה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=40}} for {{GHGheb|text=עשֶֹׁה}}, cf. {{GHGpar|116|g}}, note.—In the {{GHGterm|participle passive}} the 3rd radical still sometimes appears as {{GHGheb|text=ו}} ({{GHGpar|24|b}}), cf. {{GHGheb|text=עָשׂוּ|translate=made}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=41|verse=25}}, {{GHGheb|text=צָפוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=22}}, contracted from {{GHGheb|text=עָשׂוּו}}, {{GHGheb|text=צָפוּו}}; and before a formative ending, it even has its consonantal sound, {{GHGheb|text=העשוום}} (read {{GHGheb|text=הָֽעֲשׂוּוִם}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=23|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=עשוות}} (read ''‛<sup>a</sup>sûwôth'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=18}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}, {{GHGheb|text=נטוות}} (read ''n<sup>e</sup>ṭûwôth'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=16}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}. The shortening of the ''û''in {{GHGheb|text=רְאֻיּוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=2|verse=9}} is irregular.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|w}}
6. The defective writing is rare in such forms as {{GHGheb|text=וְהָיִ֫תָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=33}}; {{GHGheb|text=בָּנִ֫תִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=44}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=9|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּדְלֶ֫נָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=16}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=18|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=7|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=17|verse=5}}, &c.), and the pronunciation {{GHGheb|text=תִּרְאֶ֫ינָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=10}}, cf. {{GHGheb|text=תַּֽעֲנֶ֑נָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=29}} (unless they are ''sing.'' with ''suff.'' of the 3rd ''sing. fem.''). Both cases are probably to be explained according to {{GHGpar|20|i}}.

{{center|II. ''On Niphʿal''.}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|x}}
7. Here the forms with {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}} in the 1st and 2nd ''pers. sing.'' of the {{GHGterm|perfect}} predominate {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} only in {{GHGheb|text=נִקִּ֫יתָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=8}}); on the other hand in the 1st ''plur'', always {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}}, as {{GHGheb|text=נִגְלִ֫ינוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=8}}. No examples of the 2nd ''plur.'' occur.—With {{GHGheb|text=י}} retained in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=נִטָּ֔יוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=24|verse=6}}; once with an initial guttural {{GHGheb|text=נִֽחֲרוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=6}} for {{GHGheb|text=נֶֽחֱרוּ}}, probably arising from the ordinary strong form ''niḥru'', but the harshness of {{GHGheb|text=ח}} immediately followed by {{GHGheb|text=ר}} is avoided by pronouncing the {{GHGheb|text=ח}} with {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Pathaḥ}}.—In the 3rd ''sing. fem.'' {{GHGheb|text=נִשְׁתָּֽוָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=27|verse=15}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}} for {{GHGheb|text=נִשְׁתְּוָה}}) {{GHGheb|text=ו}} and {{GHGheb|text=ת}} may be transposed for euphonic reasons; but probably we should simply read {{GHGheb|text=נִשְׁוָ֫תָה}}.—Among Niphʿal forms of {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} must be classed, with Buxtorf and<section end=par75 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

237.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par75 />others (cf. Nöldeke, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} xxx. 185), {{GHGheb|text=נַֽאֲנָה}} from {{GHGheb|text=אָוָה}}, not Pi‛lel of {{GHGheb|text=נאה}} = {{GHGheb|text=נאו}}; hence, according to {{GHGpar|23|d}}, {{GHGheb|text=נָאווּ|translate=they are beautiful}} (for {{GHGheb|text=נַֽאֲווּ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=52|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=10}}; but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=93|verse=5}}, where Baer requires {{GHGheb|text=נָֽאֲוָה}}, read {{GHGheb|text=נַֽאֲנָה}} with ed. Mant., Ginsb.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|y}}
8. The ''apocope'' of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} causes no further changes beyond the rejection of the {{GHGheb|text=־ֶה}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִגָּל}} from {{GHGheb|text=יִגָּלֶה}}; in one verb ''middle guttural'', however, a form occurs with the {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} shortened to {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}}, viz. {{GHGheb|text=יִמַּח}} (for {{GHGheb|text=יִמָּח}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=109|verse=13}}, as in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}; but in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=תִּמָּֽח}} verse 14. Cf. bb.—The {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} {{GHGheb|text=נִגְלוֹת}} emphasizing an {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=6|verse=20}}, is very extraordinary; probably it is a subsequent correction of an erroneous repetition of {{GHGheb|text=הגלות}}.—The ''infin. constr.'' {{GHGheb|text=לְחֵֽרָאֹה}} occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=21}} for {{GHGheb|text=לְהֵֽרָאֹת}}; cf. above, n.—On the {{GHGterm|infinitive Niphʿal}} with the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} elided, see {{GHGpar|51|l}}.—The irregular {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽעֲלוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=36|verse=3}} has probably arisen from a combination of the readings {{GHGheb|text=תַּֽעֲלוּ}} ({{GHGterm|Qal}}) and {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽעָלוּ}} ({{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}). Similarly the solecism {{GHGheb|text=נְמִבְזָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=9}} might be due to a combination of the ''participle fem. Niphʿal'' ({{GHGheb|text=נִבְּזָה}}, cf. {{GHGheb|text=נַחְלָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֶחְפָּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=נַֽעֲשָׂח}}) with the {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} ({{GHGheb|text=מֻבְזָה}}); but it is more correct, with Wellhausen, to explain the {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}} from a confusion with {{GHGheb|text=נמס}} and to read, in fact, {{GHGheb|text=נִבְזָח וְנִמְאָ֫סָת}}.

{{center|III. ''On Piʿēl, Pôʿēl, Puʿal, and Hithpaʿēl.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|z}}
9. In the 1st and 2nd persons of the {{GHGterm|perfect Piʿēl}} the second syllable in most of the instances has {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} on the analogy of {{GHGterm|Qal}} (see f), as {{GHGheb|text=דִּמִּ֫יתָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=קִוִּ֫יתִי}}; always so in the first ''plur.'', and before ''suffixes'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כִּסִּ֫ינוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=26}}, {{GHGheb|text=דִּכִּיתָ֫נוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=44|verse=20}}. The form with {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}} is found only in the 1st ''sing.'' (e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=4|verse=21}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=17|hidebook=1}} along with the form with ''î''). On the tone of the ''perf. consec. Pi‛el'' of {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, see {{GHGpar|49|k}}.—{{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} has (besides {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=16}}) as a rule {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=50|verse=24}}). On the other hand, {{GHGterm|Puʿal}} always has {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עֻשֵּׂ֫יתִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=15}}.—A 1st ''sing. perfect Pô‛ēl'' {{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹשֵׂ֫תִי}} ( ={{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹוסֵיתִי}}) occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=13}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|aa}}
10. The ''infinitive absolute Piʿēl'' takes the form {{GHGheb|text=כַּלֵּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=קַוֵּה}} (like {{GHGheb|text=קַטֵּל}}, the more frequent form even in the strong verb, see {{GHGpar|52|o}}); with ''ô'' only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=40|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=קַוֹּה}}; with ''ôth'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=3|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=עָרוֹת}} (cf. above, n). On {{GHGheb|text=הֹגוֹ}} and {{GHGheb|text=הֹרוֹ}}, ''infinitives absolute'' of the passive of {{GHGterm|Qal}}, not of ''Pô‛ēl'', see above, n.—As {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} {{GHGheb|text=חַכֵּי}} occurs in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=6|verse=9}} (only orthographically different from {{GHGheb|text=חַכֵּה}}, if the text is correct); {{GHGheb|text=לְכַלֵּא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=9|verse=24}} (on the {{GHGheb|text=א}} see rr); {{GHGheb|text=עַד־לְכַלֵּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=24|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=31|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, for which in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=13|verse=17.19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=9|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=עד־כַּלֵּה}} with ''infin. abs.''; in {{GHGterm|Puʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=עֻנּוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=132|verse=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|bb}}
11. The apocopated {{GHGterm|imperfect}} must (according to {{GHGpar|20|l}}) lose the {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}} of the second radical, hence {{GHGheb|text=וַיְצַו|translate=and he commanded}}, {{GHGheb|text=תְּעַר}} (for {{GHGheb|text=תְּעָרֶה}}=''t<sup>e</sup>‛arrè'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=141|verse=8}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=20}}; even in the principal pause {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תְּגַֽל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=9}}; {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּתְגַּל|translate=and he uncovered himself}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=תִּתְרַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=22|verse=24}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=37|verse=1.7.8}}. With the lengthening of {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} to {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיְתָו|translate=and he made marks}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=14}} (but read with Thenius {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫תָף}}, and instead of the meaningless {{GHGheb|text=וַיְשַׁנּוֹ}}<!-- not a translation --> ''ibid.'' read {{GHGheb|text=וַיְשַׁן}}). In {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תִּתְגָּר}}, in close connexion, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=9.19}}; {{GHGheb|text=תִּשְׁתָּע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=10}}; according to ''Qimḥi'' also {{GHGheb|text=יִתְאָו}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּתְאָו}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=45|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=23|verse=3.6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=11|verse=17}}, whilst Baer and Ginsburg read with the best authorities {{GHGheb|text=יִתְאַו}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּתְאַו}} (but cf. König, ''Lehrgeböude'', i. 597).<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=34|verse=7}} f., according to verse 10, {{GHGheb|text=תִּתְאַוֻּ}} (={{GHGheb|text=תִּתְאַוּוּ}}) is intended to be read for {{GHGheb|text=תְּתָאוּ}} ({{GHGterm|imperfect Piʿēl}} from {{GHGheb|text=תָּאָה}}).</ref>—On {{GHGheb|text=אֲחַוְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=17}} (for {{GHGheb|text=אֲחַוְּךָ}}) cf. {{GHGpar|20|m}}; on {{GHGheb|text=אּכָלְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=3}}, see {{GHGpar|27|q}};<section end=par75 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

238.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par75 />on {{GHGheb|text=יְרַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=13}}, see {{GHGpar|69|g}}. Finally, on {{GHGheb|text=דַּלְיוּ}}, which is referred to {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} by some, as a supposed {{GHGterm|imperative}}, see above, u.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|cc}}
12. Examples of apocopated ''imperatives'' in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} are: {{GHGheb|text=צַו}}, also {{GHGheb|text=צַוֵּה|translate=command thou}}, {{GHGheb|text=גַּל|translate=open thou}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=18.22}}; {{GHGheb|text=מַן|translate=prepare thou}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=61|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=נַס}} for {{GHGheb|text=נַסֵּה|translate=prove thou}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=1|verse=12}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְחָ֑ל|translate=feign thyself sick}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=5}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=24}}.—On {{GHGheb|text=רַבֶּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=29}}, cf. {{GHGpar|48|l}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=137|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=עָ֫רוּ|translate=rase it}}, is found twice instead of {{GHGheb|text=עָר֫וּ}} (for ''‛arrû'') for rhythmical reasons (cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=וִיעָ֫רוּ}} in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=24|verse=11}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|dd}}
13. Examples of forms in which the {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} is retained are the ''imperfects'' {{GHGheb|text=תְּדַמְּיוּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=18}}, cf. verse 25 and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=46|verse=5|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְכַסְיֻמ֑וּ|translate=they cover them}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=5}}; {{GHGterm|participle Puʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=מְמֻֽחָיִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=25|verse=6}}; for {{GHGheb|text=אֲרַיָּ֫וֶךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=16|verse=9}} (from {{GHGheb|text=רָוָה}}) read with Margolis, {{GHGheb|text=אֲרַוַּ֫יִךְ}}.

{{center|IV. ''On Hiphʿîl and Hophʿal''.}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|ee}}
14. The 3rd ''sing.perfect Hiphʿîl'' sometimes has {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} in the first syllable instead of ''ĭ'' ({{GHGpar|53|p}}), especially in {{GHGheb|text=הֶגְלָה}} (but {{GHGterm|perfect consecutive}} {{GHGheb|text=וְהִגְלָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=24|verse=14}}), {{GHGheb|text=הֶרְאָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֶלְאָה}}; also with ''suffixes'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֶגְלָם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=8|verse=7}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָלְאָ֑נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=7}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְהֶפְדָּהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=8}}. The {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} also occurs in the 1st ''sing''., e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הָלְאֵתִ֫יךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=6|verse=3}}. On {{GHGheb|text=וְהַרְאֵיתִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=5}}, cf. {{GHGpar|53|p}}. The forms with ''ê'' in the second syllable (also written defectively, as {{GHGheb|text=וְהִכֵּתִ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=21|verse=6}}) are found throughout in the 1st ''sing''. (except {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=5|verse=13}}), rarely in the 2nd ''sing. masc.'', and never in the 1st ''plur.'' In the other persons they are about equally common with ''î'', except in the 2nd ''plur.'', where ''î'' predominates. Before ''suffixes'' the forms with ''î'' predominate throughout; cf., however, ''ê'' in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=4|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=6|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=4|verse=11}}. On the tone of the ''perf. consec. Hiph.'' of {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, see {{GHGpar|49|k}}. In {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} only {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}} occurs in the 2nd syllable.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|ff}}
15. In the {{GHGterm|infinitive Hiphʿîl}} of {{GHGheb|text=רָבָה|translate=to be abundant}}, besides the ''construct'' {{GHGheb|text=הַרְבּוֹת}} we find the ''absolute'' {{GHGheb|text=הַרְבָּה}} taking the place of the common form {{GHGheb|text=הַרְבֵּה}}, which had come to be used invariably (but König calls attention to its use as {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=20}}) as an adverb, in the sense of ''much''; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=11}} the {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} requires {{GHGheb|text=הַרְבַּת}} for the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} {{GHGheb|text=הַרְבִּית}}, an evident scribal error for {{GHGheb|text=הַרְבּוֹת}}. Cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=49}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=22|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=63}}; the pointing {{GHGheb|text=הַרְבֶּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=42|verse=2}} probably arises from regarding this form as a noun.—On {{GHGheb|text=הַמְּרוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=17|verse=2}} (with ''Dageš f. dirimens'') see {{GHGpar|20|h}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=3|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=הַכּוֹת}} (before {{GHGheb|text=א}}) is probably {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}}, used in order to avoid the hiatus, cf. {{GHGpar|113|x}}, and on a similar case in {{GHGterm|Qal}}, see above, n.—On the ''infinitives'' with elision of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, cf. {{GHGpar|53|q}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|gg}}
16. The ''shortened imperfect Hiphʿîl'' either takes no helping vowel, as {{GHGheb|text=יַפְתְּ|translate=let him enlarge}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=27}}; {{GHGheb|text=יַרְדְּ|translate=he shall subdue}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּשְׁקְ|translate=and he watered}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=10}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּרְא|translate=and he showed}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=11|verse=4}} (see {{GHGpar|28|d}}): or else has a helping vowel, as {{GHGheb|text=יֶ֫גֶל}} (for {{GHGheb|text=יַ֫גֶל}}, see {{GHGpar|27|r}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=18|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיֶּ֫פֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=105|verse=24}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַתֶּ֫מֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=5|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיֶּ֫תַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=33|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=וארב}} i.e. probably {{GHGheb|text=וָאֶ֫רֶב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=24|verse=3}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} ({{GHGheb|text=וָאַֽרְבֶּה}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}).—Examples of verbs ''first guttural'': {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּ֫עַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=2}}, {{GHGheb|text=וָאַ֫עַל}}, &c., which can be distinguished as {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} from the similar forms in {{GHGterm|Qal}} only by the sense.—The ''apocopated imperative Hiphʿîl'' always (except in verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַךְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַט}}, {{GHGpar|76|c}}) has a helping vowel, {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} or {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֶ֫רֶב|translate=increase thou}} (for ''harb'', {{GHGheb|text=הַרְבֵּה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=51|verse=4}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}, also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=38}}; where, however, it cannot be explained the text stands; {{GHGheb|text=הֶ֫רֶף|translate=let alone}} (for {{GHGheb|text=הַרְףְּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַרְפֵּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=9|verse=14}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=הַ֫עַל}} (for {{GHGheb|text=הַֽעֲלֵה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=8|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=12|hidebook=1}}; but for {{GHGheb|text=הָשַׁע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=39|verse=14}}, which could only be {{GHGterm|imperative Hiphʿîl}} of {{GHGheb|text=שָׁעַע}} (=''smear over'', as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=10}}), read with Baethgen {{GHGheb|text=שְׁעֵה|translate=look away}}.—The {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} with {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} retained occurs only in {{GHGheb|text=תּוֹגְיוּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=2}}, from {{GHGheb|text=יָגָה}}. Cf. u.<section end=par75 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

239.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par75" />{{center|V. ''In General.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|hh}}
17. In Aramaic the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} and {{GHGterm|participle}} of all the conjugations terminate in {{GHGheb|text=־ֵא}} or {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}}. The Hebrew ''infinitives, imperatives'', and ''imperfects'' in {{GHGheb|text=־ֵה}}, less frequently {{GHGheb|text=־ֵא}} or {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}}, may be due to imitation of these forms. On the ''infinitive construct Piʿēl'' {{GHGheb|text=חַכֵּי}}, see above, aa; {{GHGterm|imperative Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=הֱוֵא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=37|verse=6}} (in the sense of ''fall''); {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יֵרֵא|translate=let him look out}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=33}} (but see above, p); {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעֲשֵׂה|translate=he will do}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=64|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תִּֽהְיֵה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תֹּבֵא|translate=consent thou not}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תַּֽעֲשֵׂה|translate=do thou not}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=12}} (the same form in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=7|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=40|verse=16}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}); {{GHGheb|text=אֶֽהְיֵה}} (so Baer and Ginsburg, after cod. Hillel, &c.) ''I will be'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַנַּֽעֲשֵׂה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=9|verse=24}}; {{GHGheb|text=תִּרְאֵה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=1|verse=13}}. Cf. also in {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=יִמָּצֵה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=תִּבָּנֵה}} (according to Qimḥi) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=27}}; in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=תְּגַלֵּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=18|verse=7.8.12–17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=20|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, in each case {{GHGheb|text=לֹא תְגַלֵּה֑}}, beside {{GHGheb|text=תְּגַלֶּה}} with a minor distinctive; {{GHGheb|text=יֲנַקֵּ֑ה}} (Baer {{GHGheb|text=יְנַפֶּה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=1|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֱזָרֵה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=5|verse=12}} (with {{GHGterm|Zaqeph}}; Baer {{GHGheb|text=אֱזָרֶה}}). The fact, however, that a great number of these forms occur in {{GHGterm|pause}} and represent at the same time a {{GHGterm|jussive}} or ''voluntative'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=7|verse=9}}), suggests the view that the {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} is used merely to increase the emphasis of the pausal form, and at the same time to make a distinction in sound between the {{GHGterm|jussive}} or ''voluntative'' and the ordinary {{GHGterm|imperfect}}.<ref>Possibly these examples (like the eases of {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} in {{GHGterm|pause}}, see n) represent the view of a particular Masoretic school, which was intended to be consistently carried out.</ref> Elsewhere ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=40|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=1|verse=13}}; according to Baer also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=9|verse=5}}) the pronunciation with ''ê'' is probably intended to soften the hiatus caused by a following {{GHGheb|text=א}} or {{GHGheb|text=ע}}; cf. the analogous cases above, {{GHGpar|74|l}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|ii}}
The ending {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} appears to stand for {{GHGheb|text=־ֶה}} in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} in {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּזְנִי־שָׁם|translate=and there hath she played the harlot}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=6}}; perhaps, however, the 2nd ''sing. fem.'' is intended, or it may have been introduced into the text of Jeremiah from {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=15}}, &c. Still more strange is it in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תֶּ֑מְחִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=18|verse=23}}; but the ''Mil‛ēl''-tone probably points to {{GHGheb|text=תֶּ֫מַח}} as the correct reading (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=13|verse=14}}). The {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} stands for {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} in the {{GHGterm|perfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽחֱלִי|translate=he made sick}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=53|verse=10}}, which is probably for {{GHGheb|text=החליא}} from {{GHGheb|text=חלא}}, a secondary form of {{GHGheb|text=חלה}}; see rr. The ''plur''. {{GHGheb|text=הִמְסִיו}} (Baer {{GHGheb|text=הִמְסִיוְ}}) ''they made to melt'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=14|verse=8}}, is a purely Aramaic form.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|kk}}
18. In two verbs the rare conjugation ''Pa‛lēl'' or its reflexive ({{GHGpar|55|d}}) occurs: {{GHGheb|text=מְטַֽחֲוֵי|translate=archers}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=16}} (from {{GHGheb|text=טָחָה}}); but most frequently in {{GHGheb|text=שָׁחָה|translate=to bend}}, ''Pa‛lēl'' {{GHGheb|text=שַֽׁחֲוָה}} not in use, whence reflexive {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁתַּֽחֲוָה|translate=to bow oneself, to prostrate oneself}}, 2nd ''pers.'' in {{GHGheb|text=־ִ֫ יתָ}} and 1st ''pers.'' in {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ יתִי}}, {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁתַּֽחֲוֶה}}, {{GHGterm|consecutive}} 3rd ''sing. masc.'' {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּשְׁתַּ֫חוּ}} for ''wayyištaḥw'' (analogous to the noun-forms, like {{GHGheb|text=שָׂ֫חוּ}} for ''saḥw''); 3rd ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁתַּֽחֲווּ}}.—Instead of the aramaizing {{GHGterm|infinitive}} with ''suffix'' {{GHGheb|text=בְּהִשְׁתַּֽחֲיָיָֽתִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=18}} read with König {{GHGheb|text=בְּהִשְׁתַּֽחֲווֹתִי}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=8|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁתַּֽחֲוִיתֶם}} is still more certainly a scribal error for {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁתַּֽחֲוִים}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|ll}}
19. Before ''suffixes'' in all forms ending in {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, a connecting vowel is employed instead of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} and the connecting vowel which precedes it ({{GHGpar|58|f}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נָחַ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=27}}; in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=עָנָ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=30}}, &c., even with lesser disjunctives, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=22}}, or with a conjunctive accent, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=15}} (but Baer {{GHGheb|text=עָנַ֫נִי}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=19}}; cf. {{GHGpar|59|h}}; {{GHGheb|text=עָֽנְךָ֫}}, in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=עָנָךְ}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=19}} (and even when not in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=37}}) or like {{GHGheb|text=קָנֶ֫ךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=וְיַרְבֶּ֑ךָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְיַפְרְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=28|verse=3}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=עָנָ֫הוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָנָם}}, {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעֲנֵ֫הוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעַנְךָ֫|translate=Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִכַּ֫נִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָֽעֶלְךָ֫}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִכֶּ֫הוּ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|mm}}
Only very seldom does the ''imperat.'' or {{GHGterm|impf.}} end in {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}} before suffixes, e.g.<section end="par75" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

240.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par75 />{{GHGheb|text=אַפְאֵיהֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=26}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְכַסֵּ֫ימוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=140|verse=10}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַכֵּ֫ינִי|translate=smite me}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=35.37}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=3|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=38|verse=16}}. Even in these examples a return to the original ending ''ay'' might be assumed; but perhaps they are merely due to a less correct {{GHGterm|plene}} writing. In the 3rd ''sing. perf. fem.'' the older form {{GHGheb|text=גָּלַת}} (see i) is always used before a ''suffix'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כִּלַּ֫תּוּ}} (for {{GHGheb|text=כִּלַּתְהוּ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=5|verse=4}}; in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=עָשָׂ֑תְנִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=33|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=רָאָֽתְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=42|verse=5|hidebook=1}}.

{{center|VI. ''The Relation between Verbs'' {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה|translate=and}} {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}}}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|nn}}
20. The close relation existing between verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}} and {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} is shown in Hebrew by the fact that the verbs of one class often borrow forms from the other, especially in the later writers and the poets.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|oo}}
21. Thus there are forms of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}}—
