Moreover, the numerous abstracts of this form (e.g. even {{GHGheb|text=קְצָפָה|translate=a splintering}}, {{GHGheb|text=צְוָחָה|translate=a crying}}, &c.) are undoubtedly to be regarded (with Barth, {{GHGcite|title=Nominalbildung}}, p. 87) as feminines of infinitives of the form {{GHGpron|qăṭâl}}, the lengthening of the second syllable being balanced, as in other cases, by the addition of the feminine termination.</ref> {{GHGtranslate|righteousness}}; with an initial guttural {{GHGheb|text=אֲדָמָה|translate=earth}}.—Of the same formation from verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} are {{GHGheb|text=בָּדָד|translate=alone}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָנָן|translate=cloud}}; passive {{GHGheb|text=חָלָל|translate=pierced}}.—In verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} a final {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} is almost always rejected, and the ''ă'' of the second syllable lengthened to ''è''. Thus {{GHGheb|text=שָׂדַי|translate=field}}, after rejection of the {{GHGheb|text=י}} and addition of {{GHGheb|text=ה}} as a vowel-letter, becomes {{GHGheb|text=שָׂדֶה}} (cf. {{GHGpar|93}}, Paradigm II, {{GHGpar|93|f|nonumber=1}}); fem. e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנָה|translate=year}}; cf. {{GHGpar|95}}, Paradigm II, {{GHGpar|95|c|nonumber=1}}. From a verb {{GHGheb|text=ל״ו}} the strong form {{GHGheb|text=עָנָו|translate=afflicted}} occurs.

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|g|a}}
4. The ground-form {{GHGpron|qăṭĭl}}, fem. {{GHGpron|qăṭĭlăt}}, developed to {{GHGheb|text=קָטֵל}} (§ 93, Paradigm II, ''c–e'') and {{GHGheb|text=קְטֵלָה}}, is frequently used as participle of verbs middle ''e'' ({{GHGpar|50|b}}), and hence mostly with an intransitive meaning; cf. {{GHGheb|text=זָקִן|translate=old, an old man}}; {{GHGheb|text=כָּבֵד|translate=heavy}}; fem. {{GHGheb|text=בְּהֵמָה|translate=cattle}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲפֵלָה}} and {{GHGheb|text=חֲשֵׁכָה|translate=darkness}}.—From verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}}: irregularly, {{GHGheb|text=דָּֽלִיּוֹתָיו|translate=the branches of it}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=11|verse=16}}, &c., generally referred to a ''sing''. {{GHGheb|text=דָּלִית}} (stem {{GHGheb|text=דלה}}), and {{GHGheb|text=הָֽרִיּוֹתָיו}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=14|verse=1|translate=their women with child}} (from {{GHGheb|text=הָרָה}}, {{GHGterm|st. constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=הֲרַת}}, {{GHGterm|plur. st. absol.}} and {{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=הָרוֹת}}).—From a verb {{GHGheb|text=ל״ו}} with consonantal Wāw: {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלֵו|translate=at ease}}, incorrectly written {{GHGterm|plene}} {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלֵיו}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=23}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|h|a}}
5. The ground-form {{GHGpron|qăṭŭl}}, developed to {{GHGheb|text=קָטֹל}} (also written {{GHGheb|text=קָטוֹל}}), generally forms adjectives, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אָיֹם|translate=terrible}}, {{GHGheb|text=בָּרֹד|translate=piebald}}, {{GHGheb|text=מָתוֹק|translate=sweet}}, {{GHGheb|text=נָקֹד|translate=speckled}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָבֹת|translate=interwoven}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָגֹל|translate=round}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָמֹק|translate=deep}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָקֹב|translate=hilly}}, {{GHGheb|text=צָהֹב|translate=golden}}; {{GHGheb|text=קָטֹן|translate=small}}, only in sing. masc., with a parallel form {{GHGheb|text=קָטָן}} of the class treated under ''f'', fem. {{GHGheb|text=קְטַנָּה}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=קְטַנִּים}}. These forms are not to be confounded with those in No. III, from<section end=par84a/><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

255.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par84a/>the ground-form {{GHGpron|qăṭâl.}}—Fem. {{GHGheb|text=אֲיֻמָּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=כְּבוּדָּה}} ({{GHGtranslate|glorious}}), {{GHGheb|text=עֲבֻתָּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֲנֻגָּה}} ({{GHGtranslate|delicate}}), {{GHGheb|text=עֲגֻלָּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֲמֻקָּה}}, with sharpening of the third radical, in order to keep the original ''ŭ'' short, and similarly in the plurals {{GHGheb|text=בְּרֻדִּים}}, {{GHGheb|text=נְקֻדִּים}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֲגֻלִּים}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲסֻפִּים|translate=stores}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|i|a}}
6. The ground-form {{GHGpron|qĭṭâl}} develops to {{GHGheb|text=קֵטָל}} (cf. {{GHGpar|93}}, Paradigm II, Rem. 1), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לֵבָב|translate=heart}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֵנָב|translate=a bunch of grapes}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁבָר|translate=strong drink}}; from a verb {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, probably of this class is {{GHGheb|text=רֵעֶה}}, generally contracted to {{GHGheb|text=רֵע|translate=friend}}, ground-form {{GHGpron|riʿay}}: the full form is preserved in {{GHGheb|text=רֵעֵ֫הוּ|translate=his friend}}, for {{GHGheb|text=רֵעֵ֫יהוּ}}.

{{center|III. ''Nouns with an original Short Vowel in the First and a Long Vowel in the Second Syllable.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|k|a}}
7. The ground-form {{GHGpron|qăṭâl}} in Hebrew always develops to the form {{GHGheb|text=קָטוֹל}}, the ''â'' becoming an obscure ''ô''. The fact that this form is also written {{GHGheb|text=קָטֹל}} must not lead to the confusion of these forms with those mentioned in No. 5, from the ground-form {{GHGpron|qăṭâl}}.<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=1|verse=3}} only the {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} requires {{GHGheb|text=גְּדָל־}} (in the constr. state) for the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} {{GHGheb|text=גְּדוֹל}}.</ref> Moreover the {{GHGpron|qaṭôl}}-class includes forms of various origin, and therefore of various meaning, as (''a'') intransitive adjectives like {{GHGheb|text=גָּדוֹל|translate=great}}, {{GHGheb|text=קָדוֹשׁ|translate=holy}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=גְּדוֹלָה}}, the short vowel becoming Š<sup>e</sup>wâ, whereas in {{GHGheb|text=גָּדוֹל}}, &c., ''before the tone'' it is lengthened to ''ā''; (''b'') the {{GHGterm|infinitives absolute}} of the form {{GHGheb|text=קָטוֹל}} ({{GHGpar|45|a}}) as representing the abstract idea of the verb, and abstract substantives like {{GHGheb|text=כָּבוֹד|translate=honour}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלוֹם|translate=peace}} (Arab. {{GHGpron|sălâm}}); (''c'') substantives and adjectives in an active sense, as {{GHGheb|text=בָּחוֹן|translate=assayer}} (of metals,) {{GHGheb|text=עָשׁוֹק|translate=an oppressor}}, {{GHGheb|text=חָמוֹץ|translate=oppressing}}; in the feminine {{GHGheb|text=בָּֽגוֹדָה|translate=treacherous}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=7.10}}, the irregular retention of the ''ā'' in the third syllable from the end is no doubt to be explained, with Brockelmann, from Aramaic influence, the punctuator having in mind the Aramaic nomen agentis {{GHGpron|qâṭôl}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|l|a}}
8. The ground-form {{GHGpron|qăṭîl}} develops to {{GHGheb|text=קָטִיל}} (cf. {{GHGpar|93}}, Paradigm IV, {{GHGpar|93|a|nonumber=1}} and {{GHGpar|93|b|nonumber=1}}). Here also forms of various origin and meaning are to be distinguished: (''a'') adjectives used substantivally with a passive meaning to denote duration in a state, as {{GHGheb|text=אָסִיר|translate=a prisoner}}, {{GHGheb|text=מָשִׁיחַ|translate=an anointed one}}. These proper {{GHGpron|qăṭîl}}-forms are parallel to the purely passive {{GHGpron|qaṭûl}}-forms (see m), but others are due to a strengthening of original {{GHGpron|qaṭĭl}}-forms. These are either (''b'') intransitive in meaning, as {{GHGheb|text=צָעִיר|translate=small}}, and, from {{GHGheb|text=ל״י}} stems, {{GHGheb|text=נָקִי|translate=pure}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָנִי|translate=poor}} (see {{GHGpar|93|vv}}), or (''c'') active, as {{GHGheb|text=נָבִיא|translate=a speaker}} (prophet), {{GHGheb|text=פָּקִיד|translate=an overseer}}.—Of a different kind again (according to Do Lagarde, infinitives) are (''d'') forms like {{GHGheb|text=אָסִיף|translate=the ingathering}}, {{GHGheb|text=בָּצִיר|translate=vintage}}, {{GHGheb|text=חָרִישׁ|translate=ploughing time}}, {{GHGheb|text=קָצִיר|translate=harvest}}. On {{GHGpron|qăṭṭîl}} forms with a kindred meaning, cf. {{GHGpar|84|f|b}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|m|a}}
9. The ground-form {{GHGpron|qăṭûl}} develops to {{GHGheb|text=קָטוּל}}. As in the {{GHGpron|qaṭâl}} and {{GHGpron|qaṭîl}}-forms (see k and l), so here forms of various kinds are to be distinguished: (''a'') {{GHGpron|qaṭûl}}-forms proper, with passive meaning, especially all the passive participles of Qal; fem. e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בְּתוּלָה|translate=virgin}} (properly {{GHGtranslate|secluded}}). On the other hand, by strengthening an original {{GHGpron|qaṭŭl}}-form we get (''b'') certain stative adjectives ({{GHGpar|50|f}}), as {{GHGheb|text=אָנוּשׁ|translate=incurable}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָצוּם|translate=strong}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָרוּם|translate=subtil}}, or even transitive, as {{GHGheb|text=אָחוּז|translate=holding}}; (''c'') active substantives, as {{GHGheb|text=יָקוּשׁ|translate=a fowler}}. Further, some of the forms mentioned in {{GHGpar|84|g|b}} belong to this class; see above, the remark on l.

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|n|a}}
10. The ground-form {{GHGpron|qĭṭâl}} or {{GHGpron|qŭṭâl}}<ref>On the {{GHGpron|fuʿâl}}-forms (regarded by Wellhausen as original diminutives) see Nöldeke, {{GHGcite|title=Beiträge}} (Strassb. 1904), p. 30 ff. He includes among them {{GHGheb|text=נְעֹ֫רֶת|translate=tow}}, and {{GHGheb|text=טְחֹרִים|translate=hemorrhoids}}.</ref> in Hebrew changes the ''ĭ'' to vocal {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}},<section end=par84a/><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

256.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" />{{GHGcorrected}}</noinclude><section begin="par84a" />and develops to {{GHGheb|text=קְטָל}} (cf. {{GHGpar|93}}, Paradigm IV, {{GHGpar|93|c|nonumber=1}}) or {{GHGheb|text=קְטוֹל}}, with ''â'' obscured to ''ô'' (as above, {{GHGpar|84|k|a}}). Cf. {{GHGheb|text=שְׁאָר|translate=remnant}}, {{GHGheb|text=יְקָר|translate=honour}}, {{GHGheb|text=כְּתָב|translate=book}} (Arab. {{GHGpron|kĭtâb}}), {{GHGheb|text=קְרָב|translate=war}} (the last three probably loan-words from the Aramaic); of the other form, {{GHGheb|text=חֲלוֹם|translate=a dream}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֲמוֹר|translate=an ass}} (Arab. {{GHGpron|ḥĭmâr}}), {{GHGheb|text=אֱלוֹהַּ|translate=God}} (Arab. {{GHGpron|ʾĭlâh}}); with {{GHGheb|text=א|translate=prosthetic}} ({{GHGpar|19|m}}), {{GHGheb|text=אֶזְרוֹעַ|translate=arm}} (twice: usually {{GHGheb|text=זְרוֹעַ}}); fem. {{GHGheb|text=בְּשׂוֹרָה|translate=good news}} (Arab. {{GHGpron|bĭšârăt}}); {{GHGheb|text=עֲבוֹדָה|translate=service}}, {{GHGheb|text=כְּתֹ֫בֶת}} (Arab. {{GHGpron|kĭtâbăt}}) {{GHGtranslate|tattooing}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|o|a}}
11. The ground-form {{GHGpron|qĭṭîl}} seems to occur e.g. in Hebrew {{GHGheb|text=אֱוִיל|translate=foolish}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֱלִיל|translate=vanity}}, {{GHGheb|text=בְּדִיל|translate=lead}}, {{GHGheb|text=כְּסִיל|translate=a fool}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֲזִיר|translate=a swine}} (the prop. name {{GHGheb|text=חֵזִיר}} points to the ground-form {{GHGpron|qĭṭîl}}, cf. Arab. {{GHGpron|ḥĭnzîr}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|p|a}}
12. The ground-form {{GHGpron|qĭṭûl}} or {{GHGpron|qŭṭûl}}, Hebr. {{GHGheb|text=קְטוּל}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גְּבוּל|translate=a boundary}}, {{GHGheb|text=לְבוּשׁ|translate=a garment}}; fem. {{GHGheb|text=גְּבוּרָה|translate=strength}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֱמוּנָה|translate=faithfulness}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|q|a}}
Rem. When the forms {{GHGpron|q<sup>e</sup>ṭûl}} and {{GHGpron|q<sup>e</sup>ṭôl}} begin with {{GHGheb|text=א}}, they almost invariably take in the singular a {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} under the {{GHGheb|text=א}} instead of the ordinary {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=אֵבוּס|translate=a crib}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֵטוּן|translate=thread}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֵמוּן|translate=faithful}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֵזוֹב|translate=hyssop}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֵזוֹר|translate=a waist-band}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֵסוּר|translate=a bond}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֵפוֹד|translate=an ephod}}; cf. {{GHGpar|23|h}}, and the analogous cases of {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} for {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} in verbal forms {{GHGpar|52|n}}, {{GHGpar|63|p}}, {{GHGpar|76|d}}.

{{center|IV. ''Nouns with a Long Vocal in the First Syllable and originally a Short Vowel in the Second Syllable.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|r|a}}
13. The ground-form {{GHGpron|qâṭăl}}, in Hebrew, always changes the ''â'' into an obscure ''ô'', {{GHGheb|text=קוֹטָל}} ({{GHGheb|text=קֹטָל}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עוֹלָם}} ({{GHGpar|93}}, Paradigm III, {{GHGpar|93|a|nonumber=1}}), Arab. {{GHGpron|ʿâlăm}}, {{GHGtranslate|eternity}}; {{GHGheb|text=חוֹתָם}} (Arab. {{GHGpron|ḥâtăm}}) {{GHGtranslate|a seal}} (according to Barth a loan-word of Egyptian origin), fem. {{GHGheb|text=חֹתֶ֫מֶת}} (from {{GHGpron|ḥôtămt}}); {{GHGheb|text=תּוֹלָע|translate=worm}} (unless from a stem {{GHGheb|text=ולע}}, like {{GHGheb|text=תּוֹשָׁב}} from {{GHGheb|text=ושב}}; see the analogous cases in {{GHGpar|85|b}}). On the participles {{GHGterm|Qal}} of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} ({{GHGpar|93}}, Paradigm III, {{GHGpar|93|c|nonumber=1}}), cf. {{GHGpar|75|e}}; on the feminines of the participles {{GHGterm|Qal}}, which are formed with the termination {{GHGheb|text=ת}}, see below, s.

Rem. Of a different kind (probably from a ground-form {{GHGpron|qauṭal}}) are such forms as {{GHGheb|text=אוֹפָן}} (or {{GHGheb|text=אוֹפָן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=10|verse=9}} in the same verse) {{GHGtranslate|a wheel}}; {{GHGheb|text=גּוֹזָל|translate=a young bird}}, {{GHGheb|text=דּוֹנַג|translate=wax}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|s|a}}
14. The ground-form {{GHGpron|qâṭĭl}} also becomes in Hebrew almost invariably {{GHGheb|text=קוֹטֵל}} ({{GHGheb|text=קֹטֵל}}). Besides ''participles active masc. Qal'' this class includes also feminines of the form {{GHGheb|text=קֹטֶ֫לֶת}}, if their ground-form {{GHGpron|qôṭalt}} ({{GHGpar|69|c}}) goes back to an original {{GHGpron|qâṭilt}}. The substantives of this form, such as {{GHGheb|text=כֹּהֵן|translate=priest}} (Arab. {{GHGpron|kâhĭn}}), were also originally participles {{GHGterm|Qal}}. The fem. of the substantives has ''ē'' (lengthened from ''ĭ'') retained before the tone, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יֹֽלֵדה|translate=a woman in travail}} (cf. also {{GHGheb|text=בֹּֽגֵדָה|translate=the treacherous woman}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַצֹּֽלֵעָה|translate=her that halteth}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=4|verse=6}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=3|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=סֹֽחֵרָה|translate=a buckler}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=91|verse=4}}); the participles as a rule have the form {{GHGheb|text=יֹֽלְדָה}}, &c., the original ''ĭ'' having become {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}; however, the form with {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} occurs also in the latter, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=6.8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=34|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=16|hidebook=1}} (all in principal {{GHGterm|pause}}; in subordinate {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=14}}; with a conjunctive accent, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=6}}). {{:Gesenius' Hebrew Grammar/Additions and Corrections/232}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|t|a}}
15. The ground-form {{GHGpron|qûṭăl}}, Hebrew {{GHGheb|text=קוּטַל}} (as {{GHGheb|text=יוּבַל|translate=river}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=8}}) or {{GHGheb|text=קוּטָל}} e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עוּגָב|translate=a pipe}}, commonly {{GHGheb|text=עֻגָב}}, and to be so read, with Baer, also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=150|verse=4}}, not {{GHGheb|text=עֻגָּב}}.

{{center|V. ''Nouns with a Long Vowel in each Syllable''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|u|a}}
16. {{GHGheb|text=קִיטוֹל}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קִיטוֹר|translate=smoke}}. The few forms of this kind are probably derived from the ground-form {{GHGpron|qîṭâl}} ({{GHGpron|qĭṭṭâl}} ?), i.e. the original ''â'' has become an obscure ''ô''.<section end="par84a" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

257.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par84b />{{GHGpar-heading|84|Formation of Nouns from the Intensive Stem|b}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|a|b}}
This includes all forms which have arisen, either through the doubling of the middle radical, or the repetition of one or of two consonants of the simple stem.

{{center|VI. ''Nouns with the Middle Consonant sharpened.''}}

As in the corresponding verbal stems (cf. {{GHGpar|52|f}}), so also in some noun-formations of this class, the Dageš in the second radical expresses an intensification of the idea of the stem, either emphasizing the energy of the action or relation, or else indicating a longer continuance of the relation or state. Other nouns of this character are evidently only by-forms of the nouns derived from the simple stem, which were treated in the last section: cf. the instances adduced under {{GHGpar|84|f|b|nonumber=1}} and {{GHGpar|84|g|b|nonumber=1}}, and Barth, {{GHGcite|title=Nominalbildung}}, Introd., p. x.

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|b|b}}
17. The ground-form ''qăṭṭăl'' is mostly lengthened in Hebrew to {{GHGheb|text=קַטָּל}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=אַיָּל|translate=a stag}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=אַיָּלָה}}, ''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=אַיֶּ֫לֶת}} (from ''ʾăyyălt''); cf. also the fem. (originating from {{GHGterm|Qal}}) {{GHGheb|text=לֶֽהָבָה|translate=a flame}} (according to {{GHGpar|27|q}} for ''lăhhābhā''), {{GHGheb|text=חָֽרָבָה|translate=dry land}} (for ''ḥarrābhā''), {{GHGheb|text=דַּלֶּ֫קֶת}} and {{GHGheb|text=קַדַּ֫חַת|translate=a burning fever}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַבָּשָׁה}} and {{GHGheb|text=יַבֶּ֫שֶׁת|translate=dry land}}, {{GHGheb|text=טַבַּ֫עַת|translate=a seal-ring}}, {{GHGheb|text=שַׁחֶ֫פֶת|translate=consumption}}. Adjectives of this class (‘intensified participles of the active verb’, Barth, ''ibid.'', § 33) are {{GHGheb|text=חַטָּא|translate=sinful}}, {{GHGheb|text=נַגָּח|translate=wont to gore}}, {{GHGheb|text=קַנָּא|translate=jealous}}, {{GHGheb|text=כֶּחָשׁ}} (for ''kaḥḥâš'', by {{GHGpar|22|c}}) ''lying''. {{GHGterm|Nomina opificum}} also, curiously enough, are so treated in Hebrew (at least in the {{GHGterm|constr. state}} of the sing.), although the corresponding Arabic form ''qăttâl'' points to an original (unchangeable) ''â'' in the second syllable; cf. {{GHGheb|text=גַּנָּב|translate=a thief}}, {{GHGheb|text=דַּיָּן|translate=a judge}} (''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=דַּיַּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=6}}), {{GHGheb|text=טַבָּח|translate=a cook}}, {{GHGheb|text=חָרָשׁ}} (for ''ḥarrâš'') ''artificer'' (''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=חָרַשׁ}}, but ''plur. constr.'' {{GHGheb|text=חָֽרָשֵׁי}}); {{GHGheb|text=פָּרָשׁ|translate=horseman}} (for ''parrâš''), ''const. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=פָּרַשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=10}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|c|b}}
18. The ground-form ''qĭṭṭăl'' appears in {{GHGheb|text=צִחֶה|translate=dry}}, {{GHGheb|text=גֵּאֶה|translate=haughty}} (the ''ĭ'' being lengthened to ''ē'' according to {{GHGpar|22|c}}), if these forms go back to original ''ṣĭḥḥăy, gĭʾʾăy''. On the analogy, however, of the adjectives denoting defects (see d below), we should rather expect a ground-form ''qĭṭṭĭl''; moreover, ''ʾiwwalt'', ground-form of the fem. {{GHGheb|text=אִוֶּ֫לֶת|translate=foolishness}}, goes back to an original ''iwwilt'', see {{GHGpar|69|c}}.

19. The ground-form ''qŭṭṭăl'' and ''qŭṭṭŭl''; cf. the fem. {{GHGheb|text=כֻּסֶּ֫מֶת|translate=spelt}}, {{GHGheb|text=כֻּתֹּ֫נֶת|translate=coat}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|d|b}}
20. The ground-form ''qăṭṭĭl''; from the intensive stem, the infinitives {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} of the form {{GHGheb|text=קַטֵּל}}.

21. The ground-form ''qĭṭṭĭl'', in Hebrew lengthened to {{GHGheb|text=קִטֵּל}}. Of this form are a considerable number of adjectives which denote a bodily or mental fault or defect. Cf. {{GHGheb|text=אִטֵּר|translate=disabled}}, {{GHGheb|text=אִלֵּם|translate=dumb}}, {{GHGheb|text=גִּבֵּן|translate=hump-backed}}, {{GHGheb|text=עִוֵּר|translate=blind}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֵרֵשׁ|translate=deaf}} (for ''ḥirrēš''), {{GHGheb|text=פִּסֵּחַ|translate=lame}}, {{GHGheb|text=קֵרֵחַ|translate=bald}}, {{GHGheb|text=עִקֵּשׁ|translate=perverse}}; {{GHGheb|text=פִּקֵּחַ|translate=open-eyed}} follows the same analogy.

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|e|b}}
22. The ground-form ''qăṭṭâl'', cf. the remarks in b above, on the {{GHGterm|nomina opificum}}; moreover, to this class belong infinitives {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} of the Aramaic form {{GHGheb|text=בַּקָּרָה|translate=a searching out}}; {{GHGheb|text=בַּקָּשָׁה|translate=a request}}; with middle guttural (see {{GHGpar|22|c}}) {{GHGheb|text=נֶֽאָצָה|translate=contumely}}; but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=נָאָֽצוֹתֶ֫יךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=35|verse=12}}, with full lengthening of the original ''ă'' before {{GHGheb|text=א}}; {{GHGheb|text=נֶֽחָמָה|translate=comfort}}. From the attenuation of the ''ă'' of this form to ''ĭ'', arises undoubtedly:

23. The ground-form ''qĭṭṭâl'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אִכָּר|translate=husbandman}} (Arab. ''ʾăkkâr'').

24. The ground-form ''qĭṭṭôl'', most probably only a variety of the form ''qăṭṭâl'' with the ''ă'' attenuated to ''ĭ'' (as in No. 23), and the ''â'' obscured to ''ô'' (as in {{GHGpar|84|n|b|nonumber=1}} and<section end=par84b /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

258.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par84b" />{{GHGpar|84|r|b|nonumber=1}}); cf. {{GHGheb|text=גִּבּוֹר|translate=hero}} (Arab. ''găbbâr''), {{GHGheb|text=יִסּוֹר|translate=caviller}}, {{GHGheb|text=צִפּוֹר}} (''piper'' or ''chirper'') ''a bird'', {{GHGheb|text=שִׁכּוֹר|translate=drunkard}}. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=יִלּוֹד|translate=born}} probably arises from ''yullôd'', an old {{GHGterm|participle passive}} of {{GHGterm|Qal}}, the ''ŭ'' being dissimilated in the sharpened syllable before ''ô'': so Barth, ''ibid.'', p. 41 f.

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|f|b}}
25. The ground-form ''qăṭṭîl'', {{GHGheb|text=קַטִּיל}}, almost exclusively of persons, who possess some quality in an intensive manner, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אַבִּיר|translate=strong}}, {{GHGheb|text=צַדִּיק|translate=righteous}}, {{GHGheb|text=בָּרִיחַ|translate=fugitive}} (for ''barrî<sup>a</sup>ḥ''), {{GHGheb|text=עָרִיץ|translate=violent}} (for ''ʿărrîṣ'').

That some of these are only by-forms of the ''qăṭîl''-class (see above, remark on {{GHGpar|84|a|b|nonumber=1}}), appears from the ''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=פְּרִיץ|translate=ravenous}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=35|verse=9}} (but {{GHGheb|text=פָּֽרִיצִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=פָּֽרִיצֵי}} always), and according to Barth (''ibid.'', 35 ''a'') also from the ''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=אֲבִיר}} (but also {{GHGheb|text=אַבִּיר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=8}}) of {{GHGheb|text=אַבִּיר}}. However, the form {{GHGheb|text=אֲבִיר}}, as a name of God, may be intentionally differentiated from {{GHGheb|text=אַבִּיר}}, a poetic term for the bull.

In the same way {{GHGheb|text=אַסִּיר|translate=prisoner}}, {{GHGheb|text=סָרִיס|translate=eunuch}} (''constr. st.'' always {{GHGheb|text=סְרִיס}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=סָֽרִיסִים}}, ''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=סְרִיסֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=7}}, but in the book of Esther always {{GHGheb|text=סָֽרִיסֵי}}, with ''suffix'' {{GHGheb|text=סָֽרִיסָיו}}, &c.), and {{GHGheb|text=עַתִּיק|translate=weaned}}, may be regarded as by-forms of the ''qăṭîl''-class with passive meaning, see {{GHGpar|84|l|a}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|g|b}}
26. The ground-form ''qăṭṭûl'', {{GHGheb|text=קַטּוּל}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חַנּוּן|translate=gracious}}, {{GHGheb|text=רַחוּם|translate=compassionate}} (with virtual strengthening of the {{GHGheb|text=ח}}), {{GHGheb|text=חָרוּץ|translate=diligent}} (for ''ḥarrûṣ''), probably, again, to a large extent by-forms of the ''qăṭûl''-class, {{GHGpar|84|m|a}}. The same applies to substantives like {{GHGheb|text=אַשֻּׁר|translate=a step}} (in {{GHGheb|text=אַשֻּׁרִי}}, as well as {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֻׁרוֹ}}, &c.), {{GHGheb|text=עַמּוּד|translate=pillar}}; fem. {{GHGheb|text=חַבּוּרָה|translate=a stripe}} (''also'' {{GHGheb|text=חֲבֻֽרָתוֹ}}), {{GHGheb|text=בַּטֻּחוֹת|translate=security}}: cf. Barth, ''ibid.'', § 84.

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|h|b}}
27. The ground-form ''qăṭṭôl''; besides the infinitives absolute {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} of the form {{GHGheb|text=קַטֹּל}}, also {{GHGheb|text=קַנּוֹא|translate=jealous}} (as well as {{GHGheb|text=קַנָּא}}, an obscured form of ''qăṭṭâl'', see {{GHGpar|84|e|b|nonumber=1}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|i|b}}
28. The ground-form ''qĭṭṭûl'', {{GHGheb|text=קִטּוּל}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=צִפּוּי|translate=a coating of metal}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁלּוּם|translate=requital}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁקּוּי|translate=drink}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁקּוּץ|translate=detestable thing}}; with concrete meaning {{GHGheb|text=לִמּוּד|translate=a disciple}}, {{GHGheb|text=עִזּוּז|translate=strong}}; frequently in the plural in an abstract sense, as {{GHGheb|text=גִּדּוּפִים|translate=reproach}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִלֻּאִים|translate=filling}} (the induction of a priest), {{GHGheb|text=נִֽחֻמִים|translate=consolations, compassion}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁכֻּלִים|translate=bereavement}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁלֻּחִים|translate=dismissal}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁמֻּרִים|translate=observance}}.

{{center|VII. ''Nouns with the Third Consonant repeated.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|k|b}}
29. The ground-form ''qăṭḷăl'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שַֽׁאֲנָן|translate=quiet}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=שַֽׁאֲנַנָּה}} (with sharpening of the second ''Nûn'', in order to keep the preceding vowel short); {{GHGheb|text=רַֽעֲנָן|translate=green}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=רַעֲנַנִּים}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|l|b}}
30. The ground-form ''qăṭlĭl'', in Hebrew {{GHGheb|text=קַטְלֵל}}; of this form are e.g. the infinitives ''Pi‛lēl'' (prop. ''Pa‛lēl''), cf. {{GHGpar|55|d}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|m|b}}
31. The ground-form ''qăṭlŭl''; so the plur. {{GHGheb|text=גַּבְנֻנִּים|translate=ridges}} (with sharpening of the ''Nûn'', as in No. 29).

32. The ground-form ''qĭṭlăl'', in {{GHGheb|text=פִּרְחָח|translate=a brood}}.

33. The ground-form ''qŭṭlăl'', in {{GHGheb|text=אֻמְלָל|translate=faint}}.

34. The ground-form ''qăṭlîl'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עַבְטִיט|translate=plunder}}, {{GHGheb|text=סַגְרִיר|translate=rain-storm}}, {{GHGheb|text=שַׁפְרִיר|translate=glittering tapestry}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=43|verse=10}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}; with attenuation of the ''ă'' to ''i'' {{GHGheb|text=כִּמְרִירִים|translate=all that maketh black}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=5}} (but the better reading is {{GHGheb|text=כַּמְרִירֵי}}).

35. The ground-form ''qăṭlûl'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שַׁפְרוּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=43|verse=10}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}; {{GHGheb|text=נַֽאֲפוּפִים|translate=adulteries}}.

{{center|VIII. ''Nouns with the Second and Third Consonants repeated.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|n|b}}
36–39. ''Q<sup>e</sup>ṭălṭăl, q<sup>e</sup>ṭălṭĭl, q<sup>e</sup>ṭălṭŭl; q<sup>e</sup>ṭălṭûl, q<sup>e</sup>ṭălṭôl'' (in {{GHGterm|fem.}} and ''plur.'' often with the last consonant sharpened for the reason given in ''a'' above); cf. {{GHGheb|text=הֲפַכְפַּךְ}}<section end="par84b" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

259.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par84b" />''crooked'', {{GHGheb|text=חֲלַקְלַקּוֹת|translate=slippery places}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֲקַלְקַלּוֹת|translate=crooked}} ({{GHGtranslate|ways}}); {{GHGheb|text=פְּתַלְתֹּל|translate=tortuous}}; also words denoting colours, {{GHGheb|text=אֲדַמְדָּם}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=13|verse=42.49}} in pause) ''reddish'', fem. {{GHGheb|text=אֲדַמְדֶּ֫מֶת}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=אֲדַמְדַּמֹּת}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְרַקְרַק|translate=greenish}}, plur. fem. {{GHGheb|text=יְרַקְרַקֹּת}}; ''q<sup>e</sup>ṭalṭĭl'', {{GHGheb|text=יְפֵיפִיָּה|translate=very fair}} (to be read in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=46|verse=20}} for {{GHGheb|text=יפהפיה}}); ''q<sup>e</sup>ṭalṭŭl'', {{GHGheb|text=שְׁחַרְחֹ֫רֶת}} (fem.) ''blackish''; {{GHGheb|text=אֲסַפְסֻף|translate=a rabble}} (augmented from {{GHGheb|text=אָסוּף|translate=collected}}). From a verb {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}} with aphaeresis of the initial syllable {{GHGheb|text=צֶֽאֱצָאִים|translate=offspring}}. Moreover, of the same form, probably, is {{GHGheb|text=חֲצֽוֹצְרָה|translate=a trumpet}} (for {{GHGheb|text=חֲצַרְצְרָה}}, cf. {{GHGpar|55|e}}). Also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=2|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=לַֽחֲפַרְפָּרוֹת}} is to be read instead of {{GHGheb|text=לַחְפֹּר פֵּרוֹת}} (from the ''sing.'' {{GHGheb|text=חֲפַרְפָּרָה}} a ''digging'' or ''burrowing'' animal, perhaps the ''mole''). But {{GHGheb|text=פְּקַחְקוֹחַ|translate=opening}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=61|verse=1}} (ed. Mant., Baer, Ginsb. {{GHGheb|text=פְּקַח־קוֹחַ}}), is an evident mistake due to dittography; read {{GHGheb|text=פְּקֹחַ}} as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=7|hidebook=1}}.

{{center|IX. ''Nouns in which the Whole (Biliteral) Stem is repeated.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|o|b}}
Naturally this class includes only isolated forms of the stems {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} (on {{GHGheb|text=פִּֽיפִיּוֹת}} see {{GHGpar|96}} under {{GHGheb|text=פֶּה}}). Thus:—

40. {{GHGheb|text=גַּלְגַּל|translate=a wheel}}, and, with attenuation of the first ''ă'' to ''ĭ'', {{GHGheb|text=גִּלְגָּל}} (from {{GHGheb|text=גלל}}); fem. {{GHGheb|text=חַלְחָלָה|translate=anguish}} (from {{GHGheb|text=חוּל}} or {{GHGheb|text=חִיל}}); {{GHGheb|text=כִּכָּר}} (for ''kirkar'') ''a talent''; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=כּוֹכָב|translate=a star}} (from ''kăwkăb'', Arabic ''kaukăb'', for {{GHGheb|text=כַּבְכַּב}}), {{GHGheb|text=טֽוֹטָפֹת|translate=bands}}, for {{GHGheb|text=טַפְטָפֹת}}; {{GHGheb|text=צְלָצַל}} probably ''a whirring locust''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|84|p|b}}
41. {{GHGheb|text=כַּלְכֵּל}} infin. ''Pilpēl'' (prop. ''Palpĭl'') from {{GHGheb|text=כּוּל}}; fem. {{GHGheb|text=טַלְטֵלָה|translate=a hurling}} (from {{GHGheb|text=טוּל}}).

42. {{GHGheb|text=כַּדְכֹּד}} perhaps a ''ruby'' (for ''kădkŭd''), from {{GHGheb|text=כדד}}.

43. {{GHGheb|text=קָדְקֹד|translate=the crown of the head}} (for ''qŭdqŭd''), from {{GHGheb|text=קדד}}; fem. {{GHGheb|text=גֻּלְגֹּ֫לֶת|translate=a skull}} (for ''gŭlgŭlt''), from {{GHGheb|text=גלל}}.

44. {{GHGheb|text=זַרְזִיר|translate=girded}}, from {{GHGheb|text=זרר}}; {{GHGheb|text=בַּקְבּוּק|translate=a bottle}}, from {{GHGheb|text=בקק}}; {{GHGheb|text=בַּרְבֻּרִים|translate=fattened birds}}(?).
<section end="par84b" />
<section begin="par85" />{{GHGpar-heading|85|Nouns with Preformatives and Afformatives}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|a}}
These include nouns which are directly derived from verbal forms having preformatives (''Hiphʿîl, Hophʿal, Hithpaʿēl, Niphʿal'', &''c.''), as well as those which are formed with other preformatives ({{GHGheb|text=א}}, {{GHGheb|text=י}}, {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}}, {{GHGheb|text=נ‍}}, {{GHGheb|text=ת}}), and finally those which are formed with afformatives. The quadriliterals and quinqueliterals also are taken in connexion with these formations, inasmuch as they arise almost always by the addition or insertion of one or two consonants to the triliteral stem.

{{center|X. ''Nouns with Preformatives.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|b}}
45. Nouns with {{GHGheb|text=א}} prefixed. Cf. the substantives with {{GHGheb|text=א|translate=prosthetic}} ({{GHGpar|19|m}}), such as {{GHGheb|text=אֶזְרוֹעַ|translate=arm}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=32|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=22}}; elsewhere always {{GHGheb|text=זְרוֹעַ}}); {{GHGheb|text=אֶצְבַּע|translate=a finger}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַרְבֶּה|translate=a locust}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֶגְרוֹף|translate=fist}} (others ''mattock'', or ''clod''), {{GHGheb|text=אַשְׁמוּרָה}} or {{GHGheb|text=אַשְׁמֹ֫רֶת|translate=a watch}}. In these examples the {{GHGheb|text=א}} is a ‘euphonic’ prefix (Barth, ''ibid.'', § 150 b); in other cases it is ‘essential’; cf. especially the adjectives, {{GHGheb|text=אַכְזָב|translate=deceitful}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַכְזָר|translate=cruel}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֵיתָן|translate=perennial}} (for ''ʾaitan'') [=the Arab. ‘''elative''’, used for expressing the compar. and superl. degrees]. The fem. {{GHGheb|text=אַזְכָּרָה|translate=fragrant part}}<ref>Or perhaps more correctly with Jacob, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZAW.|Zeitschrift für die alttestamentliche Wissenschaft, ed. by B. Stade, Giessen, 1881 ff., and since 1907 by K. Marti.}}}} 1897, p. 79, ‘''declaration'',’ i.e. the part of the meal-offering which ‘announces the sacrifice and its object’.</ref> (of the {{Hyphenated word start|s=meal-|hyph=|e=offering}}<section end="par85" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

260.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" />{{GHGcorrected}}</noinclude><section begin="par85" />{{Hyphenated word end|offering|meal-offering}}) is a ''nomen verbale'' of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, answering to the Aramaic infinitive of the causal stem (''’Aph‛ēl''), hence with suff. {{GHGheb|text=אַזְכָּֽרָתָהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=2|verse=2}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|c}}
46. Nouns with {{GHGheb|text=ה}} prefixed. Besides the ordinary infinitives of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הַקְטֵל}} and {{GHGheb|text=הַקְטִיל}}, of {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=הִקָּטֵל}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִקָּטֹל}} (for ''hinq.''), and of the conjugations formed with the prefix {{GHGheb|text=הִתְ}}, this class also includes some rare {{GHGterm|nomina verbalia}} derived from {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} (cf. {{GHGpar|72|z}}), viz. {{GHGheb|text=הַכָּרָה|translate=appearance}} (from {{GHGheb|text=נָכַר}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֲנָפָה|translate=a swinging}} (from {{GHGheb|text=נוּף}}), [{{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=28}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֲנָחָה|translate=a rest-giving}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=2|verse=18}}]; {{GHGheb|text=הַצָּלָה|translate=deliverance}} (from {{GHGheb|text=נָצַל}}), [{{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=4|verse=14}} an Aram. form: cf. {{GHGheb|text=הֲזָדָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=5|verse=20}}]; perhaps also {{GHGheb|text=הֵיכָל|translate=palace}}, from ''haikăl'', unless it is borrowed from the Assyrian; see the Lexicon. <!-- begin: not listed in the correction list, but makes sense -->Cf. also<!-- end: not listed in the correction list, but makes sense --> {{:Gesenius' Hebrew Grammar/Additions and Corrections/236}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|d}}
47. Nouns with {{GHGheb|text=י}} prefixed, as {{GHGheb|text=יִצְהָר|translate=oil}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַלְקוּט|translate=wallet}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַנְשׁוּף|translate=owl}}(?); from verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יְקוּם|translate=a living thing}}, {{GHGheb|text=יתוּר|translate=a range}}; from a verb {{GHGheb|text=ע״י}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָרִיב|translate=an adversary}}. Of a different character are the many proper names which have simply adopted the imperfect form, as {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעֲקֹב}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִצְחָק}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|e}}
48. Nouns with {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}} prefixed. This ''preformative Mêm'', which is no doubt connected with {{GHGheb|text=מִי|translate=who}}, and {{GHGheb|text=מָה|translate=what}} (see § 37 and {{GHGpar|52|c}}), appears in a very large number of nouns, and serves to express the most varied modifications of the idea of the stem: (1) {{GHGheb|text=מ‍|translate=subjective}}, when preformative of the participles ''Piʿēl, Hiphʿîl, Hithpaʿēl'', and other active conjugations. (2) {{GHGheb|text=מ‍|translate=objective}}, when preformative of the participles ''Puʿal, Hophʿal'', and other passive conjugations, as well as of numerous nouns. (3) {{GHGheb|text=מ‍|translate=instrumental}}, as in {{GHGheb|text=מַפְתֵּחַ|translate=a key}}, &c. (4) {{GHGheb|text=מ‍|translate=local}}, as in {{GHGheb|text=מִדְבָּר|translate=a drive for cattle}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|f}}
As regards the formation of these nouns, it is to be remarked that the preformative {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}} was originally in most cases followed by a short ''ă''. This ''ă'', however, in a closed syllable is frequently attenuated to ''ĭ''; in an open syllable before the tone it is lengthened to ''ā'' (so also the ''ĭ'', attenuated from ''ă'', is lengthened to ''ē''), and in {{GHGheb|text=מָגֵן|translate=shield}} (with suff. {{GHGheb|text=מָֽגִנִּי}}) it even becomes unchangeable ''â''. But in an open syllable which does ''not'' stand before the tone, the ''a'' necessarily becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|g}}
The following forms are especially to be noticed: (''a'') ground-form ''măqṭăl'', in Hebrew {{GHGheb|text=מַקְטָל}},<ref>In {{GHGheb|text=מַֽמְתַֿקִּים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=5|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=8|verse=10}}, the first syllable is artificially opened to avoid the cacophony; on the ''ă'' of the second syllable cf. {{GHGpar|93|ee}}.</ref> e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מַֽאֲכָל|translate=food}}; fem. {{GHGheb|text=מַמְלָכָה|translate=kingdom}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַֽאֲכֶ֫לֶת|translate=a knife}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְלָאכָה}} (for {{GHGheb|text=מַלְאָכָה}} by {{GHGpar|23|c}}) ''business''; from a verb {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַתָּן|translate=a gift}}; from verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}}, {{GHGheb|text=מוֹצָא|translate=a going forth}}, {{GHGheb|text=מוֹשָׁב|translate=a seat}}; from verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֵיטָב|translate=the best}} (from ''maiṭăb''); with {{GHGheb|text=י}} (or {{GHGheb|text=ו}}) assimilated, {{GHGheb|text=מַצָּע|translate=a bed}}; from verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, {{GHGheb|text=מָסָךְ|translate=a screen}}, and with the shortening of the ''ă'' under the preformative, {{GHGheb|text=מֶ֫מֶר|translate=bitterness}} (from {{GHGheb|text=מְמַר}} developed to a segholate), fem. {{GHGheb|text=מְשַׁמָּה|translate=desolation}}; from a verb {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, probably of this class is {{GHGheb|text=מָקוֹם|translate=place}}, the ''ă'' lengthened to ''ā'' and obscured to ''ô'' (Arabic ''măqâm''); from verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַרְאֶה|translate=appearance}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַ֫עַן}} (for {{GHGheb|text=מַֽעֲנֶה}}) prop. ''intention'', only in {{GHGheb|text=לְמַ֫עַן|translate=on account of, in order that}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|h}}
(''b'') Ground-form ''miqṭăl'' (the usual form of the infin. {{GHGterm|Qal}} in Aramaic), Hebr. {{GHGheb|text=מִקְטָל}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מִדְבָּר}} (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=31}} also, where Baer requires {{GHGheb|text=הֲמִדְבַּר}}, read with ed. Mant., Ginsburg, &c. {{GHGheb|text=הֲמִדְבָּר}}) ''a cattle-drive'', fem. {{GHGheb|text=מִלְחָמָהּ|translate=war}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֶרְכָּבָה|translate=a chariot}} (with {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} instead of ''ĭ'', but in ''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=מִרְכֶּ֫בֶת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=43}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=מֶרְחָק|translate=distance}}), {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁמֶ֫רֶת|translate=a watch}}; from verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מֵסַב|translate=surroundings}} (from ''mĭ-săb''; ''ĭ'' in the open syllable being lengthened to ''ē''; but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=מַשַּׁק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=4}} as {{GHGterm|constr. state}} from {{GHGheb|text=שׁקק}} with sharpening of the first radical; cf. {{GHGpar|67|g}}); from verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִקְנֶה|translate=a possession}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=מִקְנָה}}.
<section end="par85" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

261.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par85 />{{GHGmargin-letter|85|i}}
(''c'') Ground-form ''măqṭĭl'', Hebr. {{GHGheb|text=מַקְטֵל}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מַשְׁעֵן|translate=a support}} (fem. {{GHGheb|text=מַשְׁעֵנָה}}), {{GHGheb|text=מַסְגֵּר|translate=a smith}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַֽעֲשֵׂר|translate=a tithe}}; fem. {{GHGheb|text=מַכְשֵׁלָה|translate=a ruin}}; from a verb {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַגֵּפָה|translate=an overthrow}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַצֵּבָה|translate=a pillar}}; from verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, {{GHGheb|text=מָגֵן|translate=a shield}}; fem. {{GHGheb|text=מְגִלָּה|translate=a roll}} (from {{GHGheb|text=גָּלַל}}), {{GHGheb|text=מְאֵרָה|translate=a curse}} (for ''m<sup>e</sup>’irrā'' from {{GHGheb|text=אָרַר}}); from a verb {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}}, {{GHGheb|text=מוֹקֵשׁ|translate=a snare}} (from ''măwqĭš'').

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|k}}
(''d'') Ground-form ''mĭqṭĭl'', Hebr. {{GHGheb|text=מִקְטֵל}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מִסְפֵּד|translate=mourning}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִוְבֵּחַ|translate=an altar}} (''place of sacrifice''); from a verb {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מֵסֵב}} ({{GHGheb|text=מֵסַב}}?) ''consessus''; (''e'') ground-from ''măqṭŭl'', Hebr. {{GHGheb|text=מַקְטֹל}}; fem. {{GHGheb|text=מַֽאֲכֹ֫לֶת|translate=food}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַשְׂכֹּ֫רֶת|translate=wages}}; from a verb {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=מְסֻכָּה|translate=a covering}} (from {{GHGheb|text=סָכַךְ}}). Also from {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, according to the Masora, {{GHGheb|text=מָעוֹז|translate=a refuge}}, with suffixes {{GHGheb|text=מָֽעֻוִּי}} and {{GHGheb|text=מָֽעוּזִּי}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=מָֽעֻזִּים}}, but, very probably, most if not all of these forms are to be referred to the stem {{GHGheb|text=עוּז|translate=to flee for safety}}, and therefore should be written {{GHGheb|text=מְעוֹזִי}}, &c. The form {{GHGheb|text=מָעֹז}}, if derived from the stem {{GHGheb|text=עזז}}, would mean ''stronghold''.—Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=מֹ֫רֶךְ|translate=faintness}}, developed to a segholate, probably from {{GHGheb|text=מְרֹךְ}}, for ''mărōkh'' from {{GHGheb|text=רָכַךְ}}, like {{GHGheb|text=מְתֹם|translate=soundness}} of body, from {{GHGheb|text=תָּמַם}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|l}}
With a long vowel in the second syllable: (''f'') ground-form ''maqṭâl'', with ''â'' always obscured to ''ô'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מַחְסוֹר|translate=want}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַלְקוֹחַ|translate=booty}}; from verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מָגוֹר|translate=fear}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=מְגוֹרָה}} and {{GHGheb|text=מְגוּרָה}} (with the ''ô'' depressed to ''û'' in a toneless syllable; cf. {{GHGpar|27|n}}), {{GHGheb|text=מְהוּמָה}}, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=5}}. (''g'') Ground-form ''mĭqṭâl'', in Hebr. again {{GHGheb|text=מִקְטוֹל}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מִסְתּוֹר|translate=a covert}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִכְשׁוֹל|translate=a stumbling-block}} (cf. above under i, ''măkhšēlā''); fem. {{GHGheb|text=מִכְמֹ֫רֶת|translate=a fishing-net}}; (''h'') the ground-forms ''maqṭîl'', ''miqṭîl'' (cf. {{GHGheb|text=מֵקִים}}) are found only in participles {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}; the fem. {{GHGheb|text=מַבְלִיגִית}}, ''cheerfulness'', is a denominative formed from a participle {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}; (''i'') ground-form ''măqṭûl'', as {{GHGheb|text=מַלְבּוּשׁ|translate=a garment}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|m}}
Rem. On {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}} as preformative of the participles of all the conjugations except {{GHGterm|Qal}} and {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, cf. {{GHGpar|52|c}}. Many of these participles have become substantives, as {{GHGheb|text=מְזַמֶּ֫רֶת|translate=snuffers}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַשְׁחִית|translate=destroyer, destruction}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|n}}
49. Nouns with {{GHGheb|text=נ‍}} prefixed. Besides the participles {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} (ground-form ''năqṭăl'', still retained e.g. in {{GHGheb|text=נוֹלָד}} for ''năwlād'', but commonly attenuated to ''nıqṭăl'', Hebr. {{GHGheb|text=נִקְטָל}}) and the infinitive {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} of the form {{GHGheb|text=נִקְטֹל}}, the prefix {{GHGheb|text=נ‍}} is found in {{GHGheb|text=נַפְתּוּלִים|translate=wrestlings}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=8}}, which is also to be referred to {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, and {{GHGheb|text=נָזִיד|translate=boiled pottage}} (stem {{GHGheb|text=זיד}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|o}}
50. With {{GHGheb|text=שׁ}} prefixed, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שַׁלְהֶ֫בֶת|translate=a flame}}. On this ''Šaph‛ēl'' formation, cf. {{GHGpar|55|i}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|p}}
51. Nouns with {{GHGheb|text=ת}} prefixed. Examples of this formation are numerous, especially from weak stems, for the purpose of strengthening them phonetically (see Barth, ''ibid.'', p. 283), and notably from verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} and {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}. They may be classified as follows:—(''a'') the ground-form ''tăqṭăl'' in {{GHGheb|text=תַּחְמָס|translate=ostrich}} (?); from verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}}, {{GHGheb|text=תּוֹשָׁב|translate=a settler}}; fem. {{GHGheb|text=תּוֹחֶ֫לֶת|translate=expectation}}, {{GHGheb|text=תּוֹכַ֫חַת}} (from the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הוֹכִיתַ}}) ''correction''; from a verb {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}}, {{GHGheb|text=תֵּימָן|translate=the south}}; from verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} and {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, {{GHGheb|text=תּוֹדָה|translate=thanksgiving}}, and {{GHGheb|text=תּוֹרָה|translate=law}}, both from {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}; from a verb {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} and {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}}, {{GHGheb|text=תּֽוֹצָאוֹת|translate=issues}}; probably belonging to this class, from verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, {{GHGheb|text=תֶּ֫בֶל|translate=confusion}}, and {{GHGheb|text=תֶּ֫מֶס|translate=a melting away}} (developed from {{GHGheb|text=תְּבַל}} and {{GHGheb|text=תְּמַס}}, from {{GHGheb|text=בָּלַל}} and {{GHGheb|text=מָסַס}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|q}}
(''b'') ''Tĭqṭăl'', e.g. fem. {{GHGheb|text=תִּפְאָרָה}} and {{GHGheb|text=תִּפְאֶ֫רֶת|translate=glory}}; from a verb {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תִּקְוָה|translate=hope}}; (''c'') ''tăqṭĭl'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תַּשְׁבֵּץ|translate=chequer work}}; fem. {{GHGheb|text=תַּרְדֵּמָה|translate=deep sleep}} (probably from the {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נִרְדַּם}}); from a verb {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}}, {{GHGheb|text=תּֽוֹכֵחָה|translate=correction}} (from the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}-stem, like the ''constr. st. plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=תּֽוֹלְדוֹת|translate=generations}}); from verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, {{GHGheb|text=תְּהִלָּה|translate=praise}}, {{GHGheb|text=תְּפִלָּה|translate=prayer}} (from the {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} of the stems {{GHGheb|text=הָלַל}} and {{GHGheb|text=פָּלַל}}).
<section end=par85 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

262.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par85 />{{GHGmargin-letter|85|r}}
With a long vowel in the second syllable: (''d'') ''tĭqṭâl'', as {{GHGheb|text=תְּהוֹם|translate=the ocean, the deep}} (for ''tĭhâm''; in Assyrian the fem. ''tiâmtu'', constr. st. ''tiâmat'', is the usual word for ''sea''), unless it is to be derived with Delitzsch, ''Prolegomena'', p. 113, from the stem {{GHGheb|text=תהם}}; (''e'') ''tâqṭîl'' (in Arabic the usual form of the infinitive of conjugation II. which corresponds to the Hebrew {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}), e.g. from a verb {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=תַּכְלִית|translate=completeness}}; {{GHGheb|text=תַּרְבִּית|translate=increase, usury}}, with a parallel form {{GHGheb|text=מַרְבִּית}}; in a passive sense, {{GHGheb|text=תַּלְמִיד|translate=a disciple}}; (''f'') {{GHGheb|text=תַּקְטוּל}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תַּפּוּחַ|translate=an apple}} (for ''tănpû<sup>a</sup>ḥ''); very frequently used to form abstracts, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תַּגְמוּל|translate=a benefit}} (also {{GHGheb|text=גְּמוּל}}); from verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=תְּבוּסָה|translate=a treading down}}, {{GHGheb|text=תְּנוּפָה|translate=a waving}} (like {{GHGheb|text=תְּרוּמָה|translate=a lifting up}}, from the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} stem), {{GHGheb|text=תְּשׁוּקָה|translate=a longing}}, &c.; very frequently also as an abstract plural, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תַּהְפֻּכוֹת|translate=perverseness}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּחְבֻּלוֹת|translate=guidance}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּמְרוּרִים|translate=bitterness}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּנְחוּמִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=תַּנְחוּמוֹת|translate=consolation}}; from a verb {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=תְּאֻנִים|translate=toil}}.

{{center|XI. ''Nouns with Afformatives.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|s}}
52. Nouns with {{GHGheb|text=ל}} affixed. Perhaps {{GHGheb|text=חַשְׁמַל|translate=amber}}(?), and probably {{GHGheb|text=בַּרְזֶל|translate=iron}}, {{GHGheb|text=כַּרְמֶל|translate=garden-land}} ({{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} in both cases is probably a modification of the original ''ă'' in the tone-syllable), {{GHGheb|text=גִּבְעֹל|translate=bloom}}, cf. {{GHGpar|30|q}}.—According to ''Prätorius'', {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1903, p. 530 ff., ''al'' is an affix of endearment in the proper names {{GHGheb|text=מִיכַל}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֲמוּטַל}} (''little lizard''?) {{GHGheb|text=אֲבִיגַל}} (also {{GHGheb|text=אֲבִיגַ֫יִל}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|t}}
53. Nouns with {{GHGheb|text=ם}} affixed. With an original ''ăm'' as afformative, {{GHGheb|text=אוּלָם|translate=vestibule}} (although the ''ā'' in the ''sing''. remains unchangeable), plur. {{GHGheb|text=אֻֽלַמִּים}}; but in {{GHGheb|text=כִּנָּם|translate=a swarm of gnats}}, the {{GHGheb|text=ם}} is radical. With original afformative ''ŭm'', {{GHGheb|text=עֵירֹם}} (also {{GHGheb|text=עֵרֹם}}) ''naked'' (from {{GHGheb|text=עור}}), plur. {{GHGheb|text=עֵיֽרֻמִּים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=7}}, parallel form {{GHGheb|text=עָרוֹם}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=עֲרוּמִּים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=25}}.—To this class also belong the adverbs in ''ām'' and ''ōm'', mentioned in {{GHGpar|100|g}}, and many proper names, as {{GHGheb|text=גֵּֽרְשֹׁם}}, also {{GHGheb|text=גֵּֽרְשׁוֹם}}, and {{GHGheb|text=גֵּֽרְשׁוֹן}} (''patronymic'' {{GHGheb|text=גֵּֽרְשֻׁנִּי}}), {{GHGheb|text=מִלְכֹּם}}, {{GHGheb|text=עַמְרָם}}, &c.; but for {{GHGheb|text=פִּדְיוֹם|translate=ransom}} (?), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=3|verse=49}}, probably {{GHGheb|text=פְּדוּיִם}} is to be read.

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|u}}
54. Nouns with {{GHGheb|text=ן}} affixed. The {{GHGheb|text=ן}} is added by means of a simple helping vowel in {{GHGheb|text=כְּנַ֫עֵן|translate=Canaan}}, and {{GHGheb|text=צִפֹּ֫רֶן|translate=a finger nail}}; more frequently the addition is made by means of a tone-bearing ''ă'', which in Hebrew is modified to {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} (as {{GHGheb|text=גַּרְזֶן|translate=axe}}) or lengthened to ''ā'' (but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אֲחֹֽרַנִּית}} and {{GHGheb|text=קְדֹֽרַנִּית}}); e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קִנְיָן|translate=a possession}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֻׁלְחָן|translate=a table}}, {{GHGheb|text=קָרְבָּן|translate=an offering}}. From an original ''â'' being changed into an obscure ''ô'' we may probably explain such forms as {{GHGheb|text=דְּאָבוֹן|translate=a pining away}}; {{GHGheb|text=דָּֽרְבוֹן}} (also {{GHGheb|text=דָּֽרְבָן}}) ''a goad''; {{GHGheb|text=רְעָבוֹן|translate=hunger}}; from verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, {{GHGheb|text=גָּאוֹן|translate=pride}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָמוֹן|translate=noise}}, {{GHGheb|text=תָזוֹן|translate=a vision}}; {{GHGheb|text=שִׁרְיוֹן|translate=a coat of mail}}; from a verb {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַשָּׁאוֹן|translate=guile}} (the only instance with both {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}} preformative and ''ôn'' afformative)<ref>The plurals {{GHGheb|text=נִצָנִים|translate=flowers}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=2|verse=12}}, and {{GHGheb|text=קִמְּשׂנִים|translate=thorns}} appear to be formed directly from the singulars {{GHGheb|text=נֵץ}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=נִצָה}}) and {{GHGheb|text=קִמּוֹשׂ}} with the insertion of ''ân'' (which in {{GHGheb|text=קמ׳}} is obscured to ''ôn''). See Nöldeke, Mand. Gr., p. 169, Rem. 3; similarly, according to Hoffmann, ‘Einige phöniz. Inschriften,’ p. 15 ({{GHGcite|title|Abh. der Gött. Ges. der Wiss.}}, xxxvi), {{GHGheb|text=עִזְּבוֹנִים|translate=wares}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=27|verse=14.16}} from {{GHGheb|text=עֶ֫זֶב}}={{GHGheb|text=עֶ֫צֶן}}.</ref>; very frequently from the simple stem with an unorganic sharpening of the second radical, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=זִכָּרוֹן|translate=memorial}}, {{GHGheb|text=כִּלָּיוֹן|translate=destruction}} (''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=זִכְרוֹן}} and {{GHGheb|text=כִּלְיוֹן}}), &c.; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=הֵֽרָיוֹן|translate=pregnancy}} (for {{GHGheb|text=הִרָּ׳}}) and {{GHGpar|93|uu}}; {{GHGheb|text=קִֽיקָלוֹן|translate=shame}}, for {{GHGheb|text=קִלְקָלוֹן}}. Proper names occur with the termination ''ûn'', as {{GHGheb|text=יְשֻׁרוּן}}, {{GHGpar|86|g}}, and others.
<section end=par85 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

263.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par85" />{{GHGmargin-letter|85|v}}
Rem. A large number of proper names now ending in {{GHGheb|text=־ֹה}} or {{GHGheb|text=־וֹ}} used to be classed as nouns originally formed with the affix {{GHGheb|text=־וֹן}}. The subsequent rejection of the final ''Nûn'' seemed to be confirmed by the form {{GHGheb|text=מְגִדּוֹן}}, once used ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=12|verse=11}}) for {{GHGheb|text=מְגִדּוֹ}} (and conversely in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=27|verse=20}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} {{GHGheb|text=אֲבַדֹּה}}, {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} {{GHGheb|text=אֲבַדּוֹ}} for {{GHGheb|text=אֲבַדּוֹן|translate=destruction}}), also by the fact that for {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלֹמֹה}} the LXX give the form {{polytonic|Σολωμών}} or {{polytonic|Σαλωμών}}, and especially that in patronymics and tribal names ({{GHGpar|86|h}}) a ''Nûn'' appears before the termination ''î'', as {{GHGheb|text=גִּֽילֹנִי|translate=Gilonite}} from {{GHGheb|text=גִּלֹה}} and {{GHGheb|text=שִֽׁילֹנִי}} from {{GHGheb|text=שִׁילֹה}} (modern name ''Sailûn''). Wetzstein, however (in Delitzsch’s ''Commentary on Job'', 1st ed., p. 599), explained the ''Nûn'' in {{GHGheb|text=מְגִדּוֹן}} as a secondary addition to the common old-Palestinian termination ''ô'' ({{GHGheb|text=יְרִיחוֹ}}, {{GHGheb|text=עַכּוֹ}}, {{GHGheb|text=רִמּוֹנוֹ}}, &c.), and Barth ({{GHGcite|title=Nominalbildung}}, §224''b'') has since shown the unsoundness of the prevailing view on other grounds: the rejection of the ''Nûn'' would be much more likely to occur in the numerous appellatives in ''ôn'' than in proper names, and {{GHGheb|text=גִּֽילֹנִי}} and {{GHGheb|text=שִֽׁילֹנִי}} are due to the necessity of avoiding, for euphonic reasons, such forms as ''gîlô-î, šîlô-î'', &c.; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=שֵֽׁלָנִי}} from {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁלָה}}.

On the afformatives {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ַי}}, {{GHGheb|text=וּת}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ִית}}, see below, {{GHGpar|86|h}}–l.

{{center|XII. ''Quadriliterals and Quinqueliterals.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|85|w}}
55. {{GHGheb|text=גַּלְמוּד|translate=barren}}, {{GHGheb|text=חַלָּמִישׁ|translate=a flint}}, and the fem {{GHGheb|text=זַלְעָפָה|translate=heat}}, &c., have probably arisen from the insertion of a {{GHGheb|text=ל}}; {{GHGheb|text=חַרְגֹּל|translate=a locust}}, {{GHGheb|text=קַרְדֹּם|translate=an axe}}, {{GHGheb|text=סַרְעַפָּה|translate=a branch}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=31|verse=5}} (verses 6, 8 {{GHGheb|text=סְעַפָּה}}), {{GHGheb|text=שַׂרְעַפִּים}} (also {{GHGheb|text=שְׂעִפִּים}}) ''anxious thoughts'', {{GHGheb|text=שַׁרְבִּיט|translate=sceptre}}, from insertion of a {{GHGheb|text=ר}}, which is common in Aramaic. Cf., moreover, {{GHGheb|text=חֶרְמֵשׁ|translate=a sickle}}, {{GHGheb|text=סְמָדַר|translate=vine-blossom}}; with an initial {{GHGheb|text=ע}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֲטַלֵּף|translate=a bat}}, {{GHGheb|text=עַכָּבִישׁ|translate=a spider}}, {{GHGheb|text=עַכְבָּר|translate=a mouse}}, {{GHGheb|text=עַקְרָב|translate=a scorpion}},<ref>Derenbourg ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}}, 1883, p. 165) infers from the above examples and a comparison of the Arabic ''‛uṣfûr'', ''sparrow'' (from ''ṣafara'', ''to chirp''), that {{GHGheb|text=ע}} was especially employed to form quadriliteral names of animals.</ref> &c.—Quinqueliteral, {{GHGheb|text=צְפַרְדֵּעַ|translate=a frog}}.
<section end="par85" />
<section begin="par86" />{{GHGpar-heading|86|Denominative Nouns}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|86|a}}
'''1.''' Such are all nouns formed ''immediately'' from another noun, whether the latter be primitive or derived from a verb, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קַדְמוֹן|translate=eastern}}, immediately from {{GHGheb|text=קֶ֫דֶם|translate=the east}} (verbal stem {{GHGheb|text=קָדַם|translate=to be in front}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|86|b}}
'''2.''' Most of the forms which nouns of this class assume have already been given in {{GHGpar|84|doublesign=1}} and {{GHGpar|85|nosign=1}}, since the denominatives, as secondary (although in some cases very old) forms, invariably follow the analogy of the verbal derivatives. As, for instance, the verbals with a prefixed {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}} ({{GHGpar|85|e}} to m) express the place, &c., of an action, so the denominatives with {{GHGheb|text=מ‍|translate=local}} represent the place where a thing is found or its neighbourhood (see e).

The most common forms of denominatives are—

{{GHGmargin-letter|86|c}}
1. Those like the {{GHGterm|participle Qal}} ({{GHGpar|84|s|a}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁעֵר|translate=a porter}}, from {{GHGheb|text=שַׁ֫עַר|translate=a gate}}; {{GHGheb|text=בֹּקֵר|translate=a herdsman}}, from {{GHGheb|text=בָּקָר|translate=a herd}}; {{GHGheb|text=כֹּרֵם|translate=a vinedresser}}, from {{GHGheb|text=כֶּ֫רֶם|translate=a vineyard}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|86|d}}
2. Those like the form ''qăṭṭāl'' ({{GHGpar|84|b|b}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קַשָּׁת|translate=an archer}}, from {{GHGheb|text=קֶ֫שֶׁת|translate=a bow}}.
<section end="par86" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

264.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par86" />Both these forms (''c'' and ''d'') indicate customary occupations, inhering in the subject, like Greek nouns in της, τεύς, e.g. πολίτης, γραμματεύς.

{{GHGmargin-letter|86|e}}
3. Nouns with {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}} prefixed, denoting the place where a thing is (cf. {{GHGpar|85|e}}), or its neighbourhood, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מַעְיָן|translate=a place of fountains}}, from {{GHGheb|text=עַ֫יִן}}; {{GHGheb|text=מַרְגְּלוֹת|translate=the place about the feet}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְרַֽאֲשׁוֹת|translate=the place about the head}}, from {{GHGheb|text=רֶ֫גֶל}}, {{GHGheb|text=רֹאשׁ}}; {{GHGheb|text=מִקְשָׁה}} (for {{GHGheb|text=מִקְשְׁאָה}}) ''a cucumber field'', from {{GHGheb|text=קִשֻּׁא|translate=cucumber}}. Cf. ἀμπελών from ἄμπελος.

{{GHGmargin-letter|86|f}}
4. Nouns with the termination {{GHGheb|text=־ָן}} or {{GHGheb|text=וֹן}} expressing adjectival ideas: {{GHGheb|text=קַדְמוֹן|translate=eastern}}, from {{GHGheb|text=קֶ֫דֶם}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַֽחֲרוֹן|translate=posterior}}, from {{GHGheb|text=אַחַר}}; {{GHGheb|text=חִיצוֹן|translate=exterior}}, from {{GHGheb|text=חוּץ}}; probably also {{GHGheb|text=לִוְיָתָן|translate=coiled}}, hence ''coiled animal, serpent'', from {{GHGheb|text=לִוְיָה|translate=a winding}}; {{GHGheb|text=נְחֻשְׁתָּן|translate=brazen}}, from {{GHGheb|text=נְח֫שֶׁת|translate=brass}}. Also ''abstracts'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עִוָּרוֹן|translate=blindness}}, from {{GHGheb|text=עִוֵּר}}. Cf. {{GHGpar|85|u}}.— With a double termination (''ôn'' or ''ân'' with ''î'') {{GHGheb|text=אַדְמֹנִי|translate=reddish}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִדְּעֹנִי|translate=a knowing}} (spirit); {{GHGheb|text=צִפְעֹנִי|translate=basilisk}}; {{GHGheb|text=רַֽחֲמָֽנִיּוֹת|translate=merciful}} [fem. plur.].

{{GHGmargin-letter|86|g}}
{{GHGheb|text=וֹן}} appears to be used as a diminutive ending (cf. the Syriac {{GHGheb|text=וּן}}) in {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁוֹן|translate=little man}} (in the eye), ''apple of the eye'', from {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}}<ref>Cf. Barth, § 212; König, ii. 1, 413. Diminutives in Semitic languages are, however, most commonly formed by inserting a ''y'' after the second radical, e.g. Aram. {{GHGheb|text=עוּלֵּימָא}}, Syr. {{syriac|text=ܥܰܠܝܡܳܐ|font=western}}, Arab. {{arabic|غُ‍لَ‍يِّ‍مٌ}} {{GHGtranslate|a very young man, kulaib, a little dog}}, &c. Since Olshausen (§ 180), {{GHGheb|text=זְעֵיר|translate=a little}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=10.13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=36|verse=2}}) has commonly been regarded as an example of the same form, to which others have added {{GHGheb|text=שְׁבִיסִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=18}} (as though a foreign dialectical form for ''šumais'', {{GHGtranslate|little sun}}), and {{GHGheb|text=אֲמִינוֹן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=20}}, as a contemptuous diminutive form of {{GHGheb|text=אַמְינוֹן}}; cf. Ewald, § 167, W. Wright, ''Arab. Gramm.''<sup>2</sup> i. § 269, De Lagarde, {{GHGcite|title=Nominalbildung}}, pp. 85–87, König. ii. 1, p. 143 f. The existence of the form in Hebrew is disputed by Barth, {{GHGpar|192|d}}.]</ref>; on the other hand {{GHGheb|text=שְׁפִיפֹן|translate=adder}}, which was formerly regarded as a diminutive, is properly an adjectival form from {{GHGheb|text=שָׁפַף|translate=to rub}} (hence, as it were, a ''rubbing'' creature); in the same way {{GHGheb|text=יְשֻׁרוּן}} is a ''denominative'' from {{GHGheb|text=יָשָׁוּר}} (={{GHGheb|text=יָשָׁר}}), properly ''upright'' (''righteous people''), and not a ''diminutive'' (''pious little people'', and the like); finally, {{GHGheb|text=שַֽׂהֲרוֹן}} is not ''lunula'', but ''an artificial moon'' (used as an ornament), and {{GHGheb|text=צַוְּרֹנִים}} not ''little neck'', but ''necklace'' (from {{GHGheb|text=צַוָּאר|translate=neck}}). Cf. Delitzsch on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=4|verse=9}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|86|h}}
5. Peculiar to denominatives is the termination {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}}, which converts a substantive into an adjective, and is added especially to numerals and names of persons and countries, in order to form ''ordinals, patronymics'', and ''tribal names''; e.g. {{GHGheb|text=רַגְלִי|translate=footman}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=רַגְלִים}}, from {{GHGheb|text=רֶ֫גֶל|translate=foot}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַכְזָרִי|translate=cruel}}, {{GHGheb|text=נָכְרִי|translate=strange}}, from {{GHGheb|text=נֹ֫כֶר|translate=strangeness}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּחְתִּי|translate=lower}}, from {{GHGheb|text=תַּ֫חַת|translate=below}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=תָּחְתִּית}} and {{GHGheb|text=תַּחְתִּיָּה}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=תַּחְתִּיִּים}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּחְתִּיּוֹת}}; {{GHGheb|text=שִׁשִּׁי|translate=the sixth}}, from {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁשׁ|translate=six}}; {{GHGheb|text=מֽוֹאָבִי|translate=Moabite}}, from {{GHGheb|text=מוֹאָב}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=מֹֽאָבִים}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=מֽוֹאֲבִיָּה}} and {{GHGheb|text=מֽוֹאָבִית}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=מֽוֹאֲבִיּוֹת}}; {{GHGheb|text=עִבְרִי|translate=Hebrew}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=עִבְרִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=עבְרִיִּים}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=עִבְרִיָּה}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=עִבְרִיּוֹת}}; {{GHGheb|text=ישְׂרְאֵלִי|translate=Israelite}}, from {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׂרָאֵל}} When the original substantive is a ''compound'', it is resolved again into two words, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־יְמִינִי|translate=Benjamite}}, from {{GHGheb|text=בִּנְיָמִין}} (cf. on the use of the article in such cases, {{GHGpar|127|d}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|86|i}}
Instead of {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} we find in a few cases (''a'') the ending {{GHGheb|text=־ַי}} (as in Aram.), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כִּילַי}} (''crafty'', or, according to others, ''churlish'') if it stands for {{GHGheb|text=נְכִילַי}} and is not rather from a stem {{GHGheb|text=כלא}} or {{GHGheb|text=כלה}}; {{GHGheb|text=חוֹרָי|translate=white cloth}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=9}} in pause; perhaps also {{GHGheb|text=גֹּבַי|translate=a swarm of locusts}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=7|verse=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=גּוֹבָ֑י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=17}}); hardly {{GHGheb|text=נְגִֽינוֹתַי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=38|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=3|verse=19}}; but certainly in proper names as {{GHGheb|text=בּרְזִלַּי}} (''ferreus'') ''Barzillai'';<ref>On {{GHGheb|text=־ַי}} as an old fem. ending, see above, {{GHGpar|80|l}}.</ref> and (''b'') {{GHGheb|text=־ֶה}},<section end="par86" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

265.text:
arising from ''ăy'', in {{GHGheb|text=אִשֶּׁה|translate=belonging to fire}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֵשׁ}}), i.e. a ''sacrifice offered by fire''; {{GHGheb|text=לִבְנֶה}} (prop. ''milky'') ''the storax-shrub'', Arabic ''lubnay''. {{GHGmargin-letter|86|k}} 6. ''Abstract'' nouns formed from ''concretes'' by the addition of {{GHGheb|text=וּת}}, {{GHGheb|text=ת}}[{{GHGheb|text=־ִי}}] ({{GHGpar|95|t}}), cf. our terminations ''-dom, -hood, -ness'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יַלְדוּת|translate=youth}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַלְכוּת|translate=kingdom}} (the omission of the {{GHGterm|Dageš}} in {{GHGheb|text=כ‍}} shows that the {{GHGterm|Šewâ}} is weakened from a full vowel; on ''malik'' as underlying the present form {{GHGheb|text=מֶ֫לֶךְ}} cf. {{GHGpar|84|a|a}}); {{GHGheb|text=אַלְמָנוּת|translate=widowhood}}, from {{GHGheb|text=אַלְמָן|translate=widower}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַלְמָנָה|translate=widow}}. In Aram. this fem. ending {{GHGheb|text=וּת}} (or {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} with rejection of the {{GHGheb|text=ת}}) is a common termination of the infinitive in the derived conjugations (cf., as substantival infinitives of this kind, {{GHGheb|text=הַשְׁמָעוּת|translate=the announcing}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=24|verse=26}}, and {{GHGheb|text=הִתְחַבְּרוּת|translate=the making of a league}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=11|verse=23}}); in Hebr. {{GHGheb|text=וּת}} as a termination to express abstract ideas (including some which appear to be directly derived from the verbal stem, as {{GHGheb|text=סִכְלוּת|translate=folly}}, {{GHGheb|text=רִפְאוּת|translate=a heating}}[See a complete list of instances in König, {{GHGcite|title=Lehrgebäude}}, ii. 1, p. 205 f.]) becomes more common only in the later books. It is affixed to adjectives ending in ''î'' (see above, h) in {{GHGheb|text=אַכְזְרִיּוּת|translate=cruelty}}, and {{GHGheb|text=קֽוֹמְמִיּוּת|translate=upright position}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=13}}, used adverbially). {{GHGmargin-letter|86|l}} The ending {{GHGheb|text=־ִית}} is found earlier, e.g. in {{GHGheb|text=שְׁאֵרִית|translate=remainder}}, {{GHGheb|text=רֵאשִׁית|translate=principium}}, from {{GHGheb|text=רֵאשׁ}}={{GHGheb|text=רֹאשׁ}} (''head'') ''princeps''. The termination ''ôth'' seems to occur in {{GHGheb|text=הָכְמוֹת|translate=wisdom}} (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=9|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, joined to a ''singular''; so also {{GHGheb|text=חַכְמוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=14|verse=1}}, where, probably, {{GHGheb|text=חָכְמוֹת}} should likewise be read) and in {{GHGheb|text=הֽוֹלֵלוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=1|verse=17}}, &c., with the parallel form {{GHGheb|text=הֽוֹלֵלוּת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=10|verse=13}}.
{{GHGpar-heading|87|Of the Plural}}
Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, i. 426 ff., and on the feminines, p. 441 ff.; M. Lambert, ‘Remarques sur la formation du pluriel hébreu,’ {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} xxiv. 99 ff., and ‘Les anomalies du pluriel des noms en Hébreu,’ {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} xliii. 206 ff.; P. ''Lajčiak'', ''Die Plural- u. Dualendungen im semit. Nomen'', Lpz. 1903; J. Barth, ‘Beiträge zur Pluralbildung des Semit.,’ {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1904, p. 431 ff., i. ‘the ''ai'' of the constr. st.’
{{GHGmargin-letter|87|a}} '''1.''' The regular ''plural'' termination for the ''masculine gender'' is {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}}, always with the tone, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=סוּס|translate=horse}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=סוּסִים|translate=horses}}; but also very often written defectively {{GHGheb|text=־ִם}}, especially when in the same word one of the vowel letters, {{GHGheb|text=ו}} or {{GHGheb|text=י}}, precedes, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=21}} {{GHGheb|text=תַּנִּינִם}}. Nouns in {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} make their plural in {{GHGheb|text=־ִיִּים}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עִבְרִי|translate=a Hebrew}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=עִבְריִּים}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=18}}); but usually contraction takes place, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עִבְרִים}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנִים|translate=crimson garments}}, from {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנִי}}. {{GHGmargin-letter|87|b}} Nouns in {{GHGheb|text=־ֶה}} lose this termination when they take the plural ending, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חֹזֶה|translate=seer}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=חֹזִים}} (cf. {{GHGpar|75|h}}).—In regard to the loss of the tone from the {{GHGheb|text=־ִם}} in the two old plurals {{GHGheb|text=מַ֫יִם|translate=water}} and {{GHGheb|text=שָׁמַ֫יִם|translate=heaven}}, cf. {{GHGpar|88|d}} and § 96. {{GHGmargin-letter|87|c}} The termination {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}} is sometimes assumed also by feminines (cf. {{GHGheb|text=נָשִׁים|translate=women}}, § 96 under {{GHGheb|text=אִשָּׁה}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנִים|translate=years}}, from {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנָה}}; {{GHGheb|text=רְחֵלִים|translate=ewes}}, from {{GHGheb|text=רָחֵל}}), so that an indication of gender is not necessarily implied in it (cf. also below, m–p).—On the use of this termination {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}} to express abstract, extensive, and intensive ideas, cf. {{GHGpar|124}}.

266.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par87 />{{GHGmargin-letter|87|d}}
The ending ''îm'' is also common in Phoenician, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=צדנם|translate=Sidonii}}; Assyrian has ''âni'' (acc. to P. Haupt originally ''âmi'', cf. {{GHGpar|88|d}}); Aramaic has ''în''; Arabic ''ûna'' (nominative) and ''îna'' (in the oblique cases, but in vulgar Arabic ''în'' is also used for the nominative); Ethiopic ''ân''. Cf. also the verbal ending {{GHGheb|text=וּן}} in the 3rd plur. perf. ({{GHGpar|44|l}}) and in the 3rd and 2nd plur. impf. ({{GHGpar|47|m}}).<ref>On the connexion between all these endings see Dietrich’s ''Abhandl. zur hebr. Gramm.'', Leipzig, 1846, p. 51 ff.; Halévy, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} 1888, p. 138 ff. [cf. also Driver, {{GHGcite|title=Tenses}}, § 6, Obs. 2].</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|e}}
Less frequent, or only apparent terminations of the plur. masc. are—

(''a'') {{GHGheb|text=־ִין}}, as in Aramaic,<ref>So also always in the Mêša‛ inscription, e.g. line 2 {{GHGheb|text=שלשן|translate=thirty}}; line 4 {{GHGheb|text=מלכן|translate=kings}}; line 5 {{GHGheb|text=ימן רבן|translate=many days}}, &c.</ref> found almost exclusively in the later books of the O.T. (apart from the poetical use in some of the older and even the oldest portions), viz. {{GHGheb|text=מְלָכִין|translate=kings}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=31|verse=3}}, {{GHGheb|text=צִֽדֹנִין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=33}}, {{GHGheb|text=רָצִין|translate=the guard}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=11|verse=13}}, {{GHGheb|text=חִטִּין|translate=wheat}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=4|verse=9}}; defectively {{GHGheb|text=אִיִּן|translate=islands}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָמִין|translate=days}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=12|verse=13}}. Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=מִדִּין|translate=carpets}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=10}}, in the North-Palestinian song of Deborah, which also has other linguistic peculiarities; {{GHGheb|text=עִיִּין|translate=heaps}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=3|verse=12}} (before {{GHGheb|text=ת}}; cf. {{GHGpar|44|k}}); {{GHGheb|text=מִלִּין|translate=words}} (from the really Aram. {{GHGheb|text=מִלָּה}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=2}}, and twelve other places in Job (beside {{GHGheb|text=מִלִּים}}, ten times in Job); further, {{GHGheb|text=חַיִּין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=22}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲחֵרִין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, and {{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹמֵמִין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=4}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּנִּין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=4|verse=3|hidebook=1}}.—The following forms are doubtful:

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|f}}
(''b'') {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} (with the {{GHGheb|text=ם}} rejected, as, according to some, in the ''dual'' {{GHGheb|text=יָדַי}} for {{GHGheb|text=יָדַ֫יִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=18}}, cf. {{GHGpar|88|c}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מִנִּי|translate=stringed instruments}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=45|verse=9}} for {{GHGheb|text=מִנִּים}} (unless it is to be so written)<ref>According to some this ''î'' is simply due to a neglect of the point ({{GHGpar|5|m}}), which in MSS. and elsewhere marked the abbreviation of the plur. ending.</ref>; {{GHGheb|text=עַמִּי|translate=peoples}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=144|verse=2}}, and, probably, also {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=3|verse=14}} (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=22|verse=44}} it may be taken as {{GHGheb|text=עַמִּי|translate=my people}}; cf. in the parallel passage {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=44}} {{GHGheb|text=עָם}}; also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=8|verse=2}} the ''î'' of {{GHGheb|text=רִמֹּנִי}} is better regarded as a ''suffix''); see also {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=23|verse=8}} as compared with {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=11|verse=11}}, and on the whole question Gesenius, {{GHGcite|title=Lehrgebäude}}, p. 524 ff. More doubtful still is—

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|g}}
(''c'') {{GHGheb|text=־ַי}} (like the constr. state in Syriac), which is supposed to appear in e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שָׂרַי|translate=princes}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=15}} (perhaps ''my princes'' is intended: read either the constr. st. {{GHGheb|text=שָׂרֵי}}, which also has good authority, or with LXX {{GHGheb|text=שָׁרִים}}); for {{GHGheb|text=חַלּוֹנָ֔י וס׳}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=14}} (according to others ''dual'', see {{GHGpar|88|c}}, or a loan word, cf. {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZA.|Zeitschrift für Assyriologie und verwandte Gebiete, ed. by C. Bezold. Lpz. 18S6 ff.}}}} iii. 93) read {{GHGheb|text=חַלּוֹנָיו סָפוֹן}}. On {{GHGheb|text=גּוֹבַי}} and {{GHGheb|text=חוֹרַי}}, which have also been so explained, see above, {{GHGpar|86|i}}.—{{GHGheb|text=חֲשׂוּפַי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=20|verse=4}} (where the right reading is certainly {{GHGheb|text=חֲשׂוּפֵי}}) must be intended by the Masora either as a singular with the formative syllable {{GHGheb|text=־ַי}} =''bareness'' or, more probably, as a constr. st. with the original termination ''ay'' (cf. {{GHGpar|89|d}}) to avoid the harsh combination ''h<sup>a</sup>sûfê šēt''<ref>Prätorius, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1903, p. 525, regards {{GHGheb|text=הֲשׂוּפַי}} as an instance of the affix of endearment (cf. {{GHGheb|text=אֲחוּמַי}}, {{GHGheb|text=כְּלוּבַי}}) transferred to an appellative, but such an explanation is rendered unlikely by the meaning of this isolated instance.</ref>; in {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנָי|translate=the Lord}} (prop. ''my lord'', from the plur. ''majestatis'', {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנִים|translate=lord}}), the ''ay'' was originally a ''suffix'', {{GHGpar|135|q}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|h}}
(''d'') {{GHGheb|text=־ָם}} a supposed ''plural'' ending in {{GHGheb|text=כִּנָּם}}={{GHGheb|text=כִּנִּים|translate=gnats}} (or ''lice''), and {{GHGheb|text=סֻלָּם|translate=ladder}} (supposed by some to be a plur. like our ''stairs''); but cf. on the former, {{GHGpar|85|t}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|i}}
'''2.''' The plural termination of the ''feminine gender'' is generally indicated by the termination {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} (often written defectively {{GHGheb|text=־תֹ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תְּהִלָּה|translate=song of praise, psalm}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=תְּהִלּוֹת}} (only in post-biblical Hebrew<section end=par87 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

267.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par87 />{{GHGheb|text=תְּחִלִּים}}, as in the headings of the printed editions, as well as {{GHGheb|text=סֵ֫פֶר תְּהִלּוֹת|translate=the Book of Psalms}}); {{GHGheb|text=אִגֶּ֫רֶת|translate=a letter}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=אִנְּרוֹת}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּאֵר|translate=a well}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=בְּאֵרוֹת}}. Feminines in {{GHGheb|text=־ִית}} form their plural in {{GHGheb|text=־ִיּוֹת}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מִצְרִית|translate=an Egyptian woman}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=מִצְרִיּוֹת}}; and those in {{GHGheb|text=וּת}} either make {{GHGheb|text=־ֻיּוֹת}}, as {{GHGheb|text=מַלְכוּת|translate=kingdom}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=מַלְכֻיּוֹת}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=8|verse=22}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=חֲנֻיּוֹת|translate=cells}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=37|verse=16}}), or are inflected like {{GHGheb|text=עֵֽדְוֹת|translate=testimonies}} (pronounced ''‛ēdh<sup>e</sup>wôth'' for ''‛ēdhŭwôth'').

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|k}}
It is only from a mistake or disregard of these feminine endings {{GHGheb|text=־וּת}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ִית}} that some words ending with them form their plural by the addition of {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}} or {{GHGheb|text=־וֹת}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חֲנִית|translate=spear}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=חֲנִיתִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=חֲנִיתוֹת}}; {{GHGheb|text=זְנוּת|translate=whoredom}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=זְנוּתִים}} (by the side of {{GHGheb|text=זְנוּנִים}}); {{GHGheb|text=אַלְמְנוּתִים|translate=widowhood}}; {{GHGheb|text=שְׁחִיתוֹת|translate=pits}}, {{GHGheb|text=כְּסָתוֹת|translate=amulets}} (if connected with Assyr. ''kâsu'', ''to bind''), &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|l}}
The termination -''ôth'' stands primarily for -''âth'' (which is the form it has in Arab., Eth., in the ''constr. st''. of Western Aramaic, in Eastern Syriac, and also in Assyrian; on the change of ''â'' into an obscure ''ô'', see {{GHGpar|9|q}}). On the other hand, it is doubtful whether this ''âth'' is to be regarded as a lengthened and stronger form of the singular fem. ending ''ăth'' (cf. {{GHGpar|80|b}}).

How the changeable vowels of a noun are shortened or become {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} in consequence of the addition of the plural endings is explained in §§ 92–5.

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|m}}
'''3.''' Words which in the singular are used both as masculine and feminine ({{GHGpar|122|d}}), often have in the plural parallel forms with the masculine and feminine terminations, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עָב|translate=cloud}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=עָבִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=עָבוֹת}}; and each form may be treated either as masculine or feminine, according to the usage of the particular word.—But even those words, of which the gender is invariable, sometimes have both plural forms, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=דּוֹר}} masc. ''a generation'', plur. {{GHGheb|text=דּוֹרִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=דּוֹרוֹת}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנָה}} fem. ''a year'', plur. {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנוֹת}} (see the Rem.). In these words the gender of both plural forms remains the same as in the singular, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֲרִי}} masc. ''a lion'', plur. {{GHGheb|text=אֲרָיוֹת}} musc., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=3|verse=3}}, {{GHGheb|text=דּוֹרוֹת}} musc., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=42|verse=16}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|n}}
Sometimes usage makes a distinction between the two plural forms of the same word. Thus, {{GHGheb|text=יָמִים|translate=days}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנִים|translate=years}} are the usual, but {{GHGheb|text=יָמוֹת}} (only twice, in the ''constr. st''. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=90|verse=15}}) and {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנוֹת}} (also only in the ''constr. st''. and before suffixes) are rarer poetic forms.

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|o}}
A difference of meaning appears in several names of members of the body, the dual (see § 88) denoting the living members themselves, while the plur. in {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} expresses something like them, but without life ({{GHGpar|122|u}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יָדַ֫יִם|translate=hands}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָדוֹת|translate=artificial hands}}, also e.g. the ''arms'' of a throne; {{GHGheb|text=כַּפַּ֫יִם|translate=hands}}, {{GHGheb|text=כַּפּוֹת|translate=handles}} (Lat.
