2. Unusual forms (but for the most part probably only scribal errors) are—''Sing.'' 2nd pers. ''fem'' {{GHGheb|text=־ֵיךְ}} (after {{GHGheb|text=אַשְׁרֵי|translate=happy!}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=10|verse=17}}, which has become stereotyped as an interjection, and is therefore unchangeable; cf. Delitzsch on the passage); {{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫ יְכִי}} (cf. Syr. {{GHGheb|text=־ֵכי}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=4|verse=3}}, and <sup>7</sup> in {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=103|verse=3–5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=116|verse=7|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=־ָ֫ יְכִי}} in {{GHGterm|pause}}).—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=31}} {{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫ יִךְ}} (so {{GHGheb|text=־ֵיכֶם}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=6|verse=8|hidebook=1}}) occurs with an ''infin.'' ending in {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}}, the {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} being therefore treated as a plural ending; similarly, the plural suffix is sometimes found with the feminine ending {{GHGheb|text=וּת}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=54|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=23|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, as well as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=20|hidebook=1}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=3|verse=20}}), with the ending ''îth'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=24}}, reading {{GHGheb|text=חֲמִֽשִׁתוֹ}}), and even with the ordinary feminine ending ''ath''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=35|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=9|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=9|verse=15}}.—Wholly abnormal is {{GHGheb|text=מַלְאָכֵ֫כֵה|translate=thy messengers}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=2|verse=14}}, evidently a case of dittography of the following {{GHGheb|text=ה}}: read {{GHGheb|text=מַלְאָכַ֫יִךְ}}.

''3rd masc.'' {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ יהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=3|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=23}}; {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=30|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=43|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=2|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=וֹ֫הִי}} (a purely Aramaic form) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=116|verse=12}}.—''3rd fem.'' {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ יהָא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=41|verse=15}}.

''Plur.'' The strange ''2nd pers. masc.'' {{GHGheb|text=תְּפוֹצֽוֹתִיכֶם}} (with ''î'', so Qimḥi; cf. Norzi) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=25|verse=34}}, is probably a mixed form combining {{GHGheb|text=תָּפ֫וּצוּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=הֲפִיצֽוֹתִיכֶם}}; {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=־ֵיכֶ֫נָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=20}}.

''3rd masc.'' {{GHGheb|text=־ֵיהֵ֫מָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=40|verse=16}}; {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=־ֵיהֶ֫נָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=1|verse=11}}.

3. The termination {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫מוֹ}} (also with the ''dual'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=58|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=59|verse=13|hidebook=1}}), like {{GHGheb|text=מוֹ}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ָ֫ מוֹ}}, occurs with the noun (as with the verb, {{GHGpar|58|g}}) almost exclusively in the later poets [viz. with a substantive in the singular, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=21|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=17|verse=10.10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=58|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=59|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=89|verse=18|hidebook=1}}; with a dual or plural, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=27.32.37.38}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=33|verse=29|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=3.3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=11|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=49|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=58|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=59|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=5.7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=83|verse=12.12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=140|verse=4.10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=23}}; after prepositions, see {{GHGpar|103|f}}, o, notes], and cannot, therefore, by itself be taken as an indication of archaic language. On the other hand there can be no doubt that these are revivals of really old forms. That they are consciously and artificially used is shown by the evidently intentional accumulation of them, e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=5.7.9}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=3.5}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=140|verse=4.10|hidebook=1}}, and also by the fact observed by Diehl (see the heading of this section) that in Ex 15 they occur ''only'' as verbal suffixes, in Dt 32 ''only'' as noun suffixes.

{{GHGmargin-letter|91|m}}
'''3.''' It is clear and beyond doubt that the {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} in these suffixes with the plural noun belongs, in reality, to the ending of the {{GHGterm|construct state}} of the masculine plural. Yet the consciousness of this fact became so completely lost as to admit of the striking peculiarity (or rather inaccuracy) of appending those ''suffix''-forms which include the plural ending {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}}, even to the feminine plural in {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} ({{GHGheb|text=סֽוּסוֹתֵ֫ינוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=סֽוּסוֹתֶ֫יךָ}}, &c.), so that in reality the result is a double indication of the plural.<ref>See an analogous case in {{GHGpar|87|s}}. Cf. also the double feminine ending in the ''3rd sing. perf.'' of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, {{GHGpar|75|i}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|91|n}}
Such is the rule: the singular suffix, however (see b), also occurs with the ending {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} (probably through the influence of Aramaic), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=צֵֽדְוֹתִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=132|verse=12}} (unless it be ''sing.'' for {{GHGheb|text=עֵֽדוּתִי}}, as, according to Qimḥi in his Lexicon, {{GHGheb|text=תַּֽחֲנֹתִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=6|verse=8}} is for {{GHGheb|text=תַּֽחֲנוּתִי}}); {{GHGheb|text=מַכֹּֽתְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=59}} (treated on the analogy of an ''infin.'' {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}});<section end=par91 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

283.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par91 />{{GHGheb|text=אַֽחֲיוֹתֵךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=52}}. On the other hand {{GHGheb|text=מִצְוֹתֶ֑ךָ}} (so Baer, Ginsb.; but Opit. {{GHGheb|text=־ֶ֫ יךָ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=98}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=9|verse=5}} is merely written defectively, like {{GHGheb|text=גַּרְגְּרֹתֶ֫ךָ}} according to Baer (not Ginsb.) in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=9}}, &c. In the ''3rd plur.'' the use of the singular suffix is even the rule in the earlier Books (see the instances in Diehl, l. c., p. 8), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֲבוֹתָם}} (''their fathers'') oftener than {{GHGheb|text=אֲבֹֽתֵיהֶם}} (this only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=15}}, and in Jer, Ezr, Neh, and Ch [in 1 K, Jer, Ezr, however, {{GHGheb|text=אֲבוֹתָם}} is more common]); so always {{GHGheb|text=שְׁמוֹתָם}}, {{GHGheb|text=שְׁמוֹתָן|translate=their names}}, {{GHGheb|text=דּוֹרותָם|translate=their generations}}. From parallel passages like {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=22|verse=46}} compared with {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=46}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=2|verse=4}} with {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=4|verse=3}}, it appears that in many cases the longer form in {{GHGheb|text=־ֵיהֶם}} can only subsequently have taken the place of {{GHGheb|text=־ָם}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|91|o}}
'''4.''' The following Paradigm of a masculine and feminine noun with suffixes is based upon a monosyllabic noun with one unchangeable vowel. With regard to the ending {{GHGheb|text=־ַת}} in the ''constr. st.'' of the fem. it should be further remarked that the short ''ă'' of this ending is only retained before the ''grave'' suffixes {{GHGheb|text=כֶם}} and {{GHGheb|text=כֶן}}; before all the others (the ''light'' suffixes) it is lengthened to ''ā''.

284.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="65.78.5.191" /></noinclude><section begin="par92" />{{GHGpar-heading|92|Vowel Changes in the Noun}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|92|a}}
'''1.''' Vowel changes in the noun may be caused (''a'') by dependence on a following genitive, (''b'') by connexion with pronominal suffixes, (''c'') by the plural and dual terminations, whether in the form of the absolute state or of the construct (before a following genitive of a noun or suffix).

{{GHGmargin-letter|92|b}}
'''2.''' In all these cases, the tone of the noun is moved forward either one or two syllables, while the tone of the {{GHGterm|construct state}} may even be thrown upon the following word. In this way the following changes may arise:—

(''a'') ''When the tone is moved forward only one place'', as is the case when the plural and dual endings {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫ יִם}} are affixed, as well as with all monosyllabic or paroxytone suffixes, then in dissyllabic nouns the originally short vowel of the first syllable (which was lengthened as being in an open syllable before the tone) becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, since it no longer stands before the tone. On the other hand, the originally short, but tone-lengthened vowel, of the second syllable is retained as being now the pretonic vowel; e.g. {{GHGheb|text=דָּבָר|translate=word}} (ground-form ''dăbăr''), plur. {{GHGheb|text=דְּבָרִים}}; with a light suffix beginning with a vowel, {{GHGheb|text=דְּבָרִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=דְּבָרֵ֫נוּ}}; plur. {{GHGheb|text=דְּבָרַי}}, {{GHGheb|text=דְּבָרֶ֫יךָ}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=בָּנָף|translate=wing}}, dual {{GHGheb|text=כְּנָפַ֫יִם}}. With an unchangeable vowel in the second syllable: {{GHGheb|text=פָּקִיד|translate=overseer}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=פְּקִידִים}}; with the ''suffix'' of the sing. {{GHGheb|text=פְּקִידִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=פְּקִידֵ֫נוּ}}, &c.; with the ''suff.'' of the plur. {{GHGheb|text=פְּקִידַי}}, {{GHGheb|text=פְּקִידֶ֫יךָ}}, &c. With an unchangeable vowel in the first syllable: {{GHGheb|text=עוֹלָם|translate=eternity}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=עֽוֹלָמִים}}, with ''suff.'' {{GHGheb|text=עֽוֹלָמִי}}, &c.<ref>The participles {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נִדַּֽחֲךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=30|verse=4}}, {{GHGheb|text=נִדְּחוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=13}}, and some plurals of the participle Niph. of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}} form an exception; cf. {{GHGpar|93|oo}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|92|c}}
But in participles of the form {{GHGheb|text=קֹטֵל}}, with tone-lengthened ''ē'' (originally ''ĭ'') in the second syllable, the ''ē'' regularly becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ mobile}} before a tone-bearing affix, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֹיֵב|translate=enemy}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽיְבִים}}, with ''suff.'' {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽיְבִי}}, &c. Likewise in words of the form {{GHGheb|text=קִטֵּל}}, {{GHGheb|text=קַטֵּל}}, &c. (with ''ē'' in the second syllable; {{GHGpar|84|d|b}}, l, p; {{GHGpar|85|i}} and k), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אִלֵּם|translate=dumb}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=אִלְּמִים}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|92|d}}
(''b'') When the tone of the {{GHGterm|construct state}}, plural or dual, is carried over to the following word, or, in consequence of the addition of the ''grave suffixes'' to the ''constr. st.'' plur. or dual, ''is moved forward two places'' within the word itself, in such cases the originally short vowel of the second syllable becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, while the vowel of the first syllable reverts to its original shortness, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=דִּבְרֵי הָעָם|translate=the words of the people}}, {{GHGheb|text=דִּבְרֵיכֶ֫ם|translate=your words}}, {{GHGheb|text=דִּבְרֵיהֶ֫ם|translate=their words}} (in all which instances the ''ĭ'' of the first syllable is attenuated from an original ''ă'').
<section end="par92" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

285.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="65.78.5.191" /></noinclude><section begin="par92" />{{GHGmargin-letter|92|e}}
In the segholate forms in the singular and mostly in the dual the suffix is appended to the ground-form ({{GHGheb|text=מַלְכִּי|translate=my king}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַלְכֵּ֫נוּ}}, &c.); on the other hand, before the endings {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} (sometimes also before {{GHGheb|text=־ַ֫ יִם}}) a ''Qames'' regularly occurs,<ref>For the rare exceptions see {{GHGpar|93|l}} and {{GHGpar|97|f}}, note 2.</ref> before which the vowel of the first syllable then becomes vocal {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} ({{GHGheb|text=מְלָכִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְלָכוֹת}}). This {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} (on which cf. {{GHGpar|84|a|a}}) remains even before the light suffixes, when attached to the plur. masc. ({{GHGheb|text=מְלָכַי}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְלָכֶ֫יךָ}}, &c.). On the other hand, the ''constr. st.'' plur. and dual, regularly, according to ''d'', has the form {{GHGheb|text=מַלְכֵי}}, with grave suffix {{GHGheb|text=מַלְכֵיכֶם}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=דַּלְתֵי}} from {{GHGheb|text=דְּלָתַ֫יִם|translate=folding-doors}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|92|f}}
(''c'') Before the {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ mobile}} which precedes the suffix {{GHGheb|text=ךָ}} when following a consonant, the ''a''-sound, as a rule, is the only tone-lengthened vowel which remains in the final syllable (being now in an open syllable ''before'' the tone), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=דָּֽמְךָ֫}}, {{GHGheb|text=דְּבָֽרְךָ֫}}, &c. (on the forms with ''ē'' in the second syllable, see {{GHGpar|93|qq}}); but before the grave suffixes {{GHGheb|text=־ְכֶם}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ְכֶן}} in the same position it reverts to its original shortness, as {{GHGheb|text=דְּבַרְכֶם}} (''d<sup>e</sup>bhărkhèm''), &c. In the same way the tone-lengthened ''ā'' or ''ē'' of the second syllable in the ''constr. st.'' sing. also becomes short again, since the ''constr. st.'' resigns the principal tone to the following word, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=דְּבַר אֱלֹהִים}}; {{GHGheb|text=חֲצַר הַבַּ֫יִת}} (from {{GHGheb|text=חָצֵר}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|92|g}}
Rem. The Masora (cf. ''Diqduqe ha-ṭ<sup>e</sup>amim'', p. 37) reckons thirteen words which retain {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} in the ''constr. st.'', some of which had originally ''â'' and therefore need not be considered. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=אוּלָם}} or {{GHGheb|text=אֻלָם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=7|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=40|verse=48}}, &c. (in spite of the ''constr. st.'' plur. {{GHGheb|text=אֻֽלַמֵּי}}); {{GHGheb|text=מִבְטָח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=65|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=מַצָּב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=23}} (so Baer, but ed. Mant., Ginsburg, &c. {{GHGheb|text=מַצַּב}}); {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁקָל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=8|verse=30}} and {{GHGheb|text=מַתָּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=18|verse=16}} are very peculiar.

{{GHGmargin-letter|92|h}}
'''3.''' The vowel changes in the inflexion of ''feminine nouns'' (§ 95) are not so considerable, since generally in the formation of the feminine either the original vowels have been retained, or they have already become {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|92|i}}
Besides the vowel changes discussed above in ''a–g'', which take place according to the general formative laws (§§ 25–28), certain further phenomena must also be considered in the inflexion of nouns, an accurate knowledge of which requires in each case an investigation of the original form of the words in question (see §§ 84–86). Such are, e.g., the rejection of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} of {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} stems before all formative additions (cf. {{GHGpar|91|d}}), the sharpening of the final consonant of {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} stems in such cases as {{GHGheb|text=חֹק}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֻקִּי}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|92|k}}
A striking difference between the vowel changes in the verb and noun is that in a verb when terminations are added it is mostly the second of two changeable vowels which becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} ({{GHGheb|text=קָטַל}}, {{GHGheb|text=קָֽטְלָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=קָֽטְלוּ}}), but in a noun, the first ({{GHGheb|text=דָּבָר}}, {{GHGheb|text=דְּבָרִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=דְּבָרִים}}), cf. § 27. 3.<section end="par92" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

286.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par93 />{{GHGpar-heading|93|Paradigms of Masculine Nouns||<ref>A sort of detailed commentary on the following scheme of Hebrew declensions is supplied by E. König in his {{GHGcite|title=Hist.-krit. Lehrgeb. der hebr. Spr.}}, it. 1, p. 1 ff.</ref>}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|a}}
Masculine nouns from the simple stem may, as regards their form and the vowel changes connected with it, be divided into ''four'' classes. A synopsis of them is given on pp. {{GHGpage|264}}, {{GHGpage|265}}, and they are further explained below. Two general remarks may be premised:

(''a'') That all feminines without a distinctive termination ({{GHGpar|122|h}}) are treated like these masculine nouns, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חֶ֫רֶב}} {{GHGterm|f.}} {{GHGtranslate|sword}}, like {{GHGheb|text=מֶ֫לֶךְ}} {{GHGterm|m.}} {{GHGtranslate|king}}, except that in the {{GHGterm|plural}} they usually take the termination {{GHGheb|text=־וֹת}}; thus {{GHGheb|text=חֲרָבוֹת}}, {{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=חַרְבוֹת}} (and so always before {{GHGterm|suffixes}}, see {{GHGpar|95}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|b}}
(''b'') That in the plural of the first three classes a changeable vowel is always retained even before the light suffixes as a lengthened pretonic vowel, whenever it also stands before the plural ending {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}}. All suffixes, except {{GHGheb|text=כֶם}}, {{GHGheb|text=כֶן}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֶם}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֶן}} ({{GHGheb|text=־ֵיכֶם}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ֵיכֶן}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ֵיהֶם}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ֵיהֶן}}), are called {{GHGterm|light}}. Cf. {{GHGpar|92|e}}.

{{center|''Explanations of the Paradigms (see pp. {{GHGpage|264}}, {{GHGpage|265}}).''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|c}}
'''1.''' Paradigm I comprises the large class of {{GHGterm|segholate}} nouns ({{GHGpar|84|a|a}}–{{GHGpar|84|a|a|nonumber=1}}). In the first three examples, from a strong stem, the ground-forms, {{GHGpron|mălk}}, {{GHGpron|sĭphr}}, {{GHGpron|qŭdš}} have been developed by the adoption of a helping {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} to {{GHGheb|text=מֶ֫לֶךְ}} (with ''ă'' modified to ''è''), {{GHGheb|text=סֵ֫פֶר}} (''ĭ'' lengthened to ''ē''), {{GHGheb|text=קֹ֫דֶשׁ}} (''ŭ'' lengthened to ''ō'').<ref>According to P. Haupt ‘The book of Nahum’ in the {{GHGcite|title=Journ. of bibl. Lit.}}, 1907, p. 29, the ''e'' in {{GHGheb|text=סֵ֫פֶר}} and the ''o'' in {{GHGheb|text=קֹ֫דֶשׁ}} are not long but accented, and hence to be pronounced {{polytonic|σέφρ}}, {{polytonic|ὄζν}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֹ֫זֶן}}), a theory unknown at any rate to the Jewish grammarians.</ref> The next three examples, instead of the helping {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, have a helping {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}}, on account of the middle (''d, f'') or final guttural (''e''). In all these cases the {{GHGterm|constr. st. sing.}} coincides exactly with the {{GHGterm|absolute}}. The singular suffixes are added to the ground-form; but in ''c'' and ''f'' an ''ŏ'' takes the place of the original ''ŭ'', and in ''d'' and ''f'' the guttural requires a repetition of the ''ă'' and ''ŏ'' in the form of a {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph}} ({{GHGheb|text=נַֽעֲרִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=פָּֽעֳלִי}}); before a following {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} this {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph}} passes into a simple helping vowel (''ă'', ''ŏ''), according to {{GHGpar|28|c}}; hence {{GHGheb|text=נַֽעַרְךָ}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|d}}
In the plural an ''a''-sound almost always appears before the tone-bearing affix {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}} (on the analogy of forms with original ''a'' in the<section end=par93 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

287.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par93 />second syllable; cf. {{GHGpar|84|a|a}}), in the form of a pretonic {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}}, whilst the short vowel of the first syllable becomes vocal {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}. The original ''a'' of the 2nd syllable is elided in the {{GHGterm|construct state}}, so that the short vowel under the first radical then stands in a closed syllable. The omission of {{GHGterm|Dageš}} in a following {{GHGterm|Begadkephath}} ({{GHGheb|text=מַלְכֵי}}, not {{GHGheb|text=מַלְכֵּי}}, &c.) is due to the loss of a vowel between {{GHGheb|text=ל}} and {{GHGheb|text=כ‍}}. On the other hand, the pretonic {{GHGterm|Qames}} of the {{GHGterm|absolute state}} is retained before the light plural suffixes, whilst the grave suffixes are added to the form of the {{GHGterm|construct state}}.—The ending of the {{GHGterm|absolute state}} of the dual is added, as a rule, to the ground-form (so in ''a–d'' and ''h'', but cf. ''k''). The {{GHGterm|construct state}} of the dual is generally the same as that of the plural, except, of course, in cases like ''m''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|e}}
Paradigms ''g'' and ''h'' exhibit forms with middle ''u'' and ''i'' ({{GHGpar|84|c|a}}, γ and δ); the ground forms {{GHGpron|maut}} and {{GHGpron|zait}} are always contracted to {{GHGpron|môth}}, {{GHGpron|zêth}}, except in the {{GHGpron|absol. sing.}}, where ''u'' and ''i'' are changed into the corresponding consonants {{GHGheb|text=ו}} and {{GHGheb|text=י}}.

Paradigm ''i'' exhibits one of the numerous forms in which the contraction of a middle ''u'' or ''i'' has already taken place in the {{GHGterm|absol. sing.}} (ground-form {{GHGterm|šauṭ}}).

Paradigm ''k'' is a formation from a stem {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} ({{GHGpar|84|c|a}}, ε).

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|f}}
Paradigms ''l'', ''m'', ''n'' are forms from stems {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, and hence (see {{GHGpar|67|a}}) originally biliteral, {{GHGpron|yam}}, {{GHGpron|ʾim}}, {{GHGpron|ḥuq}}, with the regular lengthening to {{GHGheb|text=יָם}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֵם}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֹק}}. Before formative additions a sharpening, as in the inflexion of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, takes place in the second radical, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אִמִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַמִּים}}, &c. (see {{GHGpar|84|c|a}}, β).

{{center|{{Small-caps|Remarks.}}}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|g}}
1. A. On I. ''a'' and ''d'' (ground-form {{GHGpron|qaṭl}}). In {{GHGterm|pause}} the full lengthening to ''ā'' generally takes place, thus {{GHGheb|text=כָּ֫רֶם|translate=vineyard}}, {{GHGheb|text=נָ֫עַר}}, {{GHGheb|text=זָ֫רַע|translate=seed}} (from {{GHGheb|text=זֶ֫רַע}}), and so always (except {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=48|verse=11}}), in {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫רֶץ|translate=earth}} with the article, {{GHGheb|text=הָאָ֫רֶץ}}, according to {{GHGpar|35|o}} (cf. also in the LXX the forms {{polytonic|Ἀβέλ}}, {{polytonic|Ἰαφέθ}} for {{GHGheb|text=הֶ֫בֶל}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֶ֫פֶת}}). However, the form with ''è'' is also sometimes found in pause, along with that in ''ā'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חֶ֫סֶד}} together with {{GHGheb|text=חָ֫סֶד}}; and very frequently only the form with {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מֶ֫לֶךְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=דֶּ֫שֶׁא|translate=grass}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫צַח|translate=perpetuity}}, {{GHGheb|text=פֶּ֫לֶא|translate=a wonder}}, {{GHGheb|text=צֶ֫דֶק|translate=righteousness}}, {{GHGheb|text=קֶ֫דֶם|translate=the East}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֶ֫שַׁע|translate=help}}, &c.—With two {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôls}}, although with a middle guttural, we find {{GHGheb|text=לֶ֫חֶם|translate=bread}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=לָ֫חֶם}}) and {{GHGheb|text=רֶ֫חֶם|translate=womb}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=רָ֫חֶם}}), besides {{GHGheb|text=רַ֫חַם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=30}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=רָ֫חַם}}). A helping {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} always stands before a final {{GHGheb|text=א}}, as {{GHGheb|text=דֶּ֫שֶׁא}}, {{GHGheb|text=טֶ֫נֶא}} (with {{GHGterm|suff.}} {{GHGheb|text=טַנְאֲךָ}}), {{GHGheb|text=פֶּ֫לֶא}}, {{GHGheb|text=פֶּ֫רֶא}} (also written {{GHGheb|text=פֶּ֫רֶה}}), except in {{GHGheb|text=גַּיְא}}, see ''v''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|h}}
B. The {{GHGterm|constr. st.}} is almost always the same as the {{GHGterm|absolute}}. Sometimes, however, under the influence of a final guttural or {{GHGheb|text=ר}}, Pathaḥ appears in the second syllable as the principal vowel (see below, {{GHGpar|93|s}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גְּבַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=26}}; {{GHGheb|text=זְרַע}}<section end=par93 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
