290.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par93 />(only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=7}}, before Maqqeph), {{GHGheb|text=חֲדַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=3|verse=24}} (but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=3|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=חֶ֫דֶר}}), {{GHGheb|text=נְטַע}}, {{GHGheb|text=סְחַר}} as well as {{GHGheb|text=זֶ֫רַע}}, &c.; cf., moreover, {{GHGheb|text=קְחַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=12|verse=9}} (for {{GHGheb|text=קַ֫חַת}}, {{GHGterm|infin. constr.}} from {{GHGheb|text=לָקַח}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|i}}
C. The {{GHGheb|text=־ָה|translate=locale}} is, according to {{GHGpar|90|i}}, regularly added to the already developed form, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫גְדָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=116|verse=14.18}}: {{GHGheb|text=הַפֶּ֑תְחָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=6}}, {{GHGtranslate|to the door}}; but also with a firmly closed syllable {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫גְבָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=40|verse=24}}; under the influence of a guttural or {{GHGheb|text=ר}}, {{GHGheb|text=חַ֫דְרָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַ֫רְצָה}}, in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=אָ֫רְצָה}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=גָּ֫זְרָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=14|verse=16}}, from {{GHGheb|text=גֶּ֫זֶר}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|k}}
D. The suffixes of the singular are likewise added to the ground-form, but forms with middle guttural take {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Pathaḥ}} instead of the {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ quiescens}}; {{GHGheb|text=נַֽעֲרִי}}, &c. (but also {{GHGheb|text=לַחְמִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=זַעְמִי}}, &c.). In a rather large number of {{GHGpron|qăṭl}}-forms, however, before suffixes in the sing., as well as in the {{GHGterm|constr. st.}} plur. and dual, the ''ă'' of the first syllable is attenuated to ''ĭ'',<ref>According to M. Lambert, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} 1896, p. 21, ''a'' tends to remain with labials; so in 14 cases out of 22 masculines, and in 3 out of 6 feminines.</ref> thus {{GHGheb|text=בִּטְנִי|translate=my womb}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִתְרוֹ}}; so in {{GHGheb|text=בֶּ֫גֶד}}, {{GHGheb|text=בֶּ֫צַע}}, {{GHGheb|text=גֶּ֫זַע}}, {{GHGheb|text=זֶ֫בַח}}, {{GHGheb|text=טֶ֫בַח}}, {{GHGheb|text=פֶּ֫שַׁע}}, {{GHGheb|text=פֶּ֫תַח}}, {{GHGheb|text=צֶ֫דֶק}}, {{GHGheb|text=קֶ֫בֶר}}, {{GHGheb|text=קֶ֫רֶב}}, {{GHGheb|text=רֶ֫שַׁע}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫מֶשׁ}}, and many others. In some cases of this kind besides the form with ''ă'' there most probably existed another with original ''ĭ'' in the first syllable; thus certainly with {{GHGheb|text=יֵ֫שַׁע}} beside {{GHGheb|text=יֶ֫שַׁע}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֵ֫צַח}} beside {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫צַ֫ח}}, &c. (According to the {{GHGcite|title=Diqduqe ha-ṭ<sup>e</sup>amim}}, § 36, the {{GHGterm|absolute st.}} in such cases takes ''è'', the {{GHGterm|constr. ē}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫דֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=30|verse=4}} ({{GHGterm|absol.}}) and {{GHGheb|text=נֵ֫דֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=30|verse=10|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGterm|constr.}}); {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫בֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=24|verse=20}} ({{GHGterm|absol.}}) and {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁ֫בֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=6|verse=6}} ({{GHGterm|constr.}}). According to this theory<ref>Probably only a theory of one particular school and not generally accepted, or at any rate not consistently carried out; cf. König, {{GHGcite|title=Lehrgeb.}}, ii. 22.</ref> {{GHGheb|text=פֵּ֫לֶא}} (so the best authorities) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=9|verse=5}} would be the {{GHGterm|constr. st.}}, although the accentuation requires an {{GHGterm|absol. st.}})—A weakening of the firmly closed syllable occurs in {{GHGheb|text=בִּגְדִי}}, &c. from {{GHGheb|text=בֶּ֫גֶד}} and {{GHGheb|text=יִקְבֶ֫ךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=15|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=16|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, in both cases evidently owing to the influence of the palatal in the middle of the stem. With {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} for ''ĭ'': {{GHGheb|text=הֶבְלִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֶשְׁעֲךָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֶגְדִּי}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|l}}
E. In the plural the termination {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} is found as well as {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נְפָשׁוֹת}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֲצָמוֹת}} together with {{GHGheb|text=נְפָשִׁים}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=20}} [but read {{GHGheb|text=חָפְשִׁים}}; see comm.]), &c., {{GHGterm|constr. st.}} {{GHGheb|text=נַפְשׁוֹת}}. Other nouns have only the ending {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֲרָצוֹת}}, {{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=אַרְצוֹת}} from {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫רֶץ}}. Without {{GHGterm|Qaṃeṣ}} before the ending {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}} we find {{GHGheb|text=רַֽחֲמִים|translate={{normal|(}}bowels{{normal|)}} mercy}}. On the numerals {{GHGheb|text=עֶשְׂרִים|translate=twenty}}, &c., cf. {{GHGpar|97|f}}, note 2. Moreover ''a'' is not inserted before plural suffixes with the tone on the penultima in {{GHGheb|text=אַשְׁרֶ֫יךָ}}, &c., properly {{GHGtranslate|thy happiness!}} (a word which is only used in the {{GHGterm|constr. st. pl.}} and at an early period became stereotyped as a kind of interjection).

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|m}}
F. In the {{GHGterm|constr. st. plural}} a firmly closed syllable is sometimes found, contrary to the rule, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כַּסְפֵּיהֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=25.35}}; {{GHGheb|text=רִשְׁפֵּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=8|verse=6}} ({{GHGheb|text=רִשְׁפֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=76|verse=4}}); {{GHGheb|text=טַרְפֵּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=17|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=צִמְדֵּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=10}}, and so always in {{GHGheb|text=נִסְכֵּיכֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=29|verse=39}}, {{GHGheb|text=נִסְכֵּיהֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=16|verse=4}}, &c. (on the other hand, according to the best authorities ''not'' in {{GHGheb|text=חַסְדֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=55|verse=3}}, &c., though in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=107|verse=43}} Ginsburg reads {{GHGheb|text=חַסְדֵּי}}); cf. {{GHGpar|46|d}}. Even with a middle guttural {{GHGheb|text=בַּעְלֵיהֶן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=1|verse=17.20}}.—The attenuation of ''ă'' to ''ĭ'' also occurs sometimes in this form (see above, {{GHGpar|93|k|nonumber=1}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=זִבְחֵי}}, &c., even {{GHGheb|text=יִלְדֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=57|verse=4}} beside {{GHGheb|text=יַלְדֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=1|verse=2}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|n}}
G. In the {{GHGterm|dual absol.}} beside forms like {{GHGheb|text=רַגְלַ֫יִם|translate=feet}}, with suff. {{GHGheb|text=רַגְלֶ֫יךָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=רַגְלָיו}}, &c. {{GHGheb|text=אַלְפַּ֫יִם|translate=two thousand}}, {{GHGheb|text=נַֽעֲלַ֫יִם|translate=sandals}}, {{GHGheb|text=בִּרְכַּ֫יִם|translate=knees}} (''ă'' attenuated to ''ĭ'', {{GHGterm|constr. st.}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּרְכֵּי}} with a firmly closed syllable), with suffixes {{GHGheb|text=בִּרְכַּי}}, &c. (cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=בִּרְכֵיהֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=7|verse=6}}), forms with pretonic {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} are also found (in consequence of the<section end=par93 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

291.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par93" />tendency to assimilate the dual to the plural in form: so König, {{GHGcite|title=Lehrgeb.}}, ii. 17), as {{GHGheb|text=קְרָנַ֫יִם|translate=horns}}, with suff. {{GHGheb|text=קְרָנָיו}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=8|verse=3}} ff.; elsewhere always {{GHGheb|text=קַרְנַ֫יִם}}, {{GHGheb|text=קַרְנָיו}}, &c.), and so always {{GHGheb|text=דְּלָתַ֫יִם}}, {{GHGterm|constr. st.}} {{GHGheb|text=דַּלְתֵי|translate=folding-doors}}, {{GHGheb|text=דְּרָכַ֫יִם}} (?) {{GHGtranslate|double way}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|o}}
2. On Paradigms ''b'' and ''e''. With a final {{GHGheb|text=א}} rejected (but retained orthographically) we find {{GHGheb|text=חֵטְא|translate=sin}}. An initial guttural before suffixes generally receives {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} instead of the original ''ĭ'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חֶלְקִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֶזְרִי}}, &c., so in the {{GHGterm|constr. st. plur.}} {{GHGheb|text=עֶגְלֵי}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=חֵטְא}} forms {{GHGheb|text=חֲטָאֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=10|verse=29}}, &c., retaining the {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} of {{GHGheb|text=חֲטָאִים}} before the weak {{GHGheb|text=א}}.—The pausal forms {{GHGheb|text=סָ֫תֶר}} and {{GHGheb|text=שָׁ֫בֶט}} (out of pause always {{GHGheb|text=סֵ֫תֶר}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁ֫בֶט}}) go back to by-forms {{GHGheb|text=סֶ֫תֶר}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫בֶט}}.—On {{GHGheb|text=עִשְּׂבוֹת}} ({{GHGterm|constr. st.}} plur. of {{GHGheb|text=עֵ֫שֶׂב}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=27|verse=25}}, cf. {{GHGpar|20|h}}; {{GHGheb|text=שִׁקְמִים|translate=sycamores}}, without {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} before the termination {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}} (see above, {{GHGpar|93|l|nonumber=1}}), is probably from the sing. {{GHGheb|text=שִׁקְמָה}} found in the Mišna.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|p}}
3. On Paradigms ''c'' and ''f''. {{GHGheb|text=קשְׁטְ}} occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=22|verse=21}} without a helping vowel; with a middle guttural {{GHGheb|text=פֹּ֫עַל}}, &c., but with {{GHGheb|text=ה}} also {{GHGheb|text=אֹ֫הֶל}}, {{GHGheb|text=בֹּ֫הֶן}}; with a final guttural {{GHGheb|text=גֹּ֫בַהּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=רֹ֫בַע}} &c., but with {{GHGheb|text=א}}, {{GHGheb|text=גֹּ֫מֶא}}; with a firmly closed syllable {{GHGheb|text=אָסְפֵּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|q}}
Before suffixes the original ''ŭ'' sometimes reappears in the sing., e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גֻּדְלוֹ}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=150|verse=2}}) beside {{GHGheb|text=גָּדְלוֹ}}, from {{GHGheb|text=גֹּ֫דֶל|translate=greatness}}; {{GHGheb|text=סֻבֳּלוֹ}} (with {{GHGterm|Dageš forte dirimens}}, and the ''ŭ'' repeated in the form of a {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Qameṣ}}, cf. {{GHGpar|10|h}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=9|verse=3}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=גֻּשְׁמָהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=22|verse=24}}.—Corresponding to the form {{GHGheb|text=פָּֽעָלְכֶם}} {{GHGpron|pŏʿŏl<sup>e</sup>khèm}} we find {{GHGheb|text=קָֽטָבְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=13|verse=14}}, even without a middle guttural; similarly {{GHGheb|text=קָֽטֳנִי}} (so [[Author:Daniel Ernst Jablonsky|Jablonski]] and Opitius) {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=12|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=10|verse=10}}, from {{GHGheb|text=קֹ֫טֶן|translate=little finger}}; but the better reading is, no doubt, {{GHGheb|text=קָֽטָנִּי}} (so ed. Mant., ‘the {{GHGheb|text=ק}} proleptically assuming the vowel of the following syllable’; König, {{GHGcite|title=Lehrgeb.}}, ii. 69), and the form is to be derived, with König, from {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹן}}, not {{GHGpron|qŭtŭn}}, as Brockelmann quotes him, in {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, p. 103. The reading {{GHGheb|text=קָֽטֳנִּי}} (Baer and Ginsburg) is probably not due to a confusion of the above two readings, but {{GHGheb|text=־ֳ}} is merely intended to mark the vowel expressly as ''ŏ''. In the forms {{GHGheb|text=פֹּֽעֲלוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=31}} (for {{GHGheb|text=פָּֽעֳלוֹ}}) and {{GHGheb|text=תֹּֽאֲרוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=52|verse=14}} (for {{GHGheb|text=תָּֽאֳרוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=14}}), the lengthening of the original ''ŭ'' to ''ō'' has been retained even before the suffix; cf. {{GHGpar|63|p}} and {{GHGpar|74|h}} ({{GHGheb|text=בְּמֹצַֽאֲכֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=20}}).—In the same way ''ō'' remains before {{GHGheb|text=־ָה|translate=locale}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גּ֫ׄרְנָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָאֹהֱלָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=67|hidebook=1}}, &c. Dissimilation of the vowel (or a by-form {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫כַח}}?) seems to occur in {{GHGheb|text=נִכְחוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=14|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=46|verse=9}}, for {{GHGheb|text=נָכְחוֹ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|r}}
In the {{GHGterm|absol. st. plur.}} the original ''ŭ'' generally becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} before the {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בְּקָרִים}} from {{GHGheb|text=בֹּ֫קֶר|translate=morning}}, {{GHGheb|text=פְּעָלִים|translate=works}}, {{GHGheb|text=רְמָחִים|translate=lances}}, {{GHGheb|text=שְׁעָלִים|translate=handfuls}} ({{GHGterm|constr. st.}} {{GHGheb|text=שַֽׁעֲלֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=19}}); on the other hand, with an initial guttural the ''ŭ''-sound reappears as {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph Qameṣ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חֳדָשִׁים|translate=months}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֳפָרִים|translate=gazelles}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֳרָחוֹת|translate=ways}}; and so even without an initial guttural, {{GHGheb|text=הַגֳּרָנוֹת|translate=the threshing-floors}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=23|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=2|verse=24}}; {{GHGheb|text=קָֽדָשִׁים|translate=sanctuaries}}, and {{GHGheb|text=שָֽׁרָשִׁים|translate=roots}} ({{GHGterm|qŏdhāšîm}}, &c., with ''ŏ'' for {{GHGheb|text=־ֳ}}); also {{GHGheb|text=קָֽדָשַׁי}} [but {{GHGheb|text=קֳדָשֶׁ֫יךָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=קֳדָשָׁיו}}, once {{GHGheb|text=קָֽ׳}}], where, however, the reading frequently fluctuates between {{GHGheb|text=קָֽ׳}} and {{GHGheb|text=קֳ׳}}; with the article {{GHGheb|text=הַקֳּ׳}}, {{GHGheb|text=בַּקֳּ׳}}, {{GHGheb|text=לַקֳּ׳}}, according to Baer and Ginsburg. On these forms cf. especially {{GHGpar|9|v}}. From {{GHGheb|text=אֹ֫הֶל|translate=tent}}, both {{GHGheb|text=בָּֽאֳהָלִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽהָלִים}} (cf. {{GHGpar|23|h}} and {{GHGheb|text=פֹּֽעֲלוֹ}} above) are found; with light suffixes {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽהָלַי}}, &c.; so from {{GHGheb|text=אֹרַח|translate=way}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽרְחֹתָיו}} (also {{GHGheb|text=אָרְחֹתַי}})—hence only with initial {{GHGheb|text=א}}, ‘on account of its weak articulation’ (König, {{GHGcite|title=Lehrgeb.}}, ii. 45). It seems that by these different ways of writing a distinction was intended between the<section end="par93" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

292.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par93" />plural of {{GHGheb|text=אֹרְחָה|translate=caravan}}, and of {{GHGheb|text=אֹרַח|translate=way}}; however, {{GHGheb|text=אָרְחוֹת}} is also found in the former sense (in ''constr. st.'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=19}}) and {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽרְחוֹת}} in the latter (e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=27}} according to the reading of Ben Naphtali and Qimḥi); cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אֽוֹנִיּוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=8|verse=18}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֳנ׳}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}).—The ''constr. st.'' plural of {{GHGheb|text=בֹּ֫הֶן|translate=thumb}} is {{GHGheb|text=בְּהֹנוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=1|verse=6}} f., as if from a sing. {{GHGheb|text=בְּהֹן}}: of {{GHGheb|text=נׄ֫גַהּ|translate=brightness}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=נְגׄהוֹת}} (on these ''q<sup>e</sup>ṭōl''-forms, cf. t).—If {{GHGheb|text=אָפְנָיו}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=11}} is not dual but plural (see the Lexicon) it is then analogous to the examples, given in {{GHGpar|93|l|nonumber=1}} and {{GHGpar|93|0|nonumber=1}}, of plurals without a pretonic {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=בָּטְנִים|translate=pistachio nuts}}, probably from a sing. {{GHGheb|text=בָּטְנָה}}. According to Barth, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} xlii, 345 f. {{GHGheb|text=אָפְנָיו}} is a sing. ({{GHGheb|text=אָפְנַי}}, the ground-form of {{GHGheb|text=אָפְנֶה}}, with suffix).

In the ''constr. st. plur.'' the only example with original ''ŭ'' is {{GHGheb|text=רֻכְסֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=31|verse=21}}; otherwise like {{GHGheb|text=קָדְשֵׁי}}, {{GHGheb|text=אָֽהֳלֵי}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|s}}
4. Besides the forms treated hitherto we have to consider also a series of formations, which have their characteristic vowel under the ''second'' radical, as is ordinarily the case in Aramaic (on the origin of these forms see further, {{GHGpar|84|e|a}}). Thus (''a'') of the form {{GHGheb|text=קְטַל}}; {{GHGheb|text=דְּבַשׁ|translate=honey}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְעַט|translate=little}}; in {{GHGterm|pause}}, {{GHGheb|text=דְּבָשׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְעָט}}; {{GHGheb|text=גְּבַר|translate=man}} (as ''constr. st.'', see above, {{GHGpar|93|h|nonumber=1}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=26}} (elsewhere always {{GHGheb|text=גֶּ֫בֶר}}), and ''infinitives'' like {{GHGheb|text=שְׁכַב}} ({{GHGpar|45|c}}; on {{GHGheb|text=קְחַת}}, see above, h); {{GHGheb|text=שְׁכֶם|translate=shoulder}}, ''ă'' being modified to ''è'' (but in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫כֶם}}); locative {{GHGheb|text=שְׁכֶ֫מָה}}, also {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫כְמָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=6|verse=9}}. With suffixes in the usual manner {{GHGheb|text=שִׁכְמִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁכְבָהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=33.35}} (an infin. with suffix, therefore not {{GHGheb|text=שִׁכְבָּהּ}}). On the other hand, the ''ă'' is retained in the ''plur. absol.'' by sharpening the final consonant: {{GHGheb|text=אֲגַמִּים}} ({{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=אַגְמֵי}}) ''marshes'', {{GHGheb|text=הֲדַסִּים|translate=myrtles}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְעַטִּים|translate=few}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|t}}
(''b'') Of the form {{GHGheb|text=קְטֵל}}: {{GHGheb|text=בְּאֵר|translate=a well}}, {{GHGheb|text=זְאֵב|translate=wolf}}, &c.<ref>The proposal of Haupt ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|SBOT.|Sacred Books of the Old Testament, ed. by P. Haupt. Lpz. and Baltimore, 1893 ff.}}}} ‘Proverbs’, p. 34, l. 44 ff.) to read {{GHGheb|text=בֵּאר}}, {{GHGheb|text=זֵאב}}, &c., does not seem to be warranted. The case here is quite different from that in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=22}} where the Masora requires {{GHGheb|text=תְּאֵֽהֲבוּ}}, no doubt on the analogy of {{GHGheb|text=בְּאֵר}}, &c., for {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽאהֲבוּ}}, which was probably intended, see {{GHGpar|63|m}}.</ref>; ''locative'' {{GHGheb|text=בְּאֵרָה}}, with ''suff.'' {{GHGheb|text=בְּאֵרִי}}, ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=זְאֵבִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=זְאֵבֵי}}; but {{GHGheb|text=בְּאֵרוֹת}}, {{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=בֶּֽאֱרוֹת}}; on the ''infin. constr.'' {{GHGheb|text=שְׂאֵת}}, cf. {{GHGpar|76|b}}.

(''c'') of the form {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹל}}: {{GHGheb|text=בְּאשׁ|translate=stench}} (with ''suff.'' {{GHGheb|text=בָּאְשׁוֹ}}, just as {{GHGheb|text=סֻבְּכוֹ}} occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=4|verse=7}} along with the ''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=סְבָךְ־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=74|verse=5}}; cf. for the Dageš, {{GHGpar|20|h}}), perhaps also {{GHGheb|text=לְאֹם|translate=nation}}, pl. {{GHGheb|text=לְאֻמִּים}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|u}}
5. Paradigms ''g–i'' comprise the segholate forms with middle {{GHGheb|text=ו}} or {{GHGheb|text=י}}: (''a'') of the form ''qăṭl'' with {{GHGterm|Wāw}} as a strong consonant, in which cases the original ''ă'' is almost always lengthened to ''ā'' (Paradigm ''g''), thus {{GHGheb|text=מָ֫וֶת}}, {{GHGheb|text=אָ֫וֶן|translate=vanity}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָ֫וֶל|translate=iniquity}}, {{GHGheb|text=תָּ֫וֶךְ|translate=midst}}; with final {{GHGheb|text=א}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁוְא|translate=falsehood}}; cf. however, also {{GHGheb|text=רֶ֫וַח|translate=space}}. In the ''constr. st.'' contraction always occurs, {{GHGheb|text=מוֹת}}, &c. (from original ''maut''), and likewise before suffixes {{GHGheb|text=מוֹתוֹ}}, &c. Exception, {{GHGheb|text=עָ֫וֶל}} as ''constr. st.'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=28|verse=18}} (according to Qimḥi) and with suff. {{GHGheb|text=עַוְלוֹ}}. The contraction remains also in all cases in the plural (but see below, {{GHGpar|93|w|nonumber=1}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|v}}
(''b'') Of the form ''qăṭl'' with consonantal {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} (Paradigm ''h''). With final {{GHGheb|text=א}}, {{GHGheb|text=גַּיְא}} (also {{GHGheb|text=גַּי}}), in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=גֶּיא}}, in the ''constr. st.'' (also {{GHGterm|absol.}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=14|verse=4}}) {{GHGheb|text=גֵּיא}} (also {{GHGheb|text=גֵּי}}); plur. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=2|verse=16}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=6|verse=3}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} according to Baer {{GHGheb|text=גאות}}, i.e. doubtless {{GHGheb|text=גֵּאוֹת}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=גֵּֽיאוֹתֶיךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=35|verse=8}}; according to another reading [and so Ginsburg] {{GHGheb|text=גיאות}},<section end="par93" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

293.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par93 />i.e. doubtless {{GHGheb|text=גְּיָאוֹת}}), but in {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}, and all other passages, {{GHGheb|text=נֵּֽאָיוֹת}}. The uncontracted form (in the ''absol. st.'' with helping {{GHGterm|Ḥireq}}) remains also before {{GHGheb|text=־ָה|translate=locale}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בַּ֫יְתָה}} (but in the ''constr. st.'' e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בֵּ֫יתָה יוֹסֵף}}).—{{GHGheb|text=עִירֹה}} (from {{GHGheb|text=עַ֫יִר}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=11}} is peculiar, so also {{GHGheb|text=שִׁיתוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=17}} (from {{GHGheb|text=שַׁ֫יִת}}).—In the ''plural absol.'' uncontracted forms occur, like {{GHGheb|text=חֲיָלִים|translate=hosts}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֲיָנוֹת|translate=springs}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֲיָרִים|translate=young asses}}, {{GHGheb|text=תְּיָשִׁים|translate=he-goats}}, &c.; as ''constr. st.'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=28}} {{GHGheb|text=עִינוֹת}} for {{GHGheb|text=עֵינוֹת}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|w}}
(''c'') With the contraction of the {{GHGheb|text=ו}} and {{GHGheb|text=י}} even in the ''absol. st.'' sing. (Paradigm ''i''). In this way there arise formations which are unchangeable throughout; thus from the ground-form ''qăṭl'': {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם}} (cf., however, {{GHGpar|96}}), {{GHGheb|text=סוֹף}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹר}}, &c.; with middle {{GHGterm|Yôdh}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֵיל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=9|verse=13}} (elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=חַ֫יִל}}), {{GHGheb|text=לֵיל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=11}} (elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=לַ֫יִל}}, in prose {{GHGheb|text=לַ֫יְלָה}}, see above, {{GHGpar|90|f}}); from the ground-form ''qĭṭl'', {{GHGheb|text=דִּין}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁיר}}, {{GHGheb|text=עִיר}} (see, however, {{GHGpar|96}}); from the ground-form ''qŭṭl'', {{GHGheb|text=גּוּר}}, {{GHGheb|text=רוּחַ}} &c. The plurals {{GHGheb|text=דְּוָדִים|translate=pots}}, {{GHGheb|text=שְׁוָקִים|translate=streets}}, {{GHGheb|text=שְׁוָרִים|translate=oxen}}, have a strong formation (but for {{GHGheb|text=חֲוָחִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=6}} read {{GHGheb|text=חוֹרִים}} as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=11|hidebook=1}}). Finally, forms with a quiescent middle {{GHGheb|text=א}} also belong to this class, such as {{GHGheb|text=רֹאשׁ|translate=head}} (obscured from {{GHGheb|text=רָאשׁ}}=''raʾš'', see {{GHGpar|96}}) and {{GHGheb|text=צֹאן|translate=sheep}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|x}}
6. On Paradigm ''k'': segholate forms from {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} stems. Besides the formations mentioned in {{GHGpar|84|c|a}}, ε, like {{GHGheb|text=בֶּ֫כֶה}}, &c., and {{GHGheb|text=שָׂ֫חוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=47|verse=5}}, with the original {{GHGheb|text=ו}} resolved, according to {{GHGpar|24|d}} (cf. the ''constr. plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=חַגְוֵי|translate=clefts}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ob|chapter=1|verse=3}}, &c., and {{GHGheb|text=קַצְוֵי|translate=ends}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=48|verse=11}}, &c., where the {{GHGheb|text=ו}} becomes again a strong consonant,<ref>Nöldeke, {{GHGcite|title=Beiträge}}, p. 58: the direct or indirect retention of this {{GHGheb|text=ו}} is hardly a feature of early Hebrew. The true Hebrew forms from {{GHGheb|text=קָצֶה}} would be {{GHGheb|text=קְצֵה}}, {{GHGheb|text=קָצוֹת}}, {{GHGheb|text=קְצוֹת}}, the aramaizing forms {{GHGheb|text=קָצָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=קְצָת}}, {{GHGheb|text=קְצָווֹת}}.</ref> from {{GHGheb|text=חֶ֫גֶו}} and {{GHGheb|text=קֶ֫צֶו}} or {{GHGheb|text=חָ֫גוּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=קָ֫צוּ}}), there occur also (''a'') commonly, of the ground-form ''qaṭl'', forms like {{GHGheb|text=פְּרִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=בְּכִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=גְּדִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=לְחִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=צְבִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲרִי}}, &c.; in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=פֶּ֫רִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=בֶּ֫כִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=לֶ֫חִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=צֶ֫בִי}} (cf. {{GHGpar|29|m}}), but {{GHGheb|text=אֲרִ֑י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=18}}; with suffixes {{GHGheb|text=פִּרְיוֹ}} (attenuated from ''păryô''), {{GHGheb|text=בִּכְיִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=6|verse=9}}, but also {{GHGheb|text=פֶּרְיְךָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=לֶחְיוֹ}} &c.; before a grave suffix {{GHGheb|text=פְּרִיהֶם}}, but also {{GHGheb|text=פֶּרְיְכֶם}}. Plur. {{GHGheb|text=גְּדָיִים}} (constr. {{GHGheb|text=גְּדָיֵי}}, see above, {{GHGpar|93|o|nonumber=1}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֲטָאֵי}}), {{GHGheb|text=אֲרָיִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=אֲרָיוֹת}}; with softening of the {{GHGheb|text=י}} to {{GHGheb|text=א}} (as elsewhere in {{GHGheb|text=בְּלוֹאֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=38|verse=12}} for which there is {{GHGheb|text=בְּלוֹיֵ}} in verse 11, according to {{GHGpar|8|k}}; {{GHGheb|text=עַרְבִיאִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=17|verse=11}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=26|verse=7|hidebook=1}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}; probably in {{GHGheb|text=דּֽוּדָאִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=לֻֽלָאוֹת}} from {{GHGheb|text=דּוּדַי}} and {{GHGheb|text=לוּלַי}}; also {{GHGheb|text=חלכאים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=10|verse=10}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, divided into two words by the Masora, is to be referred to a sing. {{GHGheb|text=חֶלְכַּי|translate=hapless}}): {{GHGheb|text=חֲלָאִים|translate=jewels}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=7|verse=2}} (from {{GHGheb|text=חֲלִי}}), {{GHGheb|text=טְלָאִים|translate=lambs}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=11}} (from {{GHGheb|text=טְלִי}}); but instead of {{GHGheb|text=פְּתָאִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=צְבָאִים}} (from {{GHGheb|text=פֶּ֫תִי}} and {{GHGheb|text=צְבִי}}) the Masora requires {{GHGheb|text=פְּתָאיִם}} and {{GHGheb|text=צְבָאיִם}}; dual: {{GHGheb|text=לְחָיַ֫יִם}}, ''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=לְחָיֵי}}, with ''suff.'' {{GHGheb|text=לְחָיַי}}, &c. On {{GHGheb|text=דַּל|translate=door}}, cf. {{GHGpar|95|f}}, and on such formations generally, see Barth on biliteral nouns in {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1887, p. 603 ff., and ''Nominal-bildung'' (isolated nouns), p. 1 ff.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|y}}
(''b'') From the ground-form ''qiṭl'', {{GHGheb|text=חֲצִי|translate=half}}, in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=חֵ֫צִי}}, with suff. {{GHGheb|text=חֶצְיוֹ}}, &c.—From stems with middle {{GHGterm|Wāw}} arise such forms as {{GHGheb|text=אִי}} (from ''ʾiwy''), {{GHGheb|text=עִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=צִי|translate=ship}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=אִיִּים}}, {{GHGheb|text=צִיִּים}}, &c.; instead of the extraordinary plur. {{GHGheb|text=צִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=24|verse=24}} read with the Samaritan {{GHGheb|text=יֽוֹצְאִים}}, and for {{GHGheb|text=בַּצִּים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=30|verse=9}} read probably with Cornill {{GHGheb|text=אָצִים}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|z}}
(''c'') From the ground-form ''qŭṭl'' sometimes forms like {{GHGheb|text=תֹּ֫הוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=בֹּ֫הוּ}} (from ''tŭhw, bŭhw''), sometimes like {{GHGheb|text=חֳלִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֳנִי}}, and even without an initial guttural {{GHGheb|text=דֳּמִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֳפִי}},<section end=par93 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

294.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par93 />{{GHGheb|text=צֳרִי}} (also {{GHGheb|text=יְפִי דְּמִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=צְרִי}}), {{GHGheb|text=רָאִי}}, &c; in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=חֹ֫לִי}}, &c., with suff. {{GHGheb|text=חָלְיוֹ}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=חֳלָיִים}}. From {{GHGheb|text=עֳפִי|translate=branch}}, there occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=12}} the plur. {{GHGheb|text=עֳפָאיִם}} (analogous to {{GHGheb|text=פְּתָאיִם}}, &c., see above, {{GHGpar|93|x|nonumber=1}}); the ''K<sup>e</sup>eth.'' evidently intends {{GHGheb|text=עֳפָאִים}} (so Opitius and others). Dual, with ''suff.'' {{GHGheb|text=דָּלְיָו}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=24|verse=7}}, ''bucket'' (from {{GHGheb|text=דְּלִי}}, for {{GHGheb|text=דֳּלִי}}), more correctly, with the Masora, {{GHGheb|text=דָּ֣לְיָו}} with Munaḥ for Metheg. This unusual Metheg is to be treated as following the analogy of the cases mentioned in {{GHGpar|9|v}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|aa}}
7. On Paradigms ''l–n'': segholate forms from stems {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} (see {{GHGpar|84|c|a}}, β).

(''a'') In the ''qaṭl''-form the ''ă'' of the contracted formation is sometimes lengthened in the ''absol. st.'', sing. as in {{GHGheb|text=יָם}} (so also in the ''constr. st.'', except in the combination {{GHGheb|text=יַם־סוּף|translate=the Red sea}}; and even before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָֽם־הַמֶּ֫לַח|translate=the salt sea}}), sometimes it remains short, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=פַּת|translate=morsel}}, {{GHGheb|text=עַם|translate=people}}, but even these formations generally have {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} in pause, as well as after the article (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הָעָם}}). Adjectives under the influence of a guttural either have forms like {{GHGheb|text=לַחִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=צַחִים}}, or, with ''compensatory lengthening'', {{GHGheb|text=רָעִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=רָעֵי}}. In the ''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=חַי|translate=living}} (in the plural {{GHGheb|text=חַיִּים}} also a substantive, ''life''), and {{GHGheb|text=דַּי|translate=sufficiency}}, are contracted to {{GHGheb|text=חֵי}}<ref>{{GHGheb|text=חֵי}} only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=12|verse=7}} as ''constr. st.'', since in the asseverative formulae (cf. {{GHGpar|149}}) {{GHGheb|text=חֵי פַרְעֹה}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֵי נַפְשְׁךָ}} (otherwise only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=21}}, after {{GHGheb|text=חַי יהוה}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Amos|chapter=8|verse=14}}), {{GHGheb|text=חֵי}} is a contracted form of the ''absol. st.'' (prop. ''living is Pharaoh!'' &c.). It is evidently only a rabbinical refinement which makes the pronunciation {{GHGheb|text=חַי}} distinctive of an oath by God (or of God by himself), as in the regular formulae {{GHGheb|text=חַי אָ֫נִי}} ({{GHGheb|text=חַי אָֽנֹכִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=40}}) and {{GHGheb|text=חַי יְהֹוָה}} (={{GHGheb|text=חַי אֲדֹנָי}}).</ref> and {{GHGheb|text=דֵּי}}. As a locative form notice {{GHGheb|text=הֶ֫רָה|translate=to the mountain}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=10}} (see {{GHGpar|27|q}}) beside {{GHGheb|text=הָהָ֫רָה}}. The stem is expanded to a triliteral form in {{GHGheb|text=הֲרָרִי}} (unless it is simply derived from a by-form {{GHGheb|text=הָרָר}} on the analogy of ''qătăl''-forms) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=3}} (but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=30|verse=8}} for {{GHGheb|text=הַֽרֲרִי}} read {{GHGheb|text=הַֽרֲרֵי}}) and {{GHGheb|text=הַֽרֲרָם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=6}}; plur. {{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=הַֽרֲרֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=7}}, &c. (but only in poetical passages), with suffix, {{GHGheb|text=הֲרָרֶ֫יהָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=8|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=עֲמָמִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=14}} (where, however, read probably {{GHGheb|text=בְּעַמֶּ֫ךָ}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=9|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=עַֽמֲמֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=9|verse=24}}: elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=עַמִּים}}, {{GHGheb|text=עַמֵּי}}.—Before ''suffixes'' and in the plur. ''ă'' is sometimes attenuated to ''ĭ'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=פִּתִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=פִּתִּים}}, from {{GHGheb|text=פַּת}}; {{GHGheb|text=סִפִּים}} and {{GHGheb|text=סִפּוֹת}} (also {{GHGheb|text=סַפּוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=28}}) from {{GHGheb|text=סַף}}. Before {{GHGheb|text=ח|translate=ă}} is retained in a virtually sharpened syllable, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=פַּחִים|translate=traps}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|bb}}
(''b'') ''Qiṭl''-forms: {{GHGheb|text=אֵם}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֵשׁ|translate=fire}} (with suff. {{GHGheb|text=אִשִּׁי}}, but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אֶשְׁכֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=50|verse=11}}), {{GHGheb|text=חֵן|translate=favour}}, &c.; of a triliteral form, the plur. {{GHGheb|text=חֲצָצֶ֫יךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=77|verse=18}}.

(''c'') ''Qŭṭl''-forms: {{GHGheb|text=חֹק}}, {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל|translate=totality}}, before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} {{GHGheb|text=חָק־}}, {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־}}, with suff. {{GHGheb|text=חֻקִּי}}, &c., with omission of {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}} (according to {{GHGpar|20|m}}) always {{GHGheb|text=חָקְךָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=חָקְכֶם}}, but from {{GHGheb|text=עֹז}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֻזִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֻזְּךָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֻזְּכֶם}}, for which {{GHGheb|text=עָזִּי}} and {{GHGheb|text=עָזְּךָ}} are also found. {{GHGheb|text=חִקְקֵי}}, expanded to a triliteral form, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=15}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=1}}, generally explained as a secondary form of {{GHGheb|text=חֻקְקֵי}} with abnormal weakening of the ''ŭ'' to ''ĭ'', is more probably to be referred to a ''qiṭl''-form=Arabic ''ḥiqq''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|cc}}
The forms with assimilated middle ''Nûn'' likewise follow the analogy of Paradigms ''l–n'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אַף|translate=nose, anger}} ({{GHGheb|text=אַפִּי}}, dual {{GHGheb|text=אַפַּ֫יִם}}, also ''face'') for ''ʾanp''; {{GHGheb|text=חֵךְ|translate=palate}} for ''ḥink'', {{GHGheb|text=זִקִּים|translate=fetters}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֵז|translate=goat}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=עִזִּים}}, for ''ʿinz'', probably also {{GHGheb|text=אֵב|translate=green herb}}, for ''ʾinb''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|dd}}
'''2.''' Paradigm II comprises all formations with original short vowels, whether in the first or second syllable; cf. {{GHGpar|84|f|a}}–{{GHGpar|84|f|i|nonumber=1}}, and the general laws of formation, {{GHGpar|92|b}}–{{GHGpar|92|g|nonumber=1}}.
<section end=par93 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

295.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par93 />Rem. 1. On Paradigms ''a'' and ''b'': ground-form ''qătăl''. The lengthening of the second ''ă'' to ''ā'' is maintained in the ''constr. st. sing.'' only in {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}}-forms, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=צָבָא|translate=army}}, {{GHGheb|text=צְבָא}}. For the construct forms {{GHGheb|text=חֲלֵב|translate=milk}}, {{GHGheb|text=לְבֶן־|translate=white}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=12}}, instead of the ordinary ''absolutes'' {{GHGheb|text=חָלָב}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָבָן}}, a secondary form {{GHGheb|text=חָלֵב}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָבֵן}} must be assumed; from {{GHGheb|text=עָשָׁן|translate=smoke}}, the ''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=עֶ֫שֶׁן}} occurs once, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=19|verse=18}}, beside {{GHGheb|text=עֲשַׁן}}, from {{GHGheb|text=הָדָר|translate=ornament}} the ''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=הֶ֫דֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=11|verse=20}}, beside the common form {{GHGheb|text=הֲדַר}}.—The plur. {{GHGheb|text=פָּֽרָשִׁים|translate=horses}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=7}} (instead of {{GHGheb|text=פְּרָשִׁים}}, ground-form ''părăš'') is no doubt due to a confusion with the ''qaṭṭâl''-form {{GHGheb|text=פָּרָשׁ|translate=horseman}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|ee}}
A. Sometimes a sharpening of the third radical takes place, in order to keep the preceding vowel short, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גְּמַלִּים|translate=camels}}, {{GHGheb|text=קְטַנִּים|translate=small ones}}, {{GHGheb|text=פְּלַגּוֹת|translate=brooks}} (see {{GHGpar|20|a}}).—The attenuation of the ''ă'' of the first syllable to ''ĭ'' does not take place in the ''constr. st. plur.'' as a rule after an initial guttural, as {{GHGheb|text=חַכְמֵי}}, {{GHGheb|text=עַנְוַי}}, but {{GHGheb|text=חִזְקֵי}}, and never before a middle guttural, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נַֽהֲרֵי}}; nor (according to König, owing to the influence of the nasal) in the non-guttural forms {{GHGheb|text=זַנְבוֹת|translate=tails}}, {{GHGheb|text=כַּנְפוֹת}}, and (in the dual) {{GHGheb|text=כַּנְפֵי|translate=wings}}, from {{GHGheb|text=זָנָב}}, {{GHGheb|text=כָּנָף}}.—The dual {{GHGheb|text=נַֽהֲרַ֫יִם}} from {{GHGheb|text=נָהָר|translate=river}}, shows an abnormal omission of the lengthening of the ''ă'' before a tone-bearing termination, but cf. {{GHGpar|88|c}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|ff}}
B. From {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} stems, forms like {{GHGheb|text=חָלָל}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָנָן}}, &c., belong to this class.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|gg}}
C. The few nouns of the ground-form ''qĭṭăl'' follow the same analogy, such as {{GHGheb|text=לֵבָב|translate=heart}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁכָר|translate=strong drink}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֵנָב|translate=grape}}, &c. From {{GHGheb|text=שֵׂעָר|translate=hair}}, in the ''constr. st.'' besides {{GHGheb|text=שְׂעַר}} the form {{GHGheb|text=שַׂ֫עַר}} is also found (perhaps a survival of a secondary form like those in Paradigm I, ''d''); so from {{GHGheb|text=צֵלָע|translate=rib}}, {{GHGheb|text=צֶ֫לַע}} and even {{GHGheb|text=צֵ֫לַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=16|verse=13}} (so ed. Mant., Ginsb.; but Baer {{GHGheb|text=צֶ֫לַע}}), both, probably, old secondary forms (also used for the ''absol. st.'') of {{GHGheb|text=צֵלָע}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=צַלְעִי}} and {{GHGheb|text=צַלְעוֹ}}, as well as the ''constr. st. plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=צַלְעוֹת}}; also from {{GHGheb|text=נֵכָר|translate=strangeness}}, the ''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=נֵ֫כַר־}} is found, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=31|verse=16}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|hh}}
2. On Paradigms ''c–e'': ground-form ''qăṭĭl'', developed to ''qāṭēl''; with a final guttural, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שָׂבֵעַ|translate=satisfied}}. In the ''constr. st.'' the original ''ĭ'' of the second syllable, probably on the analogy of the forms discussed in {{GHGpar|69|c}}, becomes ''ă'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=זְקַן}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֲדַל}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֲסַר}}, &c., but not before suffixes, {{GHGheb|text=כְּתֵפִי}}, &c., nor in forms from {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}} stems, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מָלֵא|translate=full}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְלֵא}}; cf., moreover, {{GHGheb|text=עֲקֵב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=25|verse=26}} from {{GHGheb|text=עָקֵב|translate=heel}}, and {{GHGheb|text=אֲבֶל־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=14}}, ''mourning''. Paradigm ''d'' represents forms which in the ''constr. st.'' instead of the ordinary {{GHGheb|text=כְּתַף}}, &c., have a segholate form, as {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫רֶךְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=גֶּ֫דֶר}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֶ֫רֶךְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=גֵּ֫זֶל}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֶ֫רֶל}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=44|verse=9}}), ''constr. st.'' of {{GHGheb|text=אָרֵךְ|translate=long}}, {{GHGheb|text=גָּדֵר|translate=wall}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָרֵךְ|translate=thigh}}, {{GHGheb|text=גָּזֵל|translate=robbery}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָרֵל|translate=uncircumcised}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=11|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּכָתֵף}} would be altogether without precedent as a ''constr. st.'' (for {{GHGheb|text=בְּכֶ֫תֶף}}); most probably the ''absol. st.'' is intended by the Masora (according to Nöldeke, ''Gött. Gel. Anzeigen'', 1871, No. 23 [p. 896] for {{GHGheb|text=בכ׳ אֶחָד|translate=with one shoulder}}, i.e. ''shoulder to shoulder''); [cf. Driver, {{GHGcite|title=Tenses}}, § 190, ''Obs''.].

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|ii}}
In the ''plur. constr.'' the ''ē'' lengthened from ''ĭ'' is frequently retained in verbal adjectives of this formation, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שְׁכֵחֵי}}, {{GHGheb|text=שְׂמֵחֵי}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲבֵלֵי}}, {{GHGheb|text=יְשֵׁנֵי}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֲפֵצֵי}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=יְתֵֽדֹתָיו}} (with ''ē'' under the protection of the secondary tone) from {{GHGheb|text=יָתֵד|translate=tent-peg.}} On the other hand from {{GHGheb|text=יָרֵא|translate=fearing}}, always {{GHGheb|text=יִרְאֵי}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=רִגְעֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=20}} from {{GHGheb|text=רָגֵעַ}}.—With ''ă'' retained in the initial syllable cf. {{GHGheb|text=אַחֵר|translate=alius}} (with a virtual sharpening of the {{GHGheb|text=ח}}).—From {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} stems come forms like {{GHGheb|text=מֵת|translate=dead person}}, {{GHGheb|text=גֵּר|translate=resident stranger}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֵד|translate=witness}}, with unchangeable {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}}; hence {{GHGheb|text=מֵתִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֵתֵי}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|kk}}
Kindred in character are the formations from the ground-form ''qăṭŭl''. This<section end=par93 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

296.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par93 />ground-form is regularly lengthened to ''qāṭōl'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עָנֹל|translate=round}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָמֹק|translate=deep}}, {{GHGheb|text=אָדֹם|translate=red}}; but before formative additions the short ''ŭ'' returns, protected by the sharpening of the following consonant (see ee above), as {{GHGheb|text=עֲגֻלִּים}}, &c. (but in stems with a third guttural or {{GHGheb|text=ר}}, {{GHGheb|text=גְּבֹהָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=שְׁחֹרִים}}). The form {{GHGheb|text=עָגוֹל}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=10|verse=19}}, is abnormal; likewise {{GHGheb|text=עֲמוּקָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=23|verse=27}}, Jablonski (ed. Mant. {{GHGheb|text=עֲמֻקָה}}, Baer and Ginsburg {{GHGheb|text=עֲמֻקָּה}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|ll}}
3. On Paradigm ''f'': ground-form ''qăṭăl'' from {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} stems. As in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} {{GHGpar|75|h}}, the general rule is that before the terminations of the plur. and dual and before suffixes beginning with a vowel, the third radical is usually elided altogether. But besides {{GHGheb|text=שָׂדֶה}} the form {{GHGheb|text=שָׂדַי}}, with the final {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} retained, is also found in poetry (cf. also the singulars with suffixes, like {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁתֵּיהֶם}}, in ss); in the same way final {{GHGheb|text=ו}} is retained in {{GHGheb|text=עֲנָוִים|translate=the poor, constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=עַנְוֵי}}. The plur. of {{GHGheb|text=שָׂדֶה}} is {{GHGheb|text=שָׂדוֹת}}, {{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=שְׂדוֹת}} (also {{GHGheb|text=שְׂדֵי}}, unless this is a ''sing.'', contracted from {{GHGheb|text=שְׂדַי}}; so Barth, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} xlii, p. 351). The ''qĭṭăl''-form (see {{GHGpar|84|i|a}}) {{GHGheb|text=רֵעֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=37}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=16|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=4|verse=5}} is remarkable as a ''constr. st.'' (the reading {{GHGheb|text=רֵעֵה}} of Opitius and others is opposed to the express statement of the Masora). To the category of these forms also belongs without doubt {{GHGheb|text=פָּנִים|translate=face}} (only in ''plur.''), {{GHGheb|text=פְנֵי}}, {{GHGheb|text=פָּנַי}}, {{GHGheb|text=פְּנֵיכֶם}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|mm}}
In a few formations of this kind the vowel of the second syllable appears to have been already lost in the ''absol. st. sing.''; so according to the ordinary view, in {{GHGheb|text=יָד|translate=hand, constr}}. {{GHGheb|text=יַד}}, with ''suff.'' {{GHGheb|text=יָדוֹ}}, but {{GHGheb|text=יֶדְכֶם}}; plur. {{GHGheb|text=יָדוֹת}}, {{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=יְדוֹת}}, dual {{GHGheb|text=יָדַ֫יִם}}, {{GHGheb|text=יְדֵי}}, with ''suff.'' {{GHGheb|text=יָדַי}}, {{GHGheb|text=יְדֵיכֶם}}, &c., and in {{GHGheb|text=דָּם|translate=blood}}, {{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=דַּם}}, with ''suff.'' {{GHGheb|text=דָּמִי}}, but {{GHGheb|text=דִּמְכֶם}} (''ă'' attenuated to ''ĭ''), plur. {{GHGheb|text=דָּמִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=דְּמֵי}}. But perhaps both these nouns are to be regarded as primitive ({{GHGpar|81}}), and as original monosyllabic formations.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|nn}}
3. Paradigm III comprises forms with an unchangeable vowel in the first syllable, whilst the vowel of the second syllable has been lengthened from an original short vowel, and is therefore changeable. The special cases are to be distinguished in which the original short vowel is lengthened both ''in'' and ''before'' the tone, but in an open syllable becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} (Paradigm ''a'', but cf. also examples like {{GHGheb|text=אֽוֹפַנִּים|translate=wheels}}, for {{GHGheb|text=אֽוֹפָנִים}}, and {{GHGheb|text=אֻֽלַמִּים|translate=porches}}), secondly, the cases in which the vowel becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} even ''before'' the tone (Paradigm ''b''), and finally, those in which the termination of {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} formations is entirely lost (Paradigm ''c'').

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|oo}}
Rem. 1. On the model of {{GHGheb|text=עוֹלָם}} (which, moreover, is obscured from ''ʿâlăm''), the following forms also are inflected: {{GHGheb|text=מִקְמָל}} ({{GHGpar|85|h}}), in some cases with virtual sharpening of the third radical (see {{GHGpar|20|a}}), as {{GHGheb|text=מִבְטַחוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=40|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=8|verse=14}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}} nouns of this form maintain the {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} in the ''constr. st. plur.'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מִקְרָאֵי}} from {{GHGheb|text=מִקְרָא}}<ref>{{GHGheb|text=מְקַדְשֵׁיהֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=7|verse=24}} for {{GHGheb|text=מִקְדְּשׁ׳}} (from {{GHGheb|text=מִקְדָּשׁ}}) is wholly irregular; perhaps, however, the ''part. Piʿēl'' is intended, without {{GHGterm|Dageš}} in the {{GHGheb|text=ד}} (according to {{GHGpar|20|m}}).</ref>; on the other hand, in the plur. of the {{GHGterm|participles Niph.}} ({{GHGpar|85|n}}) of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״אֹ}} (which likewise belong to this class), are found not only regular forms like {{GHGheb|text=נִקְרָאִים}} but also {{GHGheb|text=נֶחְבְּאִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=10|verse=17}}, {{GHGheb|text=נִטְמְאִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=20|verse=30}} f.,<section end=par93 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

297.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" />{{GHGcorrected}}</noinclude><section begin="par93" />and so always {{GHGheb|text=נִבְּאִים}} (except {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=הַנִּבָּאִ֑ים}}) and {{GHGheb|text=נִמְצְאִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=14|verse=14}}, &c. (except {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=8|verse=25}} {{GHGheb|text=הַנִּמְצָאִֽים}} in pause).<ref>Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, p. 659, observes that except in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=5|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=35|verse=17|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=הַנִּמְצְאִים}} is always followed by a preposition governing a word, so that the punctuators perhaps intended to indicate a sort of ''constr. st.''</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|pp}}
Moreover, the other participles in ''ā'' also follow the analogy of {{GHGheb|text=עוֹלָם}} as regards the final syllable ({{GHGheb|text=מְקֻטָּל}}, {{GHGheb|text=מָקְטָל}}; cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=הַמּוּשַׁב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=12}} in close connexion; see the analogous cases in {{GHGpar|65|d}}); also {{GHGheb|text=שֻׁלְחָן|translate=table}} ({{GHGpar|85|u}}; plur. {{GHGheb|text=שֻׁלְחָנוֹת}}, {{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=שֻׁלְחֲנוֹת}}), {{GHGheb|text=קָרְבָּן}}, {{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=קָרְבַּן}}, hence in plur. {{GHGterm|constr.}} with ''suff.'' {{GHGheb|text=קָרְבְּנֵיהֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=7|verse=38}}; {{GHGheb|text=עַקְרָב}} ({{GHGpar|85|w}}), plur. {{GHGheb|text=עַקְרַבִּים}} (with sharpening of the final consonant for {{GHGheb|text=עַקְרָבִים}}, cf. also {{GHGheb|text=עֵירֹם|translate=naked}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=עֵֽירֻמִּים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=7}} [but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=25|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=עֲרוּמִּים}}, according to {{GHGpar|9|o}} an orthographic licence for {{GHGheb|text=עֲרֻמִּים}} from {{GHGheb|text=עָרֹם}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַֽעֲרֻמִּים|translate=nakedness}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=28|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=קַרְדֹּם}}, {{GHGheb|text=קַרְדֻּמּוֹ}}; {{GHGheb|text=מַֽעֲמַקֵּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=נִכְבַּדֵּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=8}} f.; {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׂגַּבִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=3}}; even with attenuation of the ''ă'' to ''ĭ'', {{GHGheb|text=מֽוֹרִגִּים|translate=threshing instruments}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=24|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=21|verse=23}}, from {{GHGheb|text=מוֹרָג}}), {{GHGheb|text=מַתָּן}} ({{GHGpar|85|g}}), {{GHGheb|text=מָגֵן}} ({{GHGpar|85|i}}), {{GHGheb|text=מָעֹז}} ({{GHGpar|85|k}}), inasmuch as they retain the ''ā'' of the first syllable, contrary to rule, even when not pretonic, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מָֽגִנִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=מָֽעֻזִּי}}; {{GHGheb|text=מוֹשָׁב}} ({{GHGpar|85|g}}); {{GHGheb|text=תּוֹשָׁב}} ({{GHGpar|85|p}}), ''constr. st. plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=תּֽשָׁבֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=17|verse=1}}; also isolated forms according to {{GHGpar|84|t|a}}, and {{GHGpar|84|b|b}}, {{GHGpar|84|c|b|nonumber=1}}, {{GHGpar|84|k|b|nonumber=1}}, {{GHGpar|84|m|b|nonumber=1}}, {{GHGpar|84|n|b|nonumber=1}}, {{GHGpar|84|o|b|nonumber=1}}. Cf. finally, {{GHGheb|text=צַוָּאר|translate=neck}} (from ''ṣăwʾăr''), ''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=צַוַּאר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=28|verse=10}} ff., ''constr. st. plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=צַוְּארֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=45|verse=14}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|qq}}
2. (Paradigm ''b''; cf. {{GHGpar|84|s|a}}.) Instead of the original ''ĭ'' in such forms as {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽיִבְכֶם}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=22|verse=29}}), the second syllable more frequently has ''ĕ'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יֽׄצֶרְךָ|translate=thy creator}}; with a closing guttural (according to {{GHGpar|91|d}}; but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אֹבַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=28}}) forms are found sometimes like {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁלֵֽחֲךָ}}, sometimes like {{GHGheb|text=בֹּרַֽאֲךָ}}; ''constr. st.'' without ''suff.'' {{GHGheb|text=נֹטַ֫ע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=94|verse=9}} (according to {{GHGpar|65|d}}); with a middle guttural {{GHGheb|text=גּֽׄאַלְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=48|verse=17}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=14|hidebook=1}}.—The same analogy also is followed in the flexion of the other participles which have ''ē'' in the final syllable ({{GHGheb|text=מְקַטֵּל}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִתְקַטֵּל}}, &c.), see further, in {{GHGpar|84|d|b}}, {{GHGheb|text=גִּבֵּן}}, &c. (but with exceptions, as {{GHGheb|text=שִׁלֵּשִׁים}}, {{GHGheb|text=רִבֵּעִים}}), and ibid. {{GHGpar|84|l|b|nonumber=1}}, {{GHGpar|84|p|b|nonumber=1}}; {{GHGpar|85|i}}, {{GHGpar|85|k|nonumber=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=מִזְבֵּחַ|translate=altar}}, {{GHGterm|constr. st.}} {{GHGheb|text=מִזְבַּח}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=מִזְבְּחוֹת}}), and ibid. {{GHGpar|85|q|nonumber=1}} , but here also there are exceptions like {{GHGheb|text=מַקְהֵלִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=26|verse=12}},<!-- the comma is my addition --Amir E. Aharoni --> {{:Gesenius' Hebrew Grammar/Additions and Corrections/273}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|rr}}
3. (Paradigm ''c'': {{GHGterm|part. Qal}} of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, differing from Paradigm II, ''f'' in the unchangeableness of the vowel of the first syllable.) In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=17|verse=15}} ''ē'' in the ''absol. st.'' is abnormal, and {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} in the ''constr. st.'' in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=24|verse=11}} (so Opitius, Ginsburg; but Baer {{GHGheb|text=חֹזֵה}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=2|verse=15}} (according to Baer, but not the Mantua ed.; {{GHGheb|text=מִקְרֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=3|verse=19}} is in the ''absol. st.''). To this class belong, as regards their formation, the {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}-forms mentioned in {{GHGpar|84|r|a}}, {{GHGpar|85|g}} (with ''suff.'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַמַּֽעַלְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=20|verse=1}}, ''which brought thee up''), and ''h''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|ss}}
In a few instances, before a suffix beginning with a consonant, the original ''ăy'' of the termination has been contracted to ''ê'', and thus there arise forms which have apparently ''plural suffixes''; as {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁתֵּיהֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=1|verse=10.16}}; {{GHGheb|text=מַרְאֵיהֶם|translate=their appearance}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=1|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=21}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=2|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=נֽוֹטֵיהֶם|translate=who stretched them forth}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=5}}; ''defectively'' {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽפֵהֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=7|verse=5}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=נְוֵהֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=34|verse=14}}); on the other hand, the examples in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=17}}, which were formerly classed with the above, are really plurals. But {{GHGheb|text=מַֽחֲנֶ֫יךָ|translate=thy camp}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=23|verse=15}} ({{GHGheb|text=מַֽחֲנֶ֫ךָ}} occurs just before),<section end="par93" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

298.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par93" />{{GHGheb|text=מִקְנֶ֫יךָ|translate=thy cattle}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=23}} (probably also {{GHGheb|text=שָׂדֶ֫יךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=26}}), {{GHGheb|text=מַרְאַ֫יִךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=2|verse=14}}, and {{GHGheb|text=מַרְאָיו|translate=the sight of him}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=41|verse=1}} (with the {{GHGheb|text=י}} here retained orthographically), {{GHGheb|text=מַֽעֲלָיו}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=40|verse=31}}, &c., are still to be explained as singulars.—On a few other examples which may perhaps be thus explained, see {{GHGpar|124|k}}. Before the plural ending the original termination ''ay'' reappears in {{GHGheb|text=מְמֻֽחָיִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=25|verse=6}} (''part. Pu.'' from {{GHGheb|text=מָחָה}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|tt}}
4. Paradigm IV comprises the forms with a changeable vowel (''a, b''), or a vowel which has already become {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} (''c''), in the first syllable, and an unchangeable vowel in the second. With Paradigm ''c'' (which, however, for the most part consists merely of forms based on analogy, without biblical parallels) are also connected all the forms which have unchangeable vowels in both syllables, and therefore (like {{GHGheb|text=כְּתָב}}) cannot undergo any vowel changes.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|uu}}
Rem. 1. Analogous to {{GHGheb|text=פָּקִיד}} (ground-form ''păqîd'') are {{GHGpar|84|k|a}}, {{GHGheb|text=גָּדוֹל}}, &c. (with ''ô'', not changeable ''ô'' for ''ŭ''); in substantives like {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלוֹם}}, this ''̂'' is demonstrably obscured from ''â'' (Arab. ''sălâm''); ibid. {{GHGpar|84|k|a|nonumber=1}}, {{GHGpar|84|m|a|nonumber=1}}, {{GHGheb|text=אָסוּר}}, {{GHGheb|text=אָסִיר}}, &c.; {{GHGpar|85|u}}, {{GHGheb|text=זִכָּרוֹן}}, {{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=זִכְרוֹן}}; {{GHGheb|text=חִזָּיוֹן}}, {{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=חֶזְיוֹן}}; {{GHGheb|text=כִּלָּיוֹן}}, {{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=כִּלְיוֹן}} (cf., however, the forms in the ''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=עִצְּבוֹן}}, {{GHGheb|text=קִנְּמוֹן}}, and with the plural suffix {{GHGheb|text=עִזְּבוֹנַ֫יִךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=27|verse=12}} ff.); {{GHGpar|85|w}}, {{GHGheb|text=חַלָּמִישׁ}}, {{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=חַלְמִישׁ}}; {{GHGpar|85|l}}, {{GHGheb|text=מָקוֹם}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|vv}}
2. {{GHGheb|text=עָנִי}} (ground-form ''ʿănîy'', stem {{GHGheb|text=עָנָה}}) represents forms in which a final {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} has been resolved into ''î''; before formative additions the original {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} under the protection of a {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}} again becomes audible as a firm consonant, whilst the (originally short) vowel of the first Syllable becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}; cf. {{GHGpar|84|l|a}}, {{GHGheb|text=נָקִי}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=נְקִיִּים}}, and {{GHGpar|87|a}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|ww}}
3. {{GHGheb|text=כְּתָב}} with unchangeable ''â'' in the second syllable, whilst the {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} is weakened from a short vowel (Arab. ''kĭtâb''); ''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=כְּתָֽב־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=4|verse=8}} (readings like {{GHGheb|text=כְּתַב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=35|verse=4}} are incorrect, although {{GHGheb|text=יְקַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=1|verse=4}} and {{GHGheb|text=כְּתַב־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=4|verse=8|hidebook=1}} are supported by fairly good authority; however, these ''q<sup>e</sup>ṭâl''-forms in Hebrew are probably all loan-words from the Aramaic). The only plural form found in the O.T. is {{GHGheb|text=עֲבָֽדֵיהֶם|translate=their deeds}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=9|verse=1}}. In a narrower sense the forms enumerated in {{GHGpar|84|n|a}}–{{GHGpar|84|p|a|nonumber=1}} belong to this class; in a wider sense all those which have unchangeable vowels throughout, thus {{GHGpar|84|u|a}}, {{GHGpar|84|e|b}} ({{GHGheb|text=קַטָּל}}, cf., however, the anomalous forms mentioned there), ibid. {{GHGpar|84|f|b|nonumber=1}}–{{GHGpar|84|i|b|nonumber=1}}, {{GHGpar|84|m|b|nonumber=1}} (No. 34 f.), {{GHGpar|84|n|b|nonumber=1}} (No. 39), {{GHGpar|84|p|b|nonumber=1}} (No. 44), also partly {{GHGpar|85|b}}–{{GHGpar|85|w|nonumber=1}} (especially {{GHGpar|85|l|nonumber=1}} and {{GHGpar|85|r|nonumber=1}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|93|xx}}
In opposition to the anomalous shortening of the form {{GHGheb|text=קַטָּל}} (see above), cases are also found where pretonic vowels are retained even in the antepenultima (with the secondary tone); cf. above, {{GHGpar|93|ii|nonumber=1}} and {{GHGpar|93|pp|nonumber=1}}, also of the form {{GHGheb|text=קָטִיל}} (properly ''qăṭîl'') the examples {{GHGheb|text=סָֽרִיסִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=פָּֽרִיצִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָֽׁלִישִׁים}}, whilst the ''constr. st. sing.'' according to the rule, changes the ''ā'' into ''S<sup>e</sup>wâ'' ({{GHGheb|text=סְרִיס}}, {{GHGheb|text=פְּרִיץ}}). (These are not to be confounded with forms like {{GHGheb|text=עָרִיץ|translate=tyrant}}, which is for {{GHGheb|text=עַרִּיץ}}, and consequently has an unchangeable {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}}.) Of the form {{GHGheb|text=קָטוּל}} (''qăṭûl'') in this class are {{GHGheb|text=שָׁבוּעַ|translate=week}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=שָֽׁבֻעִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=שָֽׁבֻעוֹת}}, {{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=שְׁבֻעוֹת}}, but with {{GHGterm|Metheg}} of the secondary tone in the fifth syllable from the end, {{GHGheb|text=שָֽׁבֻעֹֽתֵיבֶם}}.—On {{GHGheb|text=מָעוֹז}}, {{GHGheb|text=מָֽעֻזִּי}}, &c., cf. {{GHGpar|85|k}}.<section end="par93" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

299.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par94 />{{GHGpar-heading|94|Formation of Feminine Nouns}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|94|a}}
'''1.''' The feminine ending {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}, when appended to the masculine forms treated in {{GHGpar|93}}, effects in almost all cases the same changes as are produced in the masculine forms by the addition of a light suffix, since in both cases the tone is moved one place farther forward (see {{GHGpar|92|b}}). The following scheme is based on the same division into four classes, with their subdivisions, as in {{GHGpar|93}}; a few special forms will be treated in {{GHGpar|95}} in connexion with the paradigms of feminine nouns.

{{GHGmargin-letter|94|b}}
Paradigm I: segholate forms, with the feminine ending always added to the ground-form, (''a'') {{GHGheb|text=מַלְכָּה|translate=queen}}, {{GHGheb|text=כַּבְשָׂ֫ה}}, and with attenuation of ''ă'' to ''ĭ'' {{GHGheb|text=כִּבְשָׂ֫ה|translate=lamb}}, {{GHGheb|text=רִצְפָּה|translate=hot stone}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=6}} (from another root {{GHGheb|text=רִֽצְפָה}}; see Baer on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=40|verse=17}}), {{GHGheb|text=חֶזְקָה|translate=strength}} (unless belonging to Paradigm ''b''); (''b'') {{GHGheb|text=סִתְרָה|translate=covering}} (masc. {{GHGheb|text=סֵ֫תֶר}}); {{GHGheb|text=עֶדְנָה|translate=pleasure}} ({{GHGheb|text=עֵ֫דֶן}}), not to be confounded with the unchangeable forms with a prefixed {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}}, derived from {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} stems, as {{GHGheb|text=מִצְוָה|translate=command}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=מִצְו‌ֹת}}; (''c'') {{GHGheb|text=חֻלְדָּה}}, proper name ({{GHGheb|text=חֹ֫לֶד|translate=mole}}), {{GHGheb|text=אָכְלָה|translate=food}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֹ֫כֶל}}); (''d'') {{GHGheb|text=נַֽעֲרָה|translate=girl}} ({{GHGheb|text=נַ֫עַר}}); (''f'') {{GHGheb|text=בָּאְשָׁה|translate=weed}}, {{GHGheb|text=טָֽהֳרָה|translate=purity}} ({{GHGheb|text=טֹ֫הַר}}); (''g'') {{GHGheb|text=עַוְלָה|translate=wrong}} (also {{GHGheb|text=עוֹלָה}}, Paradigm ''i''); (''i'') {{GHGheb|text=צֵידָה|translate=victuals}} (masc. {{GHGheb|text=צַ֫יִד}}, cf. Paradigm ''h''); from ''qiṭl'' and ''quṭl''-forms, {{GHGheb|text=בִּינָה|translate=understanding}}, {{GHGheb|text=סוּפָה|translate=tempest}}; (''k'') {{GHGheb|text=אַלְיָה|translate=fat tail}} (as if from {{GHGheb|text=אֲלִי}}), {{GHGheb|text=שִׁבְיָה}} (''ă'' attenuated to ''ĭ'') ''captivity'' {{GHGheb|text=(שְׁבִי)}}, {{GHGheb|text=לִוְיָה|translate=wreath}} (probably an original ''qiṭl''-form); (''l'') {{GHGheb|text=חַיָּה|translate=life}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִדָּה|translate=measure}} (attenuated from {{GHGheb|text=מַדָּה}}). Adjectives derived from {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} stems also belong in flexion to this class, as {{GHGheb|text=רַבָּה|translate=multa|en=numerous, f.}}, with middle guttural {{GHGheb|text=רָעָה|translate=mala|en=bad, f.}}; (''m'') {{GHGheb|text=זִמָּה|translate=plan}}; (''n'') {{GHGheb|text=חֻקָּה|translate=statute}} ({{GHGheb|text=חֹק}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|94|c}}
Paradigm II: ground-form ''qăṭălăt'', &c., (''a'') {{GHGheb|text=נְקָמָה|translate=vengeance}} ({{GHGheb|text=נָקָם}}); (''b'') {{GHGheb|text=אֲדָמָה|translate=earth}}; (''c'') {{GHGheb|text=נְבֵלָה|translate=corpse}}; (''d'') {{GHGheb|text=עֲיֵפָה|translate=languida|en=tired, f.}}; (''f'') {{GHGheb|text=יָפָה|translate=beautiful}}, {{GHGheb|text=קָצָה|translate=end}} (from {{GHGheb|text=יָפֶה}}, {{GHGheb|text=קָצֶה}}). From stems {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} arise such forms as {{GHGheb|text=עֵדָה}} (masc. {{GHGheb|text=עֵד}}, properly ''part. Qal'' from {{GHGheb|text=עוּד}}) ''female witness''. From the ground-form ''qătŭl'', {{GHGheb|text=עֲמֻקָּה|translate=profunda|en=deep, f.}} (masc. {{GHGheb|text=עָמֹק}}), {{GHGheb|text=עֲבֻדָּה|translate=servitude}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|94|d}}
Paradigm III: unchangeable vowel in the first, changeable in the second syllable, (''a'') {{GHGheb|text=יֽׄלֵדָה|translate=a woman with child}} (cf. the examples in {{GHGpar|84|s|a}}, and the retention of the ''ē'' in the ''part''. {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=22|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=26|hidebook=1}}; in the {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=5 f.}}), but also with the change of the ''ē'' (originally ''ĭ'') into {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֽשְׁבָה|translate=dwelling}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=8}}. However, in these participial forms the feminine is mostly indicated by {{GHGheb|text=־ֶת}} (see below, {{GHGpar|94|h|nonumber=1}}); (''c'') {{GHGheb|text=גּוֹלָה|translate=those of the captivity}} (masc. {{GHGheb|text=גּוֹלֶה}}), but also with a return of the final {{GHGterm|Yôdh}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֹֽמִיָּה|translate=clamorous}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=7|verse=11}}, and the examples in {{GHGpar|75|v}}. On the ''â'' of the participles of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, which also belong to this class, such as {{GHGheb|text=זָרָה|translate=peregrina|en=strange, foreign, f.}}, cf. {{GHGpar|72|g}}.
<section end=par94 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

300.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par94 />{{GHGmargin-letter|94|e}}
Paradigm IV: originally changeable vowel in the first syllable, unchangeable in the second, (''a'') {{GHGheb|text=גְּדֹלָה|translate=magna|en=great, f.}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֲסִידָה|translate=stork}}, properly {{GHGtranslate|pia|en=pious, f.}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּתוּלָה|translate=virgin}}, properly {{GHGtranslate|seiuncta|en=separated, f.}}; (''b'') {{GHGheb|text=עֲנִיָה|translate=misera|en=poor, f.}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|94|f}}
'''2.''' A simple {{GHGheb|text=ת}} is added as feminine ending in forms like {{GHGheb|text=בְּכִית|translate=weeping}} (masc. {{GHGheb|text=בְּכִי}}, {{GHGpar|93|x}}, a), {{GHGheb|text=בְּרִית|translate=covenant}}; but ''feminine participles'' of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}}, as {{GHGheb|text=יׄצֵאת}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֹצֵאת}}, may be due to contraction from ''yôṣèʾet,'' &c. (hardly to lengthening of the ''ĭ'' in the ground-form ''môṣi''), whilst forms like {{GHGheb|text=מֽוֹצְאֵת}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֽשְֹׁאֵת}} (see {{GHGpar|74|i}}) are to be explained on the analogy of the forms treated in {{GHGpar|93|t}}. Apart from the {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} formations, we find the simple {{GHGheb|text=ת}} in the participle {{GHGheb|text=מְשָׁרַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=1|verse=15}}, contracted from {{GHGheb|text=מְשָׁרַתְתְּ}}. But {{GHGheb|text=וְיׄלַדְתְּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=5.7}} is the ground-form of the ptcp. {{GHGheb|text=וְיׄלֶ֫דֶת}} (as in the same connexion in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=14}}), cf. {{GHGpar|80|d}} and the ''Q<sup>e</sup>re'' {{GHGheb|text=שַׁבְתְּ}}, &c., discussed in {{GHGpar|90|n}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|94|g}}
The forms which arise by appending the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} feminine to masculine nouns with a changeable vowel in a closed final syllable are, as a rule, developed exactly in the same way as masculine segholate forms. Thus there arise in Paradigm I (''a'') from {{GHGheb|text=גְּבַרְתְּ}} (for original ''g<sup>e</sup>birt''; {{GHGpar|69|c}}), the form {{GHGheb|text=גְּבֶ֫רֶת|translate=mistress}} (but only in ''construct st.''; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=7}} also {{GHGheb|text=גְּבֶ֫רֶת עַד}} are to be taken together; the ''absolute st.'' is {{GHGheb|text=גְּבִירָה}}); from {{GHGheb|text=מְלַכְתְּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְלֶ֫כֶת|translate=queen}} (in Paradigm II, ''a''); {{GHGheb|text=פְּחֶ֫תֶת}} ({{GHGheb|text=פְּ֫חַת}} = {{GHGheb|text=פַּ֫חַת|translate=pit}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=13|verse=55}}; (''c'') {{GHGheb|text=גָּדֵר|translate=wall}}, {{GHGheb|text=גְּדֶ֫רֶת}} (from {{GHGheb|text=גְּדַרְתְּ}} = ''g<sup>e</sup>dirt''; cf. {{GHGheb|text=זְקַן}} as ''construct st.'' of {{GHGheb|text=זָקֵן}}); on the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=חֲמֵ֫שֶׁת}} is ''construct st.'' of {{GHGheb|text=חֲמִשָּׁה|translate=five}}, with lengthening of the original ''ĭ'' of {{GHGheb|text=חֲמִשְׁתְּ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|94|h}}
Formations with a changeable ''ō'' in the second syllable belonging to this class are {{GHGheb|text=נְח֫שֶׁת|translate=bronze}} (from {{GHGheb|text=נְחֻשְׁתְּ}}), {{GHGheb|text=כְּתֹ֫נֶת}} the ''constr. st.'' of {{GHGheb|text=כֻּתֹּ֫נֶת|translate=coat}}, perhaps also {{GHGheb|text=כְּתֹ֫בֶת|translate=writing}} (unless it be obscured from {{GHGheb|text=כְּתָב}}, {{GHGpar|93}}, Paradigm IV, ''c'').—Paradigm III, (''a'') {{GHGheb|text=חֹתֶ֫מֶת}} (from {{GHGheb|text=חֹתַמְתְּ}}), masc. {{GHGheb|text=חוֹתָם|translate=seal}}; (''b'') {{GHGheb|text=יוֹנֶ֫קֶת}} (properly ''sucking'') ''sprout'' (in {{GHGterm|pause}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חֹבָ֫רֶת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=4}}, &c.), and so most feminines of participles {{GHGheb|text=קֹטֵל}}. On this transition of the ground-form ''qôṭilt'' to {{GHGheb|text=קֹטַלְתְּ}} (regularly before suffixes in {{GHGheb|text=יֽוֹנַקְתּוֹ}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֽׄלַדְתּוֹ}}, &c.), cf. {{GHGpar|69|c}}; ''qôṭalt'' serves as the ground-form under the influenee of a guttural as well as before suffixes, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יׄדַ֫עַת}}, feminine of {{GHGheb|text=יׄדֵעַ|translate=knowing}}; in a wider sense, {{GHGheb|text=גֻּלְגּׄ֫לֶת|translate=skull}} may also be included here, see {{GHGpar|95}}, Paradigm IV, ''c''.

On the endings {{GHGheb|text=וּת}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ִית}}, see {{GHGpar|86|k}}, {{GHGpar|86|l|nonumber=1}}, {{GHGpar|95}} at the end.<section end=par94 />

<section begin=par95 />{{GHGpar-heading|95|Paradigms of Feminine Nouns}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|95|a}}
In accordance with the general formative laws, stated in {{GHGpar|92|b}}–{{GHGpar|92|k|nonumber=1}}, the following cases have chiefly to be considered in the flexion of<section end=par95 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

301.text:
feminines also: (1) a tone-lengthened vowel on the removal of the tone reverts to its original shortness (thus the ''ā'' of the termination {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} becomes again ''ā'' in the ''construct st.'' {{GHGheb|text=־ַת}}). On the other hand, even an originally short vowel is retained as (a long) pretonic vowel ''before'' the endings {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} and {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} in the ''abs. st.'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=צְדָקָה}}; (2) without the tone or foretone an originally short vowel almost always becomes {{GHGterm|Šewâ}}; on the other hand, ''before'' a vowel which had thus become ''Šewâ'' the ''ă'' in the first syllable which had hitherto also been reduced to {{GHGterm|Šewâ}} returns, although usually attenuated to ''ĭ'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=צִדְקַת}} from ''ṣădhăqăth''; (3) in the plural of the feminines of segholate forms before the termination of {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} or {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}}, and in formations of the latter kind also before the light suffixes, a ''pretonic Qameṣ'' reappears, while the short vowel of the first syllable becomes {{GHGterm|Šewâ}}. This short vowel, however, returns in the ''construct st. plur.'', whether ending in {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} or {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}}; in formations of the latter kind also before the grave suffixes. The following Paradigms (with the exception of I, ''d'') deal only with such of the forms treated in § 94 as incur some vowel changes or other. All forms with unchangeable vowels follow the analogy of Paradigm I, ''d''. {{GHGmargin-letter|95|b}}

''with grave suff.'' | {{GHGheb|text=צִדְקַתְכֶם}} | {{GHGheb|text=זַֽעֲקַתְכֶם}} | {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנַתְכֶם}} | {{GHGheb|text=יֽוֹנַקְתְּכֶם}} | {{GHGheb|text=גֻּלְגָּלְתְּכֶם}} |- | ''Plur. absolute'' | {{GHGheb|text=צְרָקוֹת}} | |On {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנוֹת}} as a less frequent (poetic) form for {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנִים}} see {{GHGpar|87|n}}.{{GHGheb|text=שָׁנוֹת}} | [{{GHGheb|text=יֽוֹנְקוֹת}}] | |- | Plur.
