Moreover, it is also possible that certain verbs were originally in use at the same time both as transitive and intransitive, e.g. perhaps {{GHGheb|text=לָבֵשׁ|translate=to be clothed}} along with {{GHGheb|text=לָבַשׁ|translate=to put on}} (a garment). Finally the analogy of certain transitives in constant use may have led to intransitives of kindred meaning being also united directly with the accusative, so that, in other words, whole classes of verbs came to be regarded in a particular aspect as transitives. See below, y.<section end=par117 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

393.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par117 />{{GHGmargin-letter|117|w}}
2. The modification of the original meaning becomes especially evident when even reflexive conjugations (''Niphʿal, Hithpaʿēl'', &c.) take an accusative (cf. § 57, note 2); e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נִבָּא|translate=to prophesy}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=25|verse=13}}; {{GHGheb|text=נָסַב}} (prop. ''to put oneself round'') ''to surround'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=נִלְחַם|translate=to fight}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=109|verse=3}} (where, however, the {{GHGterm|Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּלְחֲמ֫וּנִי}} should be read; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=1}}); also {{GHGheb|text=הִתְגַּלַּח|translate=to shave}} (something) ''for oneself'', Num 6:19; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְנַחֵל|translate=to take}} some one ''for oneself as a possession'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְנַכֵּל|translate=to make}} some one ''an object of craft'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְנַצֵּל|translate=to strip}} a thing ''off oneself'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְעַבֵּר|translate=to bring on oneself the anger}} of any one, ''to anger'' him; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְבּוֹנֵן|translate=to consider}} something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=37|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְפָּרֵק|translate=to break}} something ''off from oneself'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=3}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=9}} after {{GHGheb|text=הִתְחַתְּנוּ|translate=make ye marriages}}, read {{GHGheb|text=אִתָּ֫נוּ}} instead of {{GHGheb|text=אֹתָ֫נוּ}}. Cf. {{GHGpar|54|f}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|x}}
3. So also it is only owing to a modification of the original meaning of a verb (except where the expression is incorrect, and perhaps derived from the popular language), when sometimes the remoter object (otherwise introduced by {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}) is directly subordinated in the form of an accusative suffix, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=7|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=הֲצוֹם צַמְתֻּ֫נִי אָ֫נִי|translate=did ye fast at all unto me, even to me?}} as though to say, have ye ''be-fasted'' me? have ye reached me with your fasting? Still more strange is {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=גְּדֵלַ֫נִי כְאָב|translate=he}} (the orphan) ''grew up to me as to a father''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=65|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=3}}, and in Aramaic {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=5|verse=6}}; but {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫רֶץ הַנֶּ֫גְב נְתַתָּ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=15|verse=19}} is to be regarded as a double accusative after a verb of ''giving'', see ff. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=25}} read {{GHGheb|text=וּפִלְלוּ}} for {{GHGheb|text=וּפִלְלוֹ}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=44|verse=21}}, instead of the Niphʿal, read {{GHGheb|text=תִּנְשֵׁ֫נִי}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=29|verse=3}} either {{GHGheb|text=עֲשִׂיתִיו}} is to be read with Olshausen or {{GHGheb|text=עֲשִׂיתִים}} (and previously {{GHGheb|text=יְאֹרָי}}) with Smend; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=42|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶדַּדֶּה}} or {{GHGheb|text=אֲדַדֵּם}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=55|verse=23}} (where König takes {{GHGheb|text=יְהָֽבְךָ}} as ''he has given it to thee'') we must certainly assume a substantive {{GHGheb|text=יְהָב}} (= ''fate''?).

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|y}}
4. Whole classes of verbs, which, according to ''v'' above, are regarded as ''transitive'', either on account of their original meaning or (for the sake of analogy) by a modification of that meaning, are—

(''a'') Verba ''induendi'' and ''exuendi'', as {{GHGheb|text=לָבַשׁ|translate=to put on}}, {{GHGheb|text=פָּשַׁט|translate=to put off}} a garment, {{GHGheb|text=עָדָה|translate=to put on}} ornaments, ''to adorn oneself with'' (cf. also {{GHGheb|text=מְשֻׁבָּצִים זָהָב|translate=enclosed in gold}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=28|verse=20}}). Also in poetic expressions such as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=65|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=לָֽבְשׁוּ כָּרִים הַצֹּאן|translate=the pastures are clothed with flocks}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=109|verse=29}}; 104:2 ({{GHGheb|text=עָטָה}}); 65:14b ({{GHGheb|text=עָטַף}}), &c.<ref>From the idea of ''covering oneself with'' something, we might also, if necessary, explain {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=30|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=יִרְחֲצוּ מַיִם|translate=they shall wash themselves with water}}; but the reading is simply to be emended to the ordinary {{GHGheb|text=בַּמַּיִם}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|z}}
(''b'') Verba ''copiae'' and ''inopiae'' (also called verba ''abundandi'' and ''deficiendi''), as {{GHGheb|text=מָלֵא}}, ''to be full of'' something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=8|verse=17}}; here, and also frequently elsewhere, construed with {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־}}, and hence evidently with an accusative; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=13}}; with a personal object, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=9|translate=my lust shall be satisfied upon them}}; with an accusative ''preceding'' the verb for the sake of emphasis, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=15}} ''your hands'' {{GHGheb|text=דָּמִים מָלֵ֫אוּ|translate=are full of blood}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=2}}; so also the ''Niph.'' {{GHGheb|text=נִמְלָא|translate=to fill oneself with}} something, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=7}} (where the object is connected by {{GHGheb|text=את}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=2|verse=7}} f., 6:4, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=3|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=נִזְרַע|translate=to be fructified with}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=28}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁרַץ|translate=to swarm with}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=20}}, 21 {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=7|verse=28}}; {{GHGheb|text=(שָׂבֵעַ) שָׂבַע|translate=to be full of}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=2|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=12|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=גָּבַר|translate=to become strong, to wax mighty in}} something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=פָּרַץ|translate=to overflow with}} something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=3|verse=10}} (with the object preceding); {{GHGheb|text=יָרַד}} prop. ''to descend'', poetically also ''to pour down, to overflow with'' something (cf. in Greek προρέειν ὕδωρ, δάκρυα στάζειν), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=3|verse=48}} {{GHGheb|text=פַּלְגֵי מַ֫יִם תֵּרַד עֵינִי|translate=mine eye runneth }}<section end=par117 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

394.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="ShakespeareFan00" /></noinclude><section begin=par117 />''down (with) rivers of water''; 1:16, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=136}}; so also {{GHGheb|text=הָלַךְ|translate=to run over with, to flow with}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=4|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=נָזַל}} to gush out with, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=נָטַף|translate=to drop, to overflow with}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=4|verse=18}}a; {{GHGheb|text=פָּרַח|translate=to break forth}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁטַף|translate=to overflow}}, but also (transitively) ''to overflow with'', probably in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=נוּב|translate=to bud with}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=10|verse=31}}; so perhaps also {{GHGheb|text=עָבַר|translate=to pass over, to overflow with}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=28}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָצָא|translate=to go forth}} with, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=3}}.—Especially bold, but still on the analogy of the above examples, is {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=6}}, where it is said of a vineyard {{GHGheb|text=וְעָלָה שָׁמִיר וָשָׁ֫יִת|translate=but it shall come up}} (it shall be overgrown) ''with briers and thorns''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=31}}, and still more boldly, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=34|verse=13}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|aa}}
With the opposite idea, {{GHGheb|text=חָסֵר|translate=to be in want of, to lack}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=28}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁכֹל|translate=to be bereaved of}} (as though it were ''to lose''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=45}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=22|verse=17}} even {{GHGheb|text=הַמְעַט־לָ֫נוּ}} (prop. ''was there too little for us of ...?'') as being equivalent to a verbum inopiae (= ''had we too little of'' ...?) is construed with an accusative; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=9|verse=32}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|bb}}
(''c'') Several verbs of ''dwelling''; the accusative in this case expresses either the place or the thing ''at'' which or ''with'' which any one tarries; thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=22|verse=4}} after {{GHGheb|text=יָשַׁב}}, cf. {{GHGpar|118|g}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=14}} after {{GHGheb|text=גּוּר}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=57|verse=5}} after {{GHGheb|text=שָׁכַב}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=16}} with {{GHGheb|text=שָׁכַן}}; or even the person (the people) with whom any one dwells or is a guest, as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=120|verse=5|hidebook=1}} after {{GHGheb|text=גּוּר}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=20}} after {{GHGheb|text=זָבַל}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=19}} with {{GHGheb|text=שָׁכַן}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|cc}}
'''5'''. ''Two accusatives'' (usually one of the person and one of the thing) are governed by—

(''a'') The causative conjugations ({{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, sometimes also ''Pilpel'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כִּלְכֵּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=12}}, &c.) of verbs which are simply transitive in {{GHGterm|Qal}}, and hence also of {{GHGterm|verba induendi}} and ''exuendi'', &c. (cf. above a and u, and also y, z), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=הַרְאֵ֫נִי נָא אֶת־כְּבֹדֶ֫ךָ|translate=show me, I pray thee, thy glory}}. Thus very frequently {{GHGheb|text=הוֹדִיעַ|translate=to cause}} some one ''to know'' something; {{GHGheb|text=לִמַּד|translate=docere aliquem aliquid}}, &c.; cf. further, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=42}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּלְבֵּשׁ אֹתוֹ בִגְדֵי־שֵׁשׁ|translate=and he caused him to put on vestures of fine linen}} (''he arrayed him in vestures'', &c.); cf. in the opposite sense, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=23}} (both accusatives after {{GHGheb|text=הִפְשִׁיט}} introduced by {{GHGheb|text=אֶת}}); so with {{GHGheb|text=מִלֵּא|translate=to fill, to fill up}} with something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=15|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=28|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=אִזֵּר|translate=to gird}} some one with something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=33}}; {{GHGheb|text=עִטֵּר|translate=to crown}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=8|verse=6}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=חִסֵּר|translate=to cause}} some one ''to lack'' something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=8|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽאֱכִיל|translate=to feed}} some one with something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=32}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁקָה|translate=to make}} some one ''drink'' something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=32}} ff.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|dd}}
(''b'') Many verbs (even in {{GHGterm|Qal}}) which express an influence upon the object through some external means. The latter, in this case, is attached as a second object. They are especially—

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|ee}}
(α) Verbs which express ''covering, clothing, overlaying'', {{GHGheb|text=חָגַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=29|verse=9}}, {{GHGheb|text=צִפָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=29}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=טוּחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=10}} ff., {{GHGheb|text=עָטַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=13}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=רָגַם אֶבֶן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=7|verse=25}}, &c.; hence also verbs which express ''sowing'' ({{GHGheb|text=זָרַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jud|chapter=9|verse=45}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=10}} 30:23), ''planting'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=2}}), ''anointing'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=45|verse=8}}) ''with'' anything.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|ff}}
(β) Expressions of ''giving'', thus {{GHGheb|text=נָתַן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=15|verse=19}} where the accusative of the thing precedes; ''endowing'', {{GHGheb|text=זָבַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=20}}; and its opposite ''taking away'', as {{GHGheb|text=קָבַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=22|verse=23}}; {{GHGheb|text=בֵּרַךְ|translate=to bless some one with something}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=15|verse=14}}; ''to give graciously'', {{GHGheb|text=חָנַן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=5}}; ''to sustain'' (i.e. to support, to maintain, to furnish) ''with'' anything,<section end=par117 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

395.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par117" />e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=37}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=51|verse=14}} ({{GHGheb|text=סָמַךְ}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=5}} ({{GHGheb|text=סָעַד}}); ''to do something to one'', {{GHGheb|text=גָּמַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=50|verse=15}}, 17, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=24|verse=18}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=קִדֵּם|translate=to come to meet any one with}} something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=21|verse=4}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁלַּם|translate=to repay some one}} with something (with two accusatives, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=13|verse=21}}), and for the accusative of the person cf. εὖ, κακῶς πράττειν τινά. In a wider sense we may also include such phrases as ''they hunt every man his brother with a net'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=2}}; ''to shoot at one with arrows'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=64|verse=8}} (though this is against the accents); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=13|verse=24|translate=seeks him early}} (with) ''discipline'', i.e. ''chastises him betimes'', &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|gg}}
(γ) Expressions of ''asking'' some one ''for'' something, ''desiring'' something ''from'' some one ({{GHGheb|text=שָׁאַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=14|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=137|verse=3}}); ''answering'' any one anything ({{GHGheb|text=עָנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=6|verse=5}}, &c.; cf. in the other conjugations {{GHGheb|text=הֵשִׁיב דָּבָר}} prop. {{GHGterm|verbum reddere}}, with an accusative of the person, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=12|verse=6}}, &c., also in the sense of ''announcing''; sometimes also {{GHGheb|text=הִגִּיד|translate=to declare}} something ''to'' some one, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=26|verse=4}}, &c., for {{GHGheb|text=הִגִּיד לְ}}); {{GHGheb|text=צִוָּה|translate=to enjoin a person}} something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=34|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=46|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=7|verse=23}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|hh}}
(δ) Expressions which mean ''to make, to form, to build something out of'' something; in such cases, besides the accusative of the object proper, another accusative is used for the material of which the thing is made, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּ֫יצֶר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהִים אֶת־הָֽאָדָם עָפָר מִן־הָֽאֲדָמָה|translate=and the Lord formed man of the dust of the ground}}; so with {{GHGheb|text=יָצַר}} also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=7|verse=15}}; further {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=38|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־כֵּלָיו עָשָׂה נְח֫שֶׁת|translate=all the vessels thereof made he of brass}} (for another explanation of the accusative {{GHGheb|text=נְח֫שֶׁת}} [''into brass''], linguistically possible but excluded by the context, see below, ii with kk); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=25|verse=18}}, 28, 26:1, 14 f.29, 27:1, 36:8, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=7|verse=27}}; with a preceding accusative of the material, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=25|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=29|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=27|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=אֲבָנִים שְׁלֵמוֹת תִּבְנֶה אֶת־מִזֳבַּח יְהֹוָה|translate=of unhewn stones shalt thou build the altar of the Lord}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|ii}}
(''c'') Verbs which express ''making, preparing, forming into'' anything, along with the object proper, take a second accusative of the product, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶֽעֱשֶׂה אֹתָם מַטְעַמִּים|translate=I will make them}} (the kids) into ''savoury meat''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=14}}, 16, Ex 26<sup>1 ''b''</sup>, 30:25, 32:4, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=44|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=8|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=18|verse=32}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־הָֽאֲבָנִים מִזְבֵּחַ וַיִּבְנֶה|translate=and he built the stones}} (into) ''an altar''; cf. 10:12. So also {{GHGheb|text=אָפָה}}, with two accusatives, ''to bake'' something ''into'' something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=39}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=24|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=שִׂים}} (prop. ''to set up for'' something, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=37}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=28|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=39|verse=9}}, and similarly {{GHGheb|text=הֵרִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=45}}) ''to change into'' something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=8|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=50|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=1|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=4|verse=13|hidebook=1}}; with two accusatives of the person (''to appoint, promote'' any one to the position of a...), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=נָתַן}} is also used in the same sense with two accusatives, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=5}}, and {{GHGheb|text=שִׁית}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=34}}; as a rule, however, the description of the office, and also frequently of the product, is introduced by {{GHGheb|text=לְ|translate=to}}, {{GHGpar|119|t}}; also {{GHGheb|text=שִׁית|translate=to make a thing so and so}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=1|hidebook=1}}; with a personal object, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=21|verse=7}},<ref>Cf. a very pregnant expression of this kind in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=21|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=כִּי תְשִׁיתֵ֫מוֹ שֶׁ֫כֶם|translate=for thou shalt make them}} (as) ''a neck'', i.e. ''thou shalt cause them to turn their necks'' (backs) ''to me''; similarly {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=41}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=22|verse=41}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=27}}); {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽיְבַי נָתַ֫תָּה לִּי עֹרֶף|translate=thou hast given mine enemies unto me as a back}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=18|verse=17}}.</ref> 91:9); {{GHGheb|text=הֶחְשִׁיךְ|translate=to make dark}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=8}}. Of the same class also are instances like {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=28|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫בֶן יָצוּק נְחוּשָׁה|translate=a stone they smelt into brass}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=30}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּקְרָעֶ֫הָ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר קְרָעִים|translate=and rent it}} (the garment) ''into twelve pieces''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=26}}, accusative of the product before the object proper, after {{GHGheb|text=לְהַשְׁאוֹת|translate=to lay waste}}.
<section end="par117" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

396.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par117 />On a second object with {{GHGterm|verba sentiendi}} (as {{GHGheb|text=יָדַע|translate=to know}} something ''to be'' something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=7|verse=25}}; {{GHGheb|text=רָאָה|translate=to see, find to be}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=חָשַׁב|translate=to esteem}} one ''to be'' something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=53|verse=4}}, elsewhere always construed with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} or {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}}), cf. h.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|kk}}
Rem. At first sight some of the examples given above appear to be identical in character with those treated under ''hh''; thus it is possible, e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=18|verse=32}}, by a translation which equally suits the sense, ''he built from the stones an altar'', to explain {{GHGheb|text=מִזְבֵּחַ}} as the nearer object and {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־הָֽאֲבָנִים}} as an accusative of the material, and the construction would then be exactly the same as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=27|verse=6}}. In reality, however, the fundamental idea is by no means the same. Not that in the living language an accusative of the material in the one case, and in the other an accusative of the product were consciously distinguished. As Driver ({{GHGcite|title=Tenses}}, § 195) rightly observes, the remoter accusative in both cases is, strictly speaking, in apposition to the nearer. This is especially evident in such examples as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=25|translate=thou shalt not build them}} (the stones of the altar) {{GHGheb|text=גָּזִית}} as ''hewn stones'', cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=27}}. The main point is, which of the two accusatives, as being primarily affected (or aimed at) by the action, is to be made the more prominent; and on this point neither the position of the words (the nearer object, mostly determinate, as a rule follows immediately after the verb), nor even the context admits of much doubt. Thus in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=18|verse=32}} the treatment of the stones is the primary object in view, the erection of the altar for which they were intended is the secondary; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=27|verse=6}} the case is reversed.

{{GHGmargin-letter|117|ll}}
(''d'') Finally, the second accusative sometimes more closely determines the nearer object by indicating the part or member specially affected by the action,<ref>Analogous to this is the σχῆμα καθ᾽ ὅλον καὶ κατὰ μέρος in Greek epic poetry, e.g. ποῖόν σε ἔπος φύγε ἕρκος ὀδόντων.</ref> e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=3|verse=8}} ''for thou hast smitten all mine enemies'' {{GHGheb|text=לֶ֫תִי}} (as to) ''the cheek bone'', equivalent to ''upon the cheek bone''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=21|translate=let us not smite him}} {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫פֶשׁ}} in ''the life'', i.e. let us not kill him; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=22|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=27}}; also with {{GHGheb|text=שׁוּף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=15}}; with {{GHGheb|text=רָעָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=16}}; in poetry the object specially concerned is, by a bold construction, even placed first, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=11}} (with {{GHGheb|text=מָחַץ}}).<section end=par117 />

<section begin=par118 />{{GHGpar-heading|118|The Looser Subordination of the Accusative to the Verb}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|a}}
'''1.''' The various forms of the looser subordination of a noun to the verb are distinguished from the different kinds of the accusative of the object (§ 117) by their specifying not the persons or things directly affected by the action, but some ''more immediate circumstance'' under which an action or an event takes place. Of such circumstances the most common are those of ''place, time, measure, cause'', and finally the ''manner'' of performing the action. These nearer definitions are, as a rule, placed ''after'' the verb; they may, however, also precede it.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|b}}
Rem. That the cases thus loosely subordinated to the verb are to be regarded as ''accusatives'' is seen first from the fact that in certain instances the {{GHGterm|nota accusativi}} ({{GHGheb|text=את}}) is prefixed; secondly from the fact that in one form of<section end=par118 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

397.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par118 />the ''casus loci'' a termination ({{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}) is employed, in which (according to {{GHGpar|90|c}}) the old accusatival ending is preserved; and finally from the consistency with which classical Arabic puts these nearer definitions in the accusative (which may be recognized by its form) even under circumstances in which one would be rather inclined to expect a nominative in apposition.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|c}}
The relation subsisting between the circumstantial accusative and the accusative of the object is especially apparent when the former (as e.g. in a statement of the goal after a verb of motion) is immediately connected with its verb. But even the more loosely connected circumstantial definitions are certainly to be regarded as originally objects of a governing word habitually omitted, only that the consciousness of this closer government was at length lost, and the accusative more and more acquired an independent value as a ''casus adverbialis''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|d}}
'''2.''' The accusative serves to define more precisely the ''place'' (''accus. loci''), either (''a'') in answer to the question ''whither?'' after verbs of motion,<ref>So commonly in Sanskrit; in Greek only poetically, e.g. Iliad i. 317 κνίση δ᾽ οὐρανὸν ἷκεν: in Latin, e.g. ''rus ire, Romam proficisci''.</ref> or (''b'') in answer to the question ''where?'' after verbs of ''being, dwelling, resting'', &c. (but also after transitive verbs, see the examples), or finally (''c'') to define more precisely the ''extent'' in space, in answer to the question ''how far? how high? how much?'', &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|e}}
Instead of the simple accusative, the locative (see above, {{GHGpar|90|c}})
<ref>Hence e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=26}} the Masora requires {{GHGheb|text=הַגָּ֫גָה}} instead of the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} {{GHGheb|text=הַגָּג}}.</ref> is frequently found in the cases mentioned under ''f'' (sometimes also in those under ''g'') or the preposition {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־}},<ref>So in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=18}} for {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־בֵּית י׳}} the better reading is {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־בּ׳}}.</ref> especially before persons as the aim of the movement, or {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}}, usually, to express being ''at'' a place.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|f}}
Examples of (''a''): {{GHGheb|text=נֵצֵא הַשָּׂדֶה|translate=let us go out into the field}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=11}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=לָלֶ֫כֶת תַּרְשִׁישׁ|translate=to go to Tarshish}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=20|verse=36}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=10|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=13|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=27|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=23|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=21|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=4|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=17|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=1|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=11|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=1|verse=8}} (?), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=134|verse=2}}; with {{GHGheb|text=לָקַח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=14}}; with {{GHGheb|text=נָתַן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=6|verse=24}}; with the ''accus. loci'' emphatically preceding (cf. Driver on {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=5|verse=8}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=20|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=32|verse=5|hidebook=1}}; with {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹא}} (in the sense of ''aggredi'', equivalent to {{GHGheb|text=עַל־ בּוֹא}}, cf. {{GHGpar|117|a}}, note 2) the ''personal'' aim also is poetically added in the accusative, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=32|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=38|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=10|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=28|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=20|verse=22|hidebook=1}}; but in the last passage it is better taken as an accusative of the object (cf. the German ''einen ankommen, überkommen''). See also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=10|verse=36}} (where {{GHGheb|text=שׁוּב}} can hardly be transitive); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=20}} (where, however, {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־}} has probably fallen out after {{GHGheb|text=ישראל}}; so Strack).—Finally, cf. also the use of {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} for {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר ... שָׁ֫מָּה|translate=whither}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=13|verse=27}}.—The ''accus. loci'' occurs after a passive, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=15}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|g}}
Examples of (''b''): {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=11}} ''remain a widow'' {{GHGheb|text=בֵּית אָבִיךְ}} ''in thy father’s house''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hos|chapter=12|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=6|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=33|verse=20}}; {{GHGheb|text=פֶּ֫תַח הָאֹ֫הֶל|translate=in the tent door}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=1}}, 10, 19:11, and frequently. As observed by Driver on {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=29}}, accusatives of this kind are almost without exception (but cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=16|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=33|verse=20}}) connected with a noun in the genitive. In all the above examples, however, the accusative may have been preferred to the natural construction with {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} (which is not rare even with {{GHGheb|text=בֵּית}} and {{GHGheb|text=פֶ֫תַח}}) for euphonic reasons, in order to avoid the combination of such sounds as {{GHGheb|text=בְּב׳}} and {{GHGheb|text=בְּפ׳}}; cf., moreover, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=18|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=6|verse=8}} ({{GHGheb|text=הַמִּזְבֵּחַ}} instead of the usual {{GHGheb|text=הַמִּזְבֵּ֫חָה}}<section end=par118 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

398.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par118 />{{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=29|verse=13}}, &c.); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=2}}, 19,<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=דֶּ֫רֶךְ}} is not to be taken as an ''accus. loci'' (''on the way''), but as an ''accus. of respect (with regard to the way)''; see below, m.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=7|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=9|verse=14|hidebook=1}}. On {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=30}} see {{GHGpar|116|i}}; on {{GHGheb|text=יָּשַׁב}}, with the ''accus. loci'', see {{GHGpar|117|bb}}. On the other hand, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=6|verse=3}}, according to the LXX, a verb of ''giving'' has dropped out before {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫רֶץ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|h}}
Examples of (''c''): {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=20}} ''fifteen cubits upward did the waters prevail''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=40|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=רַק הַכִּסֵּא אֶגְדַּל מִמֶּ֫ךָּ|translate=only in the throne will I be greater than thou}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=19}} ''we went'' (through) ''all that great and terrible wilderness''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=3}}. Of the same kind also are such cases as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=16}} (''according to the number of your persons'', for which elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=לְמִסְפַּר־}} is used); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=4}} (with the accus. preceding); 6:18, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=21|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=5}}.—A statement of weight is put in the accusative in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=26}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|i}}
'''3.''' The accusative is employed to determine more precisely the ''time'' (''accus. temporis''), (''a'') in answer to the question ''when?'' e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַיּוֹם|translate=the day}}, i.e. ''on the day'' (in question), ''at that time'', but also ''on this day'', i.e. ''to-day'', or finally ''by day'', equivalent to {{GHGheb|text=יוֹמָם}}, like {{GHGheb|text=עֶ֫רֶב|translate=at evening}}, {{GHGheb|text=לַ֫יְלָה|translate=noctu}}, {{GHGheb|text=בֹּ֫קֶר|translate=in the morning, early}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=4}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=צָֽהֳרַ֫יִם|translate=at noonday}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=91|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם אֶחָד|translate=on one and the same day}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=45}}; {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁנָא|translate=in sleep}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=127|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=תְּחִלַּת קְצִיר שְׂעֹרִים}} ({{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּתְ׳}}) ''at the beginning of barley harvest'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=21|verse=9}}; in stating a date, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=11|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=4|hidebook=1}} ''in the thirteenth year''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|k}}
(''b'') In answer to the question ''how long?'' e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=14}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־יְמֵי חַיֶּ֫יךָ|translate=all the days of thy life}}; 7:4 ''forty days and forty nights''; 7:24, 14:4, 15:13, 21:34, 29:18, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=9}} (''for six days''); 23:15, 31:17; {{GHGheb|text=עֽוֹלָמִים|translate=for ever}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=13}}; also with the accusative made determinate, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=13|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=אֵת שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים|translate=throughout the seven days}} in question, mentioned immediately before; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=9|verse=25}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|l}}
'''4.''' The accusative is sometimes used of abstract ideas to state the reason (''accus. causae''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=25}} ''thou shalt not come thither'' {{GHGheb|text=יִרְאַת שָׁמִיר|translate=for fear of briers}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|m}}
'''5.''' Finally the accusative is used very variously (as an ''accus. adverbialis'' in the narrower sense), in order to describe more precisely the ''manner'' in which an action or state takes place. In English such accusatives are mostly rendered by ''in, with, as, in the form'' or ''manner of ..., according to, in relation to, with regard to''. For more convenient classification we may distinguish them as—

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|n}}
(''a'') Adjectives expressing ''state'', placed ''after'' the verb to describe more accurately some bodily or other external condition, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=20|verse=2}} ''walking'' {{GHGheb|text=עָרוֹם וְיָחֵף|translate=naked and barefoot}}; cf. verse 3, 8:21, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=18|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=שָׁלֵם}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=1|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=107|verse=5}} (but in 15:2 {{GHGheb|text=תָּמִים}} is rather a substantive directly dependent on {{GHGheb|text=הוֹלֵךְ}} = ''he that walketh'' in ''uprightness''; cf. {{GHGpar|117|r}}, note); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=28}}. After an accusative, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=15|verse=18}}; to specify some mental state, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=35}} ({{GHGheb|text=אָבֵל}}).—''Before'' the verb (and then with a certain emphasis), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=2|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=5|verse=14}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=20|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=26|hidebook=1}}<section end=par118 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

399.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par118 />(unless {{GHGheb|text=יָקָר}} be a substantive); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=1|verse=21}} ({{GHGheb|text=מְלֵאָה}} parallel with the adverb {{GHGheb|text=רֵיקָם}}). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=2|verse=7}} the text is clearly corrupt.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|o}}
Those examples are especially instructive in which the adjective expressing a state, although referring to several, is nevertheless used in the singular, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=עָרוֹם הִלְּכוּ|translate=naked}}, i.e. in the condition of one naked, ''they go about''; cf. verse 7 and 12:17. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=20|verse=4}} the singular occurs ''after'' a plural object, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=5}} the {{GHGterm|masc.}} after the 2nd sing. {{GHGterm|fem.}} imperative, which clearly proves that the term expressing the state is not conceived as being in apposition, but as an indeclinable adverb.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|p}}
(''b'') Participles, again either ''after'' the verb, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=16|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=43|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=7|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=2|verse=8}}, or ''before'' it, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=57|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=36|verse=35}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=56|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=92|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=20|verse=14}}; cf. also the substantival use of the participles Niphʿal {{GHGheb|text=נֽוֹרָאוֹת|translate=in a fearful manner}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=14}}) and {{GHGheb|text=נִפְלָאוֹת|translate=in a wonderful manner}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=37|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=8|verse=24}}.—Also participles in connexion with genitives, as {{GHGheb|text=מִתְהַלֵּךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=8}} (cf. also {{GHGheb|text=בָּאָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=6}}), are to be regarded as expressing a state and not as being in apposition, since in the latter case they would have to take the article.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=7|verse=7}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=2|verse=10}} the ''explicative Wāw'' (equivalent to ''and that too'') is also prefixed to the participle. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=69|verse=4}} for {{GHGheb|text=מְיַחֵל}} read {{GHGheb|text=מִיַּחֵל}}.—On {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=10|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=19|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=1|verse=4}}, cf. the note on {{GHGpar|131|h}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|q}}
(''c'') Substantives<ref>Cf. above, {{GHGpar|100|c}}, on certain substantives which have completely become adverbs; and {{GHGpar|113|h}} and k on the adverbial use of the infinitive absolute.</ref> in the most varied relations: thus, as describing an external state, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=2|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=וְלֹא תֵֽלְכוּ רוֹמָה|translate=neither shall ye walk haughtily}} (as opposed to {{GHGheb|text=שְׁחוֹחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=60|verse=14}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=6|verse=9}} (accus. before the verb=as ''unleavened cakes''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=57|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=7|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=9}}; as stating the position of a disease, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=15|verse=23}} ''he was diseased'' {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־רַגְלָיו}} in ''his feet'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=16|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּרַגְלָיו}}), analogous to the cases discussed in {{GHGpar|117|ll}} and {{GHGpar|121|d}} (''d''); as describing a spiritual, mental, or moral state, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=32|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=9|verse=2}} ({{GHGheb|text=פֶּה אֶחָד|translate=with one accord}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=13}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=24|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=3|verse=9}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=23|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=3}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלוֹם}} is adjectival, and the passage is to be explained as in ''n''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=12|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=14|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=56|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=58|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=75|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=31|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=9}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=19|verse=16}}, &c., in the expression {{GHGheb|text=הָלַךְ רָכִיל|translate=to go up and down}} as ''a tale-bearer''; also {{GHGheb|text=בֶּ֫טַח|translate=unawares}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=30|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=מֵֽישָׁרִים|translate=uprightly}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=58|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=75|verse=3|hidebook=1}} (in both places ''before'' the verb); as stating the age, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=33}} (if the text be right) {{GHGheb|text=יָמ֫וּתוּ אֲנָשִׁים|translate=they shall die}} as ''men'', i.e. ''in the prime of life''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=18}} ({{GHGheb|text=נַ֫עַר}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=65|verse=20}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=16}}; as specifying a number more accurately, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=8}} [in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלוֹמִים|translate=wholly}} (?) is corrupt; read {{GHGheb|text=גָּלוּת שְׁלֵמָה}} with LXX for {{GHGheb|text=הָגְלָת שׁ׳}}]; as stating the consequence of the action, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=15|verse=18}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|r}}
The description of the external or internal state may follow, in poetry, in the form of a comparison with some well-known class, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּקְרָא אַרְיֵה|translate=and he cried}} as ''a lion''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=22|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=18}} ({{GHGheb|text=כַּדּוּר|translate=like a ball}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=2|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=11|verse=1}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=צִפּוֹר}} be vocative); 58:9<sup> ''b''</sup> (unless the force of the preceding {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} is carried on, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=90|verse=4}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=144|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=5}} ({{GHGheb|text=פְּרָאִים}}, before the verb); 41:7 ''shut up together'' as with ''a close seal''.<ref>It is, as a matter of fact, permissible to speak of the above examples as ''comparatio decurtata'', but it must not be assumed that the comparative particle {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}}, which is otherwise regularly prefixed (see s), has actually dropped out.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|s}}
'''6.''' To the expressions describing a state belong finally those nouns which are introduced by the comparative particle {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}},<ref>On the use of {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} as a prefix, cf. {{GHGpar|102|c}}.</ref> since the {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} is to<section end=par118 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

400.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par118 />be regarded as originally a substantive<ref>Schwabe ({{GHGcite|title={{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} nach seinem Wesen und Gebrauch im alttestam. Kanon gewürdigt}}, Halle, 1883) contests this explanation (which is defended especially by Fleischer and is certainly indisputable). He, with Gesenius and Ewald, places {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} as a preposition on the same footing as {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, and believes it to be probably connected with the stem {{GHGheb|text=כּוּן}} as well as with {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}} and {{GHGheb|text=כֵּן}}. The above view of {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} as a substantive of course does not imply that the language as we have it is still in every case conscious of the substantival meaning.—On {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} in numerical statements, in the sense of ''about, nearly'', see the Lexicon.</ref> in the sense of ''amount, kind'' (''instar''), standing in the accusative (so that {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} is equivalent to ''as a kind of, after the manner of, according to''), while the following noun represents a genitive governed by the {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}}. From this, which is the proper meaning of the {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}}, may be explained its power of representing a great many pregnant relations, which in English can only be rendered by the help of prepositions.<ref>It would be altogether unsuitable here also (see above, note 2 on r) to assume a loss of the preposition. Such examples as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=26}} ({{GHGheb|text=כְּבָרִֽאשֹׁנָה}} and {{GHGheb|text=כְּבַתְּחִלָּה}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=37}} ({{GHGheb|text=כְּמִפְּנֵי}}) are to be explained from the fact that here the preposition and substantive had already become simply ''one'' word before the {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} was prefixed. We find also {{GHGheb|text=כְּעַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=63|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=14}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=32|verse=19}}; cf. Driver on {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=14}} ({{GHGheb|text=כְּבַֽחֲצִי}}), where the text is wholly corrupt.</ref> Thus the comparison may refer to—

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|t}}
(''a'') The ''place'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is.|chapter=5|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=כְּדָבְרָם|translate=after the manner of}}, i.e. ''as in their pasture''; 23:15 as (it is said) ''in the song of the harlot''; 28:21, 29:7 {{GHGheb|text=כּֽחֲלוֹם|translate=as in a dream}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|u}}
(''b'') The ''time'', especially in the combination {{GHGheb|text=כְּיוֹם|translate=after the manner of the day}}, equivalent to ''as in the day'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=9|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=2|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=כִּימֵי|translate=as in the days of}} ..., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=2|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=9|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=12|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=9|verse=11}}; cf. moreover, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=22|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=39}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, and the expressions {{GHGheb|text=בְּיוֹם בְּיוֹם}} ''as day by day=as in the former days'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=כְּפַ֫עַם בְּפַ֫עַם|translate=as at other times}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=10}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=כְּשָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה|translate=as in former years}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=17|verse=4}}; cf. {{GHGpar|123|c}}. Of a different character is the use of {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} as a simple particle of time, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=כָּעֵת חַיָּה|translate=at this time}} (not ''about the time''), when it lives again, i.e. at the end of a year; {{GHGheb|text=כָּעֵת מָחָר|translate=to-morrow at this time}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=5}}, and the frequent connexion of {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} with the infinitive construct to express a definite time (in the sense of a pluperfect), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=34|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=29}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|v}}
(''c'') The ''person'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=31}} ''should he deal with our sister as'' with ''a harlot?''

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|w}}
(''d'') The ''thing'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=33|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=28|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=כְּמוֹ־אֵשׁ|translate=as a fire}}, i.e. ''as it were by fire'' (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=25}} {{GHGheb|text=כַּבֹּר|translate=as}} with ''lye''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=23}} {{GHGheb|text=כַּמָּטָר|translate=as}} for ''the rain'' (they waited for me); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=14}} (''as'' in ''a garment''); 38:30 {{GHGheb|text=כְּאֶבֶן|translate=as}} to ''stone'' (the waters are solidified in freezing).

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|x}}
Rem. According to the earlier grammarians, {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} is sometimes used pleonastically, i.e. not to indicate a similarity (as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=14|verse=35}} ''as it were'', i.e. ''something like''), but simply to introduce the predicate (''Kaph veritatis''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=7|verse=2}} ''for he was'' {{GHGheb|text=כְּאִישׁ אֱמֶת|translate=a faithful man}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=כְּפֶשַׂע}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=כַּמָּ֫וֶת}}. Such a pleonasm is of course out of the question. At the most a ''Kaph veritatis'' can only be admitted in the sense that the comparison is sometimes introduced by {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} with a certain emphasis (equivalent to ''in every respect like''); thus {{GHGheb|text=כְּאִישׁ אֱמֶת}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=7|verse=2}} means simply ''of the nature of a faithful man'', i.e. as only a faithful man can be; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=13|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=4|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=5|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ob|chapter=1|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=2|verse=4|hidebook=1}}; also {{GHGheb|text=כִּמְעַט}} in such passages as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=105|verse=12}} ''yea, very few''; but e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=9}} ''only just, a very small''...<section end=par118 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

401.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par119 />{{GHGpar-heading|119|The Subordination of Nouns to the Verb by means of Prepositions}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|a}}
'''1.''' In general. As is the case with regard to the looser subordination of nouns to the verbal idea (§ 118), so also their subordination by means of prepositions is used to represent the more immediate circumstances (of place, time, cause, purpose, measure, association, or separation) under which an action or event is accomplished. In the case of most prepositions some idea of a relation of ''space'' underlies the construction, which then, in a wider sense, is extended to the ideas of time, motive, or other relations conceived by the mind.

On the origin of the prepositions and the original case-relation in which they stand to the nouns governed by them, cf. § 101, where a list of the prepositions is given with their original meanings. Cf. also § 102 on the prefixes, and § 103 on the union of prepositions with suffixes.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|b}}
'''2.''' A not unimportant part is played in Hebrew by the ''compounding'' of prepositions to represent more accurately the relations of place, which either precede or follow the action. In the former case {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}}, and in the latter (which is not so frequent) {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־}} occurs before other prepositions of place; cf. e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=7|verse=15}} ''the Lord took me'' {{GHGheb|text=מֵאֽחֲרֵי הַצֹּאן|translate=from behind the flock}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=9|verse=18}} ''turn thee'' {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־אַֽחֲרָי|translate=to behind me}}, i.e., ''turn thee behind me''; {{GHGheb|text=מֵעִם־}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֵאֵת|translate=from being with}} ..., as in French ''de chez, d’après quelqu’un''.<ref>In other cases French, as well as English and German, can only emphasize ''one'' of the two combined ideas; thus, such expressions as ''il prend le chapeau sur la table'', German and English ''er nimmt den Hut vom Tisch'', ''he takes his hat from the table'', all regard the action from one point of view only; the Hebrew here brings out both aspects of it by means of {{GHGheb|text=מֵעַל־|translate=from upon}}, cf. e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=6}}.</ref> For further examples, see c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|c}}
Rem. 1. We must ''not'' regard as combined prepositions in the above sense either those ''substantives'' which have become prepositions only by their union with prefixes, as {{GHGheb|text=לִפְנֵי|translate=before}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִפְּנֵי}}, {{GHGheb|text=לְמַ֫עַן|translate=on account of}} (but e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מִלִּפְנֵי|translate=from before}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=16}}, &c., is such a compound); nor ''adverbs'', which are also formed by combining words which were originally substantives (also used as prepositions) with prepositions, as {{GHGheb|text=מִחוּץ|translate=without}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִתַּ֫חַת}} in the sense of ''below'',<ref>Hence not to be confounded with {{GHGheb|text=מִתַּ֫חַת|translate=from under}}, in such examples as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=22|verse=27}}, which is a real compound preposition. In the above-mentioned adverbs also the {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} was ''originally'' by no means pleonastic; {{GHGheb|text=מִתַּ֫חַת}} denotes properly the locality, regarded primarily as a place ''from beneath'' which something proceeds, and so on. This original sense of the {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}}, however, has become so much obscured by its regular combination with words of place to form independent adverbs, that it is even prefixed (evidently only on the analogy of such common adverbs as {{GHGheb|text=מֵעַל־}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִתַּ֫חַת}}) in cases where it is really inadmissible, owing to the meaning of the adverb, e.g. in {{GHGheb|text=מִבַּלְעֲדֵי}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִלְּבַד|translate=without}}, cf. also such examples as {{GHGheb|text=מִבְּלִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִמּוּל}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִנֶּ֫גֶד}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִשָּׁם}} (''there''), &c. Since a {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} is not usually repeated after {{GHGheb|text=מִלְּבַד}}, it appears as if {{GHGheb|text=מִלְּבַד}} by a transposition of the {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} stood for the usual {{GHGheb|text=לְבַד מִן־}}. In reality, however, the preposition which forms the adverb into a preposition is omitted here, as in {{GHGheb|text=מֵעַל}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִתַּ֫חַת}} without a following {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} (see above). Properly {{GHGheb|text=מִלְּבַד}} has a purely adverbial meaning=''taken by itself'', like {{GHGheb|text=מִלְּמַ֫עְלָה מִמַּ֫עַל}} (Syriac ''men le‛ēl'') ''above'' (adv.), as distinguished from {{GHGheb|text=מִמַּ֫עַל לְ}} or {{GHGheb|text=מֵעַל־לְ}} (Syriac ''le‛ēl men''), ''over, upon something''.—Also {{GHGheb|text=לְמִן־|translate=from ... onward}} is not for {{GHGheb|text=מִן־לְ}}, but the {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} serves merely (just like the Latin ''usqus'' in ''usque a, usque ad, usqus ex'') to indicate expressly the starting-point, as an exact ''terminus a quo'' (of place or time).</ref> {{GHGheb|text=מֵעָל}}<section end=par119 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

402.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par119 />''above'' (so also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=39}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=25|hidebook=1}}, not ''from above''). These adverbs of place, however, may become prepositions by the addition of {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מִחוּץ לְ|translate=outside as regards}} ..., i.e. ''outside of something'', in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=13}} even after a transitive verb of motion; {{GHGheb|text=מִתַּ֫חַת לְ|translate=below as regards}} ..., i.e. ''under something'' (cf. {{GHGheb|text=עַד־מִתַּ֫חַת לְ|translate=until they came under}} ..., {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=7|verse=11}}), {{GHGheb|text=מֵעַל לְ|translate=over something}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=לְבַד}} prop. ''in separation''; {{GHGheb|text=לְבַד מִן־|translate=in separation from}}, i.e. ''apart from, besides''. Only rarely in such a case is the {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} omitted for the sake of brevity, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=26|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=מִתַּ֫חַת מַיִם|translate=beneath}} the ''waters''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=3|verse=28}} ({{GHGheb|text=מֵעַל־}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|d}}
2. Real combinations of prepositions (each retaining its full force) occur—

(''a'') With {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}}, in {{GHGheb|text=מֵאַחַר}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֵאַֽחֲרֵי}} (see above) ''from behind'' something; {{GHGheb|text=מֵאֵת}} and {{GHGheb|text=מֵעִם|translate=from with}} (see above); {{GHGheb|text=מִבֵּין}} or {{GHGheb|text=מִבֵּינוֹת|translate=from between}} something (with motion in either direction, see e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=10}}); {{GHGheb|text=מִלִּפְנֵי|translate=from before}} (see above); sometimes also {{GHGheb|text=מִמּוּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=8}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=מֵעַל־|translate=from upon}}, i.e. ''off from''; {{GHGheb|text=מִתַּ֫חַת|translate=away from under}} (see footnote <sup>2</sup> on p. 377).

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|e}}
(''b'') With {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־}}, in {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־אַֽחֲרֵי|translate=to behind}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־בֵּינוֹת|translate=to between}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־מִבֵּית לְ|translate=forth between}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=11|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־מִחוּץ לְ|translate=forth without}}, i.e. ''out in front of'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־תַּ֫חַת|translate=down under}}.<ref>Also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־תַּ֫חַת}} by a pregnant construction is virtually dependent on the idea of ''coming into'', contained in the preceding {{GHGheb|text=אֵין־}}.</ref>—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=5}} the two prepositions of motion are combined in a peculiarly pregnant construction, {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־מִצִּנִּים}} (he goes thither and takes it) ''out of the thorns'', i.e. he taketh it ''even out of the thorns'', but the text is hardly correct.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|f}}
'''3.''' A general view of the union of certain verbs, or whole classes of verbs, with particular prepositions, especially in explanation of certain idioms and pregnant expressions.<ref>A summary of ''all'' the relations and senses in which a preposition may be used, belongs not to the Grammar but to the Lexicon.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|g}}
(''a'') {{GHGheb|text=(אֱלֵי) אֶל־}}<ref>Cf. Mitchell, ‘The proposition ''el'',’ in the ''Journal of the Society of Biblical Literature and Exegesis'', 1888, p. 143 ff., and especially A. Noordtzij, ''Het hebreeuwsche voorzetsel'' {{GHGheb|text=אל}}, Leiden, 1896, a thorough examination of its uses, and especially of the relation between {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־}} and {{GHGheb|text=עַל־}}.</ref> ''towards'', properly an expression of ''motion'' or at least ''direction'' towards something (either in the sense of ''up to''={{GHGheb|text=עַד}}, or ''into''={{GHGheb|text=אֶל־תּוֹךְ}}), is used after verbs not only in answer to the question ''whither?'' but by a specially pregnant construction, in answer to the question ''where?'' e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=41|verse=12}} ''they''<section end=par119 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

403.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par119 />''found him'' {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־מַ֫יִם רַבִּים|translate=by the great waters}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=16|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=13|verse=20}}, and a still more remarkable instance in 8:30 {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־מְקוֹם שִׁבְתְּךָ אֶל־הַשָּׁמַ֫יִם}}. This combination of ''two'' different ideas, of motion ''to'' a place and being or acting ''in'' the place (very plainly seen in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=16|verse=6}} ''but to the place which the Lord thy God shall choose''... shalt thou bring thine offering and ''there shalt thou sacrifice'', &c.), is the same as the Greek use of εἰς, ἐς for ἐν, the Latin ''in potestatem, in amicitiam ditionemque esse, manere'' (Cic. Verr. 5, 38; Div. 2, 14, &c.); cf. also the common German expressions ''zu'' Hause, ''zu'' Leipzig sein, ''zu'' Bette liegen, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|h}}
(''b'') {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}}.<ref>Cf. Wandel, ''De particulae Hebr.'' {{GHGheb|text=בְּ|translate=indole, vi, usu}}, Jena, 1875.</ref> Underlying the very various uses of this preposition is either the idea of being or moving within some definite region, or some sphere of space or time (with the infinitive, a simultaneous action, &c.), or else the idea of ''fastening on'' something, ''close connexion with'' something (also in a metaphorical sense, following some kind of pattern, e.g. the advice or command of some one {{GHGheb|text=בִּדְבַר פ׳}}, {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽעֲצַת פ׳}}, or in a comparison, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=26}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּצַלְמֵ֫נוּ כִדְמוּתֵ֫נוּ|translate=in our image, after our likeness}}; cf. 1:27, 5:1, 3), or finally the idea of ''relying'' or ''depending'' upon..., or even of merely ''striking'' or ''touching'' something.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|i}}
Thus the use of {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} is explained—

(1) In the sense of ''among'' (in the domain of), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=יָשָׁר בָּֽאָדָם אָ֫יִן|translate=there is none upright among men}}; in the sense of ''consisting of'', in specifying the constituents of a collective idea, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=21}} ''and all flesh died''... ''in'' (=consisting of) ''fowl'', &c. 8:17, 9:10, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=4|verse=3}}. Also after ideas of ''appearing, manifesting oneself, representing, being'', in the sense of ''as, in the capacity of'' (prop. in the sphere, after the manner of, see above), ''consisting of''..., ''tanquam'', the {{GHGheb|text=בְּ|translate=essentiae}} of the earlier grammarians, corresponding to the Greek ἐν, the Latin ''in'',<ref>e.g. ''res in praeda captae'', i.e. things taken as spoil; see Nägelsbach, ''Lat. Stilistik'', § 123:4. On the Hebrew {{GHGheb|text=בְּ|translate=essentiae}}, see Hauschild in the ''Festschrift zur Einweihung des Goethegymn''. Frankf. a. M. 1897, p. 163.</ref> and the French ''en'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=6|verse=3}} ''I appeared unto Abraham''... {{GHGheb|text=בְּאֵל שַׁדָּי|translate=as El Shaddai}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=23|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=וְהוּא בְאֶחָד|translate=but he is}} (manifests himself as) ''one'', i.e. he remains always the same; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=26|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=62|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּמְתֵי מְעָט|translate=in the condition of being few}}, cf. 10:22 ''to the number of seventy''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=39|verse=7}}.—Cf. also such examples as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=18|verse=4}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=146|verse=5|hidebook=1}}) {{GHGheb|text=בְּעֶזְרִי|translate=as my help}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=26|verse=14}} ''being unclean''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=16}} ''in Sion'' (i.e. ''I make Sion a foundation''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=20|verse=41}} ''as a sweet savour''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=3|verse=26}}, perhaps also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=2}} ''in'' (i.e. ''as'') ''a flame of fire''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=66|verse=15}} ''with'' (i.e. ''like'') ''fire''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=31|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=37|verse=20|hidebook=1}} (102:4). For the origin of all these forms of expression {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=54|verse=6}} is especially instructive, since {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנָי בְּסֹֽמְכֵי נַפְשִׁי}} is not meant to refer to the Lord as ''belonging to'' the {{GHGheb|text=סֹֽמְכִים}}, but only to ascribe to him a similar character, i.e. ''the Lord is one who upholds my soul''; so also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=99|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=35}} [the plur. as in {{GHGpar|124|g}}–i].<ref>Other instances formerly cited here ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=55|verse=19}}, where {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} is used before the subject) as well as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּיָהּ שְׁמוֹ|translate=Jah is his name}}, are textually very uncertain. Cf. Cheyne, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|SBOT.|Sacred Books of the Old Testament, ed. by P. Haupt. Lpz. and Baltimore, 1893 ff.}}}} Isaiah, p. 173, on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=4}}.</ref>—Cf. Gesenius, {{GHGcite|title=Thes. Linguae Hebr.}}, i. 174 f., and Delitzsch on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=2}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|k}}
(2) To introduce the object after transitive verbs, which denote ''touching, striking, reaching to'' (thus to some extent a fastening on, see above) something, in English sometimes rendered by ''at, on'', &c., and in German generally by compounds with ''an'', e.g. ''anfassen''={{GHGheb|text=אָחַז בְּ}}, ''anrühren''={{GHGheb|text=נָגַע בְּ}}, &c. To the same category belongs also the construction of verbs denoting ''authority'' ({{GHGheb|text=מָלַךְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=מָשַׁל}}, {{GHGheb|text=נָגַשׂ}}, {{GHGheb|text=רָדָה}}, the last prop. ''to tread on''...) with {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}}, inasmuch as the exercise of the authority is regarded as a laying hold of the person ruled; so also, the introduction of the object by {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} after certain {{GHGterm|verba dicendi}}, or when the mental action is to be represented as extending ''to'' some one or something: e.g.<section end=par119 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

404.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par119 />{{GHGheb|text=קָרָא בְ}} to call ''on'' some one, {{GHGheb|text=נִשְׁבַּע בְּ|translate=iurare per aliquem|en=to swear by}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁאַל בְּ|translate=to enquire of}} some one. Again; {{GHGheb|text=רָאָה בְ|translate=to look upon}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁמַע בְּ|translate=to hearken to}} (but cf. also {{GHGpar|404|m|nonumber=1}}), generally with the secondary idea of participation, or of the pleasure with which one sees or hears anything, especially pleasure at the misfortunes of others, hence {{GHGheb|text=רָאָה בְ|translate=to see his desire on any one ''or'' anything}}; cf. however, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=16}} ''let me not look upon the death of the child''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=19}} {{GHGtranslate|because they had looked ''[irreverently]'' at the ark of the Lord}}.

Closely related to this is the use of {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}}:

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|l}}
(3) To introduce the person or thing, which is the object of a ''mental'' act, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽאֱמִין בְּ|translate=to trust in}} (to cleave trustingly ''to'') somebody or something; {{GHGheb|text=בָּטַח בְּ|translate=to have confidence in}}...; {{GHGheb|text=שָׂמַח בְּ|translate=to rejoice in}} or ''at'' something, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=דִּבֶּר בְּ|translate=to speak of (about)}} some one or something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=6|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=3 f.}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|m}}
(4) The idea of an action as extending ''to'' something, with at the same time the secondary idea of participation ''in'' something, underlies finally the {{GHGterm|partitive}} use of {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אָכַל בְּ|translate=to share in eating}} something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=43 ff.}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=22|verse=11}}; also simply {{GHGtranslate|to eat, to taste of}} something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=25}}; so also {{GHGheb|text=לָחַם בְּ|translate=to eat of}}, and {{GHGheb|text=שָׁתָה בְ}}<ref>To be distinguished from {{GHGheb|text=שָׁתָה בְ}}={{GHGtranslate|to drink from}} (a cup, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=6|verse=6}}), as in Arabic and Aramaic ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=5|verse=2}}). Cf. also {{polytonic|ἐν ποτηρίοις}} (Xen. Anab. vi. 1, 4), {{polytonic|ἐν χρυσώμασι πίνειν}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=3 Ezr|chapter=3|verse=6}}), ''venenum in auro bibitur'', Seneca, Thyestes 453, and the French ''boire dans une tasse''.</ref> ''to drink of'' something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=9|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁמַע בְּ|translate=to hear}} a whisper ''of something'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=26|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=מָצָא בְּ|translate=they found}} remaining ''of her'' only..., {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=9|verse=35}}; {{GHGheb|text=נָשָׂא בְ|translate=to bear a share of}} something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=18|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=13}}. Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=חָלַק בְּ|translate=to give a share of}} something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=39|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=בָּנָח בְ|translate=to do building to}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=4|verse=4}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|n}}
(5) With the idea of ''touching, striking against anything'' is naturally connected that of proximity and vicinity ''near'', and further that of association ''with'' something; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּנַפְשׁוֹ|translate=with the life thereof}}; 15:14, 32:11 {{GHGheb|text=בְּמַקְלִי|translate=with my staff}}. Sometimes {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} combined with a verb of motion (''to come with'' something), expresses the idea of ''bringing'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=15|verse=1}} ''Samson visited his wife with a kid'', i.e. he brought her a kid; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=23|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=66|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=15|verse=19}} ff., 16:6.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|o}}
(6) From the idea of connexion with something, being accompanied by something (see n), is developed, finally, the ''instrumental'' use of {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}}, which represents the means or instrument (or even the personal agent), as something ''with which'' one has associated himself in order to perform an action; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=4|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=בַּשֵּׁ֫בֶט|translate=they smite with the rod}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=24}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=30}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּךָ|translate=by thee}} (so also 44:6, parallel with {{GHGheb|text=בְּשִׁמְךָ}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=34}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=1|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=12|verse=14|hidebook=1}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=עָבַד בְּ|translate=to labour by means of}} some one, i.e. to cause him to labour at it, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=14}}, &c. On {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} with the passive to introduce the means or the author, see {{GHGpar|121|f}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|p}}
A variety of the {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} {{GHGterm|instrumenti}} is {{GHGheb|text=ב}} {{GHGterm|pretii}} (the price being considered as the ''means'' of acquiring a thing), cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=23|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=18|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=בְּרָחֵל}}); 30:16, 33:19, 34:15 ({{GHGheb|text=בְּזֹאת|translate=on this}} condition); 37:28; also, in a wider sense, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=28}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּ|translate=for the sake of}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=13}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|q}}
Rem. The use of {{GHGheb|text=בְּ|translate=instrumenti}} to introduce the object is peculiar in such expressions as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=44|verse=20}} ''and thou coveredst over us'' {{GHGheb|text=בְּצַלְמָ֫וֶת|translate=with the shadow of death}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=פָּֽעֲרוּ עָלַי בְּפִיהֶם|translate=they have opened wide their mouth against me}} (prop. ''have made an opening with their mouth''); cp. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=22|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=7|verse=20}} ''he lifted up'' {{GHGheb|text=בַּמַּטֶּה|translate=the rod}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=16|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=חָגַר}} and {{GHGheb|text=צָנַף}} followed by {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=8|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=17}}. Analogous to some English expressions we find both ''to gnash the teeth'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=16}}, and ''to gnash with the teeth'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=9}}; ''to wink the eye'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=10|verse=10}}, and ''to wink with the eye'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=6|verse=13}}; ''shake the head'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=22|verse=8}}, and ''to shake with the head'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=18|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=4}}.—In all these instances<section end=par119 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

405.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par119 />the verb (intransitive) construed with {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} has a greater independence, and consequently more emphasis than the verb construed with a direct accusative; the latter conveys a sort of necessary specification of the action, while the noun introduced by {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} is used rather as a merely adverbial complement. An instructive example of this is {{GHGheb|text=נָתַן קוֹל|translate=vocem emittere}}, ''to utter a voice'', also ''to thunder'', while in {{GHGheb|text=נָתַן בְּקוֹלוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=46|verse=7}} (68:34, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=12|verse=8}}), {{GHGheb|text=נָתַן}} has an independent sense = ''he thundered with his voice'' (i.e. mightily).

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|r}}
(''c'') {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}<ref>Cf. Giesebrecht, ''Die hebr. Präpos. Lamed'', Halle, 1876.</ref> ''to'', a very general expression of ''direction towards'' anything, is used to represent the most varied ''relations'' of an action or state with regard to a person or thing. On the use of {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} as a periphrasis for the ''genetivus poseessoris'' or ''auctoris'' (the idea of belonging to), see § 129; on {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} with the passive, to introduce the author or the cause, see {{GHGpar|121|f}}; on {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} in a purely local sense (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לִימִֽינְךָ|translate=at thy right hand}}, prop. ''towards thy right hand''), or temporal (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לָעֶ֫רֶב|translate=at evening}}, &c.) or distributive, see the Lexicon

The following uses of {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} properly belong to the government of the verb:

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|s}}
(1) As a ''nota dativi''<ref>Just as in the Romance languages the Latin preposition ''ad'' (Italian ''a'', before vowels ''ad>'', French ''à'', Spanish ''á'') and in English ''to'' are used as a periphrasis for the dative.—On the introduction of the nearer object by {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, cf. {{GHGpar|117|n}}.</ref> to introduce the remoter object; also

(2) To introduce the ''dativus commodi''. This ''dativus commodi'' (or ''incommodi'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=37|verse=11}}) is used—especially in colloquial language and in later style—in the form of a pronoun with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, as an apparently pleonastic ''dativus ethicus'', with many verbs, in order to give emphasis to the significance of the occurrence in question ''for'' a particular subject. In this construction the person of the pronoun must always agree with that of the verbal form.<ref>Such expressions as the analogous English ''he plucked me ope his doublet, but me no buts'', and the like, are accordingly inadmissible in Hebrew.</ref> By far the most frequent use of this {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} is with the pronoun of the 2nd person after imperatives, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לֶךְ־לְךָ|translate=go, got thee away}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=22|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=13}} (also in the feminine, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=2|verse=10}}, 13); {{GHGheb|text=נְטֵה לְךָ|translate=turn thee aside}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=סְעוּ לָכֶם|translate=take your journey}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=עִבְדוּ לָכֶם|translate=pass ye over}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּדַח־לְךָ|translate=flee}} (to save thyself), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=43}}; {{GHGheb|text=עֲלִי־לָךְ|translate=get thee up}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=9}};
