(''b'') The collective use of substantives which at the same time serve as {{GHGterm|nomina unitatis}}; thus, {{GHGheb|text=אָדָם}} (never in plur.) means both ''man'' (homo) and ''men'' (homines); {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ|translate=a man}} (vir) and ''men'' (viri); {{GHGheb|text=אִשָּׁה|translate=woman}} and ''women'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=21|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=6}}); {{GHGheb|text=אַרְבֶּה|translate=a locust}}, but usually ''a swarm of locusts''; {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫פֶשׁ|translate=soul}} and ''souls'' (persons); {{GHGheb|text=מַקֵּל|translate=staff}} and ''staves'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=37}}); {{GHGheb|text=עַ֫יִט|translate=a bird of prey}} and ''birds of prey''; {{GHGheb|text=עָלֶה|translate=a leaf}} and ''foliage''; {{GHGheb|text=עֵ֫שֶׂב|translate=a plant}} and ''plants, herbs''; {{GHGheb|text=עֵץ|translate=a tree}} and ''trees'' (as it were ''foliage''); {{GHGheb|text=פְּרִי|translate=fruit}} and ''fruits''; {{GHGheb|text=שִׂיחַ|translate=a shrub}} and ''shrubs''; in isolated instances also nouns like {{GHGheb|text=עֶ֫בֶד|translate=man-servant}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁפְחָה|translate=maid-servant}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֲמוֹר|translate=ass}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹר|translate=ox}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=6}}).—On the singular (especially of gentilic names) with the article (which may, however, be omitted in poetry, cf. e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=12|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=חָסִיד}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=11|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=יוֹעֵץ}}) to include all individuals of the same species, cf. {{GHGpar|126|l}}. On the special meaning of the plurals formed from certain collectives, see {{GHGpar|124|l}}.

(''c'') The feminine ending; see {{GHGpar|122|s}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|123|c}}
(''d'') The repetition of single words, and even of whole groups of words, especially to express entirety, or in a distributive sense. The following cases are more particularly to be noticed:

1. The repetition of one or more words to express the idea of ''every, all'', as {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם יוֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=10}}, &c., ''day'' by ''day, every day''; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנָה שָׁנָה|translate=year}} by ''year'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=14|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ אִישׁ|translate=every}} man, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=36|verse=4}}; with {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} before each, as {{GHGheb|text=בַּבֹּ֫קֶר בַּבֹּ֫קֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=21}} ''every morning'' (and similarly before a group of words, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=24|verse=8}}), for which the ''distributive'' {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} is also used, {{GHGheb|text=לַבֹּ֫קֶר לַבֹּ֫קֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=9|verse=27}}, and with ''one'' plural {{GHGheb|text=לַבְּקָרִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=14}}, {{GHGheb|text=לִבְקָרִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=18}} parallel with {{GHGheb|text=לִרְגָעִים|translate=every moment}}. Somewhat different are the instances with {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} before the second word only, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם בְּיוֹם|translate=day}} by ''day'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=12|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה|translate=year by year}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=15|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=7}} (but in verse 3 {{GHGheb|text=מִיָּמִים יָמִ֫ימָה}}), {{GHGheb|text=כְּפַ֫עַם בְּפַ֫עַם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=24|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=30|hidebook=1}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=10}} ''as at other times''. Also With the two words united by means of {{GHGterm|wāw copulative}}, {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ וְאִישׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=87|verse=5}}, or {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ וָאִישׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=1|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=דּוֹר וָדוֹר|translate=all generations}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם וָיוֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=3|verse=4}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=8|verse=9}},<section end=par123 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

420.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par123 />{{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=10|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=26|verse=13}} and often (cf. Cheyne, ''Bampton Lectures'', 1889, p. 479, according to whom the use of the {{GHGheb|text=ו}} copulative with the second word is especially common in Ch and Est, and therefore belongs to the later language; Driver, {{GHGcite|title=Introd.}}<sup>6</sup>, p. 538, No. 35); sometimes (but with the exception of {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=45|verse=18}} only in very late passages) with a pleonastic {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־}} preceding, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=145|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=2|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=9|verse=28|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=11|verse=12}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|123|d}}
2. Repetition of words in an expressly ''distributive'' sense<ref>Cf. in the New Testament {{GHGbible-ref|book=St. Mark|chapter=6|verse=39}} f. συμπόσια συμπόσια, πρασιαὶ πρασιαί (Weizsäcker, ''tischweise, beetweise'').</ref> (which may to some extent be noticed in the examples under c) equivalent to ''one each'', &c., e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=34}} ''forty days'' {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם לַשָּׁנָה יוֹם לַשָּׁנָה|translate=counting for every day a year}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=24|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=28|verse=34}} (three words repeated); also with the addition of {{GHGheb|text=לְבַד|translate=apart}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֵדֶר עֵדֶר לְבַדּוֹ|translate=every drove by itself}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=17}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=12|verse=12}}. Most frequently with the addition of a numeral (for the simple repetition of numerals for the same purpose, cf. {{GHGpar|134|q}}), and with the words not only in groups of two ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=24|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=13|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=31|verse=4|hidebook=1}}) or three ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=7|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=21|hidebook=1}}), but even of six ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=3}}) or seven ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=25|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, 21, 25); in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=25|verse=35}} five words even three times repeated.<ref>These repetitions of larger groups of words belong entirely to the ''Priestly Code'' in the Pentateuch, and are unquestionably indications of a late period of the language. Of quite a different kind are such examples as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=6}}, where the repetition of four words serves to give greater solemnity to the promise, unless here, as certainly in 1:20, it is a mere ''dittography''; the LXX omit the repetition, in both passages.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|123|e}}
3. Repetition to express an exceptional or at least superfine quality; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=25|verse=15}} ''which were of gold, gold, of silver, silver'', i.e. made of pure gold and pure silver; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=27}} {{GHGheb|text=בַּדֶּ֫רֶךְ בַּדֶּ֫רֶךְ|translate=only along by the}} high ''way''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=3|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=8|verse=16|hidebook=1}} ''they are given, given to him'', i.e. given exclusively for his service, for his very own. Also with a certain hyperbole in such examples as {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=3|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=גֵּבִים גֵּבִים|translate=nothing but trenches}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=בֶּֽאֱרֹת בֶּֽאֱרֹת חֵמָר|translate=all asphalt-pits}}.—Repetition serves to intensify the expression to the highest degree in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=22}} ''by reason of the violent pransings of his string ones'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=8|verse=10}} (''countless heaps''), and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=4|verse=14}} (''countless multitudes''); cf. also {{GHGheb|text=מְעַט מְעַט}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=30}} ''by little and little, very gradually''; cf. {{GHGpar|133|k}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|123|f}}
4. Repetition with the copula to express ''of more than one kind''; thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=25|verse=13}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=20|verse=10}}) {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫בֶן וָאֶ֫בֶן|translate=a weight and a weight}}, i.e. two kinds of weight (hence the addition ''great and small''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=12|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּלֵב וָלֵב|translate=with two kinds of heart}}, i.e. ''with a double-dealing heart''; cf. the opposite {{GHGheb|text=בְּלֹא לֵב וָלֵב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=12|verse=33}}.<section end=par123 />

<section begin=par124 />{{GHGpar-heading|124|The Various Uses of the Plural-form||<ref>Cf. Dietrich, ‘''Über Begriff und Form des hebr. Plurals'',’ in the {{GHGcite|title=Abhandl. zur hebr. Grammatik}}, Leipzig, 1846, p. 2 ff.</ref>}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|124|a}}
'''1.''' The plural is by no means used in Hebrew solely to express a number of individuals or separate objects, but may also denote them collectively. This use of the plural expresses either (''a'') a combination of various external constituent parts (plurals of ''local extension''), or (''b'') a more or less intensive focusing of the characteristics inherent in the idea of the stem (''abstract plurals'', usually rendered in English by forms in ''-hood, -ness, -ship''). A variety of the plurals described under (''b''), in which the secondary idea of ''intensity'' or of an ''internal ''<section end=par124 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

421.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par124" />''multiplication'' of the idea of the stem may be clearly seen, is (''c'') the ''pluralis excellentiae'' or ''pluralis maiestatis''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|124|b}}
Examples of (''a''): Plurals of ''local extension'' to denote localities in general, but especially level surfaces (the ''surface''-plural), since in them the idea of a whole composed of innumerable separate parts or points is most evident, as {{GHGheb|text=שָׁמַ֫יִם}} ({{GHGpar|88|d}}) ''heaven'' (cf. also {{GHGheb|text=מְרוֹמִים|translate=heights}} of heaven, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=19}}; elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=מָרוֹם}}); {{GHGheb|text=מַ֫יִם|translate=water}}; {{GHGheb|text=יַמִּים}} (the broad surface of the sea) poetically for {{GHGheb|text=יָם|translate=sea}}; {{GHGheb|text=פָנִים}} (prop. the side ''turned towards'' any one, then) ''surface'' in general, usually ''face''; {{GHGheb|text=אֲחוֹרִים|translate=the back}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=23|hidebook=1}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=צַוָּארִים|translate=neck nape of the neck}}<ref>Cf. the same use of the plural in τὰ στέρνα, τὰ νῶτα, τὰ τράχηλα, ''praecordia'', ''cervices, fauces''; on plurals of extension in general, cf. the prepositions of place and time in the plur. form, {{GHGpar|103|n}}. {{GHGheb|text=סְפָרִים}} is not a case in point, in the sense of ''letter'' (properly a sheet folded into several pages; elsewhere also {{GHGheb|text=סֵ֫פֶר}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=8}} ff., {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=10|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=19|verse=14|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=14}}; referred to afterwards by the ''singular'' suffix); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=39|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=29|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=32|verse=14|hidebook=1}} (''after'' being folded, previously {{GHGheb|text=סֵ֫פֶר}}).</ref>; also {{GHGheb|text=מְרַֽאֲשׁוֹת|translate=the place at the head}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַרְגְּלוֹת|translate=place at the feet}}; {{GHGheb|text=עֲבָרִים|translate=place on the other side}} (of a river); {{GHGheb|text=מַֽעֲמַקִּים|translate=depth}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֶרְחַקִּים}} (also {{GHGheb|text=מֶרְחָק}}) ''distance'', {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁכָּבִים|translate=bed}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=4}} (unless, with Dillmann, it is to be explained in the sense of ''double bed'', i.e. ''torus''), {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁכָּנִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=46|verse=5}}, and {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁכָּנוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=43|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=84|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=132|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, ''dwelling'' (perhaps also {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽהָלִים|translate=encampment}}, in passages like {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=10}}). The last four belong, however, to poetic style, and are better reckoned amongst the ''plurals of amplification'' treated under {{GHGpar|124|d|nonumber=1}}–{{GHGpar|124|f|nonumber=1}}. So perhaps {{GHGheb|text=יְצֻעִים|translate=bed}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=63|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=17|verse=13}}; but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=132|verse=3}}, &c., in the singular); probably, however, {{GHGheb|text=יְצֻעִים}} (prop. ''strata'') refers to a number of coverings or pillows.

The plural of extension is used to denote a lengthened period of ''time'' in {{GHGheb|text=עֽוֹלָמִים|translate=eternity}} (everlasting ages).

{{GHGmargin-letter|124|c}}
Rem. The plural of extension includes also a few examples which were formerly explained as simply poetic plurals, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=17|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=קְבָרִים לִי|translate=graves are}} (ready) ''for me'', i.e. the place where there are many of them (as it were ''the graveyard'') is my portion, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=16|verse=14}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=22|verse=20}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|124|d}}
Of (''b''): the tolerably numerous abstract plurals, mostly of a particular form (''q<sup>e</sup>ṭûlîm, qiṭṭûlîm'', &c.), may be divided into two classes. They sum up either the ''conditions'' or ''qualities'' inherent in the idea of the stem, or else the various single ''acts'' of which an action is composed. Cf. for the first class, {{GHGheb|text=בְּחוּרִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=בְּחוּרוֹת|translate=youth}}, {{GHGheb|text=זְקֻנִים|translate=old age}}, {{GHGheb|text=נְעוּרִים|translate=youth}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּתוּלִים|translate=maidenhood}}, {{GHGheb|text=כְּלוּלוֹת|translate=bridal state}}; {{GHGheb|text=מְגוּרִים|translate=condition of a sojourner}}, {{GHGheb|text=בְּשָׂרִים|translate=fleshliness}} (only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=14|verse=30}}), {{GHGheb|text=חַיִּים|translate=life}} (the abstract idea of the qualities of a living being); {{GHGheb|text=שִׁכּוּלִים|translate=childlessness}}, {{GHGheb|text=סַנְוֵרִים|translate=blindness}}, {{GHGheb|text=עִוְעִים|translate=perverseness}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|124|e}}
There are also a number of plurals, found almost exclusively in poetry (sometimes along with the singular), which are evidently intended to intensify<ref>Cf. A. Ember, ‘The pluralis intensivus in Hebrew,’ {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|AJSL.|American Journal of Semitic Languages.}}}} 1905, p. 195 ff.</ref> the idea of the stem (plural of amplification), as {{GHGheb|text=אוֹנִים|translate=might}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=26}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֱמוּנִים}} (as well as {{GHGheb|text=אֱמוּנָה}}) and {{GHGheb|text=אֱמוּנוֹת|translate=faithfulness}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַשְׁרֵי}} (according to {{GHGpar|93|l}}, only in the construct state plural or with suffixes = ''the happiness of''), ''happy''; {{GHGheb|text=כּֽוֹשָׁרוֹת}} (complete) ''prosperity'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=בִּינוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=11}} and {{GHGheb|text=תְּבוּנוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=14}}, &c. (keen) ''understanding''; {{GHGheb|text=עֵצוֹת}} (true) ''counsel'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=28}}; {{GHGheb|text=דֵּעִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=37|verse=16}} and {{GHGheb|text=דֵּעוֹת}}<section end="par124" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

422.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par124" />{{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=3}} (thorough) ''knowledge''; {{GHGheb|text=בַּטֻּחוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=12|verse=6}} and {{GHGheb|text=מִבְטַחִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=32|verse=18}} (full) ''confidence''; {{GHGheb|text=בְּרָכוֹת}} (abundant) ''blessing'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=21|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=גְּבוּרוֹת}} (exceptional) ''strength'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=41|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַוּוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=10}} (very) ''wickedness''; {{GHGheb|text=חֲמוּדוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=9|verse=23}} (greatly) ''beloved''; {{GHGheb|text=חֵמוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=76|verse=11}}, &c.(fierce) ''wrath''; {{GHGheb|text=חֲרָפוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=12|verse=2}} (utter) ''contempt''; {{GHGheb|text=יְשֻׁעוֹת}} (real) ''help'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=18}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=מַרְאֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=46|verse=2}} (an important) ''vision''; {{GHGheb|text=מֵֽישָׁרִים|translate=uprightness}}; {{GHGheb|text=תַּהְפֻּכוֹת|translate=perversity}}; {{GHGheb|text=נְקָמוֹת}} (complete) ''vengeance'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=36}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=חֲשֵׁכִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=מַֽחֲשַׁכִּים}} (thick) ''darkness''; {{GHGheb|text=מִסְתָּרִים|translate=a}} (close) ''hiding-place''; {{GHGheb|text=נְגִידִים|translate=nobility}}; {{GHGheb|text=שְׁמָנִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=1}} ''fatness''; {{GHGheb|text=צַחְצָחוֹת}} (complete) ''aridity''; {{GHGheb|text=מַמְתַּקִּים|translate=sweetness}}; {{GHGheb|text=מַֽחֲמַדִּים|translate=preciousness}}; {{GHGheb|text=שַֽׁעֲשֻׁעִים|translate=delight}}; {{GHGheb|text=עֲדָנִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=תַּֽעֲנֻגִים|translate=pleasure}}; {{GHGheb|text=רַֽחֲמִים|translate=compassion}}; {{GHGheb|text=מְנוּחֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=23|verse=2}} ''rest, refreshment''; {{GHGheb|text=מְהוּמֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=3|verse=9}} ''tumult''. Probably also {{GHGheb|text=יְדִידֹת}} (heartfelt) ''love'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=45|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=מְרֹרוֹת}} (extreme) ''bitterness'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=26}}; {{GHGheb|text=מִרְמוֹת}} (base) ''deceit'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=38|verse=13}}; {{GHGheb|text=צְדָקוֹת}} (true) ''righteousness'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=15}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=שְׁמָחוֹת}} (the highest) ''joy'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=16|verse=11}}. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=חָכְמוֹת|translate=wisdom}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=20}}, &c.) can hardly be a ''plural'' (=the essence of wisdom, or wisdom personified), but is a singular (see {{GHGpar|86|l}}).

A further extension of this plural of amplification occurs according to P. Haupt’s very probable suggestion ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|SBOT.|Sacred Books of the Old Testament, ed. by P. Haupt. Lpz. and Baltimore, 1893 ff.}}}} Proverbs, p. 40, line 50, &c.) in {{GHGheb|text=יְאֹרִים|translate=the great river}} (of the Nile, generally {{GHGheb|text=יְאֹר}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=6|hidebook=1}} (though with the predicate in the plural), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=30|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=78|verse=44}}, but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=29|verse=3}} the usual explanation, ''arms'' or ''channels of the Nile'', can hardly be avoided; also in {{GHGheb|text=נְהָרוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=24|verse=2}} of the ocean, which encircles the earth, 137:1 of the ''great river'', i.e. the Euphrates, but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=18|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=נַֽהֲרֵי כוּשׁ}} is evidently a numerical plural.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=16|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=מְלָכִים}} (acc. to P. Haupt=the ''great king'') is very doubtful. In {{GHGheb|text=נְשִׂיאֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=19|verse=1}} the second {{GHGterm|yôdh}} is evidently due to dittography, since {{GHGheb|text=ישְׂרָאֵל}} follows.

{{GHGmargin-letter|124|f}}
The summing up of the several parts of an action is expressed in {{GHGheb|text=חֲנֻמִים|translate=embalming}}, {{GHGheb|text=כִּפֻּרִים|translate=atonement}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִלֻּאִים}} (prop. ''filling'', sc. of the hand) ''ordination to the priesthood'', {{GHGheb|text=שִׁלֻּחִים|translate=dismissal}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁלֻּמִים|translate=retribution}}, {{GHGheb|text=פִּתֻּחִים|translate=engraving}} (of a seal, &c.); {{GHGheb|text=אֳהָבִים|translate=fornication}}, {{GHGheb|text=זְנוּנִים|translate=whoredom}}, {{GHGheb|text=נִֽאֻפִים|translate=adultery}}; {{GHGheb|text=נִֽחֻמִים}} (prop. no doubt, warm compassion) ''consolation'', {{GHGheb|text=תַּֽחֲנוּנים|translate=supplication}}, {{GHGheb|text=נְדֻדִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=4}} (restless) ''tossing to and fro'', {{GHGheb|text=פְּלָאִים|translate=wonder}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=9}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֹלֵלוֹת|translate=gleaning}}; perhaps also {{GHGheb|text=נְגִינִוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=4|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=6|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, &c., if it means ''the playing on stringed instruments'', and {{GHGheb|text=שַׁלְמֹנִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=23}} ''bribery'', unless it be a plural of number.<ref>Mayer Lambert in {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} xxiv. 106 ff., enumerates no less than ninety-five words ending in ''îm'', which in his opinion are to be regarded as ''pluralia tantum''.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|124|g}}
Of (''c''): the ''pluralis excellentiae'' or ''maiestatis'', as has been remarked above, is properly a variety of the abstract plural, since it sums up the several characteristics<ref>The Jewish grammarians call such plurals {{GHGheb|text=רִבּוּי הַכֹּחוֹת}} {{GHGterm|plur. virium}} or {{GHGterm|virtutum}}; later grammarians call them {{GHGterm|plur. excellentiae, magnitudinis}}, or {{GHGterm|plur. maiestaticus}}. This last name may have been suggested by the ''we'' used by kings when speaking of themselves (cf. already {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Macc.|chapter=10|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Macc.|chapter=11|verse=31|hidebook=1}}); and the plural used by God in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=11|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=8}} has been incorrectly explained in this way. It is, however, either ''communicative'' (including the attendant angels; so at all events in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=8}}, cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=22}}), or according to others, an indication of ''the fullness of power and might'' implied in {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} (see Dillmann on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=26}}); but it is best explained as a plural of ''self-deliberation''. The use of the plural as a form of respectful address is quite foreign to Hebrew.</ref> belonging to the idea, besides possessing the secondary sense of an ''intensification'' of the original idea. It is thus closely related to the plurals of amplification, treated under {{GHGpar|e|nonumber=1}}, which are mostly found in poetry.<section end="par124" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

423.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par124 />So especially {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים|translate=Godhead, God}} (to be distinguished from the numerical plural ''gods'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=12}}, &c.). The supposition that {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} is to be regarded as merely a remnant of earlier polytheistic views (i.e. as originally only a numerical plural) is at least highly improbable, and, moreover, would not explain the analogous plurals (see below). That the language has entirely rejected the idea of numerical plurality in {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} (whenever it denotes ''one'' God), is proved especially by its being almost invariably joined with a singular attribute (cf. {{GHGpar|132|h}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים צַדִּיק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=7|verse=10}}, &c. Hence {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} may have been used originally not only as a numerical but also as an abstract plural (corresponding to the Latin ''numen'', and our ''Godhead''), and, like other abstracts of the same kind, have been transferred to a concrete single god (even of the heathen).

{{GHGmargin-letter|124|h}}
To the same class (and probably formed on the analogy of {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}}) belong the plurals {{GHGheb|text=קְדשִׁים|translate=the Most Holy}} (only of Yahweh), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=12|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=9|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=3|hidebook=1}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים קְדשִׁים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=24|verse=19}}, and the Aram. {{GHGheb|text=עֶלְיוֹנִין|translate=the Most High}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=7|verse=18}}, 22, 25); and probably {{GHGheb|text=תְּרָפִים}} (usually taken in the sense of ''penates'') the image of a god, used especially for obtaining oracles. Certainly in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=13}}, 16 only ''one'' image is intended; in most other places a single image ''may'' be intended<ref>Even in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=34}}, notwithstanding the plural suffix in {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּשִׂמֵם}} and {{GHGheb|text=עֲלֵיהֶם}}, since the construction of these abstracts as numerical plurals is one of the peculiarities of the E-document of the Hexateuch; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=20|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=35|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, and {{GHGpar|145|i}}.</ref>; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=10|verse=2}} alone is it most naturally taken as a numerical plural. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=5|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=גְּבֹהִים|translate=supremus}} (of God) is doubtful; according to others it is a numerical plural, ''superiores''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|124|i}}
Further, {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנִים}}, as well as the singular {{GHGheb|text=אָדוֹן}}, (lordship) ''lord'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנִים קָשֶׁה|translate=a cruel lord}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנֵי הָאָ֫רֶץ|translate=the lord of the land}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=30}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=19}}; so especially with the suffixes of the 2nd and 3rd persons {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנֶ֫יךָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנַ֫יִךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=45|verse=12}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנָיו}}, &c., also {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנֵ֫ינוּ}} (except {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=16}}); but in 1st sing. always {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנִי}}.<ref>On {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנָי}} (for {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנִי}}) as a name of God, cf. {{GHGpar|135|q}}.</ref> So also {{GHGheb|text=בְּעָלִים}} (with suffixes) ''lord, master'' (of slaves, cattle, or inanimate things; but in the sense of ''maritus'', always in the singular), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בְּעָלָיו}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=3}}, &c.<ref>Euting, ''Reise in Arabien'', p. 61, mentions the interesting fact that the subjects of the Emir of Ḥâyel commonly speak of their ruler as ''šiyûkh'', a plur. majestatis= ''the great sheikh''.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|124|k}}
On the other hand, we must regard as doubtful a number of participles in the plural, which, being used as attributes of God, resemble ''plurales excellentiae''; thus, {{GHGheb|text=עשָֹׁי|translate=my Maker}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=35|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=עשַֹׁ֫יִךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=54|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=עשָֹׁיו}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=149|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=עשֶֹׁיהָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=נֽוֹטֵיהֶם|translate=stretching them out}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=5}}; for all these forms may also be explained as singular, according to {{GHGpar|93|ss}}.<ref>{{GHGheb|text=בֹּֽעֲלַ֫יִךְ}}, which in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=54|verse=5}} is in parallelism with {{GHGheb|text=עשַֹׁ֫יִךְ}}, must then be explained as merely formed on analogy.</ref>—{{GHGheb|text=נֹֽגְשָׂיו}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=12}} might also be regarded as another instance, unless it be a numerical plural, ''their oppressors''; moreover, {{GHGheb|text=מְרִימָיו|translate=him who lifteth it up}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=15}} (but read probably {{GHGheb|text=מְרִימוֹ}}); {{GHGheb|text=שֹֽׁלְחָיו|translate=him who sendeth him}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=10|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=22|verse=21|hidebook=1}} (so Baer, but Ginsburg {{GHGheb|text=שֹֽׁלְחֶ֫ךָ}}), 25:13 (in parallelism with {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנָיו}}). These latter plurals, however (including {{GHGheb|text=מרימיו}}), may probably be more simply explained as indicating an indefinite individual, cf. o below.—For {{GHGheb|text=שֹֽׁמְרֶ֫יךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=121|verse=5}} (textus receptus) and {{GHGheb|text=בּֽוֹרְאֶ֫יךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=1}} (textus receptus) the singular should be read, with Baer.
<section end=par124 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

424.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="100.7.116.115" /></noinclude><section begin="par124" />{{GHGmargin-letter|124|l}}
Rem. 1. (''a'') Coherent substances, &c., are mostly regarded as ''single'', and are, accordingly, almost always represented by nouns in the singular, cf. {{GHGheb|text=אָבָק|translate=fine dust}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫פֶר|translate=ashes}}, {{GHGheb|text=בַּד|translate=linen}}, {{GHGheb|text=בְּדִיל|translate=lead}}, {{GHGheb|text=זָהָב|translate=gold}}, {{GHGheb|text=כֶּ֫סֶף|translate=silver}}, {{GHGheb|text=נְח֫שֶׁת|translate=brass}}, {{GHGheb|text=חָלָב|translate=milk}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַ֫יִן|translate=wine}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָפָר|translate=dust, the ground}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֵץ|translate=wood}}. Plurals are, however, formed from some of these words expressing materials in order to denote separate portions taken from the whole in manufacture (''plurals of the result'') or parts otherwise detached from it; thus, {{GHGheb|text=בַּדִּים|translate=linen garments}}; {{GHGheb|text=כְּסָפִים|translate=silver pieces}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=25}}, 35; {{GHGheb|text=נְחֻשְׁתַּ֫יִם}} (dual) ''fetters of brass''; {{GHGheb|text=עֵצִים|translate=ligna|en=trees, pieces of wood}} (''timber'' for building or ''sticks'' for burning); also in a wider sense, {{GHGheb|text=בְּדִילִים}} particles of ''alloy'' to be separated by smelting, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=25}}; {{GHGheb|text=עֲפָרוֹת|translate=fragments of earth}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=26}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=28|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=עַפְרֹת זָהָב|translate=dust of gold}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|124|m}}
(''b'') To the class of ''plurals of the result'' belong also a few names of natural products, when represented in an artificial condition; thus, {{GHGheb|text=חִטִּים|translate=wheat}} in grain (threshed wheat), as distinguished from {{GHGheb|text=חִטָּה|translate=wheat}} (used collectively) in the ear; cf. the same distinction between {{GHGheb|text=כֻּסְּמִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=כֻּסֶּ֫מֶת|translate=spelt}}; {{GHGheb|text=עֲדָשִׁים}} and {{GHGheb|text=עֲדָשָׁה}} (the singular preserved only in the Mishna) ''lentils''; {{GHGheb|text=שְׂעֹרִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=שְׂעֹרָה|translate=barley}}; also {{GHGheb|text=פִּשְׁתִּים|translate=linen}}, {{GHGheb|text=פֵּ֫שֶׁת}} (to be inferred from {{GHGheb|text=פִּשְׁתִּי}}) ''flax''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|124|n}}
(''c'') Finally, the distinction between {{GHGheb|text=דָּם|translate=blood}} and {{GHGheb|text=דָּמִים}} requires to be specially noticed. The singular is always used when the blood is regarded as an organic unity, hence also of menstrual blood, and the blood of sacrifices (collected in the basin and then sprinkled), and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=24}} of the blood gushing from wounds. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=דָּמִים}} as a sort of plural of the result and at the same time of local extension, denotes ''blood which is shed'', when it appears as blood-stains ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=15}}) or as blood-marks (so evidently in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=9|verse=4}}). But since blood-stains or blood-marks, as a rule, suggest blood shed in murder (although {{GHGheb|text=דָּמִים}} also denotes the blood which flows at child-birth or in circumcision), {{GHGheb|text=דָּמִים}} acquired (even in very early passages) simply the sense of a ''bloody deed'', and especially of ''bloodguiltiness'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=22|verse=1}} f., &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|124|o}}
In some few cases the plural is used to denote an indefinite singular; certainly so in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=17|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־שְׁעָרֶ֫יךָ|translate=unto ''one of'' thy gates}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=9|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־אֲתֹנוֹת}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=2|verse=9}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=22}} {{GHGheb|text=יְלָדֶ֫יהָ}} (where evidently only ''one'' child is thought of, certainly though in connexion with a contingency which may be repeated); cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=4|verse=10}} (''if one of them fall'').—So probably also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=43}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=2|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=3|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=6|verse=2|hidebook=1}}; but ''not'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=29}}, since the same document ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=13|verse=12}}) makes Lot dwell ''in the cities'' of the Jordan valley; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=בָּנִים}} denotes the class with which the action is concerned. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=12|verse=7}} instead of the unusual {{GHGheb|text=בְּעָרֵי גִלְעָד|translate=in the cities of Gilead}} (formerly explained here as ''in one of the cities of Gilead'') we should most probably read, with Moore ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|SBOT.|Sacred Books of the Old Testament, ed. by P. Haupt. Lpz. and Baltimore, 1893 ff.}}}} Judges, p. 52), {{GHGheb|text=בְּעִירוֹ בְּמִצְפֵּה גִלְעָד|translate=in his city, in Mizpeh}} (in) ''Gilead''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|124|p}}
'''2.''' When a substantive is followed by a genitive, and the compound idea thus formed is to be expressed in the plural, this is done—

(''a'') Most naturally by using the plural of the {{GHGterm|nomen regens}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גִּבּוֹרֵי חַ֫יִל|translate=mighty men of valour}} (prop. heroes of strength), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=7|verse=2}}, 9; so also in compounds, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי יְמִינִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=22|verse=7}}, as the plur. of {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־יְמִינִי|translate=Benjamite}}; but also

{{GHGmargin-letter|124|q}}
(''b'') By using the plural of ''both'' nouns,<ref>Cf. König, {{GHGcite|title=Lehrgebäude}}, ii. 438 f., according to whom the plural of the principal word exercises an influence on the determining genitive.</ref> e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גִּבּוֹרֵי חֲיָלִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=7|verse=5}};<section end="par124" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

425.text:
{{GHGheb|text=וּבְבָֽתֵּי כְלָאִים|translate=and in prison houses}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=22}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=34|verse=1}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנֵיֽ־לֻחֹת אֲבָנִים|translate=two tables of stone}} (but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=31|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=לֻחֹת אֶ֫בֶן}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=13|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=5|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=6|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=14|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=25|verse=23|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=41|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=3|verse=3}}, &c. {{GHGheb|text=עַמֵּי הָֽאֲרָצוֹת|translate=the people of the country}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=26|verse=14}}; so perhaps {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי אֵלִים|translate=sons of God}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=29|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=89|verse=7|hidebook=1}} (according to others ''sons of gods''); or finally even {{GHGmargin-letter|124|r}} (''c'') By using the plural of the ''nomen rectum'';Cf. Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, i. 482. e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בֵּית אָבוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=6|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=1|verse=2}}, 4 ff., &c., as plur. of {{GHGheb|text=בֵּית אָב}} ''father’s house, family''; {{GHGheb|text=בֵּית הַבָּמוֹת|translate=the houses of the high places}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=17|verse=29}} (also {{GHGheb|text=בָּֽתֵּי הַבָּמוֹת}} 23:19); {{GHGheb|text=בֵּית עֲצַבֵּיהֶם|translate=the houses of their idols}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=31|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=46|verse=24}}; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=7|verse=25}} ''the head of Oreb and Zeeb'', i.e. the heads, &c. {{GHGmargin-letter|124|s}} Rem. When a substantive (in a distributive sense) with a suffix refers back to a plural, the singular form of the substantive suffices, since the idea of plurality is already adequately expressed by the suffix, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=פִּימוֹ|translate=os}} (for ''ora'') ''eorum'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=17|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְמִינָם|translate=their right hand}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=144|verse=8}} [so in the English RV.], for ''hands''.
{{GHGpar-heading|125|Determination of Nouns in general. Determination of Proper Names}}
Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, i. 466 ff.
{{GHGmargin-letter|125|a}} '''1.''' A noun may either be determinate in itself, as a proper name or pronoun (see below, d and i), or be made so by its context. In the latter case, the determination may be effected either by prefixing the article (see § 126), or by the connexion of the noun (in the construct state) with a following determinate genitive, and consequently also (according to {{GHGpar|33|c}}) by its union with a pronominal suffix ({{GHGpar|127|a}}). It is to be taken as a fundamental rule, that the determination can only be effected in ''one'' of the ways here mentioned; the article cannot be prefixed to a proper name, nor to a noun followed by the genitive, nor can a proper name be used in the construct state. Deviations from this rule are either only apparent or have arisen from a corruption of the text. {{GHGmargin-letter|125|b}} Rem. Only in a few passages is a noun made expressly ''indeterminate'' by the addition of {{GHGheb|text=אֶחָד}} in the sense of our indefinite article; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=53}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=7|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, 12, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=13|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=19|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=4|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=8|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=12|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=8|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=8|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=10|verse=5|hidebook=1}} (in 8:13 {{GHGheb|text=אֶחָד קָרוֹשׁ}} i.e. ''one'', viz. ''a holy one'', is opposed to another). {{GHGmargin-letter|125|c}} It is further to be noticed, that in Hebrew the phenomenon sometimes occurs, which the Arab grammarians call ''indeterminateness for the sake of amplification''; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=31|verse=8}} ''and he shall flee'' {{GHGheb|text=מִפְּנֵי־חֶ֫רֶב|translate=from a sword}}, i.e. ''from an irresistible sword'' (God’s sword); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּיָד}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=6|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁם}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=3|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=אִשָּׁה|translate=such a woman}}, without doubt to be referred to the Gomer mentioned in cap. 1;

426.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par125 />{{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=6|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=גּוֹי}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=77|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּזְרֹעַ}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=21|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=צַדִּיק}}, if with Delitzsch it is to be referred to God; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=8|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=מִלִּים}} meaning ''important words'', but in 15:13 {{GHGheb|text=מִלִּין|translate=reproachful words}}. Cf. on this point, {{GHGpar|117|q}}, note 3, and Delitzsch, ''Psalmen'', ed. 4, p. 79.

{{GHGmargin-letter|125|d}}
'''2.''' Real ''proper nouns'', as being the names of things (or persons) only ''once'' met with, are sufficiently determinate in themselves. Such names, therefore, as {{GHGheb|text=יהוה}}, {{GHGheb|text=דָּוִד}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעֲקֹב}}, {{GHGheb|text=כְּנַ֫עַן}}, {{GHGheb|text=סְדֹם}} do not admit of the article,<ref>Consequently, {{GHGheb|text=הַֽמְנַשֶּׁח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=3|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=1|verse=12}}, &c. (in the Deuteronomist) in the combination {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁבֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּׁה}} (for which elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁבֶט מְנַשֶּׁה}}) is to be regarded ''not'' as a proper name but as a gentilic name (= ''the tribe of the Manassites''), for which in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=29|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=שׁ׳ הַֽמְנַשִּׁי}} is used, as in 10:8 {{GHGheb|text=שׁ׳ הַלֵּוִי|translate=the tribe of the Levites}}, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=18|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=שּׁ׳ הַדָּנִי|translate=the tribe of the Danites}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=13|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=הַֽמְנַשֶּׁה}} (like gentilic names in {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}}) is even used adjectivally.</ref> nor can they be in the construct state. On the other hand, not only ''gentilic'' names (as denoting the ''various'' individuals belonging to the same class), but also all those proper names, of which the appellative sense is still sufficiently evident to the mind, or at least has been handed down from an earlier period of the language, frequently (often even as a rule) take the article (according to {{GHGpar|126|e}}), and may even be followed by a genitive.

{{GHGmargin-letter|125|e}}
Examples. Like the above-mentioned proper names of individuals, countries, and cities, so also national names, which are identical in form with the name of the founder of the race (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׂרָאֵל}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֱדֹם}}, {{GHGheb|text=מוֹאָב}}), are always determinate in themselves. Of gentilic names (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הָֽעִבְרִי|translate=the Hebrew}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָֽעִבְרִים|translate=the Hebrews}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַכְּנַֽעֲנִי|translate=the Canaanite}}) the plural {{GHGheb|text=פְּלִשְׁתִּים}}, even when meaning ''the'' Philistines, is generally used without the article (but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=7}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=הַפְּ׳}}); so always {{GHGheb|text=כַּפְתֹּרִים}}.—Evident appellatives (like such modern names as ''the Hague'', ''le Havre'') are {{GHGheb|text=הַגִּבְעָה|translate=the hill}}, in the construct state {{GHGheb|text=גִּבְעַת שָׁאוּל}}, i.e. ''the Gibeah named after Saul'' to distinguish it from others; {{GHGheb|text=הָֽרָמָה|translate=the height}}; {{GHGheb|text=הָעַי|translate=the heap}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַלְּבָנוֹן}} (prop. ''the white mountain'') ''the Lebanon''; {{GHGheb|text=הַיְאֹר}} (prop. ''the river'') ''the Nile'', cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=8|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=כִּיאוֹר מִצְרָֽיִם|translate=like the river of Egypt}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַיַּרְדֵּן|translate=the Jordan}} (according to Seybold, ''Mittheil. und Nachr. des DPV.'', 1896, p. 11, probably ''the drinking-place'' [{{GHGheb|text=ירד}}, Arab. ''warada'', meaning orig. ''to go down to drink'']).

{{GHGmargin-letter|125|f}}
Rem. 1. In a few instances original appellatives have completely assumed the character of real proper names, and are therefore used without the article; thus {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים|translate=God}}, to denote the one true God (as elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=יהוה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=1}} and so generally in this document of the Pentateuch up to Ex 6, elsewhere sometimes {{GHGheb|text=הָֽאֱלֹהִים}} ὁ θεός (cf. {{GHGpar|126|e}}); also the sing. {{GHGheb|text=אֱלוֹהַּ|translate=God}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֶלְיוֹן|translate=the Most High}}, and {{GHGheb|text=שַׁדַּי|translate=the Almighty}} never take the article.—Moreover, {{GHGheb|text=אָדָם|translate=Adam}} from {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=5|verse=1}} onwards (previously in 2:7, &c., {{GHGheb|text=הָֽאָדָם|translate=the}} first ''man''); {{GHGheb|text=שָׁטָן|translate=Satan}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=21|verse=1}} (but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=3|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=6}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=הַשָּׂטָן|translate=the adversary}}); cf. {{GHGheb|text=אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד|translate=the tent of revelation}} (i.e. the tabernacle), always without the article.

{{GHGmargin-letter|125|g}}
To the class of nouns originally appellative, which the language regards<section end=par125 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

427.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par125 />as proper names, and which consequently never take the article, belong also certain archaic words mostly used only by poets, such as {{GHGheb|text=שְׁאוֹל|translate=Hades}}, {{GHGheb|text=תֵּבֵל|translate=world}}, {{GHGheb|text=תְּהוֹם|translate=ocean}}, of the body of water which encircles the earth, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=2}}, &c.; but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=63|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=106|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=בַּתְּהֹמוֹת|translate=through the depths}}, viz. of the Red Sea.<ref>That various other words, such as {{GHGheb|text=אֱנוֹשׁ|translate=man}}, {{GHGheb|text=צַלְמָ֫וֶת|translate=deep darkness}}, {{GHGheb|text=רֹזֵן|translate=prince}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁדַי|translate=field}}, {{GHGheb|text=תּֽוּשִׁיָּה|translate=effectual working}}, are always found without the article is not to be attributed to any special archaism, but is to be explained from the fact that they belong solely to poetic language, which avoids the article; in other cases, such as {{GHGheb|text=תַּרְדֵּמָה|translate=deep sleep}}, there is no occasion for the article in the passages we possess.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|125|h}}
2. When nouns which the usage of the language always treats as proper names occasionally appear to be connected with a following genitive, this is really owing to an ellipse whereby the noun which really governs the genitive, i.e. the appellative idea contained in the proper name, is suppressed. So evidently in the case of {{GHGheb|text=יְהֹוָה צְבָאוֹת|translate=Yahweh}} (the God) ''of hosts''; the fuller form {{GHGheb|text=יהוה אֱלֹהֵי צְבָאוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=5|verse=10}}, &c., or {{GHGheb|text=יהוה אֱלֹהֵי הַצְּבָאוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=3|verse=13}}, &c., is a secondary expansion of the original {{GHGheb|text=יְהֹוָה צְבָאוֹת}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים צְבָאוֹת}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=59|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=80|verse=15|hidebook=1}}, 20, 84:9 is due to the mechanical substitution of {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} for {{GHGheb|text=יהוה}} affected in the 2nd and part of the 3rd book of the Psalms. So also in geographical names such as {{GHGheb|text=אוּר כַּשְׂדִּים|translate=Ur}} (the city) ''of the Chaldees'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=11|verse=28}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֲרַם נַֽהֲרַ֫יִם|translate=Aram}} (the region) ''of the two rivers''; {{GHGheb|text=בֵּית לֶ֫חֶם יְהוּדָה|translate=Bethlehem}} (the city) ''of Judah''; {{GHGheb|text=אָבֵל בֵּית מַֽעֲכָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=14}}, &c., to distinguish it from {{GHGheb|text=אָבֵל מַ֫יִם|translate=Abel by the water}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=16|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָבֵישׁ גִּלְעָד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=11|verse=1}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=יַרְדֵּן יְרֵחוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=26|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, 63, &c.; on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=32}} cf. {{GHGpar|128|c}}; {{GHGheb|text=צִיּוֹן קְדֹוֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל|translate=the Zion of the Holy One of Israel}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=60|verse=14}}; but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=1}} for {{GHGheb|text=צוֹפִים}} read {{GHGheb|text=צוּפִי|translate=a Zuphite}}. Some of these examples (cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=6|verse=2}}) come very near to the actual construct state (cf. above, {{GHGheb|text=גִּבְעַת שָׁאוּל}}), since e.g. the addition of the genitive serves to distinguish the place from four others called Aram (see the Lexicon), or from another Bethlehem. Aram, Bethlehem, &c., are accordingly no longer names found only in one special sense, and therefore also are no longer proper names in the strictest sense.

{{GHGmargin-letter|125|i}}
'''3.''' Of the pronouns, the personal pronouns proper (the separate pronouns, § 32) are always determinate in themselves, since they can denote only definite individuals (the 3rd person, also definite things). For the same reason the demonstrative pronouns (§ 34) are also determinate in themselves, when they stand ''alone'' (as equivalent to substantives), either as subject ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=5|verse=29}}) or as predicate (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=זֶה הַיּוֹם|translate=this is the day}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫לֶּה חַדְּבָרִים|translate=these are the words}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=1}}), or as object (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־זֹאת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=17}}), or as genitive ({{GHGheb|text=מְחִיר זֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=2}}), or finally when joined to a preposition ({{GHGheb|text=לְזֹאת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=23}}; {{GHGheb|text=בָּזֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=8}}, see {{GHGpar|102|g}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|125|k}}
So also the personal pronouns {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִיא}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵם}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫מָּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫נָּה}} when they are used as demonstratives (=''is'', ''ea, id, ille'', &c.) are always determinate in themselves, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הוּא הַדָּבָר|translate=that is the thing}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=28}}. They<section end=par125 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

428.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Sylow23" /></noinclude><section begin="par125" />are made determinate by the article, when they are joined like adjectives (see {{GHGpar|126|u}}) with a determinate substantive, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חָאִישׁ חַזֶּה|translate=this man}}; {{GHGheb|text=הָֽאֲנָשִּׁים הָאֵ֫לֶּה|translate=these men}}; {{GHGheb|text=בַּיָּמִים הָהֵ֫מָּה וּבָעֵת הַהִיא|translate=in those days, and in that time}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=4|verse=1}}. The demonstrative, however, even in this case, is frequently used ''without'' the article, as being sufficiently determinate in itself (cf. {{GHGpar|126|y}}).
<section end="par125" />
<section begin="par126" />{{GHGpar-heading|126|Determination by Means of the Article}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|a}}
'''1.''' The article ({{GHGheb|text=הַ·}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֶ}}, § 35) was originally, as in other languages (clearly in the Romance; cf. also ὁ, ἡ, τό in Homer), a demonstrative pronoun. The demonstrative force of the article, apart from its occasional use as a relative pronoun (see {{GHGpar|138|i}}), appears now, however, only (''a'') in a few standing phrases, and (''b'') in a certain class of statements or exclamations.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|b}}
(''a'') Cf. {{GHGheb|text=הַיּוֹם|translate=this day, hodie}} ({{GHGpar|100|c}}.); {{GHGheb|text=הַלַּ֫יְלָה|translate=this night}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=34}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַפַּ֫עַם|translate=this time}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=23}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַשָּׁנָה|translate=this year}} (= in this year) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=28|verse=16}}.

(''b'') includes those instances in which the article, mostly when prefixed to a participle, joins on a new statement concerning a preceding noun. Although such participles, &c., are no doubt primarily regarded always as in apposition to a preceding substantive, the article nevertheless has in some of these examples almost the force of {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} ({{GHGheb|text=הִיא}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫מָּה}}) as the subject of a noun-clause; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=19|verse=10}} ''the judgements of the Lord are true''..., verse 11 {{GHGheb|text=הַנֶּֽחֱמָדִים וג׳}} prop. ''the more to be desired than gold'', i.e. ''they are more to be desired'', or ''even they, that are more to be desired'',<ref>On the analogous use of the article before participles which have a verbal suffix, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=33}}, &c., cf. above, {{GHGpar|116|f}}.</ref> &c.; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=22}} f., 44:27 f., 46:6, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=2|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=33|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=49|verse=7|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=הַבֹּֽטְחִים}} in the parallel half of the verse continued by a finite verb); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=28|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=41|verse=25|hidebook=1}} and frequently. When such a participle has another co-ordinate with it, the latter is used ''without'' the article, since according to the above it strictly speaking represents a second predicate, and as such, according to ''i'', remains indeterminate; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=10}} ''who giveth'' ({{GHGheb|text=הַנֹּתֵן}}) ''rain'', &c. ''and sendeth'' {{GHGheb|text=וְשֹׁלֵחַ}} &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|c}}
The article is sometimes used with similar emphasis before a substantive, which serves as the subject of a compound sentence ({{GHGpar|140|d}}); e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=הַצּוּר תָּמִים פָּֽעֳלוֹ}} i.e. as a fresh statement (not in apposition to the preceding dative), really equivalent to ''he is a rock, perfect in his work'' (i.e. ''whose work is perfect''); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=31}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|d}}
'''2.''' The article is, generally speaking, employed to determine a substantive wherever it is required by Greek and English; thus:

(''a'') When a person or thing already spoken of is mentioned again, and is consequently more definite to the mind of the hearer or reader; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=3}} ''and God said, Let there be light'': verse 4 ''and God saw the light'' ({{GHGheb|text=אֶת־הָאוֹר}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=3|verse=24}} ''fetch me a sword: and they brought the sword''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=9|verse=15}}. (In {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=2}} therefore {{GHGheb|text=לֶֽעָשִׁיר}} must be read.)<section end="par126" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

429.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par126 />(''b'') With a title understood and recognized by every one, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַמֶּ֫לֶךְ שְׁלֹמהֹ}} ὁ βασιλεὺς Σαλωμών: {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=35|verse=8}} ''under the oak'' (the well-known oak which was there).

(''c'') With appellatives to denote persons or natural objects which are unique, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל|translate=the high priest}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַשֶּׁ֫מֶשׁ|translate=the sun}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָאָ֫רֶץ|translate=the earth}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|e}}
(''d'') When terms applying to whole classes are restricted (simply by usage) to particular individuals (like ὁ ποιητής, meaning Homer) or things, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שָׂטָן|translate=adversary}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַשָּׂטָן|translate=the adversary, Satan}}; {{GHGheb|text=בַּ֫עַל|translate=lord}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַבַּ֫עַל|translate=Baal}} as proper name of the god; {{GHGheb|text=הָֽאָדָם|translate=the}} (first) ''man, Adam''; {{GHGheb|text=הָאֱלֹהִים}}<ref>On the subsequent change of {{GHGheb|text=שָׂטָן}}, {{GHGheb|text=אָדָם}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} into real proper names by the omission of the article, cf. above, {{GHGpar|125|f}}.</ref> or {{GHGheb|text=הָאֵל}} ὁ θεός, ''the one true God'' (cf. also ὁ Χριστός in the New Testament); also {{GHGheb|text=הַנָּהָר|translate=the river}}, i.e. ''Euphrates''; {{GHGheb|text=הַכִּכָּר|translate=the circle}}, sc. of the Jordan, ''the Jordan plain'' [{{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=17}}, &c.].

(''e'') Very often with the vocative, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=הוֹשִׁ֫עָה הַמֶּ֫לֶךְ|translate=help, O king}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=3|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל|translate=O Joshua the high priest}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=58}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=24|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=9|verse=5}}; in the plural, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=1|verse=2}}, 13; but cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=10|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=13|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=שָׁמַ֫יִם}} and {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫רֶץ}}); 23:16, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=13|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=1|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=34|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=10|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=11|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, &c.<ref>For further exceptions see Nestle, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZAW.|Zeitschrift für die alttestamentliche Wissenschaft, ed. by B. Stade, Giessen, 1881 ff., and since 1907 by K. Marti.}}}} 1904, p. 323 ff.</ref> The vocative occurs ''without'' the article in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=2}}, since it has been already defined by a preceding accusative.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|f}}
Rem. Strictly speaking in all these cases the substantive with the article is really in apposition to the personal pronoun of the 2nd person, which is either expressly mentioned or virtually present (in the imperative), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=58}} ''thou, the young man''. But such passages as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=18}}, where the vocative precedes the imperative, prove that in such cases the substantive originally in apposition eventually acquired the value of a complete clause.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|g}}
(''f'') With words denoting classes (see particulars under l).

(''g'') In a peculiar way, to specify persons or things, which are so far definite as to be naturally thought of in connexion with a given case, and must be assumed accordingly to be there (see q–s).

(''h'') With adjectives (also ordinal numbers and demonstrative pronouns used adjectivally) which are joined to substantives determined in some way (see u).

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|h}}
Rem. The article may be omitted in ''poetry'' in all the above-mentioned cases; in general it is used in poetry far less frequently than in prose. Its use or omission probably often rests on rhythmical grounds;<ref>Cf. the useful statistics of J. Ley in the {{GHGcite|title=Neue Jahrbücher für Philologie und Pädagogik}}, 2te Abteilung, 1891, Heft 7–9, and M. Lambert, ‘ ''L’article dans la po&ésie hébr.'',’ {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} 37, 263 ff.</ref> it is sometimes omitted also for rhetorical reasons. Cf. e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫רֶץ}} for {{GHGheb|text=הָאָ֫רֶץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=מְלָכִים}} as vocative, verse 10; {{GHGheb|text=מֶ֫לֶךְ}} for {{GHGheb|text=הַמֶּ֫לֶךְ}} 21:2; {{GHGheb|text=שִׁמְךָ גָּדוֹל וְנוֹרָא}} (contrary to ''u, v'') 99:3. In the instances in which the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} of the article is omitted after a prefix ({{GHGpar|35|n}}), the vowel of the article is often retained after the prefix even in poetry, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בַּשָּׁמַ֫יִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=4}}, &c.
<section end=par126 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

430.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="ShakespeareFan00" /></noinclude><section begin="par126" />{{GHGmargin-letter|126|i}}
(''i'') On the other hand, the article is always omitted when a person or thing is to be represented as indefinite (or indefinable) or as yet unknown; consequently also before the predicate, since this is from its nature always a general term, under which the subject is included, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=עוֹד הַיּוֹם גָּדוֹל|translate=as yet the day is great}}, i.e. it is yet high day; 33:13, 40:18, 41:26, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=66|verse=3}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|k}}
Rem. 1. As exceptions to the above rule it is usual to regard those examples in which a determinate adjective or participle (equivalent to a relative clause) is used apparently as a predicate, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=הוּא הַסֹּבֵב|translate=it is the compassing}}, i.e. ''that is it which compasseth''; 42:6, 45:12, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=3|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=8|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=11|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mal|chapter=3|verse=2}} (cf. in Greek, e.g. St. Mat. 10:20, where Winer, ''Gram. des neutest. Sprachidioms'', § 58, 2, Rem., explains οἱ λαλοῦντες as a predicate with the article). In reality, however, these supposed predicates are rather subjects (acc. to {{GHGpar|116|q}}), and the only peculiarity of these cases is that the subject is not included under a general idea, but is equated with the predicate.

2. Sometimes the article is used with only one of two parallel words, as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=1|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=חָרִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=הַגְּבָעוֹת}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=3|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=מִיָּמִין}} and {{GHGheb|text=מֵֽהַשְּׂמֹאול}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|l}}
'''3.''' The use of the article to determine the ''class'' is more extensive in Hebrew than in most other languages. In this case the article indicates universally known, closely circumscribed, and therefore well defined classes of persons or things. The special cases to be considered are—

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|m}}
(''a'') The employment of general names as collectives in the singular, to denote the ''sum total'' of individuals belonging to the class (which may, however, be done just as well by the plural); e.g. ''the righteous, the wicked man'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=3|verse=17}}; ''the woman'', i.e. ''the female sex'', 7:26; {{GHGheb|text=הָֽאֹיֵב|translate=the enemy}}, i.e. ''the enemies'' (?) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=9|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=הָֽאֹרֵב|translate=the liers in wait}}, i.e. ''the liers in wait''; {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽחָלוּץ|translate=the armed man}}, i.e. ''soldiers''; {{GHGheb|text=הַֽמְאַסֵּף|translate=the rearguard}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַמַּשְׁחִית|translate=the spoiler}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=17}};<ref>But in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=23}} {{GHGheb|text=המ׳}} is either to be explained as ''the destroyer'' (now mentioned for the first time) according to ''q'', or a particular angel is meant whose regular function it was to inflict punishments. Others again take {{GHGheb|text=המ׳}} even in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=23}} impersonally = ''destruction''.</ref> so also (as in English) with names of animals, when something is asserted of them, which applies to the whole species, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=10}} ''as the courage of'' {{GHGheb|text=הָֽאַרְיֵה|translate=the lion}}. Especially also with gentilic names, e.g. ''the Canaanite'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=13|verse=7}} (cf.15:19<sup> f.</sup>); so in English ''the Russian, the Turk'', &c., in Attic writers ὁ Ἀθηναῖος, ὁ Συρακόσιος, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|n}}
(''b'') Names of materials known everywhere, the elements and other words denoting classes, even though only a part and not the whole of them is considered, in which case in other languages, as e.g. in English, the article is usually omitted (cf., however, our ''to fall into the water, into the fire'', &c.), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=13|verse=2}} ''and Abram was very rich'' {{GHGheb|text=בַּמִּקְנֶה בַּבֶּסֶף וּבַוָּהָב|translate=in cattle, in silver and in gold}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=11|verse=9}} ''and he burnt their chariots'' {{GHGheb|text=בָּאֵשׁ|translate=with fire}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=42|hidebook=1}} (unless this means, ''the chain'' necessarily belonging to the official dress); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=14|hidebook=1}} (35:32), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=22}}, &c., and {{GHGheb|text=בַּשָּׁמֶן|translate=with oil}}<ref>In nearly all the above examples the presence of the article is only indicated by the vowel of the prefix ({{GHGheb|text=בַּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=כַּ‍}}, {{GHGheb|text=לַ}}) and might therefore be merely due to the masoretic punctuation. There is, however, no reason to doubt the correctness of the tradition. The same is true of the examples under ''n'' and ''o''.</ref> very commonly in the sacrificial laws, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=29|verse=2}},<section end="par126" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

431.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par126 />&c., and also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=1|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=23|verse=5}}, &c. Similarly the article is used with terms of measurement, as {{GHGheb|text=הָֽאֵפָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=36}}, &c.: {{GHGheb|text=הַחֹמֶר}} and {{GHGheb|text=הַבַּת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=45|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=הָעֹ֫מֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=בַּחֶ֫בֶל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=8|verse=2}}.

(''c'') The expression of abstract ideas of every kind, since they are likewise used to represent whole classes of attributes or states, physical or moral defects, &c.; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=5}} ({{GHGheb|text=בַּצֶּ֫דֶק}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=11}} ''and they smote the men''... {{GHGheb|text=בַּסַּנְוֵרִים|translate=with blindness}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=4|verse=9}}, &c.; but in {{GHGheb|text=הַח֫שֶׁךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=60|verse=2}} the article is no doubt due to dittography of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, and the parallel {{GHGheb|text=וַֽעֲרָפֶל}} has no article.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|o}}
(''d'') ''Comparisons'', since the object compared is treated not (as usually in English) individually but as a general term, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=18}} ''white'' {{GHGheb|text=כַּשֶּׁ֫לֶג|translate=as snow}}, {{GHGheb|text=כַּצֶּ֫מֶר|translate=as wool}}; ''red'' {{GHGheb|text=כַּתּוֹלָע|translate=like crimson}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=34|verse=4}} ''and the heavens shall be rolled together'' {{GHGheb|text=כַּסֵּפֶר|translate=as a scroll}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=9|hidebook=1}} ''as'' {{GHGheb|text=פְּתִיל־הַנְּעֹרֶת|translate=a string of tow is broken}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=26|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=8|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=53|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=33|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=49|verse=15|hidebook=1}}; cf. also such examples as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=6}}, where the object compared is determined by a determinate genitive which follows (according to {{GHGpar|127|a}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|p}}
Examples of indeterminate comparisons are rare, and perhaps due only to the Masora,—so at least in the case of singulars, while in such plurals as those in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=10|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=2|verse=4}}, 7, the omission of the article may be explained by the ordinary rules. On the other hand, the article is regularly omitted when the object compared is already defined by means of an attribute (or relative clause, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=17|verse=12}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=16|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=כְּעוֹף נוֹדֵד קֵן מְשֻׁלָּח|translate=as wandering birds}}, (as) ''a scattered nest'' (but cf. 10:14 {{GHGheb|text=כַּקֵּן}}); 14:19, 29:5 {{GHGheb|text=כְּמֹץ עֹבֵר}} (but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=1|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=כַּמֹּץ}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=27|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=14|hidebook=1}}.—In comparisons with persons also the Masora seems to avoid the use of the article, as in {{GHGheb|text=כְּגִבּוֹר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=14}} and seven other places ({{GHGheb|text=כַּגִּכּוֹר}} only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=13}}), {{GHGheb|text=כְּאָב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=18}}, {{GHGheb|text=כְּגֶ֫בֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=40|verse=7|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|q}}
'''4.''' Peculiar to Hebrew<ref>Cf., however, analogous examples in biblical Aramaic in Kautzsch’s {{GHGcite|title=Gramm. des Bibl. Aram.}}, 79 f, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=2|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=3|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, &c.</ref> is the employment of the article to denote a single person or thing (primarily one which is as yet unknown, and therefore not capable of being defined) as being present to the mind under given circumstances. In such cases in English the indefinite article is mostly used.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|r}}
Thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=19}} ''as if a man did flee from a lion'' ({{GHGheb|text=הָֽאֲרִי}}, i.e. the particular lion pursuing him at the time), ''and a bear'' ({{GHGheb|text=הַדֹּב}}) ''met him'', &c., cf. 3:12, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=36}} (John 10:12); also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=7}} f., 14:13 ({{GHGheb|text=הַפָּלִיט}}, i.e. ''one that had escaped'', the particular one who came just then; so also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=24|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=33|verse=21|hidebook=1}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=13}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=1}}, 11 18:7 ''the servant'', who is regarded as being constantly at hand and awaiting his commands; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=17}} (but {{GHGheb|text=הַנַּ֫עַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=27}} is used like {{GHGheb|text=הַפָּלִיט}} above); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=30}}, unless {{GHGheb|text=בַּמְּעָרָה}} means in ''the'' well-known ''cave''; {{GHGheb|text=בַּמָּקוֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=28|verse=11}}, according to Dillmann, upon ''the'' place suitable for passing the night, or the right place, but it may possibly also refer to ''the'' sanctuary of Bethel afterwards so sacred and celebrated; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=46|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=50|verse=26|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=4|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=20|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=23|verse=21}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=23|verse=42}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=24|verse=10|hidebook=1}} (Samaritan {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׂרְאֵלִי}} without the article); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, 9, 25:6, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=19|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=25|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=29|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=34}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=6|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=13|verse=14|hidebook=1}} (? most<section end=par126 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

432.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par126 />probably a particular tree is meant); 19:9, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=14}} ({{GHGheb|text=הָֽעַלְמָה}}, i.e. ''the'' particular ''maiden'', through whom the prophet’s announcement shall be fulfilled; we should say ''a maiden'' [cf. Driver on {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=8|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=13|hidebook=1}}]; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=31}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|s}}
So always ''to write in the book'' (or ''on the scroll'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=32|verse=10}}), i.e. not in ''the'' book already in use, but in the book which is to be devoted to that purpose, equivalent to ''in a book, on a scroll'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=17|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=10|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=23}}. Especially instructive for this use of the article is the phrase {{GHGheb|text=וַיְהִי הַיּוֹם}}, which does not simply refer back to the previous narrative in the sense of ''the same day'', but is used exactly like our ''one day'' (properly meaning on the particular day when it happened, i.e. ''on a certain day''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=4|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=11|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=6}}, 13. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=11}} even {{GHGheb|text=כְּהַיּוֹם הַזֶּה}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|t}}
The article is sometimes used in this way before collectives in the singular, which are not meant to denote (like the examples given under ''l'') a whole class, but only that part of it which applies to the given case; thus {{GHGheb|text=הָֽעֹרֵב}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַיּוֹנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=7}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַצִּרְעָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=28}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|u}}
'''5.''' When a substantive is defined by the article, or by a suffix, or by a following genitive determinate in any way (see the examples below), the attribute belonging to it (whether adjective, participle, ordinal, or demonstrative pronoun) necessarily takes the article (see, however, the Rem.), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=10|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=הָעִיר הַגְּדֹלָה|translate=the great city}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=3|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=יָֽדְךָ הַֽחֲזָקָה|translate=thy strong hand}}. A genitive following the substantive may, according to {{GHGpar|127|a}}, be determined either by the article, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=25}} {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ הַבְּלִיַּעַל הַוֶּה|translate=this worthless man}} (prop. ''man of worthlessness''; cf. also such examples as {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=36|verse=18}}, where the article is prefixed only to a second genitive following the noun); or as a proper name, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=11|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=מַֽעֲשֵׂה יְהֹוָה הַגָּדֹל|translate=the great work of the Lord}}; or by a suffix, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=36|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=עַבְדֵי אֲדֹנִי הַקְּטַנִּים}} ''the least of my master’s servants''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|v}}
When several attributes (whether connected by {{GHGterm|Wāw}} or not) follow a determinate substantive, each of them takes the article, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=10|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=הָאֵל הַגָּדֹל הַגִּבֹּר וְהַבּוֹרָא|translate=the great God, the mighty, and the terrible}}. Cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=19}}, in both of which places a demonstrative with the article also follows the adjective.<ref>The demonstrative used adjectivally is generally placed ''after'' the adjective proper; in such cases as {{GHGheb|text=עַמְּךָ הַזֶּה הַגָּדוֹל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=1|verse=10}} the adjective forms a further (fresh) addition to {{GHGheb|text=עַמְּךָ הַזֶּה}}.</ref>

Rem. 1. The article is, however, not infrequently used also—

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|w}}
(''a'') With the attribute alone, when it is added to an originally indefinite substantive as a subsequent limitation; so always with ordinal numbers after {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם}},<ref>Cf. Driver, {{GHGcite|title=Tenses}}, 3rd ed., 209; M. Lambert, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} 31, 279 f.—The omission of the article from the substantive is not to be regarded in ''this'' instance as an indication of late style, and consequently cannot be put forward as a proof of the late origin of the ‘Priestly Code’ (cf. Dillmann on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=31}}, Holzinger, ''Einl. in d. Hexateuch'', p. 465, and especially Driver in the {{GHGcite|title=Journal of Philology}}, xi. 229 f., against Giesebrecht in {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZAW.|Zeitschrift für die alttestamentliche Wissenschaft, ed. by B. Stade, Giessen, 1881 ff., and since 1907 by K. Marti.}}}} 1881, p. 265 f.). On the other hand, the common omission of the article from the substantive before a determinate adjective (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כְּנֵ֫סֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה|translate=the great synagogue}}, in the Mishna; cf.
