Segal, ''Mišnaic Hebrew'', p. 19 ff.) is certainly a later idiom.</ref> e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=31}} (cf. 2:3, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=10}}, &c.) {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי|translate=the sixth day}} (prop. ''a day'' namely<section end=par126 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

433.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par126 />''the sixth''; but {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם שֵׁנִי|translate=a second day}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=8}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=מִיּוֹם הָֽרִאשֹׁן|translate=from the first day onward}} (not before {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=10|verse=12}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=8|verse=18}} is {{GHGheb|text=מִן־הַיּוֹם הָֽרִאשׁוֹן}} used instead of it). On the other hand, the article is ''always'' found after {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}}, hence {{GHGheb|text=בַּיּוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי}}, &c., although it is possible that the original reading in these cases was {{GHGheb|text=בְּיוֹם}}, and that the article is only due to the Masora. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=25}} the text is evidently corrupt (see verse 26).—Especially also in certain frequently recurring combinations as in particularizing the gates in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=38|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=9|verse=2}}, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=14|verse=10}}, and courts in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=7|verse=8}}, 12, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=40|verse=28}}; and very often when the attribute consists of a participle, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=21|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=27|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=46|verse=16|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=חֶ֫רֶב הַיּוֹנָה|translate=the sword which oppresses}} (''?''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=14|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=11|verse=2}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} (''the impenetrable forest?'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=26|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=21}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|x}}
Of the other examples, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=29}} (where, however, the Samaritan reads {{GHGheb|text=הכבשות}}), 41:26 (but cf. verse 4), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=17}} may at any rate be explained on the ground that the preceding cardinal number is equivalent to a determinant; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=28|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, 10, &c., the substantive is already determined by {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־}}, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=29}} ({{GHGheb|text=דְּבַשׁ}}) by {{GHGheb|text=מְעַט}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=12|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=20}} (where, however, {{GHGheb|text=הַשְּׂכִירָה}} might also be understood as a subsequent explanation of {{GHGheb|text=בְּתַ֫עַר}}) and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=9|verse=35}}, the omission of the article after the preposition is certainly due merely to the Masora. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=23}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=רוּחַ אֱלֹהִים}} is to be read twice), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=4|verse=7}} (where however {{GHGheb|text=אַתָּ הָהָר}} is probably meant), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=18}} (where a {{GHGheb|text=ה}} precedes {{GHGheb|text=הָרִים}}, hence probably a case of haplography), the omission of the article before {{GHGheb|text=א}}, {{GHGheb|text=ר}} (?) and {{GHGheb|text=ה}} may be due to a regard for euphony (see z below). On the other hand, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=18}} (read {{GHGheb|text=הָאֶ֫בֶן הַגְּ׳}}), 17:12 ({{GHGheb|text=הַזֶּה}} is a later addition), 19:22 (cf. the LXX), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=32|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=40|verse=3|hidebook=1}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=2|verse=3}} (read {{GHGheb|text=גּוֹי}} or omit {{GHGheb|text=גּוֹיִם}} with Cornill), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=62|verse=4}}, either the text is corrupt, or the expression incorrect. But in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=20|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=7|verse=10}} acc. to D. H. Müller (''Anzeiger der Wiener Akad.'', phil-hist. Kl. 1902, no. x) {{GHGheb|text=הַטּוֹב}} is the genitive of a substantive, ''aromatic oil, sweet cane'' (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=20}} read {{GHGheb|text=וּקְנֵה}}), ''like spiced wine''. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=39|verse=2}} read {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫מֶן הַטּוֹב}} and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=133|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=כְּשֶׁ֫מֶן חַטּ׳}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|y}}
(''b'') No article with the attribute, while the substantive is determined either by the article, or a suffix, or a following genitive. Thus the article is sometimes omitted with demonstratives, since they are already to a certain extent determined by their meaning (cf. also the ''Mêšaʿ'' inscription, l. 3, {{GHGheb|text=הבמת זאת|translate=this high place}}); as with {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=33}} (evidently for euphony, and so probably often); 30:16, 32:23, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=10}}; with {{GHGheb|text=הִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=21}}; with {{GHGheb|text=זוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=12|verse=8}} (according to the Masora {{GHGheb|text=זוּ}} is a relative pronoun here, as always elsewhere); with {{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫לֶּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=23}}, according to the present corrupt text (the original reading {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־עַם יהוה}} became {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־עַם אֱלֹהִים}}, and {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} was then corrupted to {{GHGheb|text=אֵלֶּה}}); so, almost without exception, when the substantive is determined only by a suffix, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=10|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=1|verse=2}} and 8:8 f., where {{GHGheb|text=חלי}}, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=10|verse=19}}, has arisen by contraction from {{GHGheb|text=חָלְיִי}}, or we should simply read {{GHGheb|text=חָלְיִ}} (in all these passages with {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=8}} (with {{GHGheb|text=זֹאת}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=21}} (with {{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫לֶּה}}).

The article is sometimes omitted also with the attributes referring to proper names,<ref>Cf. Nöldeke, ''Beiträge zur semit. Sprachwiss.'', p. 48, n. 1.</ref> as {{GHGheb|text=צִידוֹן רַבָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=11|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=19|verse=28|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֲמָת רַבָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=6|verse=2}}. Other examples are {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=16|verse=3}}, 5, 18:13, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=9|verse=17}} (but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=7|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=8|verse=5}} with the article). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=11}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=תְּהוֹם רַבָּה}} is also a case of this kind, {{GHGheb|text=תְּהוֹם}} being used (almost always without the article) as a sort of proper name; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אֵל עֶלְיוֹן|translate=the most high}}<section end=par126 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

434.text:
''God'' and {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים חַי|translate=the living God}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=1|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=גֻּלּתֹ עִלִּית}} and {{GHGheb|text=גּ׳ תַּחְתִּית}} are strange; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=15|verse=19}} has {{GHGheb|text=גּ׳ עִלִּיּוֹת}} and {{GHGheb|text=גּ׳ תַּחְתִּיּוֹת}}. {{GHGmargin-letter|126|z}} Of the remaining examples {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=11|verse=9}} explains itself; the direct connexion of the attribute with its substantive is broken by the insertion of {{GHGheb|text=לַיָּם}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=34|verse=12}}, Hag. 1:4 (as Wellhausen says, a good instance of a Hebrew adjective in the stative form = {{GHGheb|text=וְהֵם סְפוּנִים}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=143|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=6|verse=12}} (?) the substantive is also (see above) determined by a suffix, and consequently the attribute is less closely attached; the same applies to {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=18}}, except that in these passages the omission of the article before {{GHGheb|text=ר}}, {{GHGheb|text=א}}, {{GHGheb|text=ע}} may at the same time be due to considerations of euphony (as also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=16|verse=1}} before {{GHGheb|text=ע}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=37}} before {{GHGheb|text=ר}}, 28:4, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=10|verse=9}} before {{GHGheb|text=א}}, 21:19 before {{GHGheb|text=ח}}).The same reason no doubt also favoured the omission of the article before {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} and {{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫לֶּה}}, see above, under y. Also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=7}} (''is this your joyous''...?) the article is omitted before {{GHGheb|text=עַלִּיזָה}} probably only for euphony. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=17}} f. ({{GHGheb|text=אֶחָד}}) and {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=25|verse=16}} ({{GHGheb|text=שְׁנַ֫יִם}} after a determinate substantive), the attribute again, being a numeral, is determinate in itself (see above, x); in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=65|verse=2}} the {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} prevents the use of the article; finally, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=26|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּחִצִּים}} and {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽאֲבָנִים}} are to be read, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=21}} {{GHGheb|text=גֶּ֫פֶן}} for {{GHGheb|text=הַגֶּ֫פֶן}}, in 22:26 {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫רֶץ}} for {{GHGheb|text=הָאָ׳}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=6|verse=3}} omit {{GHGheb|text=חֲדָשָׁה}}, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=39|verse=27}} omit {{GHGheb|text=רַבִּים}}. Without any apparent reason the article is omitted in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=8|verse=13}} and 11:31. {{GHGmargin-letter|126|aa}} 2. When, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=12}} ({{GHGheb|text=יוֹם הוּא|translate=in that day?}}), the article is omitted from both substantive and demonstrative, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=3|verse=12}}, the demonstrative even precedes ({{GHGheb|text=זֶה חַבַּ֫יִת}}={{GHGheb|text=הַבַּ֫יִת הַזֶּה}}), this is obviously due in both cases to a radical corruption of the text (not only in the words quoted). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=9|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=לַחְמֵ֫נוּ}} is either in apposition to the independent demonstrative {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} (= ''this our bread'', &c.), as in verse 13 {{GHGheb|text=נֹאדוֹת}} is to {{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫לֶּה}}, or they are complete sentences, ''this is our bread'', &c. So also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=משֶׁה}} (= ''that'' [''iste''] ''Moses'', &c.), and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=48|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} are to be taken in apposition to {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}}. On {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=8}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=13}} cf. {{GHGpar|136|d}}.
{{GHGpar-heading|127|The Noun determined by a following Determinate Genitive}}
Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, i. 475.
{{GHGmargin-letter|127|a}} When a genitive, determined in any way, follows a {{GHGterm|nomen regens}}, it also determines the {{GHGterm|nomen regens}}, which, according to {{GHGpar|89|a}}, is always in the construct state. Moreover, every pronominal suffix attached to a substantive is, according to {{GHGpar|33|c}}, to be considered as a genitive determinate by nature. An independent genitive may be determinate— (''a'') By its character as a ''proper name'' (according to {{GHGpar|125|a}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=דְּבַר יְהֹוָה|translate=the word of the Lord}}. (''b'') By having the article, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ הַמִּלְחָמָה}} (prop. the man of the war) ''the soldier'' (but {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=17|verse=1}}, ''a soldier''); {{GHGheb|text=אַנְשֵׁי הַמִּלְחָמָה}}

435.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par127 />{{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=31|verse=49}}, ''the soldiers''; {{GHGheb|text=דְּבַר הַנָּבִיא|translate=the word of the prophet}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=28|verse=9}} (but e.g., on the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=מִצְוַת אֲנָשִׁים מְלֻמָּדָה|translate=a commandment of men which hath been taught}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=13}}; {{GHGheb|text=דְּבַר־שָׁ֑קֶר|translate=word of falsehood}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=29|verse=12}}).

(''c'') By the addition of a pronominal suffix (see above), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בֵּֽית־אָבִי}} ''my father’s house''.

(''d'') By construction with another genitive determined in some way, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=מִפְּרִי עֵֽץ־הַגָּן|translate=of the fruit of the trees of the garden}}. Thus in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=12}} four, and in 21:17 even five, members of a series are determined by a concluding determinate genitive.

{{GHGmargin-letter|127|b}}
Rem. 1. The above explains also the various meanings of {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל}} (prop. a substantive in the sense of ''aggregate, whole''), according as it is followed by a determinate or indeterminate genitive. In the former case {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל}} has the meaning of ''the entirety'', i.e. ''all, the whole'' (like the French ''tous les hommes, toute la ville''), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־הָאָרֶץ|translate=the whole}} (prop. the entirety of the) ''earth'', {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־הָֽאָדָם|translate=all men}};<ref>{{GHGheb|text=הָֽאָדָם}} being a collective, cf. {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־הָאִישׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=2}}, ''all men'', {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־הַכֵּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=22}} ''all sons'', {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־הַבַּת|translate=all daughters}}; in itself {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־הָֽאָרָם}} could also mean ''the whole man''.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=18|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=15|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=4|verse=29}}, and cases like {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=4|verse=23}}, 47, 21:8 where {{GHGheb|text=כָּל}} is followed by a singular participle with the article. On the other hand, before an indeterminate genitive {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל}} is used in the more indefinite (individualizing) sense of ''of all kinds, any'' (cf. ''tout homme, à tout prix''), or distributively ''each, every'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־עֵץ|translate=every}} (kind of) ''tree'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=9}}; cf. 4:22, 24:10, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=29|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־דָּבָר|translate=any thing}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּכָל־יוֹם|translate=every day, every time}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=7|verse=12}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|127|c}}
It is, however, to be observed—

(''a'') That the article may in this case also (see {{GHGpar|126|h}}) be omitted in poetic style, although the substantive is to be regarded as determinate, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־שֻׁלְחָנוֹת|translate=all}} (the) ''tables'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=8}}.

(''b'') That the meaning ''every'' is frequent even before singulars used collectively; afterwards the idea of ''quisque'' passes naturally into that of ''totality'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־חַי|translate=each living thing}}, i.e. ''every'' (not ''every kind of'') ''living thing''; {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־בָּשָׂר|translate=all flesh}}, i.e. ''all men'' or ''all living creatures'' (with the article only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=15}} before a relative clause, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=6}}); sometimes also {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־עֵץ|translate=all trees}}, {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־עוֹף|translate=all birds}}; finally—

(''c'') That before the names of members of the human body, {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־}} frequently (as being determinate in itself) denotes the entirety, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=5}} ''the whole head, the whole heart'' (the sense required by the context, not ''every head'', &c., which the expression ''in itself'' might also mean); 9:11, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=23|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=29|verse=7}} ''all'' (i.e. ''the whole of'') ''their shoulders''... ''all'' (''the whole of'') ''their loins''; 36:5.—On {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל}} with a suffix when it follows a noun in apposition (e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=9|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=הָעָם כֻּלּוֹ|translate=the people, all of it}}, i.e. ''the whole nation'', more emphatic than {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־הָעָם}}, cf. Driver on {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=9}}), as well as when it follows absolutely in the genitive (= ''all men, every one'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=12}}),<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=10|verse=17}} instead of {{GHGheb|text=בַּכֹּל אֲנָשִׁים}} read simply {{GHGheb|text=בְּכָל־הָֽאֲנָשִׁים}}.</ref> see the Lexicon, pp. 481<sup>b</sup>, 482<sup>b</sup>.

{{GHGmargin-letter|127|d}}
2. Gentilic names (or patronymics), derived from compound proper names (consisting of a nomen regens and genitive), are determined by inserting the article before the second part of the compound (since it contains the original<section end=par127 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

436.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par127 />genitive), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־יְמִינִי}} (see {{GHGpar|86|h}}) ''a Benjamite'', {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־הַיְמִינִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=3|verse=15}}, &c., ''the Benjamite''; {{GHGheb|text=בֵּֽית־הַלַּחְמִי|translate=the Bethlehemite}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=1}}, &c. (cf., however, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=27|verse=12}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} {{GHGheb|text=לַבֵּן יְמִינִי}}); {{GHGheb|text=בֵּֽית־הַשִּׁמְשִׁי|translate=the Beth-shemite}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֲבִי הָֽעֶזְרִי|translate=the Abiezrite}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=11}}, &c., cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=16|verse=34}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|127|e}}
3. In a few instances the nomen regens appears to be used indefinitely notwithstanding a following determinate genitive; it is not so, however, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=7}}, where the reference is to a well-known fountain; 21:28, where in the original context there must have been some reason for ''the seven ewe lambs of the flock''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=30}} ''the spoil found in the city''; but it often is so before a proper name, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=חַג יְהֹוָה|translate=a feast of the Lord}} (unless it is ''the'' spring festival), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=7|verse=25}}, and frequently {{GHGheb|text=תּֽוֹעֲבַת יְהֹוָה|translate=an abomination unto the Lord}}; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=46|verse=34}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=22|verse=19}} ''a virgin of Israel''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=12}} ''a man of Benjamin''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=2|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=3|verse=9|hidebook=1}}; similarly before appellatives with the article (or before a genitive determined by a suffix, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=14|verse=34}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=20}} ''three arrows''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=23|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=חֶלְקַת הַשָּׂדֶה|translate=a plot of the ground}} (but see {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=24|verse=32}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=41|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=11}}, 13 f., 5:13, 7:3, 8:2. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁיר הַמַּֽעֲלוֹת}} in the titles of Psalms 120 to 134 (except 121:1, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁיר לַמַּֽעֲלוֹת}}) was most probably originally the title of a collection, in the sense of ''‘the pilgrimage-songs’'' (according to {{GHGpar|124|r}}), and was subsequently added to these Psalms severally.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּכָל־הַמָּקוֹם|translate=in all the place}}, sc. of the sanctuary, is a dogmatic correction of {{GHGheb|text=בְּכָל־מָקוֹם}}, ''in every place'', to avoid the difficulty that several holy-places are here authorized, instead of the one central sanctuary. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=20|verse=13}} also {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־הַמָּקוֹם}} (unless it means ''in the whole place'') is remarkable, since elsewhere ''every place'' is always (8 times) {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־מָקוֹם}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|127|f}}
4. The deviations mentioned under ''e'', from a fundamental rule of syntax, are in some cases open to suspicion on textual grounds, but much more doubtful are the instances in which the article is found before a noun already determined in some other way, as—

(''a'') Before a noun which appears to be determined by a following independent determinate genitive. The least questionable are the instances in which the genitive is a ''proper name'', since these may be elliptical forms of expression like the apparent construction of proper names with a genitive, noticed in {{GHGpar|125|h}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=הַנְּחָלִים אַרְנוֹן|translate=the valleys}}, namely the valleys ''of Arnon''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=23|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=הַמִּזְבַּח בֵּית־אֵל|translate=the altar}}, namely the altar of ''Bethel'' (i.e. with the suppression of the real nomen regens, {{GHGheb|text=מִזְבַּח}} without the article; by the pointing {{GHGheb|text=הַמִּזְבַּח}} the Masora evidently intends to allow the choice either of reading {{GHGheb|text=הַמִּזְבֵּחַ}} or correcting it to {{GHGheb|text=מִזְבַּח}}); {{GHGheb|text=הָאֵל בֵּית־אֵל|translate=the God of Beth-el}}<ref>According to Philippi ({{GHGterm|st. constr.}}, p. 38) {{GHGheb|text=בית־אל}} is rather a case of ‘sub-position’ in the accusative, as also {{GHGheb|text=הַדֶּ֫רֶךְ חֶתְלוֹן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=47|verse=15}} (for which, however, in 48:1 there is the correct reading {{GHGheb|text=דֶּ֫רֶךְ חֶתְלוֹן}}) ''by the way to Hethlon''; and in fact, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=47|verse=15}} may without difficulty be explained in this way; so {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=39|verse=27}} as an accusative of the material.</ref> (equivalent to {{GHGheb|text=הָאֵל אֵל בּ׳}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=13}} (the LXX read {{GHGheb|text=הָאֵל הַנִּרְאֶה אֵלֶיךָ כַמָּקוֹם|translate=the God who appeared to thee in the}} holy ''place''); {{GHGheb|text=הַמֶּלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר|translate=the king of Assyria}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=36|verse=16}} (probably a scribal error due to verse 13; it does not occur in the parallel passage, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=18|verse=31}}), cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=13|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=25|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=38|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=47|verse=15}}; in the vocative, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=2|verse=13}}. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=שָׂרָה אִמּוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=67}} is no doubt<section end=par127 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

437.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par127 />only a subsequent insertion; so also {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׂרָאֵל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=8|verse=33}}b (cf. LXX), {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=7|verse=13}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַמֶּ֫לֶךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=26|verse=22}} after {{GHGheb|text=הַחֲנִיה}} (simplified by the Masora to {{GHGheb|text=חֲנִית}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}); {{GHGheb|text=עֲלִיַּת אָחָז}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=23|verse=12}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַשּׁוּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=36|verse=8}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=18|verse=23}}), {{GHGheb|text=הַקֹּדֶשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=46|verse=19}} (unless the article with {{GHGheb|text=לשכות}} is to be omitted), also {{GHGheb|text=הַתָּמִיד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=8|verse=13}}, and {{GHGheb|text=עֹדֵד הַנָּבִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=15|verse=8}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=18}} read with the Samaritan {{GHGheb|text=לְמִיּוֹם}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=25}} {{GHGheb|text=לֶ֫כֶת}} might possibly be taken in apposition to {{GHGheb|text=לְמִן הַיּוֹם}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=10|verse=1}} restore {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־בְּנֵי}}, with the LXX and Lucian, before {{GHGheb|text=אַחְאָב}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=25|verse=19}} omit the article, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=52|verse=25}}, before {{GHGheb|text=סֹפֵר}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|127|g}}
A similar ellipse must also be assumed in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=23|verse=17}} ''the sepulchre is'' the sepulchre ''of the man of God'' (but most probably {{GHGheb|text=קֶבֶר}} has dropped out after {{GHGheb|text=הַקֶּבֶר}}) and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=123|verse=4}} (cf., however, the LXX, and observe that in the parallel member the genitive is paraphrased by {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}).—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=3|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=הַבְּרִית}} (verse 17 {{GHGheb|text=בְּרִית יהוה}}) has been added to the original {{GHGheb|text=הָֽאָרוֹן}} by a redactor; cf. similar syntactically impossible additions in verse 11 (also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=3}}, &c., where the LXX still had simply {{GHGheb|text=אֲרוֹן יהוה}}); in {{GHGheb|text=הַיְחַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=14}} the Masora evidently combines two different readings {{GHGheb|text=הַיָּחֵד}} and {{GHGheb|text=יְתַד הָאֶרֶג}}; and similarly in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=25|verse=26}} (where {{GHGheb|text=הָאָ֫רֶץ}} was only subsequently introduced into the text), the two readings {{GHGheb|text=הַמַּמְלָכוֹת}} and {{GHGheb|text=מַמְלְכוֹת הָא׳}} are combined.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=8|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=40}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=45|verse=16}} the article, being usual after {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־}}, has been mechanically added, and so also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=8|verse=16}} after {{GHGheb|text=עַד־}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=9|verse=4}} the second {{GHGheb|text=הַנַּ֫עַד}} (instead of {{GHGheb|text=נַ֫עַר}}) is occasioned by the first; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=7|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=מְהוּמָה}} belongs as a nominative to what follows; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=8|verse=29}} the meaning perhaps is ''in the chambers, in the house of the Lord'', or the article is to be omitted; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=15|verse=27}} the text is manifestly corrupt.

{{GHGmargin-letter|127|h}}
Of another kind are the instances in which a determinate noun is followed by a definition of the material ''in apposition'' (hence, not in the genitive; cf. § 131), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=4|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=הָאֶ֫בֶן הַבְּדִיל|translate=the weight, the lead}}, i.e. ''the leaden weight''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=39|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=16|verse=14}} ({{GHGheb|text=הַנְּח֫שֶׁת}}, both here and in verse 17, is probably only a later addition, while {{GHGheb|text=המסגרות המכנות}} in verse 17 has arisen from a confusion of two readings, {{GHGheb|text=מסגרות המכנות}} and {{GHGheb|text=המסגרות מֵהמכנות}}). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=32|verse=12}} also {{GHGheb|text=הַמִּקְנָה}} (unless the article is simply to be omitted) is in apposition to {{GHGheb|text=הַסֵּפֶר}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|127|i}}
(''b'') Before a noun with a suffix (which likewise represents a determinate genitive; see above, at the beginning of this section). This does not apply to cases in which a {{GHGterm|verbal}} (i.e. ''accusative'') suffix is affixed to a participle which has the article, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַמַּכֵּ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=9|verse=12}}, ''the one smiting him''; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=8|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=13|verse=6|hidebook=1}} also {{GHGheb|text=ךָ}} is a verbal suffix, but hardly the {{GHGheb|text=וֹ}} in {{GHGheb|text=הָֽעֹשׂוֹ}} for {{GHGheb|text=הָֽעֹשֵׂ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Job|chapter=40|verse=19}}, nor the {{GHGheb|text=־ָהּ}} in {{GHGheb|text=הַיֹּֽלְדָהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=11|verse=6}}; {{GHGpar|116|g}}. For {{GHGheb|text=הָֽעֶרְכְּךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lev|chapter=27|verse=23}}, read {{GHGheb|text=עֶרְכְּךָ}} as in verses 2, 3, 5, 7, 13, &c., twelve times (but cf. also the note on {{GHGpar|128|d}}).—Of the remaining examples {{GHGheb|text=כַּגְּבִרְתָּהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=2}} (probably an intentional alliteration with the eleven other words beginning with {{GHGheb|text=כַּ‍}}), {{GHGheb|text=לַמַּֽעֲנֵ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=16|verse=4}}, and {{GHGheb|text=בֶּֽעָרֵ֫ינוּ}} (so Baer, following the best authorities) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=10|verse=14}}, rest only on the authority of the Masoretes, not of the authors. So also in {{GHGheb|text=הָאָֽהֳלִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=7|verse=21}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַֽחֶצְיוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=8|verse=33}} (previously {{GHGheb|text=חֶצְיוֹ}}), {{GHGheb|text=הֶהָֽרוֹתֶ֫יהָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=15|verse=16}} (dittography of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}}), the article is simply to be omitted as syntactically impossible; the {{GHGheb|text=ו}} of {{GHGheb|text=הַדָּבְרוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=2|verse=12}} is the copula belonging to the next word.<section end=par127 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

438.text:
{{GHGpar-heading|128|The Indication of the Genitive Relation by means of the Construct State}}
Cf. especially Philippi’s work cited at the head of {{GHGpar|89}}.
{{GHGmargin-letter|128|a}} '''1.''' The genitive relation is regularly expressed (see {{GHGpar|89}}) by the close connexion of the {{GHGterm|nomen regens}} (in the construct state) with the ''nomen rectum'' (in the genitive). Since only ''one'' nomen regens can be immediately connected with a nomen rectum, it follows that the same genitive cannot depend on two or more ''co-ordinate'' nouns, but a second (sometimes even a third, &c.) regens must be added with a suffix referring to the nomen rectum, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי דָוִד וּבְנֹתָיו|translate=the sons of David and his daughters}} (not {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי וּבְנוֹת דָּוִד}}); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=28}}.Very rare, and only possible in very rapid utterance, are such exceptions as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=31|verse=16}} ({{GHGheb|text=מִבְחַר וְטֽוֹב־לְבָנוֹן}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=16|verse=11}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=11|verse=2}} ''the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord'', {{GHGheb|text=דַּעַ֫ת}} may at any rate also be taken as an absolute genitive, so also {{GHGheb|text=סֵ֫פֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=1|verse=4}}. The language also prefers to avoid a series of several co-ordinateIn {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=114|verse=1}} a second genitive is added even without the copula, but the parallelism of the members renders any misunderstanding impossible. genitives depending upon one and the same nomen regens (such as occur in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=20|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=31|verse=54|hidebook=1}} [{{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=13|verse=1}}], {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=23|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=8|verse=3|hidebook=1}}),In almost all these instances the two (or three) genitives form one closely connected whole, as ''heaven'' and ''earth, sons'' and ''daughters''. and rather tends to repeat the nomen regens, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהֵי הַשָּׁמַ֫יִם וֵֽאלֹהֵי הָאָ֫רֶץ|translate=the God of heaven and the God of the earth}} (so in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=8|verse=1}} the regens is five times repeated). A lengthened series of genitives may, however, be formed by a nomen rectum serving at the same time as ''regens'' to a genitive depending on it (cf. {{GHGpar|127|a}} [d]); e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=יְמֵי שְׁנֵי חַיֵּי אֲבֹתַי|translate=the days of the years of the life of my fathers}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=12|verse=24}}, where there are three genitives, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=12}} four, and 21:17 five (unless the last three are in apposition). As a rule, indeed, such an inconvenient accumulation of genitives is avoided by means of a circumlocution in the case of one of them (see {{GHGpar|129|d}}). {{GHGmargin-letter|128|b}} Rem. As the fundamental rules stated above are the necessary consequence not merely of ''logical'' but more especially of ''rhythmical'' relations (see {{GHGpar|89|a}}), we must feel the more hesitation in admitting examples in which genitives are supposed to be loosely attached to forms other than the construct state. Some of these examples (the supposed genitives following a regens which is determined by the article) have been already discussed in {{GHGpar|127|f}}–h. Compare, moreover: {{GHGmargin-letter|128|c}} (''a'') Genitives after the absolute state, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=גֵּֽיא־שְׁמָנִים הֲלוּמֵי יַ֫יִן|translate=the fat valley of them that are overcome with wine}}. The usual explanation that {{GHGheb|text=גֵּֽיא־שְׁמָנִים}} forms ''one'' single idea (in German ''Fettigkeitstal''), on which the

439.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par128 />genitive {{GHGheb|text=הֲלוּמֵי יַ֫יִן}} then depends, in reality explains nothing; the text is almost certainly corrupt. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=15|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁנֵה}} would be expected; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=3|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=הַבְּרִית}} is a later addition; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=32|verse=13}} ({{GHGheb|text=מָשׂוֹשׂ}}), and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=22}} ({{GHGheb|text=שֵׂעָר}}), the absolute for the construct state probably rests only on the authority of the Masoretes. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=25}} ff. the text is obviously in confusion. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=32}} (cf. 6:24) {{GHGheb|text=כְּעָפְרָה}} should come either after {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּקָּבֵר}} or at the end of the verse, unless, with Moore, we omit {{GHGheb|text=אֲבִי הָֽע׳}} as a gloss (from 6:24); in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=63|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=משֶׁה}} is probably a gloss on {{GHGheb|text=יְמֵי־עוֹלָם}} which has crept into the text; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=4|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=לְאִישׁ־בּ֫שֶׁת}}, according to the LXX, has dropped out before {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=6|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=רָעוֹת}} is to be omitted with the LXX; if originally in the text, it could only be genitive (= ''all abominations of evils''), not an adjective; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=21|verse=6}} the text is altogether uncertain (the LXX read {{GHGheb|text=מֽוֹקְשֵׁי}} for {{GHGheb|text=מְבַקְשֵׁי}}); in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=9|verse=13}} the preposition {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} (after a {{GHGheb|text=ל}}) has dropped out before {{GHGheb|text=מְלֶאכֶת}} (cf. 12:25).—Elsewhere ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=3|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=4|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=8|verse=5}}) the supposed genitives are to be taken rather as words of nearer definition standing in apposition, i.e. ''with high walls, gates, and bars''. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=8|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=ירושלים}} is either in apposition to {{GHGheb|text=העם הזה}} or is better (since not in the LXX) omitted as a gloss.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|d}}
(''b'') Genitives after a noun with a suffix (where the suffix prevents the direct government by the {{GHGterm|nomen regens}}). Thus in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=27|verse=3}}, 5, 6, where {{GHGheb|text=הַזָּכָר}} after {{GHGheb|text=עֶרְכְּךָ}}<ref>Halévy, ''J. A.'' xiv. 548, removes the difficulty by pointing {{GHGheb|text=עַרְכֹּךְ}}.</ref> might be taken, contrary to the accents, as subject of the following clause; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=15}}, 25 the suffix may refer to Moses. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=6|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=מִדּוֹ בַד|translate=his garment}}, namely the garment ''of linen'', unless simply in apposition, cf. {{GHGpar|131|d}} (or read {{GHGheb|text=מִדֵּי}}?); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=42}}, where {{GHGheb|text=בְּרִיתִי יַֽעֲקֹב וגו׳}} could at most be explained as an ellipse for {{GHGheb|text=בְּרִיתִי בְרִית יַֽעֲקֹב}}, cf. {{GHGpar|125|h}} (probably, however, it is a case of dittography of the {{GHGheb|text=י}}, which was repeated also before {{GHGheb|text=אברהם}}; so Valeton, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZAW.|Zeitschrift für die alttestamentliche Wissenschaft, ed. by B. Stade, Giessen, 1881 ff., and since 1907 by K. Marti.}}}} xii. 3); equally strange is {{GHGheb|text=בְּרִיתִי הַיּוֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=33|verse=20}}, &c. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=אִם יִֽהְיֶה נְבִֽיאֲכֶם יְהֹוָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=12|verse=6}} could not possibly mean ''if your prophet be a prophet of the Lord''; the text is manifestly corrupt (probably {{GHGheb|text=נְבִֽיאֲךָ מִיַּהְוֶה}} is to be read, with Marti). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=45|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּסְאֲךָ אֱלֹהִים}} (usually explained as ''thy divine throne''), {{GHGheb|text=אלהים}} is most probably a later addition [another suggestion is to read {{GHGheb|text=כֵאלֹהִים|translate=like God}}(''’s throne''): cf. {{GHGpar|141|d}}, note]. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=52|verse=20}} two readings are probably combined, {{GHGheb|text=לִנְחֻשְׁתָּם}} without any addition, and {{GHGheb|text=לִנְח֫שֶׁת בָּל־הַכֵּלִיס}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=25|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלוֹם}} is in apposition to {{GHGheb|text=בְּרִיתִי}}. On {{GHGheb|text=דַּרְכֵּךְ זִמָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=27}}, cf. {{GHGpar|131|r}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|e}}
(''c'') The interposition of a word is assumed between {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־}} (''the whole''; cf. {{GHGpar|127|b}}) and the genitive governed by it in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=1|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=3}} ({{GHGheb|text=עוֹד}}), and, if the text is correct, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hos|chapter=14|verse=3}} ({{GHGheb|text=תִּשָּׂא}}). In reality, however, in all three places the genitive relation is destroyed by the transposition of the words (instead of {{GHGheb|text=עוֹד כָּל־}}, &c.), and {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־}} is rather to be taken adverbially (equivalent to ''wholly''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=1|verse=9}} ''because my life is yet wholly in me'', i.e. my whole life; cf. Philippi, ''Stat. Constr.'', p. 10.—On the instances in which the original construct state {{GHGheb|text=אֵין|translate=non-existence}} is used without a following genitive, see the negative sentences, {{GHGpar|152|o}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|f}}
'''2.''' The dependence of the nomen rectum on the nomen regens by no means represents merely what is, properly speaking, the genitive relation (see the examples under g–i). Very frequently the nomen<section end=par128 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

440.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="132.76.81.221" /></noinclude><section begin="par128"/>rectum only adds a nearer definition of the nomen regens, whether by giving the name, the genus or species, the measure, the material, or finally an attribute of it (''genit. epexegeticus'' or ''appositionis'',<ref>The latter term is preferred especially by König, {{GHGcite|title=Theol. Stud. und Krit.}}, 1898, p. 528 ff.</ref> see the examples under k–q).

Examples. The ''nomen rectum'' represents—

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|g}}
(''a'') A ''subjective genitive'', specifying the possessor, author, &c., e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בֵּית־הַמֶּ֫לֶךְ}} ''the king’s house''; {{GHGheb|text=דְּבַר יְהֹוָה|translate=the word of the Lord}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|h}}
(''b'') An ''objective genitive'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ob|chapter=1|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=מֵֽחֲמַס אָחִיךָ|translate=for the violence done to thy brother}}<ref>Cf. in Latin a similar use of the genitive after ''iniuria'' (Caes. ''B. G.'' 1, 30), ''metus (hostium, Pompeii'', &c.), ''spes'', and other words. In Greek, cf. εὔνοια τῶν φίλων, πίστις τοῦ θεοῦ, ὁ λόγος ὁ τοῦ σταυροῦ, 1 Cor. 1:18.</ref> (but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=12|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=מֵֽחֲמַס}} is followed by a subjective genitive); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=20|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=אֵימַת מֶ֫לֶךְ|translate=the terror of a king}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=זַֽעֲקַת סְדֹם|translate=the cry concerning Sodom}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁמַע צֹר|translate=the report of}} (''about'') ''Tyre'', cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=4|verse=4}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=8|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫בֶל יָחִיד|translate=the mourning for an only son}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=20|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלַל אֹֽיְבֶיךָ|translate=praeda hostibus tuis erepta}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=14}}. In a wider sense this includes such examples as {{GHGheb|text=דֶּ֫רֶךְ עֵץ הַֽחַיִּים|translate=the way of}} (i.e. ''to'') ''the tree of life'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=24}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=7|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=20}}; {{GHGheb|text=דֶּ֫רֶךְ הַיָּם|translate=the way of}} (''by'') ''the sea'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=23}}; {{GHGheb|text=זִבְחֵי אֱלֹהִים|translate=the sacrifices of}} (i.e. ''pleasing to'') ''God'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=51|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=שְׁבֻעַת יְהֹוָה|translate=the oath of}} (i.e. ''sworn before'') ''the Lord'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=48}}; {{GHGheb|text=דִּבְרֵי לְמוּאֵל|translate=the words of}} (i.e. ''addressed to'') L., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=31|verse=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|i}}
(''c'')A ''partitive genitive''; this includes especially the cases in which an adjective in the construct state is followed by a general term, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חַכְמוֹת שָֽׂרוֹתֶיהָ|translate=the wisest of her ladies}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=29}}; cf. for this way of expressing the superlative, {{GHGpar|133|h}}, and also r below.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|k}}
Merely formal genitives (''genit. explicativus'' or ''epexegeticus, genit. appositionis'') are those added to the construct state as nearer definitions—

(''d'') Of the ''name'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נְהַר פְּרָת|translate=the river Euphrates}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫רֶץ כְּנַ֫עַן|translate=the land of Canaan}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּתוּלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל|translate=the virgin Israel}} (not ''of Israel''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=2}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|l}}
(''e'') Of the ''genus'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=15|verse=20}} (21:20) {{GHGheb|text=כְּסִיל אָדָם|translate=a fool of a man}} (=''a foolish man''); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=13|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=5|verse=4}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|m}}
(''f'') Of the ''species'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֲחֻזַּת קֶ֫בֶר|translate=a possession of a burying-place}}, i.e. ''hereditary sepulchre'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=23|verse=4}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=תְּאֵנֵי הַבַּכֻּרוֹת|translate=the early figs}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=24|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֹ֫הֶל בֵּיתִי|translate=the tabernacle of my house}}, i.e. my dwelling-place, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=132|verse=3}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|n}}
(''g'') Of the ''measure, weight, extent, number'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מְתֵי מִסְפָּר|translate=people of number}}, i.e. ''few in number'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=26|verse=5}}; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=47|verse=3}}–5 ''waters of the ankles, waters of the loins, waters of swimming'', i.e. which reached up to the ankles, or loins, or necessitated swimming; but in verse 4 in apposition (?) {{GHGheb|text=מַ֫יִם בִּרְכַּ֫יִם}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|o}}
(''h'') Of the ''material''<ref>In the almost entire absence of corresponding adjectives ({{GHGheb|text=אָרוּז|translate=made of cedar}}, a denominative from {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫רֶז}}, and {{GHGheb|text=נָחוּשׁ|translate=brazen}} are the only examples), the language regularly has recourse to the above periphrasis. On the form ''qāṭûl'', as expressing an inherent property, cf. {{GHGpar|50|f}}; cf. also the proper name, {{GHGheb|text=בַּרְזִלַּי|translate=ferreus}}.</ref> of which something consists, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כְּלִי חָ֑רֶשׂ|translate=a vessel of earthenware}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=כְּלֵי כֶ֫סֶף|translate=vessels of silver}} (cf. the French ''des vases d’or''); {{GHGheb|text=אֲרוֹן עֵץ|translate=an ark of wood}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁ֫בֶט בַּרְזֶל|translate=a rod of iron}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=9}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=7|verse=13}}, &c.
<section end="par128"/><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

441.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par128 />{{GHGmargin-letter|128|p}}
(''i'') Of the ''attribute'' of a person or thing, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=אֲחֻזַּת עוֹלָם|translate=an everlasting possession}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=17|verse=8}} ''a precious stone''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=28|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=13|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=23|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=31|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=5|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=14|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=41|verse=19}}, and the examples of the genitive with a suffix given in {{GHGpar|135|n}}. Such a periphrasis for the expression of attributes frequently occurs, even when the corresponding adjectives are in use. Thus especially {{GHGheb|text=קֹ֫דֶשׁ|translate=holiness}} very frequently serves as a periphrasis for the adjective {{GHGheb|text=קָדוֹשׁ}} (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בִּגְדֵי הַקֹּ֫דֶשׁ|translate=the holy garments}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=29|verse=29}}), since {{GHGheb|text=קָדוֹשׁ}} is used almost exclusively in reference to persons (hence also with {{GHGheb|text=עַם}} and {{GHGheb|text=גּוֹי|translate=people}}, and with {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁם}} the ''name'' of a person); the only exceptions are {{GHGheb|text=מָקוֹם קָדוֹשׁ|translate=holy place}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=29|verse=31}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=מַ֫יִם קְדשִׁים|translate=holy water}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=קָדוֹשׁ}} as the predicate of {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם|translate=day}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=8|verse=10}} f., and of {{GHGheb|text=מַֽחֲנֶה|translate=camp}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=23|verse=15}}. So also the use of {{GHGheb|text=צַדִּיק|translate=righteous}} is always confined to persons, except in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=8}}; elsewhere the periphrasis with {{GHGheb|text=צֶ֫דֶק}} or {{GHGheb|text=צְדָקָה}} is always used, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מֹֽאזְנֵי צֶ֫דֶק|translate=just balances}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=19|verse=36}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|q}}
In a wider sense this use of the genitive also includes statements of the purpose for which something is intended, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=צֹאן טִבְחָה|translate=sheep for the slaughter}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=44|verse=23}}; {{GHGheb|text=מוּסַר שְׁלוֹמֵ֫נוּ|translate=the chastisement designed for our peace}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=53|verse=5}}; cf. 51:17 (''the cup which causes staggering''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=116|verse=13}}; finally, also, the description of the material, with which something is laden or filled, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=חֲמֹר לֶ֫חֶם וְנֹאד יַ֫יִן|translate=an ass}} laden ''with bread and a bottle of wine'' (but probably {{GHGheb|text=עֲשָׂרָה}} is to be read for {{GHGheb|text=חֲמֹר}}); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=7|verse=20}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|r}}
Rem. 1. Certain substantives are used to convey an attributive idea in the construct state before a partitive genitive; thus {{GHGheb|text=מִבְחָר|translate=choice, selection}}, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=23|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=מִבְחַר קְבָרֵ֫ינוּ|translate=the choice of our sepulchres}}, i.e. our choicest sepulchres; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=24|hidebook=1}}; other examples are, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=16}} ''the evil of your doings'', emphatically, for ''your evil doings''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=24|hidebook=1}} (=''the tall cedars thereof''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=26}}.—This is the more common construction with the substantive {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל|translate=entirety}}, for ''all, the whole, every'', see {{GHGpar|127|b}}; it is also frequent with {{GHGheb|text=מְעַט|translate=a little}}, for ''few'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=28}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|s}}
2. To the periphrases expressing attributive ideas (see p above) by means of a genitive construction may be added the very numerous combinations of the construct states {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ|translate=a man}}, {{GHGheb|text=בַּעַל|translate=master, possessor}}, {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־|translate=son}}, and their feminines and plurals (including {{GHGheb|text=מְתֵי|translate=men}}, used only in the plural), with some appellative noun, in order to represent a person (poetically even a thing) as possessing some object or quality, or being in some condition. In English, such combinations are sometimes rendered by single substantives, sometimes by circumlocution.

Examples:—

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|t}}
(''a'') Of {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ דְּבָרִים|translate=an eloquent man}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=4|verse=10}} (but {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ שְׂפָתַ֫יִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=11|verse=2}} ''a man of lips'', i.e. ''a boaster''); {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ לָשׁוֹן}} = ''a slanderer'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=140|verse=12}}; {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ דַּ֫עַת|translate=a man of knowledge}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ חֵמָה|translate=a wrathful man}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=15|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ דָּמִים|translate=a man of blood}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=16|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=7}}; cf. further, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=53|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=19|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=26|verse=21|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=29|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=8|verse=18}}; also {{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫שֶׁת מִדְיָנִים|translate=a contentious woman}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=27|verse=15}}; in the plural, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=אַנְשֵׁי הַשֵּׁם|translate=the men of renown, famous}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=8}}, 10 ({{GHGheb|text=אַנְשֵׁי לֵבָב|translate=men of understanding}}); with {{GHGheb|text=מְתֵי}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=13}} ({{GHGheb|text=מְתֵי רָעָב|translate=famished men}}; but read probably {{GHGheb|text=מְזֵי רָעָב|translate=weak with hunger}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=26|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=11|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=15|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|u}}
(''b'') Of {{GHGheb|text=בַּ֫עַל}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=בַּ֫עַל שֵׂעָר|translate=hairy}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=1|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=בַּ֫עַל הַֽחֲלֹמוֹת|translate=the dreamer}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=19}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=1|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=18|verse=9|hidebook=1}} (''a destroyer''), 22:24, 23:2 (''disposed to eat, greedy''), 24:8; feminine<section end=par128 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

442.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par128" />{{GHGheb|text=בַּֽעֲלַת־אוֹב|translate=a woman that hath a soothsaying spirit}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=7}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=4}}; in the plural, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽעֲלֵי חִצִּים|translate=archers}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=23}}, {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽעֲלֵי בְרִית|translate=confederates}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=13}}; {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽעֲלֵי שְׁבוּעָה|translate=sworn supporters}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=6|verse=18}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|v}}
(''c'') Of {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־}}, &c.: {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־חַ֫יִל|translate=a hero, warrior}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=15|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־מֶ֫שֶׁק|translate=heir}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־שָׁנָה|translate=yearling}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=5}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־מְאַת שָׂנָה|translate=centum annos natus}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־מָ֫וֶת|translate=worthy to die}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=31}} (Luther, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=5}} ''ein Kind des Todes''); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=25|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּן־הַכּוֹת|translate=worthy to be beaten}}. Feminine, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בַּת־בְּלִיַּ֫עַל|translate=a wicked woman}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=16}}; frequently also {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ בְּלִיַּ֫עַל}}, {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי ב׳}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַנְשֵׁי ב׳}} and even simply {{GHGheb|text=בְּלִיַּ֫עַל}}, like the Latin ''scelus'' for ''scelestissimus'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=23|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=18}}. Plural masculine, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי מֶ֑רִי|translate=children of rebellion}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=25}}. {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־}} is used poetically of things without life, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־שָׁ֫מֶן|translate=a fat}}, i.e. a fruitful (hill); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jon|chapter=4|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּן־לַ֫יְלָה}} i.e. ''grown in a night''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=41|verse=20}} ''son of the bow'' (i.e. an arrow); so also {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי רֶשֶׁף}} = ''sparks'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=7}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=3|verse=13}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּנוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=4}} ''the daughters of song'', probably meaning the individual notes.

There is another use of {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־}} or {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי}} to denote membership of a guild or society (or of a tribe, or any definite class). Thus {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי אֱלֹהִים}} or {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי הָֽאֱלֹהִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=2}}, 4, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=2|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=7|hidebook=1}} (cf. also {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי אֵלִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=29|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=89|verse=7|hidebook=1}}) properly means not ''sons of god''(''s''), but beings of the class of {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} or {{GHGheb|text=אֵלִים}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵיֽ־הַנְּבִיאִיס}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=35}} (singular in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=7|verse=14}}) persons ''belonging to the guild of prophets''; {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־הָֽרַקָּתִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=3|verse=8}} ''one of the guild of apothecaries'', cf. 3:31 where {{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־הַצֹּֽרְפִים}} is to be read. Similarly {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי שִׁלֵּשִׁים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=50|verse=23}} are most probably not ''great-grandsons'' but ''grandsons'', i.e. those belonging to the third generation. Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי הַגֵּֽרְשֻׁנִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=4|verse=27}} f. ''Gershonites'', {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי הַקְּהָתִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=20|verse=19}}, &c., ''Kohathites''; {{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵי קֶ֫דֶם|translate=dwellers in the East}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|w}}
3. Special mention must be made of the not infrequent idiom by which adjectives (sometimes also ordinals, see {{GHGpar|134|o}}) are added in the genitive, like substantives, rather than as attributes in the same state, gender, and number as the noun which they qualify; thus, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=צִיצַת נֹבֵל|translate=the flower of that which fades}}, for which verse 1 has {{GHGheb|text=צִיץ נֹבֵל|translate=the fading flower}}; cf. further, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=17}} (?), 52:13, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=74|verse=15|hidebook=1}} (but {{GHGheb|text=אֵיתָן}} may be a substantive), 78:49; also the use of {{GHGheb|text=רַע}} as a substantive, e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=2|verse=14}} b, 6:24 ({{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫שֶׁת רַע}}), &c., analogous to the New Testament phrase ὁ οἰκονόμος τῆς ἀδικίας, Luke 16:8, and the French ''un homme de bien''.<ref>On the other hand, in such passages as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=36|verse=2}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=18|verse=17}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=14|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=8|verse=10}}, &c., there is no apparent reason why the Masora requires the construct state instead of the absolute; hence {{GHGheb|text=חֵיל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=36|verse=2}} and {{GHGheb|text=גֵּיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=14|verse=4}} must be intended as forms of the absolute state, shortened in consequence of their close connexion.</ref>—Finally, an adverb (treated as a substantive) may likewise be used as an epexegetical genitive; cf. {{GHGheb|text=דְּמֵי חִנָּם|translate=blood shed without cause}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=31}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=26|verse=2|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=30|verse=16}} ({{GHGheb|text=יוֹמָם}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|x}}
'''3.''' The epexegetical genitives include finally the numerous nearer definitions which follow the coustruct state of adjectives (and of active and passive participles, or verbal adjectives, cf. {{GHGpar|116|f}}–l). For, while the word of nearer definition is added to the verb in the accusative (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חָלָה אֶת־רַגְלָיו|translate=he was diseased in his feet}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=15|verse=23}}), it may, with participles and verbal adjectives, be either in the accusative<section end="par128" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

443.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="DjR" /></noinclude><section begin=par128 /><section begin=par128 />({{GHGpar|116|f}} and k) or in the genitive, the case of a word depending on a noun. Such a genitive relation is usually termed an ''improper annexion''. The nearer definition contains a statement either of the ''material'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=8}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫רֶץ זָבַת תָלָב וּדְבַשׁ|translate=a land flowing with milk and honey}}; or of the ''means'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חַלְלֵי־חֶ֫רֶב|translate=slain with the sword}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=2}}; or the ''cause'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=2|verse=5}} ''sick of love''; or of the ''scope'' of the attribute,<ref>Cf. the Latin ''integer vitae scelerisque purus; tristes animi'', &c.</ref> e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=יְפֵה־תֹ֫אַר|translate=fair of form}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=2}}, 4, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=34|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=32|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=1|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=37|verse=16}}; or of the ''manner'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=59|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=בֹּֽגְדֵי אָ֫וֶן|translate=faithless ones of wickedness}} (wickedly faithless).

{{GHGmargin-letter|128|y}}
Especially frequent is the use of this genitive to name the part of the body described as being affected by some physical or mental condition, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=24|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=נְקִי בַפַּ֫יִם|translate=clean as regards hands}}, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=9|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=17|verse=9}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=אַגְמֵי־נָ֫פֶשׁ|translate=grieved in soul}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=20}}. Also such examples as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=2|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=19|verse=1}}, where a suffix is attached to the substantive, must be regarded as instances of the genitive construction, on the analogy of {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=14|verse=2}}, see {{GHGpar|116|k}}.<section end=par128 />

<section begin=par129 />{{GHGpar-heading|129|Expression of the Genitive by Circumlocution}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|129|a}}
Besides the construction of a nomen rectum dependent upon a nomen regens in the construct state (§§ 89 and 128), the connexion of two nouns may also be effected otherwise, either by simply attaching the dependent noun by means of the preposition {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, which, according to {{GHGpar|119|r}}, expresses, besides other ideas, like that of ''belonging to'',<ref>Cf. the σχῆμα Κολοφώνιον in Greek, e.g. ἡ κεφαλὴ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ for τοῦ ἀνθρώπου (Bernhardy’s ''Syntax'', p. 88). The Arab grammarians distinguish a twofold genitive, one of which may be resolved by {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, and the other by {{GHGheb|text=מִן}} [see Wright’s ''Arabic Grammar'', vol. ii, {{GHGpar|75|ff}}.]. The ''de'' of the Romance languages is a development of the latter idea; the Gascon, however, says e.g. ''la fille à Mr. N.'', laying stress upon the idea of ''belonging to'' and not that of ''origin'', as in ''la fille de''... of the literary language.</ref> or by the addition of a relative clause ({{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר לְ}}, see h below).

{{GHGmargin-letter|129|b}}
1. The introduction of a genitive by {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} sometimes occurs even when the construction with the construct state would be equally possible, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=הַצֹּפִים לְשָׁאוּל|translate=the watchmen of Saul}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=37|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=28|verse=18}} (where indeed the circumlocution makes the sense much plainer); as a rule, however, this use is restricted to the following cases:—

{{GHGmargin-letter|129|c}}
(''a'') To prevent a nomen regens being determined by a following determinate genitive, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=בֵּן לְיִשַׁי|translate=a son of Jesse}} ({{GHGheb|text=בֶּן־יִשַׁי}} would be, according to {{GHGpar|127|a}}, ''the son of Jesse''); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=36|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=16|verse=22}} (27:16), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=122|verse=5}}. Hence, regularly {{GHGheb|text=מִזְמור לְדָוִד}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=3|verse=1}}, &c.) ''a psalm of David'' (properly belonging to David as the author), for which {{GHGheb|text=לְדָוִד|translate=of David}} is used alone elliptically in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=11|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=14|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, &c. Such a case as {{GHGheb|text=לְדָוִד מִזְמוֹר}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=24|verse=1}}, &c.) is not to<section end=par129 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

444.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par129 />be regarded as a transposition, but {{GHGheb|text=מִזְמוֹר}} is used epexegetically for the general term omitted before {{GHGheb|text=לְדָוִד}} (as it were, a poem ''of David, a psalm''). Moreover, the introduction of the author, poet, &c., by this ''Lamed auctoris'' is the customary idiom also in the other Semitic dialects, especially in Arabic.

{{GHGmargin-letter|129|d}}
(''b'') When a genitive is to be made dependent on a nomen regens, which is itself composed of a nomen regens and rectum, and represents, as a compound, one united idea, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=חֶלְקַת הַשָּׁדֶה לְבֹעַז|translate=the portion of field belonging to Boaz}} ({{GHGheb|text=חֶ׳ שְׂדֵה בֹעַז}} would be ''the portion of the field of Boaz''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=9}} ''at the house-door of Elisha''. This especially applies to the cases in which the compound regens represents a term in very common use, the fixed form of which cannot be altered, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=עַל־סֵ֫פֶר דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים לְמַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל|translate=in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel}}; 15:23, &c.; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=19|verse=51}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|129|e}}
(''c'') When for any other reason the construction with the nomen regens in the construct state is inadmissible; cf. e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=18|verse=20}}, where {{GHGheb|text=שְׁכָבְתְּךָ}}, on account of the suffix, cannot be used in the construct state; but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=15|verse=16}} ff., &c., {{GHGheb|text=שִׁכְבַת־זֶ֫רַע}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=3|verse=28}} ''the Jordan fords of Moab'' ({{GHGheb|text=יַרְדֵּן}} as a ''proper name'' cannot be used in the construct state); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=5}} ''upon the third and upon the fourth generation of them that hats me''; {{GHGheb|text=וְעַל־רִבֵּעִים}} must be kept in the absolute state for the sake of conformity with {{GHGheb|text=עַל־שִּׁלֵּשִׁים}}, and for the same reason also {{GHGheb|text=לַֽאֲלָפִּים לְאֹֽהֲבַי}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|129|f}}
(''d'') After statements of number in such cases as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּשִׁבְעָה וְעֶשְׂרִים יוֹם לַחֹ֫דֶשׁ|translate=on the seven and twentieth day of the month}}; cf. 7:11, 16:3 and frequently, or as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=1|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּשְׁנַת שְׁתַּ֫יִם לְדָֽרְיָ֫וֶשׁ|translate=in the second year of Darius}}; the numeral here is always one compound idea with the substantive numbered, and consequently (as in the examples under ''b'') does not admit of being in the constr. st. with a genitive. The same naturally applies also to such examples as {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=3|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=בַּיּוֹם חַשְּׁלִישִׁי לְלִדְתִּי|translate=on the third day of my giving birth}} (i.e. after my giving birth). Cf. also the standing phrase {{GHGheb|text=בְּאֶחָד לַחֹ֫דֶשׁ|translate=on the first}} (day) ''of the month'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=5}} and frequently.

{{GHGmargin-letter|129|g}}
Rem. In cases like {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=2}} ''and his firstborn was Amnon'' {{GHGheb|text=לַֽאֲחִינֹ֫עַם|translate=of Ahinoam}}, the genitive expressed by circumlocution with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} is in reality dependent on a regens which is omitted ({{GHGheb|text=בֵּן לַֽאֲחִינֹ֫עַם|translate=a son of Ahinoam}}); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=3}}, 5, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=3}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=לְבֵית יִשְׂרָאֵל}} originally depended on ''thus spake the Lord''), and the remarks on {{GHGheb|text=לְדָוִד מִזְמוֹר}} under ''c'' above.

{{GHGmargin-letter|129|h}}
2. The periphrastic expression of the genitive by means of {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר לְ}} is used principally to state the ''possessor'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=הַצֹאן אֲשֶׁר לְאָבִ֫יהָ}} ''her father’s sheep'' (prop. ''the sheep which'' belonged ''to her father''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=4}} and frequently. So also (according to {{GHGpar|128|a}}) when a genitive depends on more than one substantive, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=5}} ''the butler and the baker who'' (belonged) ''to the king of Egypt'' ({{GHGheb|text=וְֹאפֵה מֶ֫לֶךְ מִצְרַ֫יִם}} would indicate only the baker as belonging to the king); or when a genitive (as in the examples under ''d'' above) is added to a compound, which expresses one united idea ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=4|verse=3}}); or when, as a fixed term (e.g. a title), it appears always in the same form, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים אֲשֶׁר לִשְׁלֹמֹה|translate=the Song of songs, of Solomon}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=11|verse=10}}; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=43}}.<ref>In New Hebrew {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁל}} (derived from {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁלְּ}} = {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר לְ}}, see § 36, and cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=3|verse=7|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁלִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁלִּשְׁלֹמֹה}}) is used like the simple relative {{GHGheb|text=דִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=דְּ}} in Aramaic, as an independent sign of the genitive.</ref><section end=par129 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

445.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par130 />{{GHGpar-heading|130|Wider Use of the Construct State}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|130|a}}
The construct state, which, according to {{GHGpar|89|a}}, primarily represents only the immediate government by one substantive of the following word (or combination of words), is frequently employed in rapid narrative as a connecting form, even apart from the genitive relation; so especially—

(1) Before prepositions,<ref>Cf. König, ‘Die Ueberwucherung des St.-constr.-Gebrauchs im Semit.,’ {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 53, 521 ff.</ref> particularly in elevated (prophetic or poetic) style, especially when the nomen regens is a participle. Thus before {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׂמְחַת בַּקָּצִיר|translate=the joy in the harvest}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=9|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=1|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=136|verse=8}}f.; in participles, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=9|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=8|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=84|verse=7}}, and especially often when {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} with a suffix follows the participle, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־חוֹסֵי בוֹ}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=1|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=8|verse=16}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=24|verse=1}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=64|verse=9}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=רֹאֶה}} should be read); 98:7.<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=11}} the article is even used before a construct state followed by {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}}, in order to determine the whole combination {{GHGheb|text=שְׁכוּנֵי בָֽאֳהָלִים|translate=tent-dwellers}}, taken as one word; cf., however, the remarks in {{GHGpar|127|f}}–i on similar grammatical solecisms.</ref>—Before {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=9|verse=6}} (but read probably {{GHGheb|text=מַתֲמַדֵּי כַסְפָּם}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=58|verse=5}} (before {{GHGheb|text=לָמוֹ}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=18|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=2|verse=18}} (before {{GHGheb|text=לָךְ}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=6|verse=55}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=23|verse=28|hidebook=1}}; in participles, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=38|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=5}}; before {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} with an infinitive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=56|verse=10}}, and again before {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} with a suffix, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=64|verse=3|hidebook=1}};<ref>These are to be distinguished from the cases where {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} follows a construct state, which in conjunction with {{GHGheb|text=מִן}} (and the following {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}) has become a sort of preposition or adverb of place; thus, we have {{GHGheb|text=מִבֵּית־לְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=33}} (for which in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=1|verse=27}} merely {{GHGheb|text=בֵּית לְ}}) meaning simply ''within''; {{GHGheb|text=מִימִין לְ}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=23|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=10|verse=3}}) ''on the right hand'' (i.e. south) ''of''; {{GHGheb|text=מִצְּפוֹן לְ}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=8|verse=11}}, 13, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=2|verse=9}}) ''on the north of''; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=15|verse=21}} and {{GHGheb|text=לִפְנֵי מִן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=13|verse=4}}.</ref>—before {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=17}}; —before {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־}} (''with''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=6}}; —before {{GHGheb|text=מִן}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=9}} (a participle); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=7|verse=5}}; —before {{GHGheb|text=עַל־}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=10}}; —before {{GHGheb|text=בִּלְתִּי}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=6}}; —before the ''nota accus''. {{GHGheb|text=את}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=33|verse=22}}; —before a locative (which in such cases also serves as a genitive), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=27|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=1|verse=15}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|130|b}}
(2) Before ''wāw; copulative'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=10}}; but {{GHGheb|text=חָכְמַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=6}}, {{GHGheb|text=גִּילַת}} 35:2, and {{GHGheb|text=שְׁכֻרַת}} 51:21 may be cases of an intentional reversion to the old feminine ending ''ath'', in order to avoid the hiatus ({{GHGheb|text=וָ}}){{GHGheb|text=־ָה וְ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|130|c}}
(3) When it governs the (originally demonstrative) pronoun {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}}; so especially in the combination {{GHGheb|text=מְקוֹם אֲשֶׁר}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, ''the place where'' (prop. ''of that in which'') ''Joseph was bound''; cf. {{GHGpar|138|g}}; or {{GHGheb|text=בִּמְקוֹם אֲשֶׁר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=4|verse=24}}, 33, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=35}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=2|verse=1}}. We should expect {{GHGheb|text=הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר}}, {{GHGheb|text=בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר}}, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=35|verse=13}}, &c., ''at the place which...'', cf. § 138; but {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} is treated as a nomen rectum instead of as an attribute.<section end=par130 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

446.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Hftf" /></noinclude><section begin="par130" />Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=מִיּוֹם א׳}} followed by a {{GHGterm|perfect}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=29|verse=8}}, and {{GHGheb|text=יְמֵי א׳}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=13|verse=46}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=9|verse=18}}.<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=23|verse=5}} the construct state governs a sentence introduced by the ''conjunction'' {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} ({{GHGheb|text=עַל־דְּבַר אֲשֶׁר|translate=by reason of the fact that}}, i.e. ''because''); so also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=13}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|130|d}}
(4) When it governs independent sentences (cf. § 155), which virtually stand to the construct state (as nomen regens) in a sort of genitive relation, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=4|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּיַד־תְּשְׁלָח}}<ref>{{GHGcritic|Should be תִּשְׁלָח?}}</ref> prop. ''by the hand of'' him whom ''thou wilt send''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=דְּבַר מַה־יַּרְאֵ֫נִי|translate=the matter of}} that ''which he shall show me'', i.e. whatever he shall; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=קִרְיַת חָנָה דָוִד|translate=the city where David encamped}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=36}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=16|verse=3}} (if the text be right), 65:5 ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=32}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=81|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=18|verse=21}} ''the place of him that knoweth not God''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=14}} (if the text be right) ''into the hands'' of those against whom ''I cannot stand''.<ref>Probably {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=22|verse=14}} is also to be so explained (contrary to the accents), and certainly (contrary to the very unnatural division of the verses) {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=30|verse=18}}, which should read on thus: {{GHGheb|text=יְהֹוָה הַמּוֹב יְכַפֵּר בְּעַד כָּל־לְבָבוֹ הֵכִין|translate=the good Lord pardon every one that setteth his heart to seek God}}.
