[See Wickes’ ''Accontuation of the Twenty-one Prose Books of the Old Testament'', p. 140.]</ref> In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=4}} ({{GHGheb|text=כָּל־יֶשׁ־לוֹ}}) the {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־}} takes after it a noun-clause, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=4}}, still more boldly, a subst. with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}.—Very often a ''time-determination'' governs the following sentence in this way; thus {{GHGheb|text=אַֽחֲרֵי}} followed by a perfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=25|verse=48}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=5|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּיוֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=102|verse=3}} (before a noun-clause), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=6|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=3|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=22|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=59|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=138|verse=3|hidebook=1}} (in every case before a following perfect), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=56|verse=10}} (before an imperfect); {{GHGheb|text=מִיּוֹם}} followed by the perfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=36|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־יְמֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=14|verse=46}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=2}} ({{GHGheb|text=כִּימֵי|translate=as in the days when}}...<ref>Cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=2|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=מִימֵי הִיא}}, usually explained to mean ''from the days'' that ''she'' hath been, but the text is evidently very corrupt.</ref>; cf. {{GHGheb|text=כִּימוֹת}} and {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנוֹת}} before a perfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=90|verse=15}}); {{GHGheb|text=בְּעֵת}} before a perfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=15}} (cf. 49:8, 50:31); before an imperfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=תְּחִלַּת}} before a perfect {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=1|verse=2}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|130|e}}
(5) Connected with a following word in apposition; certainly so in such cases as {{GHGheb|text=בְּתוּלַת בַּת־צִיּוֹן|translate=the virgin, the daughter of Zion}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=22}}; cf. 23:12, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=14|verse=17}}; also {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫שֶׁת בַּֽעֲלַת־אוֹב|translate=a woman, possessor of a soothsaying spirit}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=21|verse=11}}.—{{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=22}} (but read probably {{GHGheb|text=אֲנָשִׁים}} with Moore, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=13|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=10}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=10|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=17|verse=13|hidebook=1}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=46|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=16}} (?), 78:9, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=20|verse=17}} ''b'' (unless {{GHGheb|text=נַֽהֲרֵי}} or {{GHGheb|text=נַֽהֲלֵי}} be a gloss).

{{GHGmargin-letter|130|f}}
Rem. Some of the above passages may also be explained by supposing that there exists a real genitive relation towards the preceding construct state, which has been, as it were, provisionally left ''in suspenso'', in consequence of the insertion of some interrupting word, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=22}}, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=20|verse=17}} ''a''. Elsewhere ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=34}}) the {{GHGterm|nomen regens}} probably governs the following construct state directly.<ref>So also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=16}} ''a corner stone of the preciousness'' ({{GHGheb|text=יִקְרַת}} is a ''substantive'' not an ''adjective'') ''of a fixed foundation'', i.e. a precious corner stone of surest foundation.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=19}} the text is wholly corrupt; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=128}} read {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־פִּקּוּדֶ֫יךָ}}.</ref>
<section end="par130" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

447.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par130 />{{GHGmargin-letter|130|g}}
(6) The numeral {{GHGheb|text=אַחַד|translate=one}} for {{GHGheb|text=אֶחָד}} in close connexion, and even with small disjunctives, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=48|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=11|verse=7}}.

The character of these passages shows that the numeral here cannot be in the construct state, but is merely a rhythmical shortening of the usual (tone-lengthened) form.<section end=par130 />

<section begin=par131 />{{GHGpar-heading|131|Apposition}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|a}}
'''1.''' Apposition in the stricter sense is the collocation of two substantives in the same case in order to define more exactly (or to complete) the one by the other, and, as a rule (see, however, below, under g), the former by the latter. Apposition in Hebrew (as in the other Semitic languages<ref>On certain uses of apposition peculiar to the Semitic languages, cf. the exhaustive discussion by Fleischer, ‘Ueber einige Arten der Nominalapposition im Arab.’ (''Kleine Schriften'', ii. 16); [and see also Driver, {{GHGcite|title=Tenses}}, Appendix IV.]</ref>) is by no means confined to those cases in which it is used in English or in the classical languages. It is not infrequently found when either the ''subordination'' of one substantive to the other or some more circumstantial kind of epexegetical addition would be expected.

'''2.''' The principal kinds of apposition in Hebrew are:—

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|b}}
(''a'') The collocation of ''genus'' and ''species'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אִשָּׁה אַלְמָנָה|translate=a woman}} (who was) ''a widow'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=7|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=נַֽעֲרָה בְתוּלָה|translate=a damsel}} (that is) ''a virgin'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=22|verse=23}}, 28, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=21|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=30|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=1|verse=2}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=13|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=20|hidebook=1}} (where, however, {{GHGheb|text=קַשָּׁת}} is probably an explanatory gloss); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=24|verse=5}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=11|verse=15}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=3|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=5|verse=29|hidebook=1}} (but probably {{GHGheb|text=סֵ֫בֶל}} should be read instead of {{GHGheb|text=סַבָּל}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=24}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=מַֽעֲשֵׂה}} is to be read), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=20|verse=1}}. Perhaps also {{GHGheb|text=כֹּחֵן הָרֹאשׁ|translate=the priest}} (who is) ''the chief man'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=25|verse=18}}, &c.; others take {{GHGheb|text=כֹּהֵן}} as constr, st.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=10|verse=7}} read {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־צְבָא הַגִּבּ׳}} with the LXX, as in the parallel passage {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=19|verse=9}} for {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־צָבָא הַגּ׳}}, which is evidently meant to refer to the reading in 2 S.

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|c}}
(''b'') Collocation of the ''person'' or ''thing'' and the ''attribute'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=20|verse=29}} (27:13) {{GHGheb|text=זֶה חֵ֫לֶק־אָדָם רָשָׁע|translate=this is the portion of a man}}, (who is) ''a wicked man'' (but {{GHGheb|text=רָשָׁע}} might also be an adject.); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=6|verse=12}}.—{{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=6|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=16|verse=4|hidebook=1}} (where, however, {{GHGheb|text=קֹ֫דֶשׁ}} is probably a gloss); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=22|verse=21}} {{GHGheb|text=אֲמָרִים אֱמֶת|translate=words}} (which are) ''truth''; (immediately after {{GHGheb|text=אִמְרֵי אֱמֶת}}) cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=1|verse=11}} (where, however, {{GHGheb|text=בּ֫שֶׁת}} is most probably a gloss on {{GHGheb|text=עֶרְיָה}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=1|verse=13}} (=''comfortable words''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=45|verse=5}} (?) 68:17 (cf. verse 16). In a wider sense this includes also such cases as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=60|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=יַ֫יִן תַּרְעֵלָה|translate=wine}} which is ''staggering'' (intoxicating drink), which causes staggering<ref>Unless it is to be translated ''thou gavest us intoxication to drink as wine'' (and so in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=27}} ''give him affliction to eat as bread'', &c.); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=80|verse=6}} and the analogous examples of apposition in the form of a second accusative in {{GHGpar|117|kk}}. Moreover, having regard to {{GHGheb|text=יַ֫יִן הָרֶ֫קַח|translate=spiced wine}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=8|verse=2}}, and {{GHGheb|text=עַ֫יִד פֶּ֫רֶא}} ''a wild ass’s colt'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=11|verse=12}} (in which passages {{GHGheb|text=יַ֫יִן}} and {{GHGheb|text=עַ֫יִר}} must certainly be in the construct state) we cannot but ask whether the Masora does not intend the {{GHGheb|text=יַ֫יִן}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=60|verse=5}} to be taken as construct state (for which elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=יֵין}}).</ref>; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=18|verse=26}} {{GHGheb|text=מַ֫יִם לַ֫חַץ}} (in<section end=par131 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

448.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par131" />{{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=20}} parallel with {{GHGheb|text=לֶ֫חֶם צַר}}) ''water'' which is ''affliction'', drunk in trouble (imprisonment). Still more boldly, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=5|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=בָּקָר רְעִי|translate=oxen}} which were taken out of the ''pastures'', and {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=6|verse=7}} ''undressed stones'' which come from the ''quarry'', probably a corruption of {{GHGheb|text=מִמַּסָּע}}. A person and a condition are in apposition in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=18|verse=6}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=בְּנִדָּתָהּ}} is to be read).—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=1}} read {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫בֶן הָע׳}}, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=5|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=7|verse=12|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|d}}
(''c'') Collocation of the ''person'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=36}}) or ''thing'' (form) and ''material'',<ref>Cf. also the examples treated above in {{GHGpar|127|h}}.</ref> or of the ''place'' or ''measure'' and its ''contents'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=15|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=נְה֫שֶׁת בִּמְצִלְתַּ֫יִם|translate=with cymbals}} which were ''brass'', i.e. of brass; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=11|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=28|verse=15}}, 18 (''?''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=28|verse=17}} ''four rows'', namely ''stones'' (for which 39:10 has {{GHGheb|text=טוּרֵי אָ֑בֶן}}); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=4|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=6|verse=3}} (see, however, {{GHGpar|128|d}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=7|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=סְאָה סֹ֫לֶת|translate=a seah of fine flour}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=7|verse=6.18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=16|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=23}} {{GHGheb|text=כִּכְּרַ֫יִם כֶּ֫סֶף|translate=two talents}} of ''silver'';<ref>On the anomalous form {{GHGheb|text=כִּכְּרַ֫יִם}} (instead of {{GHGheb|text=כִּכָּרַ֫יִם}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=כִּכָּרָ֑יִם}} immediately before), see {{GHGpar|88|b}}.</ref> cf. 5:17, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=39|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=22|verse=18}} (if the text be right). With the ''material'' placed before the ''measure'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=30|verse=23}} f..—A ''period of time'' and its contents are placed in apposition {{GHGheb|text=חֹ֫דֶשׁ יָמִים|translate=a month of days}}, i.e. a month’s time=for a whole month, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=20}}, 21, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=21|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=15|verse=13}}, and {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנָתַ֫יִם יָמִים}} ''two years’ time'', i.e. two full years, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=28|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=28|verse=3.11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=10|verse=2 f.}}.

Finally, under this head may be included all the cases in which a numeral (regarded as a substantive) is followed by the object numbered in apposition, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלשָׁה בָנִים|translate=trias}} sc. ''filii'', {{GHGpar|97|a}} and {{GHGpar|134|b}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|e}}
(''d'') Collocation of the ''thing'' and the ''measure'' or ''extent, number'', &c., e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=9|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=יָמִים מִסְפָּר|translate=days}}, (a small) ''number'', i.e. only a few days; {{GHGheb|text=כֶּ֫סֶף מִשְׁנֶה|translate=money, repetition}}, i.e. twice as much money, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=12}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=כֶּ֫סֶף}} be constr. st.); {{GHGheb|text=מַ֫יִם בִּרְכָּ֑יִם|translate=water}} which was of the measure of the ''knees'', which reached to the knees, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=47|verse=4}} (also {{GHGheb|text=מֵי מָתְנָ֑יִם|translate=water that was to the loins}}, in the same verse). This likewise includes the cases in which a noun is followed in apposition by a numeral (see {{GHGpar|134|c}}) or an adverb, originally conceived as a substantive, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=2|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=אֲנָשִׁים מְעַט|translate=men, a few}}, i.e. some few men; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=5|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=תְּבוּנָה הַרְבֵּה|translate=understanding, much-making}}, i.e. much understanding, unless {{GHGheb|text=הַרְבֵּה}} is to be taken as an adverb with {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּתֵּן}}, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=8|verse=8}} with {{GHGheb|text=לָקַה}}.<section end="par131" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

449.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par131 />{{GHGmargin-letter|131|f}}
(''e'') Collocation of the ''thing'' and its ''name'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בְּהַֽרֲרָם שֵׁעִיר|translate=in their mountainous district, Seir}} (perhaps only a later gloss), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=הָאָ֫רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן|translate=the land Canaan}} ({{GHGheb|text=כנען}} probably only a later gloss), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=34|verse=2}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=9|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=5|verse=9}} (see under g below).—For examples of nouns in the construct state before a noun in apposition, see {{GHGpar|130|e}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|g}}
Rem. 1. Only in certain combinations does the noun of nearer definition come first, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַמֶּ֫לֶךְ דָּוִד}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַמֶּ֫לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה|translate=king David, king Solomon}} (less frequently {{GHGheb|text=דָּוִד הַמֶּ֫לֶךְ}} as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=39}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=12|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=8|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=9|verse=15|hidebook=1}}, and in late Hebrew, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=1|verse=1}}, 15 [cf. the Aramaic order {{GHGheb|text=דריוש מלבא}}], and often in Chron.).—A chiasmus occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=45|verse=4}}, the name standing after the defining noun in the first part of the verse, and before it in the parallel clause.

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|h}}
2. When the {{GHGterm|nota accusativi}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֵת}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־}}) or a preposition precedes the first substantive, it ''may'' be repeated before the noun in apposition, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=22|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=29|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=66|verse=21}}; this usually occurs when the nearer definition precedes a ''proper name''. As a rule, however, the repetition does not take place ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=18|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=33|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=14}}). A noun in apposition is made determinate, even after a noun with a prefix, in the ordinary way, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=12|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּירֽוּשָׁלַ֫יִם הָעִיר|translate=in Jerusalem, the city which}}, &c.<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=8}} participles after {{GHGheb|text=לְכָל־נָשָׂיו}}, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=10|verse=6}} after {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־גְּדֹלֵי הָעִיר}}, in 19:2 after a determinate accusative, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=1|verse=4}} after {{GHGheb|text=בְּבָֽתֵּיכֶם}}, are used ''without'' the article; these, however, are probably to be explained not as in apposition, but according to {{GHGpar|118|p}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|i}}
3. Sometimes a second adjective is used in apposition to a preceding adjective, in order to modify in some way the meaning of the first, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=13|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=בַּהֶ֫רֶת לְבָנָה אֲדַמְדָּ֑מֶת|translate=a white-reddish}} (light red) ''bright spot''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|k}}
4. ''Permutation'' is to be regarded as a variety of apposition. It is not complementary like apposition proper (see a above), but rather ''defines'' the preceding substantive (or pronoun, see below), in order to prevent any possible misunderstanding. This includes cases like {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=4}} ''with the life thereof'' (which is) ''the blood thereof''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=22|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=7|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=3|verse=4}} ''an hundred thousand rams, the wool'', i.e. the wool of the rams; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=25|verse=15}} ''this cup of the wine'', that is ''of fury'' (but {{GHGheb|text=הַֽהֵמָה}} is probably a gloss); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=25}} ''he poured upon him fury'', namely ''his anger'';<ref>But {{GHGheb|text=מַ֫יִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=17}} (cf. 7:6) is to be regarded as a later gloss upon the archaic {{GHGheb|text=מַבּוּל}}.</ref> but especially the examples in which such a permutative is added to a preceding pronoun, viz.—

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|l}}
(''a'') To a separate pronoun, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=7|verse=11}}; with regard to the vocative, cf. {{GHGpar|126|f}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|m}}
(''b'') To an accusative suffix, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=6}} ''she saw him, the child'' (unless {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־הַיּ׳}} be a later gloss); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=35|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=13|verse=57}}<sup> ''b''</sup>, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=19|verse=21}} (where, indeed, {{GHGheb|text=הַבָּשָׂר}} appears to be a late gloss); 21:13, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=16|verse=15}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=3|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=2|verse=21}} (according to Delitzsch rather a double accusative).<ref>For {{GHGheb|text=וַיְשַׁנּוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=14}} either’ {{GHGheb|text=וַיְשַׁנֶּה}} is to be read or the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} is to be explained according to {{GHGpar|75|b}}, note. Also {{GHGheb|text=יִלְכְּדֻנוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=5|verse=22}} has hardly preserved the correct form.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|n}}
(''c'') To a noun-suffix, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=10|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּבֹאוֹ הָאִישׁ|translate=when he went in, the man}}; 42:14; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=13|verse=4}} (?), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=3|verse=12}}; so also after a preposition with suffix, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=4|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=אִי לוֹ הָֽאֶחָד|translate=woe to him, the one alone}}; with a repetition of the preposition, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=32|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=1|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=לָהֶם לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל|translate=to them, to the children of Israel}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=21|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=51|verse=56}},<section end=par131 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

450.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par131 />{{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=42|verse=5}} (?), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=11|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=4|verse=42}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=26|verse=14}}.<ref>But in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=6}} we should certainly divide the words differently and read {{GHGheb|text=בִּסְעִפֵי הַפֹּֽרִיָּה}}, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=44}} read {{GHGheb|text=אֵלֶּה}} for {{GHGheb|text=אֵלֶ֫יהָ}}, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=14|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=אַֽחֲרִית הַשִּׂמְחָה}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫פֶשׁ חַיָּה}} is a late gloss upon {{GHGheb|text=לוֹ}}, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=41|verse=25}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־דַּלְתוֹת הַֽהֵיבָל}} a gloss on {{GHGheb|text=אֲלֵיהֶן}}.</ref>—Cf. finally, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=3|verse=7}}, where the suffix precedes the genitive periphrastically expressed by {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁלּ׳}}, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=9|verse=1}}, where the genitive is expressed by {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}.<ref>Some of the examples given above are textually (or exegetically) doubtful, whilst in the case of others, especially those from the later Books, we cannot help asking whether such a prolepsis of the genitive by means of a suffix (as e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=10|verse=3}}) is not due to the influence of Aramaic, in which it is the customary idiom; cf. Kautzsch’s {{GHGcite|title=Gramm. des Biblisch-Aram.}}, {{GHGpar|81|e}} and § 88.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|o}}
Of a different kind are the cases in which the permutative with its proper suffix follows as a kind of correction of the preceding suffix, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=23}} ''when he'' (or rather) ''his children see'', &c. (but {{GHGheb|text=יְלָדָיו}} is clearly a gloss); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=83|verse=12}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=3}} read {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽהֲהִלּוֹ}} (infin. Hiph.) or at least its syncopated form {{GHGheb|text=בַּהִלּוֹ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|p}}
5. Cases of apposition in a ''wider sense'' are those in which the nearer definition added to the noun was originally regarded as an ''adverbial accusative''; on its use with the verb and on the relative correctness of speaking of such an accusative in Hebrew, cf. {{GHGpar|118|a}} and m. Owing to the lack of case-endings, indeed, it is in many instances only by analogies elsewhere (especially in Arabic) that we can decide whether the case is one of apposition in the narrower or in the wider sense; in other instances this must remain quite uncertain. However, the following are probably cases of apposition in the wider sense:—

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|q}}
(''a'') Such phrases as {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁנֶה כֶ֫סֶף|translate=a double amount in money}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=15}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=18}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=5}} ''five thousand shekels in brass'', but this might also be taken (as in ''d'') ''shekels'' which were ''brass''; certainly such cases as Jb 15<sup>l0</sup> ''older than thy father in days'', and the expression of the superlative by means of {{GHGheb|text=מְאֹד}} (originally a substantive), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=טוֹב מְאֹד|translate=very good}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=31}} (cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=7|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=צַדִּיק הַרְבֵּה|translate=righteous over much}}), and the very frequent {{GHGheb|text=הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד}} prop. ''a much-making exceedingly'', i.e. ''exceedingly great'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=49|hidebook=1}}, also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=23|verse=29}} {{GHGheb|text=פְּצָעִים חִנָּם|translate=wounds without cause}},<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=69|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=חִנָּם}} (like {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫קֶר|translate=in a false way, falsely}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=19}} and 38:20) is used as an ''adverbial accusative'' with a participle; cf. {{GHGpar|118|q}}.</ref> perhaps also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=25}} ({{GHGheb|text=בֶּ֫טַח}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|r}}
(''b'') A few examples, in which an epexegetical substantive is added to a substantive with a suffix; thus, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=27}} {{GHGheb|text=מִדַּרְכֵּךְ זִמָּה|translate=of thy conduct in lewdness}} (but it is also possible to explain it (as in ''c'') ''of thy conduct'', which is ''lewdness''); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=24|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=22|verse=33}} {{GHGheb|text=מָֽעוּזִּי חָ֑יִל|translate=my fortress in strength}}, i.e. my strong fortress (cf., however, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=33}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=3|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=71|verse=7}}. While even in these examples the deviation from the ordinary usage of the language (cf. {{GHGpar|135|n}}) is strange, it is much more so in {{GHGheb|text=חֲבֹֽלָתוֹ חוֹב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=18|verse=7}}, i.e. according to the context ''his pledge'' for ''a debt''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=2|verse=62}} {{GHGheb|text=כְּתָבָם הַמִּתְיַֽחֲשִׂים}}, i.e. ''their register'', namely of ''those that were reckoned by genealogy'' (but perhaps {{GHGheb|text=הַמִּתְי׳}} is in apposition to the suffix in {{GHGheb|text=כְּתָבָם}}), also the curious combinations (mentioned in {{GHGpar|128|d}}) of {{GHGheb|text=בְּרִיתִי}} with a proper name ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=42}}), and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=33|verse=20}} with {{GHGheb|text=הַיּוֹם}}.<ref>But in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=25|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלוֹם}} may also be explained, according to ''c'', as really in apposition. Cf. on the whole question Delitzsch, ''Psalmen'', 4th ed., p. 203, note 1.</ref><section end=par131 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

451.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par131 />{{GHGmargin-letter|131|s}}
6. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=4}} ({{GHGheb|text=מֽוֹרָשָׁה}}, perhaps {{GHGheb|text=מוֹר׳ לִקְהִלַּת}} is to be read), 33:27 ({{GHGheb|text=מְעֹנָה}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=7|verse=8}} ({{GHGheb|text=צֵדָה}}), the absolute state appears to be used instead of the construct to govern a following logical genitive; this, however, cannot be explained either as a special kind of apposition, or (with Hitzig) as a peculiarity of the dialect of Northern Palestine, but is merely a textual corruption. On the other hand, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=עָוֹן}} is evidently intended to combine the readings {{GHGheb|text=עֲוֹן פְּלִילִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=עָוֹן פְּלִילִי}} (as in verse 28).—The remarkable combination {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים צְבָאוֹת}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=80|verse=8}}, 15 is due to the fact that in ψψ 42–83 {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} has almost throughout been subsequently substituted by some redactor for the divine name {{GHGheb|text=יחוה}}; on {{GHGheb|text=יהוה צְבָאוֹת}} cf. {{GHGpar|125|h}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=59|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=80|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, 20, and 84:9 {{GHGheb|text=יהוה}} has been reinstated in the text before {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים צְבָאוֹת}}.<ref>Without this assumption it would be inconceivable that {{GHGheb|text=יהוה אֱלֹהֵי צְבָאוֹת}} should not have been written; that the anther of these Psalms regarded {{GHGheb|text=צְבָאֹוֹת}} already as an independent name of God (so Gesenius and Olshausen) is out of the question.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|t}}
7. Lastly, the nearer definition (qualification) of a noun may be effected by means of a preposition (either with a suffix or with an independent noun), but must then be distinguished from the cases in which the preposition is dependent on a verb or verbal idea, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=6}} ''and she gave also'' {{GHGheb|text=לְאִישָׁהּ עִמָּהּ|translate=unto her husband with her}} (= ''her husband who was with her''); in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=16}} (''that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh'') and other places, the qualification of the noun is itself also qualified.<section end=par131 />

<section begin=par132 />{{GHGpar-heading|132|Connexion of the Substantive with the Adjective||<ref>On the expression of attributive ideas by substantives, cf. above, {{GHGpar|127|h}}, and {{GHGpar|128|o}}, with the note; {{GHGpar|135|n}} and {{GHGpar|141|c}} (substantives for adjectives as predicates of noun-clauses) and {{GHGpar|152|u}} (periphrases for negative qualities). On the use of the feminine of adjectives (and participles) to express abstract ideas, see {{GHGpar|122|q}}. It remains to mention further the employment (mostly only in poetry) of certain epithets in place of the substantives to which the quality in question belongs; e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אָבִיר|translate=the strong one}}, i.e. ''God''; {{GHGheb|text=אַבִּיר|translate=the strong one}}, i.e. ''the bull'' (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=8|verse=16}}, &c., ''the horse''); {{GHGheb|text=קַל|translate=swift}}=''the runner'' (of the ''horse'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=16}}); {{GHGheb|text=לְבָנָה|translate=alba}}, i.e, ''luna''; {{GHGheb|text=פֹּֽרִיָּה}} (''fructifera'') ''a fruitful tree'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=6}} (so {{GHGheb|text=פֹּרָת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=22}}); {{GHGheb|text=רֹבֵץ|translate=a croucher}}, i.e. ''a crouching beast of prey'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=7}}. Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=רֹזֵן}} (''gravis, augustus'') and {{GHGheb|text=נָשִׂיא}} (''elatus'' ?), i.e. ''a prince''. The use of adjectives and participles for substantives is much more extensive in Arabic. In Greek and Latin poetical language cf. such examples as ὑγρή = ''the sea''; ''merum'' for ''vinum'', &c.</ref>}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|132|a}}
'''1.''' The adjective (like the participle used adjectivally), which serves as an ''attribute'' of a substantive, stands ''after'' the substantive, and agrees with it in ''gender'' and ''number'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ גָּדוֹל|translate=a great man}}, {{GHGheb|text=אִשָּׁה יָפָה|translate=a beautiful woman}}. If the substantive is immediately connected with a genitive, the attribute follows the latter, since, according to § 89 and {{GHGpar|128|a}}, the construct state and the genitive belonging to it are inseparably united, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=8|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=עֲטֶ֫רֶת זָהָב גְּדוֹלָה|translate=a great crown of gold}}.— On the attribute when attached to a ''determinate'' substantive, see above, {{GHGpar|126|u}}.
<section end=par132 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

452.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par132" />{{GHGmargin-letter|132|b}}
Rem. 1. Where an adjectival attribute appears to stand ''before'' its substantive (according to the usual explanation, for the sake of special emphasis) the relation is really appositional in character; thus, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=30}} {{GHGheb|text=עֲנִיָּה עֲנָתוֹת|translate=O thou poor one, Anathoth!}} (but probably {{GHGheb|text=עֲנִ֫יהָ|translate=answer her}}, is to be read); cf. 23:12, 53:11 (''a righteous man, my servant''; but in 28:21 {{GHGheb|text=זָר}} and {{GHGheb|text=נָכְרִיּ}} are {{GHGterm|predicates}} preceding the substantives); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=6}}, 10 f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=4}} ''him who is worthy to be praised will I call upon the Lord''; 92:12 (apposition after participles).—But {{GHGheb|text=רַבִּים}} and {{GHGheb|text=רַבּוֹת|translate=many}}, are sometimes placed, like numerals, before the substantive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=16|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=9|verse=28}} (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=145|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=רַב}} is a ''subst. regens'', in 89:51 the text is corrupt); an appositional relation can scarcely be intended in these instances.

{{GHGmargin-letter|132|c}}
2. In a few expressions (mostly poetic) the adjective appears not as an attribute ''after'' the substantive, but in the construct state governing it; so in the singular, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=16}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=גֹּדֶל}} should be read); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=7}} (''the height of his stature''); in the plural, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=40}} {{GHGheb|text=חַלֻּקֵי אֲבָנִים|translate=smooth ones of}} (among) ''stones'', i.e. ''smooth stones''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=35|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=7|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=46|verse=5}}, and with a following collective instead of a plural, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶבְיוֹנֵי אָדָם|translate=the poor among men}}, i.e. ''poor men''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=11|verse=7}}; cf. in Latin ''canum degeneres''. However, in almost all these cases the adjective which is made into a ''regens'' is strongly emphatic, and is frequently equivalent to a superlative (see below, {{GHGpar|133|g}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|132|d}}
3. When ''two'' adjectives follow a feminine, sometimes only that standing next to the noun takes the feminine termination, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=19|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=רוּחַ גְּדֹלָה וְחָזָק וגו׳}} (but read {{GHGheb|text=גָּדוֹל}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=9}} (but cf. {{GHGpar|75|y}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=20|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=63|verse=2}}. A similar dislike of the feminine form may also be observed in the case of verbal predicates referring to feminine subjects, cf. {{GHGpar|145|p}} and t.

When an attribute qualifies several substantives of different genders, it agrees with the masculine, as being the ''prior gender'' (cf. {{GHGpar|146|d}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=9|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=חֻקִּים וּמִצְוֹת טוֹבִים}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=34|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=8|verse=5}}.

When ''three'' attributes follow a substantive, the first two may stand without a conjunction, and the last be attached by {{GHGterm|wāw copulative}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=1|verse=8}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|132|e}}
4. After feminines plural ending in {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}} ({{GHGpar|87|p}}) the adjectival attribute (in accordance with the fundamental rule stated above, under a) takes the ending {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=בֵּיצִים עֲזֻבוֹת|translate=forsaken eggs}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=16}}. For a strange exception see {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=29|verse=17}} (differently in 24:2).

{{GHGmargin-letter|132|f}}
5. With regard to ''number'' it is to be remarked that—

(''a'') Substantives in the ''dual'' are followed by adjectives (or participles) in the ''plural'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=28}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=6|verse=17}}) {{GHGheb|text=עֵינַ֫יִם רָמוֹת|translate=haughty eyes}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=35|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=3}} f., cf. {{GHGpar|88|a}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|132|g}}
(''b'') ''Collective'' ideas are not infrequently joined with the ''plural'' of the adjective or participle (''constructio ad sensum''); thus, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=צֹאן|translate=sheep}} [with ''fem. plur.''], {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=43}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=עַם}}=''men'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=9|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל}}=''all the Israelites'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=גָּלוּת}}=''the exiles'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=28|verse=4}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫פֶשׁ שְׁנָ֫יִם|translate=two souls}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=46|verse=27}}.<ref>But it is impossible to take {{GHGheb|text=תְּמִימִם}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=46|verse=6}} as an attribute of {{GHGheb|text=בָּקָר}}; probably it is a correction intended to harmonize the passage with {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=28|verse=11}} where ''two'' young bullocks are required.</ref> Cf. similar phenomena in the connexion of collectives with plural predicates in {{GHGpar|145|c}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|132|h}}
(''c'') The ''pluralis excellentiae'' or ''pluralis maiestatis'' is joined, as a rule, to the singular of the attribute, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=7|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים צַדִּיק}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=19|verse=4}}, 16 (={{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=4}}, 17); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=4}}; but cf. {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים חֶיִּים}}<ref>Cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=13}}, where {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} (in the sense of ''a spirit'') is followed by {{GHGheb|text=עֹלִים}} as a second accusative; conversely in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=13}}, 16, a singular suffix refers back to {{GHGheb|text=תְּרָפִים|translate=household god}} (but not so in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=34}}), as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=46|verse=4}} to the plural of amplification {{GHGheb|text=יַמִּים|translate=sea}}. On the other hand, it is very doubtful whether {{GHGheb|text=רַבָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=78|verse=15}} is to be regarded as an attribute of {{GHGheb|text=תְּהֹמוֹת}} and not rather as the adverb, ''abundantly''.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=5|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=26}}, 36, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=10|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=36|hidebook=1}}, perhaps also<section end="par132" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

453.text:
{{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים}}= ''another god'', and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=24|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים קְדשִׁים}} (but cf. above, {{GHGpar|124|g}}–{{GHGpar|124|k|nonumber=1}}). On the other hand, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=8}} is to be explained as having been said by the Philistines, who supposed that the Israelites had several gods. On the connexion of {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} with a plural predicate, see {{GHGpar|145|i}}. '''2.''' On the adjective (in the construct state) governing a following genitive, see {{GHGpar|128|x}}; for the participle in the same construction, see {{GHGpar|116|f}}–l.
{{GHGpar-heading|133|The Comparison of Adjectives. (Periphrastic Expression of the Comparative and Superlative||'')''}}
A. Wünsche, ‘Der Komparativ im Hebr. im Lichte der arab. Gramm.,’ in ''Vierteljahrsschrift für Bibelkunde'', 1904, p. 398 ff.
{{GHGmargin-letter|133|a}} '''1.''' Hebrew possesses no special forms either for the comparative or superlative of the adjective.There is in Arabic a special form of the adjective (the ''elative'') for the comparative and superlative, which in Hebrew would have the form {{GHGheb|text=אַקְטָל}}. Instances of it, perhaps, are {{GHGheb|text=אַכְזָר|translate=daring, cruel}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַכְזָב|translate=deceptive}} (of a brook drying up), and its opposite {{GHGheb|text=אֵיתָן}} (contracted from ''ʾaitan'') ''constantly flowing'', ''perennis''. These forms are, however, used without any perceptible emphasis, and cannot be regarded as more than isolated relics of an elative formation which has become obsolete, much as the Latin comparative disappears in Italian, and still more so in French, and is supplanted by the circumlocution with ''più'', ''plus''. In order to express a comparative, the person or thing which is to be represented as excelled in some particular quality is attached to the attributive word by the preposition {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} ({{GHGheb|text=מִ‍·}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=גָּבֹהַּ מִכָּל־הָעָם|translate=higher than any of the people}}. The fundamental idea evidently is, ''tall away from all the people'' (beyond all the people); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=מַה־מָּתוֹק טִדְּבַשׁ וּמֶה עַז מֵֽאֲרִי|translate=what is sweeter than honey? and what is stronger than a lion?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=28|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=6|verse=2}} Frequently an infinitive appears as the object of the comparison, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=19}} ''it is better that I give her to thee, than that I should, give her'', &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=14|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=8}}f.In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=25}} the adjective is specially intensified by repetition, ''art thou so much better than Balak?'' It would also be possible, however, to translate ''art thou really better ...?'' {{GHGmargin-letter|133|b}} Rem. 1. This use of {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} is also very common when the attributive idea is represented by an intransitive verb, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=10|verse=23}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּגְבַּהּ מִכָּל־הָעָם|translate=and he was higher than any of the people}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=8}}. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=6}}. Elsewhere, especially after transitive verbs, {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} rather represents (on its different senses see {{GHGpar|119|v}}–{{GHGpar|119|z|nonumber=1}}) the idea

454.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par133 />of a ''separation, distinction'' or ''superiority'' of one person or thing ''from'' or ''over'' others.<ref>Cf. the Latin ablative with the comparative; also the etymology of such words as ''eximius, egregius'', and the Homeric ἐκ πάντων μάλιστα, Il. 4, 96; ἐκ πασρ́ων, 18, 431.</ref> This is evident in such cases as {{GHGheb|text=בָּחַר מִן־|translate=to choose}} something (to prefer it) ''before'' something else, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=15}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=14|verse=2}} (also {{GHGheb|text=יִתְרוֹן... מִן־|translate=the excellence of... over...}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=2|verse=13}}); it is also seen in examples like {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אָהַב אֶת־יוֹסֵף מִכָּל־בָּנָיו|translate=now Israel loved Joseph more than all his}} (other) ''children''; 29:30, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=6|verse=6}}.<ref>On the other hand, the phrase {{GHGheb|text=צָדַק מִן־}} expresses not a comparison, but only a relation existing between one person and another; thus, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=26}} {{GHGheb|text=צָֽדְקָה מִמֶּ֫נִּי}} means, ''she is in the right as against me''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=32|verse=2|hidebook=1}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=17|verse=12}} ''rather'' (to meet with so and so) ''than''... is expressed by {{GHGheb|text=וְאַל־}} before the second member.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|133|c}}
2. A somewhat different idea underlies the use of {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} after adjectives, or intransitive verbs possessing an attributive sense, when the thought to be expressed is that the quality is ''too little'' or ''too much'' in force for the attainment of a particular aim or object, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=הַמְעַט מִכֶּם|translate=is it a small thing}} (i.e. too little) ''for you to...?'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=11}}; after an intransitive verb, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=11}} ''I am too insignificant'' ({{GHGheb|text=קָטֹ֫נְתִּי}}) ''for all the mercies'' (I am not worthy of...), &c.; cf. also the expressions {{GHGheb|text=כָּבֵד מִן־|translate=to be too heavy for one}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=18|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=38|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=קָשָׁה מִן־|translate=to be too hard for one}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=מָעַט מִן־|translate=to be too few for something}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=גָּבַר מִן־|translate=to be too strong for one}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=65|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=עָצַם מִן־|translate=to be too mighty for one}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=16}}; {{GHGheb|text=רוּם מִן־|translate=to be too high for one}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=61|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=צַר מִן־|translate=to be too narrow for one}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=קָצַר מִן־|translate=to be too short for something}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=50|verse=2}}, and very frequently {{GHGheb|text=נִפְלָא מִן־|translate=to be too wonderful for one}} (and, consequently, inconceivable or unattainable), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=17|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=30|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=37|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=18}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=פְּלִיאָה}} in the same sense is followed by {{GHGheb|text=מִן}}.—This use is especially seen in the numerous instances in which the attribute is followed by {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} with an infinitive e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=64}} ''the brazen altar... was'' {{GHGheb|text=קָטֹן מֵֽהָכִיל|translate=too little to receive}} (to be able to receive) ''the burnt offering'', cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=36|verse=7|hidebook=1}} ''too great for them to dwell together''; after verbs, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=40|verse=6}}. Finally, cf. {{GHGheb|text=רַבּ לָכֶם מִן־}}, followed by the infinitive, ''it is enough'' (prop. ''too much'') ''for you to...'', meaning ''ye have... long enough'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=12|verse=28}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=28}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=44|verse=6}} ({{GHGheb|text=מִּן־}} followed by a substantive).<ref>Cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=4|verse=3}}, where the idea of ''doing something too little'' is paraphrased by the Hiph. {{GHGheb|text=הִמְעִיט}} = ''do not too little'', sc. {{GHGheb|text=לִשְׁאֹל|translate=in borrowing}} empty vessels.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|133|d}}
In all these instances {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} expresses either the ''removal'' of a thing ''from'' a person, or the ''severance'' of the person from some aim or object; cf. also the expression {{GHGheb|text=לֹֽא־יִבָּצֵר מֵהֶם כֹּל וגו׳|translate=nothing will be unattainable for them}} (prop. there shall not be cut off from them anything which, &c.), ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=11|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=42|verse=3}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|133|e}}
3. The attributive idea, on which {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} logically depends, must sometimes, in consequence of a pregnant use of the {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} (see the analogous examples in {{GHGpar|119|ff}}), be supplied from the context, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=וּפְסִֽלֵיהֶם מִירֽוּשָׁלַ֫יִם|translate=whose graven images}} were more numerous ''than'' those at ''Jerusalem'', &c.;<ref>With this ''comparatio decurtata'', cf. the still bolder pregnant construction in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=4|verse=8}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֵעֵת|translate=greater gladness than at the time}}, &c.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=4}} worse ''than a thorn hedge''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=62|verse=10}} lighter ''than a breath''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=11|verse=17}} clearer ''than the noonday''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=4|verse=17}} better ''than'', &c.<section end=par133 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

455.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par133 />{{GHGmargin-letter|133|f}}
'''2.''' The correlative comparatives ''greater—less'' (''older—younger'') are expressed by the simple adjective with the article (''the great'', equivalent to ''the greater'', &c.); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=31.34|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=15|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=16.18.26|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|133|g}}
'''3.''' To express the ''superlative'' it is also sufficient (see above, f) to make the adjective determinate, either by means of the article or a following partitive genitive (or suffix); in this case the article or genitive indicates that the attribute in question belongs especially to one or more definite individuals;<ref>Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=עֶלְיוֹן|translate=the one above}}, i.e. ''the Most High''.</ref> e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=21}} {{GHGheb|text=הַצְּעִרָה|translate=the least}}; 16:11 {{GHGheb|text=הַקָּטָן|translate=the little one}}, i.e. the ''youngest'' of eight sons; 17:14 ''David was'' {{GHGheb|text=הַקָּטָן|translate=the youngest, and the three great}}, i.e. elder, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=8}}.—So also with a qualifying adjective, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּנוֹ הַקָּטָן|translate=his youngest son}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=14|verse=15}}; also with a following genitive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=21|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹן בָּנָיו|translate=the youngest of his sons}}: {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=24}} ''the least upon the earth''; with suffix, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=טוֹבָם|translate=their good one}}, i.e. the best of them; Jan 3:5 {{GHGheb|text=מִגְּדוֹלָם וְעַד־קְטַנָּם|translate=from the greatest of them even to the least of them}}; cf. the inverse order in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=34|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|133|h}}
Rem. 1. The above examples apply only to the most common ''relative'' attributes (''great, small, good''), and to expressions which by usage easily came to be recognized as periphrases for the superlative. Other adjectives, however, when followed by a partitive genitive, also acquire the sense of a superlative; this appears from the context, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=19}} ''the most hidden treasures of the sand''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=29}} ''the wisest amongst her ladies''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=8|hidebook=1}} f., 29:19, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=28|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=11|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=45|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=6}} (''in the most horrible of valleys''), 41:22; probably also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=16}}. On this government by the adjective generally, cf. {{GHGpar|132|c}}.—Moreover, the combination of a substantive in the construct state with an adjective used substantivally ({{GHGpar|128|w}}) sometimes serves as a periphrasis for the superlative, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל כְּלֵי הַקָּטָן|translate=all the smallest vessels}}. On {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=7|verse=10}} see {{GHGpar|126|x}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|133|i}}
2. Other periphrases for the superlative are the use of a substantive in the construct state before the plural of the same word (which is naturally to be regarded as a partitive genitive; cf. our ''book of books''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=33}} {{GHGheb|text=קֹדֶשׁ הֲקָּדָשִׁים|translate=the most holy place}}; {{GHGheb|text=שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=1}}) ''the most excellent song''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=25}} (= ''servus servorum, the lowest servant''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=3|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=10|verse=17}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=136|verse=2}}, 3)<ref>''God of gods, and Lord of lords'', just as the supreme god of the Babylonians is called ''bēl bēlī'' (Tiele, ''Compend. der Rel.-Gesch.'', p. 87).</ref>; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=34|verse=10}} (cf. Gal 1:5, Rev 22:5); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=7|hidebook=1}} (''king of kings'', of Nebuchadrezzar; cf. 1 Tim 6:15, Rev 17:14, 19:16, and another kind of periphrasis in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=95|verse=3}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=1|verse=2}}. Similarly in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=28}} two participles are combined, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=10|verse=15}} two substantives in the singular. Finally, the same object is attained by connecting one substantive in the construct state with another of the same stem ({{GHGheb|text=שַׁבַּת שַׁבָּתוֹן|translate=a sabbath of solemn rest}}, i.e. an obligatory day of rest, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=31|verse=15}}, &c.) or of the same meaning (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=ח֫שֶׁךְ אֲפֵלָה|translate=a thick darkness}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=22}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|133|k}}
3. The intensification of attributes by means of repetition belongs rather to rhetoric than to syntax, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=7|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=עָמֹק עָמֹק|translate=exceeding deep}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=20|verse=14}}; the adjective is even used three times in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=3}}.—Cf. the repetition of adverbs for the same purpose in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=7}} ({{GHGheb|text=מְאֹד מְאֹד|translate=exceedingly}}, also {{GHGheb|text=בִּמְאֹד מְאֹד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=7}}, &c.); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=42|verse=15}}.—On the other hand, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=43}} the repetition expresses<section end=par133 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

456.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par133 />a continuous progress, ''higher and higher... lower and lower''; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=27}} (see {{GHGpar|123|e}}) and 16:20 (''nothing but justice'') the constancy of the action. Cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=30}} {{GHGheb|text=מְעַט מְעַט|translate=little by little, very gradually}}.<ref>Adverbs of the same stem are connected in this way in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=6|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=13|hidebook=1}}; of different stems in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=26}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=4|verse=4}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=12|verse=2}} the particles {{GHGheb|text=רַק אַךְ}} appear to be placed together for a similar purpose, equivalent to ''simply and solely''.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|133|l}}
The repetition of substantives serves also as a periphrasis for the superlative in such cases as {{GHGheb|text=לְדֹר דֹּר}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=15}}) = ''to the remotest generations''; cf. 17:16, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=8|verse=11|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGterm|perfect peace}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=32}} ({{GHGheb|text=עַוָּה}} three times);<ref>Different in kind from the triple utterance of the same words in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=7|verse=4}} and 22:29, and the double exclamation in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=4|verse=19}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=16}} (?).</ref> 35:7, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=1|verse=2}}; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=2|verse=21}} f. and the emphatic combination of synonymous verbs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=10}}. Sometimes the completeness of an action or state is expressed by placing together two or even three substantives of the same stem and of similar sound, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=6|verse=14}} (33:28<sup> f.</sup>, 35:3); 32:15, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=2|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=1|verse=15}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=27|hidebook=1}}).<section end=par133 />

<section begin=par134 />{{GHGpar-heading|134|Syntax of the Numerals}}

Cf. the exhaustive statistics collected by Sven Herner, {{GHGcite|title=Syntax der Zahlwörter im A.T.}}, Lund, 1893. E. König, ‘Zur Syntax der Zahlwörter im A.T.,’ ''AJSL''. xviii, 129 ff.

{{GHGmargin-letter|134|a}}
'''1.''' The numerals from 2 to 10, as being originally abstract substantives,<ref>Cf. {{GHGpar|97|a}}, where it is shown that the masculine is the original form of the numerals (used for both genders), and that the feminine was afterwards differentiated and used with masc. nouns, primarily in the second decade and then in the first as well.</ref> may be connected with their substantives in three different ways. They may stand either—

(''a'') In the construct state ''before'' the substantive (the object numbered being consequently in the genitive), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלשֶׁת יָמִים|translate=a triad of days}}, i.e. three days; {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנֵי הָֽאֲנָשִׁים|translate=the two men}}; or

{{GHGmargin-letter|134|b}}
(''b'') In the absolute state ''before'' it (the object numbered being in apposition, {{GHGpar|131|d}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלשָׁה בָנִים|translate=a triad}}, viz. ''sons'', i.e. three sons; {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנַ֫יִם אֲנָשִׁים|translate=two men}}; or

{{GHGmargin-letter|134|c}}
(''c'') In the absolute state (likewise in apposition) ''after'' the object numbered, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בָּנוֹת שָׁלוֹשׁ}}. So especially in long lists, since in these the substantives naturally come first, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=15}}. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=7|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=28|verse=19|hidebook=1}}. Apart from such cases, the frequency of this order in the later Books is due to the fact that the character of the numeral tended more and more to become adjectival rather than substantival.<ref>From Herner’s tables (op. cit., pp. 55–66) it appears, according to p. 68, that in the documents J, E, D of the Pentateuch, and in Jos 1–12, Judges, Samuel, Isaiah, Jeremiah, the Minor Prophets, Psalms, Megilloth, and Job, the numeral never, or very rarely, stands ''after'' its noun; in Kings and Ezekiel it stands several times ''after''; in the Priestly Code nearly always ''after''; in Chronicles, Ezra, Nehemiah, and Daniel, nearly as often ''after'' as ''before'' the noun. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=28|verse=10}} the Masora makes the numeral in the genitive follow the construct state of the substantive numbered; we should, however, read {{GHGheb|text=וְאֶת־שֵׁמוֹת הַשִּׁשָּׁה}}; for the omission of the article before {{GHGheb|text=שׁ׳}}, cf. {{GHGpar|126|w}}.</ref>
<section end=par134 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

457.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par134 />{{GHGmargin-letter|134|d}}
Rem. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=24|verse=22}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶחָד}} follows the construct state {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁפַּט}}, but here as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=15|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁפָּט}} should be read. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶחָד}} is in apposition to a substantive with a suffix (= ''one of you brethren''; but verse 33 ''the one of you brethren''). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=31|verse=28}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶחָד}} precedes the substantive in the Aramaic manner (= ''one each'').—For {{GHGheb|text=מֵאָֽה־שָׁנָה}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=17}}, &c.) we find regularly in the Priestly Code (except in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=23|verse=1|hidebook=1}}) {{GHGheb|text=מְאַת שָׁנָה}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=5|verse=3}}, &c.) ''an hundred years''. On the connexion of abstract numerals with suffixes, as {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנֵיהֶם|translate=their duality}}, i.e. ''they two'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=25}}, &c. (also with a strengthening separate pronoun, as {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנֵ֫ינוּ אֲנַ֫חְנוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=42}}), cf. {{GHGpar|97|i}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|134|e}}
'''2.''' The numerals from 2 to 10 take the object numbered in the plural,<ref>On examples such as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=46|verse=27}} ({{GHGheb|text=נֶָפֶשׁ שְׁנָ֑֫יִם|translate=two souls}}), cf. {{GHGpar|132|g}} (collectives joined with the plural of the adjective).</ref> with very few exceptions, such as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=22}} (where {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנֵי הָעֹ֫מֶר}} = ''the double of an omer''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=2|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=45|verse=1}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=8|verse=17}} and 25:17 {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} The numerals from 11 to 19 generally take the plural, but with certain substantives frequently used with numerals the singular is more common (see further, under f). The tens (from 20 to 90), when they precede, take the singular (in the accusative, cf. {{GHGpar|131|p}}) of certain nouns frequently used with numerals ({{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫לֶף|translate=a thousand}}, {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם}}, {{GHGheb|text=כֹּר}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫פֶשׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫קֶל}}—but only in Ezekiel and the Priestly Code), otherwise the plural, as {{GHGheb|text=בָּנִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=בָּנוֹת}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָרִים}} (but cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=33}}), &c.; on the other hand, the plural is necessary when they follow the object numbered in apposition (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אַמּוֹת עֶשְׂרִים|translate=twenty cubits}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=3|verse=3}} f.; with the exception of {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=24|verse=24}}, only in late Books). After {{GHGheb|text=טֵאָה}} and {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫לֶף}} the substantive numbered may be used either in the singular or plural, see further under g.

{{GHGmargin-letter|134|f}}
Rem. 1. After the numerals from 11 to 19 the singular is used, as a rule, with {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם|translate=day}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנָה|translate=year}}, {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ|translate=man}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫פֶשׁ|translate=soul}} (person), {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁ֫בֶט|translate=tribe}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַצֵּבָה|translate=pillar}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=24|verse=4}}), sometimes with {{GHGheb|text=אַמָּה|translate=cubit}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֹ֫דֶשׁ|translate=month}}, {{GHGheb|text=עִיר|translate=city}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫קֶל|translate=shekel}} (compare our ''four-year-old, ten pound''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=אַחַד עָשָׂר יוֹם}} (cf., however, such exceptions as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=4|verse=2}}, &c.).—Substantives other than these are used in the plural with the numerals from 11 to 19, and the numeral may even follow the substantive, especially in later passages, as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=7|verse=87}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=4|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=25|verse=5|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|134|g}}
2. After {{GHGheb|text=מֵאָה}} ({{GHGheb|text=מְאַת}} [so almost exclusively in the Priestly Code, e.g. always {{GHGheb|text=מְאַת אֶ֫לֶף}}], {{GHGheb|text=מֵאוֹת}}, {{GHGheb|text=מָאתַ֫יִם}}) and {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫לֶף}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֲלָפִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַלְפֵי}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַלְפַּ֫יִם}}) the substantives {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֶלֶ֫ף}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַמָּה}} (except in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=40|verse=27}}), {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם}}, {{GHGheb|text=רַגְלִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=צֶ֫מֶד}} are regularly used in the singular, generally also {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=כִּכָּר}}, {{GHGheb|text=כֹּר}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫קֶל}} (with the exception of {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=7|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=26}}, &c.); cf., moreover, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=60|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=אַלְפֵי רְבָבָה}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=1|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=21|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=7|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=5|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=9|verse=15}}.—Examples of the ''plural'' after {{GHGheb|text=מֵאָה}} are {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=16|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=18|verse=4}}; after {{GHGheb|text=מְאַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=38|verse=27}}; after {{GHGheb|text=מֵאוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=15|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=8|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=10|verse=17}},<section end=par134 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

458.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par134" />{{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=42|verse=17}}; after {{GHGheb|text=מָאתַ֫יִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=7|verse=20}}; after {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫לֶף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=3|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=5|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=3|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=90|verse=4}}; after {{GHGheb|text=אֲלָפִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=42|verse=12}}; after {{GHGheb|text=אַלְפֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=6|verse=7}}; after {{GHGheb|text=אַלְפַּ֫יִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=36|verse=8}}.— In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=12|verse=11}} the plural {{GHGheb|text=יָמִים}} precedes the numeral ''twelve hundred''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|134|h}}
'''3.''' Numerals compounded of tens and units (like 21, 62) take the object numbered either ''after'' them in the singular (in the accusative), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=5|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=שְׁתַּ֫יִם וְשִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה|translate=two and sixty years}} ({{GHGheb|text=שָׁנָה}} in the singular, according to ''e'', since it conforms to the ten immediately preceding; but also {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלשִׁים וּשְׁמֹנֶה שָׁנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=14}}), or ''before'' them in the plural, especially in the later Books, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=9|verse=26}}, &c.; or the object is repeated (but only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=6|verse=1}}, and the Priestly Code; sometimes even several times, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=23|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=25|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, 17 thrice) in the plural with the units, and in the singular with the tens and hundreds, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים וְשִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה|translate=seventy and five years}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=23|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=מֵאָה שֶׁנָה וְעֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה וְשֶׁ֫בַע שָׁנִים|translate=an hundred and twenty and seven years}}. Cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=5|verse=6 ff.}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|134|i}}
Rem. 1. It may further be remarked with regard to the order, that the thousand or thousands always precede the hundreds, &c., and the hundreds almost always come before the smaller numbers (in Kings and Ezekiel sometimes, and in the Priestly Code usually, after the smaller numbers), the tens in the earlier Books (documents J and D of the Pentateuch, in Joshua 1–12, Judges, Samuel, Isaiah, and also in Ezra and Nehemiah) ''before'' the units, but in Jeremiah, Ezekiel, the Priestly Code, Joshua 13–24 ''after'' the units (see Herner, op. cit., p. 73). After the hundreds the smaller number is very frequently added without {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}, especially in Ezra, Nehemiah, and Daniel.

On the syntax of the cardinals in general:—

{{GHGmargin-letter|134|k}}
2. The cardinals are determined by the article, when they refer back (without being connected with the object numbered; cf., however, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=25|verse=10}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=16|verse=35}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=4|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=23|verse=13}}) to a number or list already mentioned, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁם הָֽאֶחָד פִּישׁוֹן|translate=the name of the one}} (the first) ''is Pishon''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=9}} ''four kings against the five'' (enumerated in verse 2); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=11|verse=20}} f., and the determinate tens in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=29}}, 31 f. A demonstrative with the article may also be added to a numeral determined in this way, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=19|verse=9}} (but cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=22|verse=23|hidebook=1}}, where the numeral and demonstrative are practically determinate in themselves). In the case of the numerals from 11 to 19 the article may stand either before the unit ({{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=25|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=27|verse=15|hidebook=1}}) or before {{GHGheb|text=עָשָׂר}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=4|verse=4}}); it is used before all three members of a compound number (273) in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=3|verse=46}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|134|l}}
In apposition with any determinate substantive the cardinal number is used ''without'' the article, not only when it precedes the substantive, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=15|verse=14}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֶת־שְׁלוֹשָׁה בְנֵי הָֽעֲנָק}}, where {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלוֹשָׁה}} is equivalent to a substantive determinate in itself; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=6|verse=8}}, 22 {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=31}}, and the passages discussed above in {{GHGpar|126|x}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=29}}, &c.), but also when it follows the substantive, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=7|verse=27}}, 43 f. {{GHGheb|text=עֶשֶׂר}} and {{GHGheb|text=עֲשָׂרָה}}; the omission of the article may here, as in the eases noticed in {{GHGpar|126|z}}, be also due to the dislike of a hiatus, but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנַ֫יִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=25|verse=16}} after a determinate substantive. The fact that it is by nature determinate would also be a very simple explanation of {{GHGheb|text=אֶחָד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=28|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=17}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=24|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=10|verse=9}}, instead of the more usual {{GHGheb|text=הָֽאֶחָד}}, and of {{GHGheb|text=אַחַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=2}} for {{GHGheb|text=הָֽאַחַת}}.
<section end="par134" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

459.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par134 />{{GHGmargin-letter|134|m}}
Such cases as {{GHGheb|text=שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=17}} (which is determined by a following determinate genitive) are explained from {{GHGpar|127|b}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=9|verse=25}} perhaps from {{GHGpar|126|q}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=26}} probably the light of all the seven days of the week is meant; on the other hand, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=20}} and 25:38 the article is, with Wellhausen, to be omitted.

{{GHGmargin-letter|134|n}}
3. Certain specifications of ''measure, weight'', or ''time'', are commonly omitted after numerals, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=20|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫לֶף כֶּ֫סֶף|translate=a thousand}} (shekels) ''of silver''; so also before {{GHGheb|text=זָהָב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=10|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=23}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=72}}. Moreover, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=3|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁשׁ שְׂעֹרִים|translate=six}} (ephahs) ''of barley''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=10|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=שְׁתֵּי־לֶ֫חֶם|translate=two}} (sc. ''loaves'', see verse 3) ''of bread'', cf. 17:17 {{GHGheb|text=עֲשָׂרָה לֶ֫חֶם}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=16|verse=1}}, where before {{GHGheb|text=קַ֫יִץ}} a measure, or perhaps some term like ''cakes'', is to be supplied.—The number of cubits is stated in the Priestly Code ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=2}}, &c.) and in 1 K 6 and 7 (otherwise only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=40|verse=5}}, 21, 47:3. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=5|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=11|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=4|verse=2}} f.) by the addition of {{GHGheb|text=בָּֽאַמָּה}} prop. ''by the cubit''. Also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=27|verse=11}} the Samaritan and LXX read {{GHGheb|text=בָּֽאַמָּה}} after {{GHGheb|text=אֹרֶךְ}}, and in 27:15 {{GHGheb|text=אַמָּה}} after {{GHGheb|text=עֶשְׂרֵה}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|134|o}}
'''4.''' The ''ordinals'' above 10 have no special forms, but are expressed by the corresponding cardinals, which may then stand either before or after the object numbered, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּשִׁבעָה עָשָׂר יוֹם|translate=on the seventeenth day}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּאַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה|translate=in the fortieth year}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=25|verse=27}}, and, with repetition of {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנָה}} in a compound number, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=6|verse=1}}; such a cardinal occurs without {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} (and therefore in the ''accus. temporis'', according to {{GHGpar|118|k}}) in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=4}} (the Samaritan, however, has {{GHGheb|text=ובשלש}}); with the article (but without a numbered object, see under k), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=19|verse=19}}.<ref>Somewhat different from this is {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=19|verse=15}} ''be ready'' {{GHGheb|text=לִשְׁל֫שֶׁת יָמִים}} prop. ''after three days'', i.e. ''on the third day'' (in verses 11 and 16 and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=10|verse=8}} the ordinal is used), also {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=30|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=כִּי חָלִיתִי הַיּוֹם שְׁלשָׁה|translate=because three days agone I fell sick}}, prop. ''to-day three'' (days).</ref>—On the position of the numeral as a genitive following its noun, cf. e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=16|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּשְׁנַת עֶשְׂרִים וָשֶׁבַע|translate=in the twenty and seventh year}}, and with a determinate numeral, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=33|verse=38}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=15|verse=9}}. In this case, however, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנָה}} is very frequently repeated, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=13|verse=10}}; after a determinate numeral, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=25|verse=10}}.<ref>All these expressions may indeed be explained by supposing that, e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=25|verse=10}}, the proper meaning is ''the year of the fifty years'' which it completed, i.e. the fiftieth year; but it is more correct to regard {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנַת}} or {{GHGheb|text=בִּשְׁנַת}} in such cases not as a real {{GHGterm|nomen regens}}, but simply as a connective form to be explained on the analogy of the cases mentioned in {{GHGpar|128|k}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|134|p}}
Rem. In numbering days of the month and years, the cardinals are very frequently used instead of the ordinals even for the numbers from 1 to 10, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בִּשְׁנַת שְׁתַּיִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=15|verse=25}}; {{GHGheb|text=בִּשְׁנַת שָׁלשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=18|verse=1}}, &c., cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=15|verse=9}}. The months themselves are always numbered by the ordinals ({{GHGheb|text=בָּרִאשׁוֹן}}, {{GHGheb|text=בַּשֵּׁנִי}}, &c., up to {{GHGheb|text=בָּֽעֲשִׂירִי}}), but not the days of the month, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בְּאֶחָד לַחֹ֫דֶשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=5}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=בְּאַרְבָּעָה לַחֹ֫דֶשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=7|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽחֲמִשָּׁה לַחֹ֫דֶשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=1|verse=1}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=בְּשִׁבְעָה לַחֹ֫דֶשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=25|verse=8}}, {{GHGheb|text=בְּתִשְׁעָה לַחֹ֫דֶשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=23|verse=32}} (always, however, {{GHGheb|text=בֶּֽעָשׂר לַחֹ֫דֶשׁ|translate=on the tenth day of the month}}). On the<section end=par134 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

460.text:
