<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par134 />omission of {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם}} in all these cases see under n; only in late passages is {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם}} added, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=29|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּיוֹם שְׁמוֹנָה לַחֹ֫דֶשׁ}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=3|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=מִיּוֹם אֶחָד לַחֹ֫דֶשׁ}}.—Finally, when the year is stated by {{GHGheb|text=בִּשְׁנַת}} governing a determinate ordinal, viz. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=17|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּשְׁנַת הַתְּשִׁיעִית|translate=in the ninth year}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=25|verse=1}} (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=52|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּשָׁנָה}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=28|verse=1}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, 32:1 {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, 46:2, 51:59, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=7|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=בִּשְׁנַת}} in such cases is again (see note 2 on o) to be explained according to {{GHGpar|128|k}}. This is supported by the fact that the Masora on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=28|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=32|verse=1|hidebook=1}} requires in the {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} {{GHGheb|text=בַּשָּׁנָה}} for {{GHGheb|text=בשנת}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|134|q}}
'''5.''' ''Distributives'' are expressed either by repetition of the cardinal number, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=9}}, 15 {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנַ֫יִם שְׁנַ֫יִם|translate=two and two}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=21|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁשׁ וָשֵׁשׁ|translate=six each}}; with the numbered object also repeated, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=3|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ אֶחָד אִישׁ אֶחָד לַשָּֽׁבֶט|translate=for every tribe a man}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=13|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=34|verse=18|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֶחָד מִן}}, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=11|verse=1}}, ''one out of every ten''); cf. {{GHGpar|123|d}}; or a periphrasis with {{GHGheb|text=אֶחָד לְ}} is used, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=23}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=לְאֶחָד}} after ''six wings'' twice repeated; the simple distributive {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} is, however, sufficient (as in {{GHGheb|text=לַבְּקָרִים}}, {{GHGpar|123|c}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לְמֵאוֹת וְלַֽאֲלָפִים|translate=by hundreds and by thousands}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|134|r}}
'''6.''' The ''multiplicatives'' are expressed either (like the ordinals above 10, see under o) by the cardinals (in the feminine, probably owing to the omission of {{GHGheb|text=פַּ֫עַם}}, {{GHGheb|text=פְּעָמִים}}; so König, {{GHGcite|title=Lehrgeb.}}, ii. 228), as {{GHGheb|text=שְׁתַּ֫יִם|translate=twice}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=40|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫בַע|translate=seven times}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=21}}, 24, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=16}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אַחַת|translate=once}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=6|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=40|verse=5}}, for which in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=33|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּאַחַת}}<ref>But {{GHGheb|text=בְּאַחַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=10|verse=4}} is to be translated ''on one'' (trumpet).</ref> along with {{GHGheb|text=בִּשְׁתַּ֫יִם}} (the latter also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=21}}); or by the ''dual'' of the numeral, thus {{GHGheb|text=שִׁבְעָתַ֫יִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=15}} (in verse 24 along with the cardinal 77 for 77 times); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=12|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=79|verse=12|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַרְבַּעְתָּ֑יִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=6}};<ref>Probably also {{GHGheb|text=כִּפְלַ֫יִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=11|verse=6}} (from {{GHGheb|text=כֶּ֫פֶל|translate=doubling}}) does not mean ''doubled'' but ''manifold''.</ref> or periphrastically by {{GHGheb|text=פַּ֫עַם|translate=a time}} (prop. ''a step'', with the article, {{GHGheb|text=הַפַּ֫עַם|translate=this time}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=בַּפַּ֫עַם הַזֹּאת}}, with {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}}, like {{GHGheb|text=בְּאַחַת}} above), as {{GHGheb|text=פַּ֫עַם אַחַת|translate=once}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=13|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=פַּ֫עַם וּשְׁתַּ֫יִם|translate=once and twice}}), {{GHGheb|text=נַּֽעֲמַ֫יִם|translate=twice}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלשׁ פְּעָמִים}} (for which in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=28}}, 32 {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלשׁ רְגָלִים}}) ''three times''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=41|verse=6}} ''thirty-three times''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=24|verse=3}} ''an hundred times''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=11}} ''a thousand times''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=עַד־כַּמֶּה פְעָמִים|translate=until how many times}}, i.e. how often. Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=עֲשֶׂ֫רֶת מֹנִים|translate=ten times}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=17}}, 14, and {{GHGheb|text=רַבּוֹת עִתִּים|translate=many times}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=9|verse=28}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=34}}, ''five times'' is expressed by {{GHGheb|text=חָמֵשׁ יָדוֹת}} (prop. ''five hands''),<ref>But {{GHGheb|text=אַרְבַּע הַיָּדוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=24}} means ''the'' (other) ''four parts''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=11|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=11|verse=1}}.</ref> and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=5}} the ''double'' is expressed by {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁנֶה עַל־}} (prop. ''a repetition over and above that which'', &c.).—Of the ordinals {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁנִית}} is used as a numeral adverb, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=22|verse=15}}, &c., ''a second time'', cf. the Latin ''tertium consul''; {{GHGheb|text=בַּשְּׁלִישִׁת|translate=the third time}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=פַּ֫עַם חֲמִישִׁית|translate=a fifth time}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=6|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=בַּשְּׁבִעִית|translate=at the seventh}} (time), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=18|verse=44}}, and {{GHGheb|text=בַּפַּ֫עַם הַשּׁ׳}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=6|verse=16}}.
<section end=par134 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

461.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par134 />{{GHGmargin-letter|134|s}}
Rem. The collocation of a numeral with the next above it (either in the same or in different sentences) is a rhetorical device employed in ''numerical sayings'' to express a number, which need not, or cannot, be more exactly specified. It must be gathered from the context whether such formulae are intended to denote only an insignificant number (e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=6}}, ''two or'' at the most ''three''), or a considerable number, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=5|verse=4}}. Sometimes, however, this juxtaposition serves to express merely an indefinite total, without the collateral idea of intensifying the lower by means of the higher number. Thus ''one'' and ''two'' are connected by {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=33|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=40|verse=5|hidebook=1}} (without {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=62|verse=12}}); ''two'' and ''three'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=6}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Sirac|chapter=23|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Sirac|chapter=26|verse=28|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Sirac|chapter=50|verse=25|hidebook=1}}), and without {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=9|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=6|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=4|verse=8}}; ''three'' and ''four'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=36|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=1|verse=3}}–11, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=21|verse=29|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Sirac|chapter=26|verse=5}}), and with out {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=15}}; ''four'' and ''five'', without {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=6}}; ''six'' and ''seven'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=6|verse=16}}; ''seven'' and ''eight'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=5|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=11|verse=2}}; (''nine'' and ''ten'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Sirac|chapter=25|verse=7}}).<section end=par134 />

<section begin=par135 />{{center|III. Syntax of the Pronoun.}}

<!-- section begins above -->{{GHGpar-heading|135|The Personal Pronoun}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|a}}
'''1.''' The ''separate'' pronouns,—apart from their employment as the subject in noun-clauses (cf. {{GHGpar|141|a}}) and the idiom mentioned under ''d–h'', —are used, according to {{GHGpar|32|b}}, as a rule, only to give express emphasis to the subject; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=24|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=אָֽנֹכִי}} i.e. ''I myself'', so also {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=15|hidebook=1}} (after the verb), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=34|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=6}};<ref>Also {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִיא|translate=he himself, she herself}} (of persons and things), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנָי הוּא|translate=the Lord himself}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=9|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=הַיְּהוּדִים הֵ֫מָּה|translate=the Jews themselves}}. In the sense of ''the same'' (ὁ αὐτός) or (''one and'') ''the same'', {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} is used in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, 13, 46:4, 48:12 (always {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי הוּא}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=102|verse=28}} ({{GHGheb|text=אַתָּה הוּא}}), and probably also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=19}}.—The position of {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫מָּה}}, as an accusative of the object, before a perfect in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=9|verse=22}}, can at most be explained on the analogy of Aramaic ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=5|verse=12}}).</ref> but {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=10|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=45|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=אָֽנֹכִי|translate=I}} and none else; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי אֲנִי|translate=I, I!}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=5|verse=14}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=אַתָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=15|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=56}} (as in 20:8, 22:18, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=18|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=5|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=21}}, after the imperative); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַתֶּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=19}} (after the verb, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=15|verse=12}}); fem. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=22|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫מָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=5}}.—Sometimes, however, the separate pronoun appears to be placed before the verb more on rhythmical grounds, i.e. in order to give the statement a fuller sound than that of the bare verbal form (cf. the similar use of the infinitive absolute, {{GHGpar|113|o}}). Thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=2}}, and most clearly in such passages as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=30|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=8|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=12|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=21|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=18}} (in solemn promises). The same explanation applies to {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי}} at the beginning of sentences, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=45}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=5|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=10|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=12|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=39|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=82|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=3}}.<ref>As early as the Mêšaʿ inscription (line 21 ff.) {{GHGheb|text=אנך}} frequently stands at the beginning of a new sentence after the dividing stroke.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|b}}
Rem. 1. Different from this is the pleonastic addition of the separate pronoun immediately ''after'' the verb (according to Delitzsch on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=5|verse=5}} perhaps<section end=par135 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

462.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par135 />a trace of popular language), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=23|verse=22}}(?), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=5|verse=5}}, and (like other indications of the very late origin of the book) very frequently in Ecclesiastes, e.g. 1:16, 2:1, 11, 15, 3:17f. and thirteen other places; in Aramaic, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=5|verse=16}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|c}}
2. Substantival subjects also are somewhat frequently resumed, and thus expressly emphasized, by the insertion of the corresponding separate pronoun of the 3rd person before the predicate is stated, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=12}} ''the woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she'' ({{GHGheb|text=הִיא}}) ''gave me'', &c.; 14:24 ({{GHGheb|text=הֵם}}); 15:4, 24:7, &c.; but {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=14}} after the predicate and subject is equivalent to ''he himself''.<ref>Analogous to this is the resumption of a noun dependent on a preposition, by means of a pronominal suffix united with the same preposition, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=6|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=22|verse=18}}, or of an object by means of the {{GHGterm|nota accusativi}} {{GHGheb|text=את}} with suffix, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=9}} (where {{GHGheb|text=וְנִמְאֶ֫סֶת}} is certainly to be read), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=13}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|d}}
'''2.''' Not infrequently the separate pronoun serves to give strong emphasis to a suffix of the same person which precedes (or sometimes even to one which follows), whether the suffix be attached to a verb (as accusative) or to a noun or preposition (as genitive). In English such an emphasis on the pronoun can generally be rendered only by laying greater stress upon it, or sometimes by repeating it; cf., on the contrary, the French ''mon livre à moi''. The separate pronoun in such instances is not to be regarded as ''casus obliquus'' (accusative or genitive), but as the subject of an independent sentence, the predicate of which must in each case be supplied according to the context.

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|e}}
Examples of emphasis:—

(''a'') On a {{GHGterm|verbal}} suffix by means of {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי}} ({{GHGheb|text=אָ֫נִי}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=34}} {{GHGheb|text=בָּֽרֲכֵ֫נִי גַם־אָ֫נִי|translate=bless me, even me also}} (prop. ''bless me, I also'' would be blessed); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=7|verse=5}}; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=6|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=34|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, 20 {{GHGheb|text=הִנְנִי אָ֫נִי}}; by {{GHGheb|text=אַתָּה}} ({{GHGheb|text=אָ֫תָּה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=22|verse=19}} (but the text is most probably corrupt).—The separate pronoun ''precedes'' in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=27}} ({{GHGheb|text=אָֽנֹכִי}}); 49:8 ({{GHGheb|text=אַתָּה}}, not ''Judah, thou art he whom'', but ''Judah thee, thee thy brethren shall praise!''), and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=2|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=גַּם אֲנִי}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|f}}
(''b'') On a noun-suffix with a substantive, by means of {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=23|verse=15}}; by {{GHGheb|text=אָ֑תָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־דָּֽמְךָ גַּס־אָ֑תָּה|translate=thy blood, even thine}}; by {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=27|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=3}}; by {{GHGheb|text=אֲנַ֫חְנוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=42}}, after {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנֵ֫ינוּ}}, but without special stress; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=5|verse=2}} (?); by {{GHGheb|text=אַתֶּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=32}}; by {{GHGheb|text=הֵם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=38|verse=11}} (without special stress), {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫מָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=9|verse=7}}.—The separate pronoun ''precedes'' in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=4}} ({{GHGheb|text=אָֽנֹכִי}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=45|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=28|verse=2}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=9|verse=11}} ({{GHGheb|text=אַתְּ}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=23|verse=9}} ({{GHGheb|text=אַתֶּם}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=33|verse=17}} ({{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫מָּה}}).—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=89|verse=48}}, where {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי}} might be taken as strengthening {{GHGheb|text=חלד}} (equivalent in sense to {{GHGheb|text=חֶלְדִּי}}), we should read {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנָי}} for {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי}}, as in verse 51.

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|g}}
(''c'') On a suffix united with a preposition, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּי אֲנִי|translate=upon me, upon me}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=1|verse=26}} {{GHGheb|text=לִי... אֲנִי}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=35|verse=21}} {{GHGheb|text=לֹֹא־עָלֶ֫יךָ אַתָּה|translate=not against thee}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=23}} {{GHGheb|text=עָלָיו גַּם הוּא|translate=upon him also}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=5|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=כִּי אִתָּנוּ אֲנַ֫חְנוּ|translate=but with us, even us}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=1|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=לָכֶם אַתֶּם|translate=for you yourselves}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=25|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=בָּם גַּם־הֵ֫מָּה}}.—The separate pronoun precedes in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=12|verse=23}} {{GHGheb|text=אָֽנֹכִי... לִי}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=1|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=אַתָּה... עָלֶ֫יךָ}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=5|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=אַתָּה... מִמְּךָ}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=28|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=אַתֶּם עִמָּכֶם}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|h}}
The same principle also explains {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=26}} {{GHGheb|text=לְשֵׁת גַּם־הוּא|translate=to Seth, to him also}} (not {{GHGheb|text=גַּם־לוֹ}}); cf. 10:21, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=35|verse=34}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=4|verse=22}}.
<section end=par135 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

463.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par135 />{{GHGmargin-letter|135|i}}
'''3.''' The ''oblique'' cases of the personal pronouns expressed by means of a preposition (or the ''nots accus.'' {{GHGheb|text=את}}) with a suffix may be used either in a demonstrative or reflexive sense,<ref>As in Luther’s Bible ''jm'' (''ihm''), ''jr'' (''ihr'') for ''sich'', and in our version ''him, her'' for ''himself, herself''.</ref> as {{GHGheb|text=לוֹ|translate=to him}}, but also ''to himself'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=3|verse=16}} ''and Ehud made'' {{GHGheb|text=לוֹ|translate=for himself a sword}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=17}}; so also {{GHGheb|text=לָהֶם|translate=sibi}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֵלָיו|translate=unto him}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=9}} ''unto himself''; {{GHGheb|text=אִתּוֹ|translate=with him}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=22|verse=3}} ''with himself''; {{GHGheb|text=עִמָּהּ|translate=with her}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=24}} ''with herself''; also apparently as a pleonastic ''dativus ethicus'' (see {{GHGpar|119|s}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=12|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=1|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|k}}
Rarely, and only when marked emphasis is intended, is the ''accusative'' of the reflexive pronoun represented by the {{GHGterm|nota accusativi}} {{GHGheb|text=את}} with a suffix (this being ordinarily expressed by the reflexive conjugations {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} and {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}}<ref>{{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} according to {{GHGpar|51|e}} (like {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} according to {{GHGpar|54|f}}) may also include the ''dative'' of the reflexive pronoun.</ref>); thus, {{GHGheb|text=אֹתָם|translate=se ipsos}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=5|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=7|verse=19}} in sharp antithesis to {{GHGheb|text=הַֽאֹתִי}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=34|verse=2}}, 8, 10. Cf. § 57 at the end, together with note 2.

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|l}}
Rem. There is a similar emphasis in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=26}} on {{GHGheb|text=בְּשָׂרָם}} and {{GHGheb|text=דָּמָם}} in the sense of ''their own flesh, their own blood''. On the sometimes demonstrative, sometimes reflexive meaning of noun-suffixes of the 3rd person singular and plural, cf. § 91, p and q. For other circumlocutions to express the idea of ''self'', see {{GHGpar|139|f}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|m}}
'''4.''' The ''possessive pronouns'' are, according to {{GHGpar|33|c}}, expressed by the ''suffixes of the noun'' (in the genitive),<ref>Like the substantival genitive, according to {{GHGpar|129|h}}, the possessive pronoun may also be paraphrased by a relative clause, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=21}} {{GHGheb|text=הַנְּעָרִים אֲשֶׁר לִי|translate=the young men, which}} are ''to me'', i.e. ''my young men''; so especially, when the substantive, which should take a genitive suffix, is already followed by a genitive, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=40}}. In this case, however, the suffix also is sometimes attached pleonastically, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=כַּרְמִי שֶׁלִּי|translate=my vineyard, which}} belongs ''to me.'' Cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=3|verse=7}}, and the analogous pleonasms in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=22|verse=2}} (but see {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=2}}) and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=27|verse=2}}.</ref> which may represent either a ''subjective genitive'', or (like the genitives proper, {{GHGpar|128|h}}) an ''objective genitive'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חֲמָסִי|translate=the wrong done against me}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=51|verse=35}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=21|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=13|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=16|verse=12}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=21|hidebook=1}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=21}}, &c.); 50:4, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=35|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=12|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=מַֽעֲשֵׂ֫הוּ|translate=the treatment of him}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=56|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=20|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=23|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=6|hidebook=1}}. Cf. also such pregnant expressions as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=20|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁלַח עֶזְרְךָ|translate=he will send thy help}} (''help for thee''), i.e. he will send thee help; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=21|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=26}} (''and I will restore judges for thee''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=37|verse=15}}.

When several substantives are co-ordinated, the pronominal suffix must be attached to each singly, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=36|verse=6}} ''and Esau took'' {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־נָשָׁיו וְאֶת־בָּנָיו וְאֶת־ בְּנֹתָיו|translate=his wives and his sons and his daughters}}, &c.; 38:18, &c. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=23|verse=5}} the text is hardly correct.<section end=par135 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

464.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par135" />{{GHGmargin-letter|135|n}}
'''5.''' When the genitive, following a construct state, is used periphrastically to express the idea of a material or attribute ({{GHGpar|128|o}} and p), the pronominal suffix, which properly belongs to the compound idea (represented by the {{GHGterm|nomen regens}} and genitive), is, like the article (§ 127), attached to the second substantive (the genitive), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַר־קָדְשִׁי}} prop. ''the hill of my holiness'', i.e. my holy hill, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=6}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=עִיר קָדְשְׁךָ|translate=thy holy city}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=9|verse=24}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֱלִילֵי כַסְפּוֹ|translate=his idols of silver}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=2|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=31|verse=7|hidebook=1}};<ref>On the other hand, more explicitly in prose, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־גְּבִיעִי גְבִיעַ הַכֶּ֫כֶף|translate=my cup, the silver cup}}.</ref> cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=41}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=9|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=9|verse=1}}f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=41|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=150|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=18|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=צַֽעֲדֵי אוֹנוֹ|translate=his steps of strength}}; 38:6; after an adjective as {{GHGterm|nomen regens}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=13|verse=3}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=3|verse=11}}) {{GHGheb|text=עַלִּיזֵי גַֽאֲוָתִי|translate=my proudly exulting ones}}.—On the same analogy is the use of e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כְּלֵי מִלְחַמְתּוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=41}} ''his weapons of war'' [cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=12}}]; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=56|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=בֵּית תְּפִלָּתִי|translate=my house of prayer}}, although the genitive here does not convey the idea of an attribute.

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|o}}
Rem. 1. Through a weakening in the distinction of gender, which is noticeable elsewhere (cf. {{GHGpar|110|k}}, 144 a, 145 p, t, u) and which probably passed from the colloquial language<ref>According to Diehl (see the title at the head of {{GHGpar|91|a}}), who adduces numerous instances on pp. 44 ff., 54 ff., 67 f., many of these cases may be set down to corruption of the traditional text, while the sudden (and sometimes repeated) change of gender in suffixes is mainly due to the influence exercised on the copyists by the Mishnic and popular Aramaic dialects, neither of which recognizes such distinctions. Such influence, however, is insufficient to explain the large number of instances of this weakening, occurring even in the earlier documents.</ref> into that of literature, ''masculine'' suffixes (especially in the plural) are not infrequently used to refer to ''feminine'' substantives; thus a noun-suffix in the singular, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=11|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=25|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=34}};<ref>The Masora reckons six instances of {{GHGheb|text=מִמֶּ֫נּוּ}}, where {{GHGheb|text=מִמֶּ֫נָּה}} would be expected ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=34}}, where, however, the text is most probably corrupt), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=25|verse=15}} (?), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=6|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=7|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=27|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=1|verse=7}}; almost all these passages can, however, be easily explained in other ways.</ref> in the plural, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=23|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=27|verse=7}} (but the feminine suffix twice immediately after, and so the Samaritan also in verse 7); 36:6 (Samaritan {{GHGheb|text=אֲבִיהֶן}}, but also {{GHGheb|text=בְּעֵֽינֵיהֶם}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=21|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=7}}, 10b ({{GHGheb|text=בְּנֵיהֶם}}); 9:20, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=23|verse=45}} ff. (alternating with {{GHGheb|text=הֶן}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=4|verse=1}} f. (but afterwards a feminine suffix); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=39|verse=3|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=חֶבְלֵיהֶם}} in parallelism with {{GHGheb|text=יַלְדֵיהֶן}}); 42:15, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=4|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=6|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=1|verse=8}} ff. (along with feminine suffixes); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=1|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=8|verse=9|hidebook=1}}. Verbal suffixes in the singular, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=22|verse=25}}; in the plural, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=6|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=15}}. But {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=15}}, 18, 33:13, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=10}}<sup> ''a''</sup> are to be explained according to {{GHGpar|60|h}}. On {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫מָּה}} as feminine, see {{GHGpar|32|n}}. On the use of the masculine in general as the ''prior gender'', see {{GHGpar|122|g}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|p}}
2. The suffix of the 3rd person singular feminine (as also the separate pronoun {{GHGheb|text=הִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=41}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=10|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=4}}) sometimes refers in a general sense to the verbal idea contained in a preceding sentence (corresponding to our ''it''); thus the verbal suffix, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=11|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=8|verse=10}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=14}} ({{GHGheb|text=בָּהּ|translate=thereby}}), 42:36, 47:26, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=11}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֹתָהּ|translate=that}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=7}}. Elsewhere the suffix of the 3rd singular feminine refers to the plurals of things, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=3|verse=3}}<section end="par135" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

465.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par135 />[but see Kittel; so 13:2, 6, 11; 10:26, but LXX {{GHGheb|text=מַצִּבַת}}], {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=36|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=20}} (if the text is correct), 39:15 (read {{GHGheb|text=תֵּחָמֵם}} in v. 14), and to the plurals of names of animals, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=35|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=11|verse=5}}. Conversely, plural suffixes refer to collective singulars, e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=16|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=2|verse=7}} [but read {{GHGheb|text=עַל הַיָּם}}]; and to a verbal idea contained in the preceding clause, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=33|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=21}} ({{GHGheb|text=בָּהֶם|translate=thereby}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=18|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=33|verse=19|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=עֲלֵיהֶם|translate=on that account, thereby}}).<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=7|verse=10}} for {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁעֵר}} (the LXX had {{GHGheb|text=שַׁ֫עַר}}) read {{GHGheb|text=שֹֽׁעֲרֵי}}.</ref> But the suffix in {{GHGheb|text=נְתָנוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=21|verse=10}} refers to the collective idea contained in {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽיְבָ֫יךָ}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jon|chapter=1|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=עִמָּהֶם}} refers to the sailors included in sense under the term {{GHGheb|text=אֳנִיָּה}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=4}} read {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּצְפְּנֵם}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=6}} ({{GHGheb|text=מֵהֶם}}), 38:16, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=19|verse=5}} ({{GHGheb|text=בָּהֶם}}) the text is most probably corrupt.

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|q}}
3. In a few examples the force of the noun-suffix or possessive pronoun has become so weak that the language appears to be almost entirely unconscious of it. Thus in {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנָי|translate=my Lord}}, usually explained as being from the ''pluralis maiestatis'' {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנִים}} ({{GHGpar|124|i}}) with the suffix of the 1st singular (always with {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} to distinguish it from {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנַי|translate=my lords}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=2}}; but see note below), used exclusively of God, not only in addressing him ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=23}}), but ultimately (see, however, the note below), without any regard to the pronoun, as equivalent to ''the Lord''.<ref>Cf. the same weakening of the force of the possessive pronoun in {{GHGheb|text=רַבִּי}} prop. ''my master'', from the second century {{smaller|A.D.}} onwards ''the master''; so also in Syriac {{GHGheb|text=מרי|translate=my lord}}, and ultimately as a title ''the lord''; in Italian ''Madonna'', French ''Madame, Notre Dame, Monsieur, Monseigneur'', &c. It can, however, hardly be doubted that the regular distinction between {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנָי}} as a holy name, and {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנִי}} as an ordinary appellative is merely due to the practice of the later Rabbis. G. H. Dalman, ''Der Gottesname Adonaj und seine Geschichte'' (Berlin, 1889), in an exhaustive discussion, shows that apart from the book of Daniel and the eight critically doubtful passages, in which {{GHGheb|text=אדני}} is used by God himself, there is nowhere any necessity to regard the suffix as ''entirely'' meaningless, since {{GHGheb|text=אדני}} is always used either in an address ''to'' or (like {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנִי}}, which also is never a mere phrase or title) in reverent language ''about'' God—as the Lord of the speaker—like the Assyrian ''bēli-ia'', ''my lord''. Against any original distinction between {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנָי}} and {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנִי}} it may be urged especially that when unconnected with suffixes the singular {{GHGheb|text=אָדוֹן}} is always used of God, and not the ''pluralis maiestatis'' presupposed by {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנָי}}.</ref> On {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנָי}} as a ''Q<sup>e</sup>rê perpetuum'' of the Masoretes for {{GHGheb|text=יהוה}} see {{GHGpar|17|c}} and {{GHGpar|102|m}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|r}}
A similar loss of vitality in the suffix is generally assumed in {{GHGheb|text=יַחְדָּו}} prop. ''in his unitedness'', i.e. ''he'' &c. ''together'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־הָעָם יַחְדָּו}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=19|verse=8}}; then, without regard to the suffix, even after the 1st person {{GHGheb|text=אֲנַ֫חְנוּ יַחְדָּו}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=3|verse=18}} in reference to two women; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=6|verse=2}}, 7; after the 2nd person, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=45|verse=20}}, &c. But the supposed pronominal suffix is perhaps rather to be explained, with Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZA.|Zeitschrift für Assyriologie und verwandte Gebiete, ed. by C. Bezold. Lpz. 18S6 ff.}}}} xiv. 344 f., as an old adverbial ending, which survives in the Arabic adverbs in ''u'' and in Assyrian.—Cf. further {{GHGheb|text=כֻּלָּם}} prop. ''their entirety'', but also after the 2nd person equivalent to ''all together'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=1|verse=2}} (''hear, ye peoples, all of you''; cf. {{GHGpar|144|p}}), and even before the 2nd person, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=17|verse=10}} (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=4}} read {{GHGheb|text=לָכֶם}} with the LXX).—On the redundant suffix in {{GHGheb|text=הָֽעֶרְכְּךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=27|verse=23}}, cf. {{GHGpar|127|i}}.<section end=par135 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

466.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Ubufox" /></noinclude><section begin=par136 />{{GHGpar-heading|136|The Demonstrative Pronoun}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|136|a}}
The ''demonstrative pronouns'' are {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=זֹאת}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫לֶּה}} (§ 34), ''hic, haec'' (''hoc''), ''hi'', &c., and the personal pronoun {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}}, likewise used as a demonstrative, fem. {{GHGheb|text=הִיא}}, plur. masc. {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫מָּה}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫נָּה}} ({{GHGpar|32|b}}), ''is'', ''ea'' (''id''), or ''ille'', &c., ''ii'', ''eae'' or ''illi'', &c. The distinction between them in usage is that {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} (like ''hic'', ὅδε) almost always points out a (new) person or thing present, while {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} (like ''is'', ''ille'', αὐτός, ἐκεῖνος) refers to a person or thing already mentioned or known (see the examples below).<ref>On {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} and {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} standing separately as determinate in themselves, see {{GHGpar|125|i}}. On the use of determinate demonstratives as adjectives, see {{GHGpar|126|u}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|136|b}}
Rem. 1. Compare the instructive examples in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=7|verse=4}} ''of whom I say unto thee, this'' ({{GHGheb|text=זֶה}}) ''shall go with thee, he'' ({{GHGheb|text=הוּא}}) ''shall go with thee'' (so afterwards with negatives). Moreover, {{GHGheb|text=הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה|translate=this day}}, i.e. the actual day on which one is speaking or writing ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=33}}, &c.), but {{GHGheb|text=הַיּוֹם הַהוּא}} the day or period of which the historian has just been speaking ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=32|hidebook=1}}) or of which the prophet has just been foretelling ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, 20 ff.) and of which he continues to speak or foretell. Nevertheless {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} and {{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫לֶּה}} are also found in certain common combinations where {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} and {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫מָּה}} would be expected, and vice versa; thus almost always {{GHGheb|text=הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵ֫לֶּה}}, but {{GHGheb|text=בַּיָּמִים הָהֵ֫מָּה}} or {{GHGheb|text=בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם}}—With a secondary sense of contempt (like Latin ''iste'') {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} occurs, e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=10|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=10}}, &c. In the sense of the neuter, ''this'', {{GHGheb|text=זֹאת}} is more common than {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}}, as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, &c., but {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} more common than {{GHGheb|text=הִיא}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|136|c}}
2. Both {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} and {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} are sometimes used almost as enclitics to emphasize interrogative words (like the Latin ''nam'' in ''quisnam''; cf. also ''quis tandem''); e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=מִי זֶה|translate=who now}} (darkeneth, &c.)...? {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=55}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=63|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=24|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=25|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, &c; {{GHGheb|text=מַה־זֶּה|translate=what now?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=10|verse=11}}; ''how now?'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=20}}; ''why now?'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=18|verse=24}}; but before the verb {{GHGheb|text=עָשָׂה}} it is usually {{GHGheb|text=מַה־זֹּאת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=14|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=15|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=לָ֫מָּה־זֶּה|translate=wherefore now?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=25|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=23}}, &c.—So also {{GHGheb|text=מִי־הוּא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=50|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=7}} ff.; and still more emphatically {{GHGheb|text=מִי הוּא־זֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=24|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=30|verse=21}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|136|d}}
3. {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} is likewise used as an enclitic (see c above): (''a'') ''of place'', in such passages as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=21}} {{GHGheb|text=הַֽאַתָּה זֶה וגו׳|translate=whether thou}} (that art here) ''be my son Esau?'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=20}} ''is it thou?'' {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה־זֶה|translate=behold, here}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=19|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=9}};<ref>On the other hand, it is very questionable whether {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=25}} ({{GHGheb|text=זֶה הַיָּם}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=13}} ({{GHGheb|text=זֶה הָעָם}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=9}} ({{GHGheb|text=זֶה סִינַי}}) can be taken, according to the common explanation, simply as a prefixed demonstrative particle (''the sea yonder'', &c.). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=25}} {{GHGheb|text=הַיָּם}} may be in apposition to {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}}; cf. § 126 aa, on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=1}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=5|verse=7}}, where {{GHGheb|text=אִשָּׁה אַחַת}} is in apposition to {{GHGheb|text=זֹאת}} depending on {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה}}, and also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=40|verse=45}}, where {{GHGheb|text=הַלִּשְׁכָּה}} is in apposition to {{GHGheb|text=זֹה}}; otherwise it is most naturally taken as the subject, ''this is the sea''. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=14}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=9}} might also be explained in the same way; but in these passages the text is almost certainly corrupt. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=5}} in fact {{GHGheb|text=זֶה סִינַי}} is most probably to be regarded with Moore as a very early gloss, which subsequently found its way from this passage into Ps 68.</ref> cf. also the strengthen-<section end=par136 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

467.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par136 />ing of the separate pronoun by {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=25}} ({{GHGheb|text=אָֽנׄכֹי}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=7|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=44|verse=5}} ({{GHGheb|text=אַתָּה}}), and {{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫לֶּה הֵם|translate=these are}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=25|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=8}}; (''b'') ''of time'': {{GHGheb|text=עַתָּה זֶה|translate=now}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=17|verse=24}}; ''just now'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=22}}; and rather frequently before words denoting number, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=36}} {{GHGheb|text=זֶה פַֽעֲמַ֫יִם|translate=twice, now}}; cf. 31:38, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=3|hidebook=1}}; separated from the numeral in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=41}} {{GHGheb|text=זֶה־לִּי}} elliptically for ''this'', i.e. this present period, ''is to me'', i.e. makes altogether, ''twenty years'', &c. The other examples are similarly elliptical.<section end=par136 />

<section begin=par137 />{{GHGpar-heading|137|The Interrogative Pronouns}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|137|a}}
The interrogative pronoun {{GHGheb|text=מִי|translate=who}} may refer either to a masculine or feminine person ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=3|verse=6}}), or even to a plural, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מִי אַתֶּם|translate=who are ye?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=9|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=מִי־אֵ֫לֶּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=9}} (more minutely, {{GHGheb|text=מִי וָמִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=8}}, i.e. ''who exactly, who in particular?''). It is used of the neuter only when the idea of a person is implied, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מִֽי־שְׁכֶם|translate=who are the Shechemites?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=1|verse=5}}; even more boldly, with the repetition of a {{GHGheb|text=מִי}} used personally, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=7|verse=18}}.—Another interrogative is {{GHGheb|text=אֵי־זֶה|translate=which, what?}}; of persons only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=7|verse=5}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|137|b}}
Moreover, {{GHGheb|text=מִי}} may also be used in the sense of a genitive, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בַּת־מִי אַתְּ|translate=whose daughter art thou?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=55}}, 56, 58; {{GHGheb|text=דְּבַר מִי|translate=whose word?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=44|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=12|verse=3}}; in the accusative, {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־מִי|translate=quemnam?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=8}}; with prepositions, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בְּמִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=14}} (in an abrupt question ''by whom?''); {{GHGheb|text=לְמִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַֽחֲרֵי מִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=24|verse=15}}.—Similarly {{GHGheb|text=מָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַה־}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֶה|translate=what?}} is used for the nominative, or accusative, or genitive ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=8|verse=9}}), or with prepositions, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עַל־מָה|translate=whereupon?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=6}}; ''why?'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=32}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=עַד־מָה|translate=quousque?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=74|verse=9}}.<ref>A quite different use of {{GHGheb|text=מָה}} was pointed out (privately) by P. Haupt in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=5|verse=8}} ''will ye not tell him?'' i.e. ''I charge you that ye tell him'', and 7:1 = ''look now at the Shulamite'', corresponding to the late Arabic ''mâ tarâ'', ''just see! mâ taqûlu'', ''say now!'' It has long been recognized that {{GHGheb|text=מָה}} is used as a negative in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=8|verse=4}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|137|c}}
Rem. Both {{GHGheb|text=מִי}} and {{GHGheb|text=מָה}} are used also in indirect questions (on the merely relative distinction between direct and indirect questions in Hebrew, see the ''Interrogative Sentences''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=8}} (but read {{GHGheb|text=מְא֫וּמָה}} with Samar. and LXX), 43:22, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=1}}.—On the meaning of {{GHGheb|text=מִי}} and {{GHGheb|text=מָה}} as interrogatives is based also their use as ''indefinite pronouns'' (equivalent to ''quisquis, quodcunque'' or ''quicquam''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=7|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=50|verse=10}} (read {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁמַע}} in the apodosis), 54:15, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=9|verse=4}}, 16, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=36|verse=23}}; even {{GHGheb|text=שִׁמְרוּ־מִי|translate=have a care, whosoever ye be}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=12}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=לִי}} is to be read, with the LXX, for {{GHGheb|text=מִי}}); so also {{GHGheb|text=מָה}} (''whatever it be'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=22}}, 23; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=וּדְבַר מַה־יַּרְאֵ֫נִי|translate=and whatsoever he showeth me}}. Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=מִי אֲשֶׁר|translate=whosoever}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=11}}, and {{GHGheb|text=מִֽי־הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר|translate=any man who}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=20|verse=5}} ff.,<section end=par137 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

468.text:
{{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=10|verse=18}}. A still further weakening of the ''indefinite'' use of {{GHGheb|text=מָה}} is the combination {{GHGheb|text=מַה־שֶּׁ·|translate=that which}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=1|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=3|verse=15|hidebook=1}} (just like the Syriac {{GHGheb|text=מָא דְ}}); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=8|verse=1}}, and {{GHGheb|text=בַּל... מָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=9|verse=13}}, {{GHGheb|text=לֹא... מָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=2|verse=12}}, ''nothing whatever''.—On {{GHGheb|text=מְא֫וּמָה|translate=quicquam}}, ''anything at all'' (usually with a negative), and as an adverb ''in any way'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=3}}, see the Lexicon.
{{GHGpar-heading|138|The Relative Pronoun}}
Cf. Philippi, ''Stat. constr.'' (see heading of § 89), p. 71 f., and especially V. Baumann, {{GHGcite|title=Hebräische Relativsätze}}, Leipzig, 1894.
{{GHGmargin-letter|138|a}} Relative clauses are most frequently (but not necessarily; cf. {{GHGpar|155|b}}) introduced by the indeclinable {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} (see § 36).The etymology of the word is still a matter of dispute. Against the identification of {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}}, as an original substantive, with the Arabic ''‛at̄ar'', ''trace'', Aram. {{GHGheb|text=אֲתַר|translate=place, trace}}, Nöldeke urges ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} xl. 738) that the expression ''trace of''... could hardly have developed into the relative conjunction, while the meaning of ''place'' has been evolved only in Aramaic, where the word is never used as a relative. According to others, {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} is really a compound of several pronominal roots; cf. Sperling, ''Die Nota relationis im Hebräischen'', Leipzig, 1876, and König, {{GHGcite|title=Lehrgeb.}}, ii. 323 ff., who follows Ewald and Böttcher in referring it to an original {{GHGheb|text=אֲשַׁל}}. According to Hommel ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} xxxii. 708 ff.) {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} is an original substantive, to be distinguished from {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ·}} and {{GHGheb|text=שַׁ·}} (an original pronominal stem), but used in Hebrew as a ''nota relationis'', or (as {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} and {{GHGheb|text=זוּ}} are also sometimes used, see below, g and h) simply for the ''relative pronoun''. Baumann (op. cit., p. 44) sees in the Assyrian ''ša'', Phoenician, Punic, and Hebrew {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ}}, the ground-forms, of which the Phoenician and Punic {{GHGheb|text=אש}} (see above, § 36 note) and the Hebrew {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} are developments. This is not, however, a relative pronoun in the Greek, Latin, or English sense, nor is it a mere ''nota relationis'',E.g. like Luther’s use of ''so'', in ''die fremden Götter, so unter euch sind'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=35|verse=2}}. but an original ''demonstrative'' pronoun [as though ''iste, istius'', &c.].This is the necessary conclusion both from the analogy of the Arabic ''ʾallad-i'', which is clearly a demonstrative (like the Hebr. {{GHGheb|text=הַלָּז}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַלָּזֶה}}), and from the use of {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} and {{GHGheb|text=זוּ}} as relatives. Hence it is used— (1) In immediate dependence on the substantival idea to be defined, and virtually in the same case as it (hence belonging syntactically to the main clause); e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=7}}... {{GHGheb|text=יְהֹוָה אֲשֶׁר לְקָחַ֫נִי... הוּא יִשְׁלַח|translate=the Lord, iste, he took me}}... ''he shall send'', &c. (= ''who took me''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=2}} ''and God finished'' {{GHGheb|text=מְלַאכְתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה|translate=his work, istud, he had made}} (it). Such qualifying clauses may be called ''dependent relative clauses''. {{GHGmargin-letter|138|b}} Rem. 1. In the above examples {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=7}} is virtually in the nominative, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=2}} in the accusative. A further distinction between the examples is that in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=7}} the main idea ({{GHGheb|text=יהוה}}), to which {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} is added in apposition, is only resumed in the qualifying clause by the subject (''he'') inherent in

469.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par138 />{{GHGheb|text=לְקָחַ֫נִי}}, while in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=2}} it is not resumed at all. This suppression of the retrospective pronoun<ref>The instances in which, instead of a retrospective pronoun, the main idea itself is repeated ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=50|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=32}}) are most probably all due to subsequent amplification of the original text by another hand.</ref> takes place especially when it (as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=2}}) would represent an accusative of the object, or when it would be a separate pronoun representing a nominative of the subject in a noun-clause, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=הַמַּ֫יִם אֲשֶׁר מִתַּחַת לָֽרָקִיעַ|translate=the waters, those, under the firmament}}, &c. In negative sentences, however, the retrospective pronoun is not infrequently added, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}}; 7:2 {{GHGheb|text=הִיא}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=9|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫מָּה}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=20|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫נָּה}}; but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר הוּא חַי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=3}}. The addition of {{GHGheb|text=הִיא}} in a verbal clause, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=22|verse=13}}, is unusual.

The very frequent omission of the retrospective pronoun is noticeable in cases where the predicate of the qualifying clause is a {{GHGterm|verbum dicendi}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=10|verse=29}} ''we are journeying unto the place'', {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר אָמַר יָהוָֹה אֹתוֹ אֶתֵּן לָכֶם|translate=that}} place, ''the Lord said'' (of it), ''It will I give to you''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=40}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=17}}, 23, 24:5, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=32|verse=43}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|138|c}}
2. When the substantive, followed by {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} and the qualifying clause, expresses an idea of ''place'', it may also be resumed by the adverbs of place {{GHGheb|text=שָׁם|translate=there}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁ֫מָּה|translate=thither}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִשָּׁם|translate=thence}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=13|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר־הָיָה שָׁם אָֽהֳלֹה עַד־הַמָּקוֹם|translate=unto the place, that one, his tent had been there}}, i.e. ''where his tent had been''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=23}} {{GHGheb|text=מִשָּׁם}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=שָׁ֫מָּה}}. But even in this case the retrospective word may be omitted, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=35|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=20|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=64|verse=10}}, where {{GHGheb|text=שָׁם}} would be expected, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=38}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=13|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=12|verse=2}}, where {{GHGheb|text=שָׁ֫מָּה}} would be expected.—When the appositional clause is added to a word of time, the retrospective pronoun is always omitted, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=31}} ''for all the days'', {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר בֶּן־יִשַׁי חַי}} ''those—the son of Jesse is living'' (''in them''); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=45|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=46}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=9|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=42}}; see Baumann, op. cit., p. 33.

{{GHGmargin-letter|138|d}}
3. If the governing substantive forms part of a statement made in the first or second person, the retrospective pronoun (or the subject of the appositional clause) is in the same person, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=45|verse=4}} ''I am Joseph'', {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר־מְכַרְתֶּם אֹתִי}} ''he—ye sold me'', i.e. ''whom ye sold''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=23}}; 41:8 ''thou, Jacob'', {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר בְּחַרְתִּ֫יךָ}} ''he—I have chosen thee''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=33|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=10|verse=16}} f.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=7}} ''I am the Lord'', {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר הֽוֹצֵאתִ֫יךָ}} ''he—I brought thee out'', &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=2}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=5|verse=6}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|138|e}}
(2) Not depending (adjectivally) on a governing substantive, but itself expressing a substantival idea. Clauses introduced in this way may be called ''independent relative clauses''. This use of {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} is generally rendered in English by ''he who, he whom'', &c. (according to the context), or ''that which'', &c., or sometimes ''of such a kind as'' (''qualis''), cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=14|verse=13}} b, and in a dependent relative clause {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=17}}. In reality, however, the {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} is still a demonstrative belonging to the construction of the main clause as subject or object, or as a genitive dependent on a noun or preposition, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר תָּאֹר יוּאָר}} ''iste—thou cursest'' (him)—''is cursed'', i.e. ''he whom thou cursest'', &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=22|verse=8}};<ref>The absolute use of {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} is very peculiar in the formula {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר הָיָה דְבַר יי׳ אֶל־|translate=this}} (is it)—''it came as the word of the Lord to''..., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=14|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=46|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=47|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=34|hidebook=1}}.</ref> {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} as object, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=1}},<section end=par138 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

470.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="BerdeGaraiko" /></noinclude><section begin="par138" />49:1, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=3}} ff., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=6|verse=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֵת אֲשֶׁר}}); and even preceding the verb, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=52|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=69|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} as genitive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=23|verse=28}} ''I will deliver thee'' {{GHGheb|text=בְּיַד אֲשֶׁר שָׂנֵאת}} ''into the hand of those—thou hatest'' (them); depending on a preposition, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לַֽאֲשֶׁר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=10|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽאֲשֶׁר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=17}}, {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽאֲשֶׁר הוּא שָׁם|translate=in that}} (place)—''he is there'', i.e. ''where he is''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=17|verse=8}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=1|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־אֲשֶׁר|translate=whither}};<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=12|verse=10}} also, instead of the unintelligible {{GHGheb|text=אלי את אשר}}, we should probably read {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־אֲשֶׁר}}, and refer the passage to this class.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=18|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=עַל־אֲשֶׁר|translate=whither}}; {{GHGheb|text=מֵֽאֲשֶׁר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=5|verse=11}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|138|f}}
From these examples it follows that in independent relative clauses the retrospective suffix, or adverb of place, may be, and in fact generally is, omitted. As a rule, however (as in the dependent relative clause), this does not apply to eases in which the retrospective pronoun, by the construction of the sentence, depends on a preposition,<ref>Such a strong ellipse as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=31|verse=6}}, where {{GHGheb|text=מִמֶּ֫נּוּ}} would be expected after {{GHGheb|text=העמיקו}}, is only possible in elevated poetic or prophetic language.</ref> e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=9}} f. {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר יִמָּצֵא אִתּוֹ... וָמֵת}} ''he—it'' (the cup) ''is found with him,—shall die'' (for the {{GHGterm|Wāw}} of the apodosis in {{GHGheb|text=וָמֵת}} cf. {{GHGpar|143|d}}). In such cases {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} preceded by the preposition is quite anomalous, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=32}} {{GHGheb|text=עִם אֲשֶׁר תִּמְצָא|translate=with whomsoever thou findest}}, where {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} is a relative pronoun in the English sense; on the other hand, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=12}} (and probably also 56:4) {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽאֲשֶׁר}} is to be explained (with Baumann, op. cit., p. 37) by reference to 47:15, as a demonstrative pronoun, ''stand now with thine enchantments..., with those—thou hast laboured'' (with them).

[With regard to the preceding explanation of {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}}, the student will of course understand that, in Hebrew as we know it, {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} never occurs as a mere demonstrative. A particle which, whatever its origin, is uniformly used with reference to something in another, contiguous clause, will naturally have acquired in practice that force which we denote by the term ‘relative’.]

{{GHGmargin-letter|138|g}}
Like the original demonstrative pronoun {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}}, the demonstratives proper {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}}, {{GHGheb|text=זוֹ}}, {{GHGheb|text=זוּ}} (the last commonly),<ref>The etymological equivalent {{GHGheb|text=דִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=דְּ}} in Aramaic is always a relative.</ref> and sometimes the article, are used somewhat frequently in poetic language to introduce both dependent and independent relative clauses. With regard to the construction of {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}}, &c., the remarks on {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}}, under ''a'' and ''e'', also hold good.

Examples:—

(''a'') {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} in apposition to a governing substantive in the nominative, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=26}} {{GHGheb|text=לִוְיָתָן זֶה־יָצַ֫רְתָּ}} (there is) ''leviathan, he—thou hast formed'' (him), i.e. ''whom thou hast formed''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=24}} ({{GHGheb|text=זוּ}}); in the accusative, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=25|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=74|verse=2}} (in both eases with a retrospective pronoun; {{GHGheb|text=זוֹ}} is used without it in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=132|verse=12}}); in apposition to a genitive dependent on a preposition, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=23|verse=22}} {{GHGheb|text=שְׁמַע לְאָבִ֫יךָ זֶה יְלָדֶ֑ךָ}} ''hearken unto thy father, him—he begat thee'', i.e. ''who begat thee''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=17|verse=9}} ({{GHGheb|text=זוּ}}).—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־מְקוֹם זֶה יָסַ֫דְתָּ לָהֶם|translate=unto the place which thou hadst founded for them}} (cf. {{GHGpar|130|c}}), {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} is in the genitive after the construct state {{GHGheb|text=מְקוֹם|translate=to the place of that, thou hadst}}<section end="par138" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

471.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="DjR" /></noinclude><section begin="par138" />''founded'' (it) ''for them''; on the same analogy we may also take, with Baumann (op. cit., p. 48), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=78|verse=54}}, ({{GHGheb|text=חַר זֶה}}) and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=13}} ({{GHGheb|text=עַם־זוּ גָאָ֑לְתָּ}}), 15:16, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=9|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=10|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=31|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=32|verse=8|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=62|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=142|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=143|verse=8|hidebook=1}} (all examples of {{GHGheb|text=זוּ}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|138|h}}
To introduce independent relative clauses {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} is used as a nominative in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=19}}; as accusative, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=17}} and {{GHGheb|text=זוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=1|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=29}} (after a preposition, {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=13|verse=8}}; but the text is evidently corrupt).

{{GHGmargin-letter|138|i}}
(''b'') More certain examples of the use of the article as a relative pronoun (more correctly, perhaps, of the demonstrative which is otherwise used as article) are {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=26|verse=28}} {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל הַֽהִקְדִּישׁ שְׁמוּאֵל|translate=all that Samuel had dedicated}}, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=29|verse=8}} (where {{GHGheb|text=נִמְצָא}} can only be {{GHGterm|perfect Niphʿal}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=29|verse=36}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=10|verse=14}}. In connexion with a plural, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=10|verse=24}} ''the chiefs of the men of war'' {{GHGheb|text=הֶהָֽלְכוּ אִתּוֹ|translate=who went with him}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=8|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=10|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=29|verse=17}}. Finally, in the sense of ''id quod'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=13}} (where, however, we should read with the LXX {{GHGheb|text=הַדָּבָר}}). Cf. moreover, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=24}} ''the thigh'' {{GHGheb|text=וְהֶֽעָלֶ֫יהָ|translate=and that which was upon it}} (but see k below); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=1|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽהֵכִין}} equivalent to {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽאֲשֶׁר הֵכִין|translate=to the place, that he had prepared}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|138|k}}
In all the examples adduced except {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=24}} (where {{GHGheb|text=וְהָֽאַלְיָה}} should probably be read for {{GHGheb|text=וְהֶֽעָלֶ֫יהְ}} the {{GHGheb|text=הַ}} is followed by undoubted perfects; almost all the examples, moreover, belong to the latest Books (Ezra and Chronicles). On the other hand, another series of instances (even in the older texts) is extremely doubtful, in which the Masora likewise requires perfects, either by placing the tone on the penultima, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=46|verse=27|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=2|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=הַבָּ֫אָה}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=הַשָּׂ֫מָה}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=הַֽהֻלָּ֫לָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=1|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=6|hidebook=1}} and 4:3 {{GHGheb|text=הַשָּׁ֫בָה}}, or by the punctuation, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=הַנּוֹלַד}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=8|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=הַנִּרְאָה}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=56|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=הַנִּלְוָה}}, while no doubt the authors in all these cases intended participles (and in fact perfect participles, cf. {{GHGpar|116|d}}) with the article, thus {{GHGheb|text=הַבָּאָ֫ה}}, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=הַֽהֻלָּלָה}} for {{GHGheb|text=הַמְהֻלָּלָה}} according to {{GHGpar|52|s}}, and in the other examples {{GHGheb|text=הַנּוֹלָד}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַנִּרְאֶה}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַנִּלְוֶה}}.
<section end="par138" />
<section begin="par139" />{{GHGpar-heading|139|Expression of Pronominal Ideas by means of Substantives}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|139|a}}
Analogous to the periphrases for expressing materials and attributes by means of substantives ({{GHGpar|128|o}} and p), is the use of substantives to represent certain kinds of pronominal ideas, for which no special expressions exist. Thus—

{{GHGmargin-letter|139|b}}
'''1.''' {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=אִשָּׁה|translate=man, woman}}, are used to express—

(''a'') The idea of ''each, every'' (in the sense of each severally) with reference to persons,<ref>As a rule {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}} is used in the particularizing sense of ''each man'', with the plural of the verb, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=11}}; sometimes, however, as subject to a verb in the singular, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=13}}.</ref> and even animals ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=10}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=10|verse=5}}, feminine {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}} is the object, e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=12|verse=15}}. On {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}}—{{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}} cf. {{GHGpar|123|c}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|139|c}}
In a few passages {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}} in the above sense is placed for the sake of emphasis before the governing noun (always a substantive with a suffix), thus {{GHGheb|text=מִיַּד אִישׁ אָחִיו}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=5}}, according to the usual explanation, stands for {{GHGheb|text=מִיַּד אֲחִי אִישׁ|translate=at the hand of the brother of every man}}. But although the explanation seems to be<section end="par139" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

472.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par139 />supported by {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=25}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=17}}, it is inconceivable that such an inversion of {{GHGterm|nomen regens}} and ''rectum'' should occur. It is more likely, either that the second substantive is in apposition to {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}} (thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=5}} ''at the hand of every man, his brother'', [unless it is a combination of the two readings {{GHGheb|text=מִיַּד אִישׁ}} and {{GHGheb|text=מִיַּד הָֽאָדָם}}]; similarly 15:10 ''and he laid each'' or, more exactly, ''one piece of it'', &c., and so probably also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=17}} ''every one'', sc. ''his name''), or {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}} precedes as a kind of ''casus pendens'', and only receives its nearer definition from the following substantive with suffix; thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=25|hidebook=1}} (according to the context = ''to every one in his sack''); 42:35, where {{GHGheb|text=צְרוֹר־כַּסְפּוֹ בְּשַׂקּוֹ}} is virtually the predicate of {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=28|verse=21|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=26|verse=54|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=23|verse=35}}, and especially {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=7|verse=10}}.<ref>Cf. on the whole question the thorough discussion by Budde, ''Die bibl. Urgeschichte'', p. 283 ff.: according to him, the words in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=5}} are to be rendered ''at the hand of one another'' (from men mutually) ''will I require it''. [In support of this view, Budde points to {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=7|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּלְבַבְכֶם וְרָעַת אִישׁ אָהִיו אַל־תַּהְשְׁבוּ}}, which in the light of 8:17, {{GHGheb|text=וְאִישׁ אֶת־רָעַת רֵעֵהוּ אַל־תַּחְשְׁבוּ בִּלְבַבְכֶם}}, can only, he observes, be rendered ‘and devise not ''the hurt of one another'' in your heart’. So also König, ''Syntax'', § 33.]</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|139|d}}
(''b'') ''Any one, some one'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=13|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=8|verse=7}}, with a negative ''no one'';<ref>Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אֵין־אִישׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=11}}. On the expression of the idea of ''no one'' by means of {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} with a following participle, see the ''Negative Sentences'', {{GHGpar|152|l}}.</ref> so after {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=19}}, 29; before {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=23|verse=6}} and frequently.—Instead of {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}} we sometimes find in a similar sense {{GHGheb|text=אָדָם|translate=man, homo}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=1|verse=2}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=כְּאַחַד הָֽאָדָם|translate=as any one else}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=7}}, 11), {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫פֶשׁ}} (''soul'') ''person'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=2|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, &c., and in a neuter sense {{GHGheb|text=דָּבָר}} (prop. word, thing) for ''anything'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=14}}, or {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־דָּבָר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=31|verse=23}}. With a negative {{GHGheb|text=דָּבָר}} means ''nothing''; thus after {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=8}}; after {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=8|verse=5}}.—Cf. finally, {{GHGheb|text=מֵֽאַחַד|translate=any one}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=15|verse=7}}; ''anything'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=18|verse=10}} (but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=4|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=13|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=מֵֽאַחַת}}) and the expressions noticed in {{GHGpar|144|e}}. The latter include also instances like {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=18|verse=32}} ''I have no pleasure'' {{GHGheb|text=בְּמֹוֹת הַמֵּת|translate=in the death of him that dieth}}, i.e. ''of any man''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|139|e}}
(''c'') In connexion with {{GHGheb|text=אָחִיו|translate=his brother}} or {{GHGheb|text=רֵעֵ֫הוּ|translate=his neighbour}}, {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ|translate=one}}, masc. (as {{GHGheb|text=אִשָּׁה|translate=one}}, fem., in connexion with {{GHGheb|text=אֲחוֹתָהּ|translate=her sister}} or {{GHGheb|text=רְעוּתָהּ|translate=her neighbour}}) is used to represent the ideas of ''alter—alter, the one—the other''<ref>Elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=זֶה... זֶה}} are used in a similar sense, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=14|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=3}}; also {{GHGheb|text=הָֽאֶחָד... הָֽאֶחָד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=6}}, or the substantive is repeated, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=21}} (''from one end... to the other end'').</ref> (in reference to persons, animals, or things without life; see the Lexicon) or the idea of ''one another'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=13|verse=11}} ''and they separated them selves'' {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ מֵעַל אָחִיו|translate=the one from the other}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=3}} ''five curtains'' ({{GHGheb|text=יְרִיעֹת}} fem.) ''shall be coupled together'' {{GHGheb|text=אִשָּׁה אֶל־אֲחֹתָהּ|translate=one to another}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|139|f}}
2. {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫פֶשׁ|translate=soul, person}} expresses the idea of ''self'',<ref>On the representation of this idea by pronouns, separate and suffixed, see {{GHGpar|135|a}}, i and k.</ref> both in the singular, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=19|verse=8}}, 16, 29:24, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=18|verse=4}} (in all cases {{GHGheb|text=נַפְשׁוֹ}} equivalent to ''himself'') and in the plural, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=37|verse=9}}, &c. Similar to this is the use of {{GHGheb|text=בְּקִרְבָּךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=12}} (prop. ''in her inward part'') in the sense of ''within herself''.<ref>In a similar way the idea of ''self'' in Arabic, as in Sanskrit (''âtman''), is paraphrased by ''soul, spirit''; in Arabic also by ''eye''; in Rabbinic by {{GHGheb|text=גּוּף|translate=body}}, {{GHGheb|text=גֶּ֫רֶם}} or {{GHGheb|text=עֶ֫צֶם|translate=bone}}, in Ethiopic and Amharic by ''head'', in Egyptian by ''mouth, hand'', &c.; cf. also the Middle High German ''mîn lîp, dîn lîp'', for ''ich, du''. However, {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫פֶשׁ}} in such cases is never (not even in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=46|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=נַפְשָׁם|translate=they themselves}}) a merely otiose periphrasis for the personal pronoun, but always involves a reference to the ''mental'' personality, as affected by the senses, desires, &c.</ref><section end=par139 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

473.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par139 />{{GHGmargin-letter|139|g}}
