On the imperfect consecutive as expressing a logical consequence, see {{GHGpar|111|l}}; on the perfect consecutive as a consecutive clause after a participle, see {{GHGpar|112|n}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|166|b}}
2. Conjunctions introducing consecutive clauses are again (see {{GHGpar|157|c}}, note 3) {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}} and {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}}={{GHGtranslate|so that}}; especially again after interrogative sentences, according to {{GHGpar|107|u}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=16|verse=11}}, {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}} with the imperfect, {{GHGtranslate|that ye murmur}}; but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=20|verse=10}} with the perfect, in reference to an action already completed. On {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} with the imperfect (or jussive) equivalent to ''so that'', cf. further {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=13|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=22|verse=14|hidebook=1}}; with perfect and imperfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=3|verse=12 f.}}, with the demonstrative force clearly discernible, depending on {{GHGheb|text=לֵב}}; on {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר לֹא}}={{GHGtranslate|ut non}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=35}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=3|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=9|verse=37}}.

On {{GHGheb|text=מִן}} with a substantive or infinitive as the equivalent of a consecutive clause, see {{GHGpar|119|y}}.
<section end="par166" />
<section begin="par167" />{{GHGpar-heading|167|Aposiopesis, Anacoluthon, Involved Series of Sentences}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|167|a}}
1. ''Aposiopesis'' is the concealment or suppression of entire sentences or clauses, which are of themselves necessary to complete the sense,<ref>But those cases are not to be regarded as examples of aposiopesis, in which the answer, being closely connected with the question, is given simply in the infinitive with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}; cf. {{GHGpar|147|a}}, note 1.</ref> and therefore must be supplied from the context. This is especially frequent after conditional clauses; besides the examples already given in {{GHGpar|159|dd}}, cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=32}} (the LXX and Samaritan supply {{GHGheb|text=שָׂא}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=16}} (in verse 19, after a long parenthesis, an imperative follows as the apodosis to this conditional clause); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=12|verse=14}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=5|verse=8}} (where indeed the text is probably very corrupt; cf. the addition in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=11|verse=6}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=23|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=27|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=4|verse=10}}. For other examples of various kinds, see {{GHGpar|117|l}}, and especially {{GHGpar|147}}; in Aramaic, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=3|verse=15}}.—On {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=22}}, cf. {{GHGpar|152|w}} at the end.

{{GHGmargin-letter|167|b}}
2. ''Anacoluthon'' is the change from a construction which has been already begun to one of a different kind. It is found especially after long parentheses, because the speaker has either lost sight of the beginning of his sentence, or for the sake of clearness purposely makes a new beginning; thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=20|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=52|hidebook=1}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=34|verse=10}} (cf. {{GHGpar|149}} at the end); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=21 ff.}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=32|verse=20 ff.|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=17|verse=2 ff.}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=24|verse=1 ff.|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=29|verse=21 ff.|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=10|verse=11}} (where, after a series of intermediate sentences, the predicate ''I saved you'' is {{Hyphenated word start|sup|pressed}}<section end="par167" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

530.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par167 />{{Hyphenated word end|pressed|suppressed}}; but the text can hardly be correct); perhaps also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=66|verse=18}} (cf., however, Delitzsch on the passage, which is certainly corrupt).<ref>On the other hand, from the Semitic point of view the various kinds of compound sentences are ''not'' to be regarded as instances of anacoluthon, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=14.17}}, nor even {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=40}} (cf. {{GHGpar|143}}).</ref> On {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=23|verse=13}} ({{GHGheb|text=לוּ}} with the imperative), see {{GHGpar|110|e}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|167|c}}
'''3.''' We may mention as instructive examples of ''involved series'' of sentences {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=14}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=42 ff.|hidebook=v}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=28|verse=6 ff.}}<section end=par167 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>

531.text:
<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="RyanDavis" /></noinclude><!-- no section needed -->{{center|'''THE PARADIGMS.'''}}

In the paradigms of the verbs, those forms which are to be especially noticed by the beginner are marked throughout by an asterisk as model forms. Thus e.g. in the strong verb the 3rd ''sing. fem''. {{GHGheb|text=קָֽטְלָה}} is the model for {{GHGheb|text=קָֽטְלוּ}}, which likewise has only a vocalic afformative, and {{GHGheb|text=קָטַ֫לְתָּ}} is the model for {{GHGheb|text=קָטַלְתְּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=קָטַ֫לְתִּי}} and {{GHGheb|text=קָטַ֫לְנוּ}}, which in the same way have a toneless afformative beginning with a consonant. On the other hand, the forms {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתֶּם}} and {{GHGheb|text=קְטַלְתֶּן}}, where the affix beginning with a consonant has the tone, stand by themselves.—In the table of the pronouns the asterisk has a different meaning; see the footnote there.—The bracketed forms (for Paradigm G onwards) are merely analogous formations not occurring in the Old Testament.

The newly added paradigm (Q) consists of forms actually found, belonging to various verbs.<!-- no section needed --><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
